Check the Alaska must-sees off your list
blocks.text: Alaska is vast in a way that’s hard to grasp until you’re in it. Glaciers stretch for miles and calve into the sea with a crack like thunder. Humpback whales blast from the depths in explosions of muscle and mist, and awe-inspiring bald eagles perch above harbors with all the nonchalance of New York pigeons. In the space of a single day, you might walk through Gold Rush-era towns, watch brown bear

blocks.heading: 5 epic national parks
blocks.text: Our Alaska cruises and cruisetours take you to five national parks, with excursions that bring you up close to wildlife and historic landmarks. More: Alaska national parks

blocks.heading: 5 Exclusive Lodges
blocks.text: The untamed land becomes accessible with lodge stays near Kenai, Wrangell-St. Elias, and Denali national parks.

blocks.heading: Fairbanks Princess Riverside Lodge®
blocks.text: Look for inspiration in the heart of Alaska’s wild interior, filled with the potential for experiences that few people will ever know. Set on the banks of the Chena River, the Fairbanks Princess Riverside Lodge® is your gateway to this land.

blocks.heading: Historic frontier towns
blocks.text: From the capital Juneau to historical Skagway, there’s time to get acquainted with the local flavor and connect with the past. More: Alaska cruise ports of call

blocks.heading: Alaska cruise excursions for every interest and family member
blocks.text: Whether you’re amped about getting up close to glaciers or ready to follow in the steps of the gold rush, you can follow your passions in Alaska.

blocks.heading: Whales & Wildlife Cruise
blocks.text: Travel from your Alaska cruise to the Point Adolphus area, one of Alaska's premier whale-watching sites, where you're guaranteed to catch sight of these incredible creatures. As you relax in the warm main cabin, your onboard naturalist will describe the diverse marine life that congregates here each summer to feed in the nutrient-rich waters. You'll learn about the behavior and habitat of the wild

blocks.heading: Turnagain Arm, Wildlife Conservation Center & Tram with Airport Transfer
blocks.text: Discover natural treasures on this 6-hour tour during your Alaska cruise. Visit a wild animal refuge, a scenic bird sanctuary and behold the rugged majesty of Mt. Alyeska and the history of Alaska. Visit the Alaska Wildlife Conservation Center, where orphaned and displaced animals are given refuge in spacious habitats. Here, you can observe and photograph some of Alaska's biggest land animals, inc

blocks.heading: Eagle Preserve Rafting & Wildlife Quest
blocks.text: Your tour begins with a scenic, narrated drive to the "Valley of the Eagles." At the Chilkat Bald Eagle Preserve, experienced guides await to begin your rafting adventure (not whitewater). You'll float silently down the river aboard 18' inflatable rafts - the best way to observe eagles drawn to feed on the plentiful salmon. Bears and wolves are also frequent guests at the feast. Not only rich in w

blocks.heading: Discover the Birds of Hoonah
blocks.text: Whether you're an avid ornithologist, a casual birdwatcher, a nature photographer or just crave to try something different in the great outdoors, this excursion, led by a local expert birder, takes small groups from the Alaska cruise to one location to another in a quest to find the best birding locations.

blocks.heading: Birds, Bears & Barnacles
blocks.text: Witness Alaska's remarkable animal kingdom with a half-day excursion from your Alaska cruise. See guaranteed bald eagles at the Alaska Raptor Center, brown bears at the Fortress of the Bear sanctuary and a menagerie of sea creatures at the Sitka Sound Science Center.

blocks.heading: Alaska cruise spotlight: A day in Juneau
blocks.text: Imagine the perfect day in port, taking in the sights and an excursion or two.

blocks.heading: 7:00 p.m. Unwind
blocks.text: Recap the day as you sample your ship’s extensive collection of wines.

blocks.heading: 8:00 a.m. Arrive
blocks.text: Wake up as your ship docks in port. Take your first look at the city nestled at the foot of majestic snow-capped mountains.

blocks.heading: 10:00 a.m. Excursion: Ride a helicopter to Mendenhall Glacier.
blocks.text: Board your helicopter for a breathtaking flight over spectacular ice falls and rock formations, thanks to one of our award-winning shore excursions.

blocks.heading: 10:15 a.m. Touch down at dog sled camp.
blocks.text: Meet professional mushers and their dogs, and experience the thrill of zipping across the snow pack of the Mendenhall Glacier behind a team of huskies.

blocks.heading: 11:30 a.m. Bid a warm farewell to your furry friends.
blocks.text: Cuddle the camp puppies and snap a few photos before re-boarding your helicopter.

blocks.heading: 12:00 p.m. Scenic bus tour
blocks.text: Take in the landscape as you ride back to the Alaska cruise ship pier in Juneau.

blocks.heading: 12:30 p.m. Grab lunch in town after your excursion ends
blocks.text: Feast on local flavors at one of the many restaurants in downtown Juneau.

blocks.heading: 2:00 p.m. Take a spectacular ride on the goldbelt tram.
blocks.text: Take a five-minute tram ride to the top of Mt. Roberts for a panoramic view 1,800 feet above the city.

blocks.heading: 2:30-5:00 p.m. Mt Roberts.
blocks.text: Explore the trails, shops and nature displays high above the town.

blocks.heading: 5:15 p.m. Return to the pier
blocks.text: Ride the tram back down to Juneau, where your ship (and Alaska cruise) is waiting just a few steps away.

pages.title: Alaska Cruise Ports of Call - Princess Cruises
pages.metaDescription: From the sweeping mountains of Juneau to the fish-bearing seas of Ketchikan, discover Alaska cruise ports of call and the adventures that await you.

headings.text: Experience Alaska aboard a Princess cruise
10 unforgettable places to visit in Alaska
13 of the best towns in Alaska

blocks.heading: Ketchikan
blocks.text: Ketchikan, the “Salmon Capital of the World,” boasts Creek Street’s charming boardwalk, Totem Bight State Park’s vibrant totem poles and grizzly bears fishing in shallow waters. Its rich culture and natural beauty make it unforgettable.

blocks.heading: Juneau
blocks.text: Juneau, Alaska’s capital, boasts towering peaks, the 12-mile-long Mendenhall Glacier and wildlife like majestic orcas. Zipline through breathtaking elevations or hike serene meadows surrounded by panoramic beauty.

blocks.heading: Skagway
blocks.text: Step into gold rush history in Skagway, where Victorian architecture, the Klondike Gold Rush National Historical Park and the White Pass Railway offer scenic and cultural treasures. This quaint town combines historic charm with dramatic mountain vistas.

blocks.heading: Whittier
blocks.text: Whittier is an entryway to many dramatic landscapes, with cascading waterfalls and teal-blue waters framed by emerald mountains. Journey the Anton Anderson Tunnel or ascend Mt. Alyeska Tram for aerial views of sculpted glaciers.

blocks.heading: Start your Alaska adventure
blocks.text: VIEW CRUISES

blocks.heading: Sitka
blocks.text: Sitka is steeped in history, from St. Michael’s Russian Orthodox Cathedral to Sitka National Historical Park, where artisans craft Tlingit and Haida-inspired pieces. This fishing paradise also offers scenic coastal views and cultural richness.

blocks.heading: Victoria, B.C.
blocks.text: Victoria’s Butchart Gardens dazzle with glowing waterfalls, floral canopies and enchanting stairways. Horse-drawn carriages pass elegant buildings while tropical butterflies flutter in serene koi ponds, creating a storybook-like atmosphere.

blocks.heading: Haines
blocks.text: Haines offers open roads, towering mountains, and encounters with bears, foxes and moose at Kroschel Wildlife Center. At Chilkat Bald Eagle Preserve, spot over 200 eagles soaring among the trees.

blocks.heading: Vancouver, B.C.
blocks.text: Vancouver charms with Stanley Park’s forested shores, Chinatown’s bustling markets and Gastown’s steam clock chiming on cobblestone streets. Discover Native influences and stunning natural backdrops in this vibrant port city.

blocks.heading: Icy Strait Point
blocks.text: Icy Strait Point – an iconic UNESCO World Heritage Site – contains unspoiled beauty including Alaska’s largest brown bear population, record-breaking fishing and access to Glacier Bay National Park. Thrill-seekers can zip 5,459 feet above sea level on the world’s highest zipline.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Glacier Bay National Park
Watch the glaciers
blocks.text: See the towering Margerie Glacier up close, a wall of deep blue ice stretching into the sea. If you are lucky, you might witness giant ice chunks crashing into the water, sending a thunderous roar across the bay. Most ships spend several hours viewing multiple glaciers during the full-day cruise.

blocks.heading: Take in the untouched scenery
blocks.text: With no roads leading into Glacier Bay National Park, it remains one of Alaska’s most untouched destinations. Cruising through this remote wilderness feels like stepping into a world few get to see.

blocks.heading: Spot wildlife
blocks.text: Glacier Bay National Park is full of incredible wildlife. Watch for humpback whales surfacing nearby, sea otters floating on their backs and bald eagles soaring high overhead. Watch for humpback whales, sea otters, orcas, bald eagles, and brown bears. Peak viewing is typically June–July.

blocks.heading: Chat with Glacier Bay National Park Rangers
blocks.text: When you cruise to Glacier Bay National Park, Park Rangers come aboard to share stories about some of Alaska’s best glaciers, ecosystems and wildlife. Their firsthand knowledge brings the park’s remote beauty to life as you sail through its icy waters.

blocks.heading: Sail by the Johns Hopkins Inlet
blocks.text: If conditions allow, your ship may glide past Johns Hopkins Inlet, surrounded by snow-capped peaks and cascading waterfalls. It’s one of Glacier Bay National Park’s most dramatic and secluded spots, making it a top Alaska destination.

blocks.text: Step into a place where ancient traditions meet wild frontiers. In Icy Strait Point, every experience brings you closer to the soul of southeast Alaska. Watch humpback whales breach off the coast near Point Adolphus, then explore Hoonah, home to Alaska’s largest Tlingit community. Step inside the Cultural Center for traditional dance and storytelling, or hike through the lush Tongass National Fore

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Icy Strait Point
Wilderness Hike
blocks.text: Wander through the moss-draped trails of Tongass National Forest, home to centuries-old trees, wildflowers and hidden streams. Along the way, your guide will point out local wildlife and share stories of the land. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: SkyGlider Mountaintop Gondola
blocks.text: Glide through the forest canopy as you ascend Hoonah Mountain, where breathtaking views of Icy Strait and distant snow-capped peaks await. The smooth, scenic ride gives you a new perspective on Alaska’s vast wilderness. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Whales & Wildlife Cruise
blocks.text: Set out into the rich waters off Point Adolphus, one of the best whale-watching spots in the world. Watch for humpbacks, orcas, sea lions and bald eagles as you cruise past remote islands and rugged coastline. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: ZipRider Adventure & SkyGlider Mountaintop Gondola

When you cruise with Princess, you’ll have the chance to uncover this coastal gem without sacrificing comfort or style. From the moment your ship pulls into port, you’re surrounded by an entire territory’s worth of possibilities. Even with those long northern summer days, you might find that there just aren’t enough hours

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Juneau
blocks.text: White glaciers, umber-green forests, aquamarine waters — and Juneau itself provides the red carpet. From soaring above eagles along ancient icefields to noshing on alder-grilled salmon under the trees, these excursions will put vibrancy into your vacation. If you’re looking to stretch your legs, fill your belly or soak up views that look straight out of National Geographic, there’s a Princess shor

blocks.heading: Mendenhall Glacier Helicopter & Guided Walk
blocks.text: Lift off for a ‘flightseeing’ tour over alpine ridges and icy valleys before landing right on the glacier itself. Once on solid ground (or rather, ice), you’ll join a guide for a short but awe-inspiring walk across the ancient frozen surface. It’s a one-of-a-kind chance to set foot in an environment few people ever encounter and see its crevasses, peaks and glittering depths up close. VIEW EXCURSI

blocks.heading: Mendenhall Glacier Tour
blocks.text: Reach out and touch one of Alaska’s most iconic natural wonders. This laid-back excursion gives you two full hours to explore the trails, waterfalls and scenic viewpoints surrounding Mendenhall Glacier, a natural wonder that’s been slowly reshaping the landscape for millennia. Visit the interactive displays at the visitor center, meander through Tongass National Forest and, if you’re feeling ambit

blocks.heading: Evening Whale Quest Featuring Alaska Cuisine
blocks.text: Glide across the golden waters of an Alaska evening aboard an expedition vessel designed for wildlife viewing — and dinner. An onboard naturalist will narrate your journey, helping you spot humpbacks, orcas and whatever else pops up from the deep. While nature shows off outside, you’ll dig into local dishes like white fish Olympia, reindeer sausage cassoulet and wild berry desserts. This one-of-a-

blocks.heading: Goldbelt Tram On Your Own
blocks.text: Take your Juneau-based adventure to new heights with unlimited rides up Mount Roberts aboard the Goldbelt Tram. Soak in sweeping views, check out Alaska Native art and catch the award-winning Tlingit film Seeing Daylight. It’s a smooth glide from dock to summit — and a great way to squeeze in some culture between glacier hikes and gift shop stops. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Dog Sledding on the Mendenhall Glacier
blocks.text: What’s better than enjoying an eagle’s-eye view of glacial terrain from the souring comfort of a premier helicopter? Following up with a ride across icy terrain behind a team of enthusiastic huskies. After touching down on the glacier, you’ll meet seasoned mushers and take the reins for a thrilling sled run through the icy wild. And, yes: There will be puppies to snuggle once you get back. blocks.heading: Alaska Salmon Bake
blocks.text: This isn’t your typical backyard barbecue — it’s an all-you-can-eat feast in the forest, complete with open-flame grilled wild salmon, creamy au gratin potatoes, tangy barbecue ribs, salads, cornbread and more, followed up with blueberry cake and a campfire for roasting marshmallows. blocks.heading: Things to do in Ketchikan
blocks.text: Totem poles, fjords and seafood dinners await! Check out a unique state historical park where you’ll learn all about Alaskan culture and see ancient totem poles. Or take a cruise out into one of the breathtaking fjords where jagged peaks covered in mist surround you.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Ketchikan
blocks.text: Get the most out of your time on shore in Ketchikan with a few shore excursions. These experiences cover everything from nature to culture and will help you see what this unique area has to offer.

blocks.heading: Great Alaskan Lumberjack Show & Crab Feast
blocks.text: Indulge in an extravaganza of Alaskan culture and cuisine with a duo of legendary "must-dos." The fun begins with the Great Alaskan Lumberjack Show. You'll see Alaska's famed lumberjacks battle British Columbia's premier woodsmen in a no-holds-barred competition for the title "Bull of the Woods." VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Totem Bight State Historical Park
blocks.text: Discover the art and history of Alaska’s Native cultures. On this excursion, you’ll see everything from Alaska’s busiest water front to its Gold Rush “red light” district to its Native roots. Totem Bight State Historical Park has 14 colorful totem poles that you’ll learn about to really delve into Alaska’s history. Did we mention the state park is also home to jaw dropping Alaska scenery? Keep you

blocks.heading: Misty Fjords & Wilderness Explorer Cruise
blocks.text: Soar over pristine fjords and glacial valleys on this boat tour. You’ll be surrounded by 3,000 foot cliffs and deep forest — and the calls of seabirds nesting on the rockface. This tour will take you to an active bald eagle nest as well as the staggering New Eddystone Rock, an immense volcanic spire rising from the ocean around you. Duration: 5.25 hours VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Ultimate Saxman Experience: Cultural Showcase, Native Crafts & Culinary Tasting
blocks.text: Step directly into history at this cultural showcase where you’ll see the rich living culture of southeast Alaska's Native Americans. Wander through Saxman Native Village and learn about local crafts, design your own ornament, chow down on a delicious three-course meal of Alaska delicacies and finish out the day with a musical performance from the Cape Fox Dancers in the unique Beaver Clan House.

blocks.heading: Alaska Fishing & Wilderness Dining
blocks.text: No meal tastes better than one you caught yourself in the Alaska waters. Cast your line in some of the world's richest waters where you might just catch yourself a Pacific salmon. After a day on the water, the camp cook will prepare your fresh catch, so you can enjoy your hard work. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Great Alaskan Lumberjack Show
blocks.text: Curious about what it’s like to be a lumberjack up in Alaska? Wonder no more after watching this unique show where real lumberjacks will compete for the title of "Bull of the Woods." These awesome lumberjacks will participate in events like springboard chopping, buck sawing, axe throwing, log rolling and the thrilling 50-foot tree climb. And they’ll tell you lumberjack lore stories throughout. Dur

blocks.heading: Things to do in Prince Rupert
blocks.text: With a balance of immersive cultural experiences and outdoor exploration, Prince Rupert offers guests a chance to slow down and take in the wild charm of northern British Columbia. Venture into the Great Bear Rainforest in search of wildlife like the elusive spirit bear. Prince Rupert is most commonly visited as part of Alaska Inside Passage cruises, where it's included alongside other scenic coas

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Prince Rupert
Butze Rainforest Nature Hike
blocks.text: Witness the swirling waters of Butze Rapids and walk through moss-draped rainforest on this invigorating nature hike just minutes from downtown Prince Rupert. The trail offers scenic viewpoints and a peaceful immersion into one of British Columbia’s most lush coastal ecosystems. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Wilderness Waterfront Kayaking & Rainforest Walk
blocks.text: Paddle through Prince Rupert’s peaceful harbor on a guided kayak tour from Cow Bay Marina to Seal Cove. This three-hour experience brings you up close to marine wildlife and rainforest landscapes for a serene escape from the everyday. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Bald Eagle, Marine Wildlife & Historical Lighthouse Cruise
blocks.text: Cruise the surrounding waters to catch glimpses of bald eagles soaring above and seals lounging on rocky outcroppings. This half-day tour also includes views of a historic lighthouse, offering a memorable glimpse into the region’s maritime character. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Panoramic Mountain Trail Trek
blocks.text: For hiking enthusiasts, this guided trek up Mt. Oldfield in the heart of the Great Bear Rainforest delivers sweeping views and quiet trails. Although the hike can be challenging, it comes with a rewarding sense of discovery. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: North Pacific Cannery History Site Exploration Walk
blocks.text: Step back in time at the oldest intact cannery in British Columbia. Learn how the fishing industry shaped the community and explore original buildings set along the Skeena River. It’s the perfect way to enjoy a bit of history and fresh air. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Things to do in Skagway
blocks.text: From soaring over the tree tops on a zipline to panning for gold, Skagway is the perfect place to step into Alaska’s history and stunning scenery. This colorful town used to be a Gold Rush village where prospectors from all over came, and today, you can walk in their footsteps by panning for gold and taking their historic trains. Or head out into the wild Alaska wilderness for waterfalls, lush for

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Skagway
blocks.text: Skagway is a land of towering peaks, rich Gold Rush history and vibrant wildlife like moose and bears. When you visit with Princess, you can immerse yourself in the Gold Rush history by trying traditional gold panning or riding the Yukon Railway. Feeling more adventurous? You’ll love a UTV ride or ziplining through the lush Alaska forests where you can see waterfalls cascading beneath you or maybe

blocks.heading: Glacier Point Wilderness Safari
blocks.text: If you crave a taste of Alaska's wilderness, this trip is for you! This 6-hour tour is an incredible experience that takes you face-to-face with a massive glacier in one of the most spectacular settings on the planet. Your adventure begins as you explore the rugged beauty of Alaska's deepest fjord from a custom marine vessel designed for wildlife viewing. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Yukon Expedition & White Pass Scenic Railway
blocks.text: All aboard! Ride on the historic Yukon White Pass Railway to see some of Alaska’s most beautiful scenery, including the 3,290-foot White Pass Summit and Tormented Valley that looks like they came right off a postcard. You’ll be following in the footsteps of prospectors from the 1898 Klondike Gold Rush all day because they used to take this train route on their way to Skagway to search for gold. VI

blocks.heading: Gold Fever Experience: Gold Panning & Alaska Sled Dogs
blocks.text: Did somebody say puppies? That’s right, on this excursion you’ll head to the heart of the Klondike for a dog sledding demonstration — and a meet and greet with the dogs and their puppies. These dog sleds were the primary mode of winter transportation during the gold rush, and now you can see what it’s like! Afterward, experience the Gold Rush by panning for gold the old fashioned way. There’s no b

blocks.heading: Grizzly Falls Ziplining Expedition
blocks.text: Ready to get your heart pumping with a treetop adventure? Ride the 10 Grizzly Falls ziplines through the lush Alaska forest and across 4 suspension bridges spread across the towering pines. This isn’t for the faint of heart because you’ll reach speeds of 45 mph! But nothing beats soaring past a misty Alaska waterfall that’s cascading into the river beneath you. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Wilderness UTV Adventure
blocks.text: See Alaska’s wilderness the way it was meant to be seen: by UTV. This thrilling ride will take you deep into the forest and across sprawling meadows. You’ll see the Sawtooth Mountain range, the Skagway river and rolling pine forests. Keep an eye out for eagles, bears and moose — and even salmon leaping from the rivers. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Skagway Street Car City Tour with Storyteller
blocks.text: You don’t even have to leave Skagway to see some amazing sites. Hop aboard a yellow 1927 sightseeing bus to see the best Skagway has to offer and the history and stories from an expert guide. You’ll see the waterfront, the Gold Rush Cemetery where prospectors are buried, the National Park Historic District and your cruise ship sitting in port surrounded by mountains. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Haines Eagle Preserve Rafting & Wildlife Quest
blocks.text: A high-speed catamaran to Haines, a rafting adventure in the Chilkat Bald Eagle Reserve, and a riverside picnic make this a wildlife tour of a lifetime. Your tour begins as you board a high-speed catamaran for a cruise along North America's longest and deepest fjord to Haines. Next, you'll board a motorcoach for a relaxing 40-minute drive up the Haines Highway to the preserve. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Things to do in College Fjord
blocks.text: A cruise through College Fjord offers glacier viewing set against raw, untouched wilderness — right from your ship. College Fjord stands out for its high concentration of glaciers, where you can often see multiple tidewater and mountain glaciers at once during a single scenic cruise. As ships cruise through College Fjord, they often slow down or pause to allow for close-up views of the surrounding

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in College Fjord
Learn the history of College Fjord
blocks.text: Discovered during a scientific expedition at the end of the 19th century, College Fjord stands out not only for its glacial beauty but also its intellectual legacy. The naming of its glaciers after prestigious colleges was a tribute by the explorers, many of whom were Ivy League alumni. You’ll find a blend of natural wonder with academic tradition.

blocks.heading: Watch a glacier calve
blocks.text: Feel the anticipation as you wait for the telltale crack of ice breaking free. With dozens of tidewater glaciers in College Fjord, it’s one of the few places where you might witness a glacier calving. You’ll see towering chunks of ice crashing into the sea, followed by a thunderous splash that echoes through the fjord.

blocks.heading: Take in the stunning glacier views
blocks.text: College Fjord is flanked by glacier after glacier, including Harvard, Yale, Smith and Amherst (named by the Harriman Expedition of 1899). These mighty glaciers stretch for miles, creating a dramatic corridor of ice that reflects the light in brilliant shades of silver and blue. Harvard Glacier is the largest and most prominent glacier in College Fjord, and ships often slow down or pause here to al

blocks.heading: Spot wildlife in the fjord
blocks.text: Keep your binoculars ready because the nutrient-rich waters and quiet coves of College Fjord support an abundance of wildlife. Look for sea otters drifting among the ice, humpback whales surfacing in the distance or bald eagles perched atop spruce trees along the shoreline. Wildlife is often spotted in College Fjord, including seals resting on ice, sea otters in the water, and seabirds flying over

blocks.heading: Things to do around Endicott Arm & Dawes Glacier
blocks.text: Located in Southeast Alaska near Juneau, Endicott Arm is a remote fjord within the Tracy Arm-Fords Terror Wilderness, offering a pristine and untouched glacier experience. There’s no shortage of excitement along the Endicott Arm — waterfalls that tumble down from cliffs that seem to touch the sky, harbor seals resting or playing with their pups on clumps of floating ice and even pods of humpback w

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Endicott Arm & Dawes Glacier
blocks.text: Want to get even closer to the action? Princess has you covered, with two scenic catamaran excursions through the dazzling Endicott Arm and Dawes Glacier waters. The Endicott Arm Fjord & Dawes Glacier Exploration Cruise will have you back in three hours, while the Endicott Arm Fjord & Glacier Explorer gives you six hours to really get the most out of your tour. Along the way, guests may spot Alask

blocks.heading: Savor Alaska’s flavors
blocks.text: Nothing warms up like a bite of something fresh and local — and onboard, Alaska’s signature flavors are front and center. Think flaky salmon, rich chowders and other regional dishes crafted by expert chefs. It’s the perfect way to bring a little taste of Alaska to your table, no hiking boots required.

blocks.heading: Dawes Glacier viewing
blocks.text: Few sights compare to seeing Dawes Glacier up close — a massive, frozen deluge of ice that presses right to the water’s edge. As your ship draws near, you’ll witness deep blue crevasses, towering ice walls and the occasional splash of falling ice as the glacier shifts. It’s a quiet yet powerful moment — one that will give you a whole new appreciation for the forces shaping Alaska’s landscape.

blocks.heading: Wildlife spotting
blocks.text: Keep your eyes peeled and your camera ready, because the area around Endicott Arm is a haven for wild creatures big and small. You might spot harbor seals lounging on floating ice, eagles circling overhead or even the unmistakable spray of whales bursting through the surface. With nature putting on a show around every corner, there’s always something worth watching.

blocks.heading: Fjord exploration
blocks.text: Sailing through Endicott Arm is like entering another world — one carved by the inexorable forces of nature. Towering cliffs, winding passages and floating chunks of glacial ice make this a journey you’ll want to savor slowly. Whether you’re out on deck or watching from your balcony, this is the kind of scenery that will make your jaw drop (so bring an extra memory card for your camera).

blocks.heading: Experience the Endicott Arm & Dawes Glacier port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Princess heeds the call to adventure through some of the most rugged, untouched wilderness on the planet — think misty cliffs, drifting icebergs and wildlife that seems straight out of a nature documentary. And while the scenery is pure wilderness, your experience onboard is anything but, with the kind of comfort and luxury that makes every icy mile feel like a dream.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Haines
blocks.text: Haines offers a unique mix of wilderness and culture, making it one of Alaska’s best-kept secrets. Visit the Chilkat Bald Eagle Preserve, where thousands of bald eagles gather along the riverbanks each fall. Haines also offers a glimpse into local history and culture, with highlights like Fort William H. Seward and the unique Hammer Museum, both located near the cruise port. Explore the quirky Ham

blocks.heading: Best of Haines Highlights
blocks.text: See the best of Haines in one scenic, easy-paced excursion. Visit Fort William H. Seward, the American Bald Eagle Foundation and photo-worthy stops along the Chilkat River Valley. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Eagle Preserve Rafting & Wildlife Quest
blocks.text: Float through the heart of the Chilkat Bald Eagle Preserve, home to the world’s largest congregation of bald eagles. This peaceful rafting trip also offers a chance to spot bears, moose and other wildlife along the riverbank. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Glacier Point Wilderness Safari
blocks.text: Take a high-speed boat across Lynn Canal, then hike through pristine rainforest before paddling to the face of a remote glacier. It’s a rare chance to stand where ice meets sea in Alaska’s untouched wilderness. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Chilkoot Lake Kayak Experience
blocks.text: Glide across turquoise waters surrounded by forested peaks and cascading waterfalls. Keep an eye out for eagles overhead and bears fishing along the shoreline during this immersive kayaking excursion. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Takshanuk Mountain Trail by 4x4
blocks.text: Buckle up for a thrilling 4x4 adventure up rugged alpine trails. Take in panoramic views from the mountaintop and enjoy a hearty meal at a scenic lodge tucked deep in the wilderness. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Things to do in Sitka
blocks.text: From historic landmarks to wildlife experiences, Sitka offers something for every kind of traveler. Set on Baranof Island, Sitka invites you to discover its multicultural roots — exploring Russian cathedrals and Tlingit Indigenous art or heading into the wilderness for close encounters with bald eagles, sea otters, humpback whales and brown bears. Wander the totem-lined trails of Sitka National Hi

blocks.heading: Best of Sitka: Otters, Raptors & Bears
blocks.text: See Alaska’s wilderness the way it was meant to be seen: by UTV. This thrilling ride will take you deep into the forest and across sprawling meadows. Keep an eye out for eagles, bear and moose — and even salmon leaping from the rivers. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Easy Sitka: Historic City Highlights
blocks.text: All aboard! Ride on the historic Yukon White Pass Railway to see some of Alaska’s most beautiful scenery, including the 3,290-foot White Pass Summit and Tormented Valley. You’ll be following in the footsteps of prospectors from the 1898 Klondike Gold Rush all day. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: All About Sitka: Russian & Tlingit Heritage Discovery
blocks.text: Did somebody say puppies? That’s right, on this excursion you’ll head to the heart of the Klondike for a dog sledding demonstration — and a meet and greet with the dogs and their puppies. Afterward, experience the Gold Rush by panning for gold the old fashioned way. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Experience Sitka: Raptor Center, Park & Fortress of the Bear
blocks.text: Ready to get your heart pumping with a treetop adventure? Ride the 10 Grizzly Falls ziplines through the lush Alaska forest and across 4 suspension bridges. This isn’t for the faint of heart because you’ll reach speeds of 45 mph! But nothing beats soaring past a misty Alaska waterfall. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.text: Tracy Arm Fjord is a front-row seat to Alaska at its most dramatic. Watch South Sawyer Glacier calve thunderously into the sea, spot seals lounging on drifting ice or just bundle up and enjoy what might be the freshest air your lungs have ever sampled. blocks.text: Why should your eyes and ears get all the attention? The Tracy Arm is a feast for all the senses, and with Princess, fresh Alaska cuisine is a major highlight. blocks.text: A scenic cruising day through Tracy Arm Fjord isn’t just a break between ports — it’s a signature Alaska experience all on its own. blocks.heading: Things to do in Victoria
blocks.text: Victoria is home to sprawling acres of stunning gardens, rich history and humpbacks breaching from its coastal waters — making it one of the most picturesque and inviting cities in Canada to visit. The charming Inner Harbour buzzes with street performers and horse-drawn carriages, while the iconic Fairmont Empress Hotel stands as a testament to the city's elegant colonial heritage. Whether you're

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Victoria
blocks.text: Want to see the best of Victoria without stress and hassle? A shore excursion is the perfect way to visit the must-see spots and relax at the same time. Whether you want to zipline through the forest or see orcas, there’s a shore excursion for the best things to do in Victoria.

blocks.heading: Enchanting Butchart Gardens
blocks.text: Wander through some of the most magical gardens in Victoria. The gardens began in 1904 when Jennie Butchart began to plant flowers and beautify an old mine quarry, and today it’s fifty-five acres of dazzling floral displays. You won’t want to miss the beautiful Rose Fountain or the Night Illuminations. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Spot wildlife
blocks.text: All aboard! Take a whale watching boat out to Victoria’s best spots to see if you can spot orcas, humpbacks and gray whales — not to mention all of the sea lions and bald eagles. While there’s no guarantee that you’ll see wild animals, this tour has a 90% success rate, so keep your camera handy. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Guided Canopy Zipline Experience
blocks.text: If you’ve ever wanted to feel like you’re flying, you’ll love soaring over 100 acres of lush Victoria forest on this zipline experience. You’ll get to try 8 different ziplines that are up to 150 feet above the ground, and you’ll get an unforgettable view of the area. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: High Tea at Pendray Mansion & city highlights
blocks.text: Experience one of Western Canada’s oldest traditions: taking tea. Sit down for high tea — complete with delicious scones, heavy creams and finger sandwiches — at the historic Pendray Mansion. You’ll get some stunning waterfront views and a taste of the region’s history. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Craigdarroch Castle, Mt. Tolmie & city highlights
blocks.text: See the best of Victoria: tour Craigdarroch Castle, take in the panoramic views from Mt. Tolmie and explore Victoria’s historic downtown. You’ll see Chinatown, a 20,000 square foot castle and breathtaking views of Vancouver Island. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Things to do in Whittier (Anchorage)
blocks.text: You won’t find a bustling downtown or flashy tourist traps in Whittier — and that’s kind of the point. The real show happens outside the town limits, with glaciers, wildlife and epic views. And, for those who like their wilderness with a side of city life, Anchorage provides a uniquely Alaska take on urban enjoyment. Whatever your preferences, here are some nearby adventures to give you an authent

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore the Whittier/Anchorage area
blocks.text: Adventures that begin in or around Whittier are anything but small. Princess excursions take you to where the action is, with fascinating and thrilling excursion experiences that will turn your travel day into something more than just a trip from A to B. Here are a few favorites to give you a taste of Alaska — Whittier style:

blocks.heading: Turnagain Treasures Photo Adventure with Airport Transfer
blocks.text: For those who think a great photo is the best souvenir, this guided day trip lines up every frame just right — from misty rainforests to glacier-tipped peaks. With expert guidance, you'll chase the best light across Turnagain Arm, Portage Valley and Whittier. Along the way, snap shots of coastal cliffs, colorful meadows and mountain backdrops that feel too good to be real. This includes snacks and

blocks.heading: Turnagain Arm, Wildlife Conservation Center & Tram with Airport Transfer
blocks.text: This all-in-one excursion covers some of Alaska’s most scenic spots. Travel the Seward Highway, visit the Alaska Wildlife Conservation Center, and ride the Glacier Express Tram for mountain views that would make eagles jealous. It’s a full day of sights, encounters and fresh air — and a great way to travel between ship and airport. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: 26 Glacier Cruise
blocks.text: Speed through Prince William Sound on a catamaran to see 26 named glaciers. Yes, 26 — that’s not a typo. You and your fellow guests won’t be the ones experiencing these natural wonders, either; otters, bald eagles, porpoises and whales will be right there sharing in the adventure — it’s like an issue of National Geographic, but this time you get to be the photographer. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Portage Glacier Scenic Cruise & Drive with Airport Transfer
blocks.text: This tour is your all-access pass to one of Alaska’s most iconic glaciers — with a little shopping and sightseeing thrown in. It kicks off at the Begich, Boggs Visitor Center, followed by a scenic cruise on Portage Lake aboard the m/v Ptarmigan (a heated catamaran with an open-air top deck that gets you within 300 yards of Portage Glacier). After the cruise, grab lunch (on your own) and browse loc

blocks.heading: National Parks cruisetours
blocks.text: Explore up to five of Alaska’s National Parks with our National Parks Cruisetours. Cruise Glacier Bay’s pristine waters, be awe-struck by Kenai Fjords icefields, and feed your wanderlust by adventuring into Denali National Park. Venture into Wrangell-St. Elias, America’s largest national park or step back in time at Klondike Gold Rush National Historical Park in Skagway.

blocks.heading: Princess Wilderness Lodges
blocks.text: You won’t just explore Alaska’s landscapes with Princess; you’ll stay in the heart of the region's best and most beautiful attractions. Our custom-built wilderness lodges are located riverside next to some of the most renowned national parks, allowing you to unwind after your adventures with comforting amenities and breathtaking scenery.

blocks.heading: Voyage of the Glaciers
blocks.text: Sail 500 miles deeper into the Gulf of Alaska and Prince William Sound on our top-rated Voyage of the Glaciers Alaska cruise vacation. Spend seven days traveling from Anchorage (Whittier) to Vancouver, B.C., stopping in historic port cities like Ketchikan, Juneau and Skagway. Enjoy icy-blue viewings at spots like Glacier Bay National Park, Hubbard Glacier and College Fjord.

blocks.heading: Direct-to-the-Wilderness® Alaska Rail Service
blocks.text: Our exclusive Direct-to-the-Wilderness rail service features glass-domed railcars that take you into the heart of Alaska. Enjoy convenience and comfort as you move easily from ship to train, then directly to your Princess Wilderness Lodge in the Denali area.

blocks.heading: Visit Denali National Park on every Alaska cruisetour
blocks.text: Venture into a land like no other. With some of the most stunning and iconic wildlife and wilderness in the world, Denali National Park is part of the definitive experience of an Alaska adventure. No matter which Alaska cruisetour you choose, Princess takes you into the Great Land’s breathtaking interior.

blocks.heading: Explore the great land on an Alaska cruisetour
blocks.text: Every part of Alaska tells an extraordinary story, whether it's through the beauty of the region's natural masterpieces or the animated personalities of its locals. During an Alaska cruisetour with Princess, you'll discover what makes the Great Land so special and craft tales of your time on land and sea.

blocks.heading: Unforgettable Alaska cruisetour excursions
blocks.text: Don't just visit Alaska — live it with Alaska excursions that expand your cruise experience. Rush across the snow on a dog sled with a professional musher, fly-fish for salmon in breathtaking rivers and soar over miles of glacial tundra in a helicopter. Watch migrating humpback whales from the deck of a catamaran or see Native craftsman carve a traditional totem pole.

blocks.heading: Juneau, Alaska
blocks.text: Juneau is famous not only for gold and government but also for its breathtakingly beautiful glaciers and stunning views of both water and mountains.

blocks.text: Skagway was the gateway to the gold fields for the thousands who flocked to Alaska and the Yukon with the hope of striking it rich. Skagway may have boasted the shortest route to the Klondike, but it wasn't the easiest.

blocks.heading: Onboard train experience
blocks.text: We take our passion for bringing what makes the Great Land special on board, weaving it into your Alaska rail service for a seamless immersion into the North’s vast wilderness.

blocks.heading: Onboard narration
blocks.text: Thanks to knowledgeable Rail guides, enjoy a narrated trip during your ride. Gain unique insights, listen to inspiring stories and see unprecedented beauty. Our passionate guides are happy to answer questions, identify wildlife and help you understand the fascinating history of the Great Land.

blocks.heading: Dining
blocks.text: Pulling from train travel’s luxurious history, Princess prepares cuisine made to order for our guests in every one of our Alaska rail cars. Depending on your route, choose from breakfast, lunch or dinner. If a drink is all you’re after, relax in your seat and enjoy our beverage service. With food always nearby, fill up on delicious fare and the Great Land’s beauty that surrounds you.

blocks.heading: Observation platform
blocks.text: Get even closer to Alaska’s beauty with our open-air observation platforms on select cars. Step outside to feel refreshed and even more immersed in the environment as it passes by you. Enjoy a front-row seat to Alaska’s most breathtaking landscapes along the original route of the Alaska railroad.

Let Princess get you there with travel, airfare & hotels

blocks.heading: A dreamy Alaska lodge where the rivers meet and wilderness begins
blocks.text: Forged between two rivers and sitting on the edge of Wrangell-St. Elias National Park lies Copper River Princess Wilderness Lodge®. Being so close to some of Alaska’s most abundant waterways and the largest national park in the United States, this unique Alaska lodge offers you unprecedented access to the untamed wilderness of the Great Land.

blocks.heading: Amenities
blocks.text: It’s more than just a lodge in Alaska, it’s your home. Enjoy an espresso bar, a local shuttle to the Wrangell-St. Elias National Park visitor’s center and access to the Wrangell Room, with stunning views of Mt. Drum, Wrangell and Blackburn. There’s also a gift shop and guest services desk to provide you with almost anything you might need during your trip. Complimentary Wi-Fi is available property

blocks.heading: Activities
blocks.text: Compete against loved ones during shuffleboard and card/board games. Capture pictures of the local flora and fauna while strolling along the walking trails around the lodge. Or opt for a naturalist-led tour to learn more about the region’s vast landscapes and history.

blocks.heading: Excursions
blocks.text: Step out of your Alaska lodge and into the abandoned mining camp of Kennecott to hear stories of the area’s once-booming copper mines. Tour Prince William Sound by boat to see Columbia Glacier up close, and venture into the untouched lands of Wrangell-St. Elias National Park. Or hop aboard a jet boat, or raft, for a day of wild salmon fishing and the chance to take home one of the most prized fish

blocks.heading: Directory and map
blocks.text: Discover our directory and map, designed to make exploring your lodge easier than ever. These helpful resources provide clear layouts of the lodge, highlighting key amenities, dining locations, guest services, and nearby experiences.

blocks.heading: A unique Alaska lodge in the Golden Heart City
blocks.text: Look for inspiration in the heart of Alaska’s wild interior, filled with the potential for experiences that few people will ever know. Set on the banks of the Chena River, the Fairbanks Princess Riverside Lodge® is your gateway to this land. From savoring reindeer sausage for breakfast to meeting sled dogs in the afternoon, experience local life, with the ease and authenticity only our Alaska lodg

blocks.heading: Amenities
blocks.text: This Alaska lodge provides almost anything you could need to make your stay as pleasant as possible. Taste chef-prepared meals with ingredients sourced from the lodge’s own garden. Or sip on a crisp glass of wine or a hearty beer while relaxing on the large riverview deck that overlooks the Chena River. Complimentary Wi-Fi is available across the property.

blocks.heading: Activities
blocks.text: Head outside of your lodge in Alaska where nature trails abound. Stroll along paths that take you to historic sites, and walk alongside the river for unforgettable views. Or head to the Alaska Salmon Bake in historic Pioneer Park, Fairbanks’ most unique dining experience.

blocks.heading: Excursions
blocks.text: Our Alaska lodge gives you access to the best excursions in the Golden Heart City. Board a sternwheeler and embark on a Riverboat Discovery cruise along the Chena and Tanana rivers. Explore a Chena Indian village and meet a sled dog team – the region’s own local celebrities. Or visit mining camps at Gold Dredge 8 and relive history as you pan for gold alongside experts.

blocks.text: There’s a reason why this unique Alaska lodge was named one of the “Top 12 Resorts in Alaska and the Pacific Northwest” by Conde Nast Traveler readers. The Kenai Princess Wilderness Lodge® offers direct access to Alaska’s playground — also known as the Kenai Peninsula. Sail past glaciers and fish for wild salmon. Then, return to the coziness of your Alaska wilderness lodge after a day full of adve

blocks.heading: Alaska Lodge amenities & activities
blocks.text: Our Alaska wilderness lodges combine the conveniences of home with the unique experiences found only in Alaska. Discover the unique experiences this lodge offers.

blocks.heading: Amenities
blocks.text: With a wood burning stove, vaulted ceiling and a private porch in every guest room, it’s easy to feel at home at our Alaska lodge. Unwind fireside in the Main Lodge, and relish in the Great Land’s beauty on the expansive deck overlooking the Kenai River. Complimentary Wi-Fi is available in the main lodge.

blocks.heading: Activities
blocks.text: You won’t have to travel far from your Alaska wilderness lodge to get a taste of The Great Land. Explore the surrounding land by navigating the Kenai nature trail, a one-mile loop that introduces you to the sights and sounds of Alaska’s playground.

blocks.heading: Excursions
blocks.text: Our Alaska lodges offer excursions that introduce you to life in the Great Land. Observe marine life on a cruise to Kenai Fjords National Park. Sportfish for salmon or trout in the Kenai River. Pan for gold with a real prospector. Explore Historic Seward or hike Exit Glacier. Float the famous Kenai River and be on the lookout for wildlife — all exclusive to our Alaska wilderness lodge.

blocks.heading: Comfort at the foot of Denali, only at our exclusive Alaska lodge
blocks.text: One of our most popular lodges in Alaska, Mt. McKinley Princess Wilderness Lodge®, is only 40 miles from Denali and two hours south of the entrance to Denali National Park. From the Great Room in the main lodge, admire the tallest peak in North America. Or enjoy local cuisine, adventures and activities — all at this remote Alaska lodge offering a true wilderness retreat.

After sharing the construction and design on an episode of Animal Planet’s Treehouse Masters, we are excited to invite guests to delight in the surroundings from the deck, admire the rustic interior and partake in expert-crafted activities.

blocks.heading: Amenities

blocks.heading: Things to do at the Hubbard Glacier
blocks.text: A scenic cruise through Yakutat Bay brings you closer to the raw beauty of Hubbard Glacier, where towering walls of blue ice meet Alaska's rugged wilderness. Watch icebergs drift across the bay, keep an eye out for wildlife and take in breathtaking views of snow-capped peaks as you experience one of Alaska's most spectacular natural landmarks.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Hubbard Glacier
Take in the blue ice
blocks.text: Centuries of pressure have created Hubbard Glacier’s deep, luminous blues. As the light shifts across the ice, you’ll see dazzling shades dance across the towering face — an ever-changing show that feels almost otherworldly. From dramatic calving events to incredible wildlife sightings and panoramic glacier views, every moment at Hubbard Glacier offers a deeper appreciation for Alaska's untamed be

blocks.heading: Hubbard Glacier & Wilderness Exploration
blocks.text: Take a closer look at Hubbard Glacier’s icy expanse and the untouched wilderness of Yakutat Bay in a smaller, Alaska-built boat. Prepare to spot wildlife, watch calving ice tumble into the sea and catch a glimpse of Mount St. Elias — the second tallest peak in the United States. The Hubbard Glacier & Wilderness Exploration is not one to miss.

blocks.heading: Watch the ice fall
blocks.text: Hubbard Glacier is always on the move, and when giant chunks of ice break away, the spectacle is unforgettable. From your ship’s deck, feel the thrill as massive slabs crash into Yakutat Bay, sending waves and mist into the air.

blocks.heading: Spot wildlife
blocks.text: As you sail through Yakutat Bay, keep watch for humpback whales surfacing nearby or harbor seals lounging on drifting ice. Bald eagles often soar overhead, while sea otters bob playfully in the chilly waters.

blocks.heading: Learn from expert narration
blocks.text: While you cruise past Hubbard Glacier, onboard experts share fascinating stories about its formation, movement and future. Their insights bring the dynamic landscape around you to life, turning every sight into a deeper discovery.

blocks.heading: Enjoy panoramic views from the ship
blocks.text: Whether you're bundled up on the open deck or relaxing by a lounge window, breathtaking views of Hubbard Glacier stretch as far as the eye can see. With rugged peaks framing the scene, it’s a perfect moment to simply take it all in.

blocks.heading: Experience Hubbard Glacier on your next Yakutat Bay cruise
blocks.text: Nothing compares to cruising toward Hubbard Glacier, where towering walls of blue ice meet snow-capped peaks and floating icebergs drift across Yakutat Bay. As North America's largest tidewater glacier, Hubbard Glacier is one of Alaska's most spectacular natural landmarks.

blocks.heading: Explore the reaches of this legendary park
Natural History Tour - Primrose Ridge
blocks.text: This narrated tour through Denali National Park spans four and a half hours and takes you to Primrose Ridge at mile 17. Several interpretive stops enhance the experience with an hour of off-bus experience. Beginning with a stop at the Denali Bus Depot, learn about the creation of the Denali Park Road with the film “Across Time and Tundra.” Next, visit the historical Savage Cabin to learn how the c

blocks.heading: Tundra Wilderness Tour
blocks.text: This guided bus excursion through Denali National Park offers visitors the opportunity to experience Alaska's vast wilderness and spectacular mountain scenery. Typically lasting 7 to 8 hours, the tour travels approximately 64 miles into the park along the Denali Park Road, providing one of the best opportunities to view Denali's iconic wildlife. Led by a certified driver-naturalist, visitors learn

blocks.heading: Other park activities
blocks.text: A shuttle service can take you from the Denali Princess Wilderness Lodge® to the main visitor center or the Horseshoe Lake Trailhead – a 3-mile trail full of beautiful pathways and beaver dams. If you choose to explore the visitor center, watch films about the park, check out cultural and historical exhibits of Denali National Park and join hikes lead by knowledgeable park rangers.

blocks.heading: How to book or change your park tour
blocks.text: Park tour availability is limited and is assigned on a first-come, first-served basis. If your Alaska cruisetour does not include a Denali National Park tour, reserve your spot via the Manage Booking, by calling Princess Cruises or contacting your travel advisor. To change the Denali National Park tour on an existing booking, please call Princess® or your travel advisor.

blocks.heading: Helpful tips
blocks.text: Water is provided on all Denali National Park tours. A box lunch can be purchased at the Denali Princess Wilderness Lodge®. We suggest you bring warm clothes, rainwear, insect repellent, binoculars, a camera and personal medication as necessary. Tour buses are school buses. The park road isn't paved after mile 15.

sections: Preparing for your day in Glacier Bay

headings.text: Preparing for your day in Glacier Bay
Here to help you enjoy your Alaska Cruisetour journey
Let Princess get you there with travel, airfare & hotels

blocks.heading: Glacier & wildlife viewing
blocks.text: There’s a reason it’s called Glacier Bay National Park. Home to more than 1,000 glaciers, the park is alive with calving ice that rumbles and echoes across the water. Bask in the beauty of Alaska’s glaciers with Princess®.

blocks.heading: Margerie Glacier
blocks.text: Once a part of the Grand Pacific Glacier, Margerie Glacier claimed independence in the 1990s and has become its own masterpiece. Now this 21-mile landmark is the most famous glacier in the park, with one of the most active glacial faces. Sail past its powder blue walls and revel in its enormity from the comfort of your ship – which turns 360 degrees - while at the glacier, so all guests have an op

blocks.heading: Grand Pacific Glacier
blocks.text: Long ago, the Grand Pacific Glacier once included the likes of Margerie Glacier and Johns Hopkins Glacier. Now the 2-mile-long glacier resides on its own, extending into both Glacier Bay National Park in Alaska and Grand Pacific Pass in Canada. Cloaked in black, it’s easy to mistake this landmark for a rock or land. Keep an eye out for this hidden treasure, and dive deeper into the history of this

blocks.heading: Johns Hopkins Glacier
blocks.text: Named after the prominent Baltimore-based university, Johns Hopkins Glacier is just as prestigious as its academic counterpart. While its 12-mile-long terrain makes it one of the largest in the park, Johns Hopkins Glacier is most famous for being one of the few advancing glaciers that remain. Get a glimpse of the glacier as the ship sails past Johns Hopkins Inlet.

blocks.heading: Wildlife
blocks.text: Meet the many personalities of Glacier Bay National Park as you cruise through the natural habitats of Alaska’s wildlife. See humpback and killer whales break the ocean’s surface, welcoming you into the Great Land. Wave hello to the sea lions basking in the Alaska sun. Watch harbor seals float atop chunks of ice, and rejoice in the playfulness of sea otters as they float across the water on their

blocks.heading: Preparing for your day in Glacier Bay
blocks.text: Make your Alaska cruise vacation even more spectacular with a few considerations before you set sail.

blocks.heading: Meet park rangers
blocks.text: Learn about Glacier Bay National Park from the people who know it best. While sailing through the park’s deep fjords, park rangers join you on board to share history and facts of the region and its wildlife.

blocks.heading: Glacier Bay cruise for kids
blocks.text: Young nature lovers will find plenty to enjoy on a Glacier Bay cruise. Princess Cruises offers fun, age-appropriate activities tailored for kids, including a special Junior Ranger program where they can earn their own badge —available exclusively in Glacier Bay.

blocks.heading: What to wear & climate
blocks.text: With temperatures fluctuating between 30-60 degrees Fahrenheit, dress in layers to make sure you’re comfortable all day. Since it’s usually cooler on the water and near the glaciers, we recommend packing a warm coat, waterproof gear, a hat, gloves and supportive walking shoes. You may also want to bring extra memory cards for your camera so you can reminisce about all your adventures through Glaci

blocks.heading: Glacier Bay experience
blocks.text: Enjoy around 8-hours in Glacier Bay National Park cruising by spectacular scenery with one hour spent at the face of Margerie Glacier. Park rangers will provide commentary from the bridge, hold presentations in the Princess theater and wander the open decks so you may ask them questions. blocks.heading: Experience true adventure with Alaska shore excursions
blocks.text: Feel like a local with our unique land and shore excursions that give you a taste of true Alaska life. From the historical fortunes of the Klondike Gold Rush to the glacial treasures of the Inside Passage, get up close to the Great Land’s famous riches and best kept secrets.

blocks.heading: Denali national park tours
blocks.text: Home to the highest mountain in North America, Denali National Park is brimming with magnificence. Search for the Big Five — grizzly bears, Dall sheep, wolves, caribou and moose — while on a bus tour in the park. Most Princess Alaska cruisetours include a tour into Denali National Park. Learn more

blocks.heading: Wildlife
blocks.text: Alaska is teeming with wildlife. See the Great Land’s most famous animals — like humpback whales — on our Alaska shore excursions. Marvel at bald eagles in their natural habitats while in Ketchikan. See humpbacks play alongside sea lions in Juneau. Or keep a lookout for Denali National Park’s Big Five — including moose, caribou, grizzly bears, wolves and Dall sheep — while on a bus tour in the par

blocks.heading: Culture
blocks.text: The Great Land was built on a strong culture. On our Alaska shore excursions, step back in time to learn how these traditions came to fruition and how they're practiced today. Attend a lumberjack axe-throwing competition, watch a Native dance performance and excite your taste buds at a salmon bake with locals. Or watch a craftsmen thoughtfully carve totem poles at a Native Alaskan village.

blocks.heading: Gold rush history
blocks.text: Strike it rich on any of our cruise excursions in Alaska where you can pan for gold like the many treasure hunters before you. Tour mining camps and meet experienced miners. Visit a restored saloon to craft cocktails from age-old recipes. Or board a gold rush-era train that takes you through Yukon territory and brings you up close to some of Alaska's most historical sites.

blocks.heading: Fishing
blocks.text: With waters as prosperous as the treasures on land, discover what lies below the surface on our Alaska cruise excursions that take you out to sea. Hear thrilling tales from members of the award-winning TV series Deadliest Catch. Or learn to fly fish from an expert guide. As a part of our unique culinary experience, Cook My Catch, bring your fresh-caught fish on board and have our chefs prepare it

blocks.heading: Glaciers
blocks.text: Glaciers are the epitome of Alaska. Sailing past them is a sensory experience that inspires both the mind and heart. Watch as Hubbard Glacier calves into the water and listen for the rumble of “white thunder” that it leaves in its path. Land by helicopter on top of Mendenhall Glacier, and feel its strong roots beneath you. Or navigate its rugged terrain by way of flightseeing or dogsled with our A

blocks.heading: Sightseeing
blocks.text: There’s a world of sights to be seen in the Great Land and our Alaska cruise excursions give you a front-row seat to it all. Bring history books to life when you tour Skagway, the former gateway to the gold rush, and visit Gold Dredge 8 in Fairbanks to learn even more about mining. Travel along the White Pass & Yukon Route Railway, or aboard a riverboat sternwheeler for sweeping views of Alaska’s

blocks.heading: Outdoor adventures
blocks.text: There’s a reason it’s called the Great Land — including its great outdoors. Get up close to renowned glaciers on a flightseeing tour, zipline through Tongass National Forest and hike along the mountainside of Ketchikan’s Deer Mountain Trail which takes you 3,000 feet above sea level. Whether you prefer to traverse by land, sea or air, our cruise excursions in Alaska will bring you on a wild ride.

blocks.heading: Alaska Voyage of the Glaciers cruise itinerary
blocks.text: Sail 500 miles deeper into the Gulf of Alaska and Prince William Sound on our top-rated Voyage of the Glaciers cruise. Spend seven days traveling from Vancouver, B.C. to Anchorage (Whittier), stopping in historic port cities like Ketchikan, Juneau and Skagway. blocks.text: Discover the top reasons to sail on a Voyage of the Glaciers cruise.

blocks.heading: Two incredible glacier viewing experiences
blocks.text: Get up close to not one, but two of Mother Nature’s masterpieces on our Voyage of the Glaciers cruise.

blocks.heading: A visit to Prince William Sound
blocks.text: During your Voyage of the Glaciers cruise, travel 500 miles farther north across the Gulf of Alaska to see Prince William Sound, prized for its abundance of marine and coastal life.

blocks.heading: Three historic ports of call
blocks.text: Unpack once and visit three of Alaska’s best cities — gold-laden Skagway, salmon-rich Ketchikan and the capital city of Juneau.

blocks.heading: Many voyages
blocks.text: With multiple Voyage of the Glaciers sailings on four ships throughout the summer, choose your preferred date and ship.

blocks.heading: Access to Alaska’s interior
blocks.text: Add extra nights to your Voyage of the Glaciers vacation with a cruisetour that takes you to Denali National Park.

blocks.heading: Additional time in Vancouver, B.C.
blocks.text: From Gastown to Grouse Mountain, dive deeper into the ever-evolving city of Vancouver before or after your Voyage of the Glaciers cruise.

blocks.heading: Ships on this itinerary
blocks.text: Our Princess fleet includes ships that range from our smaller vessels to large ships. From a balcony stateroom, marvel at the glaciers passing by before enjoying local seafood in one of our many eateries during your Voyage of the Glaciers cruise.

blocks.heading: Cruise from Japan
blocks.text: Take in all the sights of Tokyo on a cruise to Japan. As the country’s capital city, Tokyo is Japan’s leading center of business and finance yet also boasts deep roots in history. blocks.heading: Cruise from Singapore
blocks.text: Relish the convenience of sailing roundtrip from one of the world’s great cities, where the primary language is English. Singapore’s mixed culture is a mesmerizing mix of Buddhist temples, British-inspired Victorian buildings, Arab souks and ultra-modern skyscrapers, and is easily accessible via Changi Airport, a well-connected airhub. Find cruises

blocks.heading: Cruise to Hong Kong
blocks.text: Take in the spectacle of one of the world’s great travel destinations at dusk from the seat of a vintage double-decker tram. Journey to Tai O, “Hong Kong’s Little Venice,” for a look at a fishing village built atop stilts. blocks.heading: Cruise from Australia & New Zealand

From Aboriginal Dreamtime stories in Australia to New Zealand’s elaborate Māori tattoos, expansive cityscapes and breathtaking landscapes, each port possesses its own unique culture, lifestyle, excitement and charm. blocks.heading: Art of effortless cruising
blocks.text: Japan is a country of bullet trains and mountain shrines, of midnight ramen and thousand-year rituals—and with Princess, you get to thread through it all without the usual travel chaos. No train apps. No hotel check-ins. Just a smooth glide from Hiroshima to Kyoto to Nagasaki, where every port brings a new version of Japan into focus (without packing, train schedules or language barriers). Onboard

blocks.heading: Check the Japan must-sees off your list
blocks.text: You can experience it all when you travel by sea, land, and rail with Princess

blocks.heading: Traditions that create a timeless experience
blocks.text: Japan’s cultural heritage shines through daily life—from the elegance of a tea ceremony to the energy of festival season. With Princess, you’ll witness these traditions up close. It’s not just about observing traditions—it’s about experiencing them in the places where they were born.

blocks.heading: Where history comes alive
blocks.text: Japan’s history is a living epic—from the ancient Jomon period to the rise of the samurai and the transformative Meiji Restoration. Walk in the footsteps of emperors and warriors as you explore majestic castles, sacred temples, and storied cities. Onboard, curated lectures and cultural programming offer deeper insight into Japan’s fascinating past—bringing history to life both on land and at sea,

blocks.heading: Taste the authenticity
blocks.text: Japanese cuisine is a journey—rooted in tradition, shaped by the seasons, and crafted with precision. From the elegance of sushi and sashimi to the comfort of ramen, tempura, and regional specialties, each dish reveals a new layer of culinary heritage. Whether you're sampling fresh seafood ashore or savoring expertly prepared dishes onboard, food in Japan is more than nourishment—it’s an experienc

blocks.heading: Now booking 2027-2028 voyages
blocks.text: Our biggest Japan season yet is available in 2027 with two ships, 50 unique itineraries and 45 destinations across six countries.

blocks.heading: A cruise for every season
blocks.text: Each season reveals a different face of Japan, with unique cultural experiences, seasonal cuisines, and natural wonders. Whatever time you choose to visit, Princess itineraries are thoughtfully designed to showcase the authentic seasonal traditions that make Japan endlessly fascinating.

blocks.heading: Spring
blocks.text: Witness the magical blossom season, creating an unforgettable, picturesque experience.

blocks.heading: Summer
blocks.text: Experience vibrant festivals, spectacular fireworks displays, and lush mountain landscapes.

blocks.heading: Fall
blocks.text: Marvel at a stunning display of autumn foliage, known as koyo, transforming landscapes into vibrant tapestries of red, orange, and gold.

blocks.heading: Winter
blocks.text: Cruise at the end of winter to cap off a full year of changing seasons enjoying hot springs and cultural festivals.

blocks.heading: Explore the unforgettable ports of Japan
blocks.text: Princess Cruises offers unparalleled access to Japan's ports, sailing to over 38 destinations. With a longer season, and more departure dates than any other cruise line, you’ll have even more opportunities to explore these remarkable destinations—all without the hassle of planning each stop yourself.

blocks.heading: Kobe
blocks.text: From imposing feudal-era fortifications to modern street-side food stands, the region around Kobe is rich with sights and stories that stretch across ages. Ancient temples nestle between gleaming skyscrapers, while traditional sake breweries share neighborhoods with cutting-edge research facilities, creating a tapestry where every corner reveals another layer of Japan's evolution. View port

blocks.heading: Tokyo
blocks.text: Begin your pacific adventure in the place where tradition meets technology. See neon skyscrapers cradling ancient temples as you explore Tokyo’s vibrant streets, where every corner reveals something extraordinary — from the serenity of the Imperial Palace Garden to the energy of the Shibuya district. View Port

blocks.heading: Kumano
blocks.text: Kumano is understatement turned unforgettable, inviting curiosity and contemplation in equal measure. Whether you're drawn to ancient pilgrimage trails or peaceful coastal retreats, this port destination is a tapestry of spiritual depth and raw natural energy. View port

blocks.heading: Okinawa
blocks.text: Every Okinawa cruise is full of surprises, with ancient castles, tranquil gardens, colorful markets and hidden beaches seemingly popping up out of nowhere. The island’s mix of history, nature and culture makes it easy to fill your day with once-in-a-lifetime adventure — or just find a perfect spot to slow things down and take it all in. View port

blocks.heading: Kochi
blocks.text: This is a port for travelers who like their history with a view and their sightseeing with a little of everything. A Kochi cruise can take you up a castle keep, into a limestone cave or straight to the beach, all with plenty of time to enjoy some local cuisine or make trades at an open-air market before your ship departs. View port

blocks.heading: Osaka
blocks.text: Whether you're drawn to the hushed halls of centuries-old temples or the pulsing life of busy marketplaces, this destination delivers. Osaka and Kyoto offer elegance, energy and endless exploration — with a little something for every type of traveler. When visiting the Osaka cruise port, don’t miss out on these must-experience activities. View port

blocks.heading: Japan cruise spotlight: A day in Kyoto
blocks.text: Imagine the perfect day in port, taking in the sights and an excursion or two.

blocks.heading: 9:30 p.m. Indulge in a nightcap
blocks.text: Sip on inspired local cocktails, sake and spirits, before a restful night sleep in your Princess Luxury Bed.

blocks.heading: 8:00 a.m. Wake up as your ship docks in port
blocks.text: Order coffee and breakfast to your room with OceanNow® delivery and take your first look at the city of Osaka, as Diamond Princess® sails into port.

blocks.heading: 9:30 a.m. Enjoy a scenic drive to Kyoto
blocks.text: Watch Osaka's urban sprawl give way to scenic countryside as you journey toward Nijo Castle, passing landmarks like Toji Temple and Kyoto Tower along the way.

blocks.heading: 11:15 a.m. Arrive at Nijo Castle
blocks.text: Step into the shogun’s world at this 17th-century stronghold, known for its “nightingale floors” that chirp underfoot. Then travel further back to the Golden Pavilion, a 14th-century temple wrapped in gold leaf and serene beauty.

blocks.heading: 1:00 p.m. A moment to savor
blocks.text: Relax over lunch at a local hotel, then set out to discover more of Kyoto’s iconic sights.

blocks.heading: 2:30 p.m. Step into history at the Heian Shrine
blocks.text: Visit the Heian Shrine, built in 1895 to honor the 1,100th anniversary of Kyoto’s founding. This vibrant landmark blends traditional architecture with a tranquil garden setting.

blocks.heading: 3:30 p.m. Shop for souvenirs at the Kyoto Handicraft Center
blocks.text: Cap off your adventure with a stop at the Kyoto Handicraft Center, where locally made souvenirs offer the perfect reminder of your journey.

blocks.heading: 6:00 p.m. Return to a traditional Onsen bath experience
blocks.text: Relax in Izumi, an onsen bath, at the Lotus Spa while reflecting on your day in Kyoto.

blocks.heading: 8:00 p.m. Dine at Makoto
blocks.text: Experience edoma-style sushi at Makoto Ocean starting October 2025.

blocks.heading: Excursions for every interest
blocks.text: From sumo matches to cherry blossom festivals, steaming bowls of ramen to Zen gardens—Japan is full of memorable moments waiting to happen. To make these experiences even more accessible, select excursions are also offered in both Japanese and English.

blocks.heading: Miyajima & Itsukushima Shrine
blocks.text: Travel to sacred Miyajima Island and visit Itsukushima Shrine on this half-day excursion. Designated a World Heritage Site, a National Treasure and an Important Cultural Property, the Itsukushima Shrine attracts thousands of visitors a year. The shrine's unique architecture called Shinden, is typical of the noble houses in the late Heian Period.

blocks.heading: Kakunodate Samurai Town
blocks.text: Feel the centuries unfold as you stroll through the wide streets and large courtyards of the Kakunodate Samurai District, once the home of 80 samurai and their families. Established in 1620, Kakunodate is acclaimed as one of the best examples of samurai architecture and housing in the country.

blocks.heading: Hirosaki Castle Park, Neputa Festival Floats & Garden
blocks.text: The excitement of the ancient city of Hirosaki comes alive on this full-day adventure that begins with a scenic 90-minute drive to Hirosaki Castle Park. Constructed in 1611, the original structure was struck by lightning in 1627 and burned to the ground. Although rebuilt in 1810, the castle still retains an aura of its ancient past. This historical treasure sits tucked away in the lush and peacefu

blocks.heading: Ja-Gal-Ch'i Market & Beomeosa Temple
blocks.text: This fascinating half day excursion starts with a warm welcome from your local guide, before an enjoyable drive through the city's northern suburbs. Journey through magnificent countryside to the Beomeosa Temple, one of South Korea's largest temples, which dates back to 678 A.D.

blocks.heading: Why a Princess cruise is the best choice to see Japan
blocks.text: A Princess cruise offers a convenient and deeply immersive way to experience Japan. Backed by over a decade of experience sailing these waters, we’ve crafted journeys that let you unpack just once and explore a world of cultural richness —through authentic onboard experiences, regionally inspired dining, and a wide range of shore excursions that bring each destination to life. It’s a seamless way

blocks.heading: Diverse and thoughtfully curated itineraries
blocks.text: With 38 spectacular ports of call and cruises ranging from 7-day escapes to 28-day explorations, Princess offers a wide range of Japan cruises designed to suit every traveler. Each itinerary visits multiple ports across the country—revealing the rich diversity of Japan’s regions, from bustling cities to serene coastal towns. Timed to coincide with iconic seasonal moments like cherry blossom season

blocks.heading: Specialized dining experiences
blocks.text: In addition to your favorite Princess classics, guests can enjoy a variety of authentic Japanese dining experiences throughout their journey. Savor expertly crafted edoma-style sushi at Makoto Ocean by sushi master Makoto Okuwa who brings his over 25 years of experience to the high seas. Enjoy the lively flair or Teppanyaki, or explore regional specialties featured in our “Princess Japan Favorites

blocks.heading: Personalized attentive service
blocks.text: Our expert crew provides friendly service, allowing you to relax. Powered by Medallion technology, enjoy a personalized and streamlined experience with expedited boarding, touchless payments, and easy navigation for effortless cruising.

blocks.heading: Convenience and value
blocks.text: Cruising with Princess to Japan offers the significant advantage of unpacking only once while visiting multiple destinations. Meals, entertainment, and accommodation are largely covered in the cruise fare, and inclusive packages like Princess Plus® and Princess Premier® can further enhance the value by adding amenities like Wi-Fi, premium beverages, and gratuities.

pages.metaDescription: Located just off the coast of China, the city of Taipei is an incredibly rich and diverse hub to explore on an Asian cruise vacation.

blocks.heading: Chiang Kai-Shek Memorial Hall
blocks.text: Located in the heart of Taipei in the world famous Liberty Square, Chiang Kai-Shek Memorial Hall is one of the city's defining structures. The impressive monument was completed in 1976 and stands in tribute to the late President Chiang Kai-Shek, a beloved national figure in the Republic of China. The memorial hall features a beautiful blue tile roof with a gleaming gold apex and fascinating artifa

blocks.heading: National Palace Museum
blocks.text: If you're looking to gain a first-hand look at Taiwan and China's rich and interlocking cultures, be sure to visit the National Palace Museum. The Republic of China's national museum features one of the world's largest and most impressive collection of ancient Chinese art, textiles, sculptures, artifacts and texts. Many of the exhibits within the museum date back more than 8,000 years, including a

blocks.heading: Taipei101
blocks.text: Holding the title of the world's second tallest skyscraper - behind Dubai's Burj Khalifa - Taipei 101 is sure to impress visitors with its characteristically bold postmodern design, which seamlessly blends high-tech appeal with traditional Taiwanese elements. The structure gets its name from the 101 floors standing above ground. Additionally, there are five subterranean levels to explore along wit

blocks.heading: Yang Ming Shan National Park
blocks.text: You can head outside of the city for a bit and visit the enjoyable Yang Ming Shan National Park for a taste of Taiwan's incredible natural beauty. The park is characterized by a postcard-perfect volcanic landscape that is situated next to Shamao Mountain and Qixing Mountain. Additionally, an enormous 22 foot diameter clock sits at the center of the park that is made entirely out of flowers. Water

blocks.heading: Yehliu Geographic Park
blocks.text: The Yehliu Geographic Park is located nearby, which is known for containing some of Taiwan's most incredible and otherworldly rock formations. The park is situated on the Yehliu Cape, and the rushing sea waters are responsible for many of the smooth and unusually shaped rocks dotting the area.

blocks.heading: Confucius Temple
blocks.text: Constructed by during the Ming dynasty in 1665, the Confucius Temple in Taipei is one of the many Confucian temples located on the island. The temple contains both a shrine and a school, making it a unique center of spiritual education in Taiwan.
