blocks.heading: Things to do in Alotau
blocks.text: Alotau feels both peaceful and storied, with volcanic shorelines, rainforest hills and a history shaped by one of WWII’s most pivotal battles. It’s a place where everyday life unfolds slowly, giving visitors room to explore culture, nature and the bay’s striking scenery.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Alotau
blocks.text: Alotau’s excursions offer a close look at Milne Bay’s culture, food and landscapes, from rainforest villages to volcanic coastlines. These experiences help you see how local traditions and everyday life all blend together in this quiet corner of Papua New Guinea.

blocks.heading: Remote Tawali Resort Snorkel and Skull Cave
blocks.text: Travel to secluded Tawali Resort for a day that blends culture and marine exploration. Start with a guided Skull Cave walk to view ancestral remains linked to Milne Bay’s long and complex history. After meeting local villagers, return to Tawali for lunch and two snorkel sessions along the resort’s house reef, home to epaulet sharks, ghost pipefish and vibrant coral. Free time at the pool or waterf

blocks.heading: Milne Bay Village Life
blocks.text: Immerse yourself in daily life across Milne Bay as your guide leads you through rural markets, small communities and traditional meeting places. In Bibiko Village, you’ll see how long-standing customs balance with newer influences, then watch clay pot dishes prepared over open fires. The tour ends at the Milne Bay War Memorial where you’ll hear stories from the Battle of Milne Bay, one of WWII’s m

blocks.heading: Clay Pot Cooking Class
blocks.text: Spend the day at Masurina Lodge learning the region’s signature clay pot cooking technique with help from a local chef. You’ll prepare a traditional meal using fresh ingredients, explore a small WWII exhibit tied to the Battle of Milne Bay and enjoy your finished dishes in the lodge’s dining room. After lunch, relax at the bar or cool off with a swim before returning to the pier. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Alotau

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Bangkok
blocks.text: Ready to mix temple hush with tuk‑tuk rush? These excursions blend tradition, energy and just enough “holy‑wow” for your Thailand stop.

blocks.heading: Pattaya Poolside Retreat
blocks.text: Take a seaside escape to a four‑star resort near Pattaya, where lounge chairs and buffet lunches await after a short drive and a breakfast beach walk. Optional strolls down Walking Street bring nightlife for the bold. If serenity’s your thing, the beachside pool and garden paths offer blissfully quiet alternatives. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Bangkok
blocks.text: Start with the golden Buddha at Wat Trimitr, then stroll through the Grand Palace and marvel at Wat Phra Kaeo (Emerald Buddha). Finish your day with a slow cruise on the Chao Phraya River and lunch at a local restaurant. You’ll also get free time for shopping, people‑watching or diving headfirst into Bangkok’s colorful chaos. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ayutthaya
blocks.text: Step into the former Siamese capital for ruins, royal pavilions and the haunting figure of a Buddha head entwined in tree roots (he’s fine). Lunch and photo stops round out the experience. You’ll also visit the dreamy Bang Pa‑In Summer Palace, complete with its lakeside pavilion and perfectly trimmed palace gardens. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Sanctuary of Truth
blocks.text: Visit the towering wood‑carved Sanctuary of Truth, still under construction and built entirely from teak with mythic carvings galore. Then cruise through Pattaya’s shopping scene for a mix of culture and commerce. Your guide explains the symbolism as you walk among statues of gods, demons and cosmic turtles mid‑carve. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Thai Cooking Class in Pattaya
blocks.text: Drive to Pattaya for a market tour of herbs and spices, then don your apron to cook a Thai lunch you made yourself — certificate included. Afterward wander local shops and soak in seaside vibes. Between bites and spice lessons, you’ll stroll through a lush herb garden picking ingredients straight from the source. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Wat Po & Time on Your Own in Bangkok
blocks.text: Tour Wat Po with its thousand Buddha images and enormous Reclining Buddha; afterward you’re released into the city with a drop‑off at a convenient central hotel near river cruises, shops and eateries. You set the pace — explore at your own speed, with time to browse, snack and dive deep (or just drift). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Cam Ranh
Shore excursions to explore in Cam Ranh
blocks.text: Cam Ranh excursions invite you beyond the coastline and into the heart of central Vietnam. Discover ancient temple towers, riverside villages, bustling markets and traditional craft centers.

blocks.heading: City Drive, Dam Market & Craft Village Workshop
blocks.text: Take a relaxed coach tour through downtown Nha Trang featuring colonial architecture, the cathedral and city hall. Browse the vibrant Dam Market for souvenirs and street snacks, then visit a nearby craft‑village workshop to see artisans weave mats and carve wood, an elegant mix of city sights and cultural depth. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ponagar Cham Tower, Long Son Pagoda & Truong Son Craft Village
blocks.text: Explore contrasts of Culture and Craft on this full‑day tour. Begin at the historic Ponagar Cham Tower complex, once home to the Champa dynasty. Continue to the tranquil Long Son Pagoda before visiting Truong Son Craft Village, where artisans demonstrate mat‑weaving, wood carving and other traditional techniques. The tour ends with refreshments and a light buffet lunch. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Countryside Drive, Rural Village & Farmers' Market
blocks.text: Head into Cam Ranh’s green‑belt countryside on a scenic drive along the Cai River to a working fishing village. Wander through the bustling farmers’ market filled with fresh produce and local goods, then meet village residents and learn firsthand about daily life in rural Vietnam. This immersive excursion brings the region’s traditions into clear view. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Nha Trang by Pedicab
blocks.text: Experience Nha Trang city in a timeless way aboard a pedicab. Glide past colonial‑era buildings, the beachfront boulevard and a lively fishing village at Tran Phu Bridge. Pause for a photo at Hon Chong Promontory, then visit the Dam Market to browse local handicrafts and flavors before returning to your ship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Biking through Nha Trang Countryside
blocks.text: Trade your shoes for pedals and explore Cam Ranh’s scenic backroads and lush fields. This active half‑day ride leads through quiet villages, past rice paddies and riverside lanes. Along the way, learn about the intricacies of Vietnam's local agriculture, sample tropical fruit and enjoy countryside vistas seldom seen by cruise guests. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cham Tower, River Cruise & Rural Village
blocks.text: Begin at the ancient Cham tower complex overlooking the bay, then board a riverboat for a peaceful cruise past floating homes on the Cai River. Disembark at a rural village where you’ll meet craftsmen, see traditional weaving in action and gain appreciation for Vietnam’s coastal heritage, all in one enriching journey. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Chan May
Shore excursions to explore in Chan May
blocks.text: From imperial cities to lantern-lit streets, excursions from Chan May connect you to central Vietnam’s rich heritage. Explore the ancient capital of Hue, the charming riverside town of Hoi An, and dynamic Da Nang on immersive Vietnam adventures.

blocks.heading: Da Nang On Your Own
blocks.text: Arrive by coach in Da Nang and enjoy guided drop‑off in the city center with free time to discover at your own pace. Walk the beach promenade, browse local shops or sip coffee at a riverside café before returning to ship. Experience Vietnam’s coastal gateway without the pressures of an itinerary. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Da Nang
blocks.text: Drive from Chân Mây to Da Nang and explore the city’s vibrant Han Market for local flavors and crafts. Visit Marble Mountains to view limestone caves and hillside pagodas, then pause at Mỹ Khê Beach for sea breezes and coastal views. This full‑day excursion combines city energy with scenic landscapes in central Vietnam. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hue: Imperial Citadel & Tu Duc Royal Tomb
blocks.text: Travel by motorcoach to the UNESCO‑recognized Imperial Citadel, once home to Vietnam’s royal family, then visit the pine‑forested Tu Duc Tomb, the largest private mausoleum built for a Nguyen emperor. Finish at Thien Mu Pagoda, an elegant lakeside sanctuary founded in 1601, then pause for lunch and a stop at a local craft village. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Da Nang & Hoi An
blocks.text: Head to Macau‑style Da Nang with its waterfront Dragon Bridge and waterfront promenade, then continue to Ho I An, the ancient trading port of lantern‑lit streets and tailor shops. Marvel at Japanese Covered Bridge and vibrant riverside cafés before returning to the ship after your day exploring historic Vietnam. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hoi An By Bike & On Foot
blocks.text: Cycle through the countryside into Ho I An’s UNESCO‑listed old town, then swap your wheels for a walking tour among tailor shops, riverfront lanterns and centuries‑old architecture. Pause at a market for snacks and free time to explore charming lanes where history and modern life converge. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Hue with Perfume River Cruise
blocks.text: Explore Huế’s rich history with a visit to the royal tombs and the Imperial Citadel, then board a traditional boat for a gentle cruise on the Perfume River. Admire riverside landscapes, floating temples and historic landmarks while your guide shares stories of Vietnam’s royal past in serene surroundings. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Halong Bay
blocks.text: Your stop at Cai Lan delivers two major flavors — the towering karst islands of Hạ Long Bay (a UNESCO World Heritage Site) and the vibrant streets of Hanoi. You can kayak through emerald waters, explore ancient temples and roam Hanoi’s Old Quarter where history and hip cafés collide. It’s as wild as nature gets and as cultured as city life allows.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Halong Bay
blocks.text: Dial up your explorer game with these curated tours. Each one is a mix of adventure, icon‑moments and the kind of stories you’ll tell back home.

blocks.heading: Water Puppet Show in Ha Long Bay
blocks.text: A puppet show?! Yes, but not just any puppet show. Take your seat by the water’s edge and let wooden figures dance across hidden platforms while live folk music keeps pulse and rhythm high. Vietnam’s northern water puppet tradition blends agrarian legends, puppeteer skill and splashy theatrics into one memorable evening. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: A Journey to Hanoi
blocks.text: A scenic drive takes you from the port to the heart of Hanoi where colonial boulevards, temple spires and street‑side cafés converge. You’ll visit the Temple of Literature built in 1070, step inside Ho Chi Minh’s stilted garden house, then wander the Old Quarter’s alleys, mingle with craft‑vendors and maybe sip a local ‘bai hoi’ beer before the ride back (it’s OK; you’re not the one behind the whe

blocks.heading: Halong Bay Junk Cruise
blocks.text: Board a traditional junk and glide among limestone karsts rising from jade waters in the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Halong Bay. Choose to explore grottoes like Sung Sot, drift through quiet coves and watch the sunset while the bay transforms into an other‑world of stone silhouettes and calm seas. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Halong Bay Kayaking
blocks.text: After a junk cruise (we’re not ripping on the cruise; the boat’s called a ‘junk’) among hundreds of karsts, launch into a two‑person kayak in the Luon‑Cave area and paddle between emerald walls and water shadows. Later, enjoy a seafood lunch aboard the junk, visit a floating village and let the bay’s quiet depths show you why this place stirs something inside. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Halong Bay Deluxe Cruise
blocks.text: Sail in comfort aboard a luxury junk through Halong Bay’s dramatic limestone islands and hidden beaches, greeted by rain‑forest canyons and rock arches. On board you’ll enjoy Vietnamese cuisine while a conservation expert explains the geological wonders beneath your bow. Then relax and let those cliffs etch into your memory. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hai Phong Local Village Visit
blocks.text: Venture inland from the port to Dong Minh Village, known for its wood‑carving artisans and village life still rooted in tradition. Watch master carvers at work, explore between temple shrines, sample local tea and snacks and return to the ship with new respect for culture that lives quietly outside the headline sights. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Cai Lan port (Halong Bay)
blocks.text: Docking at Cai Lan gives you a quieter entry point into Northern Vietnam’s wow‑factor — away from the mega‑crowds but right in range of the action. Transfers from Hanoi or direct local tours mean you can hit the karsts, caves, floating villages and city temples all in one go. Whether you choose the bay or the city, your Asia cruise itinerary just checked a major box.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Ho Chi Minh City
blocks.text: A cruise to Ho Chi Minh City invites you to explore one of Southeast Asia’s most captivating cultural hubs. Docking at Phu My, you’ll journey through the countryside to Vietnam’s largest city, where tradition and transformation meet in unforgettable ways.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Ho Chi Minh City
blocks.text: Explore the vibrant heart of southern Vietnam with excursions that highlight the city's historic landmarks, French colonial charm, and rural river life. Wander through ancient temples, bustling markets and picturesque countryside as you immerse yourself in Viatmamese culture.

blocks.heading: Grand Overland: Cambodia's Angkor Wat & Vietnam's Ho Chi Minh City - double accommodations
blocks.text: Head to the seaside town of Vung Tau to visit the Lang Ca Ong Whale Temple, a sacred spot where fishermen honor whale spirits. Enjoy a warm welcome inside a local home, then take in panoramic coastal views. This excursion combines culture and coastal charm just outside the bustle of Ho Chi Minh City. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Ho Chi Minh City
blocks.text: Begin your day with a scenic drive along the Saigon River to the heart of Ho Chi Minh City, where you’ll explore the historic Reunification Hall and the French‑colonial Post Office. Glide past the Botanical and Zoological Gardens, stop for photo opportunities at Notre Dame Cathedral and then enjoy a buffet lunch before shopping for handcrafted lacquerware at a local factory. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: History museum, lacquer factory & Dong Khoi Street
blocks.text: Discover Vietnam’s past at the National History Museum, then visit a local factory to see skilled lacquer artisans at work. Finish your tour with a stroll along Dong Khoi Street, home to elegant boutiques, cafés and colonial architecture, for a relaxed and memorable end to your day. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Saigon—war relics and shopping
blocks.text: Trace Vietnam’s recent past at the War Remnants Museum, home to powerful exhibits that reflect the country’s wartime history. Then shift gears with a visit to bustling Bến Thành Market, where you’ll browse everything from handmade crafts to flavorful street snacks. G a moving and multi-sensory day in the heart of Ho Chi Minh City. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Vung Tau, Lang Ca Ong Whale Temple & home visit
blocks.text: Drive to the coastal city of Vũng Tàu and visit the revered whale‑temple where fishermen honor the sea’s guardian spirits. Wander through a local home to gain insight into Thai Nguyen life, and then pause at panoramic vantage points along the peninsula before returning to Phú Mỹ with fresh memories of Vietnam’s shoreline heritage. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Market visit & cooking class
blocks.text: Begin with a stroll through a bustling Vietnamese market to select fresh herbs and spices, then head into a hands‑on cooking class where you prepare traditional dishes under local guidance. After lunch featuring your own creations, enjoy free time to explore the city’s flavors and markets on your own. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Ho Chi Minh City
blocks.text: No matter if you’re sailing through Southeast Asia or embarking on a longer journey across the region, cruises to Ho Chi Minh City from Phú Mỹ add a powerful mix of cultural depth and modern vibrance. Visit as part of a Japan, Thailand or Malaysia voyage, or build a grander adventure across Asia’s most iconic ports with Princess.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Hong Kong
Shore excursions to explore in Hong Kong
blocks.text: Explore historic neighborhoods, temples, sweeping skylines and bustling harbors on once-in-a-lifetime shore excursions. Dive deep into the vibrant culture of Hong Kong in for an unforgettable experience.

blocks.heading: Best of Macau
blocks.text: Cruise by catamaran to Macau and explore its rich Portuguese-Chinese heritage. Discover the ruins of St. Paul Cathedral, visit the Museum of Macau and admire ancient traditions at A Ma Temple. Enjoy panoramic views from the Macau Tower’s 60th floor, where you’ll also savor a buffet lunch at the revolving restaurant. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Highlights of Hong Kong
blocks.text: Begin with a stroll through downtown streets and heritage districts, then ride aboard the vintage double‑decker tram for authentic local character. The tour offers passengers a firsthand look at Hong Kong’s vibrant neighborhoods while capturing the contrast between colonial‑era architecture and gleaming modern cityscapes. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Lantau Island & Po Lin Monastery
blocks.text: Venture to Po Lin Monastery on Lantau Island, home to Hong Kong’s famed giant outdoor Buddha statue, for a serene escape from the urban buzz. The journey includes transport to the island, time in the peaceful monastery grounds and sweeping views over Lantau’s verdant hillsides and coastline. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hong Kong by Night
blocks.text: See the city glow at dusk during this evening outing featuring a harbor cruise through Victoria Harbour, a visit to the lively Temple Street Night Market and an eight‑course Beijing duck dinner. Experience city lights, lively streets and an introduction to Hong Kong’s nighttime culture. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Walking tour of Old and New Hong Kong
blocks.text: Stroll through the city’s historic and contemporary districts. Visit venerable sites such as the 1847 Man Mo Temple, which pays tribute to the god of literature, then navigate bustling streets that showcase Hong Kong’s evolving identity. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Highlights of Lantau Island
blocks.text: Explore Lantau’s natural beauty and cultural landmarks, including seaside villages, verdant hills and traditional island life. This excursion combines nature and coastal scenery to give you a broader sense of Hong Kong beyond the city skyline. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Hualien
blocks.text: Wedged between the Pacific and a marble mountain range, this seaside city is a mash‑up of temple bells, hot‑spring steam and wild coastal excitement. You’ll find calm streets, bright markets and one of Asia’s most jaw‑dropping natural attractions: Taroko Gorge (no, we’re not going to try to describe it; just go see for yourself).

blocks.heading: Take in the beauty and culture of Hualien
blocks.text: When you visit Hualien, you get to roam free — through marble-carved Taroko Gorge, past waterfall-shrouded shrines and across cliffs that dive straight into the sea. Explore temples that echo Japan and shout Taoism, soak in hilltop hot springs or dig into Hualien’s indigenous roots through food, music and art. It’s a choose-your-own-adventure town, perfect for soul-staring, snack-chasing and mild

blocks.heading: Guided in Japanese
blocks.text: Join your guide and enjoy the magnificent scenery of Taroko Gorge, a vast canyon carved out of marble by erosion. First, you'll stop at Changchun Shrine, a memorial to the workers who died during the construction of the Central Cross-Island Highway. Locals honor the deceased by lighting cigarettes instead of incense. Enjoy a short walk at Swallow Grotto, where you can take photos of swallows' nest

blocks.heading: Best of Hualien & Taroko Gorge National Park
blocks.text: This full-day deep dive hits all the hits — Taroko Gorge’s marble folds, Swallow’s Grotto and Eternal Spring Shrine. You’ll cross Marble Bridge, gaze over Qingshui Cliff, eat a local lunch that will stay in your memory long after you leave and finish with two iconic stops: Kang-Ten Temple’s riot of color and the Pine Garden’s spy-era serenity. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Highlights of Hualien
blocks.text: A half-day sampling of Hualien’s top layers: start with panoramic views and WWII secrets at Pine Garden, then switch gears with temple visits that show both Taoist flair and Japanese grace. Explore the vivid sculpture of Kang-Ten and the Zen garden vibes at Keishuin. Wrap with free time at A-Zone Cultural Center for a little shopping, culture or just well-lit loitering. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Taroko Gorge Highlights
blocks.text: Half-day, all thrill. Walk Taroko Gorge’s tunnels and cliffside paths, where geology flexes in full marble glory. Stop at Eternal Spring Shrine, peer into Swallow’s Grotto’s dramatic swallow holes and catch the ‘Indian Head’ rock (you’ve got to squint just right). The Tunnels of Nine Turns lead to next-level views, then it’s off to the Qingshui Cliff for an ocean-meets-sky finale. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Jeju
blocks.text: Jeju’s shore excursions offer the perfect blend of adventure, culture and natural beauty. Visitors can immerse themselves in breathtaking landscapes, local traditions and unforgettable coastal experiences that capture the island’s unique charm.

blocks.heading: Mt. Halla Trekking
blocks.text: Embark on a scenic trek up Korea’s tallest peak, where the lush forest floor gives way to rocky slopes and panoramic vistas that stretch across the island. As you climb, expect moments of calm reflection beside alpine lakes and glacial wetlands before reaching the grand summit, where you’re rewarded with sweeping views that make every step worthwhile. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Southern Jeju
blocks.text: Lose yourself in a day of wonder as you explore lush coastal vistas, dramatic volcanic cliffs and the vibrant pulse of local culture on this unforgettable journey to the southern edge of the island. From sweeping ocean views and ancient lava-formed landscapes to lively open markets brimming with fresh-from-the-sea treats, this excursion brings the very best of the region’s wild beauty and warm hos

blocks.heading: Seogwipo City Highlights
blocks.text: Step into a world of rugged seaside cliffs, lush greenery and gently flowing waterfalls on this coastal adventure. Wander through charming village lanes, soak in ocean vistas framed by volcanic stone and savour the island’s unique atmosphere — all in one beautifully crafted port day you’ll remember long after the ship sails. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Native Faces of Jeju
blocks.text: Discover the heart of Jeju through its stunning scenery and rich traditions. Meet the island’s famous sea-diving women, explore charming villages and markets and enjoy breathtaking coastal views. This immersive experience offers a true glimpse into the beauty, culture and spirit that make Jeju so unforgettable. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hallim Park & O’Sullock Tea Museum
blocks.text: Step into a lush world where volcanic landscapes and ancient traditions merge into one unforgettable outing. You’ll wander through a serene garden filled with bonsai pines, lava-formed caves and thatched-roof homes, then follow it with a visit to a hillside tea museum where vibrant green fields stretch to the horizon and you can enjoy rich, locally harvested matcha in a tranquil setting. LEARN MOR

blocks.text: Enjoy a peaceful escape surrounded by vibrant gardens and stunning island views. Stroll through lush indoor and outdoor landscapes, discover a tranquil temple and take in the beauty of Jeju’s nature — a relaxing and inspiring experience you won’t forget. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Kaohsiung
blocks.text: You’re docking at the energetic southern tip of Taiwan — where towering temples rub shoulders with modern solar‑powered stadiums, and every corner feels like a story in motion. Kaohsiung mixes ancient shrines, bold architecture and seaside culture in a way that just makes sense. Want island vibes with metropolitan muscle? Yep, you found it.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Kaohsiung
blocks.text: Ready to dig deeper on those Kaohsiung cruises? Here Princess® delivers hand‑picked adventures that bring history, culture and maybe even some astonishment to your day.

blocks.heading: The Buddhist Monastery at Fokuangshan
blocks.text: Feel the hush of Fo Guang Shan on a half‑day pilgrimage through peaceful countryside. Greet giant Buddha statues and the 20‑foot White‑Robed Guanyin framed by 10,000 sacred images, then explore the Cultural Museum’s jade, bronze and wood treasures. The architecture, ritual rhythm and museum artifacts combine into a quietly powerful, contemplative experience. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Kaohsiung & Tainan
blocks.text: Start at Chikan Towers, built over Dutch Fort Provintia, then slip into Tainan’s historic lanes where colonial architecture and street‑food glory mingle. Wander Lotus Lake’s ornate pagodas and pavilions, soak in the visual feast, then finish with a skyline mic‑drop at the shell‑inspired Great Harbor Bridge — a perfectly photogenic punctuation before you head back to the ship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: City Drive & Fokuangshan Monastery
blocks.text: Board your coach for a scenic hour to Fo Guang Shan, where meditation halls and towering Buddhas deliver unexpected calm. Tour the Buddha Memorial Center, browse the Cultural Museum’s rare artifacts and enjoy a peaceful vegetarian lunch. On the return, pause at Lotus Lake’s Dragon and Tiger Pagodas and peek at the solar‑powered Kaohsiung National Stadium. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Lotus Lake & Chijin Island
blocks.text: Begin at the Martyr’s Shrine for panoramic harbor views, then drift to Lotus Lake where dragon‑and‑tiger pagodas demand slow wandering. Ferry to Chijin Island, roam Old Street’s seafood stalls, sample grilled specialties and climb Taiwan’s second‑oldest lighthouse for seaside perspective. Return with salty air in your hair, pockets full of souvenirs and a very satisfied appetite. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Chikan Tower, Confucius Temple & Koxinga Shrine
blocks.text: Drive into Tainan’s layered past at Chikan Towers, ornate stone sentinels atop Fort Provintia’s remains. Wander the Confucius Temple courtyard where carved beams and courtyards keep time gently, then visit Koxinga Shrine to learn about the general who reshaped Taiwan’s destiny. It’s a compact, rich history lesson that reads better in person than in a textbook. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Kaohsiung
blocks.text: Docking at the Kaohsiung port cruise terminal puts you pretty much in the heart of southern Taiwan’s energy. Walk from the pier to waterfront cafés, ride a ferry across the harbor or hop a train to nearby temples and islands. blocks.heading: Things to do in Ko Samui
blocks.text: Ko Samui is a tropical paradise: unspoiled, lush and full of discovery. Visit serene temples like Big Buddha and Plai Laem, stroll white-sand beaches or stop at local markets filled with handicrafts and souvenirs. From sweeping ocean views to cultural landmarks, this island is the best of Thailand in one unforgettable stop.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Ko Samui
blocks.text: Each excursion on Ko Samui is designed to deepen your connection with the island’s mix of lush landscapes, ocean views and cultural heritage. Hike to waterfalls, sample Thai cuisine or unwind on a secluded beach as your time ashore becomes part of the journey.

blocks.heading: Resort & Beach Getaway
blocks.text: Spend a carefree day at a luxury beachfront resort where the hardest decision is pool or ocean. Lounge in the sun, stroll the shoreline and enjoy tropical drinks and snacks. With time to unwind and amenities at your fingertips, it’s the ideal way to recharge between your island explorations. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Ko Samui
blocks.text: Discover the island’s most beloved landmarks, including the striking Big Buddha and the serene Plai Laem Temple. Take in panoramic views, visit the colorful Guan Yu Shrine and enjoy a buffet lunch at a beachfront resort. You’ll have time to browse shops near Chaweng Beach before returning to port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Eco tour with local temple, waterfalls and snacks
blocks.text: Explore Ko Samui’s natural beauty and cultural treasures on an eco-friendly adventure. Visit a hillside temple surrounded by jungle, dip your toes at cascading waterfalls and sample tropical fruit and local snacks. Along the way, enjoy scenic countryside views and learn about the island’s traditions from your knowledgeable guide. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Angthong National Marine Park
blocks.text: Sail into a dreamlike world of limestone islands and emerald waters at Angthong National Marine Park. Cruise past towering cliffs, snorkel in crystal-clear coves and step ashore to hike or kayak. This protected archipelago is a haven for nature lovers, with unforgettable views and a peaceful escape from the everyday. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Bon Appétit recommended: Thai cooking classes
blocks.text: Uncover the secrets of Thai cuisine during a hands-on cooking class led by local chefs. You’ll learn how to prepare traditional dishes using fresh island ingredients, then savor your creations in a charming kitchen setting. It’s a flavorful journey into Thailand’s culinary heart, equal parts delicious and inspiring. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Tan, Mudsum and Rap Islands
blocks.text: Island-hop across three gems just off Ko Samui’s coast. Relax on the quiet shores of Koh Tan, snorkel vibrant reefs at Koh Madsum and soak in the tropical scenery at peaceful Koh Rap. Featuring soft beaches, clear waters and unspoiled island charm, this day trip is a postcard-perfect escape. LEARN MORE

blocks.text: Cam Ranh excursions invite you beyond the coastline and into the heart of central Vietnam. Discover ancient temple towers, riverside villages, bustling markets and traditional craft centers.

blocks.heading: Culinary Adventure, Pavilion Kuala Lumpur & Scenic Drive
blocks.text: Kick things off with a Kuala Lumpur classic: Bak Kut Teh — a brothy, herbal pork rib soup. Warmed and well-fed, head to the jaw-dropping Petronas Twin Towers to ogle skybridge angles and sleek architecture. Then it’s free time (three full hours!) at Pavilion Kuala Lumpur, the city’s upscale mega-mall-meets-cultural-playground packed with designer shops, Instagrammable cafés, art galleries and mayb

blocks.heading: Best of Kuala Lumpur
blocks.text: Begin with a scenic ride to Kuala Lumpur Tower for bird’s‑eye city views, then explore the National Museum’s galleries tracing the nation’s past — from Stone Age to colonial to independent Malaysia. Photo‑stop time at the Petronas Towers, National Mosque and Merdeka Square follow, then wrap with a lunch buffet at a leading hotel and some serious handicraft shopping at Karyaneka. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Skybridge, Petronas Tower & City Drive
blocks.text: Board your air‑conditioned motorcoach and drive into the heart of Kuala Lumpur. Stop at the National Monument, then Merdeka Square with its royal architecture. Next: the iconic Petronas Twin Towers connected by a skybridge 557 feet above street level (tickets limited). Finish with two hours in the shopping mall scene before returning. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kuala Lumpur On Your Own
blocks.text: Enjoy a 90‑minute ride from Port Kelang into the city. Disembark near the Petronas Towers and roam at your pace; Chinatown, Little India, Jalan Bukit Bintang, cafés and boutiques await. Grab lunch (perhaps at Bintang Walk), explore until ship‑time, then ride back. You determine what adventure awaits. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Batu Caves, Royal Selangor Pewter & National Museum
blocks.text: Head north to the Batu Caves shrine, with its towering Lord Murugan statue and 272 steps (feel free to count them on your way up). Back in Kuala Lumpur, visit the Royal Selangor Visitor Centre to see pewter craft in action, enjoy a Malaysian buffet lunch, then the National Museum’s rich cultural collection, before a final photo‑stop at the Petronas Towers. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Langkawi
blocks.text: Experience Langkawi’s beauty up close with shore excursions that take you from sky-high cable car rides to mangrove cruises through serene waterways. Whether you’re seeking adventure or relaxation, each shore excursion offers a new way to discover the island’s lush landscapes and charm.

blocks.heading: Geopark Day Cruise
blocks.text: Glide through calm, emerald-green waterways fringed by sheer limestone cliffs and lush mangroves, spotting sea eagles, dolphins and kingfishers along the way. Pause on a secluded beach for a refreshing swim or simply relax with stunning jungle and sea views as your backdrop for an unforgettable island cruise. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Rice Museum, Cable Car, Craft & Cultural Complex
blocks.text: Step into a world where lush jungle meets sky-high adventure and cultural heritage. You’ll ride a dramatic cable car to towering panoramas, explore a vibrant craft complex alive with batik, weavers and metal-art artisans, and wander through a captivating museum dedicated to rice cultivation that brings Malaysia’s agricultural story to life. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Underwater World, Mashuri Tomb & Eagle Square
blocks.text: Explore vibrant marine life at one of Southeast Asia’s most immersive aquariums, trace the haunting legend of a young princess whose story still echoes in the hillside tomb and museum, and pose for an iconic photo beside the soaring eagle sculpture overlooking the bay — all in one unforgettable afternoon. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Sea Eagle & Mangrove Cruise
blocks.text: Glide through shimmering mangrove waterways as sleek sea eagles wheel overhead, then peer into eerie caves carved by time and tide. After the thrill of spotting wildlife, unwind at a floating restaurant framed by lush jungle and open Andaman-Sea vistas. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Langkawi On Your Own
blocks.text: Step off the ship and immerse yourself in a vibrant island adventure. Wander through bustling markets and browse duty-free treasures, snap a photo by the iconic eagle landmark towering over the harbor and explore charming beaches where tropical waves meet golden sand. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kilim Marine Kayak Adventure
blocks.text: Paddle through calm mangrove waterways surrounded by limestone cliffs and lush greenery. Spot wildlife like eagles and monkeys as you explore hidden caves and quiet inlets. End the day with a relaxing seaside lunch, taking in the natural beauty that makes this corner of Malaysia so unforgettable. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Lautoka
blocks.text: Lautoka offers a vibrant mix of island life, local culture and coastal beauty. From its lively markets to the nearby beaches and lush countryside, there’s plenty to explore and enjoy in this welcoming city.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Lautoka
blocks.text: Shore excursions in Lautoka offer a true taste of Fiji, from scenic coastal drives to immersive cultural experiences. Each adventure reveals the island’s warm spirit and stunning natural landscapes, creating memories that go far beyond the shore.

blocks.heading: Essence of Fiji
blocks.text: Experience the vibrant spirit of Fiji through a visit that combines cultural insight, relaxation and local craftsmanship. Tour a wellness retreat where natural beauty products are made, enjoy rejuvenating treatments and browse handmade goods that celebrate Fijian artistry. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kula Eco Park Tour
blocks.text: Discover a vibrant sanctuary nestled within Fiji’s lush rainforest, where native wildlife and tropical flora thrive in harmony. Stroll along shaded boardwalks, learn about local conservation efforts and enjoy the island’s natural beauty up close. This immersive experience offers a peaceful retreat and a deeper appreciation for Fiji’s rich biodiversity. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Fijean Homestead & History
blocks.text: Step into the heart of Fijian life with a visit that blends history, culture and local charm. Explore a traditional homestead surrounded by lush gardens, learn about family traditions passed through generations and experience the warmth of island hospitality through music, storytelling and daily customs that bring Fiji’s rich heritage to life. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Fiji Natural Thermal Mud Pool
blocks.text: Immerse yourself in a unique wellness experience where native village hospitality and ancient traditions merge: you’re greeted with a ceremonial welcome, then guided into mineral-rich geothermal settings where natural mud is rubbed onto your skin and gently sun-dried. Afterward, you rinse off in soothing hot springs, emerging refreshed and revitalized. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Tau Cave & Zipline Tour
blocks.text: This excursion combines adventure and exploration as you journey through Fiji’s lush interior. You’ll glide above the treetops on a zipline before venturing into a dramatic cave system rich with history and natural beauty—an unforgettable mix of excitement and discovery in one of the island’s most scenic settings. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Leisurely Nadi
blocks.text: Journey through Fiji’s lush countryside to discover the charm of local life, from vibrant markets and coastal scenery to glimpses of traditional village culture. This easygoing excursion offers a balance of sightseeing, local flavor and scenic relaxation—perfect for travelers looking to experience Fiji’s warmth and beauty at an unhurried pace. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Pago Pago
blocks.text: Pago Pago is a South Pacific gem of natural beauty and heartfelt island hospitality. Marvel at emerald mountains, stroll quiet beaches and explore charming villages that reflect centuries of Samoan tradition as you experience the wonders of Pago Pago.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Pago Pago
blocks.text: Explore the scenic beauty and cultural heritage of American Samoa through immersive shore excursions. Visit traditional villages, meet local artisans and witness time-honored ceremonies, all set against the stunning backdrop of lush rainforests and turquoise waters.

blocks.heading: Ocean View Bay Kayak & Snorkel Tour
blocks.text: Kayak across the calm waters of Pago Pago Harbor and peer into the coral‑rich shallows where giant clams and tropical fish thrive. After paddling, snorkel in protected waters while your guide points out marine life and shares island insights before returning to shore to relax on the beach. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Island Drive & Samoan Ava Ceremony
blocks.text: Ride an open‑air bus along the coastal roads of Tutuila to Mt. Alava for sweeping views of the harbor and village below. Visit local landmarks, including the old High Court, Navy commissary and historic post office in Fagatogo. Finally, witness a Samoan ava ceremony featuring song, dance and a traditional root‑based drink. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: West Island Drive & Village Way of Life
blocks.text: Head west across quiet bays and past traditional fale homes that sit on stilts in village communities. This serene drive is the experience of a lifetime, giving you a glimpse into daily life in American Samoa as you stop at ocean lookouts and meet local families continuing time‑honored customs. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Essence of Tutuila
blocks.text: This guided tour captures the spirit of Tutuila Island with photo‑worthy vistas, cultural commentary and a chance to experience the island’s natural rhythm. Stops on this memorable Pago Pago excursion include rainforests, coastal trails and historic sites. Get an exclusive look at the intricacies of American Samoa’s landscapes and heritage. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: East Island Drive, Ocean Center & Beach Visit
blocks.text: Journey toward the tip of Tutuila’s eastern shore before arriving at the Tauese P. F. Sunia Ocean Center, where you’ll learn about marine conservation and local sea life. Afterward, enjoy time at a nearby beach to walk the sand, swim in the gorgeous waters or simply take in the tropical surroundings. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Pago Pago
blocks.text: Cruise itineraries that visit Pago Pago deliver a true taste of the South Pacific. Experience a port surrounded by emerald peaks and turquoise bays, with dramatic natural beauty reflected in a welcoming island culture. You might explore neighboring islands, cross the equator, or visit remote gems like Fiji and Tahiti along the way. Each Pago Pago sailing is an invitation to discover more.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Penang
blocks.text: From sampling delicious street food to exploring vibrant art scenes and tranquil beaches, Penang has something for every traveler. As one of the best cruise destinations in Asia, cruises in Penang offer an unforgettable way to take in its scenic coastline and bustling harbor life.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Penang
blocks.text: Discover the heart of Penang through unforgettable shore excursions that blend culture, flavor and scenery. Wander through colorful local markets, sample authentic street food, visit ornate temples or unwind on golden beaches—all easily accessible from the port, making cruises in Penang a gateway to the island’s rich experiences.

blocks.heading: Butterfly Farm & Gardens
blocks.text: Stroll through beautiful tropical gardens filled with colorful butterflies, flowing streams and lush greenery. Explore indoor exhibits featuring unique insects and reptiles, making this a relaxing and fascinating way to experience Penang’s natural beauty. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Batik Factory & Butterfly Farm
blocks.text: Step into a vibrant island-world where skilled artisans apply layers of hot wax and vivid dyes to fabric in a centuries-old batik tradition, then wander into a lush tropical sanctuary alive with thousands of fluttering butterflies and other mesmerizing insects. This excursion blends hands-on craft and nature’s magic into one rich, sensory experience. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Penang
blocks.text: Immerse yourself in the sights, scents and culture of Penang on this unforgettable island journey. Visit a lush butterfly sanctuary, watch artisans craft vibrant batik and browse a bustling spice market filled with local aromas. Savor fresh coconut water before enjoying a scenic coastal drive that perfectly captures the island’s tropical charm. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Temples & Penang Famous Homes
blocks.text: Step into Penang’s vibrant past as you explore a grand temple adorned with golden Buddhas and the gentle scent of incense. Then, wander through a beautifully restored colonial mansion filled with intricate wood carvings, antique furnishings and Peranakan treasures. This experience offers a captivating glimpse into the island’s spiritual and cultural heritage. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Suffolk House & Francis Light Cemetery
blocks.text: Step into a beautifully restored colonial mansion surrounded by tropical gardens, where stories of Penang’s early days come to life. Wander through elegant rooms, admire classic architecture and visit a peaceful nearby cemetery honoring the island’s founders—an experience that blends history, heritage and quiet charm. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Taste of Penang
blocks.text: Savor a vivid journey through Penang’s culinary heart as you wander fragrant spice lanes, sample sizzling seafood and local sweets and learn the stories behind each dish from passionate vendors—making this a flavorful and unforgettable stop in one of Asia’s premier cruise destinations. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Penang
blocks.text: Cruise itineraries to Penang showcase the island’s perfect mix of culture, cuisine and coastal charm. As one of Malaysia’s most captivating ports, Penang offers travelers a chance to explore lively markets, savor local street food and admire scenic shorelines—all within easy reach of the port. Penang is a highlight on any Asia cruise itinerary.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Phuket
blocks.text: Welcome to Phuket — the island that dares you to relax, feast or snorkel, or to just say the name out loud and do all three. Known for its dramatic cliffs, pristine beaches and a temple or ten, this Thai escape mixes sacred traditions with serious sun-lounging. Whether you're temple-hopping or hunting for street food, Phuket brings the heat and keeps the vibes just perfect.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Phuket
blocks.text: Ready to go full island mode? Princess Cruises curates unforgettable excursions that blend beach bliss, Thai tradition and just the right amount of monkey mischief (the real kind).

blocks.heading: Phuket Old Farm & The Old Town
blocks.text: Get hands-on at Old Phuket Farm, where rubber tapping, buffalo herding and tin panning aren’t just history — they’re your new hobbies. Then hit the colorful alleys of Phuket Town for a fix of Sino-Portuguese charm, old-school energy and real-deal Thai culture. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Phuket
blocks.text: Circle the island like royalty with visits to Promthep Cape (where the land runs out and the selfies begin) and Wat Chalong (Phuket’s most sacred temple). Then catch a cultural show at Phuket Thai Village and cap the day with a breezy lunch and a little retail therapy at a local shop. Just remember to stick to the dress code — respect the culture, receive some good luck in return. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Patong Exploration
blocks.text: A beach town that knows how to party, Patong is yours to explore at your own pace. Drop-off is near the action — think Bangla Road, boutique shopping and enough beachfront cafés to seriously test your willpower. Skip the jetskis (by which we mean skip them across the water) and sink into that white sand like it’s the best bed you’ve ever felt. Bring local currency and some SPF, but leave your sche

blocks.heading: Phuket Retreat and Duangjitt Beach Resort
blocks.text: Tour the island’s icons — Big Buddha, coastal roads, villages — before surrendering to the calm of Duangjitt Resort (we’re talking 36 acres of tropical gardens, three pools and no stress anywhere). With Patong Beach just a stroll away and staff trained in the art of chill, you’ll eat, float, nap and repeat. Lunch included, spa optional (inner peace unavoidable). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Phi Phi Island Beach & Swimming
blocks.text: Hop a speedboat to Bamboo Island for reef snorkeling and laid-back lounging before skipping over to Phi Phi Don, where twin bays and tropical daydreams collide. Cruise past caves and macaques, lunch at Cape Tong, swim it off and then shop your way back to the boat. Beach bliss, jungle cliffs, cheeky monkeys — all the hits, no filler. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Phang-Nga, James Bond Island Cruise & Panyi Island by Speed Boat
blocks.text: Board a speedboat, zip through limestone giants and land on a movie set — Khao Phing Kan, a.k.a. James Bond Island (even if you’re not a Bond enthusiast you’ll recognize the location). Then glide to Panyi, a floating fishing village with a soccer pitch on stilts and a marketplace built over the sea. No beach today, just wild views and salt-air stories. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Phuket
blocks.text: Depending on your ship, you’ll either tender into Patong Bay (translation: scenic and splashy) or dock at the deep sea port in Ao Makarm — each with its perks. Patong drops you right into the beachside buzz, while Ao Makarm is the jump-off for island-hopping daytrips. Both offer easy access to Phuket’s stalls, spas, temples and tuk-tuks, with transport options galore. It’s an Asia cruise itinerary

blocks.heading: Things to do in Sihanoukville
blocks.text: Sihanoukville isn’t just a beach town with a fun-to-say name — it’s a salty little slice of Cambodian coastal life with temples, tuk-tuks and seafood that slaps (sometimes literally; hey, fresh means fresh). Tucked against the Gulf of Thailand, this port mixes laid-back vibes with just enough cultural curveballs to keep you on your toes. The beaches are real, the markets are chaotic and if you kee

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Sihanoukville
blocks.text: You’ve docked, you’ve lathered on the sunscreen and now it’s time to pick your adventure. We have a few suggestions for you.

blocks.heading: Ream National Park Village & Spiritual Pagoda
blocks.text: This one goes heavy on the culture. Start with a giant copper statue of mythic lovers, stop at the God Shiva statue and swing through a rural school for a peek into local life and education. You’ll visit a traditional home, light incense at Ream Pagoda and finish at a local market where you can try to figure out which snacks are the just right intensity to help you expand your palate. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Wat Krom, Villages, Market & Beach Barbecue
blocks.text: Start at Wat Krom with its sea views and spirit shrines, then head to Psar Lu Market for a guided plunge into fruit, fish and the full sensory overload of a local bazaar. Swing by a school to meet kindergarteners (why not bring some small gifts to share!), then head to the beach for what is possibly the most satisfying seafood barbecue of your vacation. You’ll get three full hours of beach time, p

blocks.heading: Ream National Park
blocks.text: Ream is the kind of place that makes you wonder why you ever vacationed somewhere with streetlights. Cruise through mangrove canals, then hike along the coast to Prince Island where beach time comes with serious peace and zero hotel chains. You’ll stop by Giant Tree (can you guess why they call it that?), eat lunch at a beach resort and top it off at Meditation Mountain. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Wat Krom, Market & Sihanoukville Beach
blocks.text: This one’s got the full cultural sampler: temples, markets, memorials and monks. Start with Wat Krom, stop at Independence Square, browse Psar Lu Market and then wrap it all up with an hour of unbothered beach time. Bonus points if you can squeeze in a tuk-tuk tour before the sunscreen wears off. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kayaking at Ream National Park & Sihanoukville Beach
blocks.text: Paddle through the mangrove-lined river like an eco-warrior with a camera phone (just don’t drop it). After your kayak cruise, grab some coconut juice and visit Meditation Mountain, where locals collect plants allegedly blessed by ancient spirits. Wrap it up with a beach visit and stops at a Shiva statue and a Love statue. Hey, Cambodia never met a photo op it didn’t like. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Sihanoukville
blocks.text: The Sihanoukville port is about a 5-minute walk from the port entrance and a 10-minute drive from downtown and the beaches. That means you’re practically in the thick of it before you even find your sandals. Tuk-tuks line the entrance, temples crown the hills and the seafood is phenomenal. blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Suva
blocks.text: This energetic port blends colonial-era architecture, busy markets and rainforest adventures into one tropical stop. From cultural discoveries to nature escapes, Suva offers something for every type of traveler.

blocks.heading: The Jewel Of Fiji
blocks.text: Journey through Suva and visit landmarks including Parliament House, Nausori Market and the Pure Fiji facility. Tour the building and learn about local beauty rituals. On your way out, browse for skincare products created in the Suva facility. The excursion includes a scenic drive and commentary on Fiji’s culture, adding insight into traditional life and modern development. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Suva
blocks.text: Explore Suva’s landmarks on this half-day tour with stops at Government House, Walu Bay and panoramic viewpoints of the harbor. Visit the Fiji Museum to explore cultural artifacts and Fiji’s storied past, including the era of cannibalism. Shop in downtown Suva or enjoy a relaxed stroll through the capital before returning to the ship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Wainadoi zipline
blocks.text: Fly across the forest canopy on an exhilarating zipline adventure through Fiji’s lush jungle. With ten platforms and eight traverses, this guided experience offers stunning views and an adrenaline rush. Your guides ensure a safe, thrilling ride from the treetops to the forest floor. It’s an unforgettable way to experience Fiji’s tropical landscapes. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Colo - I - Suva Forest Park & waterfall tour
blocks.text: Experience authentic Fijian village life at Koromakawa. Enjoy a warm welcome, take part in a kava ceremony and watch traditional dances. A village buffet lunch and time with locals round out your cultural immersion. If time permits, you’ll visit a nearby waterfall pool for a refreshing swim before returning to the ship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: A tropical delight - the Pearl South Pacific Resort
blocks.text: Spend a relaxing day at The Pearl South Pacific Resort. After a scenic 45-minute drive, enjoy full access to the beach, pool, bars, restaurants and leisure facilities. A gourmet buffet lunch and live entertainment with a traditional Meke performance will complete your visit to this tranquil, upscale retreat. Return refreshed after a day of Fijian hospitality. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Naililili historical tour by long boat
blocks.text: Cruise to Nasali Landing in the Rewa Delta and receive a warm welcome with traditional songs. Visit Naililili Church, meet villagers and learn about local history. The journey includes scenic river views and time to interact with children at a nearby school. Discover a culturally rich and historic corner of Fiji. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Australia Cruises
blocks.text: Australia is teeming with vast treasures. Indulge in seasonal delicacies and fine wines. Snorkel among technicolor fish. Discover ancient cultures, explore historic landmarks, and tour the country’s most charming cities. Princess will help you create memories to last a lifetime. VIEW CRUISES

blocks.heading: Australia Outback Adventure Cruisetour
blocks.text: Visit two UNESCO World Heritage Sites: soak in the brilliant underwater colours of the Great Barrier Reef, and then watch the setting sun transform the sky as Uluru (Ayers Rock) glows red from afar. Photo: The beauty of Uluru (Ayers Rock) VIEW CRUISETOURS

blocks.heading: Ultimate Australia Cruisetour
blocks.text: Our most extensive Cruisetour guides you through the highlights of Sydney, radiant Uluru in the heart of the outback, scenic Kakadu National Park (a UNESCO World Heritage Site teeming with wildlife), Darwin, Cairns and the Great Barrier Reef. Photo: Australia’s magical Great Barrier Reef VIEW CRUISETOURS

blocks.heading: Excursions — your gateway to Australia's best attractions
blocks.text: Explore the Great Barrier Reef from Airlie Beach / Ngaro Country. Visit the award-winning Rainforestation National Park in Cairns / Gimuy. Ride a camel along the shore, and learn the secrets to pearl farming in Broome / Rubibi. On itineraries with More Ashore Late Night calls, we stay until at least 9 p.m. in port so you can experience some of the fabulous nightlife. And with a range of Discovery

blocks.heading: Lifestyle & culture
blocks.text: Pursue your passion for wine, beer and chocolate with a taste-testing tour in the Margaret River region. Explore the art and crafts in the charming cities of Hahndorf and Montville, or visit a variety of museums and cultural parks to celebrate Australia’s rich native and colonial history. Photo: Enjoy regional wines

blocks.heading: Natural wonders & landscapes
blocks.text: Traverse a canopy path above the forest floor for a bird’s-eye view of the ancient karri and tingle trees near Albany. Behold the otherworldly spires at Perth’s Nambung National Park. Explore the underwater beauty of the Great Barrier Reef, or travel inland to Tamborine Mountain, a fertile volcanic plateau that boasts 21 species of birds. Photo: Pinnacles Desert in Perth's Nambung National Park

blocks.heading: Unique & iconic wildlife
blocks.text: From Tasmanian devils to wombats and kookaburras, you’ll encounter fascinating animals and plants from the region and from around the globe at Brisbane’s Australia Zoo, Melbourne’s Healesville Sanctuary, Sydney’s Featherdale Wildlife Park and the Perth Zoo. Photo: The iconic Tasmanian Devil

blocks.heading: Architecture
blocks.text: Sydney hosts several architectural delights, including the iconic Sydney Opera House and the 320-meter-tall Sydney Tower and Government House, one of Australia’s finest examples of colonial-style architecture. In the heart of Melbourne sits Federation Square, and rising 230 meters into Brisbane skyline, the SkyPoint viewing deck boasts 360-degree views of the Gold Coast. Photo: The Sydney Tower is

blocks.heading: Art & museums
blocks.text: Many of Australia’s museums are closely tied to the land, its people and history. Hobart is known for its well-preserved 19th century National Trust buildings, Broome’s / Rubibi museum traces native life and the pearling industry, while in Tasmania you can discover what life was back in the early 1900s. Photo: Richmond Bridge in Hobart, Tasmania

blocks.heading: UNESCO world heritage sites
blocks.text: While the Sydney Opera House is a prime example of architectural design at its finest, Port Arthur’s humble penal colony stands as a grim reminder of Australia’s early beginnings. There are a number of natural World Heritage Sites, including the Great Barrier Reef, the Tasmanian Wilderness World Heritage Area, the Blue Mountains and the Rainforestation National Park. Photo: The Blue Mountains boas

pages.title: 10 Melbourne Travel Tips For Cruisers - Princess Cruises
pages.metaDescription: Want to blend in like a local on your Australia cruise? These 10 Melbourne travel tips from Princess Cruises will help you experience the best of this iconic Australian city as only a local would.

headings.text: 7. Don't expect to find a courthouse at Federation Square.

blocks.heading: 1. Try some Vegemite.
blocks.text: You might be familiar with the idea of the Vegemite sandwich if you've ever listen to the band Men at Work, but this salty spread never gained much popularity outside of Australia. If you can eat it without a wince, you just might pass for a local.

blocks.heading: Start your Melbourne adventure
blocks.text: VIEW CRUISES

blocks.heading: 2. Always brake for kangaroos.
blocks.text: These animals are bigger than you may think, and they're no less troublesome to locals than deer are to those in the US. When you see a sign on the road warning you to watch for kangaroos, that doesn't mean get out the camera.

blocks.heading: 3. Love sports.
blocks.text: Melbourne natives enjoy all types of sports, including rugby and cricket. The city's big sporting events — the Australian Open Tennis Championships in January and the Grand Prix in March — always get the locals buzzing with excitement.

blocks.heading: 4. Know your wine.
blocks.text: When in Melbourne, local brands such as Jacob's Creek are acceptable, and even New Zealand sauvignon blanc is common — but try not to order any wine from Napa Valley if you want to look like you belong.

blocks.heading: 5. Keep cool.
blocks.text: Temperatures fluctuate in Melbourne, especially in the summer, which occurs from December–February. Layer your clothing, and you'll be fine. Just because it's going to be hot doesn't mean you should ditch your jacket in the morning.

blocks.heading: 6. Pick your coffee.
blocks.text: Forget Starbucks — Melbourne is one of the biggest coffee-drinking cities in the world. Get familiar with the lingo: a short black is just a shot of espresso; a long black is one shot (or two) over hot water; a flat white is espresso with steamed milk and little to no froth; and if you order an iced coffee, you'll get espresso mixed with milk, then topped with ice cream and whipped cream.

blocks.heading: 7. Don't expect to find a courthouse at Federation Square.
blocks.text: This development has nothing to do with law, order, or politics. Fed Square is a hot spot, especially at night when there are events in the square, and clubs like popular Transport Public Bar are sure to be packed until the wee hours.

blocks.heading: 8. Save your "g'day."
blocks.text: This greeting may be acceptable in the Outback, but locals in Melbourne are more likely to say "ciao." Feel free to greet locals with "hi" when you get off your cruise ship in Melbourne.

blocks.heading: 9. Know the city name.
blocks.text: Melbourne is pronounced "mell-burn." But if you really want to fit in, abbreviate the name: Melbs. This term is primarily used when outside the city center.

blocks.heading: 10. Cuddle a koala — carefully.
blocks.text: Hold your excitement over these adorable creatures when you're among locals in Melbourne, but don't forget to book a shore excursion to Healesville Sanctuary, where you can see koalas, wallabies, and other native animals to this area. With these Melbourne travel tips, you’ll fit in with the locals in no time. Looking for more expert advice before cruising to Melbourne? Find more insightful article

blocks.heading: Things to do in Adelaide
blocks.text: Adelaide is the gateway to a thriving, cosmopolitan and coastal city where you can lounge on sun-soaked beaches, kayak in the downtown River Torrens or browse 45,000 paintings in the Art Gallery of South Australia. The Adelaide Central Market is a must-visit for foodies (try the cheese and seafood!) inside of a 19th century historical building.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Adelaide
blocks.text: Don’t stress over planning — experience the best Australia has to offer, stress-free, with Princess shore excursions. We’ll handle the details so you can relax and soak it all in.

blocks.heading: Dolphins, Shipwrecks & Maritime History Tour
blocks.text: From the ship's berth in Outer Harbor you’ll head to Port Adelaide’s heritage precinct, cruise the Port River to see wild dolphins and abandoned iron‑hulled ships (like the Santiago), then enjoy free time and access to the South Australian Maritime Museum for a deep dive into the region’s nautical past. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Spirit of the Coorong Cruise
blocks.text: All aboard. Sail down the ​​Murray River where you can see the historic locks that have made this river a trade hot spot. Hop off at Godfrey's Landing to see the sand dunes and the pristine white sand beaches along the Great Southern Ocean. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cleland Wildlife Park
blocks.text: Head out into the bush for a wild Australian adventure at this wildlife park. Explore the natural beauty of the Adelaide area on the trails where kangaroos can hop around you. Emus, dingoes, wallabies and Tasmanian devils all wander free — and you can even hold a koala. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Adelaide Highlights
blocks.text: From one-of-a-kind glass greenhouses to Australian Aboriginal artifacts, Adelaide has it all. Start the day at the botanical gardens with plants from 150 years ago before exploring the Moreton Bay Figs, the 1877-built glass Palm House that’s one of the last of its kind in the world. Dive into Aboriginal history and culture at the South Australia Museum, including the 27 Yuendemu school doors and o

blocks.heading: Barossa Valley & Wine Tasting
blocks.text: Nineteenth-century immigrants discovered fertile soil, pastoral hills and Mediterranean weather right outside of Adelaide, and the Barossa Valley vineyards and wineries were born. You’ll tour Seppeltsfield Wines where you can sample five wines and learn about the rich Seppelt family history. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: d'Arenburg & Handorf
blocks.text: Drive through McLaren Vale and the Adelaide Hills to the iconic d’Arenberg Cube for surreal art installations including Salvador Dalí works, then sample curated wines with a grazing lunch and finish the day exploring Hahndorf, Australia’s oldest German settlement. It might be more charm and wonder than any one day deserves. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Discover cruise itineraries sailing from Adelaide port
blocks.text: Set sail from a UNESCO City of Music and one of the wine capitals of the world: Adelaide, Australia. This southern city sits on white sand beaches next to vibrant turquoise waters and is packed full of a dazzling art scene and the best coffee in the country. With Princess Cruises®, Adelaide is only the beginning of what you’ll discover in Oceania as part of your Australia cruise.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Adelaide
blocks.text: The excursions here are built to suit your rhythm. Whether you’re after wildlife snaps, wine indulgence or city culture with a side of sand and surf, we’ve got something to suit your interests.

blocks.heading: Best of Adelaide
blocks.text: Hit the road and the hillside on this 4‑in‑1 day adventure. Hand‑feed kangaroos and eye down a koala or two (don’t worry, these ‘drop bears’ just want to say g’day). Then ride up to Mount Lofty’s summit for views so wide you’ll have to rethink what ‘horizon’ means. Lunch follows at a local hilltop restaurant before you dive into Rundle Mall, where shopping, bronze pig statues and art‑filled arcade

blocks.heading: Cleland Wildlife Park
blocks.text: Brush aside the cityscape and dive into bushland. At Cleland, set across 86 acres near the Adelaide Hills, you’ll have the chance to meet over 130 different animal species: koalas, Tasmanian devils, dingos and goannas among them. Then you’ll drive through forested slopes, feel the air change and appreciate how this city builds wilderness right into its backyard. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Port to Port Maritime & Heritage
blocks.text: Take your city day on the water and through history. Board near the Outer Harbor, ride into the Port River waters where the Adelaide Dolphin Sanctuary plays host to wild dolphins and mangrove forests. See the Ships Graveyard, the clipper City of Adelaide and immigrant era sites. Finish at the South Australian Maritime Museum. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: River E‑Bike Ride with Wines & Picnic
blocks.text: Swap coach for gears and glide along the Torrens River bike trail starting at Henley Beach. Pedal past red‑gum trees, duck‑filled banks and crisp river air. Finish at the National Wine Centre, where you’ll enjoy lunch and get a taste of why South Australia is serious about its vines. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Dolphins, Shipwrecks & Maritime History Tour
blocks.text: Board a vessel in Port Adelaide, cruise through the port’s working infrastructure and past the Adelaide Dolphin Sanctuary (one of the only urban wild dolphin populations in Australia). Spot old shipwrecks and shorebirds before having free time to explore the precinct’s cafés and warehouse‑turned galleries. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: McLaren Vale Vineyards & Wine
blocks.text: Journey south into the rich winelands of McLaren Vale, where Mediterranean‑climate vines thrive. Visit two boutique wineries with sea‑breeze views of the Gulf St Vincent, and taste shiraz and Riesling while reflecting on the agricultural history of the land. Then savour a buffet lunch of farm breads, cheeses, olives and fresh produce. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Airlie Beach
blocks.text: Airlie Beach is a must-see destination where the Great Barrier Reef meets tropical paradise. From sailing the Whitsundays Islands to lounging on sun-drenched beaches and exploring vibrant local markets, it’s the perfect gateway for adventure and relaxation.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Airlie Beach
blocks.text: Discover the best of Airlie Beach with unforgettable shore excursions that showcase its tropical beauty. From sailing crystal-clear waters to exploring lush rainforests and coral reefs, every adventure offers a unique glimpse into this coastal paradise.

blocks.heading: Local Connections - Sea Kayaking
blocks.text: Paddle across crystal-clear waters surrounded by white-sand beaches, lush rainforests and rocky islets teeming with wildlife. Feel the rhythm of the waves, spot sea turtles and dolphins and unwind on a coral beach—an unforgettable way to experience the beauty and serenity of Australia’s tropical coast. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Reef and Island Scenic Flight
blocks.text: Take to the skies for a once-in-a-lifetime adventure over the Great Barrier Reef and Whitsunday Islands. Witness the vibrant blues and swirling corals of this World Heritage wonder from above as you glide past Whitehaven Beach, Hill Inlet and secluded island gems. Every moment of this breathtaking flight reveals the unmatched beauty of Australia’s tropical coast. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Proserpine River & Crocodile Cruise
blocks.text: Get up close to Australia’s wild side on a thrilling Proserpine River adventure. Cruise through lush wetlands teeming with birdlife and keep your eyes peeled for the famous “salties” basking on the banks. Then, hop aboard a tractor-drawn wagon to explore the untouched Goorganga wetlands, where your guide reveals the secrets of this incredible natural ecosystem. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Exhilarating White Haven Expedition
blocks.text: Set out on an unforgettable adventure to Whitehaven Beach, a pristine paradise in the heart of the Great Barrier Reef. Ride a high-speed boat across turquoise waters, then sink your toes into the pure white sand of one of the world’s most eco-friendly beaches. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Jet Ski Safari
blocks.text: Feel the rush of adventure as you speed across the turquoise waters of the Whitsundays on a thrilling jet ski tour. Guided by experienced professionals, you’ll weave through scenic coastlines, spot sea turtles and seabirds and experience the ultimate mix of adrenaline and beauty. This 90-minute ride is the perfect way to see Airlie Beach from an unforgettable perspective. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ocean Rafting Marine Safari
blocks.text: Take off on a high-speed motor-raft and race through the turquoise waters of the Whitsunday Passage toward Black or Hook Island. Guided by an expert eco-guide, you’ll explore vibrant coral gardens teeming with marine life, spot sea turtles gliding beneath the surface and snorkel among giant clams, colorful corals and dazzling tropical fish. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Albany
blocks.text: Albany is what happens when a rugged coastline, a convict ship and a wind turbine walk into a bar. There’s something delightfully odd about this place: part historic whaling outpost, part windswept wilderness, part “did I just taste sandalwood in that pinot?” It’s Western Australia with its sleeves rolled up, still salty from the ocean and not the least bit interested in showing off. And somehow t

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Albany
blocks.text: Weird rocks? War stories? Whales (of the no-long-with-us variety)? Albany has the eclectic mix of adventures you’ve been looking for. These excursions make sure you get the most out of every one.

blocks.heading: Southern Wineries and Sights
blocks.text: Cruise past Dog Rock (unsurprisingly named because it looks like a dog’s head)) and into Albany’s wine country, where small vineyards punch well above their weight. Sip, sample and make your best “yes, I totally taste blackcurrant” face. No judgment — we’re all just here for the wine and the nice view. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Albany: National ANZAC Centre & Torndirrup National Park
blocks.text: This one starts strong — the Gap and Natural Bridge serve up spray, sound and the kind of views that don’t need a filter. From there, a scenic drive takes you to Mt. Clarence for a hilltop panorama of harbors, wind farms and coastline. The final stop is the ANZAC Centre, a stunning museum that tells the stories of the soldiers who left from Albany’s shores. It’s heartfelt, high-tech and self-guide

blocks.heading: Torndirrup National Park & Historic Whale Station
blocks.text: Begin with one of nature’s most impressive sculptures at the Gap and Natural Bridge, then dial it back with a visit to the historic whaling station at Discovery Bay. This once-bloody business is now a beautifully strange museum complete with immersive exhibits, vintage whaling gear and a real-deal whale chaser ship you can explore without getting splashed. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Oyster Harbour & Kalgan River Cruise
blocks.text: Cruise through calm waters as your guide serves up stories, bird facts and poetry (yes, really). Between the eagle rays, tea and damper, it’s a calm-but-charming way to explore Albany’s waterways. Pro tip: keep your eyes peeled for manta-ray-adjacent creatures that like to leap out of the water. If you’re quick with your camera you might have just found yourself a new social media background. LEAR

blocks.heading: Easy Albany: Torndirrup National Park & Albany Wind Farm
blocks.text: Short on steps, big on scenery. You’ll hit the Gap and Natural Bridge (dramatic coastal erosion is the best kind of erosion) then move on to the Albany Wind Farm, where massive turbines spin above the sea like clean-power giants. A coastal path leads to a lookout point so stunning it may cause spontaneous enlightenment. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Valley of the Giants Treetop Walk
blocks.text: Leave the coast behind and head inland to walk among 300-foot karri trees and wide-girthed red tingle trees (we’re not making up those names; it’s what they’re called). The canopy walkway gives you a bird’s-eye view of the forest and possibly a few existential thoughts. Afterward, eat lunch, sip wine and maybe buy something handmade. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Auckland
blocks.text: Māori warriors, underground galaxies, gourmet farms and an extremely overachieving jet boat await. Get in, strap on, dig in — whatever your style, there’s a tour built to make your day impossible to forget.

blocks.heading: Easy Auckland – City Highlights
blocks.text: Perfect for first‑timers or anyone who believes sightseeing shouldn’t feel like cardio. You’ll roll past Bastion Point, beaches that shimmer like glass and into Parnell Village for a look at galleries and garden‑lined streets. The route loops through Auckland Domain and past the Sky Tower before returning you to port with zero foot blisters. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Auckland: City Drive & Māori Performance at Museum
blocks.text: Auckland rolls out its highlights on this guided drive through gleaming waterfronts and leafy neighborhoods. You’ll pass Victorian villas in Parnell Village, cross the Harbour Bridge to the North Shore and stop for city views worth the flight over. The finale? A visit to the Auckland War Memorial Museum, where a live Māori performance fills the hall with drums, chants and energy that rattles your

blocks.heading: Auckland Jet Boat
blocks.text: If you crave velocity, this is your calling. Meet your skipper downtown and hang on tight as twin turbo engines roar across the harbor at 50 knots. Expect spins, slides and water spray in generous supply as the skyline blurs behind you. When you duck under the Harbour Bridge, keep an eye out for bungee jumpers; adrenaline junkies unite. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Walk, Talk, Eat Auckland
blocks.text: This one’s for flavor chasers. Led by a local food pro, you’ll wind through hidden lanes, art‑filled alleys and historic pubs while tasting Auckland’s edible identity (part Polynesian, part Asian, part European and entirely its own). Sample sweets, street bites and café staples while hearing stories of sailors, smugglers and chefs who made the city delicious. It’s equal parts food crawl and cultur

blocks.heading: Waitomo Glow Worm Grotto
blocks.text: Three hours inland and a few worlds away, you’ll descend into a subterranean universe lit by thousands of blue‑green glow worms. Your guide steers a silent boat through the limestone caverns as these tiny creatures cast an eerie, magical light above you. It’s one of New Zealand’s natural miracles. Afterwards, lunch at Crosshills Farm feels doubly alive under the open sky. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: A Gourmet’s World
blocks.text: Trade the city skyline for green valleys and farmhouse kitchens. At Vineyard Cottages, owner Elle Armon‑Jones introduces you to the region’s small‑batch artisans — cheesemakers, beekeepers, winemakers and dreamers — before you sit down to a wine‑paired lunch built around whatever’s in season. Then it’s off to Muriwai Beach, where gannets wheel over black‑sand cliffs and the surf sets its own sound
