blocks.heading: Things to do in Bay of Islands
Shore excursions to explore in Bay of Islands
blocks.text: Pick your adventure: paddle a kayak, chase waterfalls or maybe just hang out with dolphins who couldn’t care less about your personal space. Every excursion to the Bay of Islands feels like it was designed by Mother Nature and directed by a history buff.

blocks.heading: Best of Bay of Islands: Cruise & “Hole in the Rock”
blocks.text: Oh man. We are so excited to tell you about this excursion. Board a catamaran, grab a drink and drift toward the Cape Brett Peninsula where craggy coastlines and wind-sculpted cliffs steal the spotlight. The captain steers through the famous ‘Hole in the Rock,’ a wave-carved tunnel that looks like Mother Nature got creative with a cookie cutter. Add sea breezes, hidden coves and open‑air decks mad

blocks.heading: Kayaking the Waterways of Waitangi
blocks.text: Grab a paddle and see the Bay from the Māori point of view — low to the water, surrounded by mangroves. This guided kayak trip glides through the Waitangi Estuary to Haruru Falls, where the Waitangi River drops into a natural amphitheatre. Expect calm water, curious birds and frequent got-to-take-a-mental-picture moments. You’ll finish at sub-kissed Waitangi Beach. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Glow Worm Caves Express
blocks.text: Head underground for the galaxy beneath New Zealand. At Kawiti Caves, descendants of Chief Kawiti guide you through twisting limestone passages lit by thousands of bioluminescent glow worms. It’s part science lesson, part fever dream. Stalactites hang like chandeliers, and the ‘Milky Way Cavern’ gives actual space a run for its money. It’s cool, damp, beautiful — and just a tiny bit otherworldly.

blocks.heading: Best of Bay of Islands: Kerikeri and Māori Meetinghouse
blocks.text: You’ll start at Kerikeri, home to New Zealand’s oldest European building and enough fruit orchards to flavor the air. Then it’s on to a Māori marae, where you’ll be welcomed with a pōwhiri (traditional ceremony) that will give you goosebumps. Inside, elders share stories carved into the meeting house walls — tales of migration, ancestors and spirit. It’s living history with actual heart. LEARN MOR

blocks.heading: Russell Panorama & Cultural Highlights Tour
blocks.text: Sail over to Russell — New Zealand’s first capital, former whaling hotspot, current seaside charmer. A local guide spills the tea (and some rum) on the town’s scandalous past as you stroll the waterfront and visit Christ Church, the oldest in the country. There’s a snack stop at the Swordfish Club (second‑oldest game fishing club in the world) before you hit the museum and shops. History, gossip a

blocks.heading: Relaxing Russell Lunch Cruise
blocks.text: If your vacation goals include low-effort/high-reward adventures, this is your move. Settle onto a motorboat, order a drink and drift along the Bay’s coastline past oyster farms, vineyards and islands. Lunch is pure Kiwi indulgence — lamb, fish or venison with all the sides. When the boat docks, you’ll have free time to explore, shop or just contemplate making a permanent change of residence. LEAR

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Brisbane
blocks.text: Whether you're hiking rainforest paths or getting nose-to-beak with a cockatoo, these excursions show Brisbane’s best sides from every angle. Wildlife lovers, scenery seekers and anyone craving a laid-back day with a twist will find something that hits just right.

blocks.heading: Brisbane Sights & Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary Debark Tour
blocks.text: For those disembarking in Brisbane, this tour pairs a city overview with an unforgettable wildlife experience. At Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary (the first and largest of its kind) you'll meet koalas, feed kangaroos and spot dozens of other native species. It’s a low-key, high-reward way to end your trip on a distinctly Australian note. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Brisbane: CRIKEY! It's Australia Zoo
blocks.text: Head north to the Sunshine Coast for a day at Australia Zoo — the legacy of Steve Irwin and still one of the most thrilling wildlife parks anywhere. With over 1,000 animals and 14 live shows daily, this place stays busy in all the right ways. Wander at your own pace, catch a croc show in the Crocoseum or snap a selfie with a koala. Whether you're meeting a baby alligator or watching lemurs leap, y

blocks.heading: Easy Brisbane & Botanical Gardens
blocks.text: Start your tour with riverside views and a look at the city’s cultural heart, where art galleries, libraries and theaters converge. From there, ascend to Mt. Coot-tha for panoramic views that stretch from the skyline to the bay. Then it’s time to slow down among the blooms at the Botanic Gardens, a vast collection of native and exotic plants that doubles as a living museum. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Sirromet Winery, Glow Worms & Rainforest Skywalk
blocks.text: This day trip begins in the treetops with the Tamborine Rainforest Skywalk, where elevated paths take you through rainforest canopies, past waterfalls and lookout points. Then it’s lunch by the lake at Cedar Creek Estate, complete with a visit to a private glow worm cave. Wrap up the afternoon at Sirromet Winery, a local favorite known for award-winning wines and views that stretch across the hint

blocks.heading: Elite Collection: Mount Tamborine Rainforest Adventure
blocks.text: Go off the beaten path and into the highlands with a nature-first tour of Mount Tamborine. Enjoy a rainforest walk to a waterfall, explore the artisan shops of Gallery Walk and sample local wines. This is a day of quiet beauty and small discoveries (the perfect pairing to your cruise). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Brisbane City Debark Tour
blocks.text: See the city highlights before being delivered to the airport. Your guide will take you past heritage buildings, riverside parks and local landmarks (including Parliament House and City Hall). At Mt. Coot-tha, pause for a photo-worthy view that stretches from downtown to Moreton Bay. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Broome
blocks.text: Broome is where the desert meets the sea and immediately decides to throw a beach party. It’s a place where you can ride a camel past a multi-million dollar sunset, shop for pearls harvested by marine mollusks and then finish the day standing on red cliffs pretending you're in a tourism ad. It’s out there — geographically and vibe-wise — and that’s exactly why you’re going to love it.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Broome
blocks.text: This batch of excursions reads like the best group text thread ever — camels, crocs, dinosaur tracks, scenic flights and oysters that moonlight as jewelry boxes.

blocks.heading: Broome Best Beach Cruise
blocks.text: Hop a mini cruise and get all the Cable Beach lore — from undersea telegraph cables to camel-powered tourism empires — while you cruise, sip, snack and probably even learn a thing or two. The vibe is casual, the views are peak coastal glam and lunch includes drinks. Drinks always help the facts go down easier. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Broome
blocks.text: This one’s the sampler platter. Visit the Pearl Luggers Museum to see restored boats and hard-hat diving gear that looks like it belongs in a steampunk fever dream. Then it’s off to the Malcolm Douglas Crocodile Park, where massive, relocated salties stare you down like you owe them money. Gantheaume Point delivers high-drama cliffs and (if the tide’s right) dinosaur footprints, followed by a fina

blocks.heading: Horizontal Falls Explorer
blocks.text: If adrenaline had a bucket list, this would be near the top. A scenic flight takes you over the Horizontal Falls, one of those rare natural wonders that sounds like a geographical typo but is very real and wildly accurate. Throw in aerial views of the Buccaneer Archipelago, a stop at Cygnet Bay Pearl Farm (because pearls, obviously) and lunch in a remote spot that will make every picnic you have a

blocks.heading: Camel Rides on Cable Beach
blocks.text: It’s weird, it’s memorable and it’s oddly soothing — a 15-minute camel ride along Cable Beach where you get unbeatable views of sky, sea and the back of the camel in front of you. Each camel can carry two guests, which is adorable, and yes, there’s someone there to take your photo so you can prove this wasn’t just a bizarre sunstroke dream. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Willie Creek Pearl Farm
blocks.text: This is where pearl farming turns into a full-blown experience. Learn how oysters are seeded, take a boat ride out to the oyster beds and marvel at the Pinctada Maxima, a name that sounds like a Roman gladiator but is actually the kind of oyster responsible for those high-end Broome pearls. Finish in the showroom where it’s suddenly very easy to justify buying yourself a little something. LEARN MO

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Kaleidoscope of Broome
blocks.text: This is your local’s-eye-view of Broome: a little history, a lot of culture and a guided look at the Cygnet Bay Pearling Pioneers Exhibition. You'll hit Cable Beach, explore Broome’s multicultural cemeteries and spend extended time at the Broome Historical Museum (which is far more engaging than its humble exterior suggests). Spoiler: there's a lot more to this town than camels and clams. LEARN MO

blocks.heading: Things to do in Burnie
blocks.text: Strap in, ‘cause we’re heading to Burnie, Tasmania. We’re talking rugged coastlines, historic main streets, and an actual working seaport that still hauls freight (along with the occasional cruise ship). Here, you can taste scallops, sniff salty air, stroll art‑filled streets and maybe even question why you ever believed ‘big’ cities were worth your time. True to the Tasmanian spirit, this little

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Burnie
blocks.text: Small town; large list of potential options. Choose your pace — mellow coast drive, wildlife encounter or full‑on wilderness immersion.

blocks.heading: Devonport Highlights & Don River Railway
blocks.text: This one’s for the history buffs and nostalgia lovers. First, stop at the Devonport Maritime Museum where lighthouse history and nautical memorabilia await. Then visit Home Hill (the preserved home of former Aussie Prime Minister Joseph Lyons) for a rare peek into mid-20th century politics. Finally, hop aboard the Don River Railway for a ride on a vintage train along a scenic coastal route. LEARN

blocks.heading: Gunns Plains Caves & Wildlife
blocks.text: Head inland to Gunns Plains and descend deep into a limestone cave system discovered by accident in 1906. Yes, there are some steps, but also underground rivers, wild ribbon stalactites and a glowworm light show worth the cardio. After surfacing, the wild continues at Wing’s Wildlife Park where you can get face-to-fur with all manner of native and rescued animals. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Nature Lovers Tour
blocks.text: Start your morning at Fernglade Reserve, just minutes from port but worlds away in terms of atmosphere. This lush riverside pocket is one of the best places on Earth to spot wild platypus — if you're quiet, patient, and slightly lucky, one may drift by with zero regard for your excitement. Then it’s off to the Emu Valley Rhododendron Garden, where native bush meets global bloom. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Tasmanian Indulgence
blocks.text: Like chocolate and wine? You’re about to like it a whole lot more. Start at a local chocolate factory where rich, Belgian-style sweets are crafted with Tasmanian butter and cream (as if they needed help being better). After your sugar levels stabilize, head to Ghost Rock Vineyard, a boutique winery surrounded by rolling hills and salt air. You’ll get a behind-the-scenes look at their winemaking —

blocks.heading: Burnie & Surrounds
blocks.text: Hop aboard a motorcoach for a scenic spin through Burnie’s best, starting with a whisky tasting at Hellyers Road Distillery — because nothing says ‘good morning Tasmania’ like a dram of single malt. From there, you’ll cruise past the volcanic cliffs of Table Cape and wind through the coastal towns of Penguin and Ulverstone. You’ll finish with a visit to the Wonders of Wynyard — part info center, p

blocks.heading: Easy Burnie: Wings Wildlife Park & Countryside Drive
blocks.text: Ideal for those who want wildlife, scenery and a low-effort itinerary. You’ll drive through postcard farmland en route to Gunns Plains and the much-loved Wings Wildlife Park — home to Tasmanian devils, exotic reptiles and more amazing creatures than you can photograph in a single visit. On the return trip, you’ll swing by Penguin (the town and the statue) before heading back to port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Cairns
blocks.text: Cairns is a vibrant coastal city where the rainforest meets the reef, radiating a relaxed tropical energy and breathtaking natural beauty. Its warm climate, palm-lined esplanade and stunning ocean views make it a must-visit destination for anyone seeking the essence of Australia’s Far North.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Cairns
blocks.text: Shore excursions in Cairns invite travelers to immerse themselves in the region’s breathtaking scenery and vibrant culture. Whether exploring nearby wonders or simply soaking in the tropical atmosphere, every experience reflects the beauty and energy that make Cairns unforgettable.

blocks.heading: Wild River Tube Ride
blocks.text: Enjoy a half-day river tubing adventure through the stunning waterways of Queensland. After meeting your certified guide and getting a quick safety briefing, take a short walk to the river and step into your tube. Drift along calm waters and gentle rapids surrounded by lush rainforest—an authentic, unforgettable experience that combines relaxation with a touch of adventure. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Cairns: Skyrail, Kuranda & Scenic Railway
blocks.text: Soar above the rainforest canopy on the Skyrail Rainforest Cableway and take in stunning views of the Coral Sea and Green Island. Explore the charming Kuranda Village, filled with art galleries, local shops and cozy cafés. Then, ride the historic Kuranda Scenic Railway, winding past waterfalls, ravines and lush mountain landscapes in Barron Gorge National Park. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hartley’s Crocodile Adventure
blocks.text: Set at the foothills of the MacAlister Range, this 25-acre wildlife sanctuary is Northern Australia’s largest and most captivating wildlife attraction. Wander along eco-friendly boardwalks to spot koalas, cassowaries and crocs. The Gondwana Gateway offers a fascinating glimpse into Australia’s prehistoric past and the evolution of its remarkable native species. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kuranda & Skyrail Rainforest Cableway
blocks.text: Voted Australia’s Best Major Tourist Attraction, the award-winning Skyrail Rainforest Cableway offers a breathtaking journey above lush treetops and through the stunning Barron Gorge. Glide past cascading waterfalls and panoramic views before stopping at two mid-stations, where you can step into the heart of the rainforest and explore its natural beauty along scenic, winding walkways. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Gold Class Scenic Rail
blocks.text: Step aboard the historic Gold Class train and travel through North Queensland’s stunning landscapes in style. Originally built between 1886 and 1891, these beautifully restored red-wooden carriages combine Old World charm with modern comfort. Relax in plush lounge seating as you pass waterfalls, gorges and mountains—a truly elegant way to experience the region’s natural beauty. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Rainforestation, Army Duck & Wildlife
blocks.text: Journey into Australia’s World Heritage Rainforest at Rainforestation National Park, a 100-acre tropical paradise. Cruise through lush waterways on an amphibious Army Duck, meet koalas and kangaroos up close and discover Indigenous traditions through the award-winning Pamagirri Aboriginal Experience. Enjoy dance performances, cultural demonstrations and a classic Aussie BBQ lunch surrounded by the

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Cairns

As one of Queensland’s most captivating ports, it welcomes visitors with warm ocean breezes, lush landscapes, and a laid-back coastal charm. Cruises to Cairns promise unforgettable moments in Australia’s Far North.

blocks.text: Time to choose your adventure — these tours take you from sheep farms to Antarctic simulations to alpine high country and back to city‑scape.

blocks.heading: Waipara Wine Tasting
blocks.text: Waipara Valley is where the good stuff grows — Pinot Noir, Riesling and stories. You’ll journey north past wide plains and limestone hills, landing among boutique vineyards known for small batches and big flavor. Meet the winemakers, taste your way through three cellar doors and enjoy a platter lunch that turns into slow conversation. The easy going return ride is proof that good wine makes time s

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Town & Country – Canterbury Sheep Farm Experience
blocks.text: This half‑day tour captures the soul of Canterbury, from volcanic harbors to rolling farmland. The journey begins around Lyttelton Harbour before winding over Gebbies Pass to Manderley Farm, where Ross and Mary Millar welcome you like old friends. Watch the sheepdogs in action, then a live shearing that feels like part ballet, part wrestling match. Morning tea is served with local charm before you

blocks.heading: Easy Christchurch
blocks.text: This is your no‑stress, all‑access pass to Christchurch. Start with a drive up Evans Pass for sweeping views of Lyttelton Harbour and the ancient volcanic hills that frame it. Cruise along the coast to Sumner, a seaside suburb where the cafés face the water and the breeze is always on duty. Then it’s into the city, past the partially rebuilt Christchurch Cathedral, its cardboard stand‑in and the o

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Erewhon High‑country Station
blocks.text: If you’ve seen Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers, you’ve already glimpsed this place. That’s because Erewhon Station doubled as Edoras, the capital of Rohan. The road from Lyttelton leads across the Canterbury Plains and deep into the Southern Alps, where the real‑life magic kicks in. At the farm, Clydesdale horses still pull wagons, deer and merino sheep roam the hills and the landscape stretches

blocks.heading: Best of Christchurch: Airforce Wings & Antarctic Ice Adventure
blocks.text: First stop, the Royal New Zealand Air Force Museum! Then it’s off to the International Antarctic Centre, where the South Pole comes alive in wind tunnels, holograms and an honest‑to‑goodness penguin colony. Ride the Hagglund snow vehicle across simulated ice and feel the blast of an Antarctic storm. It’s half history, half science experiment, all unforgettable. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Waimakariri Jet Boat Experience
blocks.text: Strap in for a rush of river spray and pure speed. A short drive delivers you to the Waimakariri River Gorge, its silver channels twisting through pale Canterbury stone. Then your Hamilton jet boat takes over, skimming just inches above the water in heart‑racing spins and dashes. It’s a clean, wild thrill in one of the most beautiful corners of New Zealand. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Darwin
blocks.text: Darwin is a vibrant tropical city that perfectly captures the spirit of Australia’s Top End. With its striking coastal scenery, relaxed atmosphere and rich cultural heritage, it’s a must-visit destination that offers a unique blend of adventure and laid-back charm.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Darwin
blocks.text: Shore excursions in Darwin offer the perfect way to experience the city’s tropical allure and diverse landscapes. From its coastal beauty to its deep cultural roots, every adventure reveals a new dimension of this captivating destination.

blocks.heading: Darwin Pub & Craft Beer
blocks.text: The Precinct Tavern invites you to enjoy a guided craft beer experience. Stroll through the city with your guide before touring the tavern’s keg room and sampling four unique beers paired with canapés. Relax in the cool comfort of the bar, then return along Kitchener Bay or stay to explore the vibrant waterfront district at your leisure. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Jumping Crocodiles Cruise
blocks.text: Experience the thrill of seeing powerful saltwater crocodiles leap from the water during a guided cruise along the Adelaide River. As you journey past red gum trees, eucalyptus and fragrant saltbush, your expert guide reveals the park’s fascinating ecosystem. Keep your eyes peeled for wild buffalo, white-breasted sea eagles and other incredible wildlife along the way. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Iconic Darwin
blocks.text: Discover two of Darwin’s most fascinating attractions on this immersive excursion. Visit the Royal Flying Doctor Service Facility to explore interactive exhibits and step inside a decommissioned aircraft outfitted for airborne medical care. Then, journey to the Darwin Aviation Museum, home to historic aircraft, rare wartime footage and the iconic B-52 bomber—one of only three displayed outside the

blocks.heading: Darwin Jetski Tour
blocks.text: Cruise along Darwin’s stunning coastline at your own pace to soak in the scenery. Spot marine life, feed fish and race past the iconic Mindil Beach Casino before heading back to base. Afterward, relax with a complimentary drink at Bella Restaurant before heading back to the ship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Territory Wildlife Park
blocks.text: Set within 1,000 acres of pristine bushland, Territory Wildlife Park offers an immersive glimpse into Australia’s diverse habitats—from lush monsoon forests to sparkling wetlands. Wander the trails or hop aboard the open-air shuttle to encounter native wildlife up close, from wallabies to freshwater crocodiles and marvel at the vibrant marine life in the park’s walk-through aquarium. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Defence of Darwin
blocks.text: Step back in time and uncover Darwin’s rich wartime history with visits to the Darwin Military Museum and Charles Darwin National Park. Explore original WWII bunkers, immersive exhibits and historic fortifications while learning about the city’s pivotal role in Australia’s northern defense. Along the way, enjoy panoramic views and striking photo opportunities of Darwin’s harbor and wetlands. LEARN

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Dunedin
blocks.text: History, castles, wildlife, craft beer… Dunedin has it and is ready to share. Your ship’s docked, the city's buzzing and these tours know exactly where to take you.

blocks.heading: Best of Dunedin: The Taieri Gorge Train Tour
blocks.text: Ride a scenic train that snakes through tunnels and across wrought‑iron viaducts high above the Taieri River. This 19th‑century engineering marvel feels more dreamscape than railway, with plunging gorges and storybook valleys rolling by your window. Onboard commentary fills in gold‑rush history as you watch the South Island unfold. By the time you return to Dunedin’s ornate railway station, you’ll

blocks.heading: City Drive & Larnach Castle
blocks.text: Begin with a drive through Dunedin’s elegant streets, passing grand Victorian facades and The Octagon (the city’s quirky eight‑sided heart). Your guide spins tales of fortune hunters and architects as you head into the countryside toward Larnach Castle. Built in the 1870s by a politician with serious over‑compensation issues, it’s equal parts romance and ruin, with sweeping harbor views and a gard

blocks.heading: Otago Wildlife Cruise
blocks.text: Trade the streets for the sea on this harbor cruise that glides past volcanic headlands and lonely lighthouses. The Otago Peninsula is home to royal albatross, fur seals and blue penguins — and your captain knows where they hang out. You’ll understand why locals call this place the Wildlife Capital of New Zealand. Keep your binoculars ready — that ‘rock’ might be a sea lion taking a nap. LEARN MOR

blocks.heading: Albatross Cruise & Nature’s Wonders
blocks.text: Start with an albatross cruise past Taiaroa Head, where wingspans stretch wider than most cars. Then roll across a family‑run sheep farm in an 8‑wheel‑drive Argo, bouncing over ridges toward fur seals, sea lions and yellow‑eyed penguins. This tour is part wildlife safari, part off‑road rodeo — expect a few bumps and a lot to brag about to your friends back home. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Craft Dunedin
blocks.text: Follow your stomach through the city of gold rushes and great beer. Meet the makers behind small‑batch gin, artisan cheese and award‑winning chocolate while your guide dishes on Dunedin’s history — equal parts Scottish grit and student mischief. You’ll stroll cobbled lanes lined with Victorian architecture and experience taste sensations that will haunt you for years to come. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Nature’s Wonders
blocks.text: If your ideal souvenir involves seal interactions and penguin sightings, this is your calling. Journey along the coast to Nature’s Wonders, a conservation‑minded farm where off‑road Argos bump through fields of fur seals and sea lions lounging like retirees. The views over the Otago Peninsula are the kind that make you forever grateful that your phone has a built-in camera. It’s pure wild, done th

blocks.heading: Things to do in Eden
blocks.text: Perched on New South Wales’ Sapphire Coast, Eden is where wild beauty meets maritime history. Watch humpbacks breach across Twofold Bay, catch your breath at the panoramic view at Red Point Lookout, sample freshly shucked oysters straight from the estuaries and explore the town’s seafaring past along its rugged coastline.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Eden
blocks.text: Eden’s shore excursions uncover the best of Australia’s Sapphire Coast. Experience its history, wildlife and warm local hospitality with curated adventures designed to fit every pace.

blocks.heading: Capturing Eden - Photography Tour
blocks.text: Join a local photographer for a relaxed walking tour to Eden Lookout and nearby vantage points. Get hands-on guidance suited to your camera or smartphone, capture sweeping ocean views and end your morning with coffee by the pier to share favorite shots. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Legend of Old Tom - Eden's Killer Whale Trail
blocks.text: Trace the true story of Old Tom, the orca who partnered with whalers in Twofold Bay. Visit the Eden Killer Whale Museum and Boydtown’s Seahorse Inn, where the Thaua People once performed ceremonies honoring their “beowas,” or whale brothers, and enjoy morning tea by the beach before returning to your ship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Eden
blocks.text: Take in Eden’s beauty by coach with stops at Rotary Park lookout, Quarantine Bay and Boydtown’s historic Seahorse Inn. A local guide shares stories of early settlers and coastal landmarks as you enjoy photo opportunities across this charming port town. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cruising Twofold Bay
blocks.text: Relax aboard Cat Balou and cruise the calm waters of Twofold Bay surrounded by Ben Boyd National Park. Admire sights like Boyd’s Tower and Edrom Lodge, watch for dolphins and seals and learn about Eden’s storied whaling heritage as you drift past pristine beaches and forested shores. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Sea Wild Eden
blocks.text: Meet wombats, kangaroos and koalas at Potoroo Palace, then continue to Merimbula Wharf Aquarium to see sharks, seahorses and colorful reef fish. This half-day tour blends the Sapphire Coast’s natural beauty with a closer look at its remarkable wildlife. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Life On The Farm - Kameruka Estate
blocks.text: Step back into colonial Australia at Kameruka Estate, one of the oldest European settlements in the Bega Valley. Watch sheepdog and shearing demonstrations, visit the 1869 Holy Trinity Church and enjoy morning tea with the estate’s owner as you learn about its fascinating agricultural past. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Eden
blocks.text: Tucked between Beowa National Park and the deep waters of Twofold Bay, Eden offers a gateway to some of Australia’s most breathtaking coastal scenery. Many itineraries combine this charming town with destinations across Australia & New Zealand, offering a mix of adventure, coastal beauty and cultural discovery. blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Exmouth
blocks.text: Exmouth’s excursions reveal just how much beauty hides along Western Australia’s Coral Coast. From cruising coral gardens to exploring deep gorges and swimming with gentle giants, every adventure here brings you closer to the wild spirit of Ningaloo.

blocks.heading: Reef Snorkelling Tour
blocks.text: Sail from Exmouth Marina to explore two vibrant snorkel sites in the warm waters of the Indian Ocean. Between stops, enjoy lunch on board and watch for turtles, rays and colorful reef fish gliding beneath the surface. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Coral Viewer with Ningaloo Glass bottom Boat
blocks.text: Glide across the clear waters of Tantabiddi Beach aboard a glass-bottom boat and look directly into the coral gardens of Ningaloo Reef. Watch schools of tropical fish drift between vibrant bommies as your guide shares insights about this UNESCO World Heritage marine wonder. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Majestic Yardie Creek Gorge
blocks.text: Journey into Cape Range National Park to explore Yardie Creek Gorge, where sheer red cliffs rise above calm blue water. Learn about shipwrecks, and ancient landscapes before cruising to see black-flanked rock wallabies and nesting ospreys along the gorge walls. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Whale Shark Swim
blocks.text: Embark on a once-in-a-lifetime swim with the world’s largest fish. Cruise along Ningaloo Reef with expert guides who lead small groups into the water to meet these gentle giants up close. With calm seas and crystal visibility, this is the ultimate Exmouth experience. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ningaloo Whale Shark Swim on a Powerboat
blocks.text: Board a comfortable powerboat for a full-day adventure that begins with a guided snorkel among coral gardens. Once a spotter plane locates a whale shark, join your small group in the water for an extraordinary encounter before returning to a buffet lunch. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Snorkel Turquoise Bay
blocks.text: Slip into the turquoise shallows of Ningaloo Marine Park, where coral reefs lie just metres from shore. Snorkel among schools of tropical fish, enjoy morning tea on the beach and visit Vlaming Head Lighthouse for sweeping views across the Cape. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Hobart
blocks.text: Hobart serves up a brilliant blend of heritage and modern life, nestled between Mount Wellington and the River Derwent. Spend the morning sampling local flavors at the legendary Salamanca Market or trace colonial-era history in Battery Point’s winding lanes. Get a dose of natural beauty at the Royal Tasmanian Botanical Gardens or cruise off toward Tasmania’s dramatic coastlines.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Hobart
blocks.text: Don’t stress over planning—experience the best Hobart has to offer, stress-free, with Princess shore excursions. We’ll handle the details so you can relax and soak it all in.

blocks.heading: Uncorked: Coal Valley Wine Tour
blocks.text: Venture into Coal River Valley where boutique vineyards and slow‑crafted wines rule the day. Sample cool‑climate pours paired with Tasmanian cheese at a hillside estate, then sip your way through a family‑run cellar door that oozes character. Finish on a decadent note as handmade local chocolates meet their perfect wine match in one unforgettable tasting. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Bonorong Wildlife Sanctuary, Mt. Field Park & Curringa Farm
blocks.text: Get up close with Tasmanian devils, kangaroos and wombats at Bonorong Wildlife Sanctuary. Walk beneath towering tree ferns to see the stunning Russell Falls at Mt. Field National Park, then visit Curringa Farm for insights into sustainable farming and a chance to taste fresh farm produce. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Tasman Island Wildlife Cruise
blocks.text: Embark on a thrilling adventure along the Tasman Peninsula’s towering sea cliffs and hidden sea caves. Keep an eye out for fur seals, dolphins and albatrosses as you navigate the pristine waters surrounding Tasman Island. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Tempting Taste Trail to Richmond
blocks.text: Indulge your taste buds with a culinary tour through Tasmania’s finest offerings. Savor fresh oysters, wild abalone, handcrafted chocolates and local cheeses as you journey to Richmond, a historic village known for its convict-built bridge and charming Georgian architecture. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Bruny Island
blocks.text: Experience the unspoiled beauty of Bruny Island, known for its pristine beaches, dramatic cliffs and gourmet delights. Sample artisanal cheese and oysters, and take in breathtaking views from The Neck, a narrow strip of land connecting the island’s north and south ends. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Huon Valley & Tahune Airwalk
blocks.text: Glide through apple country and forest canopies on this day in Tasmania’s green heart. Cross the Huon River, breathe in the eucalyptus‑sweet air, then climb 120 feet into the treetops along the Tahune AirWalk. Pause for morning tea—sandwiches, cakes and strong Aussie coffee—before the return drive through rolling orchards and riverside hills. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Hobart
blocks.text: Hobart’s blend of historic charm and natural splendor makes it a standout departure point for adventures across the region. From its well-connected cruise terminal to the nearby attractions, every detail is designed to make your Australia cruise itinerary as seamless as it is unforgettable.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Kangaroo Island
blocks.text: Kangaroo Island stands out as one of Australia’s top travel destinations, where breathtaking landscapes meet abundant wildlife and coastal charm. From the iconic Remarkable Rocks and pristine beaches to encounters with kangaroos, koalas and sea lions, it’s a must-visit haven for nature lovers and adventure seekers.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Kangaroo Island
blocks.text: Shore excursions on Kangaroo Island invite visitors to immerse themselves in the island’s untamed beauty and tranquil atmosphere. From its rugged coastlines to its serene wildlife encounters, every experience leaves travelers with a deep sense of wonder and connection to nature.

blocks.heading: Seal Bay Boardwalk Express
blocks.text: Discover the best of Kangaroo Island on this memorable excursion. Stroll along the easy-access Seal Bay boardwalk for breathtaking views of Australian sea lions in their natural habitat. Then, visit the Emu Ridge Eucalyptus Distillery shop to explore local island products before stopping at Pennington Beach for a stunning photo opportunity on your way back to the pier. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Kangaroo Island
blocks.text: Experience the wild beauty of Kangaroo Island on a journey through its most breathtaking landscapes and encounters. Walk among a rare colony of sea lions at Seal Bay, savor a peaceful lunch surrounded by nature and explore Flinders Chase National Park’s iconic sights—including Admirals Arch and the Remarkable Rocks. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kangaroo Island Wildlife, Birds of Prey & Iconic Nature Sights
blocks.text: Experience the wild beauty of Kangaroo Island on this unforgettable adventure. Explore Flinders Chase National Park, home to the stunning Admirals Arch and the ancient Remarkable Rocks and spot koalas and fur seals in their natural habitat. Enjoy a relaxed lunch before meeting majestic birds of prey at the Raptor Domain, then end your day with scenic coastal views at Pennington Bay. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Tempting Tasting Trail
blocks.text: Embark on a flavorful journey through Kangaroo Island, sampling pure Ligurian honey and honeyed ice cream at Island Beehive before discovering the art of eucalyptus oil distilling at Emu Ridge. Enjoy cider tastings, lavender scones and local wines, all while taking in breathtaking views from Pennington Bay to Pelican Lagoon and glimpsing the island’s rich history at Reeves Point. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kangaroo Island Ocean Safari
blocks.text: Experience the thrill of Kangaroo Island’s coast on a 60-minute Ocean Safari RIB tour. Glide past stunning landmarks like Dolphin Cove and Snapper Point as you encounter dolphins, fur seals and sea lions in their natural habitat. With sea eagles soaring above and breathtaking coastal views all around, this adventure captures the island’s wild beauty from the best seat on the water. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ngarrindjeri Walk Kangaroo Island
blocks.text: Join a local guide on a cultural journey through Nurungaui to explore the rich heritage of the Ngarrindjeri people. As you walk, you’ll discover native bush foods and medicines, hear stories of resilience and trace the Ngarrindjeri journey from creation to the present day. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Kangaroo Island
blocks.text: Kangaroo Island is a must-visit stop on many Australia and New Zealand cruise itineraries, known for its breathtaking scenery and diverse wildlife. When your ship docks in Penneshaw, you’ll be greeted by rugged coastlines, pristine beaches and a warm island welcome.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Margaret River (Busselton)
Shore excursions to explore in Margaret River (Busselton)
blocks.text: Discover Margaret River’s stunning landscapes and flavors through unforgettable shore excursions, from wine tasting at renowned vineyards to exploring limestone caves and breathtaking coastal trails. Each adventure offers a true taste of this region’s natural beauty.

blocks.heading: Scenic Helicopter Flight to Lunch at Wills Domain
blocks.text: Soar above the stunning coastline of Geographe Bay on a scenic helicopter flight from Busselton Jetty to the award-winning Wills Domain Winery. Take in sweeping views of beaches, forests and vineyards before landing to savor world-class wines and exquisite cuisine. Then, enjoy a breathtaking return flight over the picturesque Margaret River region. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Geographe Bay
blocks.text: Experience the best of Western Australia on this four-hour journey from Busselton. Travel along the picturesque Geographe Bay coastline to the charming town of Dunsborough and the historic Cape Naturaliste Lighthouse. Explore the dramatic Canal Rocks, then venture inland through rolling vineyards to an award-winning winery, where you’ll enjoy tastings and time to relax amid stunning countryside vi

blocks.heading: Ngilgi Caves & Cape Naturaliste Lighthouse
blocks.text: Immerse yourself in the culture and natural wonders of Australia. Explore the legendary Ngilgi Cave, where ancient mythology and stunning limestone formations intertwine and visit the historic Cape Naturaliste Lighthouse for sweeping views of Geographe Bay. Along the way, experience the region’s breathtaking forests, coastal scenery and deep cultural roots. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Wines of Margaret River
blocks.text: Visit three of the region’s top wineries, meet passionate local winemakers and sample award-winning wines while surrounded by rolling vineyards and scenic countryside. It’s the ideal way to savor the charm and flavor of this Australian paradise. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Margaret River’s Sweet Tooth Trail

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Melbourne
blocks.text: Discover the best of Melbourne through a variety of shore excursions that highlight the city’s rich culture, scenic beauty, and lively atmosphere. From guided tours to immersive local experiences, there’s something for every traveler to enjoy.

blocks.heading: Easy Melbourne: City Drive
blocks.text: Designed for those who prefer minimal walking, this panoramic tour showcases Melbourne’s most iconic sights from the comfort of your coach. Enjoy a narrated drive past cultural landmarks and scenic suburbs, then take in breathtaking 360-degree views from the Melbourne Skydeck—the highest viewing platform in the Southern Hemisphere. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ballarat Wildlife & Sovereign Hill Goldmine Township
blocks.text: Take a scenic drive from Melbourne to Ballarat, where you’ll meet kangaroos, emus and Tasmanian devils at the wildlife park before stepping back in time at Sovereign Hill. This recreated 1850s gold-mining town lets you pan for gold, explore old mines, and experience life during Australia’s gold rush era. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Melbourne & Surrounds
blocks.text: On this full-day adventure you’ll explore the scenic heartland around Melbourne with a comfortable coach journey, sweeping coastal views, native wildlife encounters and a stop at a historic venue for lunch — all led by an expert local guide. Along the way you’ll learn about the region’s rich past, soak in natural landscapes and return to port with a deeper appreciation for this vibrant area. LEARN

blocks.heading: Healesville Sanctuary, Yara Valley & Wine
blocks.text: Venture beyond Melbourne to explore the scenic Dandenong Ranges and Yarra Valley. Enjoy time at Healesville Sanctuary to see native wildlife like kangaroos and koalas, then visit local wineries for guided tastings and a delicious lunch surrounded by beautiful vineyard views. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Puffing Billy & Dandenong Ranges
blocks.text: Set out from the wharf and travel east to the breathtaking Dandenong Ranges in a comfortable, air-conditioned coach. Stop at Grants on Sherbrooke to admire the colorful rosellas before boarding the historic Puffing Billy Steam Train. Enjoy a scenic ride through lush forests and fern gullies, then unwind with a traditional morning tea before returning to the pier. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Fitzroy Gardens & Yarra River Cruise
blocks.text: Experience Melbourne from a new perspective on a scenic Yarra River cruise and city tour. Cruise past landmarks like the Royal Botanic Gardens and Olympic Park, then explore the city’s historic and cultural highlights by motorcoach. Stroll through Fitzroy Gardens to see Captain Cook’s Cottage and visit the Shrine of Remembrance before returning to your ship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Napier
blocks.text: Napier is where wine country meets Art Deco flair, wrapped in golden‑beach sunshine and a hearty dose of Kiwi spirit. This eastern‑coast gem of New Zealand is famed for its Mediterranean‑style climate, and for the fact that it was almost entirely rebuilt in an Art Deco style after the devastating 1931 earthquake. Also, there’s a world-renown gannet colony that might just steal your heart (or at le

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Napier
blocks.text: Ready your sea legs, your appetite and your sense of adventure. These top tours take you on a direct course to architecture, wildlife, wine, history and beach‑side charm.

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Delicious Hawke’s Bay
blocks.text: Looking for something that can compete with the cruise buffet? We’ve got you covered. Start your tastebuds engine with specialty honey at the Arataki Honey Centre, cruise through orchard country to Silky Oaks Chocolate Company for handmade treats and complete the loop with local produce that might make you weep. Sweet, scenic, seamless and definitely worth spoiling your dinner for. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Napier: Hawke’s Bay Express
blocks.text: Board the custom‑designed Hawke’s Bay Express — think velvet‑covered seats, tall opening windows and a bell (you know, cause it’s a train!). You’ll cruise Marine Parade, chug past elegant Art Deco façades, catch a view from Bluff Hill overlooking the port and end among hundreds of waterbirds at the estuary of Ahuriri. Comfortable for guests with limited mobility, this one’s a stylish intro to Napi

blocks.heading: Mohaka River Raft Float Trip
blocks.text: Trade city elegance to river chill as you float down the Mohaka River on a Grade 2 rafting adventure. Navigate mild rapids, dip into whirlpools, glide through canyon scenery and end with a light lunch before heading back to the ship. It’s ideal for families or anyone who wants a nature fix with just enough thrill to keep the heart rate up. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ultimate Napier: Cape Kidnappers Offroad Safari
blocks.text: Ready to switch gears? Heat up the excitement with an offroad safari to Cape Kidnappers. Traversing farmers’ land, rugged gullies and riverbeds, you’ll arrive at a cliff‑top vantage to watch tens of thousands of gannets scream, soar and settle in to nest. blocks.heading: Hawke’s Bay Wine Country
blocks.text: Drive through the lush Tukituki River Valley toward boutique wineries set among the rolling hills. At two selected estates you’ll sample wines paired with cheese and soak in uniquely inspiring vineyard landscapes. Later, enjoy a scenic drive through the charming town of Hastings (known for its Spanish Mission and Art Deco architecture) before returning to Napier. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Napier City Drive & Aquarium
blocks.text: Start with a drive through Napier’s Art Deco architecture — the bold, geometric silver lining that came after the city’s 1931 shake-up. Then hop off and stroll Marine Parade to see sunken gardens, seaside sculptures and perfectly pruned hedges giving off big ‘municipal pride’ energy. blocks.text: Your ship pulls into Napier’s port and your day begins with sand, sea and city. blocks.text: This breezy coach tour cruises through town and out to scenic lookouts, with close-ups of the Te Rewa Rewa Bridge, the iconic Wind Wand and Mount Taranaki posing dramatically in the background. You’ll roll past the Bowl of Brooklands (concerts! ducks!) and the modernist marvel of the Govett-Brewster Art Gallery without leaving your seat. blocks.heading: Ultimate New Plymouth: Sugar Loaf Island Tour
blocks.text: Hop into a vintage English lifeboat and cruise past the jagged sea stacks of the Sugar Loaf Islands (the eroded leftovers of a very temperamental volcano). This protected marine park is just offshore, but it feels like a whole different planet. You might spot seals, dolphins or even whales doing their thing. Along the way, you’ll also cruise by the iconic Wind Wand, wobbling like a weird little gu

blocks.text: Settle in for a lush ride through Taranaki farmland, stopping first at a private garden where local green thumbs lead you through native and exotic plants with friendly enthusiasm. blocks.heading: Things to do in Newcastle
blocks.text: Newcastle, Australia — not to be confused with its more overcast UK cousin — is where convict history, coal industry roots and a thumping food-and-drink scene all live in unexpected harmony. This east coast gem delivers historic grit with a sea breeze, surf breaks next to cathedrals and wine-country day trips that are somehow both chill and fabulous. From beaches to battlements to buttery Hunter V

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Newcastle
blocks.text: From quad bikes on dunes to seafood on foot, these curated excursions deliver the best that Newcastle has to offer. Whether you’re a wine snob, a sand addict or someone who just really likes dolphins, there’s something here with your name on it.

blocks.heading: Eat Newy - Newcastle Walking Food Tour
blocks.text: Who needs a ride when you’ve got bites? This guided food crawl delivers a nonstop lineup of Newcastle flavor: golden crab doughnuts, local oysters, fancy scallops and beer-paired desserts (yep, that’s a thing). You’ll eat, learn, laugh and gelato your way through the streets, laneways and culinary oddities of a city that swapped steel mills for street eats — and never looked back. Bring your appet

blocks.heading: Best of Newcastle
blocks.text: Take a time-warp through Newcastle’s convict-era streets, from the Lock Up to Customs House and beyond. You’ll swing past coastal icons like Christ Church Cathedral and the Ocean Baths before stepping into Fort Scratchley — the only Aussie fort to clap back during WWII. Wrap it up with free time at the Newcastle Museum. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Port Stephens Dolphin Watching Cruise
blocks.text: This one's part nature tour, part splash zone. Set sail from Nelson Bay into the Dolphin Capital of Eastern Australia, where 165+ bottlenose dolphins might just photobomb your selfie. The real kicker? A waterslide and boom net for those who want to end the cruise soaked and grinning. Afterward, stick around the harbor for waterfront bites, quirky shops or just a recharge in the sun. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Quad Bike Sand Dune Adventure
blocks.text: Mount up and roll out — these aren’t your backyard sandboxes. You’ll conquer the mighty Worimi Sand Dunes (the tallest in the Southern Hemisphere) on a quad bike built for all thrill levels. It’s part adrenaline rush, part cultural insight as guides share the land’s story. Don’t forget to bring the essentials: enclosed shoes, shades and a strong grip. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hunter Valley Food & Wine Trail
blocks.text: This is what the phrase “treat yourself” was made for. Wander the rolling vineyards of Hunter Valley, one of Australia's most award-dripping wine regions, sipping your way through chardonnay, shiraz and whatever else they hand you. You’ll also snack on local cheese, chocolates and brews, then enjoy a long lunch with vineyard views that may or may not cause spontaneous sighing. Gourmet hedonism at

blocks.heading: Coastal Discovery Tour
blocks.text: Climb aboard a small-group vessel for a maritime-meets-nature deep dive. Cruise out into the Pacific, past rugged cliffs and dramatic headlands. Expect tales of shipwrecks, seabirds and salt air, with seasonal dolphins or whales as possible bonus guests. It’s the kind of boat ride where history and scenery high-five and do a little dance. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Perth (Fremantle)
blocks.text: Perth (Fremantle) offers a perfect mix of laid-back coastal charm and vibrant city life. From exploring local markets and beaches to discovering rich maritime history and modern art, there’s plenty to see and do for every type of traveler.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Perth (Fremantle)
blocks.text: Discover the best of Perth and Fremantle with shore excursions that showcase the region’s stunning beaches, rich heritage and relaxed lifestyle. From scenic drives to cultural tours, each experience offers a unique glimpse into Western Australia’s coastal beauty.

blocks.heading: West Coast Wineries
blocks.text: Journey through Western Australia’s oldest wine region, the picturesque Swan Valley. Visit two local vineyards for guided tastings led by expert winemakers who share their stories and passion for the craft. Enjoy views of lush vineyards and the winding Swan River, then browse the winery shops for wine-inspired souvenirs and locally made specialties. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Perth & Fremantle
blocks.text: Discover the highlights of Fremantle and Perth on a full-day guided tour. Enjoy a scenic drive past historic landmarks before heading to Perth for free time to explore the city’s shops, cafés and attractions. Conclude your day with a relaxing Swan River cruise back to Fremantle, taking in waterfront views and sights like King’s Park and Millionaire’s Row. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Caversham Wildlife Park & River Cruise
blocks.text: Journey through Swan Valley to Caversham Wildlife Park, where you can see native Australian animals like koalas and kangaroos up close. After exploring the park’s lush grounds, enjoy a brief city tour of Perth before boarding a comfortable riverboat for a relaxing 75-minute cruise along the Swan River, passing elegant homes and tranquil bird sanctuaries. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Dolphins & Sea Lions Oh My!
blocks.text: Discover the vibrant marine life of Rockingham, where the coast truly comes alive. Cruise through Shoalwater Bay to meet wild dolphins, watch sea lions and pelicans and learn about the area’s unique ecosystem. Then, explore the pristine beaches and clear waters of Penguin Island before returning to the mainland for a relaxing lunch in Rockingham. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Fremantle & Kings Park
blocks.text: Discover the beauty and charm of Perth on a scenic drive along the Swan River. Travel through exclusive riverside suburbs and admire stunning city views from Kings Park, a lush sanctuary filled with native flora and birdlife. Enjoy free time to explore before visiting the iconic Cottesloe Beach, where white sands and turquoise waters capture Perth’s relaxed coastal spirit. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Debark Tour - Perth City Drive
blocks.text: Experience the best of Perth and Fremantle on a half-day guided tour filled with history, scenery and charm. Travel past historic landmarks, beautiful beaches and elegant riverside neighborhoods before arriving at Kings Park, a breathtaking natural haven featuring native plants, local wildlife and sweeping views of the city skyline. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Perth (Fremantle)
blocks.text: Perth (Fremantle) is a highlight on many Australia and New Zealand cruise itineraries, offering the perfect mix of city energy and coastal charm. Stroll along lively waterfronts, enjoy fresh local cuisine or venture into nearby wine country for a taste of Western Australia’s best. This inviting port is an ideal stop for travelers seeking both relaxation and discovery.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Picton
blocks.text: Shore excursions in Picton invite you to experience the region’s stunning natural beauty and welcoming local culture. From peaceful coastal views to charming nearby towns, every excursion reveals the relaxed elegance that makes Picton unforgettable.

blocks.heading: Best of Picton: Scenic Cruising on Queen Charlotte Sounds
blocks.text: Set sail on a 2.5-hour catamaran cruise through the peaceful waters of Queen Charlotte Sound. Glide past rugged coastlines and lush forests as your captain shares stories of the region’s rich history. Enjoy light refreshments, stunning views and a stop at Double Cove to feed the famous pet fish. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Knights of the Sky: The Omaka Aviation Heritage Museum
blocks.text: Step back in time at the Omaka Aviation Heritage Centre, where lifelike WWI displays showcase authentic aircraft and replicas from Peter Jackson’s private collection. Enjoy a scenic drive to Blenheim and a relaxing miniature railway ride along the Taylor River before ending your day at the Makana Chocolate Factory, watching fine chocolates being made and sampling sweet treats before returning to p

blocks.heading: Marlborough Farm, Garden, & Sheep Round Up
blocks.text: Spend a delightful day surrounded by Marlborough’s natural beauty as you explore Woodend Gardens & Vineyard and the picturesque Winterhome farm. Wander through vibrant gardens, enjoy a sheepdog demonstration on a coastal farm and savor a fresh, locally inspired lunch at The Store café. This full-day experience captures the serene charm and rural elegance of New Zealand’s wine and garden province.

blocks.heading: Scenic Sounds Cruise & Mistletoe Bay Walk
blocks.text: Begin with a short shuttle ride to Picton Marina, then cruise through the serene bays and coves of the Marlborough region. Upon arrival at the Queen Charlotte Track, follow your expert guide along a scenic trail shaded by native bush and towering ferns. Enjoy panoramic coastal views and the tranquil beauty of one of New Zealand’s most celebrated walking paths. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Guided Bike Wine Tour & Lunch
blocks.text: Experience the Marlborough wine region in a uniquely active way on this leisurely cycling tour. Begin with a tasting at Vines Village before pedaling through scenic vineyards to two boutique wineries. Along the way, learn about local varieties and enjoy samples of Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Gris, Chardonnay and Pinot Noir, capped off with a delicious lunch paired with regional wines. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Queen Charlotte Sound by Sea Kayak
blocks.text: Discover the beauty of Queen Charlotte Sound on a guided kayaking excursion from Ngakuta Bay. Glide through calm, turquoise waters surrounded by rugged coastlines, hidden coves and sandy beaches. The area alive with seals, seabirds and playful blue penguins. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Port Arthur
Shore excursions to explore in Port Arthur
blocks.text: Choose your thrill level: historic convicts, beautiful sea caves, delectable wine tastings or the chance to meet living devils (of the marsupial kind). Each Princess Cruises excursion brings you closer to Tasmania’s wild beauty and even-more-wild history.

blocks.heading: Port Arthur Behind the Bars Walking Tour
blocks.text: Step through the gates of Australia’s most infamous penal colony and straight into the 1800s. This walking tour goes deep into convict-built cell blocks, solitary pens and the commandant’s quarters, all while your guide serves up gritty stories and the occasional gasp-worthy fact. It’s one part history, one part ghost story and 100% fascinating. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Eco Boat Adventure
blocks.text: Climb into a RIB (Rigid Inflatable Boat) and blast off into Tasmania’s wildest coast. You’ll hug towering cliffs, pluck your jaw up from the deck when you spot aquatic life and stare a lighthouse in the face on Tasma Island. One minute you’re listening to history, the next you’re in ocean spray — adventure served cold and intense. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Tasmanian Devil Unzoo
blocks.text: Brace yourself: these devils are basically the rock stars of marsupials. You’ll zoom up the Tasman Peninsula, encounter devils crunching bones with surprising gusto, hand‑feed kangaroos and sample chocolates that pair outrageously well with pure wilderness views. You’ll be able to say you tasted Tasmania’s wild side… and it tasted like chocolate. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Geological Panoramas of the Peninsula
blocks.text: This is ‘nature’s sculptor went wild’ kind of terrain. You’ll gaze at Tasman Arch (stone bridge cut by waves), Devil’s Kitchen (a sea‑engineered chasm) and the Tessellated Pavement (rock tiles that look weirdly deliberate). Sprinkled among these are accounts of the colony’s unwilling convict residents, narrow escape routes and Eaglehawk Neck (a razor‑thin strip once guarded by dogs and soldiers).

blocks.heading: Tasman Food & Wine
blocks.text: This is Tasmania served three ways: ocean air, wild landscapes and cool-climate wine. Kick things off with lavender scones and tea at a farm where everything smells like spa day. Then it’s off to a hilltop vineyard overlooking Blackman Bay, where oysters meet their soulmate (a glass of award-winning wine). Throw in coastal views, Port Arthur lore and enough fresh air to reset your brain. This is t

blocks.heading: Remarkable Caves, Lavender Farm & Wine Tasting
blocks.text: If your bucket list says ‘natural wonders and snacks,’ this tour says ‘same.’ Roam lavender fields like a fancy bee, snack at the Chocolate Foundry (quality control, obviously), sip local wines right where they’re made and finish at the Remarkable Caves — which are as dramatic as they sound. It’s a half-day that fully delivers. LEARN MORE

This former gold rush town (population boom, bust, repeat) is now the kind of place where you can spend your morning scaling treetops, your afternoon face-to-fin with a parrotfish and your evening sipping something tropical while staring at Four Mile Beach wondering what would happen if you just decided to stay foreve

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Port Douglas
blocks.text: Go reef-deep, sky-high or anywhere in between. These excursions are the ultimate choose-your-own-Aussie-adventure.

blocks.heading: Tropical Highlights & Crocodile Cruise
blocks.text: Daintree, crocs, coastlines, boardwalks and beaches — it’s a greatest hits album of Port Douglas wrapped into one. You’ll roll north by coach, glide through mangroves on a croc-spotting cruise (don’t stick your hand out too far), eat like a local and then walk where the rainforest and reef literally high-five. It ends with a jungle hike straight out of a travel show. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Port Douglas: The Great Barrier Reef
blocks.text: Board a catamaran that’s part tropical transporter, part marine biology classroom and full-blown sun deck situation. Cruise across open sea to the outer Great Barrier Reef, where three hours of snorkeling, fish-ogling and optional scuba/floating helmet madness await. Don’t want to get wet? There’s a semi-submersible coral safari that keeps you dry while your eyeballs do the swimming. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Daintree Discovery Centre
blocks.text: Hop a ferry, channel your inner Attenborough and step into the world’s oldest rainforest (the Daintree’s been around since before dinosaurs were cool). You’ll wander aerial walkways, climb a tower to canopy level and get a whole new appreciation for plants that predate your species. Pro tip: Don’t skip the insect repellent. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Sail to Beautiful Low Isles
blocks.text: ‘Wavedancer’ may sound like a My Little Poney, but it’s actually your ride to a coral cay that’s practically designed for daydreams. Snorkel alongside sea turtles, drift on a glass-bottom boat or just live your best lounging life under sun shades. Post-flood, the coral’s bouncing back, and the fish and turtles never left. Nature knows how to throw a comeback tour. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Barramundi Farm Paddock to Plate
blocks.text: If you’ve ever looked at a barramundi fish and thought, “I want to meet you, catch you, and then eat you,” this tour is your culinary spirit quest. Tour the farm, feed some future entrées and try your luck at catching one. Then chow down on a gourmet tasting platter that just might make you weep into your sashimi. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Northern Delights Tour
blocks.text: Start with a rainforest-framed bus ride so scenic it feels like you’re in a tourism ad. Cruise the Daintree River, hunting for crocs and birdlife, then lunch under the trees with chirpy feathered freeloaders who are more interested in your meal than they should be. Wrap things up at Mossman Gorge with a swim in waters so clear you’ll think shoulder deep in liquid glass.. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Port Douglas
blocks.text: This one’s an anchorage port, which means your day begins with a breezy ride via tender boat to shore — think of it as a mini excursion before the real fun begins. From there, it’s an easy launchpad to Four Mile Beach, café corners, reef tours and rainforest rendezvous. blocks.heading: Things to do in Port Lincoln
Shore excursions to explore in Port Lincoln
blocks.text: From coastal drives and heritage tours to hands-on seafood adventures, Port Lincoln’s excursions capture the best of South Australia’s Eyre Peninsula. With all kinds of shopping, galleries and local hotspots, you’ll never be bored during your cruise to Port Lincoln.

blocks.heading: Coffin Bay Oyster Farm Tour
blocks.text: Cruise the clear waters of Coffin Bay to visit one of Australia’s most famous oyster farms. Wade among the beds in provided waders, learn how oysters are grown and harvested, and taste them fresh from the shell paired with local beverages before heading back toward Port Lincoln. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Port Lincoln
blocks.text: Get to know Port Lincoln on a relaxed sightseeing drive showcasing the town’s highlights. Visit Winters Hill Lookout for sweeping views over Boston Bay, explore the marina that houses the country’s largest fishing fleet and hear stories of how this seaside town became Australia’s seafood capital. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Port Lincoln Seafood Story
blocks.text: Taste your way through Port Lincoln’s maritime legacy with a tour that dives deep into its fishing heritage. Visit the Axel Stenross Maritime Museum, meet the local fleet at the marina, and step inside a working seafood factory to sample smoked fish, pickled delicacies and freshly caught King George whiting. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Journey on Eyre
blocks.text: Travel through the dramatic landscapes of the Eyre Peninsula, from tranquil Big Swamp and the Marble Ranges to the white sands of Farm Beach. Visit the Dutton Bay Heritage Woolshed Museum for a look into South Australia’s farming history, then pause at Winters Hill Lookout for photo-worthy coastal views. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Rugged Coastline Discovery
blocks.text: You can also experience the Eyre Peninsula’s wild side on a scenic drive from Winters Hill to Fishery Bay, Cape Wiles and Cape Carnot. Watch waves crash against ancient cliffs, search for fur seals basking on the rocks and capture the dramatic beauty of Theakstone Crevasse before returning to port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Wine and Wildlife
blocks.text: Combine wine tasting with close encounters at Glen Forest Tourist Park & Vineyard, home to koalas, kangaroos, emus and native birds. Sample locally produced wines paired with cheese and biscuits before a scenic drive back toward the coast. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Sydney
blocks.text: These excursions are designed to help you connect the dots, from coastal walks and historic sites to bushland wildlife and multicultural markets. Sydney offers a wide range of day trips that let you explore at your own pace or dive deep into the local stories that shape the city.

blocks.heading: Hop On Hop Off Sydney – Discover 1 Day – In Transit
blocks.text: This hop-on, hop-off bus tour gives you access to Sydney’s biggest attractions on two flexible loops: one focused on downtown and the other on coastal highlights like Bondi. Visit the Opera House, explore Chinatown or stop for seafood in Darling Harbour. You decide where to pause and where to keep rolling, all with onboard commentary to fill in the background as you go. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Discover the Blue Mountains
blocks.text: Travel west to the Blue Mountains, where sandstone cliffs rise above forested valleys and waterfalls drop into deep canyons. Ride the Scenic Cableway for views of the Jamison Valley and its famous Three Sisters rock formation. On the way, visit Featherdale Wildlife Park to meet kangaroos, wallabies and other native species up close. Enjoy a two-course lunch at a hilltop restaurant overlooking the

blocks.heading: Manly & North Sydney Sights
blocks.text: After crossing the Harbour Bridge, your route takes you through upscale suburbs and out to the coast. Stop at North Head for wide-angle views of the harbor before heading to Manly Beach for cafes, shops and local surf culture. You’ll have time to walk, relax or grab a coffee before returning along the scenic northern route. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Sydney – Sydney Sights & Bondi Beach
blocks.text: Start in The Rocks (Sydney’s original neighborhood), where colonial buildings now house pubs, galleries and shops. Drive past Hyde Park, the Botanical Gardens and historic neighborhoods before stopping at Mrs. Macquarie’s Chair for panoramic harbor views. Finish with free time at Bondi Beach, home to lifeguard legends, shoreline cafes and some of the city’s best people-watching. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Sydney Food Tour
blocks.text: Follow your guide through Sydney’s Inner West, where global cultures converge in the most delicious ways. Sample Vietnamese pork rolls, house-made cheeses, kangaroo salami and small-batch gelato. Meet the families and producers behind each stop and learn how local ingredients and international roots have shaped this part of the city into a true culinary hub. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Sydney by Private Vehicle – Car Class Half-Day (With Guide)
blocks.text: Prefer to chart your own course? This private vehicle option includes a local guide and flexible route planning. Explore the sites that interest you most without the structure of a group itinerary. It’s ideal for small families, small groups or anyone looking to make the most of a shorter stay. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Tauranga
blocks.text: Time to pick your path. Whether you crave volcanoes, vineyards, history or high speed (or hobbits), Tauranga delivers all with a twist.

blocks.heading: Rangitaiki Rafting Adventure
blocks.text: If you’re up for something splashy and bold, the Rangitaiki River Grade 3–4 white‑water rafting tour is the obvious choice. You’ll skill‑up with paddle training, navigate rapids and then float through native forest and plantation scenery. Note: this one’s not for the faint of heart. On the other hand, it’s probably the most efficient way to prove just how ‘not faint of heart’ you are. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best Of Rotorua: Te Puia Geyser & Maori Arts
blocks.text: Your coach ride whisks you through coastal scenery toward Rotorua where the renowned Te Puia reserve awaits. You’ll witness the legendary Pohutu geyser erupt, wander through boiling mud pools and listen to the stories of master carvers and weavers at the Māori Arts & Crafts Institute. After lunch and a spirited cultural performance filled with haka and hand games, you’ll head back with a whole new

blocks.heading: Elms and Orchards: Stories of Tauranga
blocks.text: Start with a drive past the bay toward the historic Elms Mission Station (1835) and step into a slice of early colonial‑Māori encounter. Then stroll through kiwi orchards where vines hum with harvest energy and stop for local refreshment amid orchard life. Finish your loop with a look at the impressive Māori war canoe along the coast before the ship docks again. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Rotorua & Polynesian Spa Experience
blocks.text: This full‑day outing serves up big vistas and bubbling springs. After a scenic drive to Rotorua you’ll explore geothermal valleys, watch sculptors at work and enjoy a Māori‑inspired lunch at the marae. Then it’s off to the renowned Polynesian Spa for a soak in hot‑spring pools that stare right at the lake. On the way back you’ll roll through kiwifruit country. Yum. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Movie Set
blocks.text: Board your motorcoach and travel toward Matamata where the famous film set of Hobbiton awaits. Wander through Hobbit holes, cross the restored bridge and stop by the Green Dragon Inn for a drink. It’s a light‑hearted excursion that pairs lush farmland with movie history and magic. Don’t forget to treat yourself to ‘second breakfast’ before you get started. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: National Kiwi Hatchery & Agrodome
blocks.text: Meet New Zealand’s adorable feathered national symbol at the hatchery. These adorable wonders of evolution look like a mix between a mole and a chicken that lost a bet… and they own it. After some quality time with the coolest birds you’ll probably ever meet, enjoy a guided farm tour at the Agrodome and feast on a hearty lunch. This tour blends wildlife, wool and rural flair in a way only the Kiwi

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Timaru
blocks.text: Timaru’s excursions reveal the scenic heart of South Canterbury — from ancient Māori art and dramatic coastlines to high-country sheep stations and warm country hospitality. Each one captures a different side of New Zealand’s South Island, combining history, nature and genuine local connection.

blocks.heading: The Ancient Heart of Waitaki
blocks.text: Explore the Whitestone UNESCO Global Geopark, where fossils, limestone formations and Māori rock art reveal the layers of New Zealand’s natural history. Walk among the surreal Elephant Rocks, visit a whale fossil site and enjoy a locally inspired lunch in the Waitaki Valley. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Oamaru and Moeraki Boulders
blocks.text: Travel south along the coast to Oamaru, known for its limestone architecture and Victorian allure, before visiting the famed Moeraki Boulders scattered along Koekohe Beach. These perfectly spherical stones — formed over millions of years — make for some of the most photographed scenes in New Zealand. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Road to Mesopotamia
blocks.text: Venture deep into the Southern Alps to Mesopotamia Station, one of New Zealand’s most historic sheep farms. Journey through Peel Forest and the Rangitata Valley, stop for tea with local farmers and enjoy sweeping alpine views featured in The Lord of the Rings films — a true glimpse of high-country life. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Maori Rock Art
blocks.text: Discover the ancient artistry of New Zealand’s first people at the Te Ana Māori Rock Art Centre. Learn the stories behind centuries-old drawings from Ngāi Tahu guides, then visit original limestone cave sites in Opihi, a rare window into Aotearoa’s early history and enduring cultural traditions. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Lake Heron Station
blocks.text: Meet the Todhunter family at Lake Heron Station, a 50,000-acre merino wool farm that has been part of the region’s fabric for over a century. Tour the woolshed, learn about sustainable farming and enjoy a home-cooked lunch surrounded by panoramic alpine scenery. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Harlau House Southern Hospitality
blocks.text: Step into a beautifully restored 19th-century estate for morning or afternoon tea at Harlau House. Hear the story of this heritage property from its owner, taste regional delicacies like Harlau Cheese Puffs and explore the manicured gardens before a scenic stop at Blacketts Lighthouse. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Townsville
blocks.text: Experience the best of North Queensland with unforgettable shore excursions in Townsville. Whether you’re seeking adventure, relaxation, or local culture, each outing reveals a new side of this vibrant coastal destination.

blocks.heading: Magnetic Island Heli Flight
blocks.text: Take to the skies for an unforgettable aerial adventure over Townsville. After a brief transfer and safety briefing, soar above the turquoise waters of the Coral Sea, circling Magnetic Island’s rugged cliffs and rainforest-covered peaks. As you return, enjoy sweeping views of the city, Castle Hill and the Strand. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Townsville City Explorer
blocks.text: Take in the best of Townsville on a scenic tour through the city’s vibrant center and historic Flinders Street before ascending Mount Stuart for breathtaking views of the city and coastline. Continue along The Strand, where you’ll pass The Ville Townsville Hotel & Casino, the Entertainment Centre and the bustling marina. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: City Drive & Billabong Sanctuary
blocks.text: Discover the natural beauty and wildlife of Townsville on this exciting half-day adventure. Enjoy a narrated drive showcasing historic Flinders Street, The Strand, and breathtaking views from Mount Stuart before visiting the renowned Billabong Sanctuary. Get up close to native animals, from cuddly koalas to free-roaming kangaroos and experience engaging wildlife shows for an unforgettable glimpse

blocks.heading: World Heritage Rainforest Tour
blocks.text: Journey into the heart of the World Heritage Wet Tropics Rainforest, the oldest surviving rainforest on Earth. Travel through lush pineapple and sugarcane fields with your expert local guide, stopping to admire cascading waterfalls and sweeping mountain views from McLelland Lookout. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Magnetic Island
blocks.text: Discover the natural beauty of Magnetic Island on a guided adventure through lush National Park landscapes and secluded beaches. Visit Bungalow Bay Koala Village to meet Australia’s most iconic wildlife and even hold a koala for a memorable photo. This unforgettable experience blends breathtaking scenery, native wildlife encounters and a touch of island serenity. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Wellington
blocks.text: What’s your vibe? Hill climbs, wine time, forest rambles or a bit of movie magic — these curated tours serve it all up, no worries.

blocks.heading: Wineries of Wairarapa
blocks.text: Cross the Remutaka Ranges, arrive in historic Greytown with its wooden Victorian buildings, then head into Martinborough’s village charm and family‑run vineyards. Two wine‑tastings, local chocolate studio and a leisurely lunch make this one for guests who like sipping and tasting while they take it all in. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Shenandoah – A Unique Kiwi Experience
blocks.text: Travel 20 minutes outside the city to a working farm within a native bird‑life reserve overlooking the inlet. Meet Simon, your Kiwi host, tour his private museum filled with vintage motorcycles and artifacts, wander formal gardens and bird‑rich zones, then enjoy tea with local treats. You’ll come back to port with countryside cred and a deeper sense of place. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Full Day Lord of the Rings Film Locations & Weta Workshop
blocks.text: Journey through the Wellington/Wairarapa region along filming trails of Hobbits, elves and wizards, visit the Weta Workshop where cinematic magic is made, then stand atop Mt Victoria Lookout for sweeping harbour views. Whether you’re a Tolkien/Peter Jackson fanatic or you just like cool movie sets, this tour delivers with legends and landscapes. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Seal Coast Safari
blocks.text: Jump into a 4WD Mercedes, climb up to dramatic cliff‑tops near Cook Strait, peer down across fault lines and valleys and finally arrive at a rocky beach (home to New Zealand fur seals lounging, playing and diving off ledges). Nature, raw and real, from Wellington’s wild side. You can’t take the seals home back with you, but photos are free game. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ultimate Wellington: The Storm Coast Drive
blocks.text: Settle into a motorcoach and ride along rugged coast, visit a private sheep‑station farm where dogs hustle sheep and shearing happens fast, then soak in views across the strait to snow‑tipped mountains. It’s less ‘city walk’ more ‘coastline reveal’ with wind‑blasted beauty and sheepdogs. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Zealandia Eco Reserve & Otari Wilton Bush
blocks.text: Just minutes from downtown Wellington you’ll enter the predator‑fenced valley of Zealandia, home to rare kiwi, tuatara and giant wetas. Then stroll the canopy walkway at Otari‑Wilton’s native‑plant garden, seeing New Zealand’s flora like you never imagined it could be. Earthy, tranquil and oddly moving. LEARN MORE
