blocks.heading: Things to do in Yorkeys Knob (Cairns)
blocks.text: Yorkeys Knob is a tropical paradise where lush rainforests meet the sparkling Coral Sea. Spend your day snorkeling the Great Barrier Reef, lounging on golden beaches or savoring fresh local cuisine—all with breathtaking ocean views that capture the very best of Far North Queensland.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Yorkeys Knob (Cairns)
blocks.text: Experience the best of tropical Queensland with shore excursions from Yorkeys Knob (Cairns), where adventure, relaxation and natural beauty come together. Each journey offers a chance to immerse yourself in the region’s lush landscapes, vibrant culture and breathtaking coastal views.

blocks.heading: Hartley's Crocodile Adventure
blocks.text: Get up close to Australia’s incredible wildlife at Hartley’s Crocodile Adventures. Stroll along elevated boardwalks through lush habitats, cruise Hartley’s Lagoon to spot saltwater crocodiles and enjoy engaging wildlife presentations. From koala feedings to ancient Gondwana displays, this immersive experience highlights the wonder and diversity of Northern Australia’s natural world. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Rainforestation Nature Park & Skyrail Cableway
blocks.text: Journey through the heart of Australia’s tropical rainforest on this unforgettable eco-adventure. Explore Rainforestation National Park, where you’ll encounter native wildlife, experience Aboriginal culture and ride an amphibious “Army Duck” through lush terrain. Then, glide high above the treetops on the award-winning Skyrail Rainforest Cableway, taking in panoramic views of Barron Gorge and casc

blocks.heading: Green Island Discovery
blocks.text: Cruise across the sparkling Coral Sea to the breathtaking Green Island, a 6,000-year-old coral cay within the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park. Explore lush rainforest trails, stroll along white-sand beaches and witness vibrant marine life through snorkeling or a glass-bottom boat tour. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kuranda Scenic Railway
blocks.text: Journey from Yorkeys Knob through lush rainforest landscapes to the charming mountain village of Kuranda. Explore local markets filled with handmade crafts and Aboriginal art before boarding the historic Kuranda Scenic Railway. Travel through breathtaking scenery of waterfalls, ravines and tropical rainforest on this iconic route. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Wild River Tube Ride
blocks.text: Float through the lush beauty of the Goldsborough Valley on a thrilling tubing adventure down the Mulgrave River. Guided by certified river experts, you’ll drift through calm waters and gentle rapids surrounded by the vibrant rainforest of UNESCO’s Wet Tropics World Heritage Area—an unforgettable mix of excitement and natural wonder in tropical North Queensland. LEARN MORE

Whether you’re seeking relaxation or discovery, Yorkeys Knob is a highlight on many Australia and New Zealand cruise itineraries.

blocks.heading: Cruise from Sydney, Australia
blocks.text: The Sydney Opera House and the Sydney Harbour Bridge are just two of the welcoming sights greeting you as you approach Australia’s oldest and largest city on a cruise from Sydney. Once you’re in town, visit the golden sands of Bondi Beach, travel to the Blue Mountains, or explore the historic Rocks district. FIND CRUISES

blocks.heading: Cruise from Brisbane / Meeanjin, Australia
blocks.text: The gateway to the Gold and Sunshine Coasts, Brisbane is also a living museum dedicated to keeping its heritage alive with an abundance of 19th century buildings. Learn more about cruises from Brisbane. FIND CRUISES

links.text: Learn more about cruises from Brisbane

blocks.heading: Cruise from Melbourne, Australia
blocks.text: Stroll through Queen Victoria Market, a Melbourne institution since 1878, and pick up gourmet goods. For cutting-edge culture, food and shopping, Federation Square offers a city block full of galleries, restaurants and stores. FIND CRUISES

blocks.heading: Cruise from Auckland / Tāmaki Makaurau, New Zealand
blocks.text: From the ancient underground labyrinth known as the Waitomo Glowworm Caves to the helicopter rides over the city, Auckland is a city of breathtaking extremes. FIND CRUISES

blocks.heading: Cruise from Adelaide / Kaurna, Australia
blocks.text: Indulge in the unhurried charms of this carefree city. Whether you prefer to take things at a slow pace or gravitate towards a day full of fun and adventure, you’re sure to discover the many delights Adelaide has to offer. Beyond the city and the rugged Adelaide Hills lie Barossa Valley and Mackaren Vale, the most important winemaking region in Australia. FIND CRUISES

blocks.heading: Cruise from Perth (Fremantle) / Boorloo (Walyalup), Australia
blocks.text: Western Australia’s capital is a cosmopolitan mix of high rises and colonial buildings, beautiful beaches and verdant parkland, as well as the mystical yellow quartz sand of the Pinnacles Desert. FIND CRUISES

blocks.heading: Cruise from Hobart, Australia
blocks.text: Hobart, capital of Australia's island state of Tasmania, combines colonial character with a sophisticated metropolitan lifestyle. Seen from its fine deep-water harbor, Hobart spills over the lower reaches of the Derwent Valley as Mount Wellington towers in the background. Many of Tasmania's attractions are within easy reach of Hobart. FIND CRUISES

blocks.heading: Seacations
blocks.text: Princess® Seacations, lasting two to five days, make it easy to rekindle a romance, bond with family and friends, or recharge and reconnect. These short sailings offer great value over a typical hotel holiday, with meals, accommodation and entertainment all included in your cruise fare – and there’s no charge for unlimited doses of relaxation! FIND CRUISES

blocks.heading: Experience the New Zealand port on your next cruise
Onboard enrichment on New Zealand / Aotearoa cruises
blocks.text: At Princess® we want you to enjoy an unforgettable New Zealand adventure. That’s why we’ve created a unique onboard program ‘Across the Ditch’ - with special regional experiences, including: 1. See traditional folkloric performances, and learn the art yourself such as the Haka Māori War Dance or Poi Dancing. 2. Enjoy kiwi favorites served on board New Zealand cruises, including Pavlova, or Lamb, o

blocks.heading: Lifestyle & culture
blocks.text: Savor the unique tastes of an authentic Māori hangi or sample award-winning wines from Picton. See how the Māori’s rich heritage comes alive in the Bay of Islands / Pēwhairangi, and discover how Napier’s / Ahuriri beautifully preserved 1930s architecture pays homage to the Māori by merging the linear symmetry of Art Deco with tribal motifs.

blocks.heading: Natural wonders & landscapes
blocks.text: Witness the unparalleled beauty of what locals call “Godzone” (God’s own country) on a hike into Tauranga’s / Tauranga Moana Wai-O-Tapu thermal valley and be rewarded with spectacular mud pools, geysers and rainbow-colored lakes. Or venture farther south to explore the South Island’s rugged coastline and charming ports — from the Scottish-inspired city of Dunedin to Akaroa, where French influence

blocks.heading: Unique experiences on New Zealand / Aotearoa cruises
blocks.text: New Zealand’s vast, dramatic and diverse landscape is the unrivaled home of Tolkien’s mythical Middle Earth. Journey to the city of Edoras and walk in the footsteps of The Lord of the Rings in Wellington, and visit Peter Jackson’s Weta Studios. Marvel at the sight of twinkling glowworms in Auckland’s Glowworm Grotto, and explore Wellington’s Zealandia, nicknamed "Jurassic Park," in search of the g

blocks.heading: UNESCO world heritage sites
blocks.text: Sail into a world of surreal beauty in Fiordland National Park / Piopiotahi, where the verdant flanks of snowcapped peaks plunge into the crystalline waters of ice-carved fiords. Or visit the Tongariro National Park outside of Napier / Ahuriri, which holds the title of first park in the world to receive UNESCO World Heritage status for both its natural and Māori spiritual and cultural value.

blocks.heading: Landmarks
blocks.text: Don’t miss the famed Christchurch Botanic Gardens, which boasts the finest collection of exotic and indigenous plants in New Zealand, Port Chalmers’ Larnach Castle (the country’s only castle) or cruise to Auckland / Tāmaki Makaurau and see the Sky Tower, the tallest man-made structure in the southern hemisphere.

blocks.heading: Art, museums & historic treasures
blocks.text: Wellington’s number-one attraction, the Te Papa National Museum, showcases Māori and Pacific cultural treasures, New Zealand’s extraordinary natural life and its most important works of art.

Shore Excursions to explore at RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay
blocks.text: Beautiful beaches, swaying palm trees, private cabanas and endless charm set the scene at RelaxAway Half Moon Cay, a vibrant private island experience. Spend your day on a soft white sand beaches soaking up the sun and living your best Caribbean-paradise life. Dive into the island’s underwater life where you’ll see stingrays, bright fish and colorful coral or glide though the red mangrove trees by

blocks.heading: Tropical kayak adventure
blocks.text: Paddle into the natural beauty of Bonefish Lagoon on a guided kayak adventure at the heart of RelaxAway at Half Moon Cay. Glide through clear and calm waters lined with red mangroves and native vegetation, including silver buttonwood, as you explore more than 700 acres of protected habitat and its diverse ecosystem.

blocks.heading: RelaxAway cabana rental
blocks.text: Relax in your private cabana and soak in the turquoise waters and beachside experience all day from your own private retreat.

blocks.heading: Snorkeling at RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay
blocks.text: See what’s under the deep azure waters surrounding this private island resort on a snorkeling adventure with Princess. Snorkelers will love the colorful coral formations, gorgonians (soft coral-like sea fans) and sea sponges that make this spot such an underwater paradise. Keep your eyes peeled for schools of fish and even the occasional dolphin or sea turtle.

blocks.heading: Horseback riding by land & sea
blocks.text: Experience the thrill of horseback riding along the shores of RelaxAway at Half Moon Cay. Follow scenic coastal paths around Pagasus Ranch before the highlight—remaining mounted as your horse swims through calm, turquoise water. Afterward, unwind on the beach, and enjoy a complimentary barbecue lunch.

blocks.heading: Stingray adventure
blocks.text: Discover an educational experience with the southern stingrays residing in a beautiful alcove at Half Moon Cay. Snorkel in shallow, crystal-clear water where you'll encounter the stingrays and gently touch and feed them from your hands. A memorable and hands-on experience awaits along with stories worth sharing of your island adventure.

blocks.text: Discovery awaits at RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay™, an exclusive private island paradise with white sand beaches and beautiful turquoise waters. Celebrated as the Best Private Island for 20 years in a row, this retreat invites you to slow down, savor fresh flavors, explore nature and embrace the moments that feel as effortless as an island breeze.

blocks.heading: Experience the British Isles port on your next cruise
Why cruise the British Isles
blocks.text: The British pubs, Parisian artwork and Irish castles invite you to live like royalty.

blocks.heading: More ashore
blocks.text: Enjoy even more history and culture during your British Isles cruise with More Ashore late-night departures and overnight stays. Visit several pubs during an evening tour, and hear stories from locals over a pint of local brew. Savor a traditional Scottish dinner in Edinburgh, and see the Royal Mile illuminated by street lamps and the evening light. Or explore Dublin by night, and indulge in Irish

blocks.heading: Castles
blocks.text: Castles are the emblem of these regions. Between the chandeliers and tapestries, step into luxury when you visit the British Isles. Cruise to Dublin and parade through the 13th-century halls of the city’s fortress. Experience the grandeur of Urquhart Castle, and search for legendary ghosts in Glamis Castle. Or visit Edinburgh Castle, where kings, queens and nobles once lived and medieval secrets c

blocks.heading: Music
blocks.text: As the birthplace of many music icons, the British Isles invite you to sing, dance and raise a glass to songs played around the globe. Visit Liverpool to walk in the footsteps of a beloved boyband, and head to a local pub to hear the boys at their best. Cruise the British Isles for an evening of Irish song and dance in Dublin, or watch the Edinburgh Military Tattoo assemble bands, bagpipes and dru

blocks.heading: Heritage
blocks.text: The British Isles are a mecca of UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Cruise from Southampton to Liverpool, and walk along the Royal Albert Dock, the first structure in Britain to be constructed without wood. Shop along Princes Street in Edinburgh’s New Town. Or travel to Brú na Bóinne in Dublin and get up close to Europe’s largest collection of prehistoric megalithic art.

blocks.heading: Pubs
blocks.text: In lands famous for their stouts and ales, pubs are the cornerstone of tradition. Cruise the British Isles and step into age-old establishments that are bustling with spirit. In Dublin, get a taste of true pub “craic” — an Irish term that equates to an atmosphere of fun, entertainment and good company. With festive music playing in the background, sip on world-famous beers that originated nearby w

blocks.heading: Natural phenomena
blocks.text: Discern fact versus fiction on a British Isles cruise, where mysteries and mythologies abound. In Portland, learn about the 5,000-year-old stone circle that displays an advanced understanding of arithmetic and astrology. On itineraries that sail to Cork, search the sea for the Bioluminescence beams created by the region’s gleaming plankton. Or hunt for Invergordon’s legendary monster in the waters

blocks.heading: Museums & art galleries
blocks.text: No cruise to the British Isles is complete without a visit to Paris. See “Venus de Milo” and da Vinci’s “Mona Lisa,” or tour Notre Dame, a work of art in and of itself. Visit the Irish Emigration Museum in Dublin, where interactive galleries invite you to explore. Those departing from London can also stop by the Victoria and Albert Museum which houses over two million artifacts.

blocks.heading: Stargazing
blocks.text: Embark on a cosmic voyage to the heavens from our top deck through Stargazing, developed with renowned astrophysicist Hakeem Oluseyi and L.A.’s famous Griffith Observatory. On this interactive guided tour, learn how to find your bearings, identify the major constellations, and hear the secrets of the stars and the legends around them.

blocks.heading: Local connections
blocks.text: Do as the locals do. Princess has partnered with local experts to bring you immersive adventure off the beaten path. Dine at local hot spots hidden in plain sight. Attend events and have experiences only known through word of mouth. Listen as experts reveal California’s history, national parks and Spanish missions from a local point of view.

blocks.heading: New perspectives
blocks.text: Experience a new perspective of California and the West Coast on board or ashore, day or night. Learn about California from the locals who know it best and uncover the secret lives of sharks. Amaze your friends after a class at the Wizard’s Academy courtesy of the California Science Center.

blocks.text: Cuisine inspired by world-renowned chefs. Broadway-style entertainment from award-winning creators. Shore excursions crafted to immerse you into what makes the region truly unique. From the port of San Francisco, you can visit two world-renowned wine regions: Napa and Sonoma. Or stay in San Francisco to learn about the city's wine history and taste the local fare.
From the port of San Francisco, you can visit two world-renowned wine regions: Napa and Sonoma. Or stay in San Francisco to learn about the city's wine history and taste the local fare.

If you spend some time in the Oregon city of Astoria, you can take a drive to Willamette Valley and explore the wineries famous for their pinot noir, or The Cellar on 10th, a wine shop which specializes in Pacific Northwest wines.
From the cruise port in Seattle, you can visit Woodinville, which has over 117 tasting rooms and wineries for you to enjoy.
In Victoria, BC you can take a trip to the Butchart Gardens, then enjoy delicious wine paired with tapas and chocolates at the Blue Poppy Restaurant.
From Vancouver, BC, you can head to Fraser Valley, which is home to almost 30 vineyards and roughly 15 wineries.

blocks.heading: Culture & marine life on cruises from California
blocks.text: Get to the heart of life on the coast with locally inspired programs and partnerships. Witness fantastic displays of nature like expressive sea lions and migrating whales. Learn about colorful, historical cultures and more on our California Coast cruise.

blocks.heading: Stargazing
blocks.text: Embark on a cosmic voyage to the heavens from our top deck through Stargazing, developed with renowned astrophysicist Hakeem Oluseyi and L.A.’s famous Griffith Observatory. On this interactive guided tour, learn how to find your bearings, identify the major constellations, and hear the secrets of the stars and the legends around them.

blocks.heading: Local connections
blocks.text: Do as the locals do. Princess has partnered with local experts to bring you immersive adventure off the beaten path. Dine at local hot spots hidden in plain sight. Attend events and have experiences only known through word of mouth. Listen as experts reveal California’s history, national parks and Spanish missions from a local point of view.

blocks.heading: New perspectives
blocks.text: Experience a new perspective of California and the West Coast on board or ashore, day or night. Learn about California from the locals who know it best and uncover the secret lives of sharks. Amaze your friends after a class at the Wizard’s Academy courtesy of the California Science Center.

blocks.heading: The Princess difference
blocks.text: Cuisine inspired by world-renowned chefs. Broadway-style entertainment from award-winning creators. Shore excursions crafted to immerse you into what makes the region truly unique. Princess knows that the journey and the destination aren’t separate, but together they make the most cherished memories.

blocks.text: We have a wide range of comfortable accommodations for families or friends traveling together. Experience what draws people to California, from fog-covered redwood forests to bright lights and excitement.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Astoria
blocks.text: Astoria blends coastal charm with rich Pacific Northwest history, offering everything from scenic riverfront views to iconic film sites and historic landmarks. Explore the Astoria Column, stroll the waterfront or dive into local museums and breweries for a perfect mix of culture and adventure.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Astoria
blocks.text: Astoria offers a diverse range of shore excursions, from exploring historic forts and museums to discovering breathtaking coastal vistas and charming nearby towns. Whether you’re interested in nature, culture or local flavor, each excursion provides a memorable way to experience Oregon’s rugged beauty.

blocks.heading: Willamette Valley Wine Country & Tasting
blocks.text: Experience the beauty of Oregon Wine Country with a guided tour through the renowned Willamette Valley, home to more than 700 wineries. Enjoy scenic drives, strolls through peaceful vineyards and curated tasting flights at Apolloni Vineyards and Ardiri Winery, where you’ll savor pinot noirs and unique white blends while taking in breathtaking countryside views. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Mount St. Helens
blocks.text: Experience the science, beauty, and raw power of Mount St. Helens on this full-day excursion. Travel along the Columbia River to Mount St. Helens National Monument, where you’ll enjoy a boxed lunch at a stunning mountain overlook and take in breathtaking views (weather permitting). Return to the pier with a deeper appreciation for the volcano’s dramatic history and natural wonder. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Historic Astoria & Fort Clatsop
blocks.text: Explore Astoria’s rich history on a scenic motorcoach tour that begins with a photo stop at the iconic Astoria Column. Visit the replica Fort Clatsop from the Lewis and Clark expedition, then browse nautical artifacts at the Columbia River Maritime Museum. Enjoy a panoramic drive through Astoria’s Victorian neighborhoods, historic Uniontown and landmarks like the World War I "Doughboy" monument. L

blocks.heading: Astoria Scenic Waterfront Biking
blocks.text: Discover Astoria’s scenic waterfront on a guided 2.5-hour bike ride along paved and wooden pathways. Pedal at a comfortable pace as your guide shares stories of the city’s canning boom and lively seaport past. Stop for photos, taste fresh seafood at a local cannery and spot coastal wildlife before completing the six-mile loop back to the pier. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Alderbrook Lagoon Kayak Adventure
blocks.text: Glide through the calm waters of Alderbrook Lagoon on a guided sit-on kayak adventure, perfect for beginners and seasoned paddlers alike. Take in scenic views, spot local wildlife and learn about the area’s cannery history before returning to Pier 39 for a visit to the Hanthorn Cannery Museum. LEARN MORE

Visit the replica Fort Clatsop from the Lewis and Clark expedition, then browse nautical artifacts at the Columbia River Maritime Museum. blocks.text: Discover Astoria’s scenic waterfront on a guided 2.5-hour bike ride along paved and wooden pathways. Pedal at a comfortable pace as your guide shares stories of the city’s canning boom and lively seaport past. Stop for photos, taste fresh seafood at a local cannery and spot coastal wildlife before completing the six-mile loop back to the pier. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Alderbrook Lagoon Kayak Adventure
blocks.text: Glide through the calm waters of Alderbrook Lagoon on a guided sit-on kayak adventure, perfect for beginners and seasoned paddlers alike. Take in scenic views, spot local wildlife and learn about the area’s cannery history before returning to Pier 39 for a visit to the Hanthorn Cannery Museum. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Catalina Island
blocks.text: Experience Catalina Island through excursions that highlight its laid-back charm, coastal scenery and welcoming island atmosphere. From leisurely sightseeing to outdoor adventures, you’ll find options that make it easy to enjoy the best of this picturesque destination.

blocks.heading: Coastal Sailing Adventure
blocks.text: Set sail on a 38-foot Catalina 385 for a relaxing coastal cruise with a friendly crew. Enjoy your own playlist, sip champagne and take in views of serene coves, sandy beaches,and local wildlife. With snacks, refreshing beverages and plenty of scenic photo opportunities, this smooth downwind journey back to Avalon Harbor offers a memorable experience for all ages. LEARN MORE

blocks.text: Discover Catalina Island’s hidden beauty on a guided kayaking adventure through Lover’s Cove Marine Preserve. blocks.heading: Luxury Scenic Sailing
blocks.text: Sail the stunning waters off Catalina Island in private luxury aboard a 38-foot yacht, taking in Avalon's natural beauty and scenic coastline. Relax on deck with champagne in hand as you spot dolphins, sea lions and seabirds, glide past picturesque coves and reefs, and enjoy a curated charcuterie board before returning to Avalon. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Avalon History Walking Tour
blocks.text: Step back in time on a 90-minute guided walk through the charming seaside town of Avalon. This easy, one-mile tour blends history, culture and storytelling as you explore iconic landmarks and learn about the island’s colorful past. With complimentary headsets and engaging narration, it’s a relaxed and nostalgic way to connect Catalina’s golden heritage with its vibrant present. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in San Diego
blocks.text: San Diego throws more than sunshine your way — it throws seaside chill, cross‑border zest and a dose of California cool into one breezy package. And while its history runs deep (think Spanish missions, Mexican heritage and U.S. expansion), today you’ll find surf, craft beer and coastline that doesn’t quit. Here are some top suggestions on how to optimize your stay.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in San Diego
blocks.text: There’s no wrong way to explore San Diego, but these excursions make sure you skip the guesswork and head straight for the ‘wow.’ From land-to-sea hybrids to culinary deep dives, this lineup serves up the best of America’s Finest City — no planning required.

blocks.heading: City Drive & La Jolla Highlights
blocks.text: This four-hour ride gives you San Diego’s greatest hits: La Jolla’s swanky beaches, Old Town’s adobe charm, Balboa Park’s green heart and the waterfront’s Embarcadero vibes. Finish your tour or hop off for some solo exploring. Return to ship or linger near Horton Plaza for shopping? Sorry, but that’s a choice you’re going to have to make on your own. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Old Town Trolley Tour
blocks.text: Board an open-air trolley and roll through San Diego’s greatest hits — think harbor views, Gaslamp Quarter history, Coronado’s beachy charm and Balboa Park’s green sprawl. You’ll even swing by Little Italy and Old Town. Hop on, hop off or just stay parked and soak it all in. Your schedule, your call. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of the Bay Cruise
blocks.text: Glide past sea lions, shipyards and maybe even a migrating whale on this narrated 90-minute bay cruise. From the Point Loma Lighthouse to the Coronado Bridge and Hotel del Coronado, this tour serves up classic San Diego sights with an ocean breeze and zero effort. Pro tip: grab a spot on deck for the full effect. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The San Diego Seal
blocks.text: Start on land, splash into the bay and then call it a day. This amphibious adventure takes you past downtown landmarks, then dives into the harbor for a waterborne loop near Point Loma. Wildlife sightings are likely, fun facts are guaranteed and your Instagram will never recover. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: San Diego Zoo On Your Own
blocks.text: Spend a full day exploring the legendary San Diego Zoo: over 4,000 animals, 700,000 plants, tram rides, double‑deck buses and habitats built for jaguars, condors and elephants (to name a few). You roam at your own pace and decide when to pause for snacks. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Explore San Diego’s Culinary Roots
blocks.text: With Mexico’s border just 17 miles away, you better believe that local food traditions lean south. This half‑day experience plunges you into Barrio Logan’s Chicano murals, street‑style tacos and fresh agua frescas, then into Old Town’s culinary scene where guacamole, tortillas and tequila sampling redefine tradition and taste. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to San Diego
blocks.text: When you arrive at the port, you’re stepping into a city that rolls waves and sidewalks in equal measure. San Diego’s cruise terminal sits right on the Embarcadero, with walkable access to shopping, dining and historic neighborhoods. It’s one of the easiest U.S. ports to explore on foot, and a great starting point for California coast itineraries that let you roll from skyline to sand in minutes.

blocks.heading: Things to do in San Francisco
blocks.text: San Francisco has many names (the Golden City, Paris of the West), but to those who live in and around it it will always just be The City. And, when you slide into port, you’ll understand why. San Francisco is the kind of place you can get the feel of in one day ashore, or spend a lifetime there and never totally comprehend it. It’s a vertical maze of Victorian houses and innovation hubs, where ea

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in San Francisco
blocks.text: Pick from curated excursions that serve up the city’s classics — over the bridge, into redwood forests, across wine country and into open water. These tours peel back the layers of San Francisco and the landscapes that orbit it.

blocks.heading: Easy San Francisco: City Drive & Golden Gate Bridge
blocks.text: This relaxed, half-day tour checks off the icons. See the Embarcadero, Ghirardelli Square and Fisherman’s Wharf. Cross the Golden Gate Bridge, visit Lands End and stop inside Golden Gate Park. There’s a short break at Twin Peaks for panoramic views, then a final ride down Market Street before returning to the pier. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Sausalito & Muir Woods
blocks.text: Cross the Golden Gate Bridge and pause at Vista Point for sweeping views of the bay. In Sausalito, stroll the waterfront, visit art galleries or grab a coffee with a view. Then it’s off to Muir Woods, home to centuries-old redwoods that tower overhead as you walk the quiet forest trails. On your return, drive past Fisherman's Wharf and enjoy a scenic ride back through the city. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Alcatraz & Sausalito
blocks.text: Start with a ferry ride to the infamous Alcatraz Island, where a self-guided audio tour brings its eerie history to life, from the Birdman (the other one) to Al Capone. After returning to the mainland, head north to Sausalito and enjoy time on your own exploring its waterfront shops and galleries. Cap off your day with a drive back across the Golden Gate. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Sonoma Wine Country
blocks.text: Vineyards, valley views and varietals: this full-day tour is for the wine lovers. Start with a tasting at family-owned Roche Winery, followed by free time and lunch in Sonoma Square. After lunch, head to Viansa Winery, perched on a hilltop overlooking wetlands and wildlife. Taste your way through the day, then sit back and enjoy the scenic ride back to port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: San Francisco Waterfront Sail by Tall Ship
blocks.text: Board the 72-foot Gas Light (a Gold Rush-style tall ship) and set sail on the bay with a glass in hand. During the 2.5-hour cruise, take in views of Alcatraz, the Golden Gate Bridge and the city skyline. Snacks and drinks are available, and guests can even help raise the sails. This is a sightseeing cruise that’s also a trip back in maritime time. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: San Francisco Sightseeing & Chinatown Lunch
blocks.text: Glide through the city’s neighborhoods on a narrated motorcoach tour, from Union Square to the Castro and on up to Twin Peaks. Enjoy a meal in the heart of Chinatown, then explore on your own or follow your guide through this historic district. Finish your tour with photo stops at North Beach and the Golden Gate Bridge Pavilion. LEARN MORE

blocks.text: Princess Cruises docks at the centrally located Pier 27 Cruise Terminal, right along the Embarcadero and within easy reach of San Francisco’s downtown. From here, you can hop a cable car, walk the waterfront or dive into Chinatown, North Beach and the Ferry Building’s gourmet market scene. It’s a launch point that drops you right into the heart of the action and is an ideal port to launch into Ala

blocks.heading: Things to do in Santa Barbara
blocks.text: Welcome to the “American Riviera” (and that’s not Marketing fluff). Santa Barbara mixes Spanish‑Moorish elegance, palm‑lined beaches and wine country just over yonder into one satisfying destination. Expect bougainvillea garlands, centuries-old missions and seaside ease under one sun-soaked sky.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Santa Barbara
blocks.text: From tasting rooms to whale watching to cultural deep dives, this list of excursions for Santa Barbara cruises has something for every kind of guest. Choose your flavor and dive in.

blocks.heading: Santa Barbara & Los Olivos: California’s Riviera, Food & Wine
blocks.text: You could do a walking tour. Or you could eat tacos made by a celebrity chef, drink wine in rolling vineyard hill and still make it back in time for sail-away snacks. This full-day flavor-fest starts at the Mission, detours into downtown architecture, and ends in Los Olivos where cupcakes meet cabernet. Stretchy pants aren’t mandatory, but they’re a pretty solid call. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Historical Santa Barbara & Old Mission with Expert Guide
blocks.text: If you're only doing one thing in Santa Barbara, make it this. Start with a warm welcome from local legends dockside, then stroll through the Old Mission (a 1786 original that still slaps). Meet friars, wander the chapel and cemetery and download a bonus app tour because, why not? End with a scenic drive past everything that makes the American Riviera tick. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Island Whale Watching
blocks.text: This isn't some sad animal-in-a-cage situation. You're chasing the real deal on a high-speed catamaran: whales, dolphins, seals, sea lions and enough salty air to exfoliate your soul. Cruise past the Channel Islands, spy the Painted Cave (if you're lucky). Respect the wildlife, but do try to get the perfect breach pic. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Wine & Chocolate Historical Walking Tour
blocks.text: If sipping boutique wines while snacking on small-batch chocolate in an art-splattered coastal city isn’t peak vacation energy, we don’t want to know what is. This guided walk hits the Funk Zone (yes, it’s a real place), Stearns Wharf and other architectural gems — with pit stops for wine pours, chocolate chunks and historical gossip. It’s culture, sugar and sass in one delicious loop. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connection: Santa Barbara In Depth
blocks.text: Why pick between architecture, food and vibes when this tour drops all three in your lap? Walk the downtown core, climb the courthouse tower, poke through the Presidio and eat like a local — craft beer, handmade empanadas and all. With a guide who knows their stuff and a route that skips the fluff, this one goes deeper (without making you sweat). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ride Through History: Santa Barbara Historical Museum

Whether you’re headed to California or the Caribbean, immerse yourself in the best of the region on board.

Or indulge in unique beverages crafted by expert Mixologist Rob Floyd. Set sail on a true sensory experience with Getaway cruises from Princess.

blocks.heading: Historic landmarks
blocks.text: California's history stretches as far back as its visionaries look forward. From the infamous prison of Alcatraz to the nearly 400-year-old Mission Trail, to the famous Hollywood Walk of Fame, there's a lifetime of history to dive into.

blocks.heading: Culinary delights
blocks.text: With its rich agricultural lands and vibrant cultural diversity, California is home to a culinary culture unlike anywhere else. Princess partnered with famed food journalist Bill Esparza to create shore excursions that give you the perfect culinary tour. From unique tacos in the heart of Santa Barbara to the hustle and bustle of LA's famous Farmers Market, taste what makes the Golden State so spec

blocks.heading: Wine tasting
blocks.text: California contains some of the world's finest wine-growing regions which produce award-winning, palate-pleasing wines too numerous to count. You'll be guided to the best tasting rooms on the West Coast only steps away from the vineyards where the wines in your glass began. Beginner wine connoisseurs will learn what makes these wines unique and the experienced oenophile will deepen their appreciat

blocks.heading: Nature & wildlife
blocks.text: The Golden State's expansive coastline, varied geography and history of conservation show in the stunning beauty and majestic wildlife you'll see on your cruise. Year-round whales migrate through coastal waters, sea lions and seals sun themselves on rocks and in harbors, and seabirds of all types fish in the bountiful waters.

blocks.heading: 10/14-day Classic Canada
blocks.text: Discover the beauty of Canada and New England with a variety of itineraries to choose from in both summer and fall. See New England's most scenic coastlines, taste Maine’s famous lobster, and visit some of the most iconic lighthouses. Explore Cape Breton Island (Sydney) or enjoy an overnight in Québec City. The options are endless on cruises to Canada & New England with Princess.

blocks.heading: 7-day Canada
blocks.text: Calling all history buffs - follow the Founding Fathers' footsteps around the historic Virginia triangle and visit Colonial Williamsburg on excursions through Norfolk. This unique itinerary sails from New York in the summer and visits popular ports where history was made. Explore the Freedom Trail in Boston, Fort Sumter in Charleston and more to gain a deeper understanding of what shaped America.

blocks.heading: Experience the Canada port on your next cruise
Why cruise Canada?
blocks.text: A Canada cruise brings you face-to-face with the country’s timeless charm and deep-rooted history. Sail into storied harbors, wander through preserved historic districts and take in landscapes shaped by centuries of culture and nature. It’s a beautifully effortless way to discover what makes Canada so captivating.

blocks.heading: Savor fresh regional seafood
blocks.text: The quaint New England of earlier times is alive and well in charming port cities, like Portland and Newport. Grab a bowl of clam chowder or a lobster roll, or enjoy fresh Maine blueberries.

blocks.heading: Cruise from New York
blocks.text: A leading global metropolitan city, New York City influences the world’s commerce, finance, culture, fashion and entertainment. Sail roundtrip from the city that never sleeps and discover world-famous landmarks like the New York Stock Exchange or the Statue of Liberty. Explore iconic neighborhoods, and see the city through the eyes of the locals.

blocks.heading: Cruise from Quebec City
blocks.text: Feel like you’ve traveled to France without leaving North America. Duck into a café for wine and brie, and explore the architecture of Old Québec, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Enjoy the beautiful Quebéc City before you set sail on a 10-14 day Canada & New England cruise.

blocks.heading: Cruise from Boston
blocks.text: Discover the historic and cultural treasures and the quaint New England charm Boston has to offer. A city known for attracting history buffs, academics, sports fanatics and beer drinkers is now also calling foodies, outdoor enthusiasts, music lovers and cultural travelers to experience its beauty before embarking on a Canada & New England cruise.

blocks.heading: Cruise to iconic rocky coastlines
blocks.text: Cruise Eastern Canada and discover a decidedly French influence, from the idyllic coastal villages of Nova Scotia to the Rue St. Louis in Québec City. See the best-known sights, such as the lighthouse at Peggy's Cove in Halifax or the churches of Saint John.

blocks.heading: Revisit history from Colonial times
blocks.text: Cruise New England and discover America's roots along its rocky coastline. Visit historic cities like Philadelphia, home of the Liberty Bell, the house where Thomas Jefferson wrote the Declaration of Independence, as well as the great melting pot of New York City.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Boston
Freedom Trail Walking Tour
blocks.text: Celebrate Revolutionary Boston on a guided walk along the iconic Freedom Trail, a 2.5-mile route connecting centuries of American history. Explore landmarks such as Boston Common, historic churches and famous meeting houses, with stories of the Boston Tea Party, Paul Revere and the Declaration of Independence woven throughout. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Boston Highlights Scenic Drive
blocks.text: Enjoy a narrated driving tour showcasing Boston’s most treasured sights with little to no walking required. Pass elegant Back Bay mansions, Beacon Hill and historic landmarks along the Freedom Trail, with brief stops as traffic allows. See the iconic gold-domed State House and Faneuil Hall, with the option to explore Quincy Market independently before returning to the ship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Boston Hop On/Hop Off Trolley
blocks.text: Perfect for savvy, independent travelers, this hop-on, hop-off trolley experience showcases the best of Boston. Ride aboard 13-foot-tall open-air trolleys for a lively, fully narrated tour filled with history and colorful anecdotes. With over 15 unique stops across the city’s most iconic neighborhoods, you can explore at your own pace before returning to port after a memorable day. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Salem Witch History & Boston Highlights
blocks.text: Discover the patriotic history and dramatic legends of New England on a guided full-day driving tour. Travel to Salem to explore its famed witch-trial past, enjoy a theatrical presentation, browse for unique souvenirs and savor free time for lunch. Then, return to Boston for a scenic city drive with iconic photo stops before heading back to the port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Fenway Park & Boston Highlights
blocks.text: Experience the charm of America’s oldest active Major League ballpark on a half-day tour that begins with a narrated scenic drive through Boston. Upon arriving at Fenway Park, an expert guide leads you through its most iconic spots, from the famed Green Monster to historic memorabilia, sharing over a century of baseball history. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Duck Tour of Boston
blocks.text: Explore Boston aboard a World War II–style amphibious vehicle that takes you past the city’s most iconic historic sights before “splashing” into the Charles River. Enjoy sweeping views of the Boston and Cambridge skylines, the Longfellow Bridge and landmarks in the distance. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Charlottetown
blocks.text: There’s something instantly endearing about Charlottetown. Maybe it’s the gingerbread-trimmed homes, the pastel shopfronts or the way every local seems to know where to find the best lobster roll. The walkable downtown makes it easy to explore on foot, and whether you're here for the maritime heritage, the scenery or your lifelong Anne of Green Gables obsession, this port city offers plenty to lov

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Charlottetown
blocks.text: Charlottetown welcomes you with a relaxed pace, easy access and a deep sense of place tied to Canada’s beginnings. Princess excursions take you to the best parts with zero stress, letting you experience literary landmarks, seaside scenery or a taste of the island's unique culture and flavor.

blocks.heading: Local Connections: The Seafood Chef
blocks.text: Join a local culinary master for an immersive cooking experience at ADA Culinary Studio (just a 20-minute walk from the port). Watch as the chef prepares a three-course meal using the island’s freshest shellfish and seasonal ingredients, then enjoy the fruits of their labor in a cozy setting. It’s a flavorful introduction to the island’s maritime heritage, and an absolute must for food lovers. LEA

blocks.heading: The Ultimate Anne of Green Gables Experience
blocks.text: A dream for fans of Anne with an E, this literary pilgrimage begins at the Anne of Green Gables Museum, where you’ll stroll the flower gardens and sip raspberry cordial beside the Lake of Shining Waters. blocks.heading: Local Connections: Fun with Falcons with Master Falconer Peter McMurchy
blocks.text: This rare, hands-on wildlife encounter brings you face-to-beak with some of nature’s fastest predators. Learn about conservation efforts and falconry from Peter McMurchy, who’s trained hawks and falcons for years on Prince Edward Island. If conditions allow, you'll witness jaw-dropping flight demos and even have the chance to wear the falconer's glove and welcome a bird to your hand. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: A Taste of Charlottetown Walking Tour
blocks.text: Get to know Charlottetown… one bite at a time. Led by a local guide, you’ll explore historic streets while sampling Island delicacies: lobster, mussels, oysters, Prince Edward Island potatoes and locally brewed craft beer (because walking and sampling delicious foods is thirsty work). It’s part history lesson, part culinary crawl and 100% delicious. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Historical Churches of Charlottetown Walking Tour
blocks.text: Explore the spiritual backbone of this historic port with a guided tour of four of its most storied churches. Visit St. Dunstan’s Basilica with its dramatic twin spires, hear ghost stories at ‘The Kirk,’ marvel at the Rood Screen at St. Peter’s Cathedral and finish at the rust-red sandstone All Souls Chapel. Rich in heritage and haunting in legend, this tour blends spirituality, architecture and l

blocks.heading: Charlottetown by Harbour Hopper
blocks.text: All aboard for a land-and-sea adventure! This amphibious vehicle starts with a drive through Charlottetown’s historic core, passing Province House, City Hall and the Confederation Centre of the Arts. Then it’s time to make a splash (literally) as you glide into the harbor for a fresh perspective of the waterfront. It’s fun, informative and perfect for families. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Corner Brook
Shore excursions to explore in Corner Brook
blocks.text: Cruises to Corner Brook deliver a mix of outdoor excitement, geological wonder and cultural immersion. It’s perfect for guests who want a little extra to go with the beautiful scenery.

blocks.heading: Steady Brook Falls Zip‑Line Adventure
blocks.text: Get airborne above the Humber Valley when you take on the Steady Brook Falls zip‑line course — nine lines up to 2,000 ft long and 285 ft high, topping out at 30 km/h. It’s your chance to fulfill your need for speed while experiencing aerial views most guests never get to encounter. After the thrill you’ll ride back to the port, wind‑in‑hair and grin on full. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Corner Brook: Gros Morne National Park & Light Lunch
blocks.text: You’ll journey into deep‑time geology as you head to Gros Morne National Park, where the Tablelands look like another planet and inland lakes hide long‑eroded secrets of the Earth. After a guided walk you’ll stop for a light lunch at a local eatery, then take in the Lobster Cove Lighthouse and Norris Point lookout on your return. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Tablelands — A Rare Piece of Earth
blocks.text: Spend a full day discovering one of the most unusual landscapes in the world as you step into the Tablelands inside Gros Morne. You’ll shuttle to the trailhead, hike across peridotite bedrock (once buried kilometres below the surface), stop for lunch overlooking Bonne Bay, then return to Corner Brook via some of the most scenic roads you’ve ever seen. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: A Flavor of Corner Brook – Food, Frolic & Fish
blocks.text: Drive into the Bay of Islands and visit fishing communities where local life still pulses in sync with the tides. You’ll stop at a fish‑processing plant, stroll through waterfronts lined with painted dories, meet villagers for folk music and sample seafood dishes that are as authentic as they come. It's a feast for all your senses (but especially your tastebuds). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Captain Cook Monument & Old Man in the Mountain
blocks.text: This leisurely bus tour brings you to two standout landmarks: the Old Man in the Mountain rock feature looking over the Humber River, and the Captain Cook Monument with its historic maps and panoramic views. Bonus: the Heritage Tree carved with 56 depictions of Newfoundland life adds depth to your visit. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Discover Elmastukwek
blocks.text: Immerse in Mi’kmaw culture on this 3.5‑hour motorcoach journey along the Bay of Islands to Elmastukwek. You’ll learn about the region’s Indigenous heritage, view mural art by Chief Jenny Brake, taste local dishes like moose tacos and smoked arctic charr and return to port with a full stomach and a fuller sense of place. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Eastport
blocks.text: Discover Eastport’s rugged coastal beauty through memorable excursions like whale-watching cruises, cultural tours and visits to nearby islands and lighthouses. Whether you’re exploring marine wildlife or learning about the region’s rich history, Eastport offers uniquely authentic adventures.

blocks.heading: Shakeford Head State Park Hike
blocks.text: Embark on a 2.5-hour adventure through Eastport, beginning with a brief city tour before exploring the scenic trails of Shackford Head State Park. Enjoy a moderate 1.5-mile hike past pocket beaches and sheltered coves to a rocky headland overlooking Cobscook Bay, Campobello Island and Lubec. Along the way, spot wildlife, seabirds and local salmon aquaculture pens. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Eastport
blocks.text: Experience the charm of Eastport, Maine, on a relaxing 1.5-hour panoramic tour led by a local guide. See historic downtown, learn about the Passamaquoddy tribe and Roosevelt family ties, admire views of Shackford Head State Park and glimpse the famous Old Sow whirlpool. Pass Raye’s Mustard Mill and a working lobster pound before returning to port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Campobello Island: Franklin D. Roosevelt’s Summer Home
blocks.text: Discover Campobello Island on a 4.5-hour journey that begins aboard a traditional lobster boat to Lubec before crossing into Roosevelt Campobello International Park. Tour the Roosevelts’ beautifully preserved 34-room summer home, explore the park’s scenic grounds and visit iconic viewpoints like Mulholland Point Lighthouse and Friar’s Head, all offering sweeping coastal vistas. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Whale Watching
blocks.text: Set off on a 2.5-hour whale-watching adventure from the pier, cruising past Maine’s rugged coastline and landmarks like Old Sow and the East Quoddy Lighthouse. Watch for bald eagles, ospreys, dolphins and seals as you journey through pristine waters. The highlight awaits as whales breach and play nearby, with your captain positioning the vessel for incredible photo opportunities. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Eastport Harbor by Working Lobster Boat
blocks.text: Sail aboard The Lady H, an authentic Maine lobster boat, for a 90-minute Downeast Lobster & Seal Cruise through Passamaquoddy Bay. Learn the art of lobstering with a licensed fisherman, pull real traps and watch for wildlife like porpoises, whales, eagles and seals. Witness the region’s dramatic 26-foot tides and the famed Old Sow whirlpool before returning to port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: A Walk Through Historic Eastport
blocks.text: Embark on a one-hour guided walking tour through Eastport, Maine, where restored historic buildings, a lively waterfront and centuries-old stories come to life. Capture the iconic 12-foot Fisherman Statue, learn about dramatic tides and the legendary “Old Sow” and explore the town’s rich heritage. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Halifax
blocks.text: Halifax is sure a nice looking waterfront. It’s also a whole lot more. As the capital of Nova Scotia and the largest city in Canada’s Atlantic Provinces, Halifax was once Britain’s North American military bastion. Today you can still sense that legacy in the Citadel, the restored waterfront and the harbour that welcomed ships for centuries. From Scottish heritage to local pubs and seafood, Halifax

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Halifax
blocks.text: Whether you’re into cliffs, craft beer or cannon fire, Halifax has an excursion for you.

blocks.heading: Halifax Scenic Hop‑On Hop‑Off Tour with Express Pass Entrance
blocks.text: Hop aboard the double‑deck bus loop through Halifax’s key districts. Your pass includes entry to the Maritime Museum and the Halifax Citadel. Stops include Spring Garden Road, Hydrostone district, the Public Gardens and more. Walk, ride, dip in and out — ideal if you want the opportunity to see it all, and the flexibility to see it on your terms. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Halifax & Lunch
blocks.text: Start at Peggy’s Cove, the classic East Coast fishing village with its red‑and‑white lighthouse perched on surf‑polished granite (grab your camera). Enjoy a fresh lobster‑roll lunch by the sea, then drive into town to the Halifax Citadel for history up close. Finish at the Maritime Museum of the Atlantic along the waterfront where Titanic artefacts and local shipwreck stories await. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Tunnels, Tales & Mysteries of Georges Island
blocks.text: Board a ferry from the waterfront to Georges Island and follow your guide through Fort Charlotte’s mortar‑lined walls, Martello tower and subterranean tunnels. This island in Halifax Harbour guarded the city for nearly two centuries. The tour blends military history with intrigue and ends with a scenic return via ferry. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Colonial Lunenburg & Amos Pewter Experience with Local Artisan
blocks.text: Drive out of town to Lunenburg. Wander its Old Town harbour, colourful wooden buildings and the home harbor of the famous schooner Bluenose II. Then meet a local pewter artisan at Amos Pewter, try your hand at wax carving and enjoy maple taffy at a nearby cottage. This outing is part culture, part craft, part countryside and pure Halifax. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Annapolis Valley & Wine Tasting
blocks.text: Get ready to have a ‘grape’ time. Head into Nova Scotia’s countryside on a motorcoach tour through the Annapolis Valley. Visit dyked farmland, stop at award‑winning wineries for tastings (including local Tidal Bay; pair it with cheese), then return via the Bay of Fundy coastline where tides and cliffs compete for your undivided attention. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Halifax City & Harbor Hopper Tour
blocks.text: Experience the city from land and water aboard an amphibious vehicle: first a narrated drive through downtown Halifax, then a splash‑down into harbour for a cruise view of the waterfront, cable wharf and naval dockyard. Dress for wind and bring a light jacket because the Atlantic likes to remind you what a Canadian coastline should be. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Halifax
blocks.text: The port of Halifax places you right at the waterfront boardwalk, near Historic Properties and just minutes from downtown. It’s a key port in Canada cruise itineraries, typically part of longer Canada voyages. You’re in the heart of the action from the moment you step off the gangway.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Los Angeles
Shore excursions to explore in Los Angeles
blocks.text: Choose from curated tours that highlight Los Angeles’ most compelling features: classic Hollywood, beach towns, science meets archaeology and more.

blocks.heading: Beach Cities of L.A.: Venice & Santa Monica
blocks.text: You’ll be whisked to Venice’s canal district where residential streets meet street‑art and eclectic ambiance, then continue to the boardwalk at Venice Beach with its street vendors, murals and sand enthusiasts. Finally, Santa Monica’s pier and beach await — you’ll ride the solar‑powered Ferris wheel, hunt for stuffed animals and shop at 3rd Street Promenade before returning to the ship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Getty Center Museum & Santa Monica
blocks.text: You’ll start with a coach ride up the hill to the Getty Center, where an electric tram rises into manicured gardens and one of the world’s best collections of Impressionist art awaits. After that, you’ll head to the beach town of Santa Monica: stroll the historic pier, feel the salty breeze and poke through boutiques at the 3rd Street Promenade. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: La Brea Tar Pits & Griffith Observatory for Families
blocks.text: This tour begins underground in the tar pits where remnants from Ice Age mammals still sit (and the odd thrill of history still oozes out of the earth). Then trade earth for sky as you’re off to the Griffith Observatory, with hands‑on science exhibits and sweeping city‑and‑space views that make you stretch your neck in the best way possible. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hollywood Star Tour
blocks.text: Hop in a site-seer-style open‑air van and race through L.A.’s high points. Via motorcoach you’ll hit Hollywood Boulevard and the Walk of Fame, then drive through Beverly Hills and along the Sunset Strip. The highlight? A turn past the famous Hollywood sign with a camera full of envy‑inspiring memories. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Universal Studios On Your Own
blocks.text: Spend a half‑day in the heart of your favorite movies: ride the “Jurassic Park” coaster, brace for the shark from “Jaws” on the Tram Tour and see real sets in action at Universal Studios. When you’re done living out film-based fantasies, hit nearby CityWalk for dining and shopping under L.A.’s sky. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Los Angeles
blocks.text: This guided half‑day tour is the perfect shortcut for the curious. A motorcoach takes you downtown past the Civic Center and Music Center, then along Hollywood Boulevard to TCL Chinese Theatre and the Walk of Fame. Then you’ll cruise the Sunset Strip and feel the pulse of the city’s celebrity playground. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in New York
blocks.text: This is no warm-up act; New York City hits you with its full Broadway energy right out of the gate. Skyscrapers, delis, bridges, bagels and monuments — it’s all here, jammed into a city that doesn’t sleep, whisper or take it easy. You’ll cross boroughs, spot legends (buildings and people) and see the setting of probably half the movies you've ever watched. This is the Big Apple, baby, and it’s you

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in New York City
blocks.text: New York City cruises give you full-access passes to everything: museums, nightlife, skyline views and bridges that carry more history than some countries. Every borough’s got a story, and shore excursions into this city let you read a few chapters before you’ve even left the pier.

blocks.heading: Hop On Hop Off New York City: Explore 2-Day Ticket (from Manhattan)
blocks.text: With 19+ stops and the freedom to explore at your pace, this open-top bus tour covers both the Uptown and Downtown loops of the city. Cruise past Grand Central, Central Park, the Empire State Building and One World Trade Center while enjoying live commentary or a multi-language audio tour. It’s education and entertainment at your discretion. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: New York Highlights Scenic Drive
blocks.text: This air-conditioned blitz tour hits Manhattan’s highlights from the comfort of a motorcoach. You’ll coast past Central Park, Times Square, Radio City Music Hall and Lower Manhattan while your guide drops the history, the drama and the neighborhood gossip. It’s a four-hour snapshot of some of the city’s most famous icons. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: New York City At Night
blocks.text: Experience the city when it glows (literally). You’ll cross the Brooklyn Bridge for sweeping skyline views, cruise past architectural gems and dive into Times Square for an hour of pure sensory overload. The Chrysler Building, Rockefeller Center and Lady Liberty herself all make cameo appearances, so make sure you’ve got enough space on your phone for all the pictures. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of New York City: Rockefeller Center, 9/11 Memorial & Battery Park
blocks.text: You’ll start at Lincoln Center, pass Central Park and then rise up at the Top of the Rock with panoramic views from Rockefeller Plaza. There's time to explore on your own before continuing past Madison Square Garden and Wall Street, with a glimpse of the 9/11 Memorial and a drive through Chinatown, SoHo and the South Street Seaport. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Statue of Liberty & Ellis Island
blocks.text: Board a ferry and make your way to Liberty Island where Lady Liberty awaits eternally depicted in 305 feet of copper and freedom. Then head to Ellis Island, the gateway for over 12 million immigrants, where you’ll explore the Immigration Museum and stand where countless future Americans began their stories. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Manhattan to Brooklyn: Walk the Brooklyn Bridge
blocks.text: Walk the 1.5-mile stretch across one of the most iconic New York City bridges, with skyline views and the occasional falcon sighting along the way. Your guide will pause for Revolutionary War stories and scenic stops at Fulton Landing. After the bridge, you’ll drive past landmarks like Times Square and the Financial District. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Newport
blocks.text: Newport’s past still lingers in its mansions, rocky coastline and centuries-old streets. Roam its shoreline walks or explore its grand estates and you’ll see why this small coastal city became one of America’s most celebrated summer destinations.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Newport
blocks.text: Newport’s storied avenues and oceanfront vistas come to life on guided excursions that highlight the city’s mansions, coastal drives and rich colonial history. These tours offer an easy way to experience the best of this classic New England port in one relaxing day ashore.

blocks.heading: Rose Island Lighthouse & Harbor Cruise
blocks.text: Sail across Narragansett Bay on a narrated harbor cruise that introduces you to Newport’s maritime heritage. Then step ashore at Rose Island Lighthouse, a restored 19th-century beacon surrounded by coastal wildlife and historic fortifications. Explore the working lighthouse and museum before returning to the pier with a new appreciation for life on the bay. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Newport, The Breakers & Marble House
blocks.text: Step inside two of Newport’s most iconic Gilded Age estates on a tour that pairs history with stunning ocean views. Walk through The Breakers’ soaring halls, then continue to Marble House to see its grand rooms and elegant stonework. Along the way, enjoy a scenic drive through the historic district that once defined America’s summer social scene. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Grand Mansions & Ocean Scenic Drive
blocks.text: Take in Newport’s coastal beauty as your guide leads you along Ocean Drive, where rocky coves and open water frame the city’s celebrated “summer cottages.” Then tour either The Elms or Rosecliff, both noted for ornate interiors and landscaped grounds that reflect the lifestyle of the families who vacationed here during Newport’s golden era. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Newport Scenic Drive & Touro Synagogue
blocks.text: Trace centuries of history on a relaxed drive through Newport’s colonial streets, past steepled churches and stately landmarks. A visit to Touro Synagogue reveals the story of the nation’s oldest standing synagogue, followed by time to explore the Loeb Visitors Center. Afterward, choose to continue sightseeing downtown or return to the tender pier. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Newport Cliff Walk & The Breakers
blocks.text: This excursion blends ocean scenery with architectural splendor. Begin with a guided walk along the Cliff Walk, where crashing waves and hidden coves border the back lawns of Newport’s grand homes. Then visit The Breakers to see intricate details, rare materials and sweeping views that made this landmark one of the most admired estates of its time. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Newport Highlights by Land & Sea
blocks.text: See Newport from two perspectives as you tour its historic neighborhoods by land before boarding a classic wooden vessel for a harbor cruise. Landmarks like Trinity Church, Redwood Library and the mansions of Bellevue Avenue provide a glimpse of the city’s past, while the cruise offers relaxing views of the shoreline that shaped Newport’s identity. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Portland
blocks.text: Portland, Maine cruises serve up lighthouse tours, schooner sails, scenic railroads and one very serious lobster obsession. Pick your adventure and let Princess excursions do the rest.

blocks.heading: The White Mountains by Conway Scenic Railroad (Summer Sailings)
blocks.text: Same ride, different backdrop — the summer edition offers wildflowers, bright green hills and sun‑dappled forest views that look like someone turned up the saturation. Includes the same rail nostalgia, same elevation climb and same Instagram‑worthy final stop at Crawford Notch Station. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kennebunkport & Scenic Cruise
blocks.text: This half‑day hits the sweet spot of salty air and star‑studded nostalgia. You’ll cruise past Walker’s Point (the Bush family’s oceanfront compound) and get a wave of presidential history while hugging Maine’s rugged coast. Dock Square gives you time for shopping, café‑hopping or just people‑watching in Kennebunkport before heading back. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Portland Highlights & Lighthouse
blocks.text: Roll through Portland’s historic neighborhoods and along the Eastern Promenade, where Casco Bay views practically slap the phone out of your hand. The big finish? A stop at Fort Williams Park and the iconic Portland Head Light: 1797 vintage, George Washington approved and likely to make your inner lighthouse enthusiast very, very happy. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Maine Lobster Bake on Peaks Island
blocks.text: Hop a ferry across Casco Bay to Peaks Island, past House Island’s former quarantine station, for a ‘Downeast’ lobster bake with the works. We’re talking clam chowder, mussels, potatoes, corn, dessert and, of course, a 1¼ lb lobster cooked to perfection. After lunch, cruise back to the mainland or linger downtown and let your waistband regret nothing. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Portland Highlights & Schooner Adventure
blocks.text: Cruise Casco Bay aboard an 88‑foot tall ship after a narrated drive through Portland’s greatest hits, including Portland Head Light. Join the crew and help hoist the sails or just sit back and watch the harbor seals. Bonus: the pier is a five‑minute walk from the schooner, giving you time for one more beer or bakery stop on the way back. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The White Mountains by Conway Scenic Railroad (Fall Sailings)
blocks.text: All aboard for a 7.5‑hour jaunt through New England forests, rivers and trestle bridges. After a scenic ride to North Conway, hop on a 1950s railcar for a two‑hour narrated journey up to 1,886 feet of pure mountain majesty. Peak fall foliage, small‑town charm and zero cell reception (which, trust us, is a good thing). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Quebec
blocks.text: Visiting Québec City means stepping into yesterday — but in the best way possible. With its old‑stone façades, conversational French drifting down the streets and the only remaining walled city north of Mexico, this place delivers classy history without any pretense. The Old Port area puts you right within walking distance of Old Québec’s charming architecture, making it perfect for Québec cruises

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Quebec
blocks.text: Want how‑to‑history, architecture up‑close or rural French‑Canadian flavour? These tours deliver it all without the hassle.

blocks.heading: An Evening at the Sugar Shack with Dinner
blocks.text: Culture and history are good, but you know what’s even better? Culture and history you can eat. In the evening head out to a sugar‑shack style dinner: maple museum, folklore music, a maple taffy pull and hearty Québecois cuisine served family style. It’s educational, tasty and comfortably rustic. Just be sure to check your itinerary; this excursion isn’t available on every cruise. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Grand Exploration of Québec & Lunch
blocks.text: Begin with a scenic drive to Île d’Orléans and the thunderous Montmorency Falls whose 272‑foot drop outdoes Niagara’s (at a fraction of the crowds). Next stop: Sainte‑Anne‑de‑Beaupré, whose basilica draws pilgrims from around the world. After lunch of French‑Canadian fare, head into the Upper Town promontory Cap‑Diamant, browse the terrace at Château Frontenac, then descend to Place Royale in Lowe

blocks.heading: Discover Québec with Observatory & Governor’s House Visit
blocks.text: This 3.5‑hour drive and walk tour begins at La Citadelle and the Governor’s House where art and river vistas meet. Then pass Château Frontenac and pause at the Plains of Abraham (Parc des Champs de Bataille) where the British and French clashed in 1759. Wrap the tour with a visit to the Observatoire de la Capitale at 221 metres above sea level for stunning city‑and‑river panorama. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Rendez‑Vous at Wendake Cultural Village
blocks.text: Before anyone in France had ever heard of the New World, the Native peoples of Canada (now referred to as First Nations) were already well established. Leave the ship and head minutes into Wendake to learn about Huron‑Wendat heritage. From longhouse visits to food‑preserving demonstrations at the smokehouse and a walk to the Kabir Kouba waterfall, you’ll get a respectful, vivid look at First Natio

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Ste‑Anne‑de‑Beaupré, Montmorency Falls & Copper House Art Experience
blocks.text: Start with Montmorency Falls’ natural spectacle. Then immerse yourself in metal‑art at the Copper House (Maison Gilles) with a hands‑on demo and tea plus a canelé. After you’ve had your fill, finish at the shrine of Ste‑Anne‑de‑Beaupré, where religious tradition and craft merge in a uniquely neo‑Roman setting. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Walking Tour of Historic Québec
blocks.text: Explore on foot the layers of Québec City: from Upper to Lower Town through 17th‑ to 19th‑century architecture, ride the funicular, visit the Basilica and Convent of San Francisco, pass by the House of Osambela and return to the pier via cobbled streets and heritage corridors. It’s everything that makes Québec fascinating in one heart-healthy hike. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Quebec
blocks.text: Your vessel docks right in the heart of the city: the Ross Gaudreault Terminal (Wharves 21/22) sits at 84 Dalhousie Street and is steps from Old Québec and the Petit‑Champlain district. For Canada & New England itineraries, Québec City is a key port that lets you slip into Europe in North America (without the jet lag).

blocks.heading: Things to do in Saguenay
blocks.text: Saguenay offers a stunning mix of natural beauty and cultural charm, from dramatic fjord landscapes to vibrant local art and cuisine. Whether you prefer outdoor exploration or discovering Québecois heritage, this port invites you to experience its unique character at a relaxed pace.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Saguenay
blocks.text: Take in Saguenay’s breathtaking fjords, charming villages and rich culture through a variety of immersive shore excursions. Whether you’re drawn to scenic landscapes or local traditions, there are experiences suited for every type of traveler.

blocks.heading: Saguenay Heritage Route
blocks.text: Enjoy a scenic 3.5 hour sightseeing tour filled with memorable photo stops as you travel through Chicoutimi, Arvida and Jonquière. See historic landmarks, unique neighborhoods and charming local sites that highlight the region’s rich culture and industrial heritage LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Saguenay
blocks.text: Enjoy a 3.5 hour excursion that starts with a visit to the Fjord Museum to learn about the area’s unique history and geology. Capture photos of the impressive 70-foot Ha! Ha! Pyramid before continuing to the Pulp Mill of Chicoutimi. Finish at Le Chevrier du Nord goat farm, where you’ll see traditional mohair processing. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hiking Saguenay National Park
blocks.text: Hailed as one of the world’s top hiking networks, this 4-hour adventure in Saguenay Fjord National Park leads you along an intermediate 2-mile trail with breathtaking scenery at every turn. Follow your guide through lush forest, keep an eye out for local wildlife and take in sweeping views of the fjord and surrounding mountains. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Sea Kayaking at Saguenay National Park
blocks.text: Enjoy an up-close look at the breathtaking Saguenay Fjord as you glide across smooth, glassy waters in a two-person kayak. Paddle beneath towering granite cliffs, watch for wildlife and soak in views of Cape Trinity and the iconic Our Lady of the Saguenay statue. After your scenic journey, return to the Visitor Center to browse local shops before heading back. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Chicoutimi City Sights
blocks.text: This 2.25 hour excursion offers a captivating journey through Chicoutimi’s rich history, complete with scenic photo stops. Visit the famed Little White House, glimpse the historic Pulp Mill, and pass landmarks like the Fjord Museum. Before returning to the pier, enjoy a final highlight—the striking Ha! Ha! Pyramid, a unique monument honoring the region’s past. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: The Craftsman Road-Meet the Makers
blocks.text: On this immersive 3.5-hour experience, meet the artisans of Saguenay while taking in the region’s charming scenery. Visit a family-run cheese factory for a taste of tradition, watch a master glassmaker at work and stop at a local alpaca farm to learn how natural fibers are transformed into beautiful products. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in St. John's
blocks.text: St. John’s has a character you feel as soon as you arrive, shaped by its fishing-port roots, steep hills and bright row houses. The city mixes maritime history with a creative streak, making it easy to spend a day wandering between scenic viewpoints and the neighborhoods that give Newfoundland its unmistakable charm.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in St. John's
blocks.text: St. John’s offers a mix of coastal scenery and historic landmarks, and Princess shore excursions make it easy to experience the highlights without worrying about local logistics. From windswept viewpoints to museums and lively neighborhoods, each tour brings a different side of Newfoundland into focus.

blocks.heading: Walking Tour of St. John's
blocks.text: See St. John’s up close on a guided walking tour that winds through its historic downtown. Pass Jellybean Row’s brightly painted homes, explore narrow streets rebuilt after the Great Fire of 1892 and learn how merchants and mariners shaped the city’s character. The route also includes Water Street Historic District, one of the oldest commercial areas in North America. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of St. John's: Cape Spear Lighthouse, St. John's & Signal Hill
blocks.text: Take in Newfoundland’s dramatic coastline and historic landmarks on this half-day tour that begins at Cape Spear, the oldest surviving lighthouse in the province and the easternmost point in North America. Continue through St. John’s to see colorful row houses and civic buildings before heading up Signal Hill, where Marconi received the first transatlantic wireless signal. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: St. John's Highlights, Signal Hill & Historic Church
blocks.text: See the city’s past and present on a guided drive through St. John’s, from Victorian wooden homes to stone churches that reflect its colonial roots. Stop at the Commissariat House, Government House and the Garrison Church for photos, then continue to Signal Hill. Here you’ll visit Cabot Tower and learn how this rugged headland shaped both early communication and local history. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: St. John's, Signal Hill, Rooms Museum & Churches
blocks.text: Explore the cultural heart of St. John’s as you travel its oldest streets, lined with colorful wooden buildings and centuries-old churches. Visit Signal Hill for sweeping views of the Atlantic and learn about the site’s military and communication milestones. Then tour The Rooms Museum, home to art, archives and exhibits that reveal Newfoundland’s natural history and vibrant heritage. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Signal Hill & Geo-Centre
blocks.text: Uncover Newfoundland’s geological story with a visit to the Johnson GEO CENTRE, an award-winning museum built into 500-million-year-old rock. Hands-on exhibits reveal the forces that shaped the island’s cliffs and coastline. Afterward, head to Signal Hill for another look at the dramatic landscape and a chance to photograph the harbor, rugged headlands and sweeping Atlantic views. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Port Wine, Beer & Newfoundland Screech-In
blocks.text: Taste the spirit of Newfoundland on a relaxed outing through St. John’s food and drink scene. Sample port wine and local brews, then join in a traditional Screech-In ceremony that celebrates the province’s humor and hospitality. Along the way you’ll learn how local ingredients, maritime history and modern craft makers influence the flavors of this lively coastal city. LEARN MORE
