blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Sydney
blocks.text: Cape Breton’s landscapes and culture shine brightest on shore excursions. Whether you’re drawn to Scottish heritage, maritime views or hands-on museums, these tours make it easy to experience Sydney’s most storied places.

blocks.heading: Spirited Sydney - A Historic Walking Tour
blocks.text: Join a costumed guide for a walk through Sydney’s oldest neighborhoods, where folklore and ghost stories blend with real local history. Visit heritage homes, hidden lanes and atmospheric sites tied to legends that have circulated for generations. It’s a playful, engaging way to learn about the city’s past while exploring on foot. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Sydney Highlights & Coastal Drive
blocks.text: Take a relaxed introduction to Sydney as you follow a scenic coastal route lined with historic homes, 18th-century landmarks and views across the harbor. Stops include the Whitney Pier Historical Museum, where more than fifty cultural groups shaped the community, and Fort Petrie, a World War II observation post with sweeping waterfront vistas. You’ll finish with enough time at the cruise terminal

blocks.heading: Celtic Heritage: Sounds of Cape Breton
blocks.text: Experience Cape Breton’s musical heartbeat with a performance that showcases the island’s distinct Gaelic traditions. After meeting beneath the iconic giant fiddle, settle in for live fiddle tunes, step dancing and storytelling that reflect the region’s deep Scottish roots. You’ll also have time to explore the Marine Terminal’s shops and enjoy local treats like traditional oatcakes. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Cape Breton: Bell Museum, Baddeck & Bras d'Or Lake
blocks.text: Travel through rolling highlands and cross the Seal Island Bridge on your way to Baddeck, a charming lakeside village tied to Alexander Graham Bell. Explore the Bell Museum’s extensive collection of inventions, then stroll through town for lake views and boutique shopping. The route back delivers more panoramas of Bras d’Or Lake and the forested hills surrounding it. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Fortress of Louisbourg National Historic Site
blocks.text: Step into the year 1744 at Fortress Louisbourg, where costumed guides, reconstructed streets and waterfront workshops recreate life in an 18th-century French town. Explore homes, fortifications and blacksmith forges before wandering the grounds at your own pace. The drive to and from Sydney reveals rolling green hills and glimpses of the Mira River along the way. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Road Trip Along the Cabot Trail in Cape Breton
blocks.text: Follow one of Canada’s most celebrated routes as you wind along rugged coastline, forested mountains and sweeping viewpoints overlooking St. Ann’s Bay. This scenic drive includes photo stops at highland lookoffs and time in Ingonish, where you can relax over lunch near the national park. Keep your camera ready — whales often appear offshore in summer. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Vancouver: Stanley Park Visit & City Highlights Drive
blocks.text: Get the vibe without the footwork. This relaxed coach tour rolls past Vancouver’s most celebrated neighborhoods before stopping in Stanley Park for up-close views of its totem poles and forest-lined shores. English Bay Beach offers a peaceful pause before you circle back to port. It’s the kind of slow-paced, high-reward outing that hits all the right notes. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Sea to Sky Gondola Experience & Shannon Falls
blocks.text: Ride the Sea to Sky Highway to Shannon Falls and watch a 1,000‑foot cascade drop into view, then climb aboard the gondola up to a viewpoint 2,903 feet above sea level where you’ve got two‑plus hours to hike, walk the Sky Pilot Suspension Bridge or simply soak it all in at the Summit Lodge. blocks.heading: Stanley Park Visit & City Highlights Drive with Airport Transfer
blocks.text: If your cruise ends in Vancouver, disembarkation day doesn’t have to be a waiting game. Instead, squeeze every last drop out of Vancouver with a scenic city tour that hits all the highlights: Chinatown, Gastown and Stanley Park, where rainforest trails and coastal views meet totem poles and English Bay backdrops. It’s the kind of cultural send-off you want before heading to the airport. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Northwest Exploration & Suspension Bridge Tour

A comfy van whisks you between stops while your guide drops city facts and neighborhood lore. Cheers indeed. LEARN MORE

blocks.text: The Caribbean is all rhythm and color — steel drums in the streets, jerk chicken on the grill and waves warm enough to swim before breakfast. It’s the perfect all-you-can-experience cruise buffet: you sail, you sleep and you wake up somewhere new. And as for options? Why cruise the Caribbean?
blocks.text: The Caribbean really does vacations right: picture-perfect beaches, bright-blue waters and vibes as chill as the frozen drink in your hand. On a cruise with Princess, you’ll explore multiple islands – why settle for one when you can hop between several? – and enjoy the best of each destination.

blocks.heading: Explore Nature’s playground
blocks.text: The Caribbean has been a land of adventure for hundreds of years. Snorkel through a coral reef teeming with life, go off-road deep into the rainforest or sail out to explore a shipwreck.

blocks.heading: Beaches and sunshine
blocks.text: Let the soft sands and warm winds melt all your worries away. The beaches of the Caribbean are legendary for their natural beauty and tranquil turquoise waters.

blocks.heading: Culture and history
blocks.text: The culture and history of the Caribbean is rich, varied and deep. Walk the docks Nelson's Dockyard, taste and hear the deep West African influences in everyday Caribbean life, and experience the uniqueness of each island.

blocks.heading: Why cruise the Caribbean with Princess?
blocks.text: 23 islands every season. Our largest number of itineraries. And new for 2026-2027, 11 ships sailing the region, our most yet. That includes Star Princess®, who makes her North American debut here.

blocks.heading: Isla Tropicale, Roatan, Honduras
blocks.text: Relax and discover the spectacular blend of nature, wildlife, and island beauty. Enjoy your day exploring or relaxing in the pool and swim up bar while experiencing a day of sun, beaches and the aquamarine waters of the Caribbean.

blocks.heading: We sail the Caribbean year-round
blocks.text: Each season has a personality all its own. Summer is a time for family fun in the sun. Fall invites the adventurous to immerse themselves in the islands. Winter is marked by festivals and other celebrations.

blocks.heading: The Wharf Restaurant & Bar
blocks.text: For waterfront dining, The Wharf is a must-visit. Located at the edge of Seven Mile Beach, this upscale restaurant specializes in fresh seafood and Caribbean flavors. Time your visit to watch the tarpon feedings at sunset—a unique spectacle that pairs perfectly with a tropical cocktail. With an extensive wine list and romantic ambiance, The Wharf is ideal for couples or special occasions.

blocks.heading: Agua Restaurant & Lounge
blocks.text: Located at Camana Bay, Agua Restaurant blends Mediterranean and Peruvian influences with local Caribbean ingredients. Known for its ceviche and seafood dishes, Agua offers a sophisticated dining experience in a modern setting. It’s perfect for foodies seeking innovative flavors and creative presentations.

blocks.heading: Cayman Cabana Oceanside Restobar
blocks.text: Set in George Town, Cayman Cabana features farm-to-table dishes made with fresh, locally sourced ingredients. blocks.heading: Hell
blocks.text: Encompassed by rich greenery, this forest of black limestone formations is a sight to be seen. From the viewing deck, dark green iguanas can be seen perched atop of the jagged structures known as Hell. Just a few steps away lies a fiery red building — Hell’s Post Office — where visitors are encouraged to send playful postcards to loved ones at home and recount their seemingly tall tales.

blocks.text: Where the land meets the sea lies four stone-lined steps and a small pebbled platform holding the ancient memorial of ten vessels that became shipwrecked in a nearby reef. blocks.heading: Things to do in Costa Maya
blocks.text: Costa Maya is a gem on Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula in the Western Caribbean, where you can step into a tropical paradise and into ancient Mayan history. Climb towering temples from a millennium ago, see a village where locals still keep Mayan customs alive and relax on a pillowy soft white sand beach surrounded by palm trees. Costa Maya has it all: culture, history and natural beauty.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Costa Maya
blocks.text: From ancient Mayan ruins to white sand beaches and turquoise waters, Costa Maya has something for every kind of traveler. Whether you love adventure or are looking for a little sunshine and relaxation, these are some of the shore excursions to consider when you visit with Princess:

blocks.heading: Mayan Cultural Experience & Lunch
blocks.text: Immerse yourself in Costa Mayan culture by visiting this contemporary Mayan community that’s been built up around the remains of an ancient Mayan settlement. There are ruins right in the middle of town. Your guide will take you into an authentic Mayan house to see how committed the locals are to keeping their customs alive. Then finish your experience with a delicious traditional meal including bu

blocks.heading: Best of Costa Maya: Chacchoben Mayan Ruins
blocks.text: Step back nearly 1,000 years ago by visiting Chacchoben, or “The Place of Red Corn,” an ancient Mayan site where archeologists found ceremonial offerings dating back a millennium. At this well-preserved complex, you can see some original stucco and a large mural — as well as climb the Gran Basamento for unbeatable views. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Snorkeling by Power Catamaran & Margaritas
blocks.text: The waters just off of Costa Maya are home to the world's second-largest coral reef. Dive in to marvel at this underwater paradise where tropical fish, rays and turtles swim around you, as you enjoy some of the best coral formations on the coast. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: 4X4 Scenic Safari & Beach
blocks.text: See Costa Maya in a unique way by riding in a Jeep Renegade along the beach, through colorful villages and through the stunning scenery Western Mexico has to offer. You’ll see the small fishing village Mahahual where many descendants of the Mayans still live, as well as get a few hours to spend on the white powder shores of Pleasure Beach. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Lost Mayan Kingdom Adventure Park
blocks.text: Ready for adventure? Visit this adventure park where you can slip and slide down towering waterslides, get a bird’s eye view of the whole park on a zipline course or ride the 800-foot Kukulcan Zip Coaster. Looking to take it easy? Spend the day floating the lazy river and enjoying the sunshine and drinks. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Things to do in Barbados
blocks.text: Barbados offers a blend of relaxation and adventure, all centered around cultural experiences. Nature lovers can explore Harrison’s Cave, an awe-inspiring underground wonder filled with dramatic stalactites, stalagmites and flowing waterfalls. Sun-seekers will love the pristine shores of Carlisle Bay, perfect for swimming and snorkeling. History buffs can step back in time at the Mount Gay Rum Dis

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Barbados
blocks.text: For those looking to make the most of their time ashore, Princess has a selection of curated excursions that highlight the island’s natural beauty with adventure-filled activities.

blocks.heading: Harrison's Cave Signature Park Pass
blocks.text: Journey underground to explore Harrison’s Cave, a stunning limestone cavern filled with crystal-clear pools, towering formations and flowing streams. Ride a tram through its illuminated chambers, then stroll the nearby nature trail and bird aviary. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Barbados: Sunbury Plantation, Tropical Garden & Scenic Drive
blocks.text: Step into Barbados’ colonial past with a visit to Sunbury Plantation, a beautifully preserved 17th-century estate that offers a glimpse into the island’s sugarcane heritage. You can wander through rooms filled with antique mahogany furniture and historic carriages before heading to a lush tropical garden, home to vibrant Caribbean flora. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Barbados Coast to Coast Scenic Drive
blocks.text: Relax and take in Barbados’ natural beauty on an island tour that spans both the Caribbean and Atlantic coasts. Journey through quaint fishing villages and sprawling sugarcane fields, with stops at some of the island’s most scenic viewpoints. Along the way, you’ll have the chance to capture stunning photos of turquoise waters and rugged rock formations, all from the comfort of an air-conditioned v

blocks.heading: St. Nicholas Abbey, Railway & Rum
blocks.text: Discover the history and flavor of Barbados with a visit to St. Nicholas Abbey, one of the island’s oldest plantation houses that is now home to an active rum distillery. Tour the restored 17th-century Jacobean estate, ride a charming heritage railway through sugarcane fields and watch as fresh sugarcane is transformed into rich, aged rum. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Bridgetown by Bajan Bus & Three-Beach Hop
blocks.text: Experience the bustling energy of Bridgetown aboard a colorful Bajan bus, passing through streets lined with historic buildings and lively markets. After exploring the capital, you can set off on a beach-hopping adventure, stopping at three of Barbados’ most popular beaches. Whether you choose to swim, sunbathe, or simply relax on the soft golden sands, this excursion offers the perfect combinatio

blocks.heading: Sunbury Plantation, Scenic Drive & Lunch
blocks.text: Discover a well-preserved plantation home and savor a delicious island-style lunch after exploring local art at a vibrant pottery studio and gallery. Capture one last moment with a photo stop at the historic Christ Church Parish Church. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Andromeda Botanical Gardens & Scenic Country Drive
blocks.text: Explore Barbados’ natural beauty with a scenic drive to Bathsheba Beach, where dramatic rock formations rise from the surf. Stroll through the lush Andromeda Botanical Gardens, home to exotic plants, lily ponds and towering palms. The Barbados gardens are especially beautiful during the winter travel season (December through April), perfect for travelers sailing during peak cruise season. LEARN MO

blocks.heading: Things to do in Bonaire
blocks.text: You’ll find golden beaches along protected reefs and sunlit lagoons as you travel through Bonaire’s natural paradise. Bonaire National Marine Park draws snorkelers and divers from around the world with its vibrant coral gardens and crystal-clear waters. Cruise ships dock in Kralendijk, Bonaire’s primary cruise port, where most itineraries allow approximately 7–10 hours ashore to explore the island

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Bonaire
blocks.text: For those looking to make the most of their time ashore, Princess has a selection of curated excursions that highlight the island’s natural beauty with adventure-filled activities.

blocks.heading: Bonaire Cultural Heritage
blocks.text: The many cultural and natural attractions of Bonaire are yours to discover on this sight-filled three-hour adventure. Settle into the motorcoach and begin your drive along the north side of the island. You'll drive by the Beach of 1,000 Steps, actually only 67, that lead to a picturesque white-sand beach studded with coral and surrounded by rugged cliffs. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Snorkeling in Bonaire National Marine Park
blocks.text: Slip into the warm, impossibly clear waters of Bonaire National Marine Park, a world-renowned snorkeling and diving destination. Schools of tropical fish weave through vibrant elkhorn and brain coral, while sea turtles glide gracefully through this protected underwater paradise. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Klein Bonaire Beach Escape
blocks.text: Just offshore, Klein Bonaire is an uninhabited island where powdery white sand and translucent waters create a secluded retreat. A quick water taxi ride excursion to Klein Bonaire brings you to this untouched paradise, perfect for swimming, sunbathing or simply enjoying the quiet beauty of the Caribbean. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: South and East Coast Drive
blocks.text: Bonaire’s rugged coastline is full of surprises, from towering cacti to centuries-old salt pans that shimmer pink under the Caribbean sun. This scenic drive along the island’s south and east coasts reveals hidden coves, crashing waves and panoramic views unlike anywhere else in the region. You might even see pink flamingos in the distance on the South & East Coast Drive by 4WD excursion. LEARN MOR

blocks.heading: Bonaire Highlights & Beach
blocks.text: Combine sightseeing and beach time on this relaxed half-day adventure. Begin your sightseeing drive toward the southern part of the island, taking in picturesque views as you head to the original slave huts that were used as shelters for the slaves working in the beautiful, pink-colored salt flats, which you will see from up close as well during a short photo stop at the Salt Flats. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Scenic Tour of Kralendijk via Eco-Powered Tuk Tuk
blocks.text: See the sights of Bonaire's colorful capital on a fun and eco-friendly tuk tuk. Climb aboard this open air electric vehicle, a nimble and fun way to traverse the town. Your one hour tour begins with an introduction to historic Kralendijk, Bonaire's spirited capital. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Cozumel
blocks.text: Cozumel is an island in Mexico that’s home to some of the best preserved Mayan ruins that are 800 years old — and some stunning beaches with dazzling arrays of wildlife hiding just beneath the waves. Cozumel is also one of the Caribbean’s most popular cruise destinations, known for its clear waters, coral reefs, and cultural attractions. Spend the day exploring the temples of Tulum — a walled Maya

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Cozumel
blocks.text: From Mayan ruins to mouthwatering Mexican food, there’s something for everyone in Cozumel. These are some of the exciting activities that await you when you visit Cozumel with Princess:

blocks.heading: Mexican Cooking Class, Lunch & Beach
blocks.text: Is your stomach growling? Good! During this authentic cooking class where you’ll learn to make traditional Mexican food, you’ll be assigned a station with all the utensils you need and have an expert chef there to guide you through. Then you’ll get to feast on your own creation — and enjoy the open bar and Mexican wines available. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Tulum Mayan Ruins
blocks.text: Step into ancient history as you explore these 800 year old Mayan ruins that make up the best preserved coastal site. Learn about Mayan history from your expert guide as you visit El Castillo, The Temple of the Descending God, The Temple of the Water and the Temple of the Frescos. Don’t forget to take in some stunning seaside views. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Tulum Mayan Ruins, Beach Club & Lunch
blocks.text: Can’t decide if you want a day at the beach or to see Mayan ruins? Don’t choose and head out on this excursion where you’ll visit the 800 year old temples of Tulum before heading to the beach to cool off, soak in some sun and shop among the seaside markets. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: VIP Catamaran Sail & Snorkel with Lunch
blocks.text: Hop on this VIP Catamaran and head out on the turquoise Caribbean waters. Dive into the sea to find a rainbow of tropical fish and maybe a sea turtle or two. Then dry off by lounging on the open deck and enjoying the sun-soaked Caribbean weather. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Cozumel Beach Escape
blocks.text: Unwind and relax for a while on a pristine Caribbean beach with pillowy soft sand and cool azure waters. Spend the day how you want: snorkel near the shore to spot fish, head out on a paddleboard for unforgettable island views or get your heart racing with a ride down the zipline. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Xcaret Eco-Archaeological Park
blocks.text: Sample the highlights of Cozumel by visiting the Xcaret Eco-Archaeological Park where you can do everything from visit Mayan ruins and explore a reconstructed village to explore an aviary and butterfly garden. See wildlife like jaguars, turtles and stingrays before jumping into the underground river. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Things to do in Grand Cayman
blocks.text: Sun-drenched shores, hidden caves and one-of-a-kind encounters: Grand Cayman delivers. The island is a world-class snorkeling and diving destination, with vibrant coral reefs, shipwrecks and crystal-clear waters just offshore. Wander the duty-free shops and waterfront restaurants of George Town, the British colonial capital, or sample local specialties like conch fritters and rundown stew. For a m

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Grand Cayman
blocks.text: For those looking to make the most of their time ashore, Princess has a selection of curated excursions that highlight Grand Cayman's natural beauty with adventure-filled activities. Princess excursions include guaranteed ship return, professional local guides and pre-vetted operators, so you can relax and explore with peace of mind.

blocks.heading: Discover the unique landscape of Hell
blocks.text: Hell isn’t fiery red in the Caymans—it’s jagged, black limestone stretching across West Bay. This otherworldly formation known as “Hell” looks like something from another planet. Don’t forget to stop by the post office and send a postcard from the underworld during your Coast-to-Coast Scenic Island Drive, Hell & Beach excursion. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Swim with stingrays at Stingray City
blocks.text: During the Stingray Sandbar & Cayman Highlights excursion, hop into waist-deep waters where southern stingrays glide around you like underwater kites. They’re curious, social and surprisingly smooth to the touch. At Stingray City, you don’t just watch the marine life in their natural habitat—you become part of it. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Relax on Seven Mile Beach
blocks.text: Powdery white sand meets water so clear it looks unreal. Seven Mile Beach is the kind of place where time slows down, whether you’re floating in the shallows or stretching out beneath a palm tree. The Land & Sea Combination excursion is the perfect opportunity to unwind on Seven Mile Beach during your stay. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Explore the Cayman Crystal Caves
blocks.text: On the Crystal Cave Adventure excursion, twisting roots and hanging stalactites frame the entrance to a subterranean wonderland. Inside, glistening rock formations stretch toward hidden pools, creating a scene straight out of a fantasy novel. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Visit the Cayman Turtle Centre
blocks.text: Stand inches away from a green sea turtle, a species that has called these waters home for centuries. Conservation efforts at the Cayman Turtle Centre help protect them, and for a moment, you get to be part of that story. The best way to see this wonder is through our excursion: Best of Grand Cayman: Cayman Turtle Centre, Hell, Tortuga Rum Cake & Scenic Drive. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Things to do in Grenada
blocks.text: On one of our cruises to Grenada, trek into Grand Etang National Park, where towering ferns and wild orchids thrive along misty hiking trails. Discover Annandale Falls, where cascading water tumbles into a jade-colored pool surrounded by tropical blooms. Stroll through Fort Frederick, an 18th-century fortress perched high above the capital, with panoramic ocean views. Or, for a taste of the island

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Grenada
blocks.text: For those looking to make the most of their time ashore, Princess has a selection of curated excursions that highlight the island’s natural beauty with adventure-filled activities.

blocks.heading: Scenic Cruise, Snorkeling, Morne Rouge & Lunch
blocks.text: Lounge on the deck of a catamaran en route to a snorkel adventure at Flamingo Bay. Your journey begins at the pier where you'll board the High Time, a 52-foot sailing catamaran. Sip fresh fruit juice or soft drinks and enjoy the scenic views along Grenada's west coast. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Fort Frederick
blocks.text: Perched on a rugged hilltop, Fort Frederick has watched over Grenada’s coastline for more than two centuries. Built by the French and later occupied by the British, this well-preserved stronghold offers panoramic views of St. George’s, the Caribbean Sea and the rolling hills beyond. The Ft. George, Ft. blocks.heading: Spice Gardens
blocks.text: The air is rich with the scent of cinnamon, nutmeg and cloves as you wander through Grenada’s spice gardens, where the island’s famous crops grow in abundance. The Spice Garden, Grenada Distillers & Grand Anse Beach excursion takes you through these fragrant plantations before heading to a distillery, where you’ll sample the island’s award-winning rum. Cap off the day with a visit to Grand Anse Be

blocks.heading: Grand Anse Beach
blocks.text: Just minutes from the cruise port, Grand Anse Beach is Grenada’s most famous stretch of shoreline — soft white sand, clear waves and plenty of space to soak up the sun. On the Harbor Cruise, Grand Anse & Morne Rouge Beaches excursion, you’ll take in the island’s coastline from the water before spending time on this pristine beach. Whether you choose to swim, snorkel or simply sip a cocktail under

blocks.heading: Kalingo Beach Escape
blocks.text: Experience Grenada's sun, sand and surf in all their glory on a three-hour seaside retreat to Kalinago Beach Resort, where you'll enjoy free time to lounge on an uncrowded shoreline fringing the picturesque Caribbean Sea. Hop in a coach for the tranquil seafront setting of Kalinago Beach Resort, nestled along the tropical environs of BBC Beach. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Grand Etang Park & Seven Sisters Waterfalls Hike
blocks.text: A trek through the Grenadian rainforest is an adventurer's dream come true. So get ready for a hike that takes you through some of the island's most breathtaking landscapes to the Seven Sisters waterfalls (be sure to wear a bathing suit under your clothes if you decide to take a dip in its pool). blocks.heading: Things to do in Guadeloupe
blocks.text: Guadeloupe is a paradise of island landscapes and rich history, offering everything from stunning beaches to adventure-filled excursions. Visitors can wander through charming colonial towns on Grande-Terre, paddle through the serene mangroves and rainforests of Basse-Terre, lounge on the white sand beaches of Sainte-Anne and Le Gosier, and immerse themselves in the island's botanical beauty. Guade

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Guadeloupe
blocks.text: For those looking to make the most of their time ashore, Guadeloupe offers a variety of guided excursions that highlight the island's natural beauty and cultural heritage. Adventure seekers can hike the trails of Guadeloupe National Park toward La Soufrière volcano or snorkel the protected reefs of the Jacques Cousteau Marine Reserve off Pigeon Island.

blocks.heading: Zoo of Guadeloupe & A Walk in the Treetops
blocks.text: To embark on this enchanting four-hour eco-adventure, set your course from the vibrant Pointe-à-Pitre and follow the mesmerizing Route de la Traversée, which leads you on a captivating odyssey across the picturesque Basse-Terre island en route to the Zoo de Guadeloupe au Parc des Mamelles, a haven for wildlife enthusiasts. VIEW EXCURSIONS

blocks.heading: 4X4 Adventure
blocks.text: Buckle up for an off-road journey through Guadeloupe’s rugged backroads and hidden gems. This thrilling ride takes you beyond the usual tourist routes, offering a closer look at the island’s untouched beauty. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Kayaking Through the Mangroves
blocks.text: Paddle through the crystal-clear waters of a protected nature reserve. As you glide along, you’ll pass dense mangrove forests, shallow lagoons and a variety of marine life. This eco-friendly adventure is a must for nature lovers. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Amazing Eco Adventure & Snorkel
blocks.text: Discover Guadeloupe’s rich marine biodiversity with a guided snorkeling and eco-tour. You’ll get to explore pristine coral reefs and swim alongside colorful fish as you learn about the region’s underwater ecosystems. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Botanic Garden & Deshaies Beach
blocks.text: Enjoy a tranquil escape at the Jardin Botanique de Deshaies, where you’ll be surrounded by exotic flowers, towering palms and tropical birds. Afterward, you can relax on the golden sands of Deshaies Beach and soak up the Caribbean sun. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Sainte Anne & Castle Point
blocks.text: Head towards the craft village of Sainte-Anne, where you'll find a lively marketplace selling a brilliant array of island treasures. From fragrant spices to brightly painted mementos and souvenirs, fill your bags with island memories before returning to the motorcoach. Continue to Castle Point (Pointes des Châteaux), one of the most visited spots in Guadeloupe. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Things to do in Martinique
blocks.text: Martinique is a French Caribbean island where you’ll find plantations, lush jungles and white sand tropical beaches. Explore the capital city where you’ll see a unique mix of Creole-style buildings and colonial architecture and cobblestone streets. Or head out to L’Habitation Belfort to see the most famous plantation house in the Caribbean and see the antique rum distillery still on the property.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Martinique
blocks.text: From historic plantation homes to lush botanical gardens, you’ll find vibrant history and beautiful natural beauty in Martinique. These are some of the shore excursions to help you explore all the best Martinique has to offer:

blocks.heading: Discovering Creole Martinique
blocks.text: You will leave Fort-de-France for Ste Marie, named after the Blessed Virgin Mary who protects the city, situated on the east coast of the island where the famous St James Rum Distillery is. Here you will be able to visit the distillery and its Père Labat museum. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Walking Tour of Fort-de-France
blocks.text: Historic landmarks in Fort-de-France, including Fort Saint-Louis and Saint-Louis Cathedral, offer a glimpse into the island’s rich cultural and colonial history. Explore the ins and outs of Martinique’s capital city of cobbled streets lined with colonial and Creole-style buildings and houses. On this walking tour, you’ll also see Fort St. Louis, the immense fortification guarding the harbor, and t

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Belfort Plantation House & Clement Rum Tasting with Cultural Expert
blocks.text: Head out to Le Lamentin and L'Habitation Belfort, a banana plantation, where you can see the old colonial-style house that’s one of the most famous plantation homes in the Caribbean. You’ll also get to see the antique rum distillery for a guided tour and a delicious local rum tasting. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Catamaran Cruise, Grand Anse Beach & Swim

blocks.heading: Things to do in Nassau
blocks.text: There are plenty of things to do in Nassau, no matter how adventurous or laidback you want to be. Walk the 66-step Queen's Staircase, a hand-carved limestone path that leads to the historic Fort Fincastle. Once you reach the fort, you can enjoy sweeping views of the island’s bustling port. For a one-of-a-kind experience, swim alongside the famous Bahamian pigs in the warm waters. Or escape to the

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Nassau
blocks.text: Take your visit to Nassau to the next level with guided excursions that bring you up close to the island’s history and marine life.

blocks.heading: Stuart Cove Snuba & Snorkeling Adventure
blocks.text: Don't forget your underwater camera for this exciting three-hour adventure in the sea. A quick walk from the ship brings you to the dive boat. Experience a growing trend in underwater discovery-SNUBA-a unique experience that takes snorkeling to an immersive level. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Best of Nassau
blocks.text: Immerse yourself in the historical charm of Nassau on a tour of its most famous landmarks. Visit Fort Fincastle, perched high above the harbor and explore the Queen’s Staircase. This excursion also includes visits to local markets and colonial-era sites, giving you a well-rounded introduction to Nassau’s culture and heritage. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Aquaventure Oasis at Atlantis
blocks.text: Spend the day at Atlantis Resort on Paradise Island, where you can explore the stunning marine habitats filled with exotic sea life or lounge on a private beach with amazingly clear waters. For adventure seekers, Aquaventure Water Park offers thrilling water slides and a relaxing lazy river, making it the perfect mix of excitement and island bliss. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Swimming Pigs & Sun Cay Beach Club with Lunch
blocks.text: Take a scenic boat ride to a nearby cay, where you’ll meet Nassau’s famous swimming pigs. As you wade into the shallow waters, you can watch as these friendly animals paddle up to greet visitors. Afterward, head to Sun Cay Beach Club for a relaxing afternoon on powdery white sand, complete with a delicious island-style lunch. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Adults Only Beach Day at Blue Lagoon Island
blocks.text: Escape to Blue Lagoon Island, a private retreat featuring warm beaches, swaying palm trees and clear waters. This adults-only excursion offers a peaceful escape from the busy port, allowing you to relax in a quiet beachfront setting while you sip tropical cocktails and enjoy a stress-free day in paradise. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Dolphin Swim & Blue Lagoon Beach Fun with Lunch
blocks.text: Play and splash with a resident Atlantic bottlenose dolphin in a thrilling, interactive Dolphin Swim at an American Humane Certified facility. This five-hour adventure on Blue Lagoon Island introduces you to these lovable sea mammals and other marine life and includes beach time and lunch. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Things to do in St. Thomas
blocks.text: From world-class beaches to breathtaking viewpoints and vibrant marine life, St. Thomas offers something for every type of cruiser. During a cruise stop, spend the day lounging on the soft sands of Magens Bay, snorkeling among colorful reefs, or taking in the views from Paradise Point. For those looking to explore beyond the island, a quick ferry ride to St. John reveals unspoiled beaches and lush

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore St. Thomas
blocks.text: Experience the best of St. Thomas with these Princess Cruises excursions, designed to showcase the island’s rich history and culture.

blocks.heading: Sunset Catamaran Cruise
blocks.text: Sunset sail: two words that conjure up an idyllic experience of mystical beauty. Discover St. Thomas's quieter side on an approximately two-hour excursion across Charlotte Amalie harbor. From the pier, you'll board the 65-foot "Castaway Girl" catamaran. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Magens Bay Beach & Scenic Vistas
blocks.text: Visit one of the Caribbean’s most famous beaches, where calm waters and powdery white sand create a picture-perfect paradise. Before heading to the beach, take in the breathtaking island views from Mountain Top, the highest point in St. Thomas. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Shipwreck and Turtle Coves Snorkeling
blocks.text: Dive into the crystal-clear waters of St. Thomas and explore two stunning snorkel sites. Swim alongside colorful fish and sea turtles while discovering historic shipwrecks teeming with marine life. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: St. John Scenic Cruise & Eco-Hike
blocks.text: Sail from St. Thomas to the shores of St. John, where protected beaches, hiking trails and Virgin Islands National Park await. Enjoy a guided nature walk through the green landscapes, followed by time to swim and relax on a secluded beach. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: St. Thomas Island Drive
blocks.text: Enjoy the highlights of St. Thomas. Sit back and relax as you travel along mountainous roads, notably Skyline Drive, which boasts idyllic views. Soon, you'll drive up a twisting, winding road to Mountain Top, birthplace of the banana daiquiri and home to a wide array of duty-free shops. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Amazing Mountain Views & Villa Botanica
blocks.text: Enjoy the dynamic duo of breathtaking scenery and panoramic views on an adventure that takes you to the island's highest points. First on the agenda is a ride to Mountain Top, St. Thomas' highest peak. Rising 2,100 feet above St. Thomas, the observation deck affords picture-perfect vistas of the Caribbean Sea, Magens Bay, St. John and the British Virgin Islands. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Things to do in Tortola
blocks.text: Welcome to paradise! Tortola is the largest British Virgin Island and covered in lush rainforests that frame beautiful white sand beaches. Whether you love exploring open-air seaside villages or sipping a quirky cocktail next to turquoise waters, you’ll find that in Tortola. Tortola stands out from other Caribbean ports with its quieter, more laid-back atmosphere centered on nature, beaches and au

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Tortola
blocks.text: Tortola is best known as a scenic, nature-first destination, where lush green hills, dramatic coastlines and panoramic ocean views define the experience more than built attractions. From colorful seaside villages to tropical white sand beaches, there are activities on Tortola for everyone. These are a few of the shore excursions available when you travel with Princess:

blocks.heading: Jost Van Dyke Island beach break & scenic cruise
blocks.text: Sail out to Jost Van Dyk — an island famous for its laid-back lifestyle. Enjoy the pristine beaches and try the "Pain-killer," one of the Caribbean's most celebrated cocktails, from the legendary Soggy Dollar Bar. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Best of Tortola: Panoramic scenic drive, beach & shopping
blocks.text: Get some breathtaking views of Tortola by heading up For Hill and Great Mountain — where you can see miles and miles of sprawling lush green hills and turquoise waters. You’ll also head to Cane Garden Bay where you can kick back on the white sandy shores and soak in the sun or shop in the seaside markets. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Coast-to-Coast scenic drive & Pusser's landing
blocks.text: Tortola is only 12 miles from coast to coast, so you can see the whole island in a day. Start at Capoons Bay with charming seaside homes and rich white sand beaches before heading across the island to Pusser's Landing, an open-air village with West Indian-style architecture — and don’t forget to try a sip of Pusser’s Rum, a local specialty. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Cane Garden Bay Beach break & scenic drive
blocks.text: Nothing says vacation like a day spent relaxing on a slice of paradise. When you head to Cane Garden Bay Beach, you’ll find pillow soft sand, azure ocean water and rows of palm trees swaying in the breeze. Sprawl out on the white sand and enjoy one of the most beautiful beaches in Tortola. Cane Garden Bay Beach is located just 20 to 30 minutes from the cruise port, making it easy to plan a quick a

blocks.heading: The Baths at Virgin Gorda & Beach
blocks.text: One of the top excursions from Tortola is a visit to The Baths on nearby Virgin Gorda, a must-see natural landmark known for its giant granite boulders, with ferry access available from the island. Spend the day surrounded by 40 foot volcanic boulders at the geological wonder known as the Baths. You’ll start the day with a boat ride from Tortola to a smaller island called Virgin Gorda, the third l

blocks.heading: Experience the Tortola port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Cruises to Tortola arrive in Road Town, the island’s capital, where ships dock at the centrally located Tortola Pier Park cruise port. At the port, Tortola Pier Park offers a convenient arrival experience with shops, dining and excursion pickups all located just steps from the ship.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Trinidad
blocks.text: From bright red jungle birds to fried shark street food, Trinidad has something for nearly every traveler when you visit with Princess. Trinidad is home to stunning beaches and vibrant rainforests, as well as bustling port cities with colonial architecture and Carnival music. See the orange colonial mansions of the Magnificent Seven in Port of Spain, walk the surface of Pitch Lake (the world's lar

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Trinidad
blocks.text: See the vibrant culture of Trinidad or its legendary Scarlet Ibis birds perched in the deep jungles. Hike the rainforest trails at the Asa Wright Nature Centre, swim under the cascades of Maracas Waterfall or wander the colonial streets of the capital. When you visit Trinidad with Princess, you can enjoy shore excursions that take you to unbelievable destinations like these:

blocks.heading: Mount St. Benedict's Monastery
blocks.text: Perched 800 feet up the mountainside, St. Benedict’s Monastery is the oldest one in the Caribbean. This church is still home to 10 monks and a peaceful retreat for people of all faiths and no faith. Plus while you’re at the monastery, you’ll get some of the most breathtaking views of the island. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Port of Spain & Cultural Show
blocks.text: Get your taste of Trinidad by exploring its capital — home to the striking Red House of parliament and the Magnificent Seven colonial mansions. Then dive into the island’s rich cultural heritage and hear the famed steel pans, a calypso singer, colorful traditional costumes and even fire limbo at this Princess cultural show. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Best of Trinidad: Highlights & Scenic Drive
blocks.text: Surround yourself with a vibrant rainbow of tropical flora and fauna at the Royal Botanic Gardens at the heart of Port of Spain. Then head to Lady Young Lookout for a stunning overlook of the entire city before finishing at Maracas Bay with the world famous beach, endless cocoa and another birds’ eye view of the island. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Caroni Bird Sanctuary
blocks.text: Calling all bird lovers! Spend the day on a boat exploring the famous Trinidad bird sanctuary as you wind through mangrove-lined waterways. See the bright pink Scarlet Ibis in its natural habitat — just one of the 130 species that live in the sanctuary. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Maracas Beach
blocks.text: It’s as easy as a day at the beach! Spend the day sprawled on the warm sand, soaking in the sunshine on the most famous beach in Trinidad: Maracas Beach. This palm-lined beach is a picture-perfect paradise where you can take the day to relax. Don’t forget to try the shark-n-bake — a local delicacy of fried flatbread and shark meat. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Things to do in San Juan
blocks.text: As Princess's primary gateway to the Southern Caribbean, San Juan keeps you anything but bored while you wait for your cruise to depart. Here are some of the most popular things to do in San Juan. From exploring the cobblestone streets and colorful colonial architecture of Old San Juan to lounging on the beautiful beaches of Condado and Isla Verde, there's something for every type of traveler. The

blocks.heading: San Juan shore excursions
blocks.text: You don’t have to worry about over-planning — Princess shore excursions take care of everything so you can experience the very best of San Juan without lifting a finger. We handle the details so you can relax and soak it all in. Here are just a few top-rated shore excursions you can enjoy:

blocks.heading: Puerto Rico’s Favorites
blocks.text: This all-in-one excursion is the perfect well-rounded experience for first-time visitors. Explore San Juan’s most beloved landmarks — from historic Old San Juan to scenic coastal sights — enjoy authentic Puerto Rican cuisine and get a taste of the island’s rich culture. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of San Juan: Old and New San Juan City Tour & Shopping
blocks.text: Discover the best of both worlds as you explore San Juan’s historical landmarks and modern attractions. Visit sites like El Morro, marvel at the vibrant architecture in Old San Juan and enjoy free time to shop for handmade crafts and souvenirs in the city’s bustling markets. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: History & Cuisine of San Juan on Foot
blocks.text: Dive into San Juan’s vibrant culture with this immersive walking tour. Wander through cobblestone streets and enjoy a guided tasting of Puerto Rican culinary favorites, from mofongo (a deep-fried green plantain mashed together with other ingredients, typically pork) to pasteles (A dish similar to tamales, made from banana masa, filled with savory pork, and wrapped in banana leaves). This tour is a

blocks.heading: Beach Escape at Vivo Beach Club
blocks.text: Relax and recharge at Vivo Beach Club, located along Isla Verde’s picturesque coastline. Enjoy private beach access, poolside lounging and a variety of delicious dining options. Whether you want to sip on a cocktail, take a refreshing swim or simply soak up the sun, this excursion is the ultimate tropical retreat. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: El Yunque National Rainforest Scenic Drive
blocks.text: Experience the natural beauty of Puerto Rico on a guided tour through El Yunque. Marvel at waterfalls, verdant vegetation and staggering mountain views as your guide shares fascinating insights about this ecological treasure. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Antigua
blocks.text: From sun-drenched beaches to centuries-old landmarks, Antigua offers an exciting mix of history and outdoor adventure. Stroll through Nelson’s Dockyard, a UNESCO-listed site and the world’s last Georgian naval dockyard. There you will find restored colonial buildings and historic shipyards that tell the island’s maritime story. Cruises to Antigua are usually included on Eastern or Southern Caribbe

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Antigua
blocks.text: From the cruise port at Heritage Quay, you can walk straight into downtown St. John’s, with shops, restaurants and local markets just a few minutes from the ship. Get the most out of every minute you spend ashore with guided excursions that highlight the best of Antigua, from historic landmarks to tropical adventures.

blocks.heading: Rainforest Canopy Zipline Adventure
blocks.text: You've got a bird's eye view over Antigua's lush rainforest when you take to the sky on an exciting zipline adventure. This award winning eco-tour puts you right in the heart of the forest and an intricate pulley and harness system safely carries you over spectacular scenery, including a dramatic gorge. Your air-conditioned transportation takes you to the Antigua Canopy Tour, where you'll attend a

blocks.heading: Nelson's Dockyard, Shirley Heights & Dow's Hill
blocks.text: Step back in time at Nelson’s Dockyard, a beautifully restored naval base with centuries of history. Then, continue to Shirley Heights, where the views overlook English Harbour. Top it all off with a visit to Dow’s Hill Interpretation Centre, and learn more about the island’s colonial past. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Antigua Beach Break
blocks.text: Relax on one of Antigua’s legendary beaches, where soft white sand meets crystal-clear Caribbean waters. Enjoy a laid-back afternoon sunbathing, swimming, or sipping a tropical drink with refreshing sea breezes all around. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Stingray, Snorkel, Swim & Scenic Country Drive
blocks.text: Travel along Antigua’s scenic countryside before arriving at Stingray City, where you’ll wade into shallow waters to swim and interact with friendly southern stingrays. These gentle creatures glide effortlessly around you, making for an unforgettable, up-close marine encounter. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Things to do in Belize
blocks.text: From exploring ancient ruins to snorkeling in crystal-clear waters, Belize offers a plethora of activities for every traveler. Belize is an island nation covered in lush jungles where both Mayan and Spanish colonial history come together — there are nearly endless activities to try. Climb a 60-foot temple to the Sun God or see the crocodiles deep in the jungle river — or spend the day sightseeing

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Belize
blocks.text: Get ready to see the ancient and natural sides of this beautiful country with expert Princess guides to teach you. When you cruise to Belize with Princess, you can enjoy shore excursions like these:

blocks.heading: See the Best of Belize
blocks.text: The largest city in Belize sits at the mouth of the river and is surrounded by beautiful mangrove forests, and it’s the perfect place to explore the country’s colonial history — including the stately mansions and Central America’s first Anglican church. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Altun Ha Mayan Ruins & Scenic River Cruise
blocks.text: Explore the iconic ancient ruins with a complex of 13 Mayan structures and the towering 60-foot Temple of the Sun God — then cruise the Belize River to spot wildlife such as dolphins and crocodiles. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Lamanai Mayan Ruins & River Boat Safari
blocks.text: All aboard! Take a riverboat ride through the emerald green river (watch for crocodiles and manatees!) to learn about the trees of the jungle and its history in Belizean bush medicine. Then, head to the impressive Lamanai ruins for a panoramic view of ancient Mayan history. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Xunantunich Mayan Ruins & Lunch
blocks.text: Visit a staggering Mayan temple that’s 135 feet tall and the most architecturally significant in the country, and then enjoy a Belizean meal. Cruises to Belize often include excursions to Mayan ruins like Altun Ha and Lamanai, where you can explore ancient temples and learn about the region’s history. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Snorkeling Wonders of the Barrier Reef
blocks.text: Discover the underwater world of Belize by snorkeling around the Belize Barrier Reef — home to 500 fish species and 106 different species of live coral creating a dazzling underwater rainbow. Snorkeling and diving are some of the most popular activities in Belize, with the Belize Barrier Reef offering vibrant coral reefs and abundant marine life to explore. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Visit the Howler Monkey Sanctuary
blocks.text: It’s all monkey business here! Get up close and personal with the native black howler monkeys in this sanctuary — the largest monkeys in Latin American rainforests. Get a behind-the-scenes look at how these creatures live and make a few new friends. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Bermuda
blocks.text: Let one of these curated tours guide your day in a style that matches your speed: luxury, leisure or all‑action.

blocks.heading: Aquarium, Museum & Zoo, Crystal Caves
blocks.text: Start with the Bermuda Aquarium, Museum & Zoo — flamingos, turtles and coral‑reef tanks dominate. Then hop on the coach to the limestone‑carved Crystal Caves where you descend steps to lakes beneath stalactites and stalagmites. Ceilings drip and waters glimmer… just make sure to gear up accordingly (sneakers are a good idea). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Lighthouse, Hamilton & Scenic Drive
blocks.text: Bounce off the pier in a small‑group taxi/guide car and take in a sublime loop: the historic 1616 Heydon Trust Chapel, the world’s smallest working drawbridge at Somerset Bridge and the stately Gibb’s Hill Lighthouse — followed by a drive through Hamilton’s pastel‑pops and a visit to a pink‑sand beach before heading back via Harbor Road. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Bermuda: St. George, Hamilton, Scenic Drive & Shopping
blocks.text: Travel the length of Bermuda in five hours, hitting Somerset Bridge, Gibb’s Hill Lighthouse, cliff‑top Horseshoe Bay and then on to Hamilton for free time. Return via the Botanical Gardens and the 17th‑century structures in St. George with its cedar stocks and colonial stocks still standing (but thankfully no longer in use). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Tea & Tales: A Taste of British Bermuda (A Small Group Tour)
blocks.text: In a refined group setting (max six), glide through Bermuda’s British‑island fusion: visit the historic chapel above Somerset Bridge, roll along South Shore Road for reef views, then arrive at Willowbank Resort for elevated tea service — sandwiches, scones and steaming pots — served in colonial style. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Glass‑Bottom Boat Cruise & Sea Gardens
blocks.text: Board a 78‑foot glass‑bottom boat moored near the ship for a reef tour like no other. Drift above coral beds, float over the sunken 18th‑century ship Vixen and watch sea turtles peek out from the shadows — all narrated by your friendly crew and enhanced with memorable island‑tales and reef‑facts. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Scenic Catamaran Cruise, Snorkel, Swim & Beach
blocks.text: Climb aboard the spacious catamaran Rising Son II, lounge in shaded comfort or spread out on the trampoline looking at sky and sea, snorkel the shallow waters at Mangrove Bay, float on a noodle, sip a complimentary rum swizzle and sail back with sand in your hair and a longing for the sea as a permanent part of your personality. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Dominica
blocks.text: Dominica is a nature lover’s paradise. Known as the “Nature Island,” Dominica is defined by lush rainforests, dramatic waterfalls, and volcanic landscapes, offering a more rugged, adventure-focused experience than many Caribbean destinations. It got the nickname “Nature Island of the Caribbean” for its lush rainforests, volcanic landscapes and pristine waters. Dominica offers an authentic and unfo

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Dominica
blocks.text: For those looking to experience Dominica’s raw beauty and adventure, these shore excursions offer a mix of exploration and relaxation. Top natural highlights include Trafalgar Falls, Emerald Pool, and the Boiling Lake, each showcasing Dominica’s signature waterfalls and volcanic landscapes. Dominica is best experienced through adventure-focused excursions like hiking to waterfalls, river tubing, a

blocks.heading: River Tubing & Rainforest Scenic Drive
blocks.text: Wear your swimsuit under your clothes and set off on an approximately 90-minute drive past tropical vegetation and lush island scenery into the interior of the island. Eco Village, built by the Carib Indians, is your starting point for an exciting river tubing adventure. VIEW EXCURSIONS

blocks.heading: Emerald Pool & Rainforest Hike
blocks.text: Step into a tropical paradise as you trek through jungle trails leading to the secluded Emerald Pool. Take a dip beneath the cascading waterfall, surrounded by towering ferns and vibrant wildlife. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Champagne Reef Snorkeling
blocks.text: Snorkeling is a standout experience in Dominica, especially at Champagne Reef, where volcanic bubbles rise through clear waters filled with marine life. Dive into one of Dominica’s most unique underwater experiences. Volcanic vents create warm, bubbling waters that give you the sensation of swimming through a natural champagne bath. And you can enjoy it all while exploring a colorful coral reef te

blocks.heading: River Tubing on the Layou River
blocks.text: Enjoy a thrilling yet relaxing adventure as you float down Dominica’s largest river, surrounded by dense rainforest and dramatic rock formations. A mix of gentle currents and exciting rapids makes this a fun experience for all ages. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Hot Spring Adventure
blocks.text: Embark on one of the Caribbean’s most challenging hikes, leading to the world’s second-largest hot springs. The journey through steaming fumaroles and volcanic landscapes is tough — but the rewarding views make it unforgettable. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Caribbean Culinary Adventure
blocks.text: Delight all your senses on a Caribbean-style outdoor cooking adventure-a fun and tasty way to enjoy the best the region has to offer. Your 3.5-hour tour begins when set out on a short but scenic drive through rainforest terrain with vistas of mountains and sea to a private family home. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Things to do in Falmouth
blocks.text: Falmouth, Jamaica is home to lush jungles and winding rivers, stunning white sand beaches lined with palm trees and rich history. You won’t want to miss the Greenwood Great House where you can see the island’s history when sugar was king — or the Martha Brae River that used to transport sugar from the heart of Jamaica to the harbor. Plus no trip to Jamaica is complete without a day spent at one of

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Falmouth
blocks.text: With everything from palatial plantation homes to picture-perfect tropical beaches, Falmouth has something for everyone. These are a few of the short excursions you can try when you visit with Princess:

blocks.heading: Rose Hall Great House & Shopping
blocks.text: Tour one of the Caribbean's classic landmarks-Rose Hall Great House, and peer into the life of Jamaica's infamous "White Witch." Tour the mansion where Annie Palmer is said to have practiced voodoo and murdered three husbands. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Best of Falmouth: Highlights of Falmouth & Greenwood Great House
blocks.text: Step into Jamaica’s fascinating history at the Greenwood Great House. Here you can see the original furniture, a well-preserved library, a grand ballroom, oil paintings, antiques and a rare collection of musical instruments. Keep your eyes peeled for one of the three working barrel organs in the world on display! VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Bamboo Beach Club & Dunn's River Falls
blocks.text: Dive into one of Jamaica’s most beautiful natural wonders: a 600-foot waterfall called Dunn's River Falls with natural swimmable pools at its base. Then head to the beach to relax while listening to reggae music as you spread out on this perfect tropical beach. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Bamboo Beach Club VIP Experience
blocks.text: Get the VIP experience you deserve on your vacation at the Bamboo Beach Club. Kick back and relax on a white sand beach under the sun. Princess will take care of the rest! You’ll get padded lounge beds, specialty cocktails, rum punch, house sodas and lemonade — as well as a four-course lunch including jerk chicken and fish, a Jamaican specialty. Our hostesses will take care of you, so you can get

blocks.heading: River Rafting on the Martha Brae
blocks.text: Float down the beautiful Martha Brae river on a one-of-a-kind bamboo raft. Your guide will navigate the river and teach you about when it was used during the sugar trade to transport cargo to the harbor. You’ll also learn about the ancient Arawak legends about the river, so you can see how pivotal it’s been throughout the island’s long history. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Freeport
Dolphin Close Encounter
blocks.text: This heartwarming experience brings you face to face with Atlantic bottlenose dolphins in calm, shallow water. Gentle interactions and expert guidance reveal the intelligence and spirit of these remarkable animals, leaving guests smiling long after they return to shore. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Brewery, Tasting & Port Lucaya
blocks.text: Immerse yourself in the flavors and spirit of Grand Bahama. Visit Port Lucaya Marketplace, where lively vendors and colorful stalls capture the island’s character. Then head to the Bahamian Brewery, home of the iconic Sands beer. Enjoy a guided tour through the bottling line, learn about the brewing process and sample a few crisp local favorites. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Coral Vita Reef Restoration & Stoned Crab Beach
blocks.text: See how science and nature come together at Coral Vita, a groundbreaking reef restoration center bringing Bahamian coral back to life. After meeting the experts and witnessing vibrant reef tanks up close, unwind by the turquoise shallows at Stoned Crab Beach — a peaceful finish to an inspiring day. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Swimming Pigs & Crystal Beach
blocks.text: Laughter and splashes fill the air as the island’s famous swimming pigs paddle out to greet you. Share a few playful moments in the shallows, then settle into the rhythm of Crystal Beach with your toes in the sand and the scent of sea salt on the breeze. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Pirate Cove Beach & Zipline Adventure
blocks.text: You’ll hardly be able to catch your breath as you glide high above the shoreline, waves sparkling below. Back on the sand, the lively buzz of Pirate Cove calls with beach bars, volleyball courts and laid-back island tunes that make the afternoon drift by too quickly. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Glass Bottom Boat & Shark Experience
blocks.text: Gaze through crystal-clear glass at the kaleidoscope of life below — coral heads, darting fish and the occasional sea turtle. When sharks begin to circle gracefully beneath the boat, the water feels alive with quiet power and beauty. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Freeport
blocks.text: Freeport appears on a variety of Caribbean cruise itineraries aboard Princess®, including quick getaways and longer tropical voyages. Many routes also visit nearby ports in the Bahamas and Eastern Caribbean, creating a seamless blend of adventure and relaxation across the islands.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Fuerte Amador
blocks.text: Welcome to Fuerte Amador — that man‑made peninsula reaching into the Pacific where the mighty Panama Canal meets Panama City. Created by linking four islands with tons of rock dug out during the canal construction, this is where major cruise lines drop anchor (or tender in) for a full day of serious exploration.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Fuerte Amador
blocks.text: Curated, bold and ready for guests who don’t just dip their toes. These popular shore excursions hit deep — culture, nature and history are all on the docket.

blocks.heading: Monkey & Wildlife Nature Cruise on Gatun Lake
blocks.text: Hop aboard a jungle boat and cruise through Gatun Lake’s tangled maze of rainforest islands. Your naturalist guide will help you spot howler monkeys, white-faced capuchins and tropical birds flitting through the canopy. Cameras up, because this is wild Panama at its best. On the way back, glide past the Panama Canal at water level for a front-row seat to man-made marvels. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Scenic Drive & Walking Tour of “Colonial Panama”
blocks.text: Step off your ship and into centuries of layered charm: the original settlement in Panama Viejo (ruined by pirates in 1671), followed by strolls in Casco Antiguo where French plazas, cathedrals and architecture mash up into a rich cultural stew. Your guide picks the route, you pick the photo angles — history never looked so good. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Panama Canal Railway & New Locks of the Canal Expansion (Dome Car)
blocks.text: Climb into a 1938‑era dome car with glass panoramic windows, roll through rainforest and past Gatun Lake, then arrive at the New Locks Observation Center to watch massive vessels ease through the expanded canal system. Train ride, rainforest and giant ships. Yeah, it’s a gonna-do-it-all kind of day. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Fuerte Amador: Colonial Panama, Miraflores Locks Observation Center & IMAX Theater
blocks.text: Start with Casco Antiguo’s mix of colonial, art deco and Caribbean styles, then shift gears to the Miraflores Locks for up‑close lock‑action and cap it off in IMAX with a sweeping “Panama Canal 3D” show. That’s heritage, tech and a bit of personal betterment in one fun orbit. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Panama’s History in Gold
blocks.text: Travel through past and craft: ruins of Panama Viejo, then a gold‑smithing workshop where the ‘lost wax’ process is alive and well, and where you can get a close look at how Panama’s famous Gold Orchids are made. Finish in Casco Viejo. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Authentic Embera Native Village
blocks.text: Want to get out of the city and experience real, indigenous culture? Climb into a dugout canoe and glide through the emerald wilds of Chagres National Park toward a remote Embera village. After a river landing, meet the chief, watch ceremonial dances, explore their vibrant handmade crafts and enjoy a riverside snack. It’s not a show — it’s an open invitation to connect with the people that thrive

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Fuerte Amador
blocks.text: Your ship arrives at the Pacific entrance to the canal, docking at the new terminal or anchoring offshore with a quick tender ride in. Either way, you're landing right in the action zone. For Panama Canal itineraries, Fuerte Amador is the gateway you’ll thank your lucky stars you got to visit. Jungle, skyline, epic engineering — this port is a showstopper.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Limon
blocks.text: Pick your pace, pick your peak experience — your Limon cruise excursions are designed to deliver thrill, calm or something in‑between.

blocks.heading: Class II Rafting on the Reventazon River & Snack
blocks.text: Launch into the rushing Reventazon River’s Class II rapids for a 90‑minute white‑water adventure through lush jungle walls, with your guide providing gear, brushing up on paddling technique and serving up a snack by a banana plantation after the ride. Bring a change of clothes and prepare for splash, speed and rainforest spectacle. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Monster Bus & Rainforest Exploration
blocks.text: Climb aboard a hulking 6×6 ‘Monster Bus’ with panoramic windows and carve through the Banano River valley as you pass remote villages and lush river corridors. You’ll pause at lookout points for jaw‑dropping rainforest views, snack on plantain chips and casaba with a cool soft drink, then follow a naturalist guide into the jungle where poison dart frogs, monkeys and exotic birds await. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Tayutic Hacienda & Lunch
blocks.text: Drive two hours into Costa Rica’s highlands to a 100‑year‑old family‑run hacienda near Turrialba, nestled in gardens of cacao, coffee and sugar‑cane. You’ll learn colonial cultivation methods, sample freshly roasted coffee, dine surrounded by tropical foliage and explore a German‑built 1880s chapel before browsing the gift shop packed with artisan goods. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Meet the Sloths: Behind the Scenes
blocks.text: Get up‑close with sloths at Aviarios del Caribe, the world’s first sloth‑only sanctuary featured on Meet the Sloths. After an intro to adult ambassadors, you’ll canoe down the Estrella River through rainforest, spotting wildlife, before venturing behind the scenes where baby sloths live and adults who can’t return to the wild are cared for — visit a banana plantation and round out a peaceful, wild

blocks.heading: National Parks, Wildlife Refuge & Macaw Sanctuary (A Small‑Group Tour)
blocks.text: Join an intimate group (max 25) and trek into the wilds of Cahuita National Park, exploring trails where monkeys, iguanas and dense foliage dominate, then journey on to the Ara Manzanillo sanctuary where the green macaw is making a dramatic comeback. This low‑key yet immersive rainforest experience is for guests who prefer depth over dash, wildlife over souvenirs. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Original Canopy Zipline Tour at Veragua Rainforest
blocks.text: Gear up for adrenaline in this treetop thrill‑ride: you’ll fly across twelve spans (nearly two football fields) as you zip 150 feet above the rainforest canopy, sights stretching across jungle, jungle canopy and sky. After landing, wander into Veragua’s interactive displays — frogs, butterflies and hummingbirds — before a brief souvenir stop and smooth return to the ship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Ocho Rios
blocks.text: Ocho Rios invites you into a lively mash‑up of waterfalls, white‑sand beaches, reggae beats and old plantation estates — all within easy reach of your cruise ship. Expect jungle adventures, jerk chicken smells, craft markets and Jamaican heritage all wrapped into one unforgettable stop.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Ocho Rios
blocks.text: Pick your thrill‑level and board for a mix of waterfalls, rainforest rides, craft‑making and mind-numbingly good island food.

blocks.heading: Flavors of Jamaica Cooking Class
blocks.text: Take a seat in the Great House at Prospect Plantation and pick up the chef’s spoon. Work with a master to learn how jerk chicken, callaloo and island spices combine into something unforgettable. Then you eat what you made, browse the aviary and garden, chat with artisans and leave with more than a meal. It’s a personal experience worth sinking your teeth into. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Ocho Rios: Dunn’s River Falls, Scenic Drive & Shopping
blocks.text: Grab your towel, sense of adventure and rubber‑soled shoes, because you’re about to ascend the 600‑foot cascade of Dunn’s River Falls (or use the stair alternative if you’d rather stay dry). After soaking in that natural show, you’ll glide through lush vistas to the tropical gardens of Konoko and wrap it up with a duty‑free shopping stop that feels like an island bonus round. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Mystic Mountain Escape
blocks.text: Leave the pier and climb (literally) into rainforest air: Zip to the treetops on a chairlift 700 feet above the canopy at Mystic Mountain, gaze out from an observation tower, take a dip in the infinity pool, learn Jamaican heritage at the pavilions and snap souvenir shots before heading back to port. You’ll feel clouds below and the world above. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Dunn’s River Climb & Zipline Over The Falls
blocks.text: Hold hands, laugh and step into the jungle spray as you scale the natural rock steps of Dunn’s River, feeling each splash and leafy arch as you rise. Then switch gears into zipline mode — seven jungle spans, suspended bridges and real bird‑call soundtrack included. It’s equal parts waterfall and wind‑in‑your‑face. Not for the faint‑hearted, but definitely for those who want to do something unforge

blocks.heading: River Rafting on the Martha Brae
blocks.text: Trade the sightseeing bus for a mellow bamboo raft gently drifting down the historic Martha Brae River, where your guide points out birds, banana trees and old‑school legends of sugar‑era life. Thirty feet of planked raft, soft waves, tropical air and a souvenir stop near the end make this a day of ease and breeze. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Open‑Air Plantation Ride & Dunn’s River Falls
blocks.text: Blue skies, banana fields, plantation jitneys and historic great houses — this tour gives you a story‑filled drive into Jamaica’s past, followed by the full cascade marvel of Dunn’s River Falls. You’ll ride an open carriage, snack with sea views, climb or admire the falls and then head back to port ready for your next adventure. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Ocho Rios
blocks.text: When you dock in Ocho Rios as part of your Panama Canal cruise, you step right into the island’s energy — sun on your neck, spice in the air and that unmistakable Jamaican vibe humming in the background. Cabs and excursion vans line up ready to launch you toward waterfalls, beaches or jungle thrills. This port doesn’t waste time, and neither will you.

Featured ports on Your Cruise to Puerto Rico
blocks.text: Get an overview of some of the ports you could visit on your cruises to Puerto Rico (plus our main departure port, San Juan).

blocks.heading: What will you do on a Puerto Rico cruise?
blocks.text: Our Puerto Rico excursions offer unforgettable ways to connect with the island’s spirit. Step into Old San Juan’s storied streets, hike El Yunque’s misty trails or indulge in the flavors of traditional Puerto Rican cuisine.

blocks.heading: Irresistible flavors of the island
blocks.text: Savor San Juan with every step on this culinary walking tour. Sample island staples like mofongo and creole chicken, sip mojitos and explore landmarks including Plaza de Armas, the San Juan Cathedral and the Museum of Doña Fela. History & Cuisine of San Juan on Foot

links.text: History & Cuisine of San Juan on Foot

blocks.heading: Unwind at VIVO Beach Club with poolside cocktails.
blocks.text: Soak up the sun at Isla Verde’s VIVO Beach Club, where white sand meets clear, gentle surf. This all-day Beach Escape offers access to pools, oceanfront bars and private beach loungers. Immerse yourself in Puerto Rico’s coastal beauty in complete style and comfort. Golden sand and turquoise waters

blocks.heading: History and heritage come alive
blocks.text: Walk the cobblestone streets of Old San Juan and explore its iconic Spanish fortresses — El Morro and San Cristóbal — on a guided excursion that blends history with vibrant local color. Along the way, enjoy time to browse shops and galleries filled with handmade crafts and art. Old San Juan Fortresses & Shopping

blocks.heading: Adventure beyond the shoreline
blocks.text: Leave the city behind on a scenic drive to El Yunque National Forest, the only tropical rainforest in the U.S. National Forest System. Discover natural wonders, waterfalls and panoramic views along the way, perfect for travelers craving a natural escape. El Yunque National Rainforest Scenic Drive

links.text: El Yunque National Rainforest Scenic Drive

blocks.heading: Welcome to the San Juan cruise port
Caribbean cuise onboard experience featured program
blocks.text: Award-winning programs. World-class chefs. And Caribbean-themed activities, day and night. With Princess, your ship is a destination all its own.

blocks.heading: Deeper experiences of the islands
blocks.text: Discover the history of local distilleries while sampling some of the region’s best rums, meet the parrots and macaws that call the Caribbean home in the ship's Piazza, or sink into the rhythms of the region with steel pan drum lessons. Our onboard activities give you the chance to gain a deeper connection and understanding to islands you'll visit on your voyage.

blocks.heading: Comfortable accommodations
blocks.text: Your stateroom is your home away from home where you can rest up and recharge between adventures. With the expertly designed Princess Luxury Bed, luxurious 100% Jacquard-woven cotton linens and our SLEEP program, specially created by a board-certified sleep expert, you might just get the best sleep of your life. We offer staterooms ranging from interior cabins to full suites, and we even offer con

blocks.heading: Bringing local life aboard
blocks.text: Embrace the spirit of the islands the moment you step on your ship with our Rhythm of the Caribbean program. Savor island cuisine, sip signature cocktails and engage in authentic regional experiences. Dance beneath the stars to vibrant island rhythms at exclusive parties, and immerse yourself in one-of-a-kind cultural activities — from concerts and crafts to talks from shark experts and treasure h

blocks.heading: Never miss a beat
blocks.text: Say goodbye to the daily grind with our new Sail Away Party poolside on the top deck, dance to local music at one of the many Caribbean inspired concerts, or be the envy of every pirate at our high-energy gold treasure-inspired Terrace Pool Gold Party. Throughout your Caribbean cruise there will be events that invite you to fully experience the islands.

blocks.heading: Ship activities for every cruise to the Caribbean
Family
blocks.text: Enjoy a ship full of activities for the whole family, from Broadway-style shows to Discovery’s Shark Week all summer long, your family will be engaged in the Caribbean. Go stargazing under the stunning expanse of the night sky, compete in a family game night and savor the flavors of the islands together.

blocks.heading: Relaxation
blocks.text: Pamper yourself in the Lotus Spa® with a massage, facial or manicure, and feel renewed. Enjoy The Sanctuary, a lounge just for adults, where you can relax with a light meal, specialty drink and al fresco massages while digging into that novel you've been looking forward to reading. If you prefer more active relaxation, we offer Zumba, yoga and tai chi classes to burn off stress and raise your hear

blocks.heading: Celebration
blocks.text: Almost 30% of all passengers who sail with us are celebrating an important milestone in their lives. Say "I do" at sea in a ceremony officiated by the captain. Arrange for an anniversary package and let us spoil you with romantic balcony dining, chocolates and more. For us, every day is a celebration.
