blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Rome
blocks.text: You don’t have to be an expert of Rome to make the most of your time there — that’s where we come in. Experience the best Rome has to offer, stress-free, with Princess shore excursions. We’ll handle the details so you can relax and soak it all in.

blocks.heading: Rome On Your Own
blocks.text: Embrace the freedom to explore Rome at your leisure. With convenient transportation to and from the city center, craft your own adventure — be it marveling at Renaissance art, savoring authentic Italian cuisine in a quaint trattoria or shopping for exquisite leather goods. Beautiful Rome is yours to discover, at your own pace. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Etruscan Countryside & Olive Oil Tasting
blocks.text: Journey through the picturesque landscapes of Lazio to the ancient town of Tuscania, where the streets whisper tales of Etruscan civilization. Explore medieval architecture, including the Basilica of San Pietro, perched atop an ancient acropolis. Then, visit a local farmhouse to savor artisanal olive oils, each drop capturing the essence of Italy's rich agricultural heritage. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: St. Peter's, Roman Catacombs & Colosseum
blocks.text: Delve into Rome's profound history with a guided tour of sacred and ancient landmarks. Wander through the hallowed halls of St. Peter's Basilica, descend into the enigmatic Roman Catacombs and stand before the majestic Colosseum, envisioning the grandeur of ancient spectacles. This journey intertwines the spiritual and historical threads of the Eternal City. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Pasta Making & Lunch at Local Farmhouse, Meet the Cedrini Family:
blocks.text: Head into the rolling Etruscan countryside for a hands-on culinary adventure with the Cedrini family, farmers for four generations. In their charming farmhouse kitchen, learn time-honored pasta-making techniques before crafting a decadent Italian dessert. Then, gather around the table to savor your creations alongside local wine, surrounded by the warmth of true Italian hospitality. LEARN MORE

blocks.text: Set sail from the Eternal City, where every cobblestone street whispers stories of empires past. Your journey begins in Rome, a city that seamlessly blends ancient marvels like the Colosseum and Roman Forum with lively piazzas, world-class cuisine and authentic Italian charm. blocks.text: As Princess's primary gateway to the Southern Caribbean, San Juan keeps you anything but bored while you wait for your cruise to depart. Here are some of the most popular things to do in San Juan. From exploring the cobblestone streets and colorful colonial architecture of Old San Juan to lounging on the beautiful beaches of Condado and Isla Verde, there's something for every type of traveler. The

blocks.heading: San Juan shore excursions
blocks.text: You don’t have to worry about over-planning — Princess shore excursions take care of everything so you can experience the very best of San Juan without lifting a finger. We handle the details so you can relax and soak it all in. Here are just a few top-rated shore excursions you can enjoy:

blocks.heading: Puerto Rico’s Favorites
blocks.text: This all-in-one excursion is the perfect well-rounded experience for first-time visitors. Explore San Juan’s most beloved landmarks — from historic Old San Juan to scenic coastal sights — enjoy authentic Puerto Rican cuisine and get a taste of the island’s rich culture. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of San Juan: Old and New San Juan City Tour & Shopping
blocks.text: Discover the best of both worlds as you explore San Juan’s historical landmarks and modern attractions. Visit sites like El Morro, marvel at the vibrant architecture in Old San Juan and enjoy free time to shop for handmade crafts and souvenirs in the city’s bustling markets. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: History & Cuisine of San Juan on Foot
blocks.text: Dive into San Juan’s vibrant culture with this immersive walking tour. Wander through cobblestone streets and enjoy a guided tasting of Puerto Rican culinary favorites, from mofongo (a deep-fried green plantain mashed together with other ingredients, typically pork) to pasteles (A dish similar to tamales, made from banana masa, filled with savory pork, and wrapped in banana leaves). blocks.text: Relax and recharge at Vivo Beach Club, located along Isla Verde’s picturesque coastline. Enjoy private beach access, poolside lounging and a variety of delicious dining options. Whether you want to sip on a cocktail, take a refreshing swim or simply soak up the sun, this excursion is the ultimate tropical retreat. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Singapore
blocks.text: Singapore packs a punch with its mix of sleek modern architecture, historic neighborhoods and world-famous street food. You’ll find everything from sky-high observation decks to vibrant districts like Kampong Glam, where Malay heritage meets trendy boutiques. And with flavors like coconut laksa and kaya-filled pastries around every corner, it’s a place that knows how to treat your taste buds. For

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Singapore
blocks.text: Don’t stress over planning — experience the best Singapore has to offer, hassle-free, with Princess shore excursions. We’ll handle the details so you can relax and soak it all in.

blocks.heading: River Cruise & Chinatown Walking Tour
blocks.text: Glide past skyscrapers and colonial landmarks on a scenic cruise down the Singapore River, where history flows right alongside modern life. Once you’re back on land, set off on a guided walk through Chinatown, starting at Thian Hock Keng Temple and winding through hidden gems like Ann Siang Hill. Along the way, you’ll visit the Sri Mariamman Temple — the city’s oldest Hindu place of worship — and

blocks.heading: Chinatown, Little India, Sultan Mosque & Singapore Sling
blocks.text: Sip, scout and soak up Singapore’s vibrant cultural mash-up. Start your day exploring the color-drenched streets of Chinatown, where you’ll visit the Sri Mariamman Temple and sample brews at a traditional Chinese tea house. Next, head to Little India to browse saris, spices and shimmering jewelry before a stop at the golden-domed Sultan Mosque. Cap it all off with a classic Singapore Sling and a s

blocks.heading: Battlefields of Singapore
blocks.text: History buffs will love this deep dive into Singapore’s WWII history and the fall of the island to Japan in 1942. You’ll tour the restored Ford Motor Company factory where the British surrendered to Japanese forces in the Battle of Singapore and the Changi Chapel that was built by POWs and is now a museum. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: City Drive, Chinatown & S.E.A Aquarium
blocks.text: Temples, food stalls and sea critters, oh my! Start your day at one of the largest aquariums in the world that houses 100,000 marine animals, including the bottlenose dolphin and scalloped hammerhead. Then wander the winding streets of Chinatown full of colorful food stalls with mouth watering local bites and enjoy views of Sri Mariamann Temple, the oldest Hindu Temple in Singapore. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: City Drive, Chinatown & National Orchid Garden
blocks.text: Smell the roses — more like the orchids when you’re in Singapore! Explore the world’s largest collection of orchids — with over 1,000 species on display — right in the heart of the city. After that, see the dazzling white Raffles Hotel that you might recognize from the movie Crazy Rich Asians and where Charlie Chaplin and Elizabeth Taylor stayed. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Gardens by the Bay & Marina Bay Sands Observation Deck
blocks.text: Step into Guinness World Record holder of the largest glass greenhouse in the world. Gardens by the Bay is home to over 250,000 rare plants and 200 sculptures — you’ll probably recognize the twisting metal tree sculptures from the city skyline. Afterwards, you’ll step onto the most iconic building in Singapore where you can view the whole city from 650 feet above. LEARN MORE

blocks.text: Docking at the Singapore Cruise Centre or Marina Bay Cruise Centre puts you right in the heart of the action — with easy access to the city's top neighborhoods, from the glitzy waterfront to historic enclaves like Chinatown and Little India. Local food stalls, shopping arcades and lush green parks are just minutes away, making it easy to start exploring as soon as you step off the ship. Whether yo

You'll walk the same cobbled streets as exiled European convicts and early settlers while stopping at four historic pubs for drinks and tales that get more colorful with each gulp. Pick your poison at each stop (cider, beer or house wine) and soak up the scandal with a side of sandstone. LEARN MORE

What to know about cruises from Tokyo
blocks.text: Whether you're timing your cruise to Japan's cherry blossom season in March and April or setting sail later in the year, there's more than enough to catch your attention when you depart from Tokyo. Just be sure to keep the following in mind as you plan your journey, so you can comfortably explore this incredible city before setting sail.

blocks.heading: Tokyo shore excursions
blocks.text: Let Princess show you the best experiences Tokyo cruises have to offer, with our curated shore excursions. From world-famous landmarks to hidden gems, we'll handle the details so you can put your full attention towards experiencing this brilliant Metropolis.

blocks.heading: Easy Tokyo
blocks.text: If you prefer sightseeing with less walking, this relaxed tour offers the perfect way to soak up Tokyo’s highlights. Enjoy a scenic drive through the city, passing landmarks like the Kabukiza Theater and Ginza district. Then, ascend Tokyo Tower for sweeping views from its observation deck. On clear days, you may even catch a glimpse of Mount Fuji, Japan's most famous peak. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Kamakura: Image of the Great Buddha & Shrine
blocks.text: Step back into Japan's samurai era with a visit to Kamakura, home to the majestic Great Buddha at Kotokuin Temple. This 750-year-old bronze statue stands 38 feet tall, creating a literally-larger-than-life manifestation of Japan’s storied past. You’ll also visit the historic Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine (dedicated to the patron god of the samurai) and enjoy time exploring the shops, boutiques and

blocks.heading: Best of Tokyo
blocks.text: Discover Tokyo’s timeless spirituality with visits to two iconic landmarks: the Meiji Shrine and Sensoji Temple. Walk beneath the towering Torii gates of Meiji Shrine, enveloped in a tranquil forest of over 120,000 trees. Then, immerse yourself in the energy of Nakamise Shopping Street as you make your way to Sensoji Temple, Tokyo's oldest and most celebrated Buddhist temple. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Tokyo on Your Own
blocks.text: Want to explore at your own pace? This excursion provides transportation to Tokyo's lively Shinjuku district, where the day is yours to plan. Admire sweeping views from the observation deck of the Tokyo Metropolitan Government building, or lose yourself in the fun shops and eateries of the Ginza district. When you are your own guide, Tokyo’s endless possibilities are always within reach. VIEW EXCU

blocks.heading: Things to do in Venice, Italy
blocks.text: Wander through the bustling Piazza San Marco, where the intricate mosaics of St. Mark’s Basilica captivate visitors. Then cross the Rialto Bridge for picturesque views of the Grand Canal, lined with gondolas and historic palazzos. For a quieter escape, explore the island of Murano, famous for its glassmaking artisans, or indulge in authentic Venetian cuisine, from creamy risottos to freshly made c

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Venice (Trieste)
blocks.text: Don’t stress over planning—experience the best Venice has to offer, stress-free, with Princess shore excursions. We’ll handle the details so you can relax and soak it all in. Here are some must-visit sites and activities to enhance your Venetian adventure the City of Canals:

blocks.heading: Trieste & Miramare Castle
blocks.text: Travel along the Adriatic coast to explore Trieste and the romantic Miramare Castle. Wander ornate rooms filled with royal history, stroll through lush seaside gardens and soak up sweeping views of the glittering Gulf of Trieste. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Venice, Doge's Palace & time on your own
blocks.text: Explore Venice’s most iconic landmarks on a guided tour through St. Mark’s Square. Step inside Doge’s Palace and admire the Golden Staircase, then cross the Bridge of Sighs for a final look at the lagoon before wandering through shops and cafés at your own pace. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Aquileia & Redipuglia
blocks.text: Trace Italy’s layered past in Aquileia, where ancient Roman ruins and the Basilica’s vast mosaic floor reveal a city of faith and empire. Then, pay tribute at Redipuglia War Memorial, the final resting place of thousands who served in World War I. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The caves of Postumia
blocks.text: Venture beneath Slovenia’s countryside aboard an underground railway to witness Postojna Cave’s stunning limestone formations. Discover towering stalagmites, shimmering chambers and the mysterious olm — the pale salamander that calls this subterranean wonder home. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Lipica Stud Farm & horse performance
blocks.text: Marvel at Slovenia’s elegant Lipizzaner horses during a visit to the Lipica Stud Farm. Tour the historic stables, meet the prized stallions and watch a Classical School of Riding performance that showcases centuries of equestrian tradition. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: From gondolas to grand adventures on the high seas
blocks.text: Begin your journey in one of the world’s most romantic cities, where every winding canal and charming bridge evokes timeless beauty. Venice is a city steeped in history, from the grandeur of St. Mark’s Basilica to the elegance of the Rialto Bridge. With Princess, set sail from this magical port to discover Mediterranean treasures, explore Italy’s stunning coastline and bask on sun-drenched islands

blocks.heading: Things to do in Anchorage
blocks.text: Although your ship departs from Whittier, most guests spend time in Anchorage before boarding — and there’s plenty to see and do. Like the gold that attracted early settlers, the city offers a treasure trove of activities. Dive into Alaska’s rich history at the Anchorage Museum or the Alaska Native Heritage Center. For a closer connection to nature, walk or bike along the Tony Knowles Coastal Trai

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Anchorage
26 Glacier Cruise & Anchorage Transfer
blocks.text: Hop aboard a catamaran and travel 140 miles into Prince William Sound to see 26 "named" glaciers, as well as an abundance of wildlife - both on shore and below the water on this 5.25-hour cruise. A hot meal is included as well as a no-seasickness guarantee and a transfer to select Anchorage hotels and the airport. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Chugach Photo Adventure – Roundtrip
blocks.text: Start your cruise with some serious camera time. This guided photo tour winds through rainforests, mountains and the coastal beauty of Turnagain Arm and Portage Valley. With expert guidance and time to explore natural highlights like waterfalls, rainforests and mountains, it’s a creative and memorable way to kick off your cruise. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Anchorage City Highlights & Museum
blocks.text: If you're spending time in Anchorage before heading to Whittier, this tour is a smart way to dive into local culture. Visit the Anchorage Museum to explore Alaska’s history, including rare Alaska Native artifacts, then tour city landmarks and enjoy time downtown before your cruise begins. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Turnagain Arm, Wildlife Conservation Center & Tram with Airport Transfer
blocks.text: Begin your trip with a scenic drive along Turnagain Arm, followed by a stop at the Alaska Wildlife Conservation Center, where rescued animals roam natural enclosures. Then head skyward on the Mt. Alyeska Tram for panoramic views of forested valleys and glacier-fed peaks — a great first look at the kind landscapes you'll soon be seeing from the ship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Portage Glacier Cruise Tour
blocks.text: Ready to feel small and insignificant (in a good way)? Cruise across Portage Lake right up to the massive and ancient Portage Glacier. Feel the brisk air and marvel at the sheer size of this pre-historic ice. It’s an intimate way to experience one of Alaska’s most iconic natural wonders. LEARN MORE

blocks.text: As one of the primary Gulf of Alaska embarkation ports served by multiple major cruise lines, Whittier is the departure point for Princess's signature Voyage of the Glaciers itineraries — typically one-way 7-night southbound sailings between Whittier and Vancouver. blocks.heading: What will you do on an Eastern Caribbean cruise?
blocks.text: There’s no right way to pass the days in the Eastern Caribbean.

blocks.heading: Old-world charm
blocks.text: The Eastern Caribbean is a treasure trove of old-world charm, blending colonial history with enchanting landscapes. Wander through the narrow streets of Old San Juan, Puerto Rico, where pastel-colored buildings and imposing fortresses tell tales of the past. Visit the historic sites of Philipsburg in St. Maarten, or explore the serene beauty of Princess Cays with its quaint beachfront and rustic a

blocks.heading: Breathtaking beaches
blocks.text: The Eastern Caribbean is renowned for its pristine, sun-kissed beaches, offering crystal-clear waters and powdery white sands that stretch as far as the eye can see. From the famous Maho Beach in St. Maarten, where planes soar overhead, to the secluded shores of Trunk Bay in the Virgin Islands, each beach promises a unique and unforgettable experience. Whether you’re looking to relax under swaying

blocks.heading: Local culture
blocks.text: Immerse yourself in the rich and diverse cultures of the Eastern Caribbean, where each island offers a unique tapestry of traditions, music and cuisine. Explore the lively markets of San Juan, Puerto Rico, where you can savor local delicacies like mofongo and listen to the rhythmic beats of salsa and reggaeton. Discover the historic charm of Charlotte Amalie in St. Thomas, with its cobblestone str

blocks.heading: Magens Bay, St. Thomas
blocks.text: One of the top 10 beaches in the world according to National Geographic magazine, Magens Bay, is known for its picturesque beauty and deep, sheltered bay with calm waters. With gentle waves rolling onto a white sand beach that stretches three quarters of a mile, Magens Bay is your place to relax, swim and explore with ease.

blocks.heading: Trunk Bay, St. John
blocks.text: Named one of Condé Nast Traveler's Seven Cruise Wonders of the World, Trunk Bay is stunning beyond words. Snorkel along an underwater coral reef trail, swim through warm clear waters, and lounge on the white sands while looking out on a vista that can only be described as tropical perfection.

blocks.heading: Orient Beach & Little Bay Beach, St. Maarten
blocks.text: Two beaches, both with soft sand, warm water and refreshing breezes, make for the perfect day by the ocean. Snorkel with sea life, paddle through the azure waters, or relax on the beach.

blocks.heading: Caribbean cruise onboard experience featured program
blocks.text: Award-winning programs. World-class chefs. And Caribbean-themed activities, day and night. With Princess, your ship is a destination all its own.

blocks.heading: Deeper experiences of the islands
blocks.text: Discover the history of local distilleries while sampling some of the region’s best rums, meet the parrots and macaws that call the Caribbean home in the ship's Piazza, or sink into the rhythms of the region with steel pan drum lessons. Our onboard activities give you the chance to gain a deeper connection and understanding to islands you'll visit on your voyage.

blocks.heading: Comfortable accommodations
blocks.text: Your stateroom is your home away from home where you can rest up and recharge between adventures. With the expertly designed Princess Luxury Bed, luxurious 100% Jacquard-woven cotton linens and our SLEEP program, specially created by a board-certified sleep expert, you might just get the best sleep of your life. We offer staterooms ranging from interior cabins to full suites, and we even offer con

blocks.heading: Bringing local life aboard
blocks.text: Embrace the spirit of the islands the moment you step on your ship with our Rhythm of the Caribbean program. Savor island cuisine, sip signature cocktails and engage in authentic regional experiences. Dance beneath the stars to vibrant island rhythms at exclusive parties, and immerse yourself in one-of-a-kind cultural activities — from concerts and crafts to talks from shark experts and treasure h

blocks.heading: Never miss a beat
blocks.text: Say goodbye to the daily grind with our new Sail Away Party poolside on the top deck, dance to local music at one of the many Caribbean inspired concerts, or be the envy of every pirate at our high-energy gold treasure-inspired Terrace Pool Gold Party. Throughout your Caribbean cruise there will be events that invite you to fully experience the islands.

blocks.heading: Mediterranean cruise ports of call
blocks.text: Discover some of the world-renowned destinations that await you on a Mediterranean cruise with Princess.

blocks.heading: Why cruise the Mediterranean
blocks.text: In lands where the culture is as flavorful as the cuisine, the splendor of the Mediterranean speaks for itself.

blocks.heading: Sun-kissed beaches
blocks.text: Visions of sparkling coasts and crystalline waters welcome you to the Mediterranean. Dip your toes on the black-sand coast of Santorini on a Greek cruise. Head to Salerno to spend the day in Positano relaxing on the white beaches and admiring the pastel houses that decorate the cliffs around you. Or travel to Mykonos with your loved ones and daydream on the city’s long stretch of golden sand and s

blocks.heading: World-class dining
blocks.text: With mouthwatering entrees and confections, the Mediterranean invites you to embark on a gourmet tour through iconic cities. Reawaken your taste buds with Italian classics like pastas, pizzas and gelato. Or fill your plate with gyros, keftethes and baklava on a Greek cruise. From breakfast to dinner and every delectable dessert in between, the best is before you with Princess.

blocks.heading: Rich wines
blocks.text: The countryside of Italy and Greece are home to some of the most flavorful wines around the globe. With sun and warm temperatures year-round, vineyards are flourishing with grapes by the harvest season. Sip on Italy’s red wines, or sample Greece’s white blends. From sweet Lambruscos to earthy Bordeauxs, fill up your glass on a Mediterranean cruise with Princess.

blocks.heading: Ancient ruins
blocks.text: From towers and temples to cities and shorelines, the Mediterranean is sprinkled with remains of civilizations past. Step back in time on a tour through ancient ruins on a Mediterranean cruise with Princess. Imagine life as a gladiator at the Colosseum, explore Greek mythology at the Parthenon and discover the archeological excavations of Pompeii — a lost city and UNESCO World Heritage Site.

blocks.heading: Art galleries & museums
blocks.text: From the treasures on land to the jewels within museums, the Mediterranean is a true work of art. On an Italian cruise, see portraits from the Renaissance period at the Uffizi Museum in Florence, and admire Michelangelo’s masterpieces at the Vatican Museum in Rome. blocks.heading: Why cruise with Princess
blocks.text: Curated comfort, world-class entertainment and international flavors await you.

blocks.heading: Celebrations & Romance
blocks.text: It's difficult to imagine something more romantic than sailing through the alluring cities and charming countryside of Europe. While on board your European cruise, we cater to your sentimental side with private dining on your balcony — like breakfast for two or a sunset dinner — honeymoon packages, flowers and chocolates delivered to your room and couples-only massages in the Sanctuary.

blocks.heading: Accommodations
blocks.text: Your stateroom is where you rest and recharge between adventures. That’s why every room is equipped with the expertly designed Princess Luxury Bed, 100% Jacquard-woven cotton linens. Whether you go interior or all-out in a suite, our staterooms will make you feel right at home. Especially for families traveling together who can enjoy the option of connected rooms.

blocks.heading: Dining
blocks.text: From the spice of Moroccan tagine to the sweetness of Greek Baklava, Europe’s flavor profile is incredibly diverse. On a Transatlantic cruise with Princess, taste the best of Europe on board with specialty dining. Say cheers during a lively lunch at a British-style pub and try English favorites like bangers and mash or shepherd's pie. Or savor hearty Italian pastas at Sabatini’s℠ Italian Trattoria

blocks.heading: Entertainment
blocks.text: Embark on adventures by day, and indulge in entertainment by night. Watch Movies Under the Stars® at our 300-square-foot outdoor theater. blocks.text: Our European cruises were crafted with every guest in mind — even the younger ones. From 6-month old babies to 17-year old teens, kids can unwind and relax or play and explore. With engaging activities on board and ashore, kids can see history books come to life before their eyes.

blocks.text: Experience the thrill of cards, dice, roulette, and blackjack at our onboard casino during your European cruise. Learn from our expert staff or seasoned guests, and put your skills to the test. For a more relaxed pace, enjoy the slot machines, or join fellow travelers for Bingo and exciting group tournaments. blocks.text: With Princess, travel effortlessly through Mediterranean beaches, the British Isles and Norwegian fjords. On European cruises, meet locals who call these destinations home, see world-famous landmarks and relive stories of the past.

blocks.heading: Enjoy the convenience of cruising

Cruise from one destination to the next with world-class entertainment, fresh food and relaxing accommodations at your fingertips. When you return to the ship, continue your exploration with unique activities and global cuisine, or enjoy the familiar comforts of home with your favorite foods — all on our

blocks.heading: Cruising vs. land vacations
blocks.text: Revel in first-class experiences without the first-class price tag. On a European cruise, unpack once and save on transportation and baggage fees as well as dining and entertainment costs. Independent land travel through Europe adds up fast — between accommodations, restaurants, train travel, taxis and more. But with Princess, you can spend more time exploring Europe and less time checking into yo

blocks.heading: Experience different seasons of Europe
blocks.text: See the many faces of the world with seasonal European cruise sailings from Princess. In the spring, shop in France’s colorful outdoor markets for hand-crafted souvenirs. Frolic through Norway’s landscapes when they fully bloom in summer. Or visit Italy in the fall to taste the first wines of the season.

blocks.heading: Sail aboard our newest ships
blocks.text: Built in Italy, our newest ships first set sail in international waters for their inaugural season. On a European cruise, you can be one of the first to travel aboard these vessels, adding a whole new level of excitement and opportunity to your trip. Plus these are the first ships designed with Princess® MedallionClass®, making them the best European cruises at sea.

blocks.heading: See famous landmarks
blocks.text: Between the castles, towers and ruins, Europe is teeming with ancient architecture. On a European cruise, sail into Le Havre and choose to visit the beaches of Normandy or ascend the Eiffel Tower in Paris. Walk through the Colosseum in Rome and stop by Livorno to see the Leaning Tower of Pisa. Or explore hidden gems — like Belfast’s Giant’s Causeway.

blocks.heading: A vacation for every generation
blocks.text: In Europe, there are activities for all. With exciting tours through age-old cities, kids can see textbooks come to life and return with their own stories to tell. Parents can relish romance and relaxation amidst fairytale landscapes and grandparents can relive stories of memories past with their loved ones. blocks.heading: Why cruise with Princess

blocks.heading: Celebrations & romance
blocks.text: It's difficult to imagine something more romantic than sailing through the alluring cities and charming countryside of Europe. While on board your European cruise, we cater to your sentimental side with private dining on your balcony — like breakfast for two or a sunset dinner — honeymoon packages, flowers and chocolates delivered to your room and couples-only massages in the Sanctuary.

blocks.heading: Accommodations
blocks.text: Your stateroom is where you rest and recharge between adventures. That’s why every room is equipped with the expertly designed Princess Luxury Bed, 100% Jacquard-woven cotton linens and our SLEEP program created by a board-certified sleep expert. From interior cabins to full suites, unwind in any of our staterooms and enjoy peace of mind with the option of connected rooms for families of four or m

blocks.text: From the spice of Moroccan tagine to the sweetness of Greek Baklava, Europe’s flavor profile is incredibly diverse. On board your European cruise, enjoy English favorites — like bangers and mash or shepherd’s pie — during a British-style pub lunch. Then head ashore to savor fresh ingredients and iconic dishes, including fresh Greek salads and Italian gelato. From ship to shore, taste the best of a

blocks.heading: Wine
blocks.text: Home to some of the best vineyards in the world, Europe knows a thing or two about wine — and so does Princess. Visit Vines wine bar, one of the best-stocked cellars at sea and sample an assortment of reds and whites. Unwind with a drink in hand at Crooners, a vintage Sinatra-era cocktail lounge. Or enjoy a glass from the comfort of your stateroom balcony while taking in views of Europe’s most ins

blocks.heading: Cultural immersion
blocks.text: On a European cruise, explore destinations even at sea. Learn from local experts — like musicians, dancers, athletes and chefs — who come on board to show you the unique personality of each region. Or listen to stories from international crew members, many of whom call these lands home. Even kids can awaken their sense of wonder with our Youth and Teen Centers.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Berlin
blocks.text: If Berlin had a résumé, it would be... extensive. This city has witnessed empires rise, walls fall and currywurst become a national treasure. It’s part open-air museum, part cultural playground and 100% worth exploring. From landmark-hopping to back-alley art walks, Berlin’s story is the history of the modern world.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Berlin (Warnemünde)
blocks.text: When you’ve only got a day or so in one of the most important cities in Europe, how do you make it count? With a curated experience from Princess! These excursions dig into the grit and the glory, the castles and the kebabs, the Cold War and the café culture. Pick your adventure — or pile on a few. Just remember that there is no port in Berlin, so you’ll be docking in Warnemünde first and then tra

blocks.heading: Berlin by Train & the Royal Route to Potsdam
blocks.text: Start with Berlin’s greatest hits, then escape to Potsdam — a city where Prussian kings once built palaces, planted gardens and probably argued about statues. You’ll explore ornate halls, the Dutch Quarter and a bridge once used to swap Cold War spies. This isn’t your average day trip. But then, Berlin isn’t your average city, either. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Berlin by Private Vehicle Van Class Full Day with Driver & Guide
blocks.text: Want to skip the script and call the shots yourself? Book a private van with your own English-speaking driver-guide and design the day around your kind of sightseeing. Check out landmarks, linger at lunch or dive into a museum — it’s your day, your way. Perfect if you like to adventure outside the lines. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ultimate Berlin by Train
blocks.text: All aboard the history express. This jam-packed day includes iconic Berlin stops — Brandenburg Gate, Berlin Wall, Reichstag — with extras like rooftop bubbly, lunch and shopping along the city’s poshest street. If Berlin had a highlight reel, this would be it. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp & Memorial
blocks.text: This isn’t just a tour — it’s an experience you take with you wherever you go. Walk the grounds of Sachsenhausen with a guide who brings history into sharp focus, then head into Berlin for a look at how the city remembers and reflects. Heavy? Yes. Worthwhile? Absolutely. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Berlin by Train & Jewish History
blocks.text: Uncover the significance of the Jewish history in Berlin’s past with stops that span memory, resilience and living culture. Visit the Jewish Museum, see the Holocaust Memorial and stroll the city’s Old Jewish Quarter. It’s a thought-provoking look at a community that has shaped, and been shaped by, the city around it. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Schwerin Castle, Lake Schwerin Cruise & Rostock
blocks.text: Not all German castles sit on mountaintops. Schwerin Castle floats on a lake, surrounded by manicured gardens and real-life fairy-tale vibes. After a cruise and a castle wander, you’ll hit Rostock’s charming town center for even more storybook moments (plus beer, obviously). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Rostock, River Cruise & Microbrewery
blocks.text: If your dream day includes medieval architecture, riverside cruising and a freshly poured pint — this one’s for you. Wander Rostock’s storybook streets, pop into a brewery for something tall and frothy, then coast back to port by boat. Good views, good beer, good times. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Coastal Biking
blocks.text: Break up all that museum-going with a breezy coastal ride. This tour has beach-town charm, forest paths and a stop for German cake — because calories don’t count on bikes, right? It’s an active way to see another side of Germany. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Berlin port on your next cruise
blocks.text: If you’re on a Baltic & Scandinavian cruise or one touring Europe, you should be aware that Berlin doesn’t have a cruise terminal — but don’t let that fool you. You’ll dock in Warnemünde, then hop a train straight into the pulse of Germany’s capital. It’s a bold day trip, but that’s part of the thrill. And if you’d rather keep it local, Rostock and Schwerin have charm, history and fewer crowds — n

Our ship sailing to Berlin
blocks.text: There’s only one ship that gets you to Berlin like this — and it brings the modern perks, panoramic views and culinary hits you’ll wish followed you home.

blocks.text: Sky Princess® takes everything you love about European travel and adds ocean breezes, fine dining and a seriously comfy bed. Expect award-winning food, soaring entertainment venues and more staterooms than ever. After a day diving into Berlin’s big moments, this ship brings the calm, the class and the cocktails.

Why cruise the British Isles
blocks.text: The British pubs, Parisian artwork and Irish castles invite you to live like royalty.

blocks.heading: More ashore
blocks.text: Enjoy even more history and culture during your British Isles cruise with More Ashore late-night departures and overnight stays. Visit several pubs during an evening tour, and hear stories from locals over a pint of local brew. Savor a traditional Scottish dinner in Edinburgh, and see the Royal Mile illuminated by street lamps and the evening light. Or explore Dublin by night, and indulge in Irish

blocks.heading: Castles
blocks.text: Castles are the emblem of these regions. Between the chandeliers and tapestries, step into luxury when you visit the British Isles. Cruise to Dublin and parade through the 13th-century halls of the city’s fortress. Experience the grandeur of Urquhart Castle, and search for legendary ghosts in Glamis Castle. Or visit Edinburgh Castle, where kings, queens and nobles once lived and medieval secrets c

blocks.heading: Music
blocks.text: As the birthplace of many music icons, the British Isles invite you to sing, dance and raise a glass to songs played around the globe. Visit Liverpool to walk in the footsteps of a beloved boyband, and head to a local pub to hear the boys at their best. Cruise the British Isles for an evening of Irish song and dance in Dublin, or watch the Edinburgh Military Tattoo assemble bands, bagpipes and dru

blocks.heading: Heritage
blocks.text: The British Isles are a mecca of UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Cruise from Southampton to Liverpool, and walk along the Royal Albert Dock, the first structure in Britain to be constructed without wood. Shop along Princes Street in Edinburgh’s New Town. Or travel to Brú na Bóinne in Dublin and get up close to Europe’s largest collection of prehistoric megalithic art.

blocks.heading: Pubs
blocks.text: In lands famous for their stouts and ales, pubs are the cornerstone of tradition. Cruise the British Isles and step into age-old establishments that are bustling with spirit. In Dublin, get a taste of true pub “craic” — an Irish term that equates to an atmosphere of fun, entertainment and good company. With festive music playing in the background, sip on world-famous beers that originated nearby w

blocks.heading: Natural phenomena
blocks.text: Discern fact versus fiction on a British Isles cruise, where mysteries and mythologies abound. In Portland, learn about the 5,000-year-old stone circle that displays an advanced understanding of arithmetic and astrology. On itineraries that sail to Cork, search the sea for the Bioluminescence beams created by the region’s gleaming plankton. Or hunt for Invergordon’s legendary monster in the waters

blocks.heading: Museums & art galleries
blocks.text: No cruise to the British Isles is complete without a visit to Paris. See “Venus de Milo” and da Vinci’s “Mona Lisa,” or tour Notre Dame, a work of art in and of itself. Visit the Irish Emigration Museum in Dublin, where interactive galleries invite you to explore. Those departing from London can also stop by the Victoria and Albert Museum which houses over two million artifacts.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Cork (Cobh), Ireland
blocks.text: Cork is a port thick with stories of migration, resilience and everyday Irish life. It became Ireland’s busiest hub of emigration. Dock here and you’re stepping onto the front porch of Ireland’s second city and widely considered Ireland’s top culinary scene. Expect buzzing pubs, thought-provoking museums and galleries, plus castles, markets, music and mischief, with Blarney Castle nearby and the c

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Cork (via Cobh)
blocks.text: Cork is about 15 miles from the port of Cobh, and that means if you want to experience it you need to leave the ship. Book an excursion through Princess makes it easy, and let us take you directly to medieval ruins, historic locations, beautiful landscapes and more.

blocks.heading: Private & Exclusive Cork Cultural Show
blocks.text: Step inside the Commodore Hotel and let the music take over. Jigs, reels and ballads shake the floor while you sip a pint or a glass of wine. It’s intimate and loud in the best way and about as Irish as an evening can get without getting a sheepdog involved. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Cork & Countryside
blocks.text: Spend the day hopping between Kinsale’s seaside charm, Cork’s lively streets and the ivy-draped ruins of Blarney Castle. If you dare, queue up to kiss the Blarney Stone (don’t worry; they sanitize it). Lunch comes with live music, and the Woolen Mill Shop is ready to test your suitcase space with tweeds and trinkets. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Scenic Killarney
blocks.text: A coach ride through southwest Ireland sets the stage for a full day in Kerry. Stop first in Kenmare for free time, then continue through Killarney National Park for views of lakes, mountains and the elegant Muckross House. A traditional two-course Irish lunch follows, capped with time to explore Killarney town, a lively hub of shops, pubs and people-watching. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Rock of Cashel, The Vee & Lismore
blocks.text: This full-day drive cuts through some of Ireland’s most dramatic countryside. Pause near Lismore to view its grand 12th-century castle, then continue toward Cashel for lunch and time at the Rock of Cashel (a dense cluster of medieval ruins tied to Irish kings and bishops). Expect big views, ancient stone and a lot of history packed into one hilltop stop. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Titanic Heritage Trail
blocks.text: Walk Cobh’s waterfront with a local guide and follow the final footsteps of Titanic passengers who departed here in 1912. Visit the original pier, former White Star Line offices and St. Colman’s Cathedral, whose spires dominate the harbor. An Irish coffee break keeps things civil before time at the Titanic Experience Museum, located in the former White Star ticket office. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Blarney Castle
blocks.text: The ruin looks straight out of a fantasy novel, but the real headline is the Blarney Stone. Climb the twisting stairs, hang backwards off a ledge and plant your lips on it if you’re game. If not, the Woolen Mill Shop nearby will happily console you with Irish knitwear. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience Cork and Cobh on your next cruise
blocks.text: Docking in Cobh means you’re already in the thick of it. St. Colman’s Cathedral towers over you and pubs are a two-minute stroll away. But more importantly, this port serves as the front door to Cork, one of Ireland’s most engaging cities and the heart of the region. Within easy reach are Blarney Castle, the English Market, historic streets and a countryside packed with villages and landmarks. If

blocks.heading: Things to do in Cherbourg
blocks.text: Cherbourg wears its history well, but it doesn’t take itself too seriously. One minute you’re walking through a centuries-old fortress or touring long-silent battlegrounds, the next you’re eyeing a pastry that feels just as legendary. The city invites exploration — through winding streets, seaside views and flavors that make even a casual snack feel like a moment of grand cultural epiphany. Cruise

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Cherbourg
blocks.text: Cherbourg cruises give you the opportunity to choose from curated Princess excursions that dig into Normandy’s epic past, spotlight its culinary gems and take you on journeys that are equal parts moving and mouthwatering.

blocks.heading: Battles of Normandy: In Hedgerows Hell
blocks.text: Begin at the Normandy Victory Museum, where detailed dioramas and authentic artifacts bring the chaos of battle to life. Then head out to explore the Carentan region, where dense hedgerows turned fields into deadly terrain. This tour gives you an up-close view of the challenges faced by Allied troops in their push inland. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ultimate Mont Saint-Michel
blocks.text: Venture to the dramatic island commune of Mont Saint-Michel, where medieval architecture rises above a tidal bay like something from a fantasy novel. Tour the towering abbey, explore winding stone streets and enjoy time to shop or snack in the village below. This full-day excursion mixes physical exploration with a healthy dose of wonder. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Normandy: D-Day Landing Beaches
blocks.text: Step into history on this powerful journey through some of World War II’s most pivotal locations. Visit Sainte-Mère-Église, Utah Beach, Omaha Beach, Pointe du Hoc and the American Cemetery, all in one day. With time for lunch and museum stops, this excursion connects past to present in a moving and unforgettable way. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Normandy Traditions & Epicurean Delights
blocks.text: Travel into Normandy’s scenic countryside where the flavors are as rich as the history. Visit a traditional Calvados distillery for a behind-the-scenes look and a tasting of the local apple brandy, cider and pommeau. Then stop at a beloved biscuit bakery that’s been in the same family for five generations. Yes, there are samples. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cotentin D-Day Landing Sites
blocks.text: Visit key Allied invasion sites, including Utah Beach, the Azeville Battery and the town of Sainte-Mère-Église. This tour offers a closer look at the heroism and tactical brilliance that shaped D-Day. The included stop at the Airborne Museum offers a powerful tribute to the paratroopers who changed the course of history. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Bayeux & The Tapestry
blocks.text: Travel to Bayeux to see the 230-foot-long embroidered tapestry that tells the story of William the Conqueror and the Battle of Hastings. Then explore the town’s charming medieval streets, visit the cathedral and enjoy time for shopping or a coffee. It’s a laid-back excursion with deep historical roots and a side of small-town charm. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience popular cruise itineraries with the Cherbourg port
blocks.text: Arriving in Cherbourg during your European or Transatlantic cruise feels less like docking and more like dropping into a scene that’s already in motion. The city hums with activity, with inviting streets, waterfront views and a proud maritime spirit that’s hard to miss. It’s a smooth starting point for deeper exploration, whether your plans involve day trips or discovering a few unexpected favorit

Our ship sailing to Cherbourg
blocks.text: Princess ships deliver the kind of comfort that pairs perfectly with a day of castle climbing and Calvados sipping. Designed with ocean views, elevated dining and plenty of space to unwind, Princess is the ideal launch platform for cruising your way through Normandy.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Madeira
blocks.text: Madeira makes you want to ask questions. Why are those vines growing sideways up a cliff? Who first thought of taking a wicker sled down a mountain? How did one island end up with so many microclimates and such strong opinions on embroidery? Funchal invites you to become a part of every answer. The kind told through basket rides, botanical wonders and wine that carries a bouquet that can only be e

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Madeira
blocks.text: If you came for views, flavors or culture — here’s your pick of ways to go full Madeira. Princess has tours perfect for photographers, wine lovers, slow‑strollers or anyone who enjoys a little positive peculiarity in their island paradise excursions.

blocks.heading: National Geographic Day Tour – Sustainable Agriculture in Camacha
blocks.text: Join a hands-on experience at Quinta Pedagógica da Camacha, a local farm committed to sustainable agriculture. Walk the terraced hills, pick seasonal fruits, help with planting, then sit down for homemade cakes and herbal tea brewed on site. It’s a slow‑food, slow‑living excursion with a personal touch. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Foodies on Foot: Local Tastes & Traditions
blocks.text: Set off on a four‑hour walking tour through Funchal’s Old Town and market alleys. You’ll sample seafood fresh off the boat, home‑baked bread, exotic fruits, local pastries and Madeira wines, all while your guide tells tales of explorers, sugar trade and food traditions that shaped the island’s soul. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cable Car, Traditional Sled Ride & Botanical Gardens
blocks.text: Float above town in a cable car, disembark in Monte and visit the Church of Our Lady of Monte. Then grip the wicker “carros de cesto” sleds for a unique downhill sled ride to Livramento. Finish with a walk through the Botanical Gardens, where rare plants and sweeping terraces deliver a peaceful counterpoint to the thrill of the ride. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ultimate Madeira
blocks.text: Head east for dramatic views at Pináculo, stop at Ponta do Garajau for sea‑swept cliffs and Christ statue, then savor a traditional Madeira lunch paired with wine. After dining, explore Monte village’s gardens and winding streets. Top it off with the trolley‑sled descent to feel what centuries of visitors have loved. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Botanical Gardens & Monte Cable Car
blocks.text: Take the cable car up to Monte, then descend via the wicker sledges with local guides. Discover terraces of flora, rare orchids and sweeping views over Funchal. See the church in Monte and take in scenery that’s shaped by volcanic soil, ocean spray and sheer elevation. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cable Car, Traditional Sled Ride & Wine Tasting
blocks.text: This variation pairs the height, the thrill and the taste: after your cable car and sled ride, sample wines at the Oliveira Wine Lodge. The combo balances scenery with sip-worthy moments. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Funchal: Around the Island
blocks.text: Prefer fewer steps, more views? Ride in comfort on a narrated drive across Madeira’s southeastern coast. See Machico, Porto da Cruz, Poiso Pass and Monte. Optional short walks and photo stops allow you to enjoy the views without wearing out your shoes. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cabo Girão & Mercado dos Lavradores
blocks.text: Drive to the heights of Cabo Girão, one of Europe’s highest sea cliffs and peer down to the waves below. Then dip into the artistry of Madeira with a visit to an embroidery factory. Learn how threads and hands carry heritage forward, then browse showrooms filled with patterns, color and craftsmanship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Madeira port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Pulling into Funchal feels more like arriving at someone’s favorite memory than just another port of call. Cobblestone streets wind up into hillside gardens, salty air mixes with the scent of baked goods and the harbor views unfold like a watercolor in motion. Whether you’re sipping Madeira wine under a pergola or eyeing the peaks from a cable car, it all starts just steps from your ship. It's thi

blocks.heading: Discover Madeira on your next cruise
Ships sailing to Madeira
blocks.text: Think of your Princess ship as more than just transportation — it’s your private lounge, your floating restaurant row and your personal balcony on the Atlantic. After a day spent winding through Monte or clinking glasses in a wine lodge, you’ll head back to a ship that matches Madeira’s charm (with comfort and luxury to spare).

blocks.heading: Things to do in Aarhus
blocks.text: Aarhus pulses with youth, history and design — it’s both a student town and a cultural heavyweight. You’ll roam open‑air village museums, step beneath a soaring copper spire, wander parks that spill into forest — and feel how old Denmark and daring design collide along its fjords and coasts.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Aarhus
blocks.text: Vacations are all about relaxation — so leave the planning to us. Choose from our stress-free excursions that will show you the best of Barcelona, so you can experience the city without the hassle.

blocks.heading: A Day at the LEGO® House for Families
blocks.text: This all‑ages excursion heads to LEGO® House in Billund, 90 minutes away by bus. The building itself is a bold architectural statement, packed with installations, games, brick walls and giant LEGO® displays. Create, explore or just be awed — then ride back, filled with color and creative energy. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Highlights of Aarhus
blocks.text: This full‑tilt city sampler takes you past Aarhus Town Hall, the university grounds, the Botanical Garden and the ARoS Aarhus Art Museum (with its skywalk of color). After a photo stop at the massive Aarhus Cathedral, enjoy free time in the center before ending in Den Gamle By, where 75+ historic structures resurrect Danish life from centuries past. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Fast and the Foodie
blocks.text: Launch into a RIB‑boat ride along Aarhus Bay with the Sea Rangers, whipping past coastline views and hearing Viking lore. Land in the city for a lunch of creamy “smørrebrød” at a longtime café, then take a motorcoach ride back with sweeping views of the region and commentary on local culture, agriculture and coastal life. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ebeltoft & Scenic Drive
blocks.text: Venture east to Ebeltoft, a storybook town of cobblestones, half‑timbered houses and the historic frigate Jylland. Wander museums, glass studios and shops. Then cruise through Mols National Park, past Bronze Age mounds and rugged coastal vistas until you return to Aarhus with memories engraved by forest and sea. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Royal Jelling: The Birthplace of Denmark
blocks.text: Travel back 1,100 years to Jelling, where runic stones, burial mounds and temple alignments mark the founding myths of Denmark. A sensory “Experience Center” makes Viking tales visceral — complete with transitions to Christianity, warrior paths and pagan echoes. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Moesgaard Museum, City Drive & Time On Your Own
blocks.text: This tour combines architecture and archaeology. First, you’ll visit Moesgaard Museum, whose sleek glass structure sits amid forest and showcases artifacts from the Bronze Age through Viking age. Next, enjoy a guided city drive then drop off in the center for a full hour to explore shops, cafes or Danish design culture at your pace. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Aarhus: Canal Walk, ARoS & Den Gamle
blocks.text: Begin with a shaded walk along the Aarhus Canal, lined with cafés, water views and slow charm. Then explore ARoS Aarhus Art Museum (don’t miss Your Rainbow Panorama) before diving into Den Gamle By, where costumed interpreters run workshops across centuries. Motorcoach brings you home to ship at the end. VIEW EXCUSRION

blocks.heading: Easy Aarhus & the Natural History Museum
blocks.text: Perfect for those who prefer fewer steps but still want a taste of culture and nature. Drive through the city’s highlights, visit Aarhus Cathedral (with its frescoes and 16th‑century altar), and end at the Natural History Museum, where animals, ecosystems and paleontology stories draw you in. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Aarhus port on your next cruise
blocks.text: When your ship docks, you’ll arrive into a port well integrated into city life. Aarhus cruise port is conveniently located near main arteries, making it easy to hop into town via local transport, taxis, or guided shuttles. You’ll find cafés, galleries and green expanses nearby — a strong contrast to ports that dump you into nothing but terminals. This is a gateway, not a waiting room, and that’s w

blocks.heading: Things to do in Ajaccio
blocks.text: Sun‑bleached cliffs, pastel houses and the birthplace of a little fellow named Napoleon Bonaparte (you may have heard of him). Ajaccio mixes imperial ambition with island chill — narrow alleys lead from the cathedral where "Le Petit Caporal" was baptized to cafés buzzing with Corsican chatter and outdoor markets selling local cheeses, honey and wines. Expect plenty of outdoor activities, natural b

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Ajaccio
blocks.text: Time to choose your kind of Corsica: mythic coastline drives, historic city spins or forested gorge scouting — each curated for maximum local flavor.

blocks.heading: Napoleon’s Ajaccio: A Small Group Tour
blocks.text: Step into the life of Napoleon in his hometown: visit the Cathedral from 1771, the Maison Bonaparte museum filled with memorabilia and the Fesch Museum with its Italian masterpieces. This fully on‑foot tour operates in small groups, includes strict security protocols and takes you deep into Corsica’s imperial era before returning to your ship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Calanches & Cargèse
blocks.text: Take a narrated motorcoach ride along the coast past summer resorts to San Bastiano Pass and stand above the Gulfs of Ajaccio, Lava and Sagone. Visit the Greek‑heritage village of Cargèse then marvel at the red and orange granite rock formations of the Calanche, rising nearly 1,000 feet above sea level. Free time in Piana offers shopping or photo ops before you return to the ship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ajaccio’s Old Town & Surroundings
blocks.text: Start at Place d’Austerlitz to view a monumental tribute to Napoleon’s victories, then travel out along the scenic Sanguinaires Road with its rugged inlets and beaches. Visit a viewpoint over the Iles Sanguinaires archipelago and return to Ajaccio for a walking tour including the 16th‑century Cathedral (where Napoleon was baptized) and the Maison Bonaparte museum before returning to port. LEARN MO

blocks.heading: Vizzavona
blocks.text: Head inland into Corsica’s wild heart on a half‑day ride through fragrant macchia and pine‑clad hills to Bocognano’s granite houses then on to Vizzavona Forest and Pass perched around 3,300 feet above sea level. Enjoy views of Monte d’Oro and a ‘spuntinu’ lunch of cheese, cured meats and local wine. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Prunelli Gorges
blocks.text: Journey via winding mountain roads through the Zipitolli Forest and arrive at Prunelli Gorges — red granite cliffs tumble into forest‑lined rivers and Tolla Lake offers a striking photo stop. Savor a local café snack of Corsican cheese, charcuterie and wine before heading back to the harbour. Not ideal for guests who have a problem with heights (or delicious food). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ajaccio on Foot, Local Market & Tasting: A Small Group Tour
blocks.text: This walking tour begins in flow with a guide through Ajaccio Old Town where Napoleon’s birthplace, the cathedral and Place Foch await. Then move to market square for samplings of Corsican delicacies and artisan goods. The group stays small (25 or fewer) and the pace is easy even while the ground is uneven — comfy shoes recommended. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Ajaccio
blocks.text: When you book cruises to Ajaccio you’re plugging into a port that delivers shoreline glamour, historic weight and accessible outdoor adventures all in one. The ship docks at the heart of Ajaccio, meaning the cafés, local markets and major sites like Place Foch and the cathedral are only minutes away. blocks.heading: Things to do in Akureyri
blocks.text: Known as the “Capital of the North,” Akureyri is a small city with a big personality. Snow-dusted peaks frame a colorful town that feels equal parts lively and laid-back. Icelandic turf houses, geothermal pools — Akureyri has it all and offers a gateway to nature, culture and adventure.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Akureyri
blocks.text: Cruises to Akureyri with Princess mean excursions that showcase northern Iceland’s raw beauty. Guided tours balance epic landscapes with cultural insights, so you can experience both the region’s natural wonders and its traditions.

blocks.heading: Whale Watching Adventure
blocks.text: Set sail through Eyjafjörður, Iceland’s longest fjord, in search of humpback whales. With mountains rising on both sides, this excursion combines Arctic scenery with thrilling wildlife encounters. Keep an eye out for dolphins and porpoises alongside your vessel. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Akureyri
blocks.text: Explore volcanic landscapes, bizarre lava fields and the steaming geothermal areas around Lake Mývatn. Highlights include Dimmuborgir’s twisted rock formations, pseudo-craters at Skútustaðir and the steaming vents of Námaskarð. A stop at Godafoss Waterfall completes this full-day adventure, with a scenic return to Akureyri. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Godafoss Waterfall, Lava Labyrinth & Hot Springs
blocks.text: This half-day outing combines the power of Godafoss with Iceland’s geothermal drama. Walk among the otherworldly fumaroles and boiling mud pools at Námaskarð, then explore Dimmuborgir’s labyrinth of lava pillars before returning to Akureyri along the fjord. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Godafoss, Botanical Gardens & Laufás Folk Museum
blocks.text: Visit three of Akureyri’s signature sites in one tour. First, stand at Godafoss where Iceland’s conversion to Christianity became legend. Then stroll through the Akureyri Botanical Garden before exploring Laufás Folk Museum’s turf-roofed farmhouses filled with historic artifacts. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Godafoss Waterfall & Mývatn Nature Baths
blocks.text: Pair sightseeing with relaxation on this journey to Lake Mývatn. After admiring Godafoss, soak in the Mývatn Nature Baths, a geothermal lagoon where milky-blue waters and mountain views make for an unforgettable soak. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Siglufjörður, Herring Era Museum & Salting Show
blocks.text: Travel to Siglufjörður, once Iceland’s busiest herring port. Explore the award-winning Herring Era Museum and watch a salting demonstration before sampling rye bread, schnapps and herring. The scenic drive along fjords makes this a cultural and culinary favorite. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Akureyri port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Princess ships dock directly at Akureyri’s harbor, within walking distance of the town center. From the pier, it’s easy to explore cafés, shops and landmarks before heading out to Iceland’s dramatic northern landscapes. Akureyri is a highlight on Iceland & Norway cruises and part of Princess’s wider Europe itineraries.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Alesund
blocks.text: Pick your vibe — whether you crave hairpin mountain roads, island visits or city‑plus‑fjord hybrids, these curated excursions deliver memorable, off‑beat experiences.

blocks.heading: The Atlantic Ocean Park, Sunnmøre Museum & City Drive for Families
blocks.text: Start in Alesund’s German Art Nouveau district, drive to the open‑air museum with 40 historic vessels including an 8th‑century Viking longboat, then walk through Atlantic Sea‑Park’s massive tanks with divers feeding giant Atlantic species behind a 92‑foot‑long acrylic panel — wild, educational and ideal for families. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Best of Romsdal & the Troll Path
blocks.text: Depart the pier by motorcoach and follow a coastal‑fjord route through the Storfjord to Valldal, famous for strawberries, then climb the Trolls’ Path with 11 hairpin curves and views that scream ‘Norway!’ Finish at the Troll Wall — Europe’s highest rock face — before cruising the Romsdalsfjord and mountain plateau back to Alesund. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Step Back in Time: A Walk Through Alesund
blocks.text: Begin this guided tour at Jugendstilsenteret, housed in the 1907 Swan Apothecary Building, then explore the rebuilt early 20th‑century city centre, dive into harbourfront history in Norway’s major fishing port and rise above the city at Mt Aksla for a final dominant view over the islands. Your feet have never taken you so far back in time. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hiking Sugarlump Mountain
blocks.text: Gear up for three hours of outdoor adrenaline: a quick ride from Alesund takes you to the base of Sugarlump Mountain on Hessa Island where you’ll hike approximately 2.5 miles gaining nearly 1,000 feet elevation, study indigenous flora and fauna along the Sunnmøre Mountains and finally return to motorcoach at ease. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Hjorundfjord Cruise
blocks.text: Board a sightseeing boat for a relaxed cruise through the 20‑mile‑long Hjorundfjord, one of Norway’s lesser‑known yet still very dramatic fjords, framed by peaks rising 5,000 feet above sea level, keep an eye out for the ‘Trollman’ rock legend, float through Vegsundet and Borgundfjord before heading back to Alesund. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Islands of Giske & Godøy

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Alghero
blocks.text: Shore excursions from Alghero reveal the island of Sardinia's natural beauty, ancient history and vibrant coastal culture. Each experience offers a unique way to explore its stunning beaches, archaeological sites and picturesque villages.

blocks.heading: Easy Alghero & Cape Caccia
blocks.text: Take in Sardinia’s beauty on a panoramic tour along the coast near Alghero. Enjoy breathtaking views of Porto Ferro, Porto Conte Bay and Cape Caccia, with photo stops and a relaxing café break. Visit the exterior of Nuraghe Palmavera, one of Sardinia’s prehistoric stone towers, before continuing through Fertilia and returning to port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Alghero & Bosa
blocks.text: Journey along Sardinia’s breathtaking coast on a 5-hour guided tour from Alghero to the ancient town of Bosa. Explore its colorful riverfront, admire the medieval Serrevalle Castle and browse handmade lace in local shops. Back in Alghero, enjoy a guided walk through the old town’s historic landmarks and charming streets which are rich with culture. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cape Caccia & Wine Tasing
blocks.text: Immerse yourself in Sardinia’s rich culture and flavors on this 4-hour excursion from Alghero. Stroll through the medieval quarter to see landmarks like Palazzo d’Albis and the Church of San Francesco, then visit the Wine Resort Leda’ d’Ittiri for a guided tasting of local Vermentino, Cannonau and Cagnulari wines. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cruise the Gulf of Alghero
blocks.text: Embark on a scenic 4-hour cruise north from Cape Caccia, gliding past dramatic cliffs, sea-carved caves and hidden coves. Enjoy a stop at one of the coast’s most beloved beaches, where you can swim in crystalline waters, bask in the sun or stroll along the shoreline. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Castelsardo
blocks.text: Journey to the medieval hilltop town of Castelsardo, a Sardinian treasure overlooking the Mediterranean. Stop at the remarkable Elephant Rock, a natural formation shaped by the elements, before exploring Castelsardo’s 12th-century castle and Baroque cathedral on a guided tour. Conclude your visit browsing local shops for handcrafted Sardinian baskets and other authentic souvenirs. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Church of San Francesco & Nuraghe Palmavera
blocks.text: Journey to Nuraghe Palmavera to uncover the fascinating ruins of Sardinia’s ancient Nuraghi civilization. Take in sweeping views of the Riviera del Corallo and Cape Caccia’s dramatic coastline before exploring Alghero’s medieval quarter on a guided tour. Visit the 14th-century Church of San Francesco, then enjoy free time to wander the charming streets and browse local shops. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Alicante
blocks.text: Alicante is a Mediterranean beauty with Moorish history, postcard-worthy beaches and a no-rush, no-fuss local vibe. Wander the palm-shaded Explanada de España, climb Mount Benacantil for a fortress-top view or just follow the scent of churros through the Barrio de la Santa Cruz. However you choose to make the most of your day in port, the city will be your cultural treasure hunt.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Alicante
blocks.text: Alicante’s excursions range from coastal hikes and castle climbs to inland wine tastings and cave tours. For historic towns, panoramic views and lots of local flavor, there’s an activity (or maybe even two) to complete your day ashore.

blocks.heading: Alicante Express by Double-Decker, Open-Top Bus
blocks.text: This leisurely, non-stop, get-acquainted tour is the perfect introduction to Alicante's Mediterranean charm. Board the open-top double-decker bus right at the terminal and sit back as you cruise by Alicante’s most iconic landmarks. Glide past Postiguet Beach, famous for its golden sand and views of Santa Bárbara Castle, then follow the sweeping Explanada de España. You’ll also see the winding stre

blocks.heading: Best of Alicante, Benidorm & Canelobre Caves
blocks.text: This full-day adventure starts in Benidorm, where skyscrapers rise from historic roots, then heads inland to Busot to explore the drip-sculpted wonderland of the Canelobre Caves (their cathedral-like vault and strange formations will leave you blinking). Wrap up with a walking tour through Alicante, and enjoy some free time to lunch like a local. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Highlights of Guadalest
blocks.text: Trade the beach scene for the mountains with a trip to the jaw-dropping village of Guadalest. Perched high on a rocky ridge, it delivers views for days and history to match. Walk through its cobbled alleys to the ruins of San Jose Castle, then step into the preserved Orduña House to (figuratively) time travel back to the 1600s. Before heading back to port, enjoy some freedom to explore, shop or sn

blocks.heading: Novelda & Wine Tasting
blocks.text: Sip your way through Spain’s wine country on this half-day getaway to Novelda. After a scenic drive, you'll arrive at Heretat de Cecilia, a historic bodega. Taste two distinct wines, munch on local snacks and explore the cellars. Bonus: time to shop for a bottle (or three) to take home. Cap it off with a panoramic drive back through Alicante. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Alicante on Foot & Santa Bárbara Castle
blocks.text: Walk through centuries of conquest, rebellion and reinvention. Start at the top — literally — with a visit to Santa Bárbara Castle, built by the Moors and still towering over the city from Mount Benacantil. Then head down to explore Alicante's Old Quarter, passing Town Hall and the baroque grandeur of the Co-cathedral of St. Nicholas of Bari. With time to wander solo before heading back to port, y

blocks.heading: Discover Alicante by Tuk-Tuk
blocks.text: Hop into a tuk-tuk and see Alicante from the breezy seat of this three-wheeled, electric-powered ride. Zip through landmarks like Plaza del Ayuntamiento, the futuristic Water Museum and the storied streets of Barrio de la Santa Cruz. Santa Bárbara Castle offers a stop for panoramic photos, while the tiled waves of the Explana de España provide the perfect visual finale. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Alicante
blocks.text: Step off your ship and into a city that opens up fast. The cruise terminal drops you within minutes of must-see landmarks like the Explana de España, the marina and Santa Bárbara Castle towering above it all from Mount Benacantil. blocks.heading: Things to do in Alta
blocks.text: Where the tundra meets the sea, Alta blends Arctic stillness with all kinds of sightseeing and activity. From the titanium-clad Northern Lights Cathedral to prehistoric rock art and slate mountains, the Far North feels close enough to touch.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Alta
blocks.text: Wild landscapes, Sámi culture and rare Arctic light set the tone. Choose easy panoramas or lean into adventure.

blocks.heading: Snowshoeing and Ice Fishing
blocks.text: Strap on snowshoes for a gentle walk to a frozen lake. Drill a hole, settle on a reindeer hide and watch the line while hot drinks keep fingers warm. A fresh catch becomes lunch on the grill. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Sami Culture, Alta Dam and Canyon Adventure
blocks.text: Across Finnmarksvidda, the Alta Dam rises above a river that carved Sautso. Walk inside the dam tunnels, then sample local treats on the terrace. A Sámi camp adds stories, joik and daily life before canyon viewpoints frame the scale of Northern Europe’s biggest gorge. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Alta & the Northern Lights Cathedral
blocks.text: A gentle city circuit takes in Bossekop, Elvebakken and central Alta, with a photo stop at the cathedral wrapped in titanium and crowned by a 154-foot spire. As an architectural icon of the north, the Northern Lights Cathedral is a must-see. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Igloo Hotel Visit
blocks.text: At Sorrisniva, step into halls carved from snow and ice. Peek into sculpted rooms, learn how guests keep warm and toast the moment in the ice bar with a drink served in a hand-cut glass. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Northern Lights Safari at Pæskatun
blocks.text: High above the valley, slate cabins and a lavvu keep you warm between sky checks for the Northern Lights of Norway. Guides share camera tips after a short film about auroras, and clear nights can bring green ribbons right over the quarry ridge. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Sami Camp & Reindeer Sledging
blocks.text: Inside a lamplit lavvu, share coffee and cake on reindeer skins while your host sings a joik. Then glide through snow on a reindeer sledge for a quiet loop under the wide Arctic sky. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hike to Orvvos Waterfall
blocks.text: A short forest trail leads to Orvvosfossen where spray hangs in the cold air. Pause for photos, breathe the pine, then trace the same path back toward mountain views. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Whale Safari
blocks.text: Seasonal boat trips scan fjord waters for orcas and humpbacks, with sea eagles often circling overhead. When fins surface, the captain slows so you can frame the flukes against steep slate hills. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Alta port on your next cruise
blocks.text: There are endless things to do in Norway, and the Alta port is no exception. Ships typically dock at Alta’s harbor near the airport, just a short transfer from town. That makes it easy to pair a cathedral visit with canyon views or a slate-quarry aurora hunt on the same call. blocks.heading: Things to do in Amalfi Coast
Shore excursions to explore in Amalfi Coast
blocks.text: From ancient Roman cities frozen in time to cliffside towns overlooking the Tyrrhenian Sea, Princess shore excursions reveal the coast’s most unforgettable highlights. Each experience is designed to help you explore with ease so you can focus on the scenery, stories and flavors that make this region so celebrated.

blocks.heading: Mount Vesuvius & Pompeii Adventure: Hike to the Summit of Mount Vesuvius
blocks.text: Climb the winding path to the summit of Mount Vesuvius for close-up views of the crater and sweeping panoramas of the Bay of Naples. After descending, explore Pompeii on a guided tour that highlights homes, markets and mosaics preserved under volcanic ash. A visit to a cameo studio adds a final touch of local artistry. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Sorrento & Amalfi Coast
blocks.text: Drive one of Italy’s most scenic coastlines as you make your way from Salerno to Sorrento, where narrow lanes and sea views invite unhurried wandering. Enjoy free time for shopping or strolling the waterfront before continuing to Amalfi for lunch and a look at its striking cathedral. Your return by motorboat offers a new perspective of the cliffs rising above the sea. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Pompeii
blocks.text: Walk the remarkably preserved streets of Pompeii with a knowledgeable guide who brings the city’s final moments to life. See temples, baths and homes that still show frescoes and carvings from nearly two thousand years ago. After exploring the site, visit a traditional cameo workshop where artisans hand carve seashells into jewelry using centuries-old techniques. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Herculaneum
blocks.text: Discover Herculaneum, a seaside town buried in the same eruption that destroyed Pompeii but preserved in even greater detail. Your guided walk passes intact villas, marble fountains and intricate mosaics that reveal what daily life looked like in 79 A.D. A stop at a cameo factory rounds out the visit with a chance to see artisans at work. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Amalfi Coast Village and Ceramics
blocks.text: Explore Vietri sul Mare, the birthplace of Amalfi Coast majolica, where shopfronts glow with hand-painted tiles and pottery. Learn how volcanic clay from Mount Vesuvius is shaped into the region’s signature ceramics, then enjoy time to browse Corso Umberto I, home to family-run studios and displays that have defined this craft since antiquity. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Mozzarella Tasting & Paestum Excavations
blocks.text: Visit a working dairy to see Campania’s famed buffalo mozzarella made fresh each morning, then taste its rich, delicate flavor. Continue to Paestum, one of Italy’s best-preserved Greek archaeological sites, where soaring Doric temples and ancient city walls offer a glimpse into a once-thriving colony along the Gulf of Salerno. LEARN MORE
