blocks.heading: Things to do in Amsterdam
blocks.text: When your cruise docks in IJmuiden, you’re stepping into a curious mash-up of industrial edge and wind-swept beach town, where the Sea Lock is massive, the fish is fresh and Amsterdam is only a short ride away. While the city center doesn't allow large cruise ships in the city center, the North Sea Canal delivers you to this dynamic gateway. Once on land, expect a carousel of culture: canal tours,

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Amsterdam
blocks.text: Whether you want to see Rembrandt’s old digs or sip craft beer in a church-turned-brewery, there’s an excursion here that feels like it was made specifically for you. Pick one (or a few) and lean in.

blocks.heading: A Walk Through Haarlem & Tasting
blocks.text: Haarlem is what happens when Dutch charm decides to outdo itself. Your guide will lead you past market squares, gabled rooftops and cobbled streets before stopping at Jopenkerk *(that would be a church that became a brewery). Grab a craft beer, snack on local bites and toast to rethinking what the term ‘sacred space’ can mean. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Amsterdam On Your Own
blocks.text: This one’s for the self-starters and snackers. After a scenic 28-mile coach ride from port to the city, you're dropped off near the center with a map and lots of free time. Hit the Van Gogh Museum, snag a stroopwafel, shop in the Nine Streets or just park yourself canal-side and boatwatch. A guide is onboard the bus to field questions, but the day is all yours to explore. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Marken & Volendam Dairy Farm
blocks.text: Marken is that kind of village that would feel too idealized to be true if people didn’t actually live there. Walk past wooden homes propped on stilts to fight the tides, then move on to Volendam (a hamlet with drawbridges, canals and possibly the world’s cutest harbor). The grand finale? Cheese. Lots of it. At a dairy farm. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Delft Factory & The Hague
blocks.text: Meet Delft: the birthplace of that iconic blue pottery. It’s also your new favorite day trip. You’ll visit the last standing Delftware factory, watch artists hand-paint porcelain and then stroll through the charming canal-lined streets. On the way back, drive through The Hague where justice and international policy live in buildings prettier than most luxury homes. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Discover Utrecht & Visit of Castle De Haar
blocks.text: Utrecht serves Gothic realness with its Dom Tower and an old town that looks straight out of a film-location scout's dream. After your guided walk and some lunch-on-your-own time, you’ll hit up Castle De Haar: a spired fantasyland complete with drawbridges and enough turrets to make Disney jealous. It’s just this side of too much, and that makes it fantastic. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Amsterdam Canal Cruise & Time On Your Own
blocks.text: Float through the city like a 17th-century merchant (except you’ve got a camera with you). This scenic canal cruise shows off Amsterdam’s narrow, gable-topped homes and extremely ambitious staircases. After the ride, you’re free to explore on your own. May we suggest the Anne Frank House, some vintage shopping or just a deep dive into Amsterdam’s snack scene? LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Amsterdam
blocks.text: This coastal port is practical, chill and wonderfully close to the action. Amsterdam is only a short ride away, putting famous sights like the Rijksmuseum, Anne Frank House and tulip-lined neighborhoods within easy reach. Prefer to stay local? blocks.heading: Things to do in Amsterdam
blocks.text: Amsterdam’s allure lives in its details — narrow canals lined with tall houses, the quiet spin of a bike wheel and the scent of fresh waffles from a street stall. You can start by admiring art at a world-class museum and finish on the water, cruising past bridges lit at dusk. Wherever Amsterdam takes you, the city always feels both lively and easygoing.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Amsterdam
blocks.text: Storybook towns and windmill-dotted countrysides await you on your Amsterdam excursions with Princess. These activities let you see how Dutch history and daily life come together. Every stop offers something different — art, tradition or a taste of local flavor — all within easy reach of your luxury cruise ship.

blocks.heading: Marken & Volendam Dairy Farm
blocks.text: Wooden houses painted green and white line Marken’s harbor, their shutters open to the sea breeze. In nearby Volendam, fishing boats sway against the pier and the smell of fresh cheese drifts from open doors. A stop at a dairy farm rounds out the day with a few quiet moments of country life. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Delft Factory & The Hague
blocks.text: In Delft, artisans still hand paint blue-and-white porcelain the same way they have for centuries. Watch a piece come to life at the Porceleyne Fles factory, then take a walk along Delft’s quiet canals lined with gabled houses. On the way back, drive through The Hague and pass landmarks like the Peace Palace and Parliament buildings. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Discover Utrecht & Visit of Castle De Haar
blocks.text: Utrecht feels timeless, with old stone bridges crossing narrow canals and the tall spire of the Dom Tower visible from nearly everywhere. After exploring the city’s medieval streets, head to De Haar Castle, complete with drawbridges and towers rising from a surrounding moat. Inside, the furnished rooms and gardens hint will transport you to life in another era. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The First Reclaimed Land
blocks.text: See how the Dutch turned water into land. Begin at a centuries-old windmill still standing over fields once covered by the sea, then visit Broek in Waterland to walk among wooden homes and quiet waterways. The journey ends at Beemster Polder, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that shows how engineering and ingenuity shaped the Netherlands. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Windmills & Edam
blocks.text: Zaanse Schans smells faintly of sawdust and baked bread, its working windmills still creaking above the river. A little farther on, Edam’s streets are calm and flower-lined, with baskets of cheese hanging outside shop doors. There’s no rush here — just a pleasant glimpse of village life at an easy pace. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: A Walk Through Harlem & Tasting
blocks.text: In Haarlem, stone lanes lead to a market square filled with tulips and chatter. Around the corner, the Jopenkerk brewery hums softly inside a former church, sunlight glinting through stained glass. A taste of craft beer and warm hospitality make this visit feel more like meeting friends than sightseeing. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Amsterdam port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Ships dock close to the city center and give guests easy access to Amsterdam’s historic canals and lively neighborhoods. From the terminal, it’s a short walk or tram ride to top attractions, cafés and museums that line the waterfront. Many itineraries featuring Amsterdam are part of Europe cruises and Scandinavia & Baltic voyages, making this port an ideal starting or ending point for your journey

blocks.heading: Things to do in Athens
blocks.text: How'd you like to use a time machine to explore the birth of western civilization? That's essentially what a cruise to Athens (via Piraeus) is: A leap backwards in time to temples, theaters and agoras that still shape how we live today. From ancient ruins to bustling tavernas, this is a city that makes history feel alive, immediate and impossible to ignore.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Athens
blocks.text: Call it a city if you want, but Athens plays more like a stage where ancient legends and modern life share the spotlight. When you make port in Piraeus, Princess excursions deliver you to Athens and then take you behind the curtain, giving you the best seats in the house for this ongoing performance.

blocks.heading: City Drive, Acropolis Museum & Folkloric Show
blocks.text: See the artifacts of daily life at the Acropolis Museum, explore the historic Plaka and tour the city’s grand boulevards. Then, dive into an afternoon of Greek culture with a folkloric show, culinary demonstrations and a feast that invites you to join the fun, Zorba-style. Be warned: some plate smashing may occur. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Athens by Private Vehicle – Car Class Full Day (With Guide)
blocks.text: Take the reins of your own adventure with a private car, driver and guide at your service. Go where you want, linger as long as you like and skip what doesn’t interest you. This is Athens, unscripted — history on your terms, coffee stops included. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Athens
blocks.text: When time is short, go straight for the hits. See the Acropolis, the Parthenon and the Olympic Stadium, then recharge with a buffet lunch and Greek pastries. Cap it all off with time to roam the Plaka’s lively lanes of shops and cafés. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Acropolis, Ancient Corinth & Canal
blocks.text: Step back into ancient Greece at the Acropolis before heading out to Corinth, once one of the richest cities of the classical world. You’ll explore temples, mosaics and even stop for a photo at the Corinth Canal, a 19th-century feat of engineering. History, ruins and scenery — this one checks all the boxes. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Acropolis & Rock N’ Roll for Families
blocks.text: Bring the kids and channel your inner Indiana Jones. Explore the Acropolis with a guide who makes mythology come alive, then pause for lunch at the Hard Rock Café. With ancient ruins, Olympic Stadium photo stops and a lively family-friendly vibe, this tour balances history with fun (and fries). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ultimate Athens
blocks.text: Think of this as Athens turned up to eleven. You’ll marvel at the Acropolis and Parthenon, then step into the dazzling New Acropolis Museum. Lunch includes wine and traditional delicacies, and your afternoon stroll through the Plaka is the perfect mix of history and shopping. A grand finale? The original Olympic Stadium. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Acropolis, Plaka & Temple of Poseidon
blocks.text: Explore Athens’ ancient wonders, then trade the city streets for coastal views. After climbing to the Acropolis and wandering the Plaka, you’ll drive down the scenic Attic coast to Cape Sounion. There, the Temple of Poseidon rises above the Aegean Sea — a marble tribute to the god who ruled the waves. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: A Taste of Athens
blocks.text: What’s better than seeing the Parthenon? Pairing it with a glass of local wine. After a tour of the Acropolis and a city drive past iconic landmarks, you’ll stop at a traditional taverna for a wine tasting with cheese pairings. Ancient stones and modern sips — a pairing as timeless as it gets. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Athens
blocks.text: When you visit Athens on your Mediterranean or European cruise, our ship docks in Piraeus (a port city that’s been Athens’ gateway for over 2,000 years). From here, it’s a quick ride into the capital where history towers above the skyline and modern life buzzes at street level. blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Bar
blocks.text: Don’t stress over planning — experience the best Bar has to offer, stress-free, with Princess shore excursions. We’ll handle the details so you can relax and soak it all in.

blocks.heading: Wine Heritage of Montenegro
blocks.text: Taste your way through Montenegro’s wine heritage at Plantaze Winery, which produces over 95% of the country's wine. This winery’s cellar can hold 8 million gallons of wine, and the property also includes a rootstock nursery, a peach tree grove and a fish pond. You can wander rows of Krstac, Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc grapes and then sample wine in the tasting room 100 feet underground. LEARN

blocks.heading: The Capitals of Montenegro
blocks.text: Fun fact: The country of Montenegro technically has two capitals, and you can experience them both on this tour. Start by walking through the youngest capital in Europe—Podgorica, the judicial seat of the country—with winding streets. See the Sahat Kula clock tower that’s standing from the Ottoman Empire invasion in the 15th century. Finally, you’ll head to Cetinje, home to the president and the c

blocks.heading: Highlights of Budva and Stari Bar
blocks.text: Step into history by exploring Old Bar. Its 600-year-old walls and fortress may have collapsed, but many of the buildings inside have been around since medieval Bar. Your walking tour will take you to the Church of St. Katarina and the Church of St. Veneranda en route to the Turkish bath and mosque. After you have had your fill of Bar, you’ll go to Budva, a 2,500-year-old town packed full of Balka

blocks.heading: Traditional Montenegro: Old Bar & Ulcinj
blocks.text: Find yourself in ancient Montenegro in Stari Bar, a village that’s been around since the fifth century BC. It’s one of the oldest settlements on the Adriatic Coast! You’ll explore a historic Turkish bath and 600-year-old fortress walls. And then your tour will take you to Ulcinj, another ancient settlement on the coast, to learn all about the area’s history at the Archaeological Museum, Ethnologic

blocks.heading: Best of Montenegro
blocks.text: Experience one of Europe’s most beautiful cities, Kotor—a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In Kotor, you’ll wander through a maze of cobblestone streets, past simple buildings topped with sepia-toned roofs and lovely Romanesque churches. This tour will also take you to Perast, Montenegro's best-preserved Baroque city, to see the man-made islet Our Lady of the Rocks Isle. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Olive Oil Tasting & Old Bar
blocks.text: Olives first came to Montenegro 2,000 years ago, and olive oil production became a part of the culture by the 6th century. Head to Olio Monte refinery that spans 12,000 square meters and produces nearly 264 gallons of virgin and extra-virgin olive oil every year. You’ll walk the scenic olive groves and, of course, sample some of the zesty oils made right where you strolled. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Barcelona
blocks.text: This stunning Spanish city has a little something for everyone: 9 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, a towering cathedral that’s been under construction since 1882 and a world famous soccer club that draws sports fans from around the globe. Step into history in the Gothic Quarter or see the site of the 1992 Olympic Games when you cruise to Barcelona.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Barcelona
blocks.text: Vacations are all about relaxation — so leave the planning to us. Choose from our stress-free excursions that will show you the best of Barcelona, so you can experience the city without the hassle.

blocks.heading: Outside views of La Sagrada Familia & Park Guell
blocks.text: Enjoy a day of whimsy in Park Guell, an area of the city that showcases Gaudi's signature mosaics and quirky designs. See the famous serpentine bench and a mosaic dragon that guards the park. Finally, see the towering Basilica and stroll Passeig de Gracia. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Barcelona's Gothic Quarter Walking Tour
blocks.text: Experience where the city all started in the Gothic Quarter of Barcelona. Tour the Cathedral of Santa Eulalia, 600-year-old building covered with towering spires — and Plaza San Jaime that used to be a row of palaces that now house Catalonia's government. Finish off the day with La Rambla, a mile-long tree-lined pedestrian walk where you can shop until you drop. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Barcelona by Hop-on, Hop-off Bus
blocks.text: Get the best seat in the house on the hop-on, hop-off bus of Barcelona. This double decker bus will take you to all the best sites in the city, including Las Rambla and La Pedrera — the famous “stone quarry” Modernist building by Antoni Gaudi. You can get off the bus and explore any of the 20 stops and get back on to keep exploring. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Montserrat & Barcelona City Drive
blocks.text: If you’re looking for art, sports and shopping, this excursion is for you. See the Olympic Ring created for the 1992 games, the legendary Sagrada Familia Basilica and the world-famous Benedictine Monastery Complex called Monsterrat all in one day — and with time to shop the local stalls for handmade souvenirs. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: La Sagrada Familia & City Drive
blocks.text: You haven’t really seen Barcelona until you get up close to La Sagrada Familia. This cathedral has been under construction since 1882 and still isn’t finished! But that hasn’t stopped it from becoming one of the most iconic landmarks in the city. You’ll also see another one of Antoni Gaudi’s masterpieces, the house La Pedrera. Finish off the day with panoramic views of the city and harbor. LEARN M

blocks.heading: Gaudi's Barcelona
blocks.text: Calling all architecture lovers! If you want to see buildings you can only find in Barcelona, you’ll love this tour of the highlights of Antoni Gaudi’s work. See the Basilica, the well-known boulevard Passeig de Gràcia, Casa Batlló and Casa Mila with an expert guide who will teach you all about Modernism. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Barcelona
blocks.text: Barcelona is a city of eye-catching architecture, hundreds of years of history, mouthwatering food and breathtaking coastal views. Whether you want to see your favorite football club’s home base or eat your weight in tapas, you’ll love sailing to Barcelona on a European cruise.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Belfast
blocks.text: Belfast hustles between gritty history and modern swagger. It’s a city haunted by shipyards, politics, art and rebellion. Step ashore and expect to feel the pulse — your Belfast cruise isn’t just a stop, it’s an awakening.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Belfast
blocks.text: These are the ones that grab your boots and drag you into Northern Ireland’s marrow. Choose your beat.

blocks.heading: Londonderry
blocks.text: Drive west through moorland and forest, cross into Derry (Londonderry), walk its city walls, see the Guildhall and breathe in a place that’s been contested, celebrated and rebuilt. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Giant's Causeway & Antrim Coast
blocks.text: This is the Queen Mother of day trips: coastal drives, rope bridges, Dunluce Castle ruins and finally the basalt poetry of the Giant’s Causeway. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: St. Patrick Centre, Down Cathedral & Saul
blocks.text: Dive into the faith and legend: trace St. Patrick’s steps, see Down Cathedral and Saul Church, then cross Lough Strangford by ferry and explore Grey Abbey. Holy ground, human stories. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Sheepdogs & Stories
blocks.text: Drive into the countryside, meet the working dog crew on a sheep farm, push a flock where it needs to go, then snag lunch in a local pub with poetry on the walls. Real life, local style. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hop On Hop Off Belfast
blocks.text: City on your own terms. Hop on buses, hop off at murals, Titanic, pubs, gardens — 19 stops. Do it your way. (Yes, that means you can skip some of the stops, but we’re not sure why you’d want to). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Titanic Belfast® & City Drive
blocks.text: Tour the shipyard that built the Titanic, relive its launch and walk through a museum built like a hull. Then loop through the city — Queen’s, City Hall, Belfast’s heartbeat. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Belfast Highlights & Crumlin Road Gaol
blocks.text: Ride through city contrasts, see Peace Walls, murals and the gaol with its echoes. Spend time in cells and corridors and realize that history isn’t dead — it’s downright haunting. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Game of Thrones Studio Tour
blocks.text: Call this your fantasy break: drive through Belfast, land in Banbridge at Linen Mill Studios and walk through replica sets of Westeros. Dragons are strictly bring-your-own, but awe is guaranteed. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Belfast port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Most Belfast cruises dock in Belfast Harbour at D1, Stormont Dock or Pollock Dock. The new dedicated cruise terminal sits along Victoria Channel, offering deepwater access and a sleek visitor center. From there, it’s about two miles to the city center — not walkable under your own steam unless you’re really, really bold. blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Bergen
blocks.text: Pick an excursion that fits your mood. Whether you’re after mountain panoramas, city history or fjord serenity, these tours give you the full-throttle Bergen experience.

blocks.heading: Easy Mt. Fløien Funicular & City Drive
blocks.text: Put the ‘fun’ in ‘funicular’ as you ride to Mt. Fløien for sweeping views of Bergen’s harbour, islands and sea. Spend time at the summit restaurant and gift shop then board a motorcoach for a narrated drive through historic sites such as King Haakon’s Hall, Rosenkrantz Tower and the waterfront workhorse Bryggen. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Bergen Highlights & Cable Car
blocks.text: Drive through the city’s core where the Fish Market, Griffon Hall and old Hanseatic buildings line the way, then board the cable car to Mount Ulriken at 2,109 feet above sea level. Up there, enjoy panoramic fjord and island views (and maybe some vertigo if that’s your thing) while sipping coffee and cake in the summit restaurant. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Mt. Fløien Funicular & Hike
blocks.text: Start with the Fløibanen funicular up to 1,000 feet and then hike along wooded trails to Skomakerdiket lake, continue to Rundemanen peak at about 1,800 feet, breathe in the view across the fjord and islands then loop back down through terrain that tests your boots, your lungs and your sense of wonder. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Highlights of Bergen
blocks.text: Walk through Bryggen, the old waterfront with its signature wooden houses, tour Schøtstuene, the medieval merchant hall, visit the Old Bergen open‑air museum with its 18th‑ and 19th‑century wooden houses and historic atmosphere before heading back to port with a heart full of heritage. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Fjords and Waterfall
blocks.text: Hardangerfjord region by coach through Kvamskogen cabins, stop at Steinsdalsfossen waterfall that you can walk behind, continue to Norheimsund’s harbourfront for free time and then cruise along the Hardangerfjord with mountains photographed, glaciers glimpsed and small village stops thoroughly visited before returning to Bergen. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: A Walk Through Bergen and Ice Bar
blocks.text: Begin with a guided walk among Bryggen’s historic waterfront and the market’s lively stalls, then make your way to an Ice Bar Arctic‑style, suit up for your welcome drink served in an ice glass (as in a glass made of gosh-darn-for-real ice) while viewing Norwegian artistry. LEARN MORE

Panoramic Bilbao and Gorka Izagirre Winery
Explore itineraries with cruises to Bilbao
Discover Bilbao on your next cruise

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Bilbao
blocks.text: Choose your path: slow city stroll, cliffside panorama, wine‑with‑history mash‑up. Bilbao has it all, and a Princess excursion is the best way to experience it.

blocks.heading: Bermeo, Bizcaia Coast & City Drive
blocks.text: As a tour that moves from city spark to sea spray, this one checks every box. Start with a drive past Bilbao’s boldest buildings — including a close-up stop at the Guggenheim — before veering off to the Biscayan coast. In Bermeo, you’ll explore winding streets and harbour views, then sit down to a Basque-style lunch with wine and regional specialties. It’s culture, cuisine and coastline; you’ll be

blocks.heading: Easy Bilbao
blocks.text: Sit back in the coach and let the old mining and ship‑yard lines of Bilbao pass you by as you trace the estuary and cruise down the Gran Vía. Snap a photo of the museum from afar before stepping into the Old Quarter where history keeps a pintxo in one hand and a beer in the other. Minimal walking, maximum ‘I’m loving this’ moments. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Bilbao Old Quarter Walk
blocks.text: This one’s all in the footwork: gothic cathedrals, tapas spots and streets that feel like open-air galleries. Your guide leads you through Bilbao’s Old Quarter, from postmodern curves to medieval corners — with wine, bites and boutique stops in between. It’s everything a walk should be. Come curious, leave charmed. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Bermeo, Guernica & the Cantabrian Coast
blocks.text: Outside Bilbao, the Basque coast gets wilder, steeper and more storied. You’ll start with a photo stop overlooking the rocky islet of San Juan de Gaztelugatxe, (a jaw-dropper long before Game of Thrones filmed here). In Bermeo, time slows down among stone streets, church bells and fishing boats. Then it’s on to Guernica, where a tree became a symbol of freedom, a town became a target and Picasso t

blocks.heading: Panoramic Bilbao and Gorka Izagirre Winery
blocks.text: Begin above the skyline at Mount Artxanda, where Bilbao stretches out like a city-sized sculpture garden. Then, swap concrete for vineyards as you wind into the countryside for a tour and tasting at Gorka Izagirre (a sleek, family-run winery where tradition meets tech). Expect crisp txakoli, bold reds and local cheeses that you won’t have any problem spoiling your appetite for. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of San Sebastian & Hondarribia
blocks.text: Two towns, two vibes: Hondarribia gives you medieval walls and old-world calm; San Sebastian hits you with surf, skyline and the kind of food scene that rewrites your standards. You’ll walk, taste, wander and wonder why anyone would ever consider skipping this delightful destination. LEARN MORE

pages.metaDescription: Cruise to Bordeaux, France, in luxury with Princess. Award-winning Europe cruises with exceptional service. Book your 2026–2027 voyage today.

headings.text: Shore excursions to explore in Bordeaux
Bordeaux on Your Own & Cité du Vin
Explore itineraries with cruises to Bordeaux

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Bordeaux
blocks.text: Choose your pace and palate: city chic, vineyard indulgence or coastal history. Each tour brings the magic of this region to life.

blocks.heading: Highlights & Bordeaux on Your Own
blocks.text: Perfect for the independently curious. This tour kicks off with a scenic drive along the vineyard-studded Route des Châteaux and a short guided intro to Bordeaux. Then you're off on your own — shop the elegant boutiques, wander medieval alleyways or just lounge at a café with a glass of Bordeaux’s best. Regroup with your coach for a relaxing ride back. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Bordeaux on Your Own & Cité du Vin
blocks.text: This one’s for the wanderers and wine nerds. After a scenic two-hour drive past vineyards and estuary views, you’ll arrive in Bordeaux with a few hours to roam on your own. Explore leafy squares, art galleries and historic cathedrals, or hit the shops on Rue Sainte-Catherine. Cap it off at Cité du Vin, the striking, twisty wine museum where you’ll sip Bordeaux at the top-floor bar overlooking the

blocks.heading: Germany’s Atlantic Wall
blocks.text: It’s seaside charm meets chilling history. In Soulac-sur-Mer, you’ll visit WWII-era bunkers that were once part of Hitler’s Atlantic Wall defense system. A local guide brings the story to life as you step into these concrete relics and walk along dunes that saw decades of silence before restoration efforts began. You’ll leave with a very different perspective on France’s Atlantic coast. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hennessy Distillery
blocks.text: A full-day journey through French refinement (and a little seafaring flair). Travel by coach, ferry and riverboat to reach the famed Hennessy Distillery in Cognac — because why arrive to a tasting on foot when you could arrive by boat? Tour the cellars, learn the secrets of eaux-de-vie blending and enjoy a guided tasting. A leisurely lunch at a local restaurant rounds out the day. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Medoc Château & Wine Tasting
blocks.text: This is the half-day escape wine lovers dream of. Drive through the storied Route des Châteaux, where elegant estates peek from the vines like something out of a period drama. Tour a fairytale château, sip its finest reds and whites and take in the terroir that’s made Bordeaux wines world-famous. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Bordeaux
blocks.text: Get your fix of vineyards and city charm in one seamless day. Start with a tasting at a classic Médoc estate, where centuries of winemaking unfold in every sip. Then it’s on to Bordeaux, a neoclassical gem packed with riverside boulevards, towering spires and wide, sun-drenched squares. Enjoy a French brasserie lunch and soak up the easy elegance of this UNESCO-listed city. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Bornholm
blocks.text: Bornholm’s history and landscape come to life on shore excursions that highlight its coastal villages, medieval landmarks and long-standing artisan traditions.

blocks.heading: A Walk Through Ronne
blocks.text: Explore Bornholm’s capital on a guided walking tour that leads through centuries of local history. Your route passes half-timbered houses, “bomb-houses” rebuilt after 1945 and cobblestone alleys that reveal Rønne’s past as a busy Baltic port. Visit a local museum to see artifacts from the island’s long timeline, then return to the waterfront with new insight into this distinctive town. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Svaneke On Your Own
blocks.text: Spend a relaxed morning in Svaneke, one of Bornholm’s most alluring towns and a showcase of perfectly preserved 16th- and 17th-century streets. You’ll have three hours to explore at your own pace, visiting confectionaries known for handmade treats, sampling brews at the local brewhouse or browsing artisan galleries and studios. Historic trading posts and timbered houses add to the town’s distincti

blocks.heading: The Best of Bornholm
blocks.text: Discover Bornholm’s signature sights on a scenic circuit around the island. Explore Hammershus Fortress, northern Europe’s largest castle ruin, then continue to Baltic Sea Glass to watch skilled glassblowers at work. You can enjoy some free time in the fishing village of Gudhjem before finishing with a photo stop at one of the island’s medieval round churches. The return trip passes through the ex

blocks.heading: A Cultural Adventure Through Bornholm
blocks.text: Experience Bornholm’s growing food and spirits scene on a half-day journey through the island’s countryside. Visit Høstet, an organic sea buckthorn farm where you’ll meet the owners and taste their bright, citrusy products. Back in Rønne, stop at Bornholm Distillery to sample small-batch gin infused with local botanicals. End the tour with time to explore the nearby Market Hall for regional specia

blocks.heading: Medieval Bornholm
blocks.text: Step into the island’s medieval past with visits to Hammershus Ruins and the Bornholm Medieval Center. Learn how power shifted between monarchs and the Church as you explore fortifications, replica buildings and interactive exhibits populated by costumed volunteers. The tour concludes at Østerlars, Bornholm’s largest round church, whose thick walls and unique architecture served both religious and

blocks.heading: Easy Bornholm, Svaneke & Fishing Village
blocks.text: Travel through rolling countryside to Gudhjem, a fishing village famous for its smoked herring and brightly painted houses. Enjoy time on your own to try local specialties or browse galleries before continuing along the coast to Svaneke. Here you can explore sweet shops, artisan studios and historic merchant homes. The route back winds through the green expanse of Almindingen Forest. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Catania
blocks.text: You’ll discover a mix of volcanic intensity, ancient ruins and vibrant Sicilian culture that keeps even seasoned travellers on their toes. From the lava‑strewn slopes of Mount Etna (Europe's tallest active volcano) to the baroque splendour of Catania’s rebuilt historic centre, you’ll find big history and bold flavor in equal measure.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Catania
blocks.text: Unravel Sicily’s epic past and sun-drenched present with excursions that dive into hilltop hamlets, lava-carved landscapes and cinematic secrets. You pick the adventure; Princess handles the details.

blocks.heading: Easy Catania and Coastline
blocks.text: For lighter walking and greater impact, this 3.5‑hour excursion begins in Catania’s core. It then winds along the lava‑coast to the village of Aci Castello and its rugged Norman‑era castle perched on volcanic rock. This is the perfect option if you want maximum Sicilian scenery with minimal strain. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Castelmola and Taormina
blocks.text: You’ll begin with a walking tour of Taormina, taking in the 3rd‑century‑B.C. theatre carved into the hillside, then preview sweeping views of the sea and Mt. Etna. After time for shopping on Corso Umberto you head to the hamlet of Castelmola for lunch and narrow‑street charm. End the day by reboarding your coach for the drive back to the ship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Piazza Armerina & Villa del Casale
blocks.text: A full‑day excursion to Piazza Armerina takes you to the Villa del Casale, a Roman luxury complex with one of the finest surviving mosaic floors in the world. You’ll wander through dozens of rooms where ancient floors depict chariot races, mythic beasts and the famed ‘Bikini Girls.’ After a relaxing lunch you return to Catania, your mind filled with Roman opulence and Sicilian sunlight. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Godfather on Location
blocks.text: This particularly cinematic tour visits the town of Savoca and other filming sites from the famed ‘Godfather’ film series. Walk where Michael and Apollonia met, explore the village scenes locations and feel the film’s world of small‑town Sicily. It’s an offer you can’t (or at least won’t want to) refuse. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Silvestri Craters & Sicilian Wine
blocks.text: Rise high on Mt. Etna to the Silvestri Craters at 6,233 feet. See the lava‑formed landscape that erupted in 1892, and then travel to the San Michele Estate winery. There you’ll taste wines grown in volcanic soil and pair them with regional treats in one of Sicily’s best kept secrets. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Taormina Walking Tour
blocks.text: This half‑day tour gives you all the time you’ll need to really experience Taormina. Ride up via lift to the town gates and amble past medieval mansions, flower‑decked balconies and the famous Greco‑Roman theatre (complete with panoramic coastline views). After a relaxed visit you’ll return to Catania ready for your next adventure. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Catania
blocks.text: When your ship docks in Catania, you’re stepping into a port where gritty industrial edges meet boundless Sicilian character. Just minutes from the pier, you’ll find baroque facades, loud open‑air markets and cafes that fuel your day with espresso and arancini. blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Chania
blocks.text: Pick a path and roll with it; each of these popular shore excursions offers local flavour, cultural depth or spectacular scenery with easy shore access (Chania is an island, after all). Across this vibrant and diverse landscape, you’ll encounter breathtaking rivers and lakes, hidden waterfalls and coastal caves, along with powdery pink and red sand beaches set beneath dramatic cliffs and mountain

blocks.heading: Cretan Wine Tasting & Agreco Farm
blocks.text: Kick things off in Rethymno’s Old Town, where centuries-old charm pairs perfectly with a five-glass flight of Greek wine. Then head to Agreco Farm for a peek at olive presses, water mills, wood ovens and the kind of raki-soaked snack that makes you wonder why you ever left lunch to amateurs. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Beach Break at Agia Marin
blocks.text: Just 30 minutes from the pier you’ll hit Agia Marin Beach for three hours of sunbed comfort and umbrella‑shade refuge. When the sea calls, dive in for water skiing, windsurfing or floating tubes. When hunger strikes, a seaside restaurant serves up Cretan dishes amid the sand and surf. Return to port refreshed and still on schedule. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Rethymnon Town & Arkadi Monastery
blocks.text: Drive along winding roads to the golden‑facade Monastery of Arkadi built in 1587 — a symbol of Cretan resistance enhanced by sweeping mountain views. Then wander medieval Rethymnon’s harbour town, alleyways and cafés for free time before cruising back to your ship. History, architecture and free time all wrapped in one. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Chania and Botanical Gardens
blocks.text: Begin with a guided walk through Chania’s old town around its Venetian harbour and market stalls selling local honey and herbs. Then transfer to the Botanical Gardens of Crete where you’ll walk among Mediterranean flora, learn how traditional dishes are crafted and sample local wines. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: 4 × 4 Adventure
blocks.text: This isn’t your beachfront lounge —it’s countryside grit. Hop into 4×4 vehicles to tackle stony trails, olive‑groves, hidden villages and the rugged landscapes of Crete. A stop at village Hiliomoudou beneath the White Mountains yields fresh traditional cuisine and real off‑beat scenery before the route loops you back to the harbour. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Sea Kayaking Adventure, Swim & Lunch for Families
blocks.text: Perfect for active guests and families: you’ll launch from Chania’s Venetian harbour in two‑person sea kayaks toward Marathi and Kastelli Hill, paddle along the Aegean, swim in inviting water and finish with a beachfront lunch. Gear, safety instructions and a full outdoor dose of Crete included. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Corfu
blocks.text: Corfu rises from the Ionian Sea like a story in full color: palms, stone walls, seaside taverns and so much more. The Old Town’s alleys, palaces and fortresses hold layers of Venetian, French and British culture. Everywhere you wander, the island’s blend of charm, history and Mediterranean warmth invites you to linger a little longer.

blocks.heading: Corfu shore excursions to explore in Greece
blocks.text: These routes take you off the beaten quay — deeper into olive groves, hidden chapels, sea islands and lasting memories. CEach one is a choose-your-own-adventure into the soul of Corfu.

blocks.heading: Paleokastritsa, Monastery & Beach Getaway
blocks.text: Step into Corfu’s rugged west — drive past the New Fortress and coastline lanes to Paleokastritsa. Tour the Monastery of Virgin Mary perched above coves. Then descend to Glyfada Beach for swimming, sun time or watercraft fun. Cafés lie steps away. Wrap up with a coastal ride back to port, savory salt air all around you. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Corfu
blocks.text: You’ll begin with Achilleion’s gardens, statues and mythic air, then drive to Paleokastritsa for sea‑lined cliffs and olive groves. Next stop: Mouse Island via boat — a tiny isle with dreamy views. Lunch follows, then you head into Corfu Town, wander the Old Fortress, visit St. Spyridon Church, soak up cobbled squares and sea breeze. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Achilleion Palace, St. Spyridon Church & Corfu Town
blocks.text: Start your drive to Achilleion Palace and walk its gardens — the statues, blooms and sea-framed vistas demand attention. Return toward Corfu Town, passing the Old Fortress. In town, your guide leads you past the Palace of St. Michael & St. George, through narrow streets and plazas and finally to St. Spyridon Church for more bell towers and history than you’ll be able to process. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Fun at the Waterpark
blocks.text: Need a break from stone walls and hot sun? This excursion takes you to Aqualand, a sprawling waterpark surrounded by green hills. Slides, lazy rivers, pools and shaded lounge spots let you recharge. Ideal for kids, families or anyone who wants to trade heat and walking for splash and thrill for a few hours. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Catamaran Coastal Cruise & Swim
blocks.text: Board a sleek catamaran at Gouvia and glide past Corfu’s cliffs and fortress walls. Swim or snorkel over reefs near Mouse Island. Drop anchor in a serene bay below Mon Repos. Drift toward Vidos for wildlife, beaches and chill. All the while the Ionian sun works its magic — sea, motion, salt and lots of serenity. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kickin’ Corfu! A 4‑Wheel‑Drive Adventure
blocks.text: Climb into a rugged 4×4 and head away from the coast into olive groves, hills, fragrant forests and narrow mountain roads. Scale Mount Pantokrator with its 27 hairpin turns. Pause in Njegusi village for meze and mountain views. Then roam rustic villages, dip toward Paleokastritsa’s coast and return to port with exhilaration still pumping through your veins. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: City Drive, Old Town & Wine Tasting
blocks.text: Drive past the Old Fortress, then enter Corfu Town with its narrow alleys and colonial facades. Your guide leads you to St. Spyridon Church, then onward to a local winery (Ambelonas or Theotokis). Taste wines, learn regional flavors, stroll Old Town’s squares, markets and cafés. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Achilleion Palace & Garouna
blocks.text: Begin at Achilleion Palace, walk its gardens and soak in mythology. Then climb into Garouna’s hills, visit a traditional olive‑mill museum, watch carpet‑weaving demonstrations and sip local wine and cheese in a taverna. The drive winds through forested slopes and valleys, ending in calm light, sea views and your return to port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Corfu port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Your ship pulls up and Corfu hands you its heart. Cobbled alleys catch the light, citrus trees shake overhead and the Old Fortress waits with that look it always gives first-timers (think stern grandpa). If your European or Mediterranean cruise stops here, consider it a challenge. This isn’t just another scenic stop. It’s a maze, a memory and maybe your new favorite adventure.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Cornwall
blocks.text: Cornwall is what happens when England gets bored of being polite and starts channeling ancient bards, rogue smugglers and rock-obsessed painters. This isn’t some dainty countryside. It’s jagged coastlines, pagan legends and local cream that starts actual fights. Falmouth? That’s just the first step along the path.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Cornwall
blocks.text: When you book a Cornwall cruise, the real work is choosing which scenic overload you’ll tackle first. Here are your stories, not stops:

blocks.heading: Lanhydrock House & Fowey
blocks.text: Live out your Victorian drama fantasies at Lanhydrock (corset not included), then chill in Fowey — a town so quaint it practically writes its own cozy murder mystery series. The harbor views slap, and the Cornish pastries are worth the crumbs on your shirt. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Land's End Peninsula Complex & St. Ives
blocks.text: Rugged cliffs, that iconic Land’s End sign and an amusement park (yes, really) mark the start. Then it’s off to St. Ives — part artist haven, part surf town, part “I wasn’t planning to buy a handmade ceramic owl, but now I own two.” You’ll have time to explore, eat and rethink your life choices in the best way. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: St. Michael's Mount
blocks.text: Only accessible by foot when the tide’s low (or boat if that’s how you want to play it), this rocky island is basically Cornwall’s flex. Creep up to the castle like a medieval intruder, tour its echoing halls and wonder why your local library doesn’t look this cool. The views? Weaponized scenery. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Lizard Peninsula Walk & Pub Lunch
blocks.text: Your boots hit the path, the Atlantic roars back. This cliffside walk pulls no punches — wildflowers, lighthouses, salt-smeared skies. Then a proper pub lunch because you’ve earned it, you magnificent beast. Bonus: serpentine rock shops that sound fake but are extremely real. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Countryside Drive & Cornish Cream Tea
blocks.text: Let’s get scandalous: the Cornish put cream before jam, and they’ll fight you on it. This slow-roll countryside drive ends in Marazion, where tea is hot, scones are fluffy and St. Michael’s Mount looms just far enough away to keep the mystery alive. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Polperro On Your Own
blocks.text: Think smuggling but make it charming. Polperro is a fishing village where the streets are too narrow for cars and just wide enough for your curiosity. Poke into alleys, chase down the perfect pasty and don’t ask what kind of criminal dealings used to happen in those basements… LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Land’s End Peninsula Complex & Scenic Drive
blocks.text: Paragraph write-up Fewer shops, more sea spray. This version skips St. Ives and lets you get cozy with the edge of the world. The cliffs don’t care how philosophical you get, but you’ll definitely leave changed. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Falmouth port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Hoping Falmouth will roll out a red carpet? It’s got something better: a fog bank, a blast of sea wind and a harbor full of boats with personality. Once ashore, it’s all steep hills, stone walls and pubs that laugh in the face of your schedule. This is where Transatlantic voyages, European adventures and round-Britain cruises come to get their salt.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Crete (Heraklion)
blocks.text: When you step off the gangway onto the Island of Crete, you step into a place where the Minoans, Venetians and Byzantines have all left their mark. As the fabled homeland of Zeus himself, Crete’s blue‑sea vistas and hillside windmills are a match for the gods themselves. The port city of Heraklion invites you to dive into ancient palaces, volcanic slopes, craft villages and seaside retreats, and P

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Crete
blocks.text: Crete’s excursions let you dive into Bronze Age ruins, sail past island fortresses and sip wines grown in volcanic soil. Whether you’re tracing legends at Knossos or watching master potters shape clay by hand, each Princess-curated outing adds a vivid layer to your cruise.

blocks.heading: Knossos in 3D
blocks.text: Take a full‑day tour to the heart of Minoan civilization with a walk through Knossos’s palatial ruins enhanced by an augmented‑reality experience that allows you to use your smartphone or tablet to view virtual recreations of famous archaeological sites. Then pause in Heraklion for free time among shops and cafés before the comfortable ride back to the port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Crete
blocks.text: Begin at the Minoan Palace of Knossos exploring the labyrinthine layout, vivid frescoes and throne room ruins that once symbolized power on Crete. Then travel to Aghios Nikolaos for some souvenir shopping before heading to Elounda and the haunting silhouette of Spinalonga Island. Lunch follows, then a sightseeing tour through Heraklion’s Old Town, where bustling squares, lively tavernas and open-a

blocks.heading: Easy Crete & Heraklion Archaeological Museum
blocks.text: Start in Thrapsano Village, where potters work clay the way their ancestors did (and maybe try your hand at the wheel yourself). Then return to Heraklion to visit the museum’s libraries of Minoan artifacts like the Phaistos Disc and the Bull‑Leaping fresco. Finish with a walk through Heraklion’s main square before heading back. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Knossos & Boutari Winery
blocks.text: Dive into history at Knossos Palace, then traverse to the Boutari Winery where Volcanic‑soiled vineyards produce striking wines. Tour the cellar, enjoy a tasting paired with local snacks and take in how nature, tradition and craft blend seamlessly on this fabled island. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Spinalonga Island Adventure & Elounda Resort
blocks.text: Ride via motorcoach to Elounda and then boat over to Spinalonga Island, famous for its Venetian fortress and more recent history as a leper colony. After exploring tunnels and towers, return to Elounda for free time to stroll, relax or linger by the marina. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Crete & Cretaquarium For Families
blocks.text: Perfect for younger guests or anyone young at heart: visit Knossos Palace with its myths and murals then head to Cretaquarium where over 2,000 marine creatures showcase Mediterranean marine life. After lunch, drive through Heraklion to return to the ship a little more aware of the ecological world that surrounds you. LEARN MORE

blocks.text: When your ship docks in Heraklion as part of your Mediterranean or European cruise itinerary, you’re ideally positioned for a deep dive into both island history and seascape. blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Dublin
blocks.text: Ready to dive into Dublin’s energy and charm? Here’s where the rubber hits the cobblestones. Grab your coat (hey, you didn’t come to Ireland to get a tan, did you?) and let’s go!

blocks.heading: Glendalough and the Monastic Ruins
blocks.text: These ruins have seen more centuries than your whole family tree. Travel through Wicklow to Glendalough, where the lakes are quiet and the history hits heavy. It’s the kind of place that makes you want to sit in respectful silence without really knowing why. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Dublin Coast & Irish Traditions
blocks.text: Cruise along Dublin’s jagged coastline before landing at the fairytale-worthy Malahide Castle. Tour the towers, hit Howth for sea views and settle in for a traditional lunch with live Irish music at the Abbey Tavern. Yes, that means jigs. No, you’re not allowed to sit quietly in the corner. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Town & Country
blocks.text: City grit meets countryside calm. Peek into Christchurch Cathedral, then hit the road to Wicklow, aka Ireland’s botanical flex. Browse woolens, eat like a local and get lost (metaphorically) in Glendalough’s ancient monastic ruins. You’ll leave with grass on your boots and old stories in your head. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Scone Baking Demo at Ballyknocken House
blocks.text: Scones so fresh they practically flirt with you. Step inside Ballyknocken House and watch the pros do their thing — then eat the results. There’s tea, jam, herb gardens and Victorian vibes. Feels less like a tour, more like crashing a countryside kitchen party. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: A Taste of Ireland: Whiskey in the Jar
blocks.text: History goes down smoother with a splash of whiskey. Tour Jameson’s home turf, learn how it’s made, then sip like someone who knows what ‘triple distilled’ means. This is where local culture meets straight-up swagger. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Horseback Riding in the Garden of Ireland
blocks.text: You, a horse and the Irish countryside — what could go wrong? (Very little, actually, they cover the basics first.) Ride through serene estates and wild fields beneath Little Sugar Loaf Mountain. It’s cinematic. It’s peaceful. It’s probably the only time you’ll have to worry about whether your ear-to-ear grin is going to dislodge your helmet. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Powerscourt Estate & Waterfall
blocks.text: Come for the waterfall, stay for the smug satisfaction of out-photoing your friends. Powerscourt is what happens when nature hires a landscape architect. Hike the trails, stroll the gardens and soak up the kind of scenery that turns casual guests into wannabe druids. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hop On Hop Off Dublin with Transfer from Dun Laoghaire
blocks.text: Get dropped in the center of Dublin and take ta seat on a Dublin bus tour. This massive double-decker lets you hop between museums, pubs, parks and all the bits in between. You’ll feel like a local — just maybe a little more photo happy. LEARN MORE

Speedboat Adventure, Snorkel & Beach: A Small Group Tour

blocks.heading: Dubrovnik shore excursions to explore Croatia
blocks.text: You can stroll the marble or scale the ramparts, sail the coastline or slip into nearby Cavtat. Pick your lane and let the city take you for an adventure.

blocks.heading: Spectacular Evening in Dubrovnik
blocks.text: Enter Old Town at golden hour, toast the city with a pre-dinner cocktail, then thread past Sponza, the Rector’s Palace and Onofrio’s Fountain. Sit down at Azur for a dinner that earns its name, then walk the lamplit Stradun back to Pile Gate. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Dubrovnik & Cavtat
blocks.text: Walk the Old Town with a guide who moves you smartly from Pile Gate to the Franciscan Monastery, past the Old Pharmacy, then through the Rector’s Palace and the Cathedral’s glittering treasury. After free time, head to Cavtat for lunch and seaside ambiance before the ride back along the coast. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Coastline Cruise and St. Jacob Beach Escape
blocks.text: Glide along the walls on a relaxed boat tour, circling forts and Lokrum’s green shoreline. Land at St. Jacob beach, claim your lounger and dip into glass-clear water with the Old Town set like a stage across the bay. Sail back with salt in your hair and time to explore. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cavtat & Folkloric Show
blocks.text: Start with a lookout over Dubrovnik that will hijack your camera roll, then roll south to Cavtat for a pretty harbor break. Return via Konavle for a lively folklore performance inside the Old Town and finish with an easy stroll to Pile Gate for your pickup. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Dubrovnik Highlights by Tuk-Tuk
blocks.text: Trade a bus for an electric tuk-tuk (a sort of three-wheeled, motorized rickshaw) and climb to the bridge viewpoint and Srđ Hill for widescreen city shots. Get dropped at Pile Square and walk Stradun to Onofrio’s Fountain at your own pace. Shuttle back when you’re done collecting smug photos. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Scenic Road Train & Wine Tasting
blocks.text: Leave the walls for Konavle’s vineyards. Sip local varietals in family cellars, ride a charming mini-train between rows of vines, see the old mill in Ljuta and tuck into a hearty field lunch. Rustic, tasty and very easy to brag about later. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Game of Thrones Tour
blocks.text: Trace ‘King’s Landing’ through the real city: Pile, the walls, Lovrijenac as the Red Keep and sweeping views of ‘Blackwater Bay.’ Then continue to Trsteno Arboretum, the show’s palace gardens. It’s TV lore layered on centuries of Dubrovnik history. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Speedboat Adventure, Snorkel & Beach: A Small Group Tour
blocks.text: Open the throttle to Koločep’s Blue Cave, mask up and swim through sapphire light. Add a hop to Lopud’s Šunj beach, then back to Koločep for another swim before a smooth run across Zaton Bay. Sun, snorkel, soft sand and just the right amount of adrenaline. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Edinburgh, Floors Castle & Dryburgh Abbey
blocks.text: Head into the Borders for sweeping views and deep history. Visit the ruins of 12th-century Dryburgh Abbey, then explore Floors Castle (still a family residence today). A scenic drive back to Edinburgh completes the journey. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: South Queensferry by Private Vehicle - Car Class Half Day (With Guide)
blocks.text: Hire your own private car and guide for half a day in Edinburgh. The flexibility lets you decide where to go and how long to linger, whether it’s castles, shopping or just exploring. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Edinburgh
blocks.text: Spend the day at the city’s biggest landmarks: the formidable Edinburgh Castle, bustling Princes Street and stately Holyrood Palace. Free time for shopping or exploring makes it a well-rounded day in the capital. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Whisky & Bagpipes with Local Expert
blocks.text: Sample three drams of Scottish whiskey before learning the basics of playing the bagpipes with Edinburgh’s own Louise Marshall, Piper to the Lord Provost. This hands-on cultural experience ends with time to do a little souvenir shopping. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Glamis Castle & St. Andrews
blocks.text: Tour Glamis Castle, famous for its antiques, ghost stories and connection to Shakespeare’s Macbeth. Then continue to St. Andrews, known both as the birthplace of golf and for its medieval university town charm. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Edinburgh On Your Own
blocks.text: Take a motorcoach into the city center and spend the day exploring at your own pace. Maps are provided, so you can decide between shopping, sightseeing or simply soaking up the atmosphere. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: St. Andrews - Home of Golf
blocks.text: Make a pilgrimage to the Royal & Ancient Golf Club and the storied Old Course, then explore St. Andrews’ cathedral, university and seaside streets. Independent time lets you take it in at your own pace. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Royal Mile Walking Tour
blocks.text: Walk with a guide along Edinburgh’s most famous street. Visit Holyrood Palace, hear stories of the city’s past and snap photos of the monuments, statues and cobblestone that make the Royal Mile unforgettable. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Elba
blocks.text: Shore excursions in Elba showcase the island’s best—from golden beaches and charming harbor towns to scenic drives through its rugged hills. Whether you prefer history, nature or time by the sea, there’s an excursion to match your pace.

blocks.heading: Hiking the slopes of Mt Capanne
blocks.text: Enjoy a scenic drive to Marciana, Elba’s oldest village, before beginning an invigorating hike along the wind-carved slopes of Mount Capanne. Take in diverse forests and sweeping views of the island’s northern coast as you make your way to the historic Church of San Cerbone. Continue downhill to Poggio, where a rustic local restaurant awaits with a well-earned light dinner and ocean views. LEARN M

blocks.heading: Napoleon's Summer residence & Porto Azzurro
blocks.text: Enjoy a scenic drive past Elba’s charming villages on your way to Villa San Martino, Napoleon Bonaparte’s summer residence during his exile. Explore the museum and its fascinating history before continuing to the quaint fishing village of Porto Azzurro, where you’ll have free time to shop, stroll the harbor or relax at a café. Conclude with beautiful views of Portoferraio Bay on your return. LEARN

blocks.heading: Elba Countryside & Wine tasting
blocks.text: Enjoy a half-day exploration of southern Elba, beginning with a scenic motorcoach ride from Portoferraio to the charming village of Capoliveri. Stroll its winding streets and browse local boutiques before heading to the 17th-century La Chiusa winery, set among vineyards and olive groves overlooking the sea. Tour the cellar and savor a tasting of Passiti wine paired with light snacks before returni

blocks.heading: A Walk Through Portoferraio
blocks.text: Walk in the footsteps of Napoleon on a guided tour through Portoferraio, a historic town built atop the ancient Roman village of Fabricia. From the port, wander the narrow streets of the old center, once called Cosmopoli, passing landmarks like Le Fortezze Medicee and the Church of the Nativity. blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Florence
blocks.text: Want to just sort of wander around Livorno? Don’t let us stop you. But if you’d rather get the absolute most out of your visit to Pisa, hop on one of these excursions to enter full Tuscan mode. Art, towers, pesto, wine — it’s all yours.

blocks.heading: Tuscan Countryside & Wine Tasting
blocks.text: This is Tuscany doing what Tuscany does best — medieval hilltop villages, fortified stone walls and wine that somehow tastes better just because you’re standing in a vineyard. Montecarlo di Lucca sets the scene, and a family-owned cellar does the pouring. Add some local bites, a walkable little town and countryside views that go full screensaver. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Florence, Pisa & Santa Croce Church
blocks.text: Start with Florence, where every corner is name-dropping a Renaissance legend. You’ll hit the Duomo, Giotto’s Bell Tower, the Baptistery (those are the Gates of Paradise) and Piazza della Signoria. Then it’s time for the Ponte Vecchio, Santa Croce Church (final resting place of Michelangelo, NBD) and some free time to strut around like you live there. Cap it off with a countryside cruise to Pisa f

blocks.heading: Florence, Statue of David & Uffizi Museum
blocks.text: This one’s for the art crowd. After rolling into Florence, you’ll check out Michelangelo’s David (hey, eyes up here) at the Accademia, gawk at the Duomo and Baptistery, swing past Piazza della Signoria and Ponte Vecchio, then lunch like a local. But the crown jewel? A deep dive into the Uffizi Gallery — a museum so stuffed with masterpieces you might get whiplash. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cinque Terre
blocks.text: The Cinque Terre is what happens when the Italian coastline decides to show off. This full-day trip visits two of the five cliff-hugging villages, lets you cruise the Ligurian Sea and gives you enough wine to justify every photo you’ll maybe want to reconsider posting. Expect narrow lanes, steep inclines and serious views. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Leaning Tower of Pisa
blocks.text: Here’s your moment to hold up the Tower of Pisa (thanks to the magic of perspective tricks). After a quick coach ride and a short walk, you’ll land in Piazza dei Miracoli with 60 glorious minutes to explore the Duomo, Baptistery and Leaning Tower. Take the photos, dodge the crowds try not to fall over yourself doing the pose. Here’s to gravity doing a questionable job since 1173. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Tuscany Farmhouse Experience with Farmers Davide and Francesca
blocks.text: Sometimes the best museum is someone’s backyard. On this excursion, you’ll meet Davide, Francesca and their daughter Vittoria on a real working Tuscan farm — truffle trees, olive groves, garden tours and a carriage ride included. Then comes the wine. And the homemade pasta. And the cantuccini with Vin Santo (aka biscotti dunked in nectar). It’s family-style everything — served with the a side of w

blocks.heading: Things to do in Gdańsk
blocks.text: Gdańsk is a city made for exploration. Its amber glow, cobbled lanes and riverside views invite you to slow down and take it all in. The Old Town hums with energy, yet every quiet courtyard or market archway still hints at its centuries-old soul. Full of hidden gems and historical sites to marvel at, guests will never get tired of wandering Gdańsk.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Gdańsk
blocks.text: Every inch of Gdańsk tells a story, and our excursions help you explore as much as possible. You can trace the city’s fight for freedom or listen to the echo of pipe organs in vaulted cathedrals. No matter what you pick, all of the details are handled by Princess so you can simply lean in and enjoy.

blocks.heading: Gdańsk & Amber Exhibit
blocks.text: Did you know Gdańsk is known as the world’s amber capital? Visit the Amber Museum to see how this golden resin is shaped into art, then stop by local workshops to watch jewelers polish each piece by hand. The glow of Baltic amber feels unmistakably tied to this city’s identity. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ultimate Gdańsk & Oliwa Cathedral
blocks.text: Inside Oliwa Cathedral, the sound of its massive pipe organ fills the nave with music you can feel in your chest. Afterward, wander through Gdańsk’s Old Town, where cobblestone streets lead to cafés, amber shops and quiet courtyards tucked between pastel façades. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Gdańsk & St. Mary’s Church
blocks.text: Centuries of craftsmanship come together at St. Mary’s Basilica, built entirely of brick and towering above the Old Town. Inside, sunlight filters through stained glass and lights the carved altars. Just outside, market stalls offer handmade amber jewelry and local sweets. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Gdańsk, Sopot & Gdynia
blocks.text: See three faces of Poland’s northern coast in a single day. Gdynia’s harbor brims with ships and seaside cafés, Sopot’s wooden pier stretches into open water and Gdańsk offers centuries of architecture along its winding streets. Each stop shows a different side of life by the Baltic Sea. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Gdańsk & The Solidarity Movement
blocks.text: At the European Solidarity Centre, exhibits and film clips share the story of shipyard workers whose strike helped reshape Poland’s future. Outside, the cranes and gates of the old yard still stand — reminders of how this city helped turn a movement into lasting change. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Gdańsk, St. Mary’s Basilica & Time On Your Own
blocks.text: After a guided introduction to Gdańsk’s Old Town, enjoy time to explore at your own pace. You might stop for pierogi at a local café, browse amber jewelry or sit by Neptune’s Fountain to watch daily life unfold around you. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Gdynia port on your next cruise
blocks.text: On cruises to Gdańsk, ships dock in Gdynia, a modern seaside city where wide boulevards meet the Baltic coast. It’s the gateway to Gdańsk, just a short drive away, and part of many itineraries through Baltic & Scandinavia cruises or broader Europe cruise routes.

Explore itineraries with cruises to Genoa

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Genoa
blocks.text: Choose your adventure: coastal elegance, rural charm, palace grandeur or gelato strolls. These shore access options give you a dose of Genoa’s best without overselling it.

blocks.heading: Late Riser Genoa City & Aquarium
blocks.text: Designed for slower mornings: meet your guide mid‑day, visit Genoa Aquarium to see penguins, sharks and tropical marine habitats, then stroll the old harbour’s shops and cafés. No early alarm, no rush — just seamless shore access and a taste of Genoa’s heritage. Hey, the early bird may get the worm, but late risers get to sleep in and still experience Genoa. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Portofino, Santa Margherita & Genoa
blocks.text: Board a motorboat to Portofino, visit the cliff‑top 12th‑century church of Saint George, float back to Santa Margherita’s seaside promenade and end in Genoa for lunch where you’ll learn to make pesto alla Genovese before diving into the city’s lively streets. Villages, sea spray, cuisine and city, all in one loop. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Rapallo & Pesto Tasting
blocks.text: Arrive in Rapallo, pass by pastel buildings and the 16th‑century seaside castle that once repelled pirate raids, snack on focaccia fresh from a bakery and then sit down for a handmade meal topped with pesto in a local restaurant before the coach takes you back to your ship. It’s a little past and a lot of pasta; two great experiences that go great together. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Camogli, Santa Margherita and Portofino
blocks.text: Begin in Camogli, a fishing‑village‑turned‑shipyard town, where you’ll taste focaccia and soak in the harbour atmosphere. Then a motorboat whisks you to Santa Margherita’s seaside promenade and gelato stops, before you cruise into Portofino, visit the Church of Saint George and absorb the sweeping Piazzetta view. Return by boat to the harbour and your ship just waiting to continue what might be yo

blocks.heading: Da Vinci’s Last Supper & Milan
blocks.text: Board your coach at dawn and head inland for a big‑city contrast: first a guided viewing of Da Vinci’s ‘Last Supper’ in Milan’s refectory, followed by landmark tours of Milan’s architecture and art. This excursion flips your port day into an urban sprint filled with heritage, style and sophistication before you return to the Ligurian coast. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Jewels of Cinque Terre: Riomaggiore, Manarola & Monterosso
blocks.text: Travel through three iconic villages of the Cinque Terre: a motorcoach ride to Levanto, then train to Monterosso, minibus to Manarola and final visit to Riomaggiore’s seaside cafés. Terraced vineyards, sea‑wrapped houses and narrow streets combine into a full‑day escape where the coast’s vertical drama meets village rhythm. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Gibraltar
blocks.text: Gibraltar’s excursions showcase a destination shaped by sea, stone and centuries of stories. From panoramic viewpoints to underground tunnels and cross-border day trips, each tour reveals a different layer of this legendary place.

blocks.heading: Cork & Cattle Farm
blocks.text: Venture into Andalusia’s countryside to visit a family-run cork and cattle farm. Learn how cork is harvested from oak trees, meet the distinctive Retinto cattle breed and enjoy local tapas with olive oil and sherry before returning to port along the Bay of Gibraltar. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Marbella & Puerto Banus
blocks.text: Cross the Spanish border for a day on the Costa del Sol. Stroll the cobbled streets of Marbella’s Old Town, browse boutiques around Plaza de los Naranjos and stop in Puerto Banús to see luxury yachts and waterfront cafés along one of Spain’s most glamorous marinas. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Interactive Flamenco Experience
blocks.text: Step into Andalusian culture with a hands-on flamenco lesson just across the border in La Línea. Learn the rhythm and steps from a professional dancer, then celebrate your new moves with a glass of champagne before returning to Gibraltar. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Top of the Rock - Gibraltar On Your Own
blocks.text: Ride the cable car to Gibraltar’s summit for views stretching from Europe to Africa. Spot the famous Barbary macaques and explore at your own pace with time to browse Main Street or relax in town before returning to the ship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cable Car & Great Siege Tunnels
blocks.text: Experience the Rock from above and below. Ride the cable car for panoramic views, visit the Great Siege Tunnels and hear stories of how British soldiers defended Gibraltar centuries ago. Along the way, meet the island’s mischievous macaques and stop at Europa Point for scenic photos. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: World War II Tunnels & Europa Point
blocks.text: Explore Gibraltar’s military legacy on a guided tour through its World War II tunnels — an underground network carved into solid limestone. See historic photos, walk through wartime command centers and step out onto Jock’s Balcony for a striking view over the runway and sea. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Gothenburg
blocks.text: This vibrant, cosmopolitan city, founded at the mouth of the Göta River by King Gustav II Adolph in 1621, offers something for everyone, whether you want to explore the rocky, rugged islands of the archipelago or sample the city’s history, culture and world-class seafood. The functional canals running through the city still allow access to pleasure craft such as the famous, flat-topped Paddan that

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Gothenburg
blocks.text: Curated Princess excursions are some of the best ways to experience the local flavors, culture and scenery without having to arrange transportation.

blocks.heading: Kayaking in the Savean Moat
blocks.text: See Gothenburg from the water on a guided 3.5 hour kayaking adventure through the city's historic canals and 17th century moat. After a safety briefing and paddling instruction, enjoy about 2.5 hours on the water taking in iconic waterfront landmarks and scenic views before returning to your ship. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Archipelago Island Hopping
blocks.text: Explore Gothenburg's northern archipelago on a four hour excursion featuring scenic drives, ferry rides and island villages. Visit the historic 560 year old Öckerö Church, enjoy coffee and homemade pastry at the Folklore Center, stroll through the village of Hönö and take in the region's beautiful coastal landscapes before returning to the ship. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Gothenburg City & Haga Sightseeing
blocks.text: Discover Gothenburg's historic charm on a panoramic coach tour featuring landmarks such as the Opera House, Poseidon Fountain and Avenyn. Stop at Masthugg Church for sweeping city views, then explore the charming Haga district with its cobbled streets, wooden houses, cozy cafés and artisanal shops. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Easy Gothenburg & Canal Cruise
blocks.text: See Gothenburg by land and water on a panoramic coach and canal boat tour. Pass landmarks including Gustav Adolf Square, Slottskogen Park and Poseidon Fountain, then board a traditional Paddan boat to cruise the city's historic canals, admire centuries old architecture and glide beneath Gothenburg's famously low bridges. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Easy Gothenburg
blocks.text: Experience Gothenburg's highlights on a 2.5 hour coach tour. Visit Masthugg Church for panoramic views, pass Götaplatsen and the iconic Poseidon Fountain, travel along Avenyn, and see Gustaf Adolf Square, home to City Hall, the courts and the city's historic canal. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: West Coast Islands & Herring Tasting
blocks.text: Explore the scenic island of Tjörn on a coach tour from Gothenburg. Enjoy views of Bohus Fortress and the Tjörn Bridge, stroll through the historic fishing village of Klädesholmen, then visit Skärhamn for free time and a tasting of locally prepared herring before returning to your ship. VIEW EXCURSION

Shore excursions to explore in Gran Canaria (Las Palmas)
blocks.text: Choose from a lineup of excursions that show off Gran Canaria’s greatest hits alongside its lesser-known corners. These curated tours balance history, scenery, food and hands-on experiences that go far beyond a simple city tour.

blocks.heading: Grand Canaria Discovery
blocks.text: Maspalomas, Tejeda, Teror and Arucas each show a different side of Gran Canaria. This excursion links them together in a single route that moves naturally from coast to interior. Free time in Tejeda allows for lunch and exploring, while the remaining stops provide cultural context without lingering too long. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Grand Canaria
blocks.text: This excursion pulls together the island’s greatest contrasts in one well-paced day. You’ll move from leafy city parks and historic Las Palmas streets into mountain villages where views stretch wide and quiet settles in like an ocean fog. Stops in Tejeda and Teror add altitude and history, while the gardens of Arucas bring things back down to earth with color and calm. It’s a big-picture look at G

blocks.heading: Wine Cellar and Mojo Workshop
blocks.text: The road into the Agaete Valley feels like a shift into a slower gear. At a family-run farm tucked beneath the Tamadaba cliffs, you’ll taste local wines and learn how mojo sauces anchor Canarian cooking. Vineyards, coffee plants and citrus trees surround the property, grounding the experience in the land itself. This one is intimate, hands-on and refreshingly unpolished. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: A Day at Maspalomas Beach
blocks.text: This is a choose-your-own-adventure kind of day, set in Gran Canaria’s most famous beach destination. After arriving in Maspalomas, you’re free to swim, relax, explore the shoreline, or take a long look at the vast dune reserve nearby. The dunes stretch for miles and change shape with the wind, creating a setting that feels both wild and accessible. When hunger strikes, the surrounding town offers

blocks.heading: Teror & Jardín de la Marquesa
blocks.text: This tour leans into elegance and tradition without overdoing either. You’ll begin in the Jardín de la Marquesa, where tropical plants fill a carefully preserved estate outside Arucas. A brief stop at the volcanic-stone church highlights the island’s architectural character before continuing to Teror. The basilica anchors the town both visually and culturally, making this a stop that stands out mo

blocks.heading: Bandama Crater Hike & Wine
blocks.text: This is Gran Canaria stripped back to its geological core. A guided hike leads you into the Caldera de Bandama, where trails wind through pine, fig and citrus trees inside an ancient volcanic crater. From the rim, the coastline stretches out in every direction. The excursion ends with a winery visit, because volcano hopping is thirsty work. LEARN MORE
