blocks.heading: Featured Greece cruise ports
blocks.text: Across Athens and the Greek Isles, Greece's cruise ports unfold at a lively tempo shaped by history, daily life and enduring tradition. Each destination brings its own character — but all share that distinctly Greek energy that keeps travelers coming back.

blocks.heading: Athens (Piraeus)
blocks.text: As the gateway to Greece’s capital, Piraeus leads you straight into Athens’ ancient heart, where landmarks like the Acropolis, Parthenon and Temple of Olympian Zeus tell the story of Western civilization’s beginnings. Between archaeological marvels, lively markets and vibrant cafés, the city offers a captivating blend of history and modern life.

blocks.heading: Katakolon (for Olympia)
blocks.text: Katakolon is the gateway to Ancient Olympia, birthplace of the Olympic Games. Walk the ancient stadium, explore the ruins of the Temple of Zeus and visit the Archaeological Museum — one of Greece's most rewarding archaeological sites.

blocks.heading: Santorini
blocks.text: Famous for its whitewashed villages and dramatic volcanic cliffs, Santorini enchants visitors with much more than postcard views. Explore the remarkably preserved ancient ruins of Akrotiri, swim at black, red and white sand beaches unlike any other in Greece, and sample the island's celebrated Assyrtiko and Mavrotragano wines from hillside vineyards overlooking the caldera.

blocks.heading: Corfu
blocks.text: Corfu combines Venetian architecture, emerald hills and turquoise waters. Cruise guests can stroll through the UNESCO-listed Old Town, sample olive oils or relax on scenic Ionian beaches.

blocks.heading: Mykonos
blocks.text: Mykonos is perhaps best known for its iconic windmills — 16 in total, with seven perched dramatically on a hilltop in Chora, most dating back to the 16th century. Beyond the landmark views, the island delivers cosmopolitan energy, golden beaches, boutique shopping and seaside dining, with Little Venice's waterfront cafés offering one of the most picturesque spots in the Aegean.

blocks.heading: Chania
blocks.text: Located on the island of Crete, Chania captivates with its Venetian harbor, colorful old town and rich Cretan traditions. It’s the perfect place to explore local markets, ancient ruins and authentic Mediterranean cuisine.

blocks.heading: Heraklion
blocks.text: Crete's capital pairs a vibrant waterfront city with easy access to the Palace of Knossos, the legendary center of Minoan civilization just outside town. The city's Archaeological Museum, Venetian harbor fortress and celebrated Cretan food scene make it well worth exploring beyond the port.

blocks.heading: Rhodes
blocks.text: Step into the past on Rhodes, where medieval walls and cobblestone streets meet crystal-clear beaches. The Old Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, showcases centuries of Greek, Byzantine and Crusader influence.

blocks.heading: Why cruise to Greece
blocks.text: A cruise to Greece offers a seamless way to explore the country’s diverse islands, ancient history and sparkling coastlines — all while enjoying the comfort and convenience of your ship between destinations.

blocks.heading: Landmarks & cultural masterpieces
blocks.text: Greece is a living museum of ancient wonders and timeless artistry, where every ruin, temple and monument tells the story of Western civilization’s beginnings. From archaeological marvels to sacred monasteries, these landmarks capture the spirit and history that make Greece unforgettable.

blocks.heading: Celebrations & Romance
blocks.text: It's difficult to imagine something more romantic than sailing through the alluring cities and charming countryside of Europe. While on board your European cruise, we cater to your sentimental side with private dining on your balcony — like breakfast for two or a sunset dinner — honeymoon packages, flowers and chocolates delivered to your room and couples-only massages in the Sanctuary.

blocks.heading: Accommodations
blocks.text: Your stateroom is where you rest and recharge between adventures. That’s why every room is equipped with the expertly designed Princess Luxury Bed, 100% Jacquard-woven cotton linens. Whether you go interior or all-out in a suite, our staterooms will make you feel right at home. Especially for families traveling together who can enjoy the option of connected rooms.

blocks.heading: Dining
blocks.text: From savory Norwegian meatloaf to sweet Icelandic celebration cake, Northern Europe is bursting with flavor. Head ashore to enjoy Icelandic skyr with porridge for breakfast, and savor a Norwegian seafood dinner. Or embark on an all-encompassing culinary tour right on board with our Chef’s Table Lumiere. On a Norway and Iceland cruise with Princess, appease your appetite with one-of-a-kind dining o

blocks.heading: Entertainment
blocks.text: Embark on adventures by day, and indulge in entertainment by night. Watch Movies Under the Stars® at our 300-square-foot outdoor theater. Attend original productions from Broadway legend Stephen Schwartz, composer of Wicked. Or learn traditional moves, like flamenco or Irish stepdance, and listen to popular music from the destinations on your itinerary. On a European cruise with Princess, the choi

blocks.heading: Relaxation
blocks.text: Your European cruise should be every bit as refreshing as it is inspiring. Unwind in the Sanctuary, a retreat just for adults, and relish in tranquility. Or book an appointment at the Lotus Spa®. Enjoy soothing treatments — like facials, hot stone massages and detoxifying wraps — that will leave you energized for upcoming adventures.

blocks.heading: Casino
blocks.text: Experience the thrill of cards, dice, roulette, and blackjack at our onboard casino during your European cruise. Learn from our expert staff or seasoned guests, and put your skills to the test. For a more relaxed pace, enjoy the slot machines, or join fellow travelers for Bingo and exciting group tournaments. The casino promises nonstop excitement, whether you're a seasoned player or just playing

blocks.heading: Things to do in Grundarfjörður
blocks.text: At the edge of the Snæfellsnes Peninsula and on the shores of Breiðafjörður fjord, Grundarfjörður serves up saga-soaked scenery with a side of small-town charm. Colorful houses pop against a backdrop of lava fields, glacier-fed peaks and the ever-watchful Kirkjufell. This working fishing village is still powered by the sea, but it also draws guests chasing the Northern Lights and drawn to landscap

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Grundafjörður
blocks.text: From puffin colonies to hidden waterfalls, these adventures dive into Iceland’s wilder side. Each tour reveals something new: dramatic cliffs, vibrant birdlife, glacier views, winding hiking trails — all made for nature lovers (or anyone chasing that perfect shot).

blocks.heading: Puffin & Wildlife Boat Tour
blocks.text: Set sail from Stykkishólmur aboard a traditional fishing boat and drift through puffin colonies, basalt cliffs and seal‑haunted coves. Hear stories of the islands once inhabited by hardy locals, and watch for dolphins playing in your wake. With seabirds circling above and history echoing below deck, it’s Iceland’s wild heart — afloat. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Snæfellsnes Peninsula
blocks.text: See the peninsula that inspired Journey to the Center of the Earth. This full‑day adventure takes you from the holy hill of Helgafell to Stykkishólmur’s colorful streets, across cliffs at Arnarstapi and through Snæfellsnes National Park. You’ll hear sagas, feel sea spray at Djúpalónssandur’s black beach and watch fishermen’s lifting stones that clink in the tide. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Djúpalónssandur & Arnarstapi
blocks.text: Spend a half‑day tracing Iceland’s coastal environment. Walk the black‑pebble beach of Djúpalónssandur, gaze at the glacier‑topped Snæfellsjökull and stand on Arnarstapi’s bird‑filled cliffs while your guide unpacks centuries of Viking lore with Icelandic humor as sharp as the wind. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Bjarnarhöfn Shark Farm & Helgafell
blocks.text: Step into a living saga on this half‑day tour. Taste hákarl, the famously fermented shark, paired with Brennivín schnapps at Bjarnarhöfn Farm, then climb Helgafell, where Vikings once prayed to Thor. Between goat pastures and stone‑walled farms, you’ll meet Icelandic tradition face‑first — brave, bold and maybe a little bit tipsy. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Top of the Diamond by Snowcat
blocks.text: Hop a snowcat (it’s a vehicle for traveling in snow) and scale the Snæfellsjökull glacier to discover a glittering, otherworldly summit said to be one of Earth’s ‘energy centers’. Your guide drives slowly so you can take in the lava plains, cloud‑wrapped peaks and wind‑bitten silence that make this Iceland’s most mystical spot. You’ll swear the horizon’s been edited by the gods. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Grundafjörður port on your next cruise
blocks.text: This tender port unfolds like a Norse fever dream. Just off the pier, you’ll find walking tours through a fishing village still pulsing with old‑world rhythm. You’ll enjoy sea‑scented air, lava rock paths and bright tin roofs against a backdrop of glaciers. blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Hamburg
blocks.text: Pick from curated tours that highlight the rich history, vibrant culture and architectural charm of Hamburg, plus day trips that venture out to Berlin or fairytale towns straight out of a storybook.

blocks.heading: Ultimate Berlin
blocks.text: Why confine yourself to just one major German city? Take a scenic train ride to Berlin, then dive into the city’s greatest landmarks — the Brandenburg Gate, the broken Berlin Wall, the Reichstag and more. Enjoy lunch in a traditional German restaurant. It’s Berlin in a day, without missing a beat. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Hamburg
blocks.text: See the heart of Hamburg without breaking a sweat. This panoramic tour gives you the city’s greatest hits: historic churches, lively squares, lakeside views and a glimpse of the Reeperbahn, where the Beatles got their start. You’ll also get time to wander, snack or shop like a local. A great intro for first-timers or those short on time. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: A Tale of Two Cities – Hamburg, Schwerin & a Fairytale Castle
blocks.text: If you’ve ever wanted to walk through a real-life storybook, this is your moment. Start in Schwerin, where a castle rises from its own island like something out of a fantasy film. Explore the charming old town, enjoy a local lunch, then head to Hamburg for a highlights reel of historic sights and modern marvels. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Sweet Hamburg – Chocoversum
blocks.text: Chocolate lovers, prepare yourselves. At the Chocoversum museum, you’ll follow the cocoa bean’s epic journey — and then create your very own custom bar. Along the way, you’ll pass through Hamburg’s historic warehouse district and get a sweet taste of the city’s industrial past with a side of sugar. It’s hands-on, and you better believe those hands are gonna get messy. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Hamburg on your next cruise
blocks.text: Step right off the ship and into a city that doesn’t waste time with warmups. Hamburg’s cruise port drops you close to its beating heart — the canals, churches, cafes and chaotic cool of a working seaport with style. And, you’re just a short drive or train ride from Berlin, making this port the perfect jump-off point for exploring two German powerhouses in one stop. It’s a must-visit stop on any B

blocks.heading: Things to do in Haugesund
blocks.text: Calling all Viking lovers! If you’re a history buff, nature lover or seafood aficionado, you won’t want to miss Haugesund — the birthplace of Norway and ancient Viking village. Explore the reconstructed Viking village or see the very spot where a Viking king unified Norway before dining on delicious seafood.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Haugesund
blocks.text: Don’t stress over planning — experience the best Haugesund has to offer, stress-free, with Princess shore excursions. We’ll handle the details so you can relax and soak it all in.

blocks.heading: Haugesund-Hop-on, Hop-off Sightseeing
blocks.text: Get the best seat for the top sites of Haugesund on the hop-on, hop-off bus that will take you around the city. Visit the Avaldsnes (the ancient seat of Viking kings), see history come to life at a Viking reenactment village and Haraldshaugen where Norway became a country. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Highlights of Haugesund
blocks.text: Welcome to the home of the Vikings! Haugesund is Norway’s birthplace with hundreds of years of history that you can see on this tour. Princess will take you to the only pink town hall in the world, the spot where Norway became a country and the stunning Mount Steinsfjellet Viewpoint for views of the sea. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Mortholmen – a Taste of Norway's Maritime Legacy
blocks.text: Calling all fishing fans! If you love the sea and maritime history, visit Mortholmen, a 100-year property that was once a herring plant and is now featured in Deadliest Catch. After touring the old herring plant, chow down on a seafood lunch straight from the waters around you. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Medieval Church and Viking Village
blocks.text: Step back into time at St. Olav’s Church that was constructed in 1250 A.D. by King Haakon Haakonson. See “Virgin Mary’s Needle,” a massive stone that legend says will touch the wall on Judgment Day. Then head to the Viking Farm on Bukkøy Island for a look at ancient agriculture. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Haugesund port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Whether you want to explore a traditional Viking longhouse, tour a historic herring plant or see the lush green natural scenery Norway is famous for, you’ll love sailing to Haugesund as part of a Norway and Iceland cruise.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Helsinki
blocks.text: Helsinki balances sleek Nordic design with storybook charm. Neoclassical boulevards meet colorful market stalls, while offshore islands and leafy parks give the city room to breathe. Known as the Pearl of the Baltic Sea and the home of the midnight sun, Finland’s capital reflects the spirit of the world’s happiest country — where architecture, nature and everyday life flow beautifully together.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Helsinki
blocks.text: Helsinki’s shore excursions connect the city, countryside and sea. One moment you’ll be in a neoclassical square, the next surrounded by forests, castles or archipelago waves.

blocks.heading: Archipelago Adventure
blocks.text: Strap into a high-speed RIB boat and skim across the Gulf of Finland. Pass Suomenlinna Fortress, summer cottages and narrow straits as the spray rises around you. Between adrenaline bursts, you’ll pause to stretch your legs on an island and hear stories of local life on the water. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Savijärvi Farm, Porvoo & Temppeliaukio Church
blocks.text: Journey from city squares to rolling countryside with stops in Porvoo’s medieval lanes and the granite-carved Temppeliaukio Church. At Savijärvi Farm, meet horses and enjoy a hearty Finnish lunch in a rustic setting. It’s a day that blends history, rural charm and Helsinki’s most celebrated architecture. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Nuuksio Forest Walk & Open-Fire Pancakes
blocks.text: Cruises to Helsinki go beyond the sea and into the verdant world of Finland, too. Breathe in the scent of pine on a guided walk through Nuuksio National Park. After the forest trails, gather around an open fire to flip Finnish pancakes, served with jam and hot coffee. It’s an outing that feels both rustic and restorative. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Vintage Train Ride & Porvoo Old Town
blocks.text: Climb aboard a vintage train and watch forests, rivers and fields pass by before arriving in Porvoo. This second-oldest city in Finland charms with its red riverside warehouses and winding streets. A walking tour reveals a medieval past that still lingers in every timbered façade. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Traditional Finnish Country Life & City Drive
blocks.text: In the forests of Sipoo, visit a country home for coffee and a taste of Finnish hospitality. Learn about village traditions before returning to Helsinki for a narrated drive past landmarks like Senate Square and the shoreline views of Suomenlinna Fortress. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Highlights & Fazer Chocolate Visitor Centre
blocks.text: Chocolate lovers head straight for Fazer’s visitor centre, where exhibits and tastings reveal the sweet side of Finland. Paired with a city highlights drive, this excursion is a chance to see Helsinki’s landmarks and enjoy its most beloved treat in one outing. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Helsinki port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Princess ships dock at Hernesaari, just a couple of miles from downtown Helsinki. The ride is short by shuttle or taxi, but many guests enjoy walking along the waterfront to reach Market Square and the historic center. From here, cruises often pair Helsinki with Baltic & Scandinavia ports, making it a perfect gateway to Northern Europe.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Holyhead
blocks.text: Expect a blend of sea‑facing cliffs, ancient forts, Celtic culture and train whistles cutting through rugged North‑Wales air. The port of call presents dramatic coastal vistas and bold history — from Roman forts and medieval castles to modern seaside energy. You’ll have chances to explore rugged island terrain, taste local fare and feel the energy of a primary gateway to the Welsh lands.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Holyhead
blocks.text: Get ready to dig into the heart of North Wales with excursions that cover everything you could want to see (and by that, we mean lots of countryside, and castles galore).

blocks.heading: South Stack RSPB Reserve Experience
blocks.text: If your idea of fun includes puffins, cliffs and a very satisfying pair of binoculars, this is your jam. Led by a birding expert who knows guillemots from fulmars, you’ll explore the wild headlands of South Stack — a windswept, wave-crashed, bird-packed paradise. In spring and summer, the cliffs come alive with blooms and feathers. The visitor center wraps it all up with info, gear and some cheeky

blocks.heading: Penrhyn Castle
blocks.text: Brace yourself for architecture with a flair for the dramatic. Penrhyn Castle is less medieval fortress and more stately home playing dress-up. Penrhyn is a neo-Norman fantasy filled with lavish interiors, ornate ceilings and fine art. The 60-minute drive across Anglesey and into Bangor sets the stage for this National Trust showstopper. And once inside, you’re free to explore the opulent rooms an

blocks.heading: Conwy Castle & Llanfair P.G.
blocks.text: Welcome to Conwy Castle — a UNESCO World Heritage Site made up of hulking medieval walls, royal ruins and views that feel like they should belong on the bog screen. After exploring its towers and taking in the town’s charming shops, you'll head to the land of the unpronounceable place name: Llanfair­pwll­gwyngyll­gogery­chwyrn­drobwll­llan­tysilio­gogo­goch (don’t worry, PG is fine). Here you’ll h

blocks.heading: Caernarfon Castle
blocks.text: Caernarfon Castle isn’t just an icon of 13th-century military might, it’s where centuries of Welsh and British history collide in a tangle of towers, battlements and symbolism. Your guided tour hits all the highs, both architectural and allegorical. After soaking in its grandeur (and maybe picking up some fun souvenirs), you'll roll back to port feeling like you’ve just walked through a chapter of

blocks.heading: Snowdon Mountain Railway
blocks.text: All aboard the time machine disguised as a scenic train. The Snowdon Mountain Railway climbs to the highest point in England and Wales. From the valleys to the volcanic ridges, every glance out the window hits like a… well, we were going to say ‘like a train’ but that somehow feels redundant. At the summit, it's all panoramic glory with the Irish Sea and Isle of Man waving at you from the horizon.

blocks.heading: Easy Countryside Drive & Welsh Tea
blocks.text: For guests who like their sightseeing with a side of scones, this one’s a keeper. You’ll cruise past hedgerows and heritage as the landscapes of Anglesey unfurl like a well-ironed picnic blanket. The Menai Strait glints beside you, the hills roll politely in the distance, and before long you’re at a cozy local spot for proper Welsh tea. Think buttery cakes hot off the griddle and slices of bara br

blocks.heading: Things to do in Honningsvåg
blocks.text: There’s north, and then there’s Honningsvåg. Up here, the sun can’t be bothered to set, reindeer treat the roads like crosswalks and cliffs casually drop into the Arctic (not all at once or anything; don’t worry). It’s a place that doesn’t follow the usual sightseeing script — which is exactly why it sticks with you. Pack your curiosity and your spirit or adventure, because you’ll be leaving with

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Honningsvåg (for North Cape)
blocks.text: Hungry for adventure? Sight-seeing? Seafood? Whatever your appetite, Princess delivers. When you’re in Honningsvåg, the dancing arctic skies are the limit.

blocks.heading: King Crab & Campfire
blocks.text: Settle into a lavvo (a Sami-style tent) after a motorcoach ride, communal fire lit and sea air sharp. Crabs crack. Butter melts. Coffee steams. Stories swirl. Arctic cuisine is anything but cold, and this excursion will rewrite your definition of warmth. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Stappen Island Bird Safari
blocks.text: Board a bus and coast across Magerøya heading toward Gjesvær, then head into open water for a bird sanctuary adventure. See puffins, sea eagles, razorbills and more as they bob, dive and wheel. Reindeer grazing nearby might sneak into view. It’s wildlife theater with spray from the sea and ice in the air. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: North Cape Hall & Cliffs
blocks.text: Drive across tundra-like terrain and arrive at Nordkapp Hall, perched above ocean emptiness. Inside you’ll find a chapel, a panoramic film that hums with Arctic light and a post office stamping letters with one of the world’s most northern postmarks. Walk outside to cliffs bold enough to make the horizon dizzy. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Honningsvåg ATV Safari
blocks.text: Grab a partner and hop on an ATV built for two. Throttle through moonscape-like ridges and up NATO Mountain. At the summit, Arctic wind and views collide: fjord below, rugged rock all around. It’s loud, it’s bumpy and it’s an experience that will make you feel like you’ve earned every brisk breath. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: King Crab RIB Safari
blocks.text: Board a raft, glide into prime crab territory and haul in pots full of the word’s most royal crustaceans straight from the ocean. Then retreat to a Sami tent — fire crackling and crab meat steaming — for stories and snacks shared under Arctic lights. Sensory overload in the best possible way. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: RIB Ride Adventure
blocks.text: Feel the spray, hear the engine and follow your RIB through the fishing village Kjelvik and past old lighthouses. Dress for cold and thrill. The pace is quick, the views jagged and by the end, whatever chill was biting will be replaced by the exhilaration of having seen the edge of Europe. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience Honningsvåg (for North Cape) port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Enjoy a Transatlantic or European cruise and pull up to dock at the top of the world. Honningsvåg’s pier drops you into a town where few roads curve, many windows peer north and the sky gives back nearly all the daylight at high summer. Shops are warm, locals are friendly and the line of the horizon looks as abrupt as the drop at the edge of some ancient map

blocks.heading: Things to do in Ibiza
blocks.text: Ibiza — or the “White Isle” — dazzles with its beautiful beaches and coastal views, UNESCO World Heritage sites and a bohemian Old Town that overlooks the harbor. Whether you’re here for adventure or just delicious wine, you’ll find it in Ibiza.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Ibiza
blocks.text: Don’t stress over planning — experience the best Ibiza has to offer, stress-free, with Princess shore excursions. We’ll handle the details so you can relax and soak it all in.

blocks.heading: Ibiza Wine Tasting At Can Maymo Winery
blocks.text: Calling all wine lovers! If you want a sip of something delicious, join this excursion to Can Maymó. Taste your way through a collection of Cabernet Sauvignon, Tempranillo, Merlot and Syrah and traditional varietals such as Monastrell and Malvasía. After you’ve had your fill, we’ll take you to the charming village of Santa Gertrudis to see a whitewashed fortress church. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Best of South Ibiza and Dalt Vila
blocks.text: Wander through whitewashed alley streets, stand atop a panoramic hill and explore a 13th century cathedral on this tour of the highlights of Ibiza. See the beautiful Maria de les Neus Cathedral, explore the Diocesan Museum with 14th century religious artifacts and Dalt Vila, a town-within-a-town from the 16th century that sits high above the rest of the city. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: South Ibiza & Las Salinas Nature Park
blocks.text: If you’re feeling a little salty, you’ll love this “salty” excursion to Las Salinas Nature Park. This UNESCO World Heritage Site was prized for its salt pits for centuries, and the salt from Ibiza was so valuable the word “salary” has come from it. See the current salt production sites and the hundreds of birds who call this slice of Spain home. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Highlights of North Ibiza
blocks.text: Explore the oldest church in Ibiza on the beautiful northern side of the island. You’ll go to Jesús Village, home to a 16th-century church that’s the oldest in Ibiza. The altarpiece is from the 1500s and depicts the Annunciation and other chapters from the life of Mary. This tour will also take you to Santa Eulalia, a historic windmill, and Puig de Missa, a historic fortress built to defend from p

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Isafjordur
blocks.text: Shore tours in the Westfjords take you deep into Iceland’s quieter corners. Picture puffin colonies, abandoned villages, fjord cruises and can’t-miss opportunities to hear traditional folk songs inside local churches.

blocks.heading: Arctic Fox Center & Icelandic Folk Music Performance
blocks.text: Head to Sudavik to learn about Iceland’s only native mammal at the Arctic Fox Center. Then, settle in for a performance of traditional folk music in a local church — poetry, song and history all rolled into one. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Whale Watching & Wildlife Cruise
blocks.text: Sail through Ísafjarðardjúp fjord, keeping an eye out for whales, seals and dolphins while mountains tower overhead. The area’s wildlife is abundant, and sightings are common. As you glide along the rugged coastline, you’ll also spot Vigur Island, known for its teeming birdlife. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Calm Fjord Kayaking
blocks.text: Paddle out from the kayak center near the Maritime Museum and take in the fjords at water level. The calm waters are great for beginners, and you’ll get views of mountains and bird colonies that feel even bigger when seen from a kayak. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cruise to Vigur Island
blocks.text: Cross the bay and step into another world. Vigur Island is a haven for puffins, Arctic terns and eider ducks, with a historic windmill and rowboat to see along the way. Your visit ends with pastries and coffee at a 19th-century home. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Bolungarvik Church, Osvör Museum & Maritime Museum
blocks.text: This tour ties together the region’s history and scenery. See Bolungarvik Church, then walk through the Ósvör Outdoor Museum and its fisherman’s hut. Wrap it up at Isafjordur’s Maritime Museum, where dried fish and schnapps tell their own stories. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Skrudur & Flateyri Village
blocks.text: Walk through Iceland’s oldest botanical garden before continuing on to Flateyri, a fishing village with roots in the 18th century. Along the way you’ll hear Icelandic music in the village church, visit the old bookstore and enjoy coffee with pastries. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: A Walk through Isafjordur
blocks.text: Join a local guide for a two-hour stroll through town. You’ll pass colorful houses, see the fisherman’s monument, peek into shops and get a feel for life in the Westfjords’ largest community. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hesteyri & Glacier Fjord Cruise
blocks.text: Cruise the fjords to the abandoned village of Hesteyri, now part of Hornstrandir Nature Reserve. Explore its meadows and rocky shoreline before visiting the Doctor’s House for pancakes and smoked lamb. The fjord ride back is a chance to spot seals and seabirds. LEARN MORE

pages.metaDescription: Explore the magic of Istanbul, Turkey on a Princess cruise. Discover historic mosques, ancient palaces and Bosphorus views with top-rated excursions.

blocks.heading: Explore with Istanbul shore excursions
blocks.text: What do you take away from the city that has everything? These excursions offer a richly layered view of Istanbul, bringing you distinctive experiences that reveal the city’s history, culture and modern energy — from a place that still carries its stories in its streets, architecture and daily life.

blocks.heading: Breakfast Cruise, Blue Mosque & Grand Bazaar
blocks.text: Board a boat at dawn, breakfast in hand, sail against the Bosphorus rising around you. Disembark into the Grand Bazaar’s frenzy, where colors and goods fight for your attention, then slip off your shoes, enter the Blue Mosque and watch silence settle beneath its domes. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Istanbul
blocks.text: You’ll motor into Old Istanbul, where the Blue Mosque looms like an invitation in stone, then slip through Topkapi Palace’s jeweled secrets and hushed harem passages. After lunch, you’re unleashed into the Grand Bazaar’s labyrinth of spice, silk and chaos. Cap it off beneath Hagia Sophia’s dome — where history holds its breath just for you. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Istanbul Highlights & Bosphorus Cruise
blocks.text: Hit the Hippodrome’s ancient footprint, snap the Blue Mosque’s domed silhouette, then slide onto a boat and let the Bosphorus Strait carry you between Europe and Asia. Palaces, seaside mansions and castle towers drift past. Land again for the Grand Bazaar’s swirl of colors and Topkapi’s view over continents. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Treasure Hunt in the Grand Bazaar for Families
blocks.text: Why go sight-seeing when you can hunt for treasure? Turn shopping into a challenge for the whole family. Kids get maps and clues to guide your group through dozens of streets and past thousands of shops, chasing riddles and prizes. The adults? You’ll be right behind, bargaining, laughing and maybe regretting not buying that lamp. Whoever unearths the hidden loot wins bragging rights. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Istanbul City Walls & Spice Bazaar
blocks.text: Trace the old city’s skeletal walls — gates, towers, battles echoing in stone. Then step into Spice Bazaar: smoke scents, sweet teas, saffron clouds and impossibly soft Turkish Delight. Taste, sniff, argue prices and walk away with pockets full of spice (and probably a few new obsessions). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hippodrome, Byzantine Cistern & Blue Mosque
blocks.text: Start at the Hippodrome — whisper where chariots once thundered. Descend into the Underground Cistern, where columns dive into darkness and dripping echoes follow you. Then enter the Blue Mosque, where walls explode in blue. Cap it off with a glimpse of Hagia Sophia and a bazaar stroll. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Late Riser – Ottoman Istanbul
blocks.text: Wake up when the streets feel more forgiving, then hit Rüstem Pasha Mosque to see tiles blot the walls like poetry. Wander the Islamic Arts Museum — artifacts, manuscripts and designs pushing your idea of ‘delicate.’ Finish in the Grand Bazaar; shop slow, snack often, drift back to port asking “Did I dream that?” LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Turkish Food Experience
blocks.text: This is sniff‑and-chew diplomacy. You’ll dart from simit with sesame seeds to smoky kebabs, nut-crusted baklava and strong Turkish coffee or thick tea. Learn spices you didn’t know existed. Laugh, taste, repeat — and return to the ship with a happy stomach. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Featured Italy cruise ports
blocks.text: Italy’s cruise ports offer a captivating mix of history, culture and coastal beauty. Each stop invites you to experience something unique—from ancient cities filled with art and architecture to seaside towns bursting with charm and flavor.

blocks.heading: Experience Italy ports on your next cruise
Why cruise Italy
blocks.text: Italy rewards cruisers like few destinations can — each port unlocks a different chapter of the country's rich history, celebrated cuisine and stunning coastal landscapes, from ancient ruins to vibrant piazzas.

blocks.heading: Celebrations & Romance
blocks.text: It's difficult to imagine something more romantic than sailing through the alluring cities and charming countryside of Europe. While on board your European cruise, we cater to your sentimental side with private dining on your balcony — like breakfast for two or a sunset dinner — honeymoon packages, flowers and chocolates delivered to your room and couples-only massages in the Sanctuary.

blocks.heading: Accommodations
blocks.text: Your stateroom is where you rest and recharge between adventures. That’s why every room is equipped with the expertly designed Princess Luxury Bed, 100% Jacquard-woven cotton linens. Whether you go interior or all-out in a suite, our staterooms will make you feel right at home. Especially for families traveling together who can enjoy the option of connected rooms.

blocks.heading: Dining
blocks.text: From savory Norwegian meatloaf to sweet Icelandic celebration cake, Northern Europe is bursting with flavor. Head ashore to enjoy Icelandic skyr with porridge for breakfast, and savor a Norwegian seafood dinner. Or embark on an all-encompassing culinary tour right on board with our Chef’s Table Lumiere. blocks.text: Embark on adventures by day, and indulge in entertainment by night. Watch Movies Under the Stars® at our 300-square-foot outdoor theater. blocks.heading: Relaxation
blocks.text: Your European cruise should be every bit as refreshing as it is inspiring. Unwind in the Sanctuary, a retreat just for adults, and relish in tranquility. Or book an appointment at the Lotus Spa®. Enjoy soothing treatments — like facials, hot stone massages and detoxifying wraps — that will leave you energized for upcoming adventures.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Katakolon
blocks.text: Katakolon may be small, but it opens the door to one of Greece’s most storied sites — ancient Olympia. Spend your day uncovering centuries of history, enjoying local wine and olive oil or simply relaxing by the sea in this walkable coastal town.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Katakolon
blocks.text: History runs deep in Katakolon, and every excursion offers a new way to experience it. You might trace the roots of the Olympic Games, savor local wine on a family estate or unwind along the coast where the Ionian breeze meets golden sand.

blocks.heading: Olympia & Beach Getaway
blocks.text: Balance discovery and downtime on this leisurely day. Visit the ruins of Olympia, then head to Kourouta Beach for an afternoon of swimming, strolling or simply relaxing at a seaside café with a view of the Ionian Sea. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Olympia
blocks.text: Explore the birthplace of the Olympic Games on a guided tour of the Olympia Archaeological Site, including the Temple of Zeus and the ancient stadium. Visit two museums that preserve artifacts and sculptures from the site, then enjoy a traditional Greek lunch and time for shopping in the nearby village. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Olympia & Archaeological Museum
blocks.text: Travel back more than 2,000 years as you explore ancient Olympia, home to temples, altars and the original Olympic arena. The Archaeological Museum brings the site’s grandeur to life through marble statues, pottery and relics of Greece’s sporting past. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Archaeological Museum & Folkloric Show
blocks.text: This tour pairs ancient artistry with modern celebration. Admire works like Hermes of Praxiteles in the Olympia Archaeological Museum, then head to a local taverna for traditional music, dance and light bites that capture the warmth of Greek hospitality. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Olympia Gi Winery & Wine Tasting
blocks.text: Surrounded by vineyards, Olympia Gi Winery offers a relaxed introduction to regional winemaking. Learn how local grapes are cultivated, tour the production area and enjoy a guided tasting of crisp whites and rich reds alongside small Greek delicacies. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Magna Grecia Local Farm Visit with the Karambelas Family
blocks.text: Spend the day at Magna Grecia Farm, where the Karambelas family shares their love of Greek cuisine and culture. Taste olive oil, sip local wine and watch a lively folkloric dance in the courtyard before browsing handmade goods in the boutique. LEARN MORE

blocks.text: Princess cruise itineraries that visit Katakolon often weave through both Mediterranean and European routes, and occasionally appear on world cruise segments that highlight Greece’s ancient heritage. This peaceful port serves as the gateway to Olympia, where the first Olympic Games took place. blocks.heading: Things to do in Kirkwall
blocks.text: Kirkwall may be small, but its history runs deep. Viking legacies, medieval cathedrals and cozy distilleries sit side by side in this Orkney capital, giving visitors a glimpse of Scotland’s rugged spirit.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Kirkwall
blocks.text: Step off your ship and into landscapes carved by wind, sea and time. Orkney excursions reveal prehistoric stone circles and dramatic cliffs that make this string of over 70 islands a world of its own.

blocks.heading: St. Magnus Cathedral & Earl’s Palace Walk
blocks.text: On a guided walk, see St. Magnus Cathedral, a masterpiece of Romanesque and Gothic stonework. Nearby, the ruins of Earl’s Palace and Bishop’s Palace reveal Renaissance ambition and medieval power. End with Tankerness House Museum, where Orkney’s story comes alive through artifacts and gardens. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Gin Tasting & Kirkwall Walking Tour
blocks.text: Begin with a guided tour and tasting at Orkney Distillery, then stroll through Kirkwall’s cobbled streets. Highlights include St. Magnus Cathedral, Bishop’s Palace and Earl’s Palace, plus time to explore Tankerness House Museum. It’s the perfect blend of flavor, history and local storytelling. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ultimate Orkney
blocks.text: Don’t miss a thing on this “Ultimate Orkney” trip, where you will see the Italian Chapel, the cliffs of Yesnabey, the Neolithic stone circles and more. Tour Highland Park Distillery, explore Neolithic stone circles and walk through Skara Brae, a Stone Age village uncovered by a storm. At Skaill House, Orkney’s grandest mansion, history feels close enough to touch. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ring of Brodgar, Skara Brae & Skaill House
blocks.text: Step back 5,000 years at the Heart of Neolithic Orkney. See the towering stones of Stenness and Brodgar, then wander Skara Brae, where stone houses still hold echoes of prehistoric life. You’ll feel transported through time when you end with a tour of Skaill House, a 17th-century mansion overlooking the sea. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ancient Standing Stones
blocks.text: In just a few hours, experience Orkney’s most dramatic scenery. Walk the wind-battered cliffs of Yesnaby, then visit the Ring of Brodgar and see the Standing Stones of Stenness, some of the oldest in Britain. Each site whispers of ancient rituals and sky-watchers from millennia ago. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: West Mainland Sightseeing
blocks.text: Drive Orkney’s wide coastal roads past seabird colonies and open skies. Stop for photos across Eynhallow Sound, stroll Stromness’s stone-paved streets and see the Neolithic monuments that dot the Heart of Orkney. Along the way, you’ll glimpse Scapa Flow, where naval history shaped the 20th century. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Kirkwall port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Your Princess ship docks a short walk from Kirkwall’s center, making it one of the most accessible ports in Scotland. From here, you can wander into town, join a guided tour of the Neolithic sites or head into Orkney’s windswept countryside. You can easily see Kirkwall during British Isles cruises or European ones when you sail with Princess.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Klaipeda
blocks.text: Immerse yourself in European charm and beauty in the stunning city of Klaipeda. Here you can stroll a white sandy dune with seaside views, explore picturesque fairytale villages and step straight into 1962 and see the underground tunnels of a Soviet missile facility. Klaipeda has a little something for everyone and is the perfect addition to your European cruise.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Klaipeda
blocks.text: Don’t stress over planning — experience the best Klaipeda has to offer, stress-free, with Princess shore excursions. We’ll handle the details so you can relax and soak it all in.

blocks.heading: Legends of Witches' Hill & Baltic Gold
blocks.text: Feel ancient Lithuanian legends and lore come to life all around you in the quaint fishermen's village of Juodkrante. The village is full of over 80 wooden fairytale statues carved from oak on Witches Hill that will make you feel like you stepped into folklore. Then we’ll take you to a honey-colored shoreline beach where you can soak in the natural beauty of Lithuania. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: The Best of Nida: A UNESCO World Heritage Site
blocks.text: Picture this: cute Lithuanian cottages nestled in a sandy strip of land that juts into the azure sea around Lithuania. That’s Nida — the largest settlement on the Curonian Spit, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. You’ll see adorable fishermen’s cottages, go out on flat-bottomed boats, see the museum packed full of amber jewelry and stand atop the 52-meter-high Great Dune. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Klaipeda Old Town, Amber Museum & Palanga
blocks.text: Step into history with a stroll through the winding cobblestone streets of Old Town. Head to Theatre Square where you can see the burnt orange Market Hall and the statue that represents love, all in the heart of the city. Finally, head to the legendary amber museum and Palanga's Basanavicius promenade where you can shop until you drop. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Soviet Nuclear Missile Site
blocks.text: History buffs won’t want to miss the chance to visit this Soviet site where the very missiles deployed to Cuba in 1962 that launched the Cuban Missile Crisis were stored. You can wander the underground tunnels and empty 100-foot-deep silos that once housed missiles during the Cold War. To finish off the day, relax in the stunning Zemaitija National Park and on the shores of the crystalline Plateli

blocks.heading: Experience the Klaipeda port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Klaipeda is a charming city nestled right near the Baltic Sea, the perfect place to stop on your Baltic and Scandinavia cruise. It’s got Old World charm with narrow, winding streets as well as stunning beaches stretching along the coast.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Kotor
blocks.text: Kotor punches above its weight. Nestled inside fjord-like Boka Bay and flanked by sheer stone walls, this UNESCO World Heritage Site — recognized for its outstanding natural beauty and rich cultural history — feels like someone pressed ‘pause’ on time 800 years ago. The old town is a maze of stone alleys, palaces, churches and so, so much history.

blocks.heading: Kotor shore excursions to explore Montenegro
blocks.text: Start in a medieval maze, end with sea spray on your face or mountain wind in your lungs. Pick one to try to cram several into your schedule. Either way, you’ll be taking the spirit of Kotor back with you when you leave.

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Olive Oil Tasting & Panoramic Budva: Meet the Celanovic Family
blocks.text: Drive toward Budva, stop at the Celanović olive mill to meet the geniuses that make the magic happen. Watch olives become oil, and then taste it fresh. After, drift above Budva’s coastline and sample cheese, anchovies and wine in a scenic restaurant with sea on one side, cliffs on the other. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Montenegro
blocks.text: You’ll walk inside Kotor’s walls, hear its stories, then drive into baroque Perast. Board a little boat to Our Lady of the Rocks isle and explore its church of votive paintings. Return to Perast for a guided stroll and coastal lunch before cruising back through the bay. This is Kotor, six senses at full tilt. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ultimate Kotor: Lunch in a Local Home
blocks.text: Kick off in Kotor’s market — fruits, cheese, smokehouse meats, local wine. Then slip over to a chef’s home where you go behind scenes: stories, cooking, table chatter. Eat regional dishes with a family who lives between Adriatic salt and mountain mist. After full bellies and new friends, you return to the ship kinder, heavier and more connected. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: From Sea to Sky: Scenic Cable Car Ride and Old Town of Kotor
blocks.text: You start on the road to Dub, board the cable car and rise over crags until Lovćen challenges your sense of what a landscape can be. Snap photos of the Bay of Kotor stretched before you like a painting. Ride down, walk ancient walls and duck into palaces, sculptures and alley corners in the Old Town. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Bay of Kotor by Tuk‑Tuk
blocks.text: This is joy on three wheels. You’ll zip through winding streets, cruise by coastal villages, dip into Kotor’s old town, then buzz past Our Lady’s church, past Boka’s villages and end with a fresh view of the bay. No walking required — just sit back and enjoy the ride. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kickin’ Kotor
blocks.text: Hop into a 4×4 and get ready to hug switchbacks and ride some steep turns into Lovćen National Park. Wind your way uphill to Njeguši — birthplace of dynasties (and the occasional cheeses and smoked meats) — pause for a farm stop, and then do some tasting. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Montenegro Rock Climbing at Via Ferrata
blocks.text: Strap on your gears because you’re about to take on a vertical trail on Uvita Greda ridge, clipped into steel cables and counting your breaths. You gain altitude, absorb sea and stone and then descend into Kotor. It’s steep, raw, visceral — not for the faint of heart. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Lipa Cave Exploration for Families
blocks.text: Drive past Budva’s Mediterranean blur and arrive at the Lipa Cave entrance. Hop aboard a trolley train and then descend with your family into chambers of dripping stone, shadows and ancient air. Hear echoed legends in cavern halls and when you emerge, head up toward Njeguši for good food and mountain air before the trip back to the ship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Kotor
blocks.text: Your ship anchors just off Kotor’s medieval walls; this is an anchorage port, and the tenders drop you straight into legend. The Bay of Kotor feels ancient and alive, hemmed in by cliffs that lean like watchers and alleys that twist into secrets. Book a Mediterranean or European cruise and don’t just visit Kotor — drop straight into its story.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Kristiansand
blocks.text: Kristiansand sits on Norway’s sunniest southern rim — a coastal gem where forested hills meet salty breeze and wooden houses catch light just right. History, steam engines, village charm and sea cliffs all live a short walk away from the docks.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Kristiansand
blocks.text: These tours offer thrills, heritage, nature and local flavors — pick your flavor and dive deep into scenic southern Norway’s story.

blocks.heading: Kristiansand Sea Fishing Adventure
blocks.text: Step aboard a four‑passenger fishing boat and sail into Kristiansand’s coastal waters. Learn gear, sonar and techniques from your guide, then drop lines into fjord-blue depths. This catch-and-release experience lets you engage with sea, fish and solitude. Return with stories of tugged lines and salty breeze. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Rib Tour Of Kristiansand
blocks.text: You’ll blast off the pier in a RIB (rigid inflatable boat) for a high-octane view of Kristiansand’s rugged coastline, lighthouses and hidden coves. Hold tight as your captain threads through the waves, possibly spotting dolphins or seals, then returns you to shore brimming with sea salt and adrenaline. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kristiansand Adventure: Rafting in Setesdal
blocks.text: Leave the coast behind and head inland toward the Setesdal Valley. After a safety briefing, you’ll launch your raft down Class III/IV rapids on the Otra River. Rapids, sprays, forested cliffs and heartbeats combine into an immersive outdoor rush you’ll replay in stories back on board. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kayaking Kristiansand & Historic Odderoya
blocks.text: Hop in a tandem sea kayak and paddle your way around Odderøya Island’s coastline. You’ll glide past sea cliffs, lighthouses, bays and fishing jetties. Guides reveal local history, point out marine life and help you read the water’s mood as you return along Kristiansand’s downtown waterfront. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: City Walk, Posebyen Quarters & Cannon Museum
blocks.text: Start in Posebyen — Kristiansand’s white‑wooden old town — where humble homes conceal history. Then transfer to the weed‑cracked bunkers of the Cannon Museum, where Germany’s wartime battery still lords the coast. This combo gives you two very different slices of local life: quiet past and the dramatic horrors of the WW2 war machine. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Setesdal Vintage Railway
blocks.text: Head north through the valley to Grovane and board the narrow-gauge Setesdal Vintage Railway. Steam puffs, whistle calls and countryside views carry you toward Røyknes. Then return by motorcoach, letting rhythm and wood‑smoke linger in your mind as you roll back toward the sea. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Kristiansand port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Kristiansand cruises drop you a stone’s throw from its heart. The port is compact, access to walkability is high and many top attractions (Kristiansand Zoo and Amusement Park, Kristiansand Cathedral, and the Kristiansand Maritime Museum) lie within reach. blocks.heading: Things to do in Kusadasi
blocks.text: Kuşadası is your gateway to the wonders of the ancient world. Just beyond this seaside town lies Ephesus — one of the best-preserved classical cities on Earth. Within minutes of the pier, guests can stroll the waterfront promenade, browse lively markets or relax at a café overlooking the Aegean. Inland, historic villages and sacred sites reveal the depth of Turkey’s cultural heritage.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Kusadasi
blocks.text: Princess® shore excursions reveal Turkey’s past and present — ancient ruins, immersive villages and vineyard-covered hills that offer a taste of everyday life along the Aegean.

blocks.heading: Horseback Riding to the Beach
blocks.text: Ride through scenic orchards and quiet forests before arriving at a sandy stretch of coastline where you can wade into the Aegean on horseback. This leisurely half-day tour offers a new perspective on Kuşadası’s natural beauty. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ephesus , Terrace Houses and Ancient Priene
blocks.text: Trace the footsteps of philosophers and emperors as you explore Ephesus and its hillside Terrace Houses, followed by the ancient Ionian city of Priene. Intricate mosaics, temples and grand theaters showcase the artistry of a world long gone but never forgotten. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ephesus, Sirince Village & Home Visit
blocks.text: Combine history and hospitality with a day that begins in Ephesus and ends in the countryside. Visit Sirince Village to sample local fruit wines and enjoy a home-cooked meal in a traditional Turkish household. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ephesus, St. John's & Virgin Mary Shrine
blocks.text: Walk through the ruins of Ephesus, visit the Basilica of St. John and pause at the serene House of the Virgin Mary. These sacred and historic sites together tell the spiritual story of the region. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Turkish Vineyard & Wine Tasting
blocks.text: Spend a relaxing afternoon at Seven Sages Vineyard, where modern winemaking meets ancient tradition. Sample locally crafted wines and cheeses in a lavender-scented setting before browsing handmade carpets at a nearby artisan village. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kusadasi Jeep Adventure & Swim
blocks.text: Go off-road to explore mountain trails and coastal views before cooling off with a swim at Pamucak Beach. It’s an invigorating way to see the countryside beyond the ruins. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Kusadasi

blocks.heading: Best of Santiago de Compostela
blocks.text: Board your coach for the hour‑long drive to Santiago and arrive at Obradoiro Square, facing the cathedral where pilgrims once journeyed for months to see. Inside you’ll tour the museum, admire the 18th‑century facade and wander through plazas that echo with centuries of footsteps. Free time follows for browsing local shops or just soaking in the quiet awe of this ancient city. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Beer Museum, Tasting & La Coruña
blocks.text: Start in La Coruña itself with a spin through the Estrella Galicia Museum (MEGA), where you’ll see how a family‑owned Galician brewery built its legacy. Then explore the city’s coastline — beaches, the Tower of Hercules lighthouse and the cafés of María Pita Square — before sampling beers and cheeses that feel locally legendary. It’s a day of learning and lunching that neither your brain nor your

blocks.heading: Discover Historic Lugo
blocks.text: Drive inland through Galicia’s green hills until you hit the 3rd‑century Roman walls of Lugo — an unbroken stone loop of nearly 2.2 km that still towers above the town today. You’ll stroll sections of the wall, glance out over terracotta rooftops and winding alleys, then head into the Old Town for a mix of Roman arches, medieval churches and local cafés. blocks.heading: Santiago de Compostela
blocks.text: Leave the coast behind and arrive at the monumental square of Santiago de Compostela, where the cathedral looms as both spiritual anchor and architectural showpiece. blocks.heading: Things to do in La Spezia
Shore excursions to explore in La Spezia
blocks.text: Curated tours in La Spezia serve up history, art, culinary depth and endless vistas — pick your trail, strap on sensible shoes and let the day deliver.

blocks.heading: Leaning Tower of Pisa
blocks.text: Here’s your moment to hold up the Tower of Pisa (thanks to the magic of perspective tricks). After a quick coach ride and a short walk, you’ll land in Piazza dei Miracoli with 60 glorious minutes to explore the Duomo, Baptistery and Leaning Tower. Take the photos, dodge the crowds try not to fall over yourself doing the pose. Here’s to gravity doing a questionable job since 1173. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cinque Terre Panoramic Drive by open-top bus & Wine Tasting
blocks.text: No, you won’t walk Cinque Terre; you’ll glide above it in an open-top bus, snapping overhead shots of olive groves, vineyards and cliff-clinging villages. Then it’s on to Cantina Cinque Terre, a wine co-op with serious preservation cred and even better pours. Expect crisp whites, local bites and a story behind every stone terrace. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ultimate Florence & Pisa
blocks.text: This is the greatest hits album of Tuscany. It’s a full-day sprint through Florence’s big names (Duomo, David, Uffizi, Ponte Vecchio), topped with a Tuscan lunch and a swing through Pisa to gaze at its infamous tilt. Expect walking, wonder and the occasional “wait, is that the statue?” moment. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Tuscany Farmhouse Experience with Farmers Davide And Francesca
blocks.text: Get rural. A horse-drawn carriage takes you to Davide and Francesca’s picture-perfect farm where you'll tour truffle patches, veggie plots and olive groves, before diving into a Tuscan feast starring homemade pasta, Vin Santo and almond biscotti. Warning: you may feel a nearly irresistible urge to move in. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Tuscan Countryside & wine tasting
blocks.text: Spend your day channeling your inner noble peasant. Visit a tiny hilltop village — either Montecarlo di Lucca or Lari — where stone alleys echo with history and espresso orders. Then head to a local wine cellar for tastings that may or may not (but probably will) lead to bouts of unbridled enjoyment. Scenic doesn’t even begin to cover it. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Gulf of the poets by land & sea: Fishing villages of Lerici and Portovenere
blocks.text: Travel through living poetry, basically. Start with Lerici (seaside views, tight alleys and a castle just sort of nonchalantly hanging out above it all) then cruise to Portovenere, where your guide leads a walk through pastel facades and a centuries-old church with front-row sea views. You’ll see why Byron wouldn’t shut up about it. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Limassol
blocks.text: Once one of the most important city-kingdoms of antiquity, Limassol blends ancient history with a lively Mediterranean atmosphere. Archaeological excavations in the area have revealed impressive ruins and fascinating artifacts from this once rich and powerful kingdom, offering a glimpse into Cyprus’s remarkable past. Today, visitors can explore nearby Greco-Roman sites, wander historic streets and

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Limassol
blocks.text: Choose from curated tours that highlight Limassol’s most compelling features — from catamaran cruises and mountain hikes to medieval villages and archaeological wonders. Each excursion brings you closer to history, nature or culinary delight (often all three).

blocks.heading: Kolossi Castle, Kourion and Temple of Apollo
blocks.text: This half‑day tour is a history buff’s dream. Visit the Kourion archaeological site overlooking the Mediterranean, explore the medieval Kolossi Castle of the Crusaders and wander the site of the Temple of Apollo in the citrus‑vinegar scented countryside. You’ll finish in Limassol town centre near Castle Square. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Nicosia, the divided Capital of Cyprus
blocks.text: Explore the only remaining divided capital in Europe on this full‑day guided adventure. After your motorcoach ride you’ll walk through the old town ringed by Venetian walls and visit Archbishopric Palace Square and Saint John’s Cathedral. Wander Laiki Geitonia’s 18th‑century lanes and browse the Leventis Municipal Museum for a dose of local heritage. A traditional lunch is included before you retu

blocks.heading: Sun & Sea Catamaran Cruise
blocks.text: Grab your swimsuit and head out on a four‑hour catamaran cruise around Akrotiri Bay off the Cypriot coast. You’ll relax on deck, float into clear water at Lady’s Mile Beach and refresh with soft drinks and fresh fruit on board. When ready, dive in for a swim and soak in the underwater clarity of the Mediterranean before heading back to the pier. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Omodos Village
blocks.text: A half‑day walking tour brings you into the heart of historic Omodos (a village built for wandering). Ride by motorcoach from Limassol, stroll through the plaza, sample local wine and halloumi cheese and visit the Monastery of the Holy Cross that supposedly houses a section of the rope that bound Jesus to the cross. On the return drive you’ll glimpse citrus groves, vineyards and the distant silhou

blocks.heading: The Flavors of Cyprus
blocks.text: Taste your way through Cyprus with a mezze‑style lunch in a traditional taverna near Tochni. You’ll enjoy olives, bread, fresh vegetables, seafood and local wines while folk music plays in the background. After lunch you’ll explore Limassol’s medieval castle area and the Public Garden before returning to the ship enriched and relaxed. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kalidonia Nature Hike
blocks.text: Nature lovers will rejoice on this half‑day excursion into the Troodos Mountains. Your guided hike follows a mountain stream and ends at Kaledonia Waterfalls, where spray from a 50‑foot drop and cool pine‑forest air are your reward. After a stop for refreshments at Platres you’ll drive back to port along a scenic route. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Limassol
blocks.text: When you board a ship for Cruises to Limassol you’ll arrive at the modern Limassol port, which is about 3 miles west of the city center. From the terminal a bus or taxi will get you into town swiftly so you can begin exploring. Whether you’re off to old town shops, castle ruins or Akrotiri Bay, the port sets you up for Mediterranean or European cruise itineraries with minimal fuss.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Lisbon
blocks.text: Pop quiz: Where can you ride a yellow tram older than your grandma, eat a pastry with its own cult following and stumble into a medieval alleyway on your way to a Roman ruin? If you said Lisbon, congratulations — your answer is also the prize you’ve been waiting for. This city isn’t here to impress you with flashy skyscrapers or futuristic light shows. It’s more into surprise tile art, sun-warmed

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Lisbon
blocks.text: These tours are your backstage pass to Lisbon’s layers. Whether you want fresh seafood, sweeping vistas or chilling with centuries‑old secrets, there’s an adventure in your arrival.

blocks.heading: Local Connections: A Journey into Portugal’s Flavors
blocks.text: Join a local chef for a food-first look at Lisbon. Start at Mercado Alvalade Norte — a market once featured on “No Reservations” with Anthony Bourdain — where you’ll shop for fresh produce, seafood and spices alongside your culinary host. While the chef preps lunch, enjoy a guided drive through the city. Then head to Restaurant Clara, tucked inside an 18th-century mansion above Lisbon, where a che

blocks.heading: The Best of Lisbon
blocks.text: Walk through Belém, catch the spires of Jerónimos Monastery and pose by the Monument to the Discoveries. Take a break in Rossio Square for people‑watching and a pastry. Finish with a view of Cristo Rei that stretches from storybook to horizon. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Sintra & Cascais Highlights & Time on Your Own
blocks.text: Drive into green hills, past Moorish castles and palaces, then coast down to Cascais where surf whispers and seafood smells make you slow your pace. Bonus: free time to get lost or found, your choice. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Lisbon by Tram & Coach
blocks.text: Hop in a vintage tram that rattles up cobblestones, then switch to coach for wide views over Alfama, waterfronts and grand squares. And yes—the Pastel de Nata stop is worth the entire trip. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Fátima: The Religious Heart of Portugal
blocks.text: Head out for a quiet pilgrimage to Our Lady of Fátima. The basilica, chapel and pilgrimage square carry prayers and peace, plus the chance to reflect on what centuries of faith and spirituality can mean to a culture. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: City Walk & Funicular Ride
blocks.text: Feet on old stone, eyes on rooftops. Walk Alfama, cross Baixa, climb the funicular or lift. City sounds, smells, color—Lisbon shows up in tiny details and big views. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Panoramic Lisbon, Tiles Factory & Wine Tasting
blocks.text: Cross the 25th of April Bridge, tour a tile workshop where azulejos still come alive under local hands, then taste Portuguese wine at sunset. Crafted artistry, local flavor and a sky full of possibility. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Lisbon Highlights
blocks.text: Lisbon for the individual with lots to do and too few hours to do it. This is a ‘best of’ approach, just condensed and curated: Maritime Museum, Jerónimos Monastery, Belém Tower and Monument to the Discoveries. Fast‑paced beauty with enough time to breathe. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Lisbon port on your next cruise
blocks.text: When you stop over on your Transatlantic or European cruise, Lisbon’s port drops you directly into living pulse and dynamic culture. The terminal sits close to Alfama, Baixa and Belém—so instead of long rides, you spend a few minutes walking through the kind of place most people never get to experience. blocks.heading: Things to do in Liverpool
blocks.text: Liverpool wears its history proudly, from its UNESCO-listed waterfront to a music legacy that still echoes worldwide. Named a UNESCO City of Music and famed as the world capital of pop, the city boasts more #1 hit singles than anywhere else on the planet. Combine that with standout museums, grand architecture and lively pubs, and it’s easy to see why the city keeps travelers coming back.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Liverpool
blocks.text: Liverpool is a gateway to music history, dramatic Welsh castles and the tranquil beauty of England’s lake country. With Princess® excursions, you can experience it all without the hassle of planning ahead — we take care of everything.

blocks.heading: A Walk through Liverpool & Pub Visit
blocks.text: See Liverpool from street level with a guided walk through its historic districts, then end with a pint in a traditional pub. It’s a relaxed way to get to know the city — stories of its seafaring past mixed with a taste of its famous hospitality. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of the Lake District
blocks.text: England’s largest national park is a place of mountains, lakes and timeless villages. Cruise across Lake Windermere, then ride a vintage steam train through the Leven Valley. In Bowness, wander streets lined with Victorian cottages before returning to Liverpool with snapshots of a landscape that inspired generations of poets. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of North Wales
blocks.text: North Wales brims with rugged beauty and medieval fortresses. Journey to Llangollen for a steam train ride along the River Dee, then step into the storied halls of Chirk Castle. Between mountain vistas and playful gardens, you’ll see why this region feels like a storybook brought to life. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Wales & Chester
blocks.text: Cross the border into Wales, then on to Chester, a city with nearly 2,000 years of history. Explore Roman towers, medieval gates and the famous two-story “rows” of timbered shops. A visit to Chester Cathedral reveals centuries of music and worship, while the Eastgate Clock keeps watch over the bustling streets. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Conwy Castle & Town
blocks.text: Conwy Castle dominates the Welsh coast with its eight towers and soaring curtain walls. Explore the fortress and imagine life in a medieval stronghold, then continue to Betws-y-Coed for a taste of Welsh village charm, where rivers, bridges and cafés offer a scenic pause. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cheshire Oaks Outlet: A Shopper’s Paradise
blocks.text: Spend the day at the UK’s largest designer outlet, with brands ranging from Burberry to Bose. With six hours to shop and dine, it’s the perfect way to find a stylish souvenir or a special gift before your journey continues. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Trail of the Fab Four
blocks.text: Follow in the footsteps of The Beatles, from Penny Lane and Strawberry Field to The Beatles Story at Albert Dock. Rare memorabilia, immersive exhibits and iconic photo stops bring the Fab Four’s rise to life — a must for music fans. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Liverpool
blocks.text: Liverpool Cruise Terminal sits right on the River Mersey, placing you within walking distance of the city center. You can enjoy all of the conveniences of modern life while diving into history, including ancient fortresses and more recent eras. blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Málaga
blocks.text: From Granada’s palaces to cliff-hugging footpaths, a Malaga cruise delivers drama at every turn. Choose an easy panoramic outing or lean into an all-day adventure.

blocks.heading: Hiking the Caminito del Rey
blocks.text: Once a daredevil path, now a safely restored walkway anchored high on a canyon wall. Trace boardwalks above the Guadalhorce River, cross thrilling footbridges and pause for sweeping photos. Expect exposure to heights, steady footing and unforgettable views. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Alhambra & Generalife
blocks.text: A masterwork of Islamic art unfolds in stucco lace, carved cedar and mirror-still pools. Tour the Alhambra’s palaces and courtyards. You’ll wander the terraced water gardens of the Generalife, too. A stop for lunch and time to browse the gift shop completes a day steeped in Granada’s Moorish legacy. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Granada
blocks.text: Granada’s Old Quarter pairs spiritual grandeur with royal history. Step beneath the cathedral’s luminous dome, followed by a visit to the Royal Chapel, where Isabella and Ferdinand rest in marble splendor. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ronda
blocks.text: One of Spain’s oldest cities straddles a dizzying gorge. See the Plaza de Toros and museum, admire Santa María la Mayor, then pause at Puente Nuevo where stone spans the El Tajo ravine. Free time invites browsing and lunch before the return along the Costa del Sol. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Marbella & Puerto Banús
blocks.text: Old-town Marbella charms with orange-scented squares and whitewashed lanes. Continue to glossy Puerto Banús where superyachts bob beside designer boutiques and café terraces. Enjoy free time to shop, people-watch or sip a coffee by the quay. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy El Chorro Natural Park Drive & Wine Tasting
blocks.text: Trade the coast for pine-capped hills, turquoise reservoirs and the sheer walls of El Chorro Gorge. Stop for lake views, stroll to a lookout, then continue to the white village of Álora for a tasting of local wine and cheese. A gentle way to sample inland Andalusia. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Málaga’s Alcazaba, Picasso Birthplace and Cathedral
blocks.text: See three city icons in one seamless outing. Explore the Alcazaba’s cool patios and gardens, view masterpieces at Picasso’s Birthplace Museum, then step inside the cathedral known as La Manquita for its single tower. History, art and architecture in a compact circuit. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Marseille
blocks.text: Marseille welcomes you with Mediterranean air, ancient roots and a vibrant modern energy. Around Le Vieux Port, the city’s oldest quarter, history hides in every turn while fishermen, ferries and cafés keep the harbor buzzing. Its diverse cuisine and colorful neighborhoods make it a place where cultures mingle and stories unfold at every corner.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Marseille
blocks.text: You came for scenery, but what you’re getting is storylines, flavors, and maybe one tiny existential crisis — hey, the right excursions can change you. These are the ones that whisper secrets, drag you into misty hinterlands and force you to slow down just enough to feel the weight of history.

blocks.heading: Chateau de Lourmarin & Roussillon
blocks.text: Start with stone — the Renaissance kind, wrapped around Lourmarin’s chateau like a lace collar. Then onto Roussillon, where the buildings wear rust and gold like the earth decided to get glamorous. Lunch is a leisurely affair and the wine is plentiful, and by the time you hit the overlook toward Gordes, you’ll be more than halfway convinced to move here. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Avignon & Palace of the Popes
blocks.text: You’ll thread through Provençal vineyards and dusty valleys, land in Avignon and storm the palace where popes once played politics in velvet robes. The Pont d’Avignon waits for your feet (and your courage). There’s history in the walls, wine at lunch and enough old-world drama to keep your inner monarch thoroughly entertained. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Luberon Villages & Lavender Museum
blocks.text: This one smells like sunlight. Meander through Lourmarin’s fountains and Roussillon’s ochre-splashed streets — the kind of places where time forgets to tick. Then hit the lavender museum, where even the air wears perfume. You’ll leave with a camera roll full of reds, yellows and purples and a new respect for flowers that fight to bloom. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Marseille by Private Vehicle – Car Class Half Day
blocks.text: Throw out the itinerary. You’re the captain now — with a driver who knows shortcuts, secrets and where to find bouillabaisse that’ll knock the vowels out of your mouth. Skip the crowds, chase murals, loiter in a market or chase down alleyway espresso. This is not a tour. It’s a provocation with an engine. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Avignon & Le Pont du Gard
blocks.text: Roll past vineyards and arrive at Pont du Gard — a Roman marvel flexing its ancient geometry over a sleepy river. Then it’s off to Avignon for a side of popes, plazas and that charming bridge you kind of want to dance across. Between the stones, the skyline and your Provencal lunch, it’s a masterclass in how to time travel. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Arles & Les Baux de Provence
blocks.text: Van Gogh lost his mind here; you’ll probably only lose your breath. Arles gives you Roman arches and medieval echoes; Les Baux throws down castle ruins and panoramic mountain drama. It’s the south of France at its most cinematic — churches, cobblestones and the kind of light that makes you want to make a day last. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Olive Growing Farm & Tasting with Owner Mill de la Coquille
blocks.text: This is not just olive oil — it’s generational obsession in a bottle. Walk the groves, meet the mill owner, taste oils that slap in the best way. Then hit Les Baux de Provence, a village carved from rock and sunshine. Expect stories, laughter and enough local flavor to justify shipping a crate home. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Aix en Provence & Marseille
blocks.text: Aix is all polished fountains, flirtatious market stalls and aristocratic snootiness (in the atmosphere, not the people). After soaking that up, drive down to Marseille where cliffs meet the sea and Notre-Dame de la Garde holds court. You’ll dip into the chaos of Le Vieux Port, sweep past cathedrals and maybe (if you’re lucky) taste something you can’t pronounce but will never forget. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Marseille port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Visit Marseille as part of a Mediterranean or European cruise and your ship docks at Marseille Provence Cruise Terminal (MPCT). The terminal is plugged into city transit — buses, shuttle walks and taxis deliver you fast into neighborhoods. From Joliette you can reach the Vieux Port and Le Panier under your own steam.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Messina
blocks.text: Cinematic landmarks, natural wonders — there are endless new sights to see with Princess® shore excursions, which reveal the full spectrum of Sicily.

blocks.heading: Bay of Naxos and Panoramic Taormina by the sea
blocks.text: Cruise the Bay of Naxos for views of Taormina, Isola Bella and The White Lotus filming locations. Swim in hidden coves and enjoy a traditional Sicilian aperitif before exploring the fishing village of Giardini Naxos. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Mt. Etna & Taormina
blocks.text: Journey from coastal Messina to Taormina’s cliffside streets, where ancient history meets Italian style. Then, ascend the slopes of Mount Etna to explore its volcanic craters and take in some of the most dramatic views in the Mediterranean. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Messina
blocks.text: See the best of Messina, from its seaside promenade to the breathtaking Piazza del Duomo. Pause at the Cathedral and its world-famous clock tower, then visit panoramic overlooks that frame the Strait of Messina and the hills beyond. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: In the Steps of "The Godfather"
blocks.text: Film meets folklore in this half-day adventure through Savoca and Forzà d’Agrò, the picturesque villages where Francis Ford Coppola shot The Godfather. Enjoy lemon granita at Bar Vitelli and explore historic churches featured in the iconic films. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Sicilian Beach Break
blocks.text: Unwind on the sun-soaked shores of Giardini Naxos, the first Greek colony in Sicily. Swim, stroll or sample local pizza while admiring the view of Mount Etna rising in the distance. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: San Michele Estate Vineyards & Wine Tasting
blocks.text: Travel through Sicily’s fertile countryside to the San Michele Estate for a guided vineyard tour and tasting. Sample wines shaped by volcanic soil and savor regional cheeses while taking in views that stretch from Taormina to Capo Mulini. LEARN MORE
