blocks.heading: Things to do in Molde
blocks.text: Molde offers a mix of outdoor beauty and cultural charm, from exploring its famous fjord views to enjoying vibrant local museums and festivals. It’s a perfect base for hiking, cruising and discovering Norway’s natural wonders.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Molde
blocks.text: From panoramic lookout points to peaceful fjord adventures and local cultural experiences, Molde’s shore excursions make the most of your time in port. Each one showcases the region’s natural beauty and charm.

blocks.heading: Norway's Fjord and a Taste of Tingvoll Cheese
blocks.text: Journey along the scenic Tingvollfjorden to historic Tingvoll Farm, rooted in 1303 and home to four generations of the Waagen family. Learn about their award-winning cheesemaking traditions as a guide walks you through the cheese and ripening rooms, including the famed Kraftkar blue cheese. Conclude your visit with a tasting of their exceptional varieties. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hiking Along the Varden Path
blocks.text: Get your heart pumping on this active half-day adventure combining scenic hiking and local culture. Ride to Varden Viewpoint, then hike a moderate-to-strenuous downhill trail with stunning views of Molde, the fjord and snowcapped peaks. At the Romsdal Open-Air Museum, enjoy a Norwegian pancake and explore historic buildings before a short walk back to the pier via Reknes Hill and city highlights.

blocks.heading: Fjord Kayaking in Molde
blocks.text: Discover why Molde is a top spot for sea kayaking as you paddle through calm, glassy waters framed by 222 snow-capped peaks. After meeting your expert guide and gearing up, set off toward Seterøya and the idyllic Moldive Islands. Glide through a shallow, hidden lagoon near Hjertøya, stopping for photos and possible wildlife sightings along the way. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Atlantic Ocean Road
blocks.text: Set out from Molde for a half-day adventure along the famed Atlantic Ocean Road, a 5-mile stretch of bridges and causeways linking tiny islands against dramatic ocean views. Cross the striking Storseisundet Bridge, stop in the quaint fishing village of Bud and admire vistas toward the Bjørnsund Islands. Conclude your journey atop Varden Viewpoint, 1,200 feet above Molde. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Highlights of Molde
blocks.text: Discover Molde’s charm on a highlights tour showcasing the “Town of Roses” and its stunning fjord and mountain scenery. Visit the Romsdal Museum to explore authentic Norwegian buildings and enjoy a folk dance performance by children in traditional dress. Continue to Molde Church to admire its Gothic design, then take in sweeping views from Varden Viewpoint before returning to port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Bergtatt Marble Caves
blocks.text: Experience the mystery of the Bergtatt Caves as you journey deep underground to discover their geological wonders. After a scenic 40-minute drive from Molde, meet your guide and travel through a dark tunnel to a hidden, illuminated clearing. Board a barge and glide across a shadowy subterranean lake to a marble hall lit by chandeliers, then enjoy a short film on the quarry’s history before returni

blocks.heading: Tourlos, Mykonos Shore Excursions to explore Greece
blocks.text: Don’t stress over planning — experience the best Mykonos has to offer, stress-free, with Princess shore excursions. We’ll handle the details so you can relax and soak it all in.

blocks.heading: Panoramic Mykonos & Assimomitis Winery
blocks.text: Whether you’re a wine aficionado or someone who likes a good drink, you’ll love a visit to the Assimomitis Winery. Tour the historic winery with an expert guide—with classical music playing around you. Then taste your way through a Greek buffet full of delicacies with a delicious wine tasting. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Delos & Mykonos
blocks.text: Welcome to paradise and the birthplace of the Greek god Apollo. See the best sites in this all-in-one tour with an expert guide. Start in the beautiful Delos where you’ll see artifacts, mosaics and statues showing the city’s ancient splendor. Then head back to Mykonos and see Panagia Tourliani Monastery, a whitewashed church built in 1542, before finishing the day strolling on Kalafatis Beach. LEA

blocks.heading: Ultimate Mykonos Island & Town
blocks.text: Beach lovers will be obsessed with the stunning island of Mykonos. Begin your perfect day with a trip to Agios Ioannis Beach, where you can stand on pillow soft sand and take in panoramic views of the island of Delos. Then head to Kalafatis Beach where you can catch views of azure water that looks like Caribbean seas as you stroll along the shore. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Delos: Birthplace of Apollo
blocks.text: Walk in the footsteps of the god Apollo on the island where legend says he was born. See the architectural sites where ancient ruins will spread out before you as far as the eye can see, walk the Avenue of Lions and visit the museum where you can learn more about the history of the island and the archaeology done here. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ancient Delos in 3D
blocks.text: Step into ancient history with this tour of the best of ancient Delos. You’ll explore a UNESCO archaeological site that’s also considered one of the most sacred in Greece. See the grand Apollo Sanctuary, the historic peer and ancient markets. To make your tour even more unique, you’ll have access to a QR code that gives you the Virtual Reality experience of Delos where you get virtual reconstructi

blocks.heading: Mykonos Beach Getaway
blocks.text: Picture this: you stretched out on pillowy soft Mediterranean sand soaking in some rays and views of cerulean seas. That’s what you’ll get on this excursion to Elia Beach, one of Mykonos’s most famous beaches. The beach is equipped with all the amenities you might need for a great day, including sun beds, umbrellas, refreshments and meals. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Mykonos Town & Aegean Maritime Museum
blocks.text: Mykonos is the “Jewel of the Aegean Sea” for a reason, and you’ll see why on this excursion. See Little Venice, the famous windmills, the narrow whitewashed streets of downtown, Paraportiani Church and Matoyianni Street, a shopping district with adorable boutiques. Finish the day at the Aegean Maritime Museum to Hellenistic ship models. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Naples, Capri, & Pompeii
Naples shore excursions: explore Capri & Pompeii
blocks.text: Naples is surrounded by day trips that read like a history book and a wish list rolled into one. With Princess Cruises, you get curated adventures that let you chase ruins, islands, coastlines, or simply your appetite.

blocks.heading: Walking Tour with Borbonic Gallery & Pizza Tasting
blocks.text: Naples above and below, all in one tour. Start with castles and piazzas, then descend into the Borbonic Gallery, a cavernous underground passage full of history and shadows. Pop back up for seaside photos and wrap it all with pizza at a local spot—because Naples always ends in pizza. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of the Bay of Naples: Pompeii, Sorrento & Capri
blocks.text: A marathon of highlights: ancient ruins, coastal cliffs, and one very famous island. Tour Pompeii with a guide who’ll make the ash feel fresh, stop in Sorrento for lunch with a view, then board a hydrofoil to Capri. Shop, sip, or just stare at the scenery before heading back across the bay. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Pompeii & Amalfi Coastal Cruise
blocks.text: Kick things off with a motorboat ride along the Amalfi Coast, where cliffs drop straight into the sea and towns cling to the rocks. Spend time in Amalfi’s square, then break for lunch before heading to Pompeii. There, streets and plaster casts whisper stories from 79 A.D. Throw in a stop at a cameo factory and you’ve checked off three centuries in one day. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Pompeii & National Archaeological Museum: A Small Group Tour
blocks.text: Go deep into the details of Roman life. First, explore Pompeii’s ash-preserved homes and temples, then pause for lunch before heading to Naples. At the Archaeological Museum, admire statues and mosaics that once decorated the same cities you just walked through. It’s a one-two punch of archaeology and art, with fewer people jostling your elbows. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Herculaneum
blocks.text: If Pompeii feels too sprawling, Herculaneum is the sharp, concentrated version. A guided tour shows off villas, frescoes, and mosaics that survived under 50 feet of volcanic mud. Add in a backdrop of Vesuvius and you’ve got history at its most dramatic. A cameo factory stop rounds out the trip. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Island of Procida
blocks.text: Capri’s glamorous cousin may get the headlines, but Procida is pure charm. Cruise over by jetfoil, snack on lemony pastries, and explore streets painted in enough pastels to fill an artist’s palette. Terra Murata’s castle looms overhead, while the fishing port of Corricella looks like it was staged for cinema. No wonder Hollywood keeps coming back. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Naples Eating Italy Foodie Walking Tour
blocks.text: Three hours, endless flavors. Naples invented pizza and still serves the best, but the city’s food culture goes way beyond that. This walking tour leads you through tucked-away eateries, espresso counters, and street stalls while pointing out historic landmarks in between bites. Bring stretchy pants. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ischia Sightseeing & Thermal Baths
blocks.text: Sail to the lush island of Ischia, famed for its volcanic hot springs. After some free time in Lacco Ameno, head to the Poseidon Gardens, where pools and steam rise against the Bay of Citara. Relaxation level: absolute. History and sightseeing can wait until tomorrow. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Celebrations & Romance

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Olden
blocks.text: Olden and Briksdalen Valleys were molded in the arms of the Josedalsbreen glacier over thousands of years. Olden’s excursions put you eye-to-eye with this natural history written in ice, water and sky. Choose easy viewpoints or full-on hikes — either way, the fjord scenery does the heavy lifting during cruises to Olden.

blocks.heading: Fjord RIB Adventure
blocks.text: Suit up and skim along the inner Nordfjord in a high-powered RIB. Waterfalls streak the cliffs, snow sits high on serrated ridges and the boat dances over wake at speed. Short, scenic pauses let you catch your breath between adrenaline bursts. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Olden Panoramic Sightseeing
blocks.text: Settle in for a relaxed circuit of Nordfjord highlights. Pause by frothing Laukifossen for photos, then continue to Krokesandane for a picture-perfect view of Briksdal Glacier tucked between sheer cliffs. With time to soak in each stop, this ride trades rush for vistas. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Briksdal Glacier Hike
blocks.text: Trace a scenic valley past farms and waterfalls to Briksdal Inn, then follow a well-marked trail toward the blue snout of Briksdal Glacier. The round-trip hike takes about ninety minutes at a steady pace. Reward awaits back at the inn with pastries and hot drinks. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Loen Skylift & Stryn
blocks.text: Ride along Nordfjord to Stryn Lake’s mirror-bright water, then board the Loen Skylift for a swift ascent to Mount Hoven. From the viewing platforms, scan for glacier caps, knife-edge ridgelines and the fjord curling toward the sea. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kayaking on the Nordfjord
blocks.text: Paddle tandem kayaks from the pier into calm, protected waters. As you trace the shoreline, listen for folk tales and local lore while waterfalls thread down the rock faces around you. It’s a quiet, close-to-the-water way to feel the scale of the fjord. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Brenndalsbreen & Briksdalbreen: Hike to Two Glaciers
blocks.text: Double down on ice country with two valley hikes split by a cozy lunch at Briksdal Inn. Brenndalen reveals serrated peaks and distant Melkevoll Glacier, while Briksdal delivers that up-close glacial blue. Expect sturdy footing, big views and a day well spent. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Oslo
blocks.text: Each excursion here offers a slice of Oslo’s spirit — from fjord-front architecture to forest retreats to Viking tales. Catch a longboat (or whatever) and get ready for some adventure.

blocks.heading: Secrets of the Lake & Forest: A Small Group Tour
blocks.text: Leave the bustle behind and ride train to Sognsvann, Norway’s forest‑lake seal. You’ll follow shaded trails through pine and birch, pause at a campfire to warm roots and toast marshmallows, then be led back to the pier carrying quiet air, needle‑soft moss light and wood whispers as souvenirs. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hop On Hop Off Sightseeing by Bus & Boat
blocks.text: Your dual‑mode ticket lets you move through Oslo’s avenues, passing the Oslo Opera House, Royal Palace and City Hall by bus, then slip onto a fjord cruise for a water‑side view of the city’s islands and skyline. It’s part urban storyteller, part sea whisper — architecture and shoreline in one tour. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Best of Oslo
blocks.text: Drive past Akershus Fortress and City Hall, cross to the Bygdøy Peninsula and tour maritime halls honoring Viking ships, polar exploration and Norse sea lore. After lunch you push upward to the Holmenkollen ski jump, then descend into Frogner Park to witness Vigeland’s human sculpture saga. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Open-Air Museum, Vigeland Sculpture & Ski Jump
blocks.text: You’ll visit the Open‑Air Folk Museum, wandering historic homes and farm dwellings. Then the tour moves into Frogner Park to decode Vigeland’s unveiled truths in stone. Finally, ascend to Holmenkollen, drop off for photo panoramas, feel altitude and perspective, then return with a fuller sense of Oslo’s layered soul. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Oslo Highlights & the Munch Museum
blocks.text: Explore Oslo’s bold lines — from the Opera House edge to the Royal Palace gardens and Parliament façade. Then you’ll settle into Frogner’s sculptural heart before entering the Munch Museum, home to The Scream and expressive canvases imagined by Edvard Munch. Art, architecture and emotional tension, all in one sweep. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Fram, Kon-Tiki & Maritime Museums
blocks.text: Roll into Bygdøy Peninsula where Norway’s sea stories unfold across three museums: the Viking Museum, Fram and Kon‑Tiki. Touch the decks of expedition vessels, peer into ocean lore and get to know Norse sailors of yore. Afterwards, return via the harbor’s edge so your last views are salt‑brushed and unforgettable. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Palermo
blocks.text: Immerse yourself in Palermo’s vibrant blend of history, art and flavor. Wander through lively markets, marvel at the golden mosaics of the Palatine Chapel and savor authentic Sicilian cuisine—each moment revealing the city’s rich culture.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Palermo (Sicily)
blocks.text: Set out on captivating shore excursions from Palermo that showcase the very best of Sicily. From exploring ancient temples and vibrant markets to tasting world-famous Sicilian cuisine, every experience reveals the island’s irresistible charm and cultural richness.

blocks.heading: Capuchin Catacombs & Mysteries
blocks.text: See landmarks like the Politeama and Massimo Theatres, then visit the eerie Capuchin Catacombs, home to thousands of mummified remains. Finish your journey at the Oratories of Santa Cita and San Domenico, where stunning artwork and intricate details showcase Sicily’s rich heritage. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Erice & the Ruins of Segesta
blocks.text: Experience Sicily’s fascinating past on this full-day adventure. Explore the medieval village of Erice with its Norman gates, ancient castles and sweeping sea views, then savor a delicious local lunch. Continue to Segesta to marvel at the remarkably preserved 5th-century BC temple. If time allows, enjoy a scenic drive through Palermo’s historic district before returning to port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Norman Wonders of Palermo
blocks.text: Step back in time to Sicily’s Norman period on this half-day tour through Palermo’s historic heart. Visit the grand Palazzo dei Normanni and its glittering Palatine Chapel, adorned with intricate mosaics and carvings. Then marvel at the Cathedral of Palermo, a stunning blend of architectural styles and dazzling Byzantine and Venetian tile work. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Palermo’s Gardens
blocks.text: Begin your journey with a scenic motorcoach ride to Villa Malfitano, a magnificent 19th-century palace surrounded by 22 acres of lush gardens filled with rare trees and ornate fountains. Explore its elegant interiors before continuing to the Botanical Gardens of Palermo, a tranquil haven of exotic plants, towering trees and vibrant blooms—one of the oldest and most beautiful in the Mediterranean.

blocks.heading: The Medieval Village of Erice
blocks.text: Journey to the enchanting hilltop town of Erice, where medieval charm meets sweeping sea views. Wander cobblestone streets past ancient churches, explore the legendary Castle of Venus and the scenic Balio Gardens and browse artisan shops filled with Sicilian ceramics and sweet almond treats. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Palermo Orientation & Monreale
blocks.text: Make the most of your time in Palermo on this half-day sightseeing adventure through the city’s most iconic landmarks. See the Royal Palace, Palermo Cathedral and the grand Massimo Theatre before traveling to Monreale. There, marvel at the stunning 12th-century cathedral adorned with glittering mosaics, considered one of the most magnificent Norman masterpieces in Italy. LEARN MORE

Nestled on the island’s northwest coast, this captivating stop offers a blend of ancient architecture, lively markets and mouthwatering cuisine. blocks.text: Mallorca offers a variety of unforgettable shore excursions that showcase the island’s stunning scenery, local culture and timeless appeal. Whether you’re seeking relaxation or discovery, every experience captures the essence of this Mediterranean paradise.

blocks.text: Discover the essence of Mallorca on this half-day adventure through Palma and the island’s stunning countryside. At the renowned Bodegas Macià Batle winery, savor exquisite wines amid sun-drenched vineyards. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Vintage Train, Ancient Oil Mill & Tasting

blocks.heading: Palma City Sightseeing

Visit Bellver Castle, known for its round shape and incredible views, then explore the stunning La Seu Cathedral with its Gothic design and Gaudí-inspired details. Finish your day with free time in the city center, including a stop at a local pearl shop. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Paris
blocks.text: Picture this: You and your significant other strolling hand-in-hand along the Seine after touring the city and snacking on croissants. If that sounds like your ideal vacation, set sail with Princess to Le Havre, France where we can take you two hours to the City of Love where you can see the Eiffel Tower and Arc de Triumph.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Paris
blocks.text: Don’t stress over planning — experience the best Paris and Normandy have to offer, stress-free, with Princess shore excursions. We’ll handle the details so you can relax and soak it all in.

blocks.heading: Romantic Honfleur
blocks.text: Wander a picturesque 13th-century Norman fishing village. You’ll be able to see why this quaint town was the birthplace of Impressionist and Romantic art! Stop at Vieux Bassin, the old dock that dates back to 1681, and pass the Lieutenance and don’t miss Ste. Catherine's Church, a 15th-century structure that's the largest wooden church with a separate bell-tower in France. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Paris
blocks.text: Welcome to the City of Light! See all the sites you’ve been dreaming about on this whirlwind tour, including the elegant, tree-lined Champs-Élysées, the majestic Arc de Triomphe and the iconic Eiffel Tower. Stroll the Pont Neuf, 'the new bridge," now the oldest bridge in Paris — and see the outside of the Louvre and the two natural islands in the Seine. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Normandy Landing Beaches
blocks.text: Step into history at the D-Day landing beaches, including Omaha Beach and the Museum of the Landing Day. This tour will also take you to the American Cemetery where 10,000 servicemen were laid to rest in France and marble crosses sprawl as far as the eye can see. It’s a reverent and special experience that you won’t forget. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Versailles Palace & Gardens
blocks.text: Let them eat cake — and visit the iconic Palace of Versailles where Marie-Antoinette once lived. This chateau has been on UNESCO's World Heritage List for 30 years, and it shows. You’ll wander through seven suites, the king’s old apartment and even the iconic Hall of Mirrors where kings used to be coronated. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: A Day with Claude Monet in Giverny
blocks.text: Calling all art lovers! Monet fans won’t want to miss the chance to visit his historic home full of colorful rooms and some of his art. Then head out to Monet’s gardens where you’ll see the lily pond that inspired some of his most famous paintings — and walk over the very bridge you can see memorialized in art museums. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Rouen & Notre Dame Cathedral of Rouen
blocks.text: See the ancient capital of Normandy, Rouen, where Monet came to paint and Joan of Arc was burned at the stake. Wander the winding, narrow cobblestone streets surrounded by ancient, timbered houses that open up at a grand Gothic cathedral that’s famous in Monet painting. Finally, explore Place du Vieux Marché, the Old Marketplace, the site where the English burned Joan of Arc at the stake. LEARN MO

blocks.heading: Mont Saint Michel
blocks.text: Experience a real-life fairytale at the “Wonder of the West” or Mont Saint Michel. You’ll start at the base of this island and circle up until you reach the abbey at the top — a building from 709 A.D. that’s been a church and a prison! After exploring the abbey, you can wander the tiered medieval town where you can shop and eat to your heart’s content. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Paris
blocks.text: The Le Havre area and Paris are full of history, stunning architecture and even beautiful natural landscapes. See it all when you take a European cruise to Paris via Le Havre! Return to the golden age of travel on a Transatlantic cruise that will port in Le Havre for Paris. You can sail across the Atlantic like they did for hundreds of years before exploring the historic city of Paris.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Portland
blocks.text: Princess Cruises lines up tours here that aren’t just pleasant—they’re jaw-dropping. These excursions throw you into prehistoric circles, Tudor halls, giant chalk figures, swan colonies, tanks and vineyards (because exploring is thirsty work).

blocks.heading: Stonehenge
blocks.text: A direct hit of prehistoric awe. Two hours from port, you’ll arrive at the visitor center then head to the stones themselves along an encircling path. The site’s sheer scale, precise alignment and ancient engineering remain as staggering today as they were to the builders. Audio guides and exhibits fill in the blanks while your eyes do the rest. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Stonehenge & Salisbury
blocks.text: Step into 5,000 years of mystery with a two-hour drive to Stonehenge, where you’ll circle the massive stones like a druid with a camera. Afterwards, head to Salisbury, one of the world’s most charming cathedral cities, to see the spire, the cloisters and an original Magna Carta (no, you can’t touch it). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Visit to an English Countryside Vineyard with the Langham Family
blocks.text: Ahhh, the Langham Wine Estate. This 30-acre vineyard grows Champagne grapes in Dorset soil and makes award-winning sparkling wine entirely on site. You’ll be guided by a member of the Langham Family or winemaker Daniel Ham through the vines, the production area and into the tasting room for a tutored sampling. A countryside picnic built on local ingredients rounds out this very English twist on lu

blocks.heading: Abbotsbury Swannery & Gardens
blocks.text: Step into a living swan colony founded by monks in the 14th century and still thriving today. Over 1,000 swans nest here, and between May and June you might see hundreds of tiny cygnets tottering through the reeds. After the lagoon, visit the subtropical gardens first planted in 1765 and now a riot of rare botanicals. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Relics from the Great War: The Bovington Tank Museum
blocks.text: Swap swans for steel at the world’s largest collection of armored fighting vehicles. Bovington Tank Museum holds over 300 tanks from 26 countries, including the German Tiger 131 and the British Mark I. Interactive exhibits, soldiers’ stories and six enormous halls make this a thunderous half-day journey through 20th-century warfare. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Athelhampton and The Stone Giant of Cerne Abbas
blocks.text: Drive through the Dorset countryside to meet the 180-foot-tall Cerne Abbas Giant carved into the hillside—a chalk figure whose origins are as mysterious as Stonehenge. Then tour a Tudor manor built in 1485, exploring its Great Hall, King’s Room and award-winning gardens before pausing for refreshments. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Scenic Countryside & Corfe Castle
blocks.text: This 1,000-year-old ruin once guarded the Purbeck Hills and still dominates its village below. Walk through crumbling towers, secret stairways and open courtyards where kings and knights once chilled (and sometimes killed each other). Afterwards, enjoy free time in the village to browse, sip or snack before heading back through the rolling Dorset hills to port.

The port is minutes from coastal trails, cafés and quirky pubs, and an easy springboard to icons like Stonehenge and Salisbury. blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Rhodes
blocks.text: Major historical sites? Out of the way corners? A little wine to wrap it all up? These curated tours check every box. Whether you're scaling Acropolis steps or walking medieval streets that haven’t changed in centuries, you’ll get a full‑flavored taste of Rhodes — ancient past, delightful present and maybe a little myth mixed in.

blocks.heading: The Acropolis of Lindos in 3D Augmented Reality
blocks.text: You read that right; we’re doing ruins and tech. Hike to the Lindos Acropolis, then pull out your AR tablet to see temples and fortresses as they once were (gladiators not included). Once you’ve virtually time-traveled through centuries of sieges and sanctuaries, descend to Lindos Village to grab a snack or browse local shops — because real life still has to compete with digital reconstructions. L

blocks.heading: Rhodes, Grand Masters Palace & Kalithea Springs
blocks.text: Start strong with the architectural fever dream that is Kalithea Springs — domes, mosaics and throwback glamour, originally built for Roman-style healing dips. Then march through the past at the Grand Masters Palace, where knights once brooded and the vibe is still ‘castle chic.’ Wrap it up with a stroll down the cobbled Street of Knights in Rhodes Old Town, where medieval history still clings to

blocks.heading: Best of Rhodes
blocks.text: This is Rhodes, unfiltered and all-in. You’ll conquer the Lindos Acropolis (270 steps with an epic payoff), check out a working ceramics studio where the goods are handmade and then take in the atmospheric Old Town with a guide who knows where the ghosts live. There’s also lunch at a local venue, because surviving centuries of conquest works up an appetite. Palaces, temples and history that slaps

blocks.heading: Lindos Acropolis
blocks.text: The road to Lindos is a coastal showstopper, with Mandraki Harbor flashing by like a Greek myth in fast-forward. At the Acropolis, you’ll climb past the remains of ancient structures that make the word ‘ruin’ sound positive. blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Riga
Riga by Bus & Boat: A Small Group Tour
blocks.text: You’ll get a little bit of everything without the tourist-clogged crowds. Drive through the city’s architectural high notes, then explore Old Town on foot before boarding a vintage-style wooden boat for a cruise down the Daugava River. It’s a low-key, high-payoff way to cover Riga’s greatest hits — with better angles and more elbow room. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Latvian Ethnographic Open-Air Museum
blocks.text: Slip into another century without leaving the forest. This lakeside open-air museum covers 200 acres and more than 100 historic buildings — farmhouses, windmills, churches and workshops included. Watch blacksmiths hammer out the past, listen to traditional folk songs and catch a glimpse of life long before Wi-Fi. It’s hands-on history, with fresh air and zero velvet ropes. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Riga's Jewish Heritage
blocks.text: A powerful walk through one of Riga’s hardest chapters. Visit the ruins of the Great Choral Synagogue, stop at the site of the Rumbula massacre and see the only synagogue still in use today. This is a deep dive into stories that deserve time and respect. Your guide brings the history into sharp focus without softening the edges. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Easy Riga
blocks.text: Kick back without checking out. This slower-paced tour covers Riga’s essentials — Art Nouveau standouts, the House of Blackheads and the maze-like charm of Old Town. You’ll have time to wander, snack, shop or people-watch from a café. Think of it as a scenic stroll with a cheat sheet for what’s worth seeing along the way. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: City Drive & Walk
blocks.text: Start with a coach ride past some of the city’s proudest architectural moments, then hit the ground for a walking tour that threads you through the heart of Old Riga. The Small and Great Guild Houses, St. Peter’s Church and the famously aloof Cat House all make an appearance. A few photo stops on the return route seal the deal. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Retro Tram & Riga Old Town: A Small Group Tour
blocks.text: Ride through town in a 1900s-style tram that’s more charm than speed. You’ll cruise past the National Opera, the Freedom Monument and other headline sights before stepping into Old Town for a walking tour. Your guide sets the pace, but there’s time for your own detours — think local crafts, small cafés and enough atmosphere to fill a dozen travel journals. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Flavors of Riga
blocks.text: Start with bites, end with big stories. Taste your way through the Central Market — housed in former zeppelin hangars — and sample everything from earthy cheeses to smoked meats. Afterward, walk it off through Old Town where churches, statues and rebuilt landmarks give the city’s culinary culture a little extra context. Food tour meets streetwise history lesson. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Experience the Riga port on your next cruise
blocks.text: The port keeps things simple. You’ll be close enough to hear church bells before the gangway even hits the pier. Walk five minutes and you’re in the middle of it all — cafés, galleries, grocery stalls and buildings that feel like they’ve seen some things. It’s an easy spot to explore without needing a minute-by-minute plan. As a popular transatlantic port of call, it’s a can’t miss destination to

blocks.heading: Things to do in Rome
blocks.text: Rome rewards every glance with layers of history and life — ancient arches beside Baroque fountains, lively piazzas echoing with church bells, espresso and street chatter. Spend your hours tracing emperors and artists, then toss a coin for a return.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Rome
blocks.text: Civitavecchia is your gateway to the Eternal City. Go all-in on icons or slip into the countryside for wine, olive oil and timeless hill towns.

blocks.heading: Debark Tour – Vatican, Sistine Chapel & St. Peter’s
blocks.text: On disembarkation day, extend your Roman journey with a guided tour of the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel. St. Peter’s Square provides a memorable final glimpse of the Eternal City before your transfer to the city center or hotel. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: St. Peter’s, Roman Catacombs & Colosseum
blocks.text: Descend into the hush of the catacombs, where early Christian art is etched in soft volcanic rock. Later, the grandeur of St. Peter’s Square sets the stage for views of the basilica before lunch. The day closes at the Colosseum, with time to reflect on Rome’s vast scale from outside the ancient arena. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ultimate Rome
blocks.text: A feast of art and architecture unfolds at the Vatican Museums and the Sistine Chapel, where Michelangelo’s ceiling takes center stage. Lunch offers a pause before an afternoon of Roman icons, from the arches of the Forum to the elegance of the Trevi Fountain where you can make a wish. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Orvieto
blocks.text: Perched high on volcanic rock, Orvieto greets visitors with its striking striped cathedral. Inside, frescoes depict vivid biblical scenes. After a traditional Umbrian lunch, stroll cobbled streets lined with artisan shops selling lace, pottery and woodcrafts, each rooted in centuries of skill. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Pasta Making & Lunch at a Farmhouse
blocks.text: In the Etruscan hills, the Cedrini family welcomes you into their kitchen. Roll dough, cut ribbons and learn why pasta is Italy’s most beloved staple. The reward: a warm farmhouse meal paired with local wine, finished with a homemade dessert. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Etruscan Countryside & Olive Oil Tasting
blocks.text: Tuscania’s medieval lanes lead to sweeping views of the Basilica of San Pietro. Nearby, a family estate reveals the craft of olive oil making. Tasting oils paired with breads and cheeses adds flavor to the day’s rural calm. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Lake Bracciano & Wine Tasting
blocks.text: Tranquil waters reflect the medieval town of Anguillara, set on a peninsula in Lake Bracciano. From here, head into the Tuscia hills for a wine tasting that highlights the region’s rich volcanic soil. Local cheeses and cured meats complete the experience. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: National Geographic Day Tour – Hiking Monte Raschio
blocks.text: Step into a UNESCO-listed beech forest where a naturalist guide shares insights into centuries-old ecosystems. The hike moves at a measured pace beneath tall canopies, offering moments of quiet reflection and discovery. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Rome port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Your ship docks in Civitavecchia (for Rome), about 64 miles from the city center. Join a long line of mariners who have sailed this storied coast where empires rose and ideas crossed seas. Rome features on Mediterranean cruises and broader Europe.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Rotterdam
blocks.text: Rotterdam is not here to charm you with windmill fluff and tulip fluffier. It’s industrial, edgy, and constantly reinventing itself like a city that got bored and hit restart. Don’t expect quaint — expect fascinating.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Rotterdam
blocks.text: Skip the passive sightseeing — Rotterdam’s excursions come with moving parts, strong opinions and a mild obsession with dairy (it’s a good thing).

blocks.heading: Bikes & Bites
blocks.text: Rotterdam by bike with frequent snack breaks? Yes, please. Ride past the Delfsepoort, the harbor and public art installations, tasting cheese, Moroccan tapas, banana bread and cider like you were born for this. You’ll leave full, cultured and maybe just a little sweaty. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Hague, Madurodam & Mauritshuis Visit
blocks.text: Start big with tiny things at Madurodam — a scale model city where you can pretend you’re a benevolent Dutch Godzilla. After lunch (on your own, you're a grown-up), roll into The Hague and gaze upon Dutch masterworks at the Mauritshuis, including Vermeer’s moody icon “Girl with a Pearl Earring.” Bonus: Rembrandt gets a whole room. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Windmills at Kinderdijk
blocks.text: Nineteen windmills. Actual working windmills (the kind that run on wind). Some so old they probably saw Napoleon. You’ll walk uneven ground, climb steep steps and meet the unsung heroes of Dutch flood control. Bonus theater experience explains how this whole windmill gig keeps the country from becoming Atlantis. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: A Hands-on Experience: Pottery Workshop at Royal Delft
blocks.text: Ever painted a tile at a 400-year-old ceramic factory? Now you can. Channel your inner artisan at Royal Delft, then strut your stuff past Markt and the New Church where Dutch royalty naps eternally. Pro tip: Ship your painted tile home unless you enjoy babysitting fragile items all cruise long. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Rotterdam
blocks.text: Minimal walking, maximal bragging rights. Glide past architectural weirdness like the Cube Houses and the Coolsingel on a narrated drive. Stop in Delfshaven just long enough to feel historic, then hop back on the coach and let someone else do the heavy sightseeing. Hey, who ever said you have to break a sweat to see the best of the Netherlands? LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Rotterdam by Boats & Brews
blocks.text: Water taxi. Beer. Water taxi. Beer. Snack. Beer. That’s the cycle, and you’re the star of this amphibious pub crawl. Chat with locals, raise a glass or four and let a guide walk you through the bold and boozy side of Rotterdam. Age 18+ only — toddlers don’t handle beer well. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Walking Tour of Gouda & Cheese Farm
blocks.text: First, meet the cows behind the Gouda at a working cheese farm. Yes, there are samples. Then walk through Gouda proper, past Gothic buildings and narrow lanes that smell suspiciously of aged dairy and smug satisfaction. If you love cheese, this is your pilgrimage. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Amsterdam & Time On Your Own with Dinner Cruise
blocks.text: Two cities, one day, sooooo many delicious carbs. Arrive in Amsterdam, explore at your pace, then hop on a glass-domed boat for a canal dinner cruise that serves up three courses with a side of scenery. UNESCO World Heritage canals aren’t a bad dinner guest. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Rotterdam port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Stepping off the ship in Rotterdam feels like walking into a city mid-thought. Cranes swing, ships dock, glass towers shimmer. Right near port, the SS Rotterdam stands like a cruise ship that aged into a museum. Markethal hits you with food, color and angles from every direction. Book a stop in Rotterdam along your Baltic & Scandinavia or European cruise, and experience it all.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Santa Cruz De Tenerife
blocks.text: Santa Cruz de Tenerife is a city of contrasts — gleaming modern architecture rises beside colonial-era streets, while beaches and mountains frame the skyline. It’s the largest and most populous island of the Canary Islands, and at its heart is a spirit of discovery, with cultural treasures, volcanic landscapes and seaside escapes all within easy reach.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Santa Cruz De Tenerife
blocks.text: With such diverse and historic landmarks, there is practically a world within an island. Discover this little world for yourself on a Princess excursion.

blocks.heading: Whale Watching by Catamaran
blocks.text: Sail from Playa de las Américas aboard a catamaran to search for marine life along Tenerife’s southern coast. Pilot whales are common here, and dolphins often join in playful pods. Between sightings, relax on deck, enjoy complimentary drinks and stop for a swim in a sheltered cove before returning to port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Tenerife
blocks.text: Mountains, valleys and seaside towns combine on this full-day tour. Drive through pine forests to Las Cañadas National Park, stopping at dramatic viewpoints in Ucanca Valley. Pause at Humboldt’s Belvedere for sweeping views of the Orotava Valley before continuing to Puerto de la Cruz, Tenerife’s historic resort town. Free time and a visit to the Orchid Garden round out the day. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Puerto de la Cruz & Orotava Valley
blocks.text: A half-day tour explores Tenerife’s lush north. Travel the Orotava Valley, a fertile stretch nicknamed the “garden of Tenerife,” then stop at Humboldt’s Belvedere for sweeping views. Continue to Puerto de la Cruz, where cafés and shops line the seaside promenade. A visit to the historic Orchid Garden, founded in 1774, completes this scenic excursion. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Basilica de Candelaria & Guimar Pyramids
blocks.text: History and mystery come together on this outing. Visit the Basilica de Candelaria, home to the Virgin of Candelaria, the island’s patron saint. Then travel to the Pyramids of Guimar, a complex of step pyramids that sparked debate among archaeologists and explorers alike. A museum and audiovisual presentation offer insight into this unique site. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: La Laguna & Taganana
blocks.text: Travel across Tenerife’s Anaga Mountains to the fishing village of Taganana, known for its vineyards and rugged cliffs. Pause for a tasting of local wine and cheese before continuing to La Laguna, the island’s cultural and religious capital. Colonial houses, convents and lively squares make this UNESCO-listed city a highlight of northern Tenerife. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: National Geographic Day Tour – The History of Wine in the Canary Islands
blocks.text: This exclusive experience dives into Tenerife’s winemaking traditions. Begin at La Casa del Vino, a 17th-century estate, then continue to Bodegas El Lomo for guided tastings paired with creative tapas. Learn about nearly extinct grape varieties, explore vineyards in the Valley of Tegueste and discover how the island’s volcanic soil shapes its distinctive wines. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Santa Cruz De Tenerife port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Ships dock right in the city, so Santa Cruz’s shops, plazas and cafés are steps from the pier. As one of the Canary Islands’ busiest ports, Santa Cruz features in Europe and Transatlantic cruises, linking Spain to both sides of the Atlantic.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Tenerife
blocks.text: Tenerife’s excursions capture the island’s many sides. Explore landscapes shaped by nature, culture and time, all within easy reach of Santa Cruz.

blocks.heading: Whale Watching by Catamaran
blocks.text: Sail from the southern coast to spot dolphins and whales in the clear Atlantic waters near Playa de las Américas. Relax on deck with refreshments and take in Tenerife’s rugged shoreline during a swim stop in a secluded bay. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Panoramic Las Canadas National Park
blocks.text: Travel through pine forests and mountain roads to Las Cañadas National Park, home to Mount Teide, Spain’s tallest peak. The park’s colorful volcanic rocks and sweeping vistas make it one of the most extraordinary landscapes in the Canary Islands. Enjoy photo stops at Ucanca and El Portillo before returning to port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Puerto de la Cruz & Orotava Valley
blocks.text: Follow the northern coast through the lush Orotava Valley to the resort town of Puerto de la Cruz. Explore its seaside promenade and the historic Orchid Garden, founded in the 18th century, then pause at Humboldt’s Belvedere for panoramic views across the valley and coastline. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Basilica de Candelaria & Guimar Pyramids
blocks.text: See the island’s spiritual and archaeological heritage on a tour that combines the Basilica de Candelaria, dedicated to the Virgin of Candelaria, and the mysterious Pyramids of Guimar. Learn how these stepped structures puzzled historians and see exhibits that link Tenerife’s past to civilizations across the world. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: La Laguna & Taganana
blocks.text: Cross the Anaga Mountains to the fishing village of Taganana, where vineyards cling to the hillsides and the sea seems close enough to touch. Then travel to La Laguna, Tenerife’s UNESCO-listed old capital, filled with colonial mansions, shaded courtyards and a sense of timeless calm. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: National Geographic Day Tour - The History of Wine in the Canary Islands
blocks.text: Trace Tenerife’s winemaking tradition on this immersive day tour. Visit historic estates and family-run vineyards, learn about the island’s volcanic soils and taste local vintages paired with tapas while hearing stories from the winemakers who keep these traditions alive. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Santa Margherita
blocks.text: Santa Margherita is a must-see gem on the Italian Riviera, where timeless elegance meets coastal beauty. With its colorful harbor, grand villas and captivating sea views, it perfectly captures the allure of Italy’s most enchanting seaside towns.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Santa Margherita
blocks.text: Shore excursions from Santa Margherita unveil the beauty and sophistication of the Italian Riviera. Each experience highlights the region’s stunning scenery, historic charm and coastal atmosphere.

blocks.heading: Portofino, Santa Margherita & Rapallo
blocks.text: Discover the Ligurian coast on a guided walking and boating tour through Santa Margherita, Rapallo and Portofino. Explore historic landmarks like Villa Durazzo and Saint George’s Church, enjoy espresso in Rapallo’s old town and stroll Portofino’s scenic paths to the lighthouse for panoramic views before returning by motorboat to Santa Margherita’s picturesque harbor. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Cinque Terre
blocks.text: Experience the breathtaking beauty of Italy’s Cinque Terre on a full-day excursion from Santa Margherita. Visit the seaside villages of Manarola, Vernazza and Monterosso, each known for stunning views and colorful architecture. Travel by boat, bus and train as you explore these coastal treasures and enjoy time to shop and dine. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Paradise Coast Cruise - Camogli, San Fruttuoso & Portofino
blocks.text: Set sail along the Italian Riviera on a private boat to discover the timeless beauty of San Fruttuoso and Camogli. Admire the ancient abbey nestled in San Fruttuoso’s secluded bay, stroll through the colorful fishing village of Camogli and enjoy local wine and focaccia as you return to Portofino for a scenic walk and leisurely exploration before heading back to Santa Margherita. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Olive Oil Tasing at Villa Esedra
blocks.text: Journey from Santa Margherita to the family-owned Villa Esedra Estate, one of Liguria’s few producers of the prized Celso olive oil. Enjoy a private tour led by the Rimassa family through the mansion, oil mill and gardens, followed by a tasting of their award-winning olive oil paired with homemade bread and local wine—all set against breathtaking coastal views. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hiking Adventure to Portofino
blocks.text: Journey from Santa Margherita to Portofino on a guided hike through Portofino National Regional Park. This five-kilometer trail winds past fragrant Mediterranean flora, seaside villages and panoramic sea views. Stop at a restored olive oil mill for wine and focaccia before arriving in the postcard-perfect town of Portofino, where free time awaits before returning to Santa Margherita. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Rapallo Foodie Walking Tour
blocks.text: Savor the flavors of Liguria on an epicurean tour through Rapallo. After a sparkling wine toast and focaccia welcome, learn to make traditional pesto in your host’s bottega. Explore local markets, sample regional delicacies and gelato and finish with a tasting of aged balsamic vinegars—a delicious journey through one of Italy’s most iconic culinary regions. LEARN MORE

blocks.text: Santa Margherita is a highlight on many Mediterranean cruise itineraries, offering travelers a glimpse into the elegance and beauty of the Italian Riviera. This charming port invites visitors to wander its colorful streets, admire the harbor views and discover nearby gems like Portofino and Rapallo. blocks.heading: Things to do in Santorini
blocks.text: Santorini looks unreal until your shoes hit the cobblestones and the caldera wind messes up your hair. Whitewashed villages perch on lava cliffs, blue domes glare at the sun and the Aegean keeps photobombing. Ancient Akrotiri adds the plot twist, wineries add the pour. You come for views, you stay because it feels like someone built a city-sized balcony over the sea just for you.

blocks.heading: Santorini shore excursions to explore in Greece
blocks.text: Santorini hands you the greatest hits and dares you to keep up. Pick your adventure, grab your hat and let the island show off.

blocks.heading: Horse-back Riding Adventure & Swim
blocks.text: Saddle up on sure-footed horses and follow dusty trails over wind-carved dunes to Eros Beach. Black sands, sculpted cliffs, the Aegean doing its best impression of liquid glass. Take a dip, snack, then transfer to Fira for free time and the cable car finale. Beginner friendly with helmets and island pace. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ultimate Santorini
blocks.text: Seven hours of peak Santorini. Walk Akrotiri’s excavation and hear how a Bronze Age city went quiet for 3,500 years. Stroll Oia’s cliff lanes and pause for those blue domes. Sample Assyrtiko at a vineyard, climb to Pyrgos for all-direction views, swing by Kamari’s black sand and finish in Fira for caldera gazing before gliding to the tender by cable car. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Oia, Fira, Winery & Pre Historic Museum
blocks.text: Start with Oia’s photogenic lanes, then crest Pyrgos for a hilltop look at the whole island. Taste at a volcanic-soil winery and refuel with a Greek lunch. Check the caldera viewpoint and Kamari’s dramatic shore, then explore the Prehistoric Museum in Fira to connect artifacts with Akrotiri’s story. End at the cable car if you want extra time in town. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Exclusive Caldera by Catamaran
blocks.text: Sail the flooded crater like a local with a boat. Slide past rust-red cliffs and sugar-white villages, drop anchor near Nea Kameni for a swim where the water shifts color, then trace the lighthouse at Akrotiri while your captain dishes out caldera lore. Disembark in Fira for free time and a cable car ride back to sea level. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ancient Akrotiri & Santorini Island
blocks.text: Walk the roofed site of Akrotiri with a guide who makes the ash layers and streets feel vivid. Roll up to Pyrgos for vantage points and quiet chapels, then continue to Fira for shopping, cafés and that cliff-edge promenade. Keep the motorcoach or split off to linger longer and descend later by cable car. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Oia Village, Wine Tasting & Cooking
blocks.text: Oia gives you the cliff scenes, then a local winery pours Santorini’s signature whites. Head to Akrotiri area for a cooking demo where tomatoes, capers and island herbs do the heavy lifting. Lunch is the proof. Option to remain in Fira afterward for a slow browse before the cable car back to the tender. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Island Drive
blocks.text: Sit back while the island does the work. Crest Pyrgos for photo stops, pull up to a caldera overlook that explains why everyone talks about “the view,” admire Agios Nektarios’ striking exterior and check Kamari’s black sands. End in Fira with the choice to stay and ride the cable car or return directly to the tender pier. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cruise & Hike to Santorini Volcano
blocks.text: Boat to Nea Kameni and climb the cinder trail to steam vents and crater rims. Sulfur in the air, lava underfoot, caldera spread out like a map. Cool down back on board with a swim stop near the hot springs, where mineral water paints the sea bronze. Fierce, stark and wildly photogenic. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Skala pier on your next cruise
blocks.text: Mediterranean and European cruises to Santorini anchor in the caldera and tender you to Skala Pier below Fira. You’ll choose your ascent: the cable car up to Fira, the footpath or pre-booked tours that whisk you to Oia, wineries and viewpoints. Cafés, shops and that cliff-edge skyline sit minutes away, making this an easy launch point for island-wide exploring.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Sarandë
blocks.text: Choose from excursions that pull back the curtain on ancient cultures, natural wonders and wine-fueled hilltop panoramas.

blocks.heading: Traditional Albania
blocks.text: This one’s for the culture buffs. Begin with a stop at Lëkurësi Castle, then view the exterior of the Mesopotam Monastery. After a short break for local refreshments, head back toward town for a deep dive into the ruins of Onchesmos. Mosaics, basilicas and ancient cisterns reveal a side of Albania that’s as complex as it is underrated. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Sarande
blocks.text: Start at the UNESCO World Heritage site of Butrint, where the Romans, Venetians and Greeks all left their fingerprints. Walk past temples, theaters and fortresses, then continue to the mystical Blue Eye spring. Local legend once blamed a 12-headed dragon for hoarding its waters (but today you’re more likely to find tourists doing slow 360s with their phones). After lunch at the Foinike restaurant

blocks.heading: Ancient Butrint and Sarande on Foot
blocks.text: Step back 2,500 years at Butrint, one of the most impressive Greco-Roman ruins on the Illyrian coast. Marvel at the baptistery mosaics and Roman forums before heading back to Sarandë for a stroll through its own buried past. You’ll visit the Onhezmi Synagogue, built atop a Christian basilica and later converted for Jewish worship. The mosaic floors tell stories in symbols: menorahs and ram’s horns

blocks.heading: Sarande, Lekuresi Castle & Wine Tasting
blocks.text: Start with a hilltop view from Lëkurësi Castle, then sip your way through Albanian wine history at the Isak Winery. You’ll sample local vintages and raki alongside cheese and fruit, with a crash course in wine production dating back 3,000 years. Wrap it all up with a visit to the ruins of Onchesmos with its ancient basilicas and water cisterns. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Porto Palermo Castle and Himara Village
blocks.text: Travel south along the coast to the 15th-century Porto Palermo Castle, a triangular fortress with five towers and panoramic views of the Ionian Sea. Then continue to the seaside village of Himara for a short walking tour, a taste of raki and a snack at a local café. Between the sunshine, the sea and the storybook setting, this is coastal Albania at its most charismatic. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Lekuresi Castle, Mesopotam Monastery and Blue Eye National Park
blocks.text: Kick off your day with a drive up to Lëkurësi Castle and views stretching from Sarandë to Ksamil. Then it’s on to the Mesopotam Monastery, one of the oldest Byzantine churches in Albania. Cap it off at the Blue Eye, where cold spring water bubbles up in brilliant blue from an underwater cave. A traditional lunch rounds out the adventure. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Seville
blocks.text: Pick your kind of adventure — grand architecture, wine country, seaside paddles — the region serves up variety with style.

blocks.heading: Kayak Tour Sancti Petrí
blocks.text: Swap plazas for paddles and head to the protected coasts of the Cádiz Bay natural park. You’ll set off in two‑person kayaks through marshes, past old fortifications and out to islands like Sancti Petrí (stopping to swim or snorkel if the mood strikes). Waves, wind and open water — this one’s for people who literally want to immerse themselves. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cadiz Walking Tour
blocks.text: Take in one of Europe’s oldest cities and feel the layers of history under your feet. Start at the neoclassical Town Hall from 1799, then drift into the golden‑domed Cádiz Cathedral, built at a time when Spain’s unmatched riches poured directly into the Church. You’ll wander narrow alleys, pop into plazas where locals meet and peer down from a watchtower. Shoes that can handle cobblestones are you

blocks.heading: Jerez de la Frontera & Sherry Bodega
blocks.text: Head inland where vineyards roll and sherry rules. Your coach takes you past Cádiz Cathedral Square, through Jerez’s historic centre to the bodega where barrels age patiently and your tasting begins. Learn how the region turned sun and soil into something rich and liquid and raise a glass to a moment you’ll always remember. Open edges, wine lanes and vineyard light — pure Andalucía. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: A Taste of Andalusia – Adventure in Tapas
blocks.text: This half‑day tour flips the script: you’re not just tasting tapas, you’re making them. You’ll arrive at a 19th‑century estate in Jerez, meet your host and roll up your sleeves for a cooking demo (pay attention, because you’re the one who gets to eat the results). Enjoy the fruits of your labour, along with shrimp, regional wine and probably a heaping helping of laughter. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Seville
blocks.text: Leave the coast behind for a full‑on dive to Seville’s best-known icons. Begin with the enormous 15th‑century cathedral. Step through the Christian‑Moorish Alcázar with its gardens and ornate rooms, then sit down to lunch and finish your day at Plaza de España — one of Spain’s grandest urban statements. This is the kind of excursion some people build their entire vacations around. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Seville River Cruise & Time on Your Own
blocks.text: Mix it up with land, water and freedom. Start with a coach ride through olive groves into Seville, then board a boat and glide along the Guadalquivir River. After docking you’re free to roam streets, cafés and boutique shops before one last photo stop at Plaza de España and your return to the ship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Seydisfjordur
blocks.text: At the head of a narrow East Iceland fjord, Seydisfjordur puts one of the region’s most distinctive small-town scenes within walking distance: Rainbow Street leading to the Blue Church, with 19th-century wooden homes extending through town. Cruises to Seydisfjordur also open the door to the Icelandic landscapes beyond, from waterfall hikes to seasonal puffin viewing.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Seydisfjordur
blocks.text: On a Seydisfjordur cruise, Princess® shore excursions open several paths into East Iceland, from coastal wildlife sites to the valleys beyond town. Local guides add the human history behind the landscape, giving each stop an expert’s insight into the context and culture of the region.

blocks.heading: Hike to Hengifoss
blocks.text: Cross Fjardarheidi Pass and follow Lake Lagarfljot before setting out on foot toward Hengifoss. The trail climbs toward the waterfall, where bands of red clay cut across dark basalt cliffs. Along the way, Litlanesfoss drops through columns of basalt, adding another memorable geological feature to a hike that reveals the volcanic character of East Iceland’s interior. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Borgarfjordur Eystri & Hafnarholmi
blocks.text: Travel across East Iceland to Borgarfjordur Eystri, a small coastal village with deep ties to local folklore, then continue to Hafnarholmi for seasonal seabird viewing. Platforms and stairs overlook nesting areas where puffins and kittiwakes gather at close range. The drive adds a broader sense of the fjords beyond Seydisfjordur, with mountain passes and coastal vistas unfolding along the way. LEA

blocks.heading: Skriduklaustur Museum & Valthjofsstadur
blocks.text: Cross Fjardarheidi Pass and travel inland toward Lake Lagarfljot. Then visit Skriduklaustur, the former home of author Gunnar Gunnarsson, for a closer look at East Iceland’s literary heritage. The excursion also includes Valthjofsstadur and the Snaefellsstofa visitor center, adding local history and natural-history to a day spent exploring the region beyond the fjord. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Traditions of Iceland: Food & Culture
blocks.text: Travel past Lake Lagarfljot to the Wilderness Center, where a restored farm brings earlier highland life into the present. Spend time with local hosts and learn how people adapted to this remote part of Iceland. A traditional Icelandic meal prepared in the farmhouse kitchen gives the visit a warm finish, and helps guests form a delicious personal connection to the region. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Skalanes Nature Reserve
blocks.text: Travel along the fjord toward Skalanes, a nature reserve and research center where conservation work meets a long record of human settlement. Visit the Thorarinsstadir archaeological site before hiking toward coastal viewpoints. In season, the cliffs support abundant birdlife, while the route is optimized for chances to spot seals or whales in the water below. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Chasing Waterfalls
blocks.text: Follow a guide into Vestdalur Valley, where waterfalls cut through a protected landscape on the way to Vestdalseyri. This former settlement was once home to a whaling station and later one of Iceland’s largest cooperatives before the community was abandoned in 1963. The route gives you a closer look at both the valley’s natural features and its working past. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Seydisfjordur port on your next cruise
blocks.text: On cruises to Seydisfjordur as part of select Princess European cruises/Iceland & Norway cruise itineraries, the town center sits just 0.2 miles from the cruise piers, putting much of Seydisfjordur within walking distance. blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Siracusa
blocks.text: Cruise visitors can dive into Siracusa’s rich past with guided tours of Ortigia, the Archaeological Park, and the Ear of Dionysius, or opt for scenic adventures like winery visits and coastal boat trips. Each excursion offers a curated taste of Sicily’s history, flavors and breathtaking landscapes.

blocks.heading: Baroque Noto: A UNESCO World Heritage Site
blocks.text: Discover the beauty of Noto, one of Sicily’s most enchanting Baroque cities, on a guided walking tour through its meticulously rebuilt historic center. Stroll from the grand Porta Reale along Corso Vittorio Emanuele, admiring ornate palaces and churches carved from white limestone. Climb the monumental staircase to Piazza Municipio before returning to port inspired by this architectural gem. LEARN

blocks.heading: Best of Siracusa
blocks.text: Discover Siracusa’s ancient wonders on a half-day tour through the Neapolis Archaeological Park, home to the Latomia del Paradiso, the grand Greek Theatre and the Roman amphitheater once walked by gladiators. Continue into Ortigia’s medieval streets to see the Arethusa Fountain, the Bay of Siracusa and the stunning cathedral built atop the ancient Temple of Athena before returning to port. LEARN M

blocks.heading: Ragusa Ibla & Modica
blocks.text: Explore two remarkable Sicilian towns on a scenic journey from Siracusa. Visit Ragusa Ibla for a guided walk past baroque gems like St. George’s Church and the tranquil Giardino Ibleo, then enjoy lunch before heading to Modica. Wander its tiered historic center and savor famous local chocolate before returning to port with unforgettable memories. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Catania & Mt Etna
blocks.text: Experience a full day of culture and natural beauty as you travel by motorcoach to Catania, a 2,700-year-old UNESCO World Heritage Site. Explore Piazza Duomo’s iconic landmarks before heading to Mount Etna’s Silvestri Craters for sweeping gulf and vineyard views. Enjoy a delicious local lunch before returning to port, completing this unforgettable Sicilian adventure. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Pupillo Winery & Wine Tasting
blocks.text: Savor the flavors of Siracusa on a half-day journey through the scenic countryside to the family-owned Azienda Agricola Pupillo Winery. Explore the picturesque estate and gardens with a knowledgeable guide before sampling their celebrated Moscato di Siracusa, produced in dry, semi-sweet and sweet varieties paired with local delicacies. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: A Stroll through Ortiga: Old-Town Siracuse
blocks.text: Siracusa’s rich past comes to life as you cross into Ortigia and wander its winding streets toward the legendary Fountain of Arethusa, overlooking the Ionian Sea. Explore the stunning Piazza del Duomo and its centuries-old cathedral, admire the historic palace, and enjoy a local refreshment in the vibrant market. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Skagen
blocks.text: Skagen sits at Denmark’s northern tip — where the Baltic and North Sea elbow each other out — and delivers a mix of sea, sand, history and art. You’ll find rugged dunes, maritime museums, cozy galleries and hearty fish dishes that celebrate its fishing‑town roots.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Skagen
blocks.text: This port serves its adventures like it serves its fish — fresh, diverse and straight from the source. Whether you’re into bikes, brushes or bunkers, Skagen’s excursions dive deep into what makes this place tick.

blocks.heading: Engine Room, Rescue Station & Marina Walk
blocks.text: This walking tour opens the doors to Skagen’s mechanical soul. Step into the Engine Room museum, a treasure trove of vintage marine motors, mopeds and diesel nostalgia. Continue past the Skagen Rescue Station and fish auction, learning how locals have faced the sea for generations. It’s hands-on, oil-scented and packed with the kind of stories you won’t find in a brochure. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Best of Skagen
blocks.text: This half-day highlight reel gives you a front-row seat to Skagen’s essentials. Cruise past the harbor, then climb Denmark’s largest migrating sand dune, Raabjerg Mile. After that, a tractor-pulled trolley takes you to Grenen, where you can straddle two seas like a mildly aquatic superhero. It’s dramatic, scenic and ideal for guests who like their sightseeing with a little salt. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Danish Occupation & Resistance – WWII
blocks.text: Explore Denmark’s wartime shadows at Bangsbo Fort, where German bunkers remain frozen in time. Then continue to the Jutland Resistance Museum, set in a manor barn, to uncover the stories of Danish resistance and Cold War escalation. Rich in context and layered with history, this tour peels back the curtain on a part of Europe’s past that rarely makes the headlines. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Meet the Skageners: A Small Group Tour
blocks.text: Trade the tourist path for something a bit more personal. This small-group walking tour introduces you to the people of Skagen through cobblestone strolls and actual conversations. You’ll visit Ancher’s House, learn about the town’s artistic roots and end up in a local’s home for pastries, tea and real talk. It’s culture by way of connection — warm, authentic and deeply Danish. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Legacy of the Skagen Painters
blocks.text: Get inside the minds of the artists who turned Skagen into a muse. With a curator as your guide, explore the Skagen Museum, then visit Anchers Hus and the home of Holger Drachmann. This tour unpacks how light, landscape and local life shaped the iconic Skagen painters. It’s immersive, atmospheric and tailor-made for guests who travel with a sketchbook. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Skagen by Bike
blocks.text: Grab your helmet, hop on and explore Skagen’s beauty at your own pace — just faster. Pedal past the Sand-Covered Church, the Klitgaarden artist retreat and quiet beachside paths toward Grenen, where you can literally dip your toes in two oceans. With scenic detours and steady terrain, this ride gives you an intimate, sweat-earned look at Skagen’s coastal character. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: A Taste of Skagen
blocks.text: Walk, taste, repeat. This walking tour introduces you to Skagen through its flavors, with stops for cheese, fresh seafood, a classic fish cake at Pakhuset and a candy finale at a local sweets shop. You’ll also get a chance to chat with vendors and explore tucked-away food spots. It’s a delicious way to understand a place that treats every meal like a memory. VIEW EXCUSRION

blocks.heading: Easy Skagen by Accessible Vehicle
blocks.text: Skagen’s scenery is just as stunning from the comfort of a motorcoach. This relaxed three-hour tour includes photo stops at the Raabjerg Mile sand dune and several historic neighborhoods, along with drive-bys of landmarks like the Klitgaarden and Old Skagen. Ideal for guests looking for a less strenuous way to experience Skagen’s culture, coastline and natural drama. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Skagen port on your next cruise
blocks.text: When you dock in Skagen as part of your European or Baltic & Scandinavian cruise, you're stepping into a working fishing and cruise port that hums with both tradition and tourism. The shuttle bus service to the town center makes it easy to dive right in. You’ll find yellow houses, white picket fences and a town center brimming with personality. It’s a perfect jump-off for art lovers, seafood chase

blocks.heading: Things to do in Skjolden
blocks.text: Tucked deep inside Sognefjord, the village of Skjolden feels like it was dropped straight into the middle of a Norwegian fairy tale. Mountains tower above, waterfalls crash down cliffsides and stave churches silent and strong (as if they’ve gotten used to posing for centuries’ worth of visitors). The village may be small, but the experiences here stretch in every direction — including access to Jo

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Skjolden
blocks.text: These tours pull you straight into Norway’s drama — ancient woodwork, icy mountains, waterfalls that demand attention and fjords that stretch on towards an endless horizon.

blocks.heading: Kayak the Hidden Wonders of Lustrafjord
blocks.text: Paddle through Lustrafjord’s calm waters with towering cliffs on either side. Waterfalls spill into the fjord, seals and porpoises sometimes tag along and seabirds circle overhead. No prior experience is needed — just a willingness to dip your paddle into one of Norway’s most peaceful landscapes. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Skjolden
blocks.text: Take in the views from Northern Europe’s highest mountain pass before visiting the 12th-century Lom Stave Church and the Norwegian Mountain Museum. Lunch is included, with stops at the Saga Column and the roaring Åsafossen Waterfall. This full-day trip showcases the area’s most striking landmarks in one sweep. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: RIB Adventure
blocks.text: Hop into a rigid inflatable boat and skim across Lustrafjord’s emerald water. The ride is fast and fun, with commentary from your captain as waterfalls and tiny farms slide past. You’ll get up-close views of Feigumfossen Waterfall — all 720 feet of it — and maybe spot seals or porpoises playing in the fjord. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Mørkid Valley Bike & Hike
blocks.text: Pedal through peaceful Mørkrid Valley, then trade wheels for boots on a hike to Drivande Waterfall. Along the way you’ll hear about Skjolden’s history and culture, pause for local flatbread and cured meats and snap photos at one of the valley’s most dramatic cascades. It’s active, rewarding and full of scenery worth the sweat. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Sognefjell Mountain Scenery
blocks.text: A scenic drive across the Sognefjell Mountain Pass delivers endless vistas of lakes, peaks and waterfalls. With stops for photos in the Hurrungane range and up on the plateau itself, this is a relaxed way to experience some of Norway’s grandest landscapes from the comfort of a motorcoach. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Walking with Llamas in Skjolden
blocks.text: A village stroll gets a playful twist when you add a llama to the mix. Meet your furry walking partner at a local farm, then head out along the Fortun River and into Mørkrid Valley. Your guides share stories of farming life while the llamas set the pace. The tour wraps with drinks, biscuits and a viewpoint over the valley. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Jostedal Glacier National Park
blocks.text: Travel to Jostedal Valley and stand in sight of Nigardsbreen, one of Norway’s largest glaciers. Visit the Breheim Glacier Center for exhibits and sweeping views, then walk a newly built nature path that brings you closer to the ice. It’s a look at a frozen giant that’s been shaping the land since the last ice age. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Urnes Stave Church & Viking Shipyard
blocks.text: Visit Norway’s oldest stave church, a UNESCO site dating back to 1130, then tour the Ornes shipyard where Viking-era woodworking techniques are still alive. The drive along Lustrafjord, nicknamed the Romantic Road, includes waterfalls, storybook villages and plenty of photo stops. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Skjolden port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Docking in Skjolden puts you right inside a natural amphitheater of fjords and mountains. The port is a small and easy-to-navigate stop along your Iceland & Norway or European cruise, with the village just steps away. Cafés, shops and trailheads are all within reach, and shore excursions depart directly from the pier. It’s the kind of place where you don’t need to go far to feel surrounded by Norw

blocks.heading: Things to do in Split
blocks.text: Discover Split, where ancient history meets a lively Mediterranean spirit. At its heart lies Diocletian's Palace, the vast 4th-century Roman complex that forms the city’s Old Town and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Explore highlights such as the Peristyle Square, the Cathedral of Saint Domnius and the atmospheric palace cellars — famously used as a filming location for Game of Thrones. Beyond the p

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Split
blocks.text: Set out on unforgettable shore excursions from Split that reveal the best of Croatia’s Adriatic coast. From breathtaking landscapes to charming coastal towns, every experience captures the region’s natural beauty and cultural richness.

blocks.heading: Diocletian's Palace, Cathedral & Temple of Jupiter
blocks.text: Explore the best of Split on a guided walking tour through the historic Diocletian’s Palace. Stroll its ancient courtyards and narrow lanes, visit St. Dominus’s Cathedral for stunning city views and pass through the Temple of Jupiter before ending your tour in Split’s charming Old Town, where shops and cafés line the lively marble streets. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Split
blocks.text: Explore the best of Split on a guided tour that blends history, art and local flavor. Stroll through Diocletian’s Palace and Old Town, admire the views from St. Dominus’s Cathedral, and visit the Mestrovic Gallery, home to Croatia’s famed sculptor. End your day with a relaxing lunch and wine by the scenic Cetina River countryside. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Trogir & Solin
blocks.text: Step back in time on this captivating excursion through Croatia’s ancient past. Explore the Roman ruins of Salona, once the capital of Dalmatia and uncover centuries-old amphitheaters, baths and churches. Then journey to the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Trogir, where medieval charm awaits with its grand cathedral, Venetian palaces and picturesque streets. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: ATV Quad Adventure
blocks.text: Embark on an exhilarating ATV adventure through the rugged beauty of Dalmatia. After a scenic drive to Ciovo Island, follow your guide along winding trails lined with Mediterranean vegetation. Stop for breathtaking views at the abandoned Prizidnica Monastery and enjoy panoramic vistas of Split and the Adriatic before relaxing with free time on one of the island’s stunning beaches. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Imotski Lakes and Countryside
blocks.text: Set out on a scenic journey through Croatia’s countryside, beginning with stunning views of the Cetina River in the coastal town of Omiš. Explore the charming streets of Imotski and visit the striking Blue and Red Lakes before continuing to a traditional eco-village. Enjoy an authentic homemade lunch and discover the region’s timeless culture before returning to port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Diocletian's Palace, Cathedral, Temple & Trogir
blocks.text: Begin your adventure with a scenic drive to Trogir, a charming island town filled with architecture and winding stone streets. Explore landmarks like St. Lawrence Cathedral and Cipiko Palace before returning to Split to tour the magnificent Diocletian’s Palace. Conclude your day browsing the shops, markets and cafés of Split’s vibrant Old Town. LEARN MORE
