blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Stavanger
blocks.text: Pick the tone you want: fjords, farms, history or brews. All options carry you deeper into southern Norway’s mix of rugged and refined.

blocks.heading: Waffles at Summer’s Paradise
blocks.text: A short scenic jaunt brings you to Jørpeland, where you’ll devour crisp Norwegian waffles topped with jam and cream while soaking in unbeatable views of the fjord. Explore peaceful gardens, browse quaint shops or just savor the slow pace. It’s sweet, it’s scenic and the coffee is strong enough to rewrite your morning routine. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Stavanger and Surroundings
blocks.text: This half-day journey dives into Stavanger’s contrasts — fjord-side serenity and quirky inland charm. Ride through the lush Dirdal Valley to Byrkjedalstunet, a revived 1920s cheese factory turned artisan enclave. Feast on lapper pancakes with sour cream and jam, then explore Norway’s largest boulder field at Gloppedalsura. Cap it off with a city highlights drive and optional Old Stavanger walk. LE

blocks.heading: Utstein Kloster & Music Recital
blocks.text: Travel to Moster Island for a rare sensory treat: a guided tour of 13th-century Utstein Kloster followed by a live music recital inside the monastery’s historic chapel. You’ll cross through pastoral landscapes dotted with sheep and seaside views, then return via Stavanger’s cobbled quarters. It’s part history, part harmony and totally worth crossing a fjord for. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cruise Along Lysefjord
blocks.text: Board a boat and brace for one of Norway’s most dazzling fjords. Cruise past rugged cliffs, plunging waterfalls and the iconic Pulpit Rock towering 1,800 feet overhead. Keep an eye out for sea eagles and seals, and enjoy a refreshment stop mid-voyage. This ~3-hour escape offers raw, cinematic views best seen from the water. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Iron Age Farm & Petroleum Museum
blocks.text: Explore 1,500 years of Norwegian history — starting with Iron Age dwellings featuring turf roofs and reconstructed longhouses. Then jump centuries forward at the Petroleum Museum, a modern marvel built like a mini oil platform. Bonus: panoramic views from Ullandhaug Viewpoint and a possible stroll through Old Stavanger. It’s like time travel, but without the weird side effects. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Old Town & Beer Tasting
blocks.text: Old Stavanger’s whitewashed streets set the stage for a two-hour microbrew adventure with centuries of backstory. A local guide leads the way past cobbled lanes and Viking tales before dropping you in a pub picked by The New York Times to be included in their 2019 list of “50 places to go.” Sample six beers — mead to brown ale — with crunchy snacks and a side of local lore. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Stockholm
blocks.text: Stockholm occupies islands and embraces water like few cities can — often referred to as the Venice of the North. You’ll pass copper-green rooftops, step through medieval alleyways in Gamla Stan and feel the calm energy that comes when a city respects both history and design. It’s elegant without being pretentious, ambitious without being showy.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Stockholm
blocks.text: Time in Stockholm is best spent on tours that let you lean into what you came for — art, history, quirky museums or gliding through waterways.

blocks.heading: Stockholm Ice Bar & Gamla Stan
blocks.text: Want to do something ‘cool?’ Ride through Old Town to the Stockholm Ice Bar. Wrap up in a fur poncho and sip a drink from an ice glass in a room held at 23°F. Then explore Gamla Stan on foot. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Stockholm by Private Vehicle – Car Class Half Day (Driver Only)
blocks.text: You’ll have a private, air-conditioned car and English-speaking driver for a half- or full-day experience. The route’s yours (within time limits), though stops are up to you. Entrance fees, meals and gratuities are on you. Book early — these are limited and nonrefundable. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Stockholm
blocks.text: See Stockholm’s crown jewels: City Hall (venue of the Nobel banquet), the Vasa Museum and historic Gamla Stan. After lunch, stroll past stately buildings, visit the 13th-century Royal Palace and explore Old Town at your own pace before returning. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Vikings to the Vasa: a Journey into the Past
blocks.text: Start at the Viking Museum with immersive exhibits, smoke, fire and stories of Norse life. Then head to the Vasa Museum to examine the nearly intact 17th-century ship, its artifacts and its tragic tale. The return ride passes through Stockholm’s landmarks. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Nobel Prize Museum & City Hall
blocks.text: Explore the Nobel Museum in Gamla Stan, then drive to City Hall to tour the Blue Hall and Golden Hall — rooms decked with mosaics and stories. Finish at a high vantage point for sweeping views of Stockholm’s waterways and rooftops. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Stockholm & SkyView
blocks.text: This is your minimal-walking option. Drive through Gamla Stan, Södermalm and Östermalm while key sights roll by. Pause for photos from a skyline viewpoint, then ride the SkyView for elevated panorama of the city. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Stockholm’s Waterways Cruise
blocks.text: Glide through Stockholm’s archipelago. Your launch departs near the pier, passing the Royal Palace, Opera House, Grand Hotel and more. Green parks, island neighborhoods and architectural highlights slide past your window. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Royal Palace, Old Town & Canal Cruise
blocks.text: Drive to Gamla Stan, visit the Royal Palace and Coronation Church, then walk the cobbled streets. Later, board a motor launch for a 50-minute canal cruise through the National City Park and out toward archipelago islands like Fjäderholmarna and Grona Lund. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Stockholm port on your next cruise
blocks.text: When your Baltic & Scandinavian or European cruise drops you off in Stockholm, the city is quite literally your backdrop. You’re near waterways and historic neighborhoods, within walking or short-ride reach of Gamla Stan’s cafés, museums and scenic bridges. You don’t have to travel far to feel like you’re in the heart of Stockholm’s story from the moment you dock.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Stornoway
blocks.text: On the far reaches of the Outer Hebrides, Stornoway sits on the Isle of Lewis like a Gaelic fever dream: moody moors, Standing Stones older than Egypt’s pyramids and waves that can topple cliffs (given a few million years to work). This island is the heart of Gaelic culture. It’s also a can’t miss stop when you’re touring the British Isles. If you're looking for Neolithic monuments, reconstructed

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Stornoway
blocks.text: Every tour from this port feels like a portal. Step into ancient circles, castle ruins, whisky tastings and coastlines that will end up monopolizing your memories for decades to come.

blocks.heading: Harris Whisky Distillery & Tweed Shop
blocks.text: This one's for the fabric lovers and whiskey romantics. Travel south past lochs and mountain views to Tarbert, where the Harris Distillery serves up critically acclaimed whisky and some very friendly storytelling. You’ll tour the facilities, learn about their ‘nothing-but-the-best’ distilling methods and then sample two pours that’ll make lesser drams feel like tap water. Before you head back, vis

blocks.heading: The Historic Island of Lewis
blocks.text: This tour is basically a highlight reel of everything ancient and awe-worthy on Lewis. Start with the Callanish Standing Stones — arranged in a Celtic cross shape and towering up to 15 feet tall. Then it’s off to the Carloway Broch, a fortified tower built around 100 BC. Wrap up with a stroll through the reconstructed Gearrannan Blackhouse Village to see how folks lived, farmed and weaved in the 1

blocks.heading: Uig’s Dramatic Coastline
blocks.text: Scotland’s coastline is something else, and Uig takes the cake. To see it for yourself, you’ll drive to Miavaig Harbour, board a boat and skim past Riof Beach’s white sands, sea stacks, crags and the uninhabited isles of Siaram and Pabbay Mor. Don’t be surprised if seals pop up to say hello. Highlights include Geodha na Sgarbh’s natural sea arch and the aquamarine stillness of Pabbay Lagoon. Cap i

blocks.heading: Lewis Lighthouse & Northern Beaches Scenic Drive
blocks.text: This is your North Coast beach day, Hebrides style. Drive over peat-dotted moorlands to reach the Butt of Lewis Lighthouse (the UK’s windiest point and possibly the least subtle). Gaze over cliffs that feel maybe a little too high when you’re standing on them, then head to Port of Ness Beach to wander gold sand and maybe snag a snack at the local café. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Stornoway RIB Adventure
blocks.text: If your version of ‘seeing the coastline’ includes speed and sea spray, this is your excursion. Head to the marina, suit up in a lifejacket and board a rigid inflatable boat (RIB) for a fast-paced ‘Seafari’ along some of Scotland’s most rugged, wildlife-filled waters. Expect scenery, seabirds and adrenaline. And yes, you’ll almost certainly get wet. That’s part of the charm. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Lews Castle Grounds on Foot
blocks.text: This is the slow-sipping scotch of excursions. Start at the pier and meander through Stornoway’s waterfront, cross a scenic bridge and climb into the forested grounds of Lews Castle. Having been everything from a WWII hospital to a college, today’s Lews Castle grounds are all lush gardens and hidden footpaths. End at the Woodland Center, where you can snack like royalty. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Tallinn
blocks.text: You don’t need to be a medieval historian or a local foodie to enjoy Tallinn — Princess shore excursions bring the best of the city (and beyond) right to you. Each experience blends history, culture and scenery, with all the details handled so you can focus on the adventure.

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Estonia in Love and War with Historian Andres Kraas
blocks.text: Join noted historian Andres Kraas for a day that threads together art, architecture and Estonia’s long struggle for independence. Walk through Toompea Hill and descend into the Bastion Passages beneath the city walls, where echoes of conflict linger. Along the way, hear first-hand stories that bring Estonia’s triumphs and trials vividly to life.

blocks.heading: Old Town Tallinn & Rakvere
blocks.text: Step into Estonia’s storybook past at Rakvere Castle, where medieval walls and live cannon fire bring history alive. After lunch in its courtyard, return to Tallinn and stroll Toompea Hill, a district crowned by towers, spires and centuries-old churches. It’s a day that blends countryside charm with the capital’s Gothic heart.

blocks.heading: Upper Old Town & Kadriorg Palace
blocks.text: Tallinn’s Upper Town is a treasure trove of castles, cathedrals and sweeping views over red-tiled rooftops. Wander Palace Square and step inside St. Mary’s Cathedral before heading to Kadriorg Palace. Built by Peter the Great, its gilded hall and manicured gardens offer one of Northern Europe’s most dazzling displays of Baroque style.

blocks.heading: Coastal Sightseeing & Lighthouses
blocks.text: Along Estonia’s rugged coast, lighthouses rise above cliffs and crashing surf. Pause at the limestone Suurupi beacon, admire the red-painted Pakri Tower and feel sea breezes as you gaze out toward rows of windmills. This outing pairs maritime lore with striking Baltic scenery, capped by time in Tallinn’s medieval center.

blocks.heading: Medieval Towers of Tallinn
blocks.text: Tallinn’s skyline bristles with fortifying pillars, each with a tale to tell. Walk through stone gates and past onion-domed churches before arriving at Stout Margaret Tower. Once an artillery post, it now invites visitors to climb its 150 steps for panoramic views — the perfect vantage point to admire this medieval city.

blocks.heading: Estonian Black Bread: Traditions, Tales & Taste
blocks.text: In the seaside village of Pringi, step into the past at the Viimsi Open Air Museum. Wander rustic farmhouses, learn how black bread has shaped Estonian life for centuries and savor a warm slice with homemade butter. It’s a small-group experience that blends storytelling, local culture and the comforting aroma of bread straight from the oven.

blocks.heading: Exclusive Liviko Distillery & Glimpse of Old Town
blocks.text: Raise a glass to Tallinn’s spirited side with a guided tasting at Liviko Distillery, a 120-year-old producer of renowned Estonian liqueurs. Explore the interactive museum and see how tradition meets innovation before strolling into the UNESCO-listed Old Town. Between Gothic spires and cobbled lanes, you’ll discover why this capital is as intoxicating as its spirits.

blocks.heading: Experience the Tallinn port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Your gateway to Tallinn begins at the city’s modern cruise terminal, just a short walk from Old Town. Within minutes, you’ll find yourself surrounded by medieval towers, market squares and cobblestone streets that make this Baltic capital feel like a step back in time. Many itineraries connect Tallinn with other Baltic & Scandinavia gems, making it a highlight of European cruises.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Toulon / Provence
Shore excursions to explore in Toulon & Provence
blocks.text: Ready to trade your ship deck for a sun-soaked vineyard or a medieval hill town? These excursions bring Provence to life with local flavor, timeless architecture and yes, plenty of wine.

blocks.heading: Hyères
blocks.text: Step back in time on a five-hour visit to Hyères. Walk uphill through narrow streets to the 12th-century Tour des Templiers and past Gothic churches and Romanesque buildings. Visit Castel Saint Claire (once home to Edith Wharton) and take in views from the lush gardens. At the top: ruins of a medieval castle. Enjoy free time before heading back to the ship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Provence
blocks.text: Explore the heart of Aix-en-Provence, hometown of Cézanne and poster child for French elegance. Your guide leads you along Cours Mirabeau, past fountains and 17th-century mansions before heading into Old Town. After a guided intro, you're free to wander, shop or sip espresso in the sun. On the way back, take in the country road of Le Tholonet and glimpse Sainte Victoire Mountain, Cézanne’s muse an

blocks.heading: Bormes-les-Mimosas & Hyères
blocks.text: Visit Bormes-les-Mimosas, a flower-drenched 12th-century village with sweeping views of Lavandou Bay. Wander its medieval lanes and photograph the fairy-tale Parcours Fleuri. Then head to Hyères, the oldest resort on the French Riviera, for a walking tour and free time to shop, snack or soak in the history. Bonus points if you catch the scent of mimosa or lavender drifting through the streets. LEA

blocks.heading: Wines & Delicacies at Domaine de Souviou
blocks.text: In the heart of Bandol wine country, Domaine de Souviou serves up Provençal hospitality with a side of terroir. Walk the estate, learn its history, then dig into a buffet of local fare — meats, cheeses, salads and rosé. Afterward, stroll the cobbled streets of Le Castellet, a fortified village perched for maximum photo ops and boutique browsing. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Marseille – The Phocean City
blocks.text: Dive into Marseille’s old-world energy with a walking tour through the Vieux Port. After time to explore on your own, hop on the coach for a sightseeing ride past Marseille Cathedral, Villa Méditerranée and Palais Longchamps. Climb to Notre Dame de La Garde for panoramic views of this cultural capital, where the Mediterranean sparkles and history refuses to take a backseat. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Afternoon: Toulon Bay Cruise and Walking Tour
blocks.text: Get two views of Toulon: by boat and by foot. Start with a scenic cruise around the Bay of Toulon, past the naval base and beaches, with a glass of Bandol rosé in hand. Back on land, walk through La Seyne-sur-Mer with your guide, visit Sainte-Marie-de-la-Seds Cathedral and explore Liberty Square. It’s a mellow way to meet the city that’s more than just a port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Toulon
blocks.text: Choose your pace: city‑splurge, village charm or coastal wine‑and‑waves. Princess Cruises to Toulon provides the curated excursion options you crave.

blocks.heading: Wines & Delicacies at Domaine de Souviou
blocks.text: Here’s a day made for your tastebuds and your soul. Begin at Domaine de Souviou in Bandol, where you’ll wander the estate, toast wine, shovel in olive oil‑drizzled plates and quietly celebrate that you saved your appetite for this. Then you’ll meander to Le Castellet — a hill‑top village so intoxicating it should come with a warning sign. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Marseille - The Phocean City
blocks.text: Wander the old harbor of Marseille. From the Vieux Port you’ll zigzag through medieval alleys, snap a pose at Notre‑Dame de la Garde and grin at the grandeur of Palais Longchamps. Lunch is yours to commandeer — pick a terrace, order something chic (or messy) and relish being in France without the Paris price tag. If you don’t buy a beret how can you prove you were here? LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Provence
blocks.text: Escape inland to Aix‑en‑Provence where Cézanne once painted. Your guide will parade you through the stately Mazarin Quarter while you try to look casually rich among 17th‑century mansions. Then you’re off to the Old Town with free time that begs you to sip, shop or simply stare at plaster‑pink facades. Don’t be surprised when your train of thought gets derailed and just says ‘wow.’ LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Bormes-les-Mimosas & Hyeres
blocks.text: Brace yourself for village charm turned up to onze. In Bormes‑les‑Mimosas you’ll breathe in flower‑filled lanes and drink in views of Lavandou Bay like it’s your favorite beverage. Then you roll into Hyères, the Riviera’s vintage resort where palm trees dapple the ground and cafés spill laughter in Provençal sun. Expect boutiques, food and the kind of free time that makes you forget you have a lif

blocks.heading: St. Tropez on Your Own
blocks.text: St. Tropez: What was once a humble fishing port is now a runway for mega‑yachts and sun‑lit adventure. You’ll get a guided intro, then you’re set loose. Cafe‑hop at the Vieux Port and browse boutiques that might make you want to start a line of credit. Or just park yourself with an iced drink and watch the harbour do its thing. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Afternoon: Toulon Bay Cruise and Walking Tour
blocks.text: Start with a boat ride across Toulon Bay (waves, naval ships, beach‑front villages), all with a glass of chilled Bandol rosé because you earned it. Then it’s boots on land: a walking tour of the National Navy Museum and a wander into Liberty Square. It’s educational and indulgent, making it a perfect guilt-free day ashore. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Trieste (for Venice)
Shore excursions to explore in Trieste
blocks.text: Trieste serves as a gateway to both Italian charm and cross‑border adventures. Shore excursions let you discover historic castles, sea cliffs, inland wonders and wine‑country culture to get a different taste of Adriatic and Central‑European heritage.

blocks.heading: Lipica Stud Farm & Horse Performance
blocks.text: Visit the historic Lipica Stud Farm, home of the famed Lipizzaner horses, where you can tour stables, meet majestic white stallions, and enjoy a classical riding demonstration. It’s a graceful blend of equestrian tradition and pastoral beauty. This is a standout experience for animal lovers and culture seekers alike. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Slovenia
blocks.text: This full‑day excursion takes you across the border to Slovenia’s capital for a guided walking tour of historic neighborhoods, charming streets and cultural landmarks, Experience a seamless blend of Mediterranean energy and Central European character that shows a completely different face of Trieste’s region. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Aquileia & Redipuglia
blocks.text: Travel inland to the ancient Roman city of Aquileia, once a major Mediterranean port, then visit the Redipuglia War Memorial, a moving monument honoring thousands of World War I soldiers. Explore archaeological ruins, historic streets, and a sobering piece of European history. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Caves of Postumia
blocks.text: Head into Slovenia’s karst landscape for a guided visit to Postojna Cave, a spectacular limestone cave system carved over millions of years. Ride a train through vast underground chambers, marvel at dramatic stalactites and stalagmites, and experience one of Europe’s most impressive subterranean wonders. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Castles of Trieste & Wine Tasting
blocks.text: Explore the elegant coastline and aristocratic past of Trieste with a visit to historic castles and coastal estates. Then enjoy a wine tasting featuring regional Friuli‑Venezia Giulia vintages, the perfect pairing of history, scenic views and local flavors for travelers who appreciate the finer sides of the Adriatic. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Panoramic Slovenian Coast & Farmer’s Market
blocks.text: Drive along the Adriatic’s scenic coastline into Slovenia and discover a relaxed coastal lifestyle. Wander vibrant markets where locals sell fresh produce, sample regional specialties, and soak in coastal views. This is a laid‑back, authentic escape that highlights the cultural bridge between Italy and Slovenia. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Tromsø
blocks.text: These aren’t your run‑of–the‑mill tours. Each one is a wild beat in the Arctic heart. What’s on your bucket list — frost, fur, fjord or folklore?

blocks.heading: Experience Sami Culture and Reindeer Feeding
blocks.text: Venture through tundra roads into Sami lands, hand-feed reindeer, hear legends under wide sky. Wrap it with a visit to Arctic Cathedral, where stone and glass echo cold light. Personal, quiet, elemental — and did we mention the reindeer feeding? I mean, we did, but it’s worth reiterating. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Scenic RIB Adventure
blocks.text: Hop aboard a RIB (rigid inflatable boat) and slice through Tromsø’s frigid fjord waters. Your captain will drop throttle for tight turns, cliff closeups and wild anecdotes. Watch for eagles, porpoises or WWII wreck markers near Håkøya. It’s speed, sea, stories and spray — all woven into one blistering half-day. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Polaria Arctic Center, Arctic Cathedral & Museum
blocks.text: Cross the Tromsø Bridge, enter the angular arches of the Arctic Cathedral, then step inside Polaria to meet bearded seals and explore Arctic exhibits. Finish at Tromsø Museum — ancient artifacts, Viking relics, arctic culture displays — a sharp stroll through heritage and habitat. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Tromsø Highlights and Cable Car
blocks.text: You’ll tour historic streets, modern architecture and cultural anchors before riding the cable car to Mt. Storsteinen (when open). From that raised vantage, the city recedes, and a sort of fjord/island patchwork takes over. Dramatic, crisp… unforgettable. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Charm and Beauty of Sommarøy Island
blocks.text: Travel out to Sommarøy, a remote set of isles where tide, sky and salt reign. Walk quiet lanes, visit memorials, breathe fjord air and photograph cliff edges and sea foam. Return to Tromsø feeling you’ve touched the Arctic edge of the world. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Polar Museum & Husky Wilderness Camp
blocks.text: Drive out to Kvaløya, where you’ll meet sprinting Alaskan huskies and see their lives in the Arctic wild. Then return to Tromsø Museum, housed in a 19th-century warehouse, to walk through tales of polar conquest — tents, skis, instruments and more than a few old weapons. History meets paws and purpose. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Trondheim
blocks.text: Some cities feel like they were designed. Trondheim feels like it was sketched out on a vellum scroll by a medieval architect with a flair for drama (and who somehow also knew how to optimize for tramways). Here, Viking lore lives next door to Gothic cathedrals, and your scenic hike might end at a ski jump. There’s grandeur, certainly — but with a side of curiosity that keeps you guessing.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Trondheim
blocks.text: Pick from Princess excursions that dig deep into local history, celebrate Norway’s musical soul and put you in the middle of landscapes that make you want to go throw back a mug of mead.

blocks.heading: Bymarka Hike
blocks.text: Nature lovers, lace up. After a city-skirting drive, this guided hike takes you through Bymarka’s forested trails to Gråkallen Hill. With small lakes, sweeping vistas and (on a good day) views into Sweden, this is peak Norway — literally. Bring water and your best sense of wonder. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Trondheim
blocks.text: Don a hard hat and descend into the depths of the Løkken copper mines, active from the 1600s through the 1980s. After this underground adventure, enjoy a hearty Norwegian buffet lunch before heading to Nidaros Cathedral for a photo stop. You’ll get a great mix of history, engineering and saintly stories — all in a day’s exploration. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Open-Air Folk Museum & Nidaros Cathedral
blocks.text: Wander through recreated 16th-century life at Sverresborg Folk Museum, where turf-roof houses and old tools tell rural tales. Then, step into the towering Nidaros Cathedral, built over the grave of Norway’s patron saint. It’s a double-dose of Norwegian culture, capped with city views from a scenic lookout. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Trondheim By Bike
blocks.text: Pedal your way through scenic Trondheim on a guided bike tour that passes fortress islands, colorful neighborhoods and cobbled alleys. Snap photos at Nidaros Cathedral and Bakklandet, and ride by the world’s only bicycle lift. Great for active guests who want equal parts scenery and stories, with a breeze to ruffle their hair (once the helmet comes off) LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Nidaros Cathedral & Archbishop's Palace
blocks.text: Take in Trondheim’s best-known landmarks with a walkable combo of soaring Gothic arches and royal artifacts. Nidaros Cathedral and the Archbishop’s Palace sit side by side, but their stories span centuries. Wrap up with a visit to the 17th-century Kristiansten Fortress and sweeping city views. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Classical Music Museum, Exclusive Recital & City Drive
blocks.text: Spend the morning with musical legends at the Ringve Museum, home to more than 2,000 instruments. After a live recital and bubbly toast, you’ll swing by Nidaros Cathedral and glide past scenic sights like the old town bridge. It’s like a symphony of sightseeing. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Trondheim By Street Car & Coach
blocks.text: Hop on the Gråkallbanen streetcar for a nostalgic ride to the edge of Trondheim’s green belt. Then switch to a motorcoach for a relaxed tour past Nidaros Cathedral, colorful houses and the famed Old Town Bridge. You’ll see Trondheim the way locals do: laid-back and full of character. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Bakklandet Walking Tour & City Drive
blocks.text: Start with a city drive and a panoramic stop at Kristiansten Fortress, then stroll the charming lanes of Bakklandet. Wooden houses, boutique shops and the quirky bike lift offer photo ops galore. Cross the historic City Bridge en route to Nidaros Cathedral. You’ll finish with lots of steps and even more stories. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Trondheim port on your next cruise
blocks.text: It’s not every day you step off a ship and immediately feel like you’ve wandered into a Scandinavian epic poem. Trondheim delivers that kind of energy. The buildings are bold, the streets are walkable and the locals somehow manage to be both laid-back and impeccably efficient. It’s the kind of port that makes a Transatlantic or European cruise a major bucket-list item. There’s no script — just see

Ships sailing to Trondheim
blocks.text: After a day of cathedral climbs and fjord breezes, your Princess ship is the ideal place to recharge. Think late-night bites, balcony sunsets and entertainment that doesn’t stop just because the sun went down. It’s comfort with a view — and then some.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Valletta
blocks.text: Valletta rises from stone and sea, shaped by Roman, Arabic and British influence. Inside the walls, Baroque facades and narrow streets lead to cocktail bars like Ting Tong, where vintage photos and old-school drinks nod to the city’s wilder nights. Malta’s landscape flips between white cliffs, turquoise lagoons and ancient ruins, with Comino Island offering standout swims. As one of Europe's best

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Valletta
blocks.text: Whether you’re thirsty for temples older than Rome or want to drift through fortified towns, these tours touch every layer of Malta.

blocks.heading: Vittoriosa & Mdina
blocks.text: Your day begins inside Vittoriosa, exploring fort gates, palatial courtyards, the Inquisitor’s Palace and painted churches. Next is Mdina, with its ramparts, Knight’s Museum and sweeping views. Historic scenes and architectural contrasts mingle freely throughout, ending with rich lunch and quiet transition back to ship dock. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ultimate Three Islands
blocks.text: You begin by skimming the Maltese coast by motorboat — past Comino’s caves, over St. Paul’s Island and Mellieha Bay. Then cross to Gozo and pile into 4x4s for off-road terrain, dramatic cliffs, historic domes and unspoiled views. Lunch, swimming, rugged beauty and heritage all wrapped into one marathon day. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Mdina On Your Own
blocks.text: A 30‑minute drive delivers you to Mdina, a fortress city of shadows, narrow alleys and hushed awe. Within its walls you’ll find medieval dwellings, the ornate St. Paul’s Cathedral, Palazzo Falson and underground catacombs. With a self‑paced path, you set the rhythm for pause, discovery and delicious pastizzi sampling. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: History in Stone
blocks.text: Travel by motorcoach to Ħaġar Qim, then continue to the Tarxien Temples, where ancient carved stones, spiral motifs and altar fragments still endure. Your final stop: Ghar Dalam cave, home to extinct animal remains and prehistoric artifacts layered beneath its earthen floor. This tour reads like a history (or pre-history) textbook you can tactually live. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Hal Saflieni Hypogeum & Tarxien Temples
blocks.text: You’ll descend into Hal Saflieni Hypogeum, an underground necropolis with chambers carved into rock over millennia. Only a few dozen visitors gain access daily, but you’ll experience its Oracle Room, Snake Pit and decorated chambers. Then explore Tarxien’s open temple ruins overhead with their carved reliefs and grand stone architecture. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Island Drive – Vittoriosa & Marsaxlokk Village
blocks.text: This relaxed drive is for the curious with minimal walking. You’ll pass Vittoriosa’s fortifications, waterfront views of Grand Harbour and Senglea creeks, then continue to Marsaxlokk to browse the fishing village, markets and local fare. Visit Ta’ Qali crafts and sample Maltese pastries at a scenic stop. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Marsaxlokk and Malta National Aquarium for Families
blocks.text: Begin in MSaxlokk’s colorful harbor and bubbling market life, then explore nearby coastal villages, the Blue Grotto and dramatic Dingli Cliffs. The highlight: the Malta National Aquarium, where over 175 species are on display in immersive environments. After lunch and marine magic, return to Valletta with seaside views and new favorites. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Malta’s Treasures for Small Groups
blocks.text: This immersive outing navigates Valletta’s Upper Barrakka Gardens, Castille Palace and St. John’s Co‑Cathedral exterior. Then it moves to Rabat for local flavors and Mdina’s mighty ramparts and hidden alleys. Finish in Mosta to confront a miraculous church that survived wartime destruction. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Valletta port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Valletta sits right where past and present collide, with sandstone streets, seaside forts and a harbor that’s seen more than its share of history. You’ll dock near the heart of it all, so it’s easy to walk straight into grand cathedrals, palace courtyards and sweeping views over the Mediterranean. blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Vigo
blocks.text: Vigo offers an unforgettable gateway to Galicia’s treasures, from sacred pilgrimage sites to breathtaking coastal views. Whether you’re exploring historic Santiago de Compostela or savoring fresh seafood by the sea, every shore excursion reveals a new side of Spain’s vibrant northwest.

blocks.heading: Cíes Islands Nature Reserve
blocks.text: Sail by catamaran to the stunning Cíes Nature Preserve, part of the Atlantic Islands of Galicia National Park. Relax on the scenic cruise before arriving at Monteagudo Island and world-famous Rodas Beach — once named the best beach in the world. Spend three blissful hours swimming, sunbathing or hiking to the Alto do Príncipe viewpoint for breathtaking coastal views. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Santiago de Compostela
blocks.text: Journey to Santiago de Compostela, one of the world’s most famous pilgrimage sites, to visit the magnificent St. James Cathedral. Explore its ornate Romanesque and Baroque details and fascinating museum before enjoying lunch at the historic Parador Hostal de los Reyes Católicos. Afterwards, wander the surrounding squares for unique souvenirs and soak in centuries of spiritual and architectural spl

blocks.heading: Gourmet Galicia
blocks.text: Set sail on a full-day adventure through Galicia’s stunning coast, beginning with a catamaran cruise around the Bay of Vigo. Savor fresh mussels, savory pie and a glass of crisp Albariño wine before docking in the medieval village of Bayona. Enjoy lunch at the historic Parador Conde de Gondomar, then explore the charming town before cruising back to Vigo. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Vigo Scenic Drive
blocks.text: Take in the best of Vigo on a scenic journey through its highlights. Begin atop El Castro Hill with sweeping views of the bay, then explore Castrelos Park and the elegant 17th-century Quinones de Leon Palace. Conclude your tour at the luxurious Pazo Los Escudos Hotel, savoring Galician tapas and wine as you enjoy breathtaking seaside vistas before returning to your ship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Agro De Bazan Winery & Spanish Wine Tasting
blocks.text: Immerse yourself in Galicia’s celebrated Albariño wine country on this half-day tour to the renowned Agro de Bazan Winery. Enjoy a guided tasting of three signature wines, each showcasing unique notes of fruit and fennel, before visiting the charming village of Cambados. At the elegant Parador de Cambados, savor regional wines and tapas in a beautifully restored 17th-century manor. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Bayona La Real
blocks.text: Discover Bayona, a charming seaside village brimming with history and coastal beauty. Enjoy a scenic drive to El Castro Hill for panoramic views of Vigo Bay, then savor coffee and snacks at the Parador Conde de Gondomar within the ancient Monte Real Fortress. Stroll through Bayona’s cobbled Old Quarters, visit historic landmarks and enjoy free time to shop or explore. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Visby
blocks.text: Visby feels like a time capsule, framed by Ringmuren — a 13th‑century town wall that hugs the medieval core. Roses climb rubble, spires puncture the skyline and cafés spill into narrow alleys. Here you’ll find Viking history, Gothic ruins, pastoral farms and coastal charm all wrapped in ancient stone.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Visby
blocks.text: Each tour peels back a layer of Visby — from medieval architecture to pastoral fields. Choose the one that matches your mood, be it rugged, relaxed or somewhere weirdly in between.

blocks.heading: Easy Visby
blocks.text: If your style leans more toward ‘sit and see,’ this relaxed motorcoach tour delivers sweeping scenic views with minimal walking. Cruise past Ringmuren, roll through the storybook streets of Visby and stop at Almedalen’s grassy harborside. The route continues past Visby Hospital and up to Gallows Hill, where stone pillars from Europe’s last known gallows offer a haunting silhouette against the Balt

blocks.heading: Best of Visby: Island Drive & Museum
blocks.text: Ride through Visby’s narrow alleys, slip through Almedalen’s harborside past historical towers, then dive into the Gotlands Fornsal Museum to absorb 8,000 years of local heritage. After that, motor through the countryside and stop at rural medieval churches before reaching Gnisvärd to gape at the ship‑shaped stone graves. Return to port with your camera memory full. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: A Taste of Gotland
blocks.text: Start by sampling local delicacies at Tofta Lodge & Beach Resort, then visit Ansarve Farm to meet sheep, jam makers and rural artisans. Finally, wander Visby’s rose‑cloaked lanes with a guide who’ll point out ruins, alleys and local culture details others miss. Eat it. Experience it. Wish you never had to leave it. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Biking in Visby
blocks.text: Grab your helmet and ride. This 2½‑hour cycling tour winds through Almedalen, passes the Kruttornet and Maiden’s Tower and then climbs toward Högklint for panoramic scenic views over sea and stone. You’ll also pedal through Botanical Gardens, coastal edges and countryside routes, finishing back in town with your bike‑legs humming. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Highlights of Visby: A Town of Roses & Ruins
blocks.text: Visit Almedalen, see Powder Tower and Fisherman’s Gate, motor along the coast to Gallows Hill with its haunting pillars and enter the old town via Dalmansporten. On foot you’ll wander cobbled lanes up to St. Mary Church and town viewpoints that frame these ruins against the Baltic. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Medieval Visby & Surroundings
blocks.text: Begin at Gallows Hill, then walk through Dalmansporten gate into the heart of Visby. Visit St. Mary Church and the harbor at Almedalen. After the walking portion, motor through rural lanes to photograph medieval church remnants and finally see Gnisvärd, with its ghost‑ship stones standing against wind and waves. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Visby on Foot
blocks.text: Step off near Ringmuren, cross a bridge into the medieval lane network and pass past ruins, red‑rosed cottages and St. Mary Church. You’ll walk through Fisherman’s Gate, climb to a viewpoint, drop into the Botanical Garden and catch Almedalen before returning to your ship. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Visby Hop On Hop Off Sightseeing
blocks.text: Let the double‑decker bus handle the driving while you absorb Visby’s essence. Hop off at Ringmuren, medieval ruins, churches and the botanical gardens. Snap photos, grab a saffron pancake and slip back on whenever you’re ready. You’re in charge, just don’t expect them to let you steer. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Experience the Visby port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Visby cruise docking drops you almost within the embrace of Ringmuren itself. Step off and you’re inside a living medieval stage. This port along the Baltic & Scandinavian and European cruise routes is compact; local walking routes lead you through alleys, rose‑thick yards and toward Almedalen’s scenic waterfront. From here, historic stones, sea sprays and layered culture are your constant compani

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Zeebrugge & Bruges
blocks.text: Choose the adventure that satisfies your curiosity: Belgian war history, chocolate & beer, canals or countryside castles. Each tour speaks a different dialect of Belgium.

blocks.heading: The Flemish Countryside & Castle of Loppem
blocks.text: Start in Damme, stroll its medieval square and see the Church of Our Ladies. Then head to Loppem Castle, admiring Gothic Revival towers, arched windows and landscaped gardens. Meander over quiet bridges and forested walks before returning to Zeebrugge, having drifted through both fairy-tale towns and peaceful countryside LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Brussels
blocks.text: You’ll see Brussels from crown to courtyard. Start with Laeken Castle, snap the Atomium, then head into the Old City: Grand Place, Baroque guild façades, the Town Hall and Manneken‑Pis. Lunch is yours in the heart of the city, followed by time to shop Belgian chocolate or browse lace boutiques before returning to Zeebrugge. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ypres, In Flanders Fields Museum & Bruges
blocks.text: Begin in solemn reflection at Tyne Cot Cemetery, then pause at the Menin Gate Memorial. Head into the Flanders Field Museum for wartime narratives, before transferring to Bruges. There, visit canals, admire the Belfry and pass through historic squares. Return to Zeebrugge after a layered day of memory, beauty and contrast. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Bruges, Ghent & Canal Cruise
blocks.text: Your day begins on a canal ride through Ghent, giving you water-level views of medieval facades and quiet lanes. Then you’ll arrive in Bruges to see the Belfry Tower, St. Bavo’s Cathedral, the Basilica of the Holy Blood and Gothic town squares. Enjoy local eats and weave in quiet shopping before the return trip. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Bruges Highlights & Time On Your Own
blocks.text: This tour blends guided and independent time. Walk with a guide through Bruges’ striking squares, see the Belfry, Church of Our Lady, Guild Halls and canals. Then take a relaxing canal cruise before being left to wander quaint lanes, snack cafés and shops on your own — until it’s time to reboard. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Bruges & Belgian Chocolates
blocks.text: Start with a guided tour past Bruges’ historic icons, including the Belfry, Guild Halls and Church of Our Lady. Then shift gears into chocolate mode: a demo reveals cocoa-to-confection secrets, followed by a tasting. You’ll finish with free time to explore local chocolatiers, boutiques or get one last waffle fix before heading back. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Bruges & Beer Tasting
blocks.text: Walk past the Belfry, Town Hall and the Basilica of the Holy Blood, all wrapped in old-world atmosphere. Your guide then leads you to a cozy tavern for a tasting of Belgian beers. Sip, savor, chat, then rejoin the group and return to Zeebrugge — with both architecture and local flavors lingering in your senses.

blocks.heading: A Walking Tour of Bruges
blocks.text: Travel by coach through Flemish countryside to Bruges. Once there, your guide walks you through Burg Square, past Basilica, Belfry Tower, Gothic churches and narrow alleyways. Exploration time follows, during which you can dive into chocolate shops or enjoy waffle stands. Return to Zeebrugge enriched with architecture, history and flavor. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Zeebrugge port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Zeebrugge is the entrance to both medieval magic and European power. Dock here and you'll step into excursions toward Bruges’ canals, Brussels’ institutions or Flanders’ landscapes. For Baltic & Scandinavian or European cruise itineraries, Zeebrugge offers an ideal balance: deep history without losing access to modern city pulse.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Glasgow
blocks.text: Glasgow has a way of surprising people. One minute you’re standing in a medieval cathedral, the next you’re sipping a whisky in a lively pub or browsing bold modern art. It’s a city that feels both historic and fresh, and that mix is what makes exploring here so memorable.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Glasgow
blocks.text: Some places just have it all, and when you join Princess on cruises to Glasgow, you can see it all on our incredible excursions. Castles, cathedrals, highlands and lochs await.

blocks.heading: Glengoyne Distillery & Whisky Tasting
blocks.text: Nestled at the edge of the Highlands, Glengoyne has been distilling since 1833. Learn how its slow, peat-free process creates a whisky known for subtlety, then taste the results yourself. With every sip, you’ll discover why Scotch is called the “water of life.” LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of the Scottish Highlands
blocks.text: The Highlands feel like a painting come to life with its dramatic glens, shimmering lochs and stone villages tucked into the hills. Step inside Inveraray Castle, where centuries of history echo in its grand halls, then pause for a traditional country lunch. Along the way, you’ll find photo stops and views that will stay with you long after you sail away. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Loch Lomond Cruise & Scenic Drive
blocks.text: Scotland’s largest loch invites you to slow down. Drift past wooded islands and Victorian homes as the water mirrors the surrounding hills. Hear tales of Inchmurrin’s ancient ruins before browsing at Loch Lomond Shores, where modern shops sit against a backdrop of timeless scenery. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Edinburgh
blocks.text: Edinburgh mixes storybook charm with royal grandeur. Wander cobbled streets where history clings to every stone, then look up to see the mighty castle crowning the city. Inside, treasures like the Scottish Crown Jewels await, but so does time to simply soak in the energy of the Royal Mile. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Exploring Inveraray & the Highlands
blocks.text: Stone cottages, castle towers and lochs shimmering in the distance — this is the Highlands at their most inviting. Linger in the storybook village of Luss, then follow the road to Inveraray Castle, where portraits, tapestries and a vast armory bring Scotland’s past into focus. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Culzean Castle & Ayr
blocks.text: Clinging to cliffs above the Firth of Clyde, Culzean Castle looks like something from a romantic novel. Its ornate interiors and sweeping sea views make every corner worth exploring. Nearby Ayr adds a modern twist — a seaside town where Scottish woolens and cozy cafés invite you to linger. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Glasgow Cathedral & Kelvingrove Gallery
blocks.text: Glasgow Cathedral’s soaring stone vaults are a rare medieval survivor, where light filters through centuries of stained glass. Just across the city, Kelvingrove Art Gallery offers a different kind of wonder: 22 themed galleries packed with treasures ranging from Renaissance paintings to natural history. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Glasgow port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Your ship docks at Greenock, a welcoming port just 25 miles west of Glasgow. From here, the city’s museums, architecture and music scene are within easy reach, while the Highlands and castles lie just beyond. It’s also a perfect starting point to explore more of the British Isles or even wider Europe, with itineraries that weave together history, culture and unforgettable scenery.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Inverness
blocks.text: If ‘Capital of the Highlands’ sounds dramatic, wait until you hit the excursions. Castles with ghost stories, monster hunts, royal retreats and boat rides across lochs that may or may not contain prehistoric celebrities.

blocks.heading: Easy Loch Ness Scenic Cruise
blocks.text: A boat ride over the impenetrable depths and murky darkness of Lock Ness? Time to test your Highland courage. What are the chances you’ll actually encounter a monster anyway? And back on shore you can compare ‘fish’ tales in scenic Inverness. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Meet the Gardener at Cawdor Castle
blocks.text: Shakespeare’s MacBeth made Cawdor Castle famous, but the gardens make it gorgeous. Meet one of the estate’s expert gardeners, who’ll spill secrets about maintaining Scotland’s top-ranked gardens. After your behind-the-scenes stroll, step inside to admire the castle’s interiors. It’s history and horticulture (just ignore any ghostly floating daggers you might encounter). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Highlights of Loch Ness & Urquhart Castle Ruins
blocks.text: Few things say ‘Scotland’ quite like a castle crumbling on the edge of a loch that allegedly houses a monster. Urquhart Castle’s walls and keep still stand guard over the brooding waters of Loch Ness, and the visitor center fills in the history. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Best of the Scottish Highlands
blocks.text: Here’s the cheat code to the Highlands: Cawdor Castle, Loch Ness, Urquhart Castle and Inverness. You’ll get them all, one after another, with lunch thrown in so you don’t faint from historical overload. Macbeth’s murder site? Check. Monster sightings? Maybe. Centuries of blood-soaked clan history? Absolutely. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Invergordon by Private Vehicle - Van Class Full Day (With Guide)
blocks.text: If you’re more “I’ll make my own tour, thanks,” then this private van gives you the wheel (figuratively) and a guide. Perfect if you’ve got a list longer than your arm or simply want Scotland all to yourself for a day. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Inverness On Your Own
blocks.text: Spend a half day tossing yourself into the ‘Capital of the Highlands’ with no guide, no schedule and no one to stop you from buying that entire kilt outfit you’ve always wanted. Inverness packs Old Town charm, a Victorian Market with plenty of quirks and a castle perched on the River Ness like it’s still waiting for trouble. Add in a pint and you’ve got Scotland handled. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Queen Mother’s Castle of Mey
blocks.text: Once known as Barrogill Castle, this 16th-century estate became the Queen Mother’s summer escape. Touring its rooms feels less like visiting a museum and more like stepping into someone’s very posh holiday home (just don’t let anyone catch you napping in the master bedroom). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Dunrobin Castle
blocks.text: If Versailles and a Highland fortress had a baby, it would look a lot like Dunrobin Castle. Dating back to the 1300s, it’s still dripping with grandeur thanks to the Sutherland family. Explore its state apartments and vibrant nurseries, and lose yourself in gardens inspired by (but never limited to) French aesthetics. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Invergordon port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Here’s the insider tip: British Isles and European cruises to Inverness actually dock in Invergordon, a small town about 45 minutes away. But that’s no drawback — the port’s well connected with trains, buses, and tours that zip you straight into the action. blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Lanzarote
blocks.text: From volcanic landscapes to seaside towns, our shore excursions highlight the best of Lanzarote without the stress of planning. We’ll take care of the details so you can focus on soaking it all in.

blocks.heading: Timanfaya National Park & Camel Ride
blocks.text: Step into another world at Timanfaya National Park, where camel rides carry you past black lava fields and jagged craters. The journey continues to La Geria, Lanzarote’s wine valley, where vines thrive in volcanic ash. Sample the island’s distinctive Malvasía wine before returning through landscapes shaped by centuries of eruptions. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Arrecife
blocks.text: This full-day tour has it all, from the most exciting experience in the volcano. Ride camels at Timanfaya National Park, sip local Malvasía wine in La Geria and enjoy a traditional lunch in Haría. Then, marvel at sweeping views from Mirador del Río before exploring Jameos del Agua, an underground world of gardens and pools. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Craters, Lava Tubes & Cactus Gardens
blocks.text: Experience César Manrique’s creative legacy on this half-day tour. Walk through Jameos del Agua, where lava tubes have been turned into gardens, pools and an auditorium. Continue to Jardín de Cactus, home to more than 10,000 plants, and pause at Mirador del Río for panoramic ocean views. The tour concludes at El Castillo de San José, a fortress reborn as a modern art museum. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Jameos del Agua & the Valley of a Thousand Palms
blocks.text: Travel into northern Lanzarote to Haría, known as the Valley of a Thousand Palms. A winding drive offers dramatic views of cliffs and the island’s highest peak before reaching Mirador del Río for a sweeping coastal panorama. Continue to Jameos del Agua, a volcanic tunnel transformed into a cultural center with gardens and a turquoise pool set within lava rock. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Lanzarote Wine Route
blocks.text: Indulge in the flavors of Lanzarote on a tour of its celebrated wine region. Visit bodegas in La Geria; the vines are carefully cultivated in volcanic ash. Taste the island’s signature Malvasía wines and pause at the Monumento al Campesino, Manrique’s homage to the agricultural traditions that define Lanzarote’s cultural identity. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Puerto del Carmen Beach Getaway for Families
blocks.text: Spend a leisurely day in Puerto del Carmen, Lanzarote’s most popular resort town. Relax on Playa Grande, a wide stretch of Blue Flag beach with calm Atlantic waters perfect for swimming. Enjoy over three hours of free time to shop, dine or simply soak in the sun along the lively promenade. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in the Shetland Islands
blocks.text: This isn’t some cozy Scottish village with polite charm. Lerwick is the real deal — sea-lashed, windbitten and proud of it. When you land here, you’re stepping into 5,000 years of salt and unconquerable human tenacity.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Shetland Islands
blocks.text: Shetland surprises in the best way — rugged landscapes wrapped around a community that loves to celebrate. From Lerwick, its small but spirited capital, you’ll find festivals, music and traditions woven into everyday life. These excursions bring you into the heart of that culture and the wild scenery that inspires it.

blocks.heading: Scalloway & Shetland Ponies
blocks.text: History with side-eye. See Scalloway Castle and the museum that tracks everything from Norse immigrations to Nazi resistance. Then go meet the Shetland ponies — sturdy, shaggy, completely uninterested in your selfie. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Southernmost Shetland – Sumburgh Head
blocks.text: Drive the coast, watch the sea get rougher and the cliffs get steeper. Then hike around Sumburgh Head, home to Scotland’s oldest lighthouse and thousands of screeching seabirds. Puffins, maybe dolphins? Maybe whales? No guarantees — just the wild doing its thing. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Jarlshof Ruins & Hoswick Visitors’ Centre
blocks.text: Get lost in layered time. Start with the Jarlshof Ruins — Bronze Age through Viking era. Then head to Hoswick, where weaving looms, local lore and art combine in a quiet, powerful celebration of Shetland’s daily life. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The UK’s “Top” Fish And Chips
blocks.text: Grab a hot plate of vinegar-drenched pride at Da Haaf in Scalloway. The fish comes straight from the Shetland waters, the stories from folks who’ve worked them. You’ll eat well and leave full of grease and knowledge. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Nature Walk of Mousa Island
blocks.text: This island doesn’t have residents. It has brochs, seals, seabirds and whatever mood the sea’s in that day. After a short ferry ride, take the long way around — past storm petrels, over turf trails and up into the oldest tower you’ll probably ever climb. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Northernmost Scotland
blocks.text: Drive north past Mavis Grind, where you can throw a rock between two oceans. Stop at Tangwick Haa Museum for a look at Shetland’s past lives, then walk Eshaness cliffs where the wind slaps you into the present. Lighthouses, laird houses and sharp air — you’ll feel all of it. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Shetland: Scenic Western Drive
blocks.text: If you like your drama slow-burn, this is your ride. Moors, lochs, medieval castles and Norse-style jewelry workshops, all stitched together with landscape that shifts between eerie and serene. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: WILDLIFE SAFARI
blocks.text: Step aboard a catamaran and cruise past cliffs where seabirds stage full-volume nesting wars. Look out for seals, gannets, puffins and rock arches the sea hasn’t swallowed yet. Bring binoculars because these locals fly fast. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Lerwick port on your next cruise
blocks.text: When your British Isles or European cruise anchors offshore in the Shetland Islands cruise, you’ll board tenders that whisk you to Victoria Pier near downtown Lerwick. Some smaller ships dock directly at Holmsgarth or Mair’s Pier, and free shuttle buses carry guests the rest of the way. Stepping onto the quay, you'll find the town compact, walkable and ready with shops, culture, sea air and that s

blocks.text: In lands where the culture is as flavorful as the cuisine, the splendor of the Mediterranean speaks for itself.

blocks.text: Visions of sparkling coasts and crystalline waters welcome you to the Mediterranean. Dip your toes on the black-sand coast of Santorini on a Greek cruise. Head to Salerno to spend the day in Positano relaxing on the white beaches and admiring the pastel houses that decorate the cliffs around you. blocks.heading: World-class dining
blocks.text: With mouthwatering entrees and confections, the Mediterranean invites you to embark on a gourmet tour through iconic cities. Reawaken your taste buds with Italian classics like pastas, pizzas and gelato. Or fill your plate with gyros, keftethes and baklava on a Greek cruise. From breakfast to dinner and every delectable dessert in between, the best is before you with Princess.

blocks.heading: Rich wines
blocks.text: The countryside of Italy and Greece are home to some of the most flavorful wines around the globe. With sun and warm temperatures year-round, vineyards are flourishing with grapes by the harvest season. Sip on Italy’s red wines, or sample Greece’s white blends. From sweet Lambruscos to earthy Bordeauxs, fill up your glass on a Mediterranean cruise with Princess.

blocks.heading: Ancient ruins
blocks.text: From towers and temples to cities and shorelines, the Mediterranean is sprinkled with remains of civilizations past. Step back in time on a tour through ancient ruins on a Mediterranean cruise with Princess. Imagine life as a gladiator at the Colosseum, explore Greek mythology at the Parthenon and discover the archeological excavations of Pompeii — a lost city and UNESCO World Heritage Site.

blocks.heading: Art galleries & museums
blocks.text: From the treasures on land to the jewels within museums, the Mediterranean is a true work of art. On an Italian cruise, see portraits from the Renaissance period at the Uffizi Museum in Florence, and admire Michelangelo’s masterpieces at the Vatican Museum in Rome. blocks.heading: Celebrations & Romance
blocks.text: It's difficult to imagine something more romantic than sailing through the alluring cities and charming countryside of Europe. While on board your European cruise, we cater to your sentimental side with private dining on your balcony — like breakfast for two or a sunset dinner — honeymoon packages, flowers and chocolates delivered to your room and couples-only massages in the Sanctuary.

blocks.heading: Accommodations
blocks.text: Your stateroom is where you rest and recharge between adventures. That’s why every room is equipped with the expertly designed Princess Luxury Bed, 100% Jacquard-woven cotton linens. Whether you go interior or all-out in a suite, our staterooms will make you feel right at home. Especially for families traveling together who can enjoy the option of connected rooms.

blocks.heading: Celebrations & Romance
blocks.text: It's difficult to imagine something more romantic than sailing through the alluring cities and charming countryside of Europe. While on board your European cruise, we cater to your sentimental side with private dining on your balcony — like breakfast for two or a sunset dinner — honeymoon packages, flowers and chocolates delivered to your room and couples-only massages in the Sanctuary. Whether you go interior or all-out in a suite, our staterooms will make you feel right at home. Especially for families traveling together who can enjoy the option of connected rooms. Learn more

blocks.text: From savory Norwegian meatloaf to sweet Icelandic celebration cake, Northern Europe is bursting with flavor. Head ashore to enjoy Icelandic skyr with porridge for breakfast, and savor a Norwegian seafood dinner. Or embark on an all-encompassing culinary tour right on board with our Chef’s Table Lumiere. blocks.heading: Things to do in Ponta Delgada
Shore excursions to explore in Ponta Delgada
blocks.text: With volcanic lakes, lush gardens and geothermal valleys, São Miguel is the Azores’ crown jewel — and excursions from Ponta Delgada showcase its beauty.

blocks.heading: Crater Lakes, Sete Cidades & Wine Tasting
blocks.text: Sete Cidades’ volcanic caldera reveals two lakes, one green and one blue, fringed by steep crater walls. Stop at scenic lookouts, then descend to the village inside the crater. You’ll get a look at Santiago Lake before heading to a local hotel veranda for a wine tasting paired with island cheeses. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ribeira Grande, Terra Nostra Garden & Furnas Valley
blocks.text: Begin in Ribeira Grande, the island’s oldest town with 16th-century architecture. Stop at Pico do Ferro Belvedere for sweeping views of the Furnas Valley, then stroll Terra Nostra Gardens, known for its grottoes, hydrangeas and camellias. A traditional lunch with wine is included before exploring Furnas, where hot springs, fumaroles and mud pools showcase the island’s geothermal heart. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ribeira Grande & Pineapple Greenhouse
blocks.text: Travel across São Miguel's volcanic plateau to Ribeira Grande. Walk its cobbled streets lined with colonial buildings and pause at a local liqueur factory. Continue to Pico da Barrosa for views over Lagoa do Fogo, then visit a pineapple greenhouse to learn how the fruit thrives in volcanic soil. A gift shop offers pineapples, liqueurs and souvenirs to take home. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Crater Lakes, Gardens & Pineapple Greenhouse
blocks.text: Hit all of the best highlights of São Miguel on this half-day tour. Wander António Borges Botanical Gardens, filled with fern gullies and grottos, then drive to a volcanic rim for views over twin crater lakes, one green and one blue. Legends surround Sete Cidades, said to be the site of lost utopian cities. A pineapple greenhouse visit completes the experience. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Terra Nostra Gardens & Furnas Hot Springs
blocks.text: You can see the Ribeira Grande and the Terra Nostra Gardens, where lakes, streams and exotic flora surround thermal pools. Then go to Furnas Valley, where fumaroles vent steam and mineral waters bubble across the volcanic landscape. Here, you can learn how locals cook traditional dishes in geothermal heat. Don’t forget to stop at Pico do Ferro Belvedere for panoramic views before returning to port

blocks.heading: Things to do in Reykjavik
blocks.text: Reykjavik sits where volcanic drama and icy calm fight for the spotlight, and the city doesn’t feel the need to pick a winner. You’ll find hot springs that steam in the middle of nowhere, waterfalls that seem engineered for awe and streets that hum with cafes and culture. It’s a gateway to the wild but with plenty of city-life character of its own.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Reykjavik
blocks.text: These tours dig into the reasons outsiders say that Iceland feels like another planet — geysers, glaciers, lava fields and experiences that remind you of just how powerful nature can be.

blocks.heading: Lunar Landscapes & Viking World Museum
blocks.text: Drive across the Reykjanes peninsula, where geothermal fields vent steam and mud pools bubble in wild colors. Visit Viking World Museum to see a full-scale replica of a Viking longship and learn about the craft and voyages that shaped northern Europe. The trip ends at Valahnúkamöl, a dramatic stretch of cliff where waves crash against black rock. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Countless Craters by Helicopter
blocks.text: Take to the sky and trace Iceland’s volcanic scars from above. This one-hour flight sweeps you over steaming vents, fresh lava fields, crater lakes and the jagged coastline. From the Seltún geothermal area to the Blue Lagoon and the cone-shaped peak of Mount Keilir, it’s all on display. Your pilot shares the island’s volcanic backstory while you capture the kind of photos you can’t get from ground

blocks.heading: Lava Fields & Lobster Tails by 4WD
blocks.text: Trade smooth roads for rough trails as a 4x4 carries you past lakes, hot springs and wild geothermal fields. Stops include Krysuvik’s bubbling mud pools, the small Strandarkirkja church and Stokkseyri, where langoustine lobster is the star of a hearty lunch. The route back to Reykjavik crosses rivers and ridges, showing off a landscape that feels like it’s being constantly remade. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Glacier Walk & Waterfalls
blocks.text: Strap on crampons and head out onto Sólheimajökull glacier with an expert guide. You’ll see blue ice, deep crevasses and jagged formations that look like frozen waves. The day also includes visits to two of Iceland’s most photogenic waterfalls: Seljalandsfoss, which you can walk behind, and Skógafoss, a curtain of water that demands attention. It’s challenging but unforgettable. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Into the Blue Snorkeling Adventure
blocks.text: Float between continents in Thingvellir National Park. At the Silfra fissure, crystal-clear water lets you see nearly 300 feet down as you drift between the North American and Eurasian plates. Snorkeling gear and dry suits are provided, meaning only your hands and face touch the icy water. The result is otherworldly-yet-comfortable (and the bragging rights last forever). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of the Golden Circle & Icelandic Horse Show
blocks.text: See three of Iceland’s marquee sights in one full day: Thingvellir National Park, Gullfoss Waterfall and the geyser Strokkur (which erupts like clockwork). After lunch, watch the famously sturdy Icelandic horses perform. These small but powerful animals have been purebred for a thousand years, and their unique gait has to be seen up close to be believed. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Flyover Iceland Virtual Experience
blocks.text: Soar without leaving your seat at this immersive ride in downtown Reykjavik. A huge wraparound screen, moving platform and plenty of effects make you feel like you’re diving into craters, sweeping past glaciers and flying over cliffs. Before liftoff, you’ll hear Icelandic stories in a Viking-style longhouse — then buckle in for an unforgettable virtual ride across the island. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Bathing in the Sky Lagoon
blocks.text: Warmth, ocean views and open sky define this geothermal spa experience. Slip into steaming pools carved into the rocky shoreline, then cycle through a series of hot, cold and misty treatments designed to leave you relaxed and clear-headed. The Northern Lights might even join the show. LEARN MORE

blocks.text: The Reykjavik cruise port keeps things convenient. Your Iceland & Norway or European cruise itinerary will drop you off a short drive from downtown Reykjavik, where shops, museums and street art wait around every corner. blocks.text: From astounding fjords to astonishing palaces, the treasures of Scandinavia and Baltic region welcome you to explore.

blocks.heading: Deep-rooted sauna
blocks.text: Deep-rooted sauna culture of the Baltic region – often paired with a bracing polar plunge – a revitalizing tradition that dates back to the 13th century. More than a ritual, sauna is a way of life, valued for cleansing the body and mind, restoring balance, fostering deep relaxation, and the sharing of ideas, it remains a place where time slows and connections are strengthened, best experienced the

blocks.heading: Museums
blocks.text: Get up close to historical gems on a Baltic cruise with Princess. View ships and treasures found in royal burial mounds of the Oslo fjord at the Viking Ship Museum. Or learn what it’s like to be a prize winner at Stockholm's Nobel Peace Museum, and get up close to the world’s oldest preserved warship at the Vasa Museum

blocks.heading: Fjords & viking legends
blocks.text: A Baltic cruise is your key to the Norwegian Fjords — Mother Nature’s crown jewel. Upon arriving in Stockholm, ride along the brinks of Tyrifjord, a 52-mile inlet that boasts greenery and deep blue waters. Relax amidst the serenity of Oslo Fjord, and discover treasures from beneath its seas at the Viking Ship Museum. With Princess, sail to Scandinavia’s oldest capital and revel in the natural wond

blocks.heading: Unique architecture
blocks.text: Travel to lands where ancient architecture abounds. Wander the cobbled streets of Stockholm’s old town, Gamla Stan, one of the largest and best-preserved medieval city centers in Europe. Explore a treasure trove of late Renaissance and Rococo architecture in Copenhagen, like Rosenborg Castle, Kronborg Castle or Frederiksborg Castle. Or walk through 'Upper Old Town,' home to some of Tallin's oldest

blocks.heading: Comfort culture
blocks.text: A region renowned for exceptional quality of life, deeply rooted in the cultural philosophies of hygge and lagom. These guiding ideals emphasize balance, comfort, and intentional living – fostering environments where wellbeing, community connection, and harmony with nature are prioritized.

blocks.heading: Why cruise with Princess
blocks.text: Curated comfort, world-class entertainment and international flavors await you.

blocks.heading: Celebrations & Romance
blocks.text: It's difficult to imagine something more romantic than sailing through the alluring cities and charming countryside of Europe. While on board your European cruise, we cater to your sentimental side with private dining on your balcony — like breakfast for two or a sunset dinner — honeymoon packages, flowers and chocolates delivered to your room and couples-only massages in the Sanctuary.

blocks.heading: Accommodations
blocks.text: Your stateroom is where you rest and recharge between adventures. That’s why every room is equipped with the expertly designed Princess Luxury Bed, 100% Jacquard-woven cotton linens. Whether you go interior or all-out in a suite, our staterooms will make you feel right at home. Especially for families traveling together who can enjoy the option of connected rooms.

blocks.heading: Dining
blocks.text: From the spice of Moroccan tagine to the sweetness of Greek Baklava, Europe’s flavor profile is incredibly diverse. On a Transatlantic cruise with Princess, taste the best of Europe on board with specialty dining. Say cheers during a lively lunch at a British-style pub and try English favorites like bangers and mash or shepherd's pie. Or savor hearty Italian pastas at Sabatini’s℠ Italian Trattoria

blocks.heading: Entertainment
blocks.text: Embark on adventures by day, and indulge in entertainment by night. Watch Movies Under the Stars® at our 300-square-foot outdoor theater. Attend original productions from Broadway legend Stephen Schwartz, composer of Wicked. Or learn traditional moves, like flamenco or Irish stepdance, and listen to popular music from the destinations on your itinerary. On a European cruise with Princess, the choi

blocks.heading: Relaxation
blocks.text: Your European cruise should be every bit as refreshing as it is inspiring. Unwind in the Sanctuary, a retreat just for adults, and relish in tranquility. Or book an appointment at the Lotus Spa®. Enjoy soothing treatments — like facials, hot stone massages and detoxifying wraps — that will leave you energized for upcoming adventures.

blocks.heading: Casino
blocks.text: Experience the thrill of cards, dice, roulette, and blackjack at our onboard casino during your European cruise. Learn from our expert staff or seasoned guests, and put your skills to the test. For a more relaxed pace, enjoy the slot machines, or join fellow travelers for Bingo and exciting group tournaments. The casino promises nonstop excitement, whether you're a seasoned player or just playing

blocks.heading: Discover the stories behind every destination
blocks.text: Some places you visit. Others become stories you tell for years. Walk streets shaped by centuries of history, taste recipes passed down through generations and discover the people, traditions and unexpected moments that give each destination its character. With Princess shore excursions, you’ll experience the Europe you’ve always dreamed of — and discover stories you never knew you’d bring home.

blocks.heading: Experience natural wonders
blocks.text: Adventure through Mother Nature’s playground with any of our Europe shore excursions. Frolic among the lavender fields of Provence, where vibrant gardens fade into sapphire skies to create a pastel dreamland. Explore the basalt columns of the Giant's Causeway, considered to be the eighth wonder of the world. Or kayak along the Geirangerfjord, and glide past the mountains and waterfalls that surrou

blocks.heading: Iconic sightseeing on private tours
blocks.text: From Big Ben to the Leaning Tower of Pisa, Europe is home to some of the world’s most famous landmarks. With our Europe shore excursions, photograph the architectural elements inspired by nature in La Sagrada Familia in Barcelona. See Scotland’s Crown Jewels at Edinburgh Castle, and kiss the stone at Blarney Castle. Or ascend the Eiffel Tower, explore the Colosseum and toss a coin into the Trevi F

blocks.heading: Discover galleries, museums & more
blocks.text: From art galleries and museums to distilleries and pubs, Europe is painted in culture. At the Scotch Malt Whisky Society, sample local liquors and learn to play the bagpipes during our unique Europe cruise activities. Visit the Palace of Versailles and admire the 18th-century art that embellishes the halls. Or explore the Guggenheim Museum's changing exhibits of modern art from its expansive colle

blocks.heading: Sample local cuisine
blocks.text: Travel to destinations where the food is as rich as the cultures and history within them. Stroll along the streets of Naples, and taste pizza in the land where it was not only created, but also perfected. Or journey to a bed and breakfast in the Irish countryside where you can bake scones and sip tea alongside an acclaimed chef. On Europe shore excursions, let the unique flavors speak to the diver

blocks.heading: Set sail to the Mediterranean
blocks.text: Leave the ordinary behind and immerse yourself in the pure perfection of the Mediterranean & Greek Isles.

blocks.heading: Best of Mt. Etna
blocks.text: Soak up the drama of Sicily’s iconic landmark from the seat of a 4WD vehicle. Enjoy the panoramic views as you ascend thousands of feet up one of the world’s most active volcanoes. Then, discuss your adventure with fellow travelers over lunch at a nearby restaurant. VIEW EXCURSIONS

blocks.heading: Best of Granada
blocks.text: Fall under the mesmerizing spell of Granada on this exceptional full day excursion that includes tours of two of the city’s most renowned landmarks. Explore the awe-inspiring Granada Cathedral, the first Renaissance church built in Spain. Behold the Royal Chapel, the final resting place of King Ferdinand and Queen Isabella. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Acropolis, Plaka & Temple of Poseidon
blocks.text: A guided walking tour celebrates Athens' most treasured sights. Explore the historic temples of the Acropolis, browse the famed Plaka shopping district, and take a scenic drive to Cape Sounion, en route to the stunning 5th-century B.C. Temple of Poseidon, overlooking the Aegean Sea. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: La Sagrada Familia & City Drive
blocks.text: Discover Barcelona's most breath-taking sights on this laid-back, four-hour narrated city drive. Visit Antonio Gaudi's masterpiece, the epic La Sagrada Familia church before viewing the Olympic village, the stunning Columbus Monument, picturesque Plaza Catalunya, and the incredible city panoramas atop Montjuic Mountain. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Dubrovnik's City Walls
blocks.text: Here's a unique way to experience this port's beauty and history. You'll stroll along the ancient city walls, part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site. Enjoy stunning views of life both inside and outside the walls and visit the Maritime Museum for more insight into Dubrovnik's nautical past. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Best of Portofino, Santa Margherita & Genoa
blocks.text: Walk in the footsteps of history during a day-long adventure to three of Italy’s most enchanting Ligurian villages: Portofino, Santa Margherita and Genoa. Enjoy guided walking tours, savor the flavors of Ligurian cuisine in Genoa, and set off on your own adventure and shop or relax in an outdoor café. VIEW EXCURSIONS

blocks.heading: Olympia & Archaeological Museum
blocks.text: Get your walking shoes on for this tour that takes you through ancient Olympia where the Olympics began over 3 millenniums ago. You'll see the Temple of Zeus that housed one of the Seven Wonders of the World. You'll also visit the Archaeological Museum and view some of the temple’s finest decorative sculpture. VIEW EXCURSIONS

blocks.heading: Florence, Statue of David & Uffizi Museum
blocks.text: Experience the beauty of Florence, the cultural center of the Renaissance on a guided walking tour. Marvel at the Duomo. Explore the Accademia Museum. Peruse the notable works in the Uffizi Gallery. Savor a three-course lunch. VIEW EXCURSIONS
