blocks.text: Our departure ports are as iconic as the destinations we visit. You can a little extra vacation to your vacation by arriving early or staying after your cruise and exploring the wonders that lie within these cities.

blocks.heading: Why cruise with Princess
blocks.text: Curated comfort, world-class entertainment and international flavors await you.

blocks.heading: Celebrations & Romance
blocks.text: It's difficult to imagine something more romantic than sailing through the alluring cities and charming countryside of Europe. While on board your European cruise, we cater to your sentimental side with private dining on your balcony — like breakfast for two or a sunset dinner — honeymoon packages, flowers and chocolates delivered to your room and couples-only massages in the Sanctuary.

blocks.heading: Accommodations
blocks.text: Your stateroom is where you rest and recharge between adventures. That’s why every room is equipped with the expertly designed Princess Luxury Bed, 100% Jacquard-woven cotton linens. Whether you go interior or all-out in a suite, our staterooms will make you feel right at home. Especially for families traveling together who can enjoy the option of connected rooms.

blocks.heading: Dining
blocks.text: From the spice of Moroccan tagine to the sweetness of Greek Baklava, Europe’s flavor profile is incredibly diverse. On a Transatlantic cruise with Princess, taste the best of Europe on board with specialty dining. Say cheers during a lively lunch at a British-style pub and try English favorites like bangers and mash or shepherd's pie. Or savor hearty Italian pastas at Sabatini’s℠ Italian Trattoria

blocks.heading: Entertainment
blocks.text: Embark on adventures by day, and indulge in entertainment by night. Watch Movies Under the Stars® at our 300-square-foot outdoor theater. blocks.heading: Relaxation
blocks.text: Your European cruise should be every bit as refreshing as it is inspiring. Unwind in the Sanctuary, a retreat just for adults, and relish in tranquility. Or book an appointment at the Lotus Spa®. Enjoy soothing treatments — like facials, hot stone massages and detoxifying wraps — that will leave you energized for upcoming adventures.

blocks.heading: Casino
blocks.text: Experience the thrill of cards, dice, roulette, and blackjack at our onboard casino during your European cruise. Learn from our expert staff or seasoned guests, and put your skills to the test. For a more relaxed pace, enjoy the slot machines, or join fellow travelers for Bingo and exciting group tournaments. Visit iconic cities, indulge in international cuisine and immerse yourself in new cultures. After a few days of relaxation on board and exploration ashore, you can decide which adventure to embark on next with Princess.

blocks.text: Every special occasion is better shared together, and what better way to celebrate than a Getaway cruise with Princess. From birthdays and anniversaries to vow renewals and family reunions, find onboard activities and adventures ashore for every guest in your party. With our Getaway cruise deals, discover even more reasons to celebrate with your friends or family on a cruise vacation.

Every trip earns you credit – even short Getaway cruises – to get you one step closer to the next membership tier. This means more discounts, upgrades and pre-sale opportunities. Depending on the loyalty level, you can also enjoy complimentary services, like wine-tastings and hors d’oeuvres

blocks.heading: Featured Greece cruise ports
blocks.text: Across Athens and the Greek Isles, Greece's cruise ports unfold at a lively tempo shaped by history, daily life and enduring tradition. Each destination brings its own character — but all share that distinctly Greek energy that keeps travelers coming back.

blocks.heading: Athens (Piraeus)
blocks.text: As the gateway to Greece’s capital, Piraeus leads you straight into Athens’ ancient heart, where landmarks like the Acropolis, Parthenon and Temple of Olympian Zeus tell the story of Western civilization’s beginnings. Between archaeological marvels, lively markets and vibrant cafés, the city offers a captivating blend of history and modern life.

blocks.heading: Katakolon (for Olympia)
blocks.text: Katakolon is the gateway to Ancient Olympia, birthplace of the Olympic Games. Walk the ancient stadium, explore the ruins of the Temple of Zeus and visit the Archaeological Museum — one of Greece's most rewarding archaeological sites.

blocks.heading: Santorini
blocks.text: Famous for its whitewashed villages and dramatic volcanic cliffs, Santorini enchants visitors with much more than postcard views. Explore the remarkably preserved ancient ruins of Akrotiri, swim at black, red and white sand beaches unlike any other in Greece, and sample the island's celebrated Assyrtiko and Mavrotragano wines from hillside vineyards overlooking the caldera.

blocks.heading: Corfu
blocks.text: Corfu combines Venetian architecture, emerald hills and turquoise waters. Cruise guests can stroll through the UNESCO-listed Old Town, sample olive oils or relax on scenic Ionian beaches.

blocks.heading: Mykonos
blocks.text: Mykonos is perhaps best known for its iconic windmills — 16 in total, with seven perched dramatically on a hilltop in Chora, most dating back to the 16th century. Beyond the landmark views, the island delivers cosmopolitan energy, golden beaches, boutique shopping and seaside dining, with Little Venice's waterfront cafés offering one of the most picturesque spots in the Aegean.

blocks.heading: Chania
blocks.text: Located on the island of Crete, Chania captivates with its Venetian harbor, colorful old town and rich Cretan traditions. It’s the perfect place to explore local markets, ancient ruins and authentic Mediterranean cuisine.

blocks.heading: Heraklion
blocks.text: Crete's capital pairs a vibrant waterfront city with easy access to the Palace of Knossos, the legendary center of Minoan civilization just outside town. The city's Archaeological Museum, Venetian harbor fortress and celebrated Cretan food scene make it well worth exploring beyond the port.

blocks.heading: Rhodes
blocks.text: Step into the past on Rhodes, where medieval walls and cobblestone streets meet crystal-clear beaches. The Old Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, showcases centuries of Greek, Byzantine and Crusader influence.

blocks.heading: Why cruise to Greece
blocks.text: A cruise to Greece offers a seamless way to explore the country’s diverse islands, ancient history and sparkling coastlines — all while enjoying the comfort and convenience of your ship between destinations.

blocks.heading: Landmarks & cultural masterpieces
blocks.text: Greece is a living museum of ancient wonders and timeless artistry, where every ruin, temple and monument tells the story of Western civilization’s beginnings. From archaeological marvels to sacred monasteries, these landmarks capture the spirit and history that make Greece unforgettable.

blocks.heading: Celebrations & Romance
blocks.text: It's difficult to imagine something more romantic than sailing through the alluring cities and charming countryside of Europe. While on board your European cruise, we cater to your sentimental side with private dining on your balcony — like breakfast for two or a sunset dinner — honeymoon packages, flowers and chocolates delivered to your room and couples-only massages in the Sanctuary.

blocks.heading: Accommodations
blocks.text: Your stateroom is where you rest and recharge between adventures. That’s why every room is equipped with the expertly designed Princess Luxury Bed, 100% Jacquard-woven cotton linens. Whether you go interior or all-out in a suite, our staterooms will make you feel right at home. Especially for families traveling together who can enjoy the option of connected rooms.

blocks.heading: Dining
blocks.text: From savory Norwegian meatloaf to sweet Icelandic celebration cake, Northern Europe is bursting with flavor. Head ashore to enjoy Icelandic skyr with porridge for breakfast, and savor a Norwegian seafood dinner. Or embark on an all-encompassing culinary tour right on board with our Chef’s Table Lumiere. On a Norway and Iceland cruise with Princess, appease your appetite with one-of-a-kind dining o

blocks.heading: Entertainment
blocks.text: Embark on adventures by day, and indulge in entertainment by night. Watch Movies Under the Stars® at our 300-square-foot outdoor theater. Attend original productions from Broadway legend Stephen Schwartz, composer of Wicked. Or learn traditional moves, like flamenco or Irish stepdance, and listen to popular music from the destinations on your itinerary. On a European cruise with Princess, the choi

blocks.heading: Relaxation
blocks.text: Your European cruise should be every bit as refreshing as it is inspiring. Unwind in the Sanctuary, a retreat just for adults, and relish in tranquility. Or book an appointment at the Lotus Spa®. Enjoy soothing treatments — like facials, hot stone massages and detoxifying wraps — that will leave you energized for upcoming adventures.

blocks.heading: Casino
blocks.text: Experience the thrill of cards, dice, roulette, and blackjack at our onboard casino during your European cruise. Learn from our expert staff or seasoned guests, and put your skills to the test. For a more relaxed pace, enjoy the slot machines, or join fellow travelers for Bingo and exciting group tournaments. The casino promises nonstop excitement, whether you're a seasoned player or just playing

blocks.heading: Things to do in Hilo
blocks.text: Big Island energy hits differently. It’s humid. It’s lava-scorched. It’s wrapped in rainforest and occasionally smells like… cookies? Hilo goes big — it’s all about waterfalls, volcanoes and endless seas in every direction. And whether you're in it for the geological drama or just want to eat tropical fruit like it’s your last chance ever, Hilo's got what you’re looking for.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Hilo
blocks.text: You came for adventure. You’re getting jungle zips, lava strolls and helicopter views that’ll make you reevaluate what you thought a ‘good day’ could be. These excursions serve up Hilo’s weird, wild and wonderful heart in the best ways possible.

blocks.heading: Volcanic Landscapes by Helicopter
blocks.text: You haven’t seen Hilo until you’ve seen it all at once… by flying over it in a helicopter, staring down at lava scars and black beaches that look like something out of a planetarium fever dream. Fifty minutes of jaw-drop views, followed by the smug satisfaction of knowing your vacation is objectively cooler than anyone else you know. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Ultimate Hilo: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park & Tastes of Hawaii
blocks.text: Spend the day hiking through freshly minted lava fields with a guide who knows where all the good secrets are buried (sometimes literally). Then toast to molten rock with a glass of wine grown on a volcano. How’s that for dangerously decadent? Also, there’s going to be cookies. Cookies make every adventure even better. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Honolii Orchards Chocolate Tasting & Farm Tour
blocks.text: Climb Maunakea’s flank to a cacao farm where you’ll meet locals who grow chocolate like their tending to the most important crops in the world (and, who are we kidding, they are). Learn how it’s made, why it matters and taste your way through 10 bars that’ll ruin grocery store chocolate forever. Pro tip: the ‘talk-story’ part is real — and it slaps. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Waterfall, Pana‘ewa Zoo & Black Sand Beach
blocks.text: Start with coffee. Obviously (you’re gonna want to be alert, after all). Then chase waterfalls, chill at a zoo in the middle of the rainforest and walk a black-sand beach that may or may not have sea turtles just vibing on the shore. Finish with a picnic lunch and some Boiling Pots — because apparently even rivers get spicy here. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Rainforest Zipline & Waterfall Adventure
blocks.text: Rainforest? Check. Eight ziplines? Oh yes, very much check. One literal half-mile flight across a waterfall. Che— wait, what? Yeah, it’s what ziplining should be, provided you’ve got the nerve. You’ll be strapping into a harness, soaring over treetops and making Tarzan look like an amateur. Bonus: suspension bridge walk just to make sure your knees are still functioning. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Jungle Falls Bike Adventure
blocks.text: Trade fair winds and following seas for pedal power. Ride through old plantation roads and jungle trails, past waterfalls and sugar ghosts, with a guide who probably has stories you’ll want to Google later. End with tropical smoothies and handmade sweets because you earned them — or at least sweated for them. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.text: Hilo’s cruise port keeps it chill. blocks.heading: Things to do in Honolulu
blocks.text: Honolulu is where beach day meets battlefield, and royal palaces share space with spam musubi. You’ll see volcano craters, sacred valleys and food trucks that’ll ruin you for takeout forever. This is the kind of place where a catamaran might float past a WWII battleship, and no one bats an eye. If you like your vacation destinations packed with options — congrats, you’ve found the blueprint.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Honolulu
blocks.text: From summit hikes to sunset cruises, Honolulu excursions do not believe in subtle. These tours hand you binoculars, history, cocktails and chaos — in the best possible way. This is how you turn a port stop into a core-memory machine.

blocks.heading: Behind-the-Scenes Exclusive at Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum & Battleship Missouri
blocks.text: Walk the hangars of the Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum and climb the historic Ford Island control tower for a view few ever get. Then board the ‘Mighty Mo’ and stand where WWII officially ended. This five-hour deep dive into history includes fighter planes, giant guns and exclusive access that’ll have your inner history nerd fist-pumping through lunch. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Famous Oahu Sights, Bites & Sips
blocks.text: This full-day flex takes you from Diamond Head’s famous rim to Hanauma Bay’s volcanic curve, with geysering blowholes (the kind made of rock)) and royal statues in between. Refuel with a lunch stop made famous by Diners, Drive-Ins & Dives, then sip your way through a wine tasting at Oeno Winery. This is your chance to snack, sip and selfie your way across the entire island. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Monarchs & Missionaries: Hawaii's Royal History
blocks.text: Step into Hawaii’s royal era with a self-guided tour of Iolani Palace, once home to King Kalākaua and Queen Liliʻuokalani. You'll pass through historic churches, visit royal tombs and stop at Pali Lookout for sweeping views of Oahu’s windward cliffs. Wrap the experience with a guided look at the Hawaiian Mission Houses and their lasting impact on island life and leadership. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Iconic Diamond Head Adventure Hike
blocks.text: It’s one of the most iconic hikes in the Pacific — a 1.5-mile roundtrip trek to the summit of Diamond Head Crater. You’ll climb staircases, pass through a tunnel and emerge to views that’ll drop jaws (and possibly camera-phone batteries). Along the way, your guide will serve up geological history, local legends and enough facts to make your hike feel both epic and earned. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Oahu by Helicopter
blocks.text: Take to the skies and watch Oahu unfold like a living atlas. You’ll fly above Waikiki, swoop into Diamond Head Crater and pass over sacred waterfalls and historical landmarks (like Pearl Harbor and the USS Missouri). Your pilot will handle the views; you just sit back, soak it up and try not to lose your mind over the scale of it all. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Waikiki Sunset & Cocktail Cruise
blocks.text: Board the Majestic, a double-decker catamaran with serious after-dark energy. Cruise past the Honolulu skyline while the sun does its dramatic-descent thing. Your welcome cocktail sets the mood, and live Hawaiian music keeps it going. Top deck offers panoramic views; bottom deck brings the vibes. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Honolulu

Step off the ship and you’re already in the mix — minutes from world-class beaches, legendary landmarks and the kind of food scene that makes layovers feel criminally short. blocks.heading: Things to do in Kahului
blocks.text: Maui’s natural beauty shines in Kahului, a gateway to some of the island’s most awe-inspiring sights. From volcanic craters and tropical gardens to oceanfront towns and cultural gems, there’s discovery in every direction.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Kahului
blocks.text: Maui’s excursions with Princess highlight the island’s wild beauty and rich culture. Discover towering volcanoes, tropical sea life and unforgettable drives through paradise, all with careful guidance and easy transportation from ship to shore.

blocks.heading: Molokini Crater & turtle snorkel experience
blocks.text: Take to the water for an unforgettable snorkeling adventure at Molokini Crater, a crescent-shaped volcanic caldera teeming with marine life. Then head to Turtle Town, where Hawaiian green sea turtles glide through the sea. Crystal-clear water, vibrant coral reefs and guided support make this a must for snorkelers. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Maui: Haleakala Crater & Maui Ocean Center
blocks.text: Journey to Haleakalā National Park to witness the massive volcanic crater that helped shape Maui’s landscape. After scenic high-elevation views, enjoy an island-style lunch before heading to the Maui Ocean Center. Walk through a glass tunnel surrounded by marine life and visit interactive exhibits to experience Hawaii’s unique ocean ecosystem up close. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Haleakala Crater
blocks.text: Ascend winding mountain roads to reach Haleakalā’s summit. At more than 10,000 feet above sea level, this dormant volcano unveils sweeping island views and an enormous crater floor surrounded by cinder cones. It’s a breathtaking way to witness one of Maui’s most iconic natural wonders, and a memory sure to last long after your cruise. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hana Road & picnic
blocks.text: Explore the iconic Road to Hana, a scenic highway that twists through lush rainforest and past dramatic coastlines. Stops along the way include waterfalls, beaches and cultural sites. Pause midday for a relaxing picnic lunch in a beautiful natural setting. It’s an unforgettable way to experience Maui’s untamed east side. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Maui Ocean Center
blocks.text: Discover Hawaiian marine life inside one of the top aquariums in the country. Highlights include a 54-foot underwater tunnel, reef displays, sea turtles and interactive exhibits focused on conservation. The Ocean Center is an ideal excursion for families and ocean lovers looking to connect with the vibrant sea life of the Hawaiian Islands. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Whale watching cruise
blocks.text: Set sail on Maui’s waters during whale season to witness humpback whales in their natural habitat. Expert guides share insights into whale behavior and migration patterns as you watch for breaching, tail slaps and spouts. Calm seas and Maui’s scenic backdrop enhance this awe-inspiring adventure on the open ocean. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Kahului
blocks.text: Cruise itineraries to Kahului bring you straight to the heart of Maui. This port pairs natural beauty with adventure, connecting guests to volcanoes, beaches and cultural treasures. Many sailings through Hawaii feature Kahului as a standout destination. Select a Kahului itinerary to add lush rainforests and island history to your Hawaii cruise.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Kauai
blocks.text: Kauai is nature at its most dramatic — lush, wild and soul-stirring. Explore Hawaii’s rugged canyons, cascading waterfalls and golden beaches, or slow down in small towns that feel a world away from the everyday.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Kauai
blocks.text: Kauai’s shore excursions put you right in the heart of the island’s legendary beauty. Sail up a jungle river, gaze across vast canyons or wander botanical gardens surrounded by waterfalls and wildlife. Each adventure adds a new dimension to Hawaii’s most rugged, romantic island.

blocks.heading: Discover Kauai
blocks.text: Spend the day immersed in Kauai’s rugged beauty and rich heritage. Visit Waimea Canyon, cruise the Wailua River and marvel at the Fern Grotto. This tour combines natural sights with cultural stops for a comprehensive, full-day adventure. It’s a memorable way to discover what makes the Garden Isle unforgettable. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Kauai: Waimea canyon, Wailua river & fern grotto
blocks.text: Experience Kauai’s most celebrated landmarks by road and river. A scenic drive takes you to Waimea Canyon, with panoramic views of volcanic gorges and emerald cliffs. Then, cruise the Wailua River to Fern Grotto where Hawaiian music and hula bring local culture to life. This full-day experience includes lunch and stops at Opaekaa Falls and Spouting Horn. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kauai scenic tour
blocks.text: Take in the island’s lush beauty on a relaxing drive past valleys, waterfalls and ocean overlooks. This laid-back excursion is a great way to see Kauai’s top sights, including Hanapepe Valley and Wailua Falls. Along the way, guides share local insight into the island’s culture, geology and history, giving you a well-rounded view of the Garden Isle. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Wailua river cruise & fern grotto
blocks.text: Cruise up the Wailua River, surrounded by jungle-covered hills and peaceful scenery. At the Fern Grotto, step into a natural lava-rock amphitheater where musicians perform traditional Hawaiian songs. It’s a beautiful, meaningful excursion that blends Kauai’s tropical beauty with its rich cultural roots. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Jewels of Hawaii: Allerton & McBryde tropical gardens & waterfall
blocks.text: Wander through two of Hawaii’s most exquisite botanical gardens, filled with rare plants, towering trees and serene waterfalls. Discover the biodiversity of the Allerton and McBryde Gardens with a knowledgeable guide, and take in views of the Lawai Valley. This peaceful tour reveals the island’s natural wonders through the lens of conservation and beauty. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy panoramic Kauai - Opaekaa Falls, plantation & train
blocks.text: Perfect for guests who prefer minimal walking, this relaxing Kauai excursion showcases the island’s scenic highlights. Enjoy sweeping views at Opaekaa Falls, a plantation visit with a narrated train ride and a glimpse into Kauai’s agricultural history. It’s an easy, photo-worthy way to see the island’s lush terrain. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Kauai
blocks.text: Cruise itineraries featuring Kauai transport you to a wilder, greener Hawaii. Often paired with stops in Oahu, Maui and the Big Island, Kauai itineraries round out a journey that highlights the state's diversity. Each sailing gives you time to soak in the island’s quiet charm, from volcanic canyons and the famous Napali coast to jungle rivers and palm-fringed shores.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Kona
blocks.text: Kona brings together rich history, oceanfront beauty and the island charm Hawaii is so well known for. Stroll through royal landmarks, snorkel in clear bays and browse markets filled with local art and tropical fruit. Every moment here invites you to slow down, soak it in and discover something new.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Kona
blocks.text: Kona is rich in historic adventure and ocean wonder. Explore sea caves on a raft, snorkel among coral reefs or ride a real submarine beneath the waves. From volcanic landscapes to historic landmarks, Kona excursions let you experience the Big Island’s beauty in every way.

blocks.heading: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park & Black Sand Beach
blocks.text: Travel across the island to Hawai‘i Volcanoes National Park and witness striking island landscapes shaped by lava and time. Walk along volcanic craters, learn about active eruptions and stop at Punaluʻu Black Sand Beach to see sea turtles and unique shoreline views. A scenic drive ties together nature and geology. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Kona by land & sea
blocks.text: Combine panoramic coastal views with marine exploration on this land-and-sea combo tour. Board a motorcoach to see local highlights, then transfer to a comfortable boat to cruise the Kona coast. Along the way, learn about the island’s past, snap photos of lava landscapes and enjoy breezes and storytelling from your local guide. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Captain Zodiac Rafting & snorkeling adventure
blocks.text: Get close to sea caves, lava tubes and marine life on a high-speed raft ride. This small-group adventure includes snorkeling in pristine waters and the chance to see dolphins, manta rays, or turtles. Guides share island lore and natural history while leading you to some of the coast’s most picturesque and secluded snorkeling spots. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kona coast whale watching
blocks.text: During whale season, set sail on a cruise to look for humpback whales breaching and playing along the Kona coast. Naturalists on board share insights about whale behaviors and migration. This leisurely ride features incredible wildlife spotting opportunities with spectacular ocean views, perfect for nature lovers of all ages. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Atlantis submarine adventure
blocks.text: Descend 100 feet below the surface in a real submarine for a unique view of the world under Kona’s island waters. Large viewing portholes reveal coral reefs, tropical fish and even sunken vessels. This narrated tour explores the Kona coast’s vibrant marine environment, all while staying comfortably dry. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Glassbottom boat reef tour
blocks.text: Step aboard a glass-bottom boat and glide across the calm waters of Kailua Bay. Look through crystal-clear panels to see coral reefs, tropical fish and other fascinating sea creatures. A local guide will add to the experience by sharing cultural and ecological insights during this relaxing and family-friendly excursion. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Kona
blocks.text: Cruise itineraries featuring Kona bring you to the heart of the Big Island’s sunny west coast. This port is a highlight on sailings through the Hawaiian Islands, featuring ocean activities, gorgeous black sand beaches and historic charm. Each Kona itinerary builds in cultural depth and scenic beauty to create a truly immersive island experience.

blocks.heading: Featured Italy cruise ports
blocks.text: Italy’s cruise ports offer a captivating mix of history, culture and coastal beauty. Each stop invites you to experience something unique—from ancient cities filled with art and architecture to seaside towns bursting with charm and flavor.

blocks.heading: Experience Italy ports on your next cruise
Why cruise Italy
blocks.text: Italy rewards cruisers like few destinations can — each port unlocks a different chapter of the country's rich history, celebrated cuisine and stunning coastal landscapes, from ancient ruins to vibrant piazzas.

blocks.heading: Celebrations & Romance
blocks.text: It's difficult to imagine something more romantic than sailing through the alluring cities and charming countryside of Europe. While on board your European cruise, we cater to your sentimental side with private dining on your balcony — like breakfast for two or a sunset dinner — honeymoon packages, flowers and chocolates delivered to your room and couples-only massages in the Sanctuary.

blocks.heading: Accommodations
blocks.text: Your stateroom is where you rest and recharge between adventures. That’s why every room is equipped with the expertly designed Princess Luxury Bed, 100% Jacquard-woven cotton linens. Whether you go interior or all-out in a suite, our staterooms will make you feel right at home. Especially for families traveling together who can enjoy the option of connected rooms.

blocks.heading: Dining
blocks.text: From savory Norwegian meatloaf to sweet Icelandic celebration cake, Northern Europe is bursting with flavor. Head ashore to enjoy Icelandic skyr with porridge for breakfast, and savor a Norwegian seafood dinner. Or embark on an all-encompassing culinary tour right on board with our Chef’s Table Lumiere. On a Norway and Iceland cruise with Princess, appease your appetite with one-of-a-kind dining o

blocks.heading: Entertainment
blocks.text: Embark on adventures by day, and indulge in entertainment by night. Watch Movies Under the Stars® at our 300-square-foot outdoor theater. Attend original productions from Broadway legend Stephen Schwartz, composer of Wicked. Or learn traditional moves, like flamenco or Irish stepdance, and listen to popular music from the destinations on your itinerary. On a European cruise with Princess, the choi

blocks.heading: Relaxation
blocks.text: Your European cruise should be every bit as refreshing as it is inspiring. Unwind in the Sanctuary, a retreat just for adults, and relish in tranquility. Or book an appointment at the Lotus Spa®. Enjoy soothing treatments — like facials, hot stone massages and detoxifying wraps — that will leave you energized for upcoming adventures.

blocks.heading: Casino
blocks.text: Experience the thrill of cards, dice, roulette, and blackjack at our onboard casino during your European cruise. Learn from our expert staff or seasoned guests, and put your skills to the test. For a more relaxed pace, enjoy the slot machines, or join fellow travelers for Bingo and exciting group tournaments. The casino promises nonstop excitement, whether you're a seasoned player or just playing

blocks.heading: Art of effortless cruising
blocks.text: Japan is a country of bullet trains and mountain shrines, of midnight ramen and thousand-year rituals—and with Princess, you get to thread through it all without the usual travel chaos. No train apps. No hotel check-ins. Just a smooth glide from Hiroshima to Kyoto to Nagasaki, where every port brings a new version of Japan into focus (without packing, train schedules or language barriers). Onboard

blocks.heading: Check the Japan must-sees off your list
blocks.text: You can experience it all when you travel by sea, land, and rail with Princess

blocks.heading: Traditions that create a timeless experience
blocks.text: Japan’s cultural heritage shines through daily life—from the elegance of a tea ceremony to the energy of festival season. With Princess, you’ll witness these traditions up close. It’s not just about observing traditions—it’s about experiencing them in the places where they were born.

blocks.heading: Where history comes alive
blocks.text: Japan’s history is a living epic—from the ancient Jomon period to the rise of the samurai and the transformative Meiji Restoration. Walk in the footsteps of emperors and warriors as you explore majestic castles, sacred temples, and storied cities. Onboard, curated lectures and cultural programming offer deeper insight into Japan’s fascinating past—bringing history to life both on land and at sea,

blocks.heading: Taste the authenticity
blocks.text: Japanese cuisine is a journey—rooted in tradition, shaped by the seasons, and crafted with precision. From the elegance of sushi and sashimi to the comfort of ramen, tempura, and regional specialties, each dish reveals a new layer of culinary heritage. Whether you're sampling fresh seafood ashore or savoring expertly prepared dishes onboard, food in Japan is more than nourishment—it’s an experienc

blocks.heading: Now booking 2027-2028 voyages
blocks.text: Our biggest Japan season yet is available in 2027 with two ships, 50 unique itineraries and 45 destinations across six countries.

blocks.heading: A cruise for every season
blocks.text: Each season reveals a different face of Japan, with unique cultural experiences, seasonal cuisines, and natural wonders. Whatever time you choose to visit, Princess itineraries are thoughtfully designed to showcase the authentic seasonal traditions that make Japan endlessly fascinating.

blocks.heading: Spring
blocks.text: Witness the magical blossom season, creating an unforgettable, picturesque experience.

blocks.heading: Summer
blocks.text: Experience vibrant festivals, spectacular fireworks displays, and lush mountain landscapes.

blocks.heading: Fall
blocks.text: Marvel at a stunning display of autumn foliage, known as koyo, transforming landscapes into vibrant tapestries of red, orange, and gold.

blocks.heading: Winter
blocks.text: Cruise at the end of winter to cap off a full year of changing seasons enjoying hot springs and cultural festivals.

blocks.heading: Explore the unforgettable ports of Japan
blocks.text: Princess Cruises offers unparalleled access to Japan's ports, sailing to over 38 destinations. With a longer season, and more departure dates than any other cruise line, you’ll have even more opportunities to explore these remarkable destinations—all without the hassle of planning each stop yourself.

blocks.heading: Kobe
blocks.text: From imposing feudal-era fortifications to modern street-side food stands, the region around Kobe is rich with sights and stories that stretch across ages. Ancient temples nestle between gleaming skyscrapers, while traditional sake breweries share neighborhoods with cutting-edge research facilities, creating a tapestry where every corner reveals another layer of Japan's evolution. View port

blocks.heading: Tokyo
blocks.text: Begin your pacific adventure in the place where tradition meets technology. See neon skyscrapers cradling ancient temples as you explore Tokyo’s vibrant streets, where every corner reveals something extraordinary — from the serenity of the Imperial Palace Garden to the energy of the Shibuya district. View Port

blocks.heading: Kumano
blocks.text: Kumano is understatement turned unforgettable, inviting curiosity and contemplation in equal measure. Whether you're drawn to ancient pilgrimage trails or peaceful coastal retreats, this port destination is a tapestry of spiritual depth and raw natural energy. View port

blocks.heading: Okinawa
blocks.text: Every Okinawa cruise is full of surprises, with ancient castles, tranquil gardens, colorful markets and hidden beaches seemingly popping up out of nowhere. The island’s mix of history, nature and culture makes it easy to fill your day with once-in-a-lifetime adventure — or just find a perfect spot to slow things down and take it all in. View port

blocks.heading: Kochi
blocks.text: This is a port for travelers who like their history with a view and their sightseeing with a little of everything. A Kochi cruise can take you up a castle keep, into a limestone cave or straight to the beach, all with plenty of time to enjoy some local cuisine or make trades at an open-air market before your ship departs. View port

blocks.heading: Osaka
blocks.text: Whether you're drawn to the hushed halls of centuries-old temples or the pulsing life of busy marketplaces, this destination delivers. Osaka and Kyoto offer elegance, energy and endless exploration — with a little something for every type of traveler. When visiting the Osaka cruise port, don’t miss out on these must-experience activities. View port

blocks.heading: Japan cruise spotlight: A day in Kyoto
blocks.text: Imagine the perfect day in port, taking in the sights and an excursion or two.

blocks.heading: 9:30 p.m. Indulge in a nightcap
blocks.text: Sip on inspired local cocktails, sake and spirits, before a restful night sleep in your Princess Luxury Bed.

blocks.heading: 8:00 a.m. Wake up as your ship docks in port
blocks.text: Order coffee and breakfast to your room with OceanNow® delivery and take your first look at the city of Osaka, as Diamond Princess® sails into port.

blocks.heading: 9:30 a.m. Enjoy a scenic drive to Kyoto
blocks.text: Watch Osaka's urban sprawl give way to scenic countryside as you journey toward Nijo Castle, passing landmarks like Toji Temple and Kyoto Tower along the way.

blocks.heading: 11:15 a.m. Arrive at Nijo Castle
blocks.text: Step into the shogun’s world at this 17th-century stronghold, known for its “nightingale floors” that chirp underfoot. Then travel further back to the Golden Pavilion, a 14th-century temple wrapped in gold leaf and serene beauty.

blocks.heading: 1:00 p.m. A moment to savor
blocks.text: Relax over lunch at a local hotel, then set out to discover more of Kyoto’s iconic sights.

blocks.heading: 2:30 p.m. Step into history at the Heian Shrine
blocks.text: Visit the Heian Shrine, built in 1895 to honor the 1,100th anniversary of Kyoto’s founding. This vibrant landmark blends traditional architecture with a tranquil garden setting.

blocks.heading: 3:30 p.m. Shop for souvenirs at the Kyoto Handicraft Center
blocks.text: Cap off your adventure with a stop at the Kyoto Handicraft Center, where locally made souvenirs offer the perfect reminder of your journey.

blocks.heading: 6:00 p.m. Return to a traditional Onsen bath experience
blocks.text: Relax in Izumi, an onsen bath, at the Lotus Spa while reflecting on your day in Kyoto.

blocks.heading: 8:00 p.m. Dine at Makoto
blocks.text: Experience edoma-style sushi at Makoto Ocean starting October 2025.

blocks.heading: Excursions for every interest
blocks.text: From sumo matches to cherry blossom festivals, steaming bowls of ramen to Zen gardens—Japan is full of memorable moments waiting to happen. To make these experiences even more accessible, select excursions are also offered in both Japanese and English.

blocks.heading: Miyajima & Itsukushima Shrine
blocks.text: Travel to sacred Miyajima Island and visit Itsukushima Shrine on this half-day excursion. Designated a World Heritage Site, a National Treasure and an Important Cultural Property, the Itsukushima Shrine attracts thousands of visitors a year. The shrine's unique architecture called Shinden, is typical of the noble houses in the late Heian Period.

blocks.heading: Kakunodate Samurai Town
blocks.text: Feel the centuries unfold as you stroll through the wide streets and large courtyards of the Kakunodate Samurai District, once the home of 80 samurai and their families. Established in 1620, Kakunodate is acclaimed as one of the best examples of samurai architecture and housing in the country.

blocks.heading: Hirosaki Castle Park, Neputa Festival Floats & Garden
blocks.text: The excitement of the ancient city of Hirosaki comes alive on this full-day adventure that begins with a scenic 90-minute drive to Hirosaki Castle Park. Constructed in 1611, the original structure was struck by lightning in 1627 and burned to the ground. Although rebuilt in 1810, the castle still retains an aura of its ancient past. This historical treasure sits tucked away in the lush and peacefu

blocks.heading: Ja-Gal-Ch'i Market & Beomeosa Temple
blocks.text: This fascinating half day excursion starts with a warm welcome from your local guide, before an enjoyable drive through the city's northern suburbs. Journey through magnificent countryside to the Beomeosa Temple, one of South Korea's largest temples, which dates back to 678 A.D.

blocks.heading: Why a Princess cruise is the best choice to see Japan
blocks.text: A Princess cruise offers a convenient and deeply immersive way to experience Japan. Backed by over a decade of experience sailing these waters, we’ve crafted journeys that let you unpack just once and explore a world of cultural richness —through authentic onboard experiences, regionally inspired dining, and a wide range of shore excursions that bring each destination to life. It’s a seamless way

blocks.heading: Diverse and thoughtfully curated itineraries
blocks.text: With 38 spectacular ports of call and cruises ranging from 7-day escapes to 28-day explorations, Princess offers a wide range of Japan cruises designed to suit every traveler. Each itinerary visits multiple ports across the country—revealing the rich diversity of Japan’s regions, from bustling cities to serene coastal towns. Timed to coincide with iconic seasonal moments like cherry blossom season

blocks.heading: Specialized dining experiences
blocks.text: In addition to your favorite Princess classics, guests can enjoy a variety of authentic Japanese dining experiences throughout their journey. Savor expertly crafted edoma-style sushi at Makoto Ocean by sushi master Makoto Okuwa who brings his over 25 years of experience to the high seas. Enjoy the lively flair or Teppanyaki, or explore regional specialties featured in our “Princess Japan Favorites

blocks.heading: Personalized attentive service
blocks.text: Our expert crew provides friendly service, allowing you to relax. Powered by Medallion technology, enjoy a personalized and streamlined experience with expedited boarding, touchless payments, and easy navigation for effortless cruising.

blocks.heading: Convenience and value
blocks.text: Cruising with Princess to Japan offers the significant advantage of unpacking only once while visiting multiple destinations. Meals, entertainment, and accommodation are largely covered in the cruise fare, and inclusive packages like Princess Plus® and Princess Premier® can further enhance the value by adding amenities like Wi-Fi, premium beverages, and gratuities.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Akita
blocks.text: Akita offers a quieter, more traditional side of Japan, known for its deep-rooted culture, seasonal festivals and well-preserved historical sites Akita wears its heritage with pride. Known for its year-round festivals, storied samurai roots and deep connections to nature, this coastal gem in Japan’s Tōhoku region is where the past and present share the spotlight. Step off the ship and into a place

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Akita
blocks.text: Historic samurai towns, mountain observatories, windswept capes — Akita shore excursions offer you a backstage pass to northern Japan’s traditions and natural drama. These curated experiences, featuring centuries-old craftsmanship and traditional Japanese cuisine, add even more depth to your time ashore.

blocks.heading: Akita Wonders & Maiko Dance Showcase
blocks.text: Sample regional flavors at the indoor market, then learn the roots of the Kanto Festival at the Performing Arts Center, where towering lanterns and performance gear tell a tale of summer celebration. Finally, enjoy tea and a Maiko performance in Senshu Park for a serene, cultural close to your time ashore. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kakunodate On Your Own by Exclusive Bullet Train
blocks.text: Hop aboard Japan’s famed bullet train and be whisked to Kakunodate, where you’ll step back into Edo-period elegance. With time to wander at your own pace, explore preserved samurai residences, pop into museums and browse local shops for hand-crafted souvenirs. These activities are all set along tree-lined streets brought to life by cherry blossoms in spring. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Akita
blocks.text: This full-day tour blends nature and history with stops at the 1400-feet-deep Lake Tazawa — Japan’s deepest lake — and the samurai streets of Kakunodate. Along the way, you’ll hear legends of dragons, explore traditional manor homes and enjoy a peaceful lunch that lets you soak up the atmosphere between each storied stop. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Akita City Red Brick Folklore Museum & Sake Brewery
blocks.text: Start with a step into Akita’s artistic soul at the Red Brick Folklore Museum, showcasing metalwork, woodblock prints and the stories behind them. Then explore the local market before heading to a traditional sake brewery for a behind-the-scenes look at how rice becomes ritual — with a tasting to top it off. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kakunodate Samurai Town
blocks.text: Walk in the footsteps of samurai through the cobbled streets of Kakunodate. Visit restored homes like Aoyagi and Ishiguro, where you’ll see antique armor, elegant gardens and artifacts passed down through generations. Cap off your cultural immersion with a classic Japanese lunch that ties the day together. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Oga Peninsula: Mt. Kanpuzan Observatory & Namahage Museum
blocks.text: Venture out to the dramatic Oga Peninsula, where rotating views from Mt. Kanpuzan Observatory reveal forests, coastlines and the Sea of Japan. Then it’s on to the Namahage Museum, where you’ll meet the region’s fearsome folk figures — horned demons that have patrolled these hills in legend for centuries. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Tradition & Art Museums of Akita
blocks.text: Immerse yourself in local craftsmanship with visits to the Red Brick Folklore Museum and the Performing Arts Heritage Center, home to dazzling displays of Kanto lanterns and festival traditions. A stop at the lively market and a glimpse of a historic samurai-era home add texture to your Akita day. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Akita port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Cruises to Akita might not be as well-known as Tokyo or Kyoto, but that’s part of the magic. As a port of call for Japan cruises, it delivers a rare blend of peaceful scenery, vibrant local life and deeply rooted traditions — all just steps from where your ship docks. blocks.heading: Things to do in Aomori
blocks.text: Sitting at the northern tip of Honshu in Japan's Tohoku region, Aomori is a city where nothing just sits still — not the history, not the landscapes and definitely not the Nebuta Matsuri festival floats. This is a city where music echoes through the streets, hot springs steam in the shadow of snowy peaks and centuries-old customs are constantly rejuvenated with new life and intensity. The rhythm o

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Aomori
blocks.text: Aomori invites you to go big (and not want to go home). The statues are enormous, the floats are elaborate and the landscapes stretch as far as the stories behind them. Princess excursions tap into that energy, offering experiences that are bold and layered, with each one feeling like a slice of larger-than-life.

blocks.heading: Trekking in Shirakami Mountains
blocks.text: Lace up your boots and head into the UNESCO-protected Shirakami range, one of Japan’s last virgin beech forests. Your trek includes wildlife sightings, ancient trees and a rare glimpse into the country’s untouched natural heart. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Best of Aomori
blocks.text: This full-day adventure checks all the boxes. Start with a visit to the enormous bronze Buddha at Seiryu Temple, then ascend Mt. Hakkoda by aerial tram to see the big picture. Tour a reconstructed Jomon-era village and wrap up at the Nebuta Warasse Museum, where festival spirit is always alive and well. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Hirosaki Castle Park, Nebuta Festival Floats & Garden
blocks.text: A castle with centuries of stories, a museum of glowing floats and one of Japan’s most idyllic gardens — all in one unforgettable outing. Enjoy a buffet lunch and then step into the heart of Hirosaki’s summer tradition at Neputa-mura, where artistry, legend and local pride are the life of the party. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Mt. Hakkoda Aerial Tram & Lake Towada Cruise
blocks.text: Take your sightseeing to new heights — and depths. Ride high above volcanic ridges on the Mt. Hakkoda ropeway, then descend to Lake Towada for a boat cruise across crater-born waters. Keep an eye out for waterfalls, wild flora and photo ops galore. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Highlights of Aomori
blocks.text: Pressed for time? This half-day tour delivers maximum impact with minimum effort. See Japan’s largest bronze seated Buddha, tour the Nebuta Warasse Museum and still make it back to the ship with time for shopping or a bite to eat (the region is renowned for its distinctive seafood dishes). VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Hirosaki Castle Park & Neputa Festival Exhibition Hall
blocks.text: Bring the past to life with a trip to Hirosaki’s historic castle and its surrounding park. Then get more modern with a look at float culture at the Neputa Exhibition Hall. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Highlights of Tsugaru
blocks.text: This cultural sampler serves up local craftsmanship, astonishing views and a bit of sweetness. Visit a pottery studio, snap shots of Japan’s longest wooden triple-arched bridge and wrap things up at Apple Hill Namioka — home to some of Aomori’s best apple goodies. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Sukayu Hot Spring Onsen Experience
blocks.text: Sink into serenity at one of Japan’s most beloved hot springs. After a traditional lunch, unwind in the mineral-rich waters of Sukayu Onsen, where silence and relaxation are golden. Just be aware that etiquette is equally valued, so read up on the excursion notes beforehand. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Things to do in Beppu
blocks.text: Beppu is a city full of little surprises. Steam curls up from the sidewalks, mineral waters bubble beneath the surface and traditional ryokans peek out from forested hillsides. Although some may think of it as a simple hot spring town, it’s really a place where nature and ritual come together in unexpectedly beautiful ways. A Beppu cruise invites you to settle into the moment. Wander among the geo

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Beppu
blocks.text: If Beppu’s streets seem to breathe steam, its excursions breathe adventure into your Beppu cruise. Each one is grounded in the land’s natural rhythms and stories.

blocks.heading: Yufuin Village & Onsen
blocks.text: Yufuin offers a softer side of Japan. Shop a bit, stroll along Kinrinko Lake or stop for matcha and handmade sweets. Top it off by easing into one of the area’s scenic hot spring baths. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Usa Jingu Shrine & Boiling Hell Hot Springs
blocks.text: Start with a stroll through the stately halls of Usa Jingu, one of Japan’s oldest shrines. Then make your way back into town for a walk past Beppu’s “Boiling Hells,” where mineral waters spout and shimmer in every shade imaginable. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Mt. Takasaki Monkey Park & Boiling Hell Hot Springs
blocks.text: The monkeys are the main draw here, but the landscape is no slouch either. Watch the macaques roam, then visit Beppu’s famous hot springs where the Earth shows off what it’s got bubbling under the surface. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Usuki Stone Buddhas & Castle Ruins
blocks.text: Trace Japan’s religious roots at the Usuki Buddhas — timeworn, humbling and quietly grand. Then wander the nearby castle ruins, where samurai once stood and now gardens take their place. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Things to do in Busan
blocks.text: Busan might be South Korea’s second-largest city, but it doesn’t play second fiddle when it comes to memorable experiences. This is a city that embraces opposites — and invites you to dive into the in-between. You’ll find ancient temples tucked into wooded hillsides, bold street markets humming with life and modern neighborhoods that seem to climb the sky. Whether you’re tracing history, tasting y

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Busan
blocks.text: Busan’s shore excursions cover the spectrum, from spiritual sanctuaries to modern cityscapes. Whether you're tracing the legacy of ancient dynasties or taking in views from the coastline, there’s no shortage of ways to see South Korea’s second city through a fresh lens. Fan favorite shore excursions in Busan include visiting Gamcheon Culture Village, exploring Jagalchi Fish Market, and touring the

blocks.heading: Temple by the Sea & X the SKY Observatory
blocks.text: From the crashing waves near Haedong Yonggungsa Temple to the clouds above X the SKY, this tour hits high notes. After exploring the seaside sanctuary, head 100 floors up for panoramic views of Busan. Cap off your journey in Gukje Market, where alleyways burst with local flavors and finds. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Best of Gyeong-Ju
blocks.text: Spend a day exploring Gyeong-Ju, the ancient capital of the Silla Kingdom. Visit Tumuli Park to see royal tombs, browse treasures at the National Museum and enjoy a traditional Korean lunch. Then head to Bulguksa Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site tucked into Mt. Tohamsan. History, architecture and nature meet in this immersive full-day outing. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Best of Busan
blocks.text: See the full spectrum of Busan life such as the sea-swept Haedong Yonggungsa Temple or city markets buzzing with color. This day tour includes photo stops at Haeundae Beach and a walk through Yongdusan Park, with shopping stops at Gukje Market and Jagalchi Fish Market. It's a deep dive into local culture with a flavorful buffet lunch. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Haedong Yonggungsa Temple
blocks.text: Soak up ocean views and spiritual calm at Haedong Yonggungsa Temple, uniquely set along the rocky coast. After climbing 108 steps past statues and pagodas, take in this serene landmark. You'll also visit Dongbaekseom Island and the APEC House before heading to Gukje Market, with a glimpse of the 24,000-foot Gwangan Grand Bridge en route. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Ja-Gal-Ch’i Market & Beomeosa Temple
blocks.text: Visit two of Busan’s cultural icons on this half-day outing. First stop: Beomeosa Temple, founded in 678 A.D. and home to a centuries-old three-stone pagoda. Then head downtown to Ja-Gal-Ch’i Market, a seafood haven founded by women vendors during the Korean War — and still buzzing with life, flavors and local color. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Korean Spa Experience & Market
blocks.text: Slip into pure relaxation at Spa Land in Shinsegae Centum City, a public bathhouse with 13 themed spas and a traditional Finnish sauna. After your soak, head to Gukje Market to browse for gifts, try street food or just soak up the scene. It’s a blissful combo of pampering and people-watching. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Busan — Past & Present
blocks.text: Explore Busan’s evolving story on this tour of culture, history and shopping. Begin at Bokcheon Museum, home to artifacts from the Three Kingdoms period and nearby ancient tombs. Then head to modern-day Busan with stops at Yongdusan Park and Lotte Department Store, one of Korea’s premier shopping destinations. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Gamcheon Culture Village & Markets
blocks.text: Explore Gamcheon Culture Village, a hillside neighborhood of color, murals and maze-like alleys that locals have lovingly transformed. Then stroll the Songdo Sky Walk for ocean views and dragon-like curves. End your outing at Jagalchi and Gukje Markets, where food, crafts and keepsakes bring Busan’s spirit to life. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Experience the Busan port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Cruises to Busan blend coastal beauty with vibrant city life, and arriving by sea lets you experience both from the moment you step off the ship. This bustling port is your jumping-off point to temples that hug the shore, markets alive with seafood and souvenirs and neighborhoods where tradition meets the modern edge. blocks.heading: Things to do in Hakodate
blocks.text: Hakodate is located on Hokkaido, Japan’s northernmost main island. Positioned along the southern coast of Hokkaido, the city serves as a gateway to the region and is known for its blend of natural scenery, historic sites, and coastal views. Hakodate doesn’t try to impress with flash. Instead, it wins you over with quiet confidence — a market humming with local life, a star-shaped fort that rewrote

blocks.heading: Top attractions and shore excursions in Hakodate
blocks.text: Princess shore excursions help you unlock the real Hakodate — complete with seafood, cityscapes and a little architecture-based time travel.

blocks.heading: Guided in Japanese: Onuma Quasi-National Park
blocks.text: Board the bus and drive about 20km to Onuma Quasi-National Park. This park was designated a quasi-national park in 1958 and is characterized by its beautiful scenery formed by the ancient volcanic activity of Mt. Komagatake. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Hakodate
blocks.text: This all-in-one tour takes you to the city’s headline spots, including the buzzing Morning Market, peaceful Trappistine Convent, pentagon-shaped Goryokaku Fort and the scenic summit of Mt. Hakodate. A ride on the aerial tram and some time at the historic red brick warehouses round out the experience. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Mt. Hakodate & Morning Market
blocks.text: Early risers and city-view chasers will love this half-day excursion. Visit the Morning Market to see what’s fresh (spoiler alert: it’s all fresh), then ascend Mt. Hakodate by ropeway for sweeping city and harbor views. The outing also includes a guided walk through the character-rich Motomachi District. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Fort Goryokaku
blocks.text: History buffs take note: this tour focuses on Goryokaku Park, Japan’s first Western-style fort and the site of a major 19th-century battle. Climb Goryokaku Tower for a sky-high look at the fort’s unique star-shaped layout before heading back to port. It is especially beautiful in the spring, particularly April and May, as these months are when the cherry blossoms are their brightest. However, summ

blocks.heading: Easy Hakodate
blocks.text: Ideal for guests who prefer a panoramic experience without having to break a sweat. Take in views from Mt. Hakodate, then enjoy a relaxing drive through the city’s highlights including Motomachi, Goryokaku Tower and the brick-lined waterfront. Snap a few pictures and savor the city’s laid-back charm. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Hakodate port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Princess Japan cruise destinations bring you face to face with the country’s many moods — and Hakodate offers one of the most unique. You’ll step off the ship and straight into a place where history feels close and the connection feels even closer. Cruises to Hakodate make discovering Hokkaido easier than ever.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Hiroshima
blocks.text: Hiroshima is a city that has transformed heartbreak into hope and remembrance into resilience. Forever marked in history as the first city struck by an atomic bomb, today it stands powerful and full of hope for the future, a testament to peace and renewal. Those who visit gain an understanding that there's more to Hiroshima than the iconic Atomic Bomb Dome and Peace Memorial Park — this city is al

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Hiroshima
blocks.text: From thought-provoking memorials to scenic sanctuaries and unique bites, these Princess excursions offer distinct ways to experience Hiroshima and its surroundings. Expand your cruise to Hiroshima with one or more of these curated activities.

blocks.heading: Hiroshima by Tram & Foot
blocks.text: See the city like a local — hop on a tram, travel through the urban core and dig into Hiroshima’s signature okonomiyaki at a dedicated eatery. Wrap it up with a visit to the Shukkeien Garden, where miniaturized landscapes provide a relaxing end to your day. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Best of Hiroshima
blocks.text: This full-day tour covers both emotional and aesthetic highlights. Begin on Miyajima Island, where the red torii of Itsukushima Shrine appears to float at high tide, then return to the city for a visit to Peace Memorial Park and Museum. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Peace Memorial Park, Atomic Bomb Dome & Museum
blocks.text: A focused and reflective journey through Hiroshima’s most iconic memorials. This guided visit walks you through the history, heartbreak and hope of a city that became the symbol of a global call for harmony. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Iwakuni Castle & Historical Wooden Arch Bridge
blocks.text: History buffs, take note: This excursion pairs a sweeping castle view with a walk across Kintai-kyo, one of Japan’s architectural marvels. Add in a cable car ride, a traditional lunch and scenic parkland, and you’ve got a day full of heritage and perspective. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Miyajima & Itsukushima Shrine
blocks.text: A half-day escape to sacred Miyajima Island, where you’ll visit one of Japan’s most picturesque shrines. Itsukushima Shrine’s striking red structures and serene shoreline setting create a peaceful change of pace and postcard-perfect photo ops. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.text: A must-visit destination in the Japan itineraries — typically 9 to 11 day voyages roundtrip from Tokyo (Yokohama), with stops in ports like Osaka (Kobe), Kochi, Nagasaki and Busan, South Korea — the Hiroshima cruise port places you right next to the city's most meaningful attractions.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Hitachinaka
blocks.text: Hitachinaka, located in Ibaraki Prefecture along Japan's Pacific coast roughly 100 km north of Tokyo, is renowned for its vibrant and colorful landscapes, particularly at Hitachi Seaside Park, where spring brings a breathtaking display of over 4.5 million baby blue nemophila flowers, and autumn transforms the hills into a sea of crimson kochia bushes. You won’t want to miss the bustling Nakaminato

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Hitachinaka
blocks.text: With so much to see and do in Hitachinaka, Princess can make it easy. We’ll take you to local sites like the seaside park and to farther away must-see spots like Nikko.

blocks.heading: Easy Hitachinaka
blocks.text: Settle in for a relaxed, easy day that includes some of Hitachinaka's top photo opportunities. Begin with a scenic drive through the Hitachi Seaside Park to the Oarai area, where you'll stop to photograph Oarai Isosaki Shrine, set dramatically overlooking the turbulent waters and protected by a torii gate, aptly named "Kamiiso-no-Torii," which translates to "gate at the beach of the gods." LEARN M

blocks.heading: Best of Ibaraki
blocks.text: If you love gardens and flowers, look no further than Kairakuen Garden. We’ll take you to this wonder that’s considered one of the three most beautiful gardens in all of Japan. This garden is home to over 300 plum trees that bloom in the spring and paint the branches in pink. Right next door is Tokiwa Shrine, a Shinto shrine dedicated to the spirits of two prominent local lords from the nineteenth

blocks.heading: Word Heritage Nikko Toshogu Shrine
blocks.text: See one of the most beautiful and lavish shrines in all of Japan during this daytrip to nearby Nikko. Nikko Toshogu Shrine is a memorial for Tokugawa Ieyasu, the first shogun who created a 250 year dynasty, and features more gold leaf and intricate carvings than the other shrines you’ll see in the country. There’s a reason it’s a UNESCO World Heritage Site. You’ll see both Shinto and Buddhist elem

blocks.heading: Highlights of Ibaraki
blocks.text: Ready to walk through rolling hills of bright blue blossoms? That’s what happens when you visit Hitachi Seaside Park in the spring — around 4.5 million Nemophila flowers bloom in the park. If your cruise is later, no worries. The flower colors change with the season. Bringing the kids? There’s also a ferris wheel that gives you great views and a fun ride. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ushiku Buddha and Mt. Tsukuba Ushiku Buddha and Mt. Tsukuba
blocks.text: Get ready to feel small when you stand next to this monument in Japan: the Ushiku Buddha is one of the tallest bronze Buddha statues in the world! After you take in the sheer size of this statue, enjoy the Japanese gardens at its base and the Mt. Tsukuba Shrine. This particular shrine has been a place of worship in Japan for 3,000 years — and from there you can take a cable car up the mountain for

blocks.heading: Historical Mito "Tokugawa"
blocks.text: Ibaraki Prefecture, the area ruled by the Mito Tokugawa family, is celebrated on this fascinating adventure that pays tribute to this prominent branch of the Tokugawa clan. Your first stop is The Tokugawa Museum, built in 1977 and displaying more than 30,000 family heirlooms that showcase the family's cultural influence. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kasama Pottery and Kasama Inari Shrine
blocks.text: A day of artistry and spirituality awaits on this delightful sojourn to the City of Kasama, famed for its distinctive pottery production and namesake shrine. Begin with a visit to the Ibaraki Ceramic Art Museum and delve into the history of the unique local pottery that involves mixing several types of clay with pieces of granite. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Hitachinaka port on your next cruise
blocks.text: From towering statues of the Buddha to rolling hills of millions of blossoms, the historical and natural beauty of Hitachinaka makes it a must-visit destination on your Japan cruise. Plus it’s a perfect gateway to the stunning Nikko shrine and nearby national park that draws visitors from all over the world. blocks.text: Ishigaki offers a distinctly tropical side of Japan, with a subtropical climate, white-sand beaches and clear turquoise waters. The island is surrounded by vibrant coral reefs, making it a popular destination for snorkeling and diving, while inland areas feature lush greenery, mangroves and scenic viewpoints. blocks.heading: Things to do in Kagoshima
blocks.text: Nestled on the southwestern tip of Japan’s Kyushu Island, Kagoshima is a picturesque coastal city famous for its striking views of the active Sakurajima volcano across the bay that’s erupted 30 times. Sakurajima, one of Japan’s most active volcanoes, sits directly across from Kagoshima’s port and is easily accessible by a short ferry ride, making it the city’s most iconic and must-see attraction.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Kagoshima
blocks.text: Top shore excursions in Kagoshima include visiting Sakurajima volcano, exploring Sengan-en Garden, shopping and dining in Tenmonkan, and relaxing in nearby hot springs. Stand at the base of a conical volcano, walk in the footsteps of samurai, take a relaxing sand bath and maybe spot a glimpse of the magical lake monster Issie when you visit Kagoshima with Princess.

blocks.heading: Kinko Bay Highlights: Shrines, Volcano and Vinegar Fields
blocks.text: Japanese black vinegar has been heralded as a culinary staple and cultural icon, and you can see how it's made. Explore the expansive “pot fields” where the freshly made jars of vinegar are set out to age for six months. Plus, this excursion will also take you to the Terukuni Shrine where you can walk under a massive torii gate and tree trimmed to look like a crane — the symbol of the Satsuma clan

blocks.heading: Best of Kagoshima

Sakurajima — the volcano that dominates Kagoshima Bay — where you’ll journey up to the clouds to see the crater spread out below you. blocks.text: Walk in the footsteps of some of the most historic samurai in Japan. Head to the samurai house in Chiran — nicknamed the “Little Kyoto of Satsuma" because it’s home to over 500 Edo period samurai homes. blocks.text: Relax in a one-of-a-kind sensory experience: a sand bath. During your bath, you’ll be covered in warm sand up to your neck and cocooned for a little while. Doing so can help increase blood flow, which can boost circulation and give your skin a little extra love. After you’ve soaked in the sand, you’ll shower off and get to try the traditional Japanese bath, the onsen. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Museum of the Meiji Restoration & Terukuni Shrine
blocks.text: Experience the Meiji Restoration for yourself by exploring this museum housed inside of the first Western-style factory ever built in Japan. blocks.heading: Things to do in Kanazawa
blocks.text: Kanazawa is the kind of city where exploration pays off. Follow a moss-lined path and you might find a teahouse where modern Geisha pay homage to storied traditions, then turn a corner near the castle and maybe discover a cutting-edge art installation. This is a place where time folds in interesting ways, and every neighborhood has its own story tucked behind a noren curtain.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Kanazawa
blocks.text: Whether you want hands-on art or hands-off serenity, Princess excursions give you insider access to this coastal jewel’s best-kept secrets.

blocks.heading: Shirakawago On Your Own
blocks.text: Prefer to march to the beat of your own taiko drum? This self-guided outing to Shirakawago lets you explore at your own pace. Take in scenic vistas, roam among gassho-style farmhouses and craft your own perfect day. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Best of Kanazawa
blocks.text: Make every moment count on a full-day adventure through Kanazawa’s highlights: geisha quarters, market halls, landscaped gardens and a museum that is a work of art all by itself. This outing layers Kanazawa’s history, creativity and cuisine into one unforgettable package. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Shirakawago Village & Gokayama Village
blocks.text: Leave the city behind and swap paved roads for timeless mountain charm. These historic hamlets are all steep roofs, peaceful lanes and the soft clatter of daily life. Shirakawago invites you to slow down and see what centuries of tradition feel like under your feet, then Gokayama gets your hands involved with some traditional paper-making. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Eiheiji Buddhist Temple & Tojinbo
blocks.text: Trade city sounds for temple bells on this contemplative journey to Eiheiji, a sacred Zen sanctuary deep in the woods. Afterward, head seaside to Tojinbo to see volcanic cliffs and wave-carved rock pillars come together to create one of Japan’s most dramatic natural cathedrals. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Gold Leaf Art & Japanese Sweet Making
blocks.text: In this hands-on workshop, you’ll create shimmering gold leaf art, then balance the bling by learning how to make ‘wagashi’ (seasonal treats that often accompany tea ceremonies). This is one feast for the senses that you can really chew on. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Kenrokuen Gardens, Samurai & Geisha Districts
blocks.text: Take a daytrip through Kanazawa’s greatest hits. Begin your journey in Kenroku-en Garden (a living masterclass in landscape design), then trace the footsteps of samurai in Nagamachi’s historic district. Finally, visit the softly lit lanes of Higashi Chayamachi. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Experience the Kanazawa port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Cruises to Japan reveal a country that is both ancient and evolving — and Kanazawa proves it. Step ashore into a city where tradition is preserved not just in buildings, but in the way people live, eat and create. blocks.heading: Things to do in Keelung (Taipei)
blocks.text: What’s your pleasure? Soaking up centuries of Chinese art or soaking in a thermal spring, this port promises moments you won’t soon forget. Cruises to Keelung, the primary cruise gateway to Taipei, and uncover cultural treasures, natural wonders and more noodles than you can shake a chopstick at.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Keelung and Taipei
blocks.text: With Princess, your time ashore becomes a choose-your-own-adventure filled with history, hot springs and hidden-gem villages. Here are a few excursions that might catch your eye — or your camera lens.

blocks.heading: City Drive, Lungshan Temple & Handicraft Center
blocks.text: Cruise through Taipei’s highlights on wheels and by foot (but mostly wheels). Stop at Lungshan Temple, browse 40,000 handmade items at the Handicraft Center and snap your own picture-perfect moment in front of the gleaming Taipei 101. Check your watch, because it’s time for souvenirs. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Yang Ming Shan Hot Springs & Yehliu Geographic Park
blocks.text: Slip into misty bliss at Tienlai Hot Springs Resort, where the volcanic slopes of Yangmingshan set the scene for a soothing soak. After lunch, head to the coastline’s lunar playground — Yehliu Geo Park — to witness wind-carved rock formations that feel more sci-fi than seaside. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: National Palace Museum, Chiang Kai Shek & Temples
blocks.text: History buffs, prepare for a triple hit of culture. Visit ornate temples, see the guard ceremony at Martyr’s Shrine and explore one of the world’s most impressive collections of Chinese artifacts at the National Palace Museum — all capped off with a buffet fit for an emperor. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Chiufen Walking Tour
blocks.text: Once a mining village, now a maze of steep alleys and red lanterns, Chiufen feels like it stepped out of an animated Japanese fairytale — think dreamlike bathhouses and glowing lanterns. Wind your way through hillside streets packed with craft stalls, sizzling dumplings and sweeping views. It’s cinematic in every sense. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: National Palace & Chiang Kai Shek's Memorial Hall
blocks.text: Take in Taipei’s icons — from the stoic Martyr’s Shrine to the commanding presence of Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall. Visit the National Palace Museum and catch a glimpse of Taipei 101, the skyscraper that looks like a stack of lucky charms reaching into the clouds. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Experience the Keelung port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Keelung cruises are typically included within larger Asian cruise itineraries: including Japan, Korea, or Southeast Asia. This quaint location somehow feels both tucked away and yet intrinsically connected to Taiwan’s cultural core. blocks.heading: Things to do in Kobe
blocks.text: From imposing feudal-era fortifications to modern street-side food stands, the region around Kobe is rich with sights and stories that stretch across ages. Ancient temples nestle between gleaming skyscrapers, while traditional sake breweries share neighborhoods with cutting-edge research facilities, creating a tapestry where every corner reveals another layer of Japan's evolution. The mountains th

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Kobe
blocks.text: Whether you’re craving something educational, something scenic or just some warm sake, Princess excursions make the most of every minute on shore. Here are a few of the Princess curated experiences designed to turn Kobe cruises into even more-unforgettable adventures.

blocks.heading: Kobe, Sake Brewery Museum & Mt Rokko
blocks.text: You don’t want to leave Kobe without sampling the local flavor — especially when that flavor comes from a centuries-old sake brewery. Learn the steps behind the sip, enjoy a tasting and then head to the top of Mt Rokko for panoramic views that stretch from Kobe Bay to the Inland Sea. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Temples of Nara
blocks.text: This full-day excursion heads to Nara, Japan’s first capital and a UNESCO-recognized cultural treasure. From the towering Great Buddha at Todaiji Temple to the peaceful grounds of Toshodaiji and Yakushiji, this tour is ideal for those seeking spiritual depth (and pmaybe a little photogenic self satisfaction). VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Kyoto: Fushimi-Inari Shrine, Sanjusangendo Temple & Zen Garden
blocks.text: Get swept up in Kyoto’s sacred spaces with a visit to its iconic red torii gates, over 1000 golden Kannon statues and one of the most famous Zen rock gardens in the world. With a traditional lunch and plenty of legroom on the coach, it’s a full day of meditative marvels. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Himeji Castle & Kokoen Garden
blocks.text: Nicknamed the White Heron Castle, Himeji is Japan’s most elegant fortress — and you’ll see why when its towers and turrets come into view. Afterward, unwind in the harmony of Kokoen Garden, a beautifully designed tribute to the art of landscape and leisure. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Best of Kyoto: Golden Pavilion, Nijo Castle & Heian Shrine
blocks.text: Kyoto’s all-stars await: the gold-leaf shimmer of Kinkakuji, the squeaky ‘nightingale floors’ of Nijo Castle and one of Japan’s largest torii gates at Heian Shrine. Cap it off with lunch and a shopping stop at the Kyoto Handicraft Center before heading back to the ship. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Experience the Kobe port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Kobe is a port (and an historically significant one at that), but it’s also so much more. This beautiful city is a strategic and cultural touchpoint that ties together some of Japan’s most sought-after destinations. blocks.heading: Things to do in Kochi
blocks.text: Kochi is a culture- and history-focused destination, known for its traditional Japanese experiences rather than resort-style attractions. This is a port for travelers who like their history with a view and their sightseeing with a little of everything. From historic Kochi Castle to the vibrant atmosphere of Hirome Market and the scenic beauty of Katsurahama Beach, Kochi offers a range of cultural

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Kochi
blocks.text: Princess shore excursions in Kochi take you right to the center of the island’s story, landscapes and culture of creativity. Whatever your interests, a Princess excursion can help you find what you’re looking for.

blocks.heading: Ryugado Cave & Katsurahama Beach
blocks.text: Step into the depths of time inside Ryugado Cave, a sprawling limestone labyrinth filled with stalactites and underground waterfalls. Then swap shadows for sea spray at Katsurahama Beach, a dramatic stretch of coastline where history stands tall and the sea is a surging, azure blue. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Monet’s Garden & Makino Botanical Garden
blocks.text: Wander through blooming paths and botanical wonders as you explore two of Kochi’s most scenic sanctuaries. Begin at Monet’s Garden, a tribute to the French artist’s lush landscapes, reimagined in Japanese soil. After a locally inspired lunch, continue to Makino Botanical Garden, where thousands of plant species pay homage to one of Japan’s pioneering botanists. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Oboke Gorge
blocks.text: Brace yourself for this journey through Iya Valley across the vine-woven Kazurabashi Bridge (we’d tell you not to look down, but that’s all part of the experience). Once you’ve got your feet back on solid ground, hop a boat and float through Oboke Gorge on the beautiful Yoshino River. Expect dramatic rock formations, lush forested slopes and a whole lot of excited pointing. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cape Muroto & Muroto Geopark Center
blocks.text: Only in Kochi can a morning hike turn into a geology lesson and a spiritual awakening. Traverse a landscape shaped by earthquakes, peek into the cave where a legendary monk may have had his big ‘aha!’ moment, then climb to a temple with views so lofty they practically come with their own enlightenment. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kochi Castle & Katsurahama Beach
blocks.text: Get two icons in one outing. First, scale the heights of Kochi Castle and step into the shoes of a 17th-century warlord. Then head to Katsurahama Beach to pay homage to the renegade samurai Sakamoto Ryoma, a man whose vision of a unified Japan helped topple the Tokugawa shogunate. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Best of Kochi with Local Artisans, Sake and Lunch at Bunzo
blocks.text: Channel your inner artisan with a deep dive into local craft and culture. Paint calligraphy at a high school club, tour a flag-making studio, taste test sake and leave your wish behind at a Shinto shrine — all with local experts guiding the way. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Kochi port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Kochi is usually visited as part of broader Japan and Asia cruise itineraries, often alongside other cultural and coastal destinations.
