blocks.heading: Things to do in Kushiro
blocks.text: Kushiro may be known as the “town of mist,” but there’s nothing hazy about its appeal. This port city on Hokkaido’s southeastern coast is where wild marshlands meet a vibrant town life, and where red-crowned cranes glide as gracefully as the boats along its harbor. With Japan’s largest wetlands, sweeping ocean views and a rich seafood culture, Kushiro is filled with both quiet, natural wonders and

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Kushiro
blocks.text: Shore excursions with Princess are always breathtaking, and cruises to Kushiro are no exception. Enjoy drifting across the still waters of a volcanic lake or seeing the expansive landscapes in person — whatever you choose, these excursions in Kushiro connect you to Japan’s natural rhythms and ancient traditions.

blocks.heading: Kushiro Crane Reserve & Fish Market
blocks.text: See graceful cranes up close at the conservation-focused Kushiro Crane Reserve. Then step into local life at the Washo Fish Market, where you can create your own seafood bowl by choosing toppings stall by stall. With a quick stop at the Kushiro Museum along the way, this excursion blends nature, culture and cuisine. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Lake Akan Boat Excursion Tour
blocks.text: Travel inland to Lake Akan, a serene crater lake known for its rare marimo algae and volcanic beauty. Cruise across its calm waters, visit the Marimo Exhibition Center, and pause at a lakeside resort for a Japanese-style lunch. Along the way, enjoy sweeping views of the Kushiro Wetlands and a stop at the scenic Shitsugen Observatory. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kushiro’s Natural Wonders
blocks.text: Begin your day at the Kushiro Crane Reserve, where red-crowned cranes — once nearly extinct — roam freely. Then head into Japan’s largest marshland, Kushiro Shitsugen National Park. From an observatory, you’ll take in views of vast wetlands and distant volcanic peaks, soaking in the natural beauty that defines this protected region. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Kushiro port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Kushiro may be a little off the radar, but that’s what makes it such a special stop on Japan cruises. From the moment you step off the ship, you’re surrounded by raw natural beauty and authentic local culture — no tour buses required. The port’s compact, walkable location means you can easily explore shops, museums and markets on foot or head out into the wild marshlands just beyond the city.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Maizuru
blocks.text: This coastal city knows how to make an entrance. Maizuru opens wide with a bay full of naval history, a horizon of red-brick buildings and enough panoramic views to eat up your phone storage. It’s calm, compact and ready to surprise you.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Maizuru
blocks.text: From UNESCO World Heritage Sites to seaside legends that stretch toward the heavens, Maizuru offers a launchpad for some of Japan’s most captivating experiences.

blocks.heading: Amanohashidate & Motoise Konojinja Shrine
blocks.text: This excursion combines legendary landscapes with sacred architecture. Walk the length of Amanohashidate (one of Japan’s three top scenic views), then visit Motoise Kono Shrine, where centuries of Shinto history are carved into every detail. Wrap it up with a ride to Kasamatsu Park for one last sky-high view before heading back to the ship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Kyoto
blocks.text: Kyoto is less of a city and more of a time machine, and this tour hits its biggest moments. Start at the Golden Pavilion, where gold leaf and reflection pools create one of Japan’s most iconic scenes. Continue to Nijojo Castle, a UNESCO-listed site that takes architecture very seriously. End with a visit to Heian Jingu Shrine, where the torii gate alone is worth the trip. Lunch is included, and th

blocks.heading: Kinkakuji Temple & Arashiyama District On Your Own
blocks.text: Spend the day exploring Kyoto at your own pace. After admiring the Golden Pavilion’s brilliant glow, you’ll head to the Arashiyama District for free time to eat, shop or just get delightfully lost. The bamboo groves, riverside paths and indie boutiques make this an ideal stop for guests who want less lecture and more choose-your-own-adventure. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kyoto On Your Own
blocks.text: This is your chance to see Kyoto your way. Get dropped off in the heart of the city and chart your own course through centuries of culture and craftsmanship. You might climb the steps of Kiyomizu Temple, explore the shogunate grandeur of Nijo Castle or wander Gion’s stone-paved streets, where traditional teahouses still hum with quiet elegance. blocks.heading: Things to do in Matsuyama
blocks.text: Some ports feel like a stop. Matsuyama feels like an invitation. This city has a way of slowing you down, handing you a rice dumpling and telling you to take a bath (of the hot-spring variety). With its literary roots, deep history and soothing onsen, it’s the kind of place that stays with you long after your towel’s dried.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Matsuyama
blocks.text: These excursions are proof that Matsuyama is more than just peaceful baths and pretty views; it’s a city layered with stories, secrets and excellent snacks.

blocks.heading: Dogo Onsen Hot Spring & Ishiteji Temple
blocks.text: Ease into your day at Asuka-no-Yu, a bathhouse styled after ancient Japanese architecture. Slip into the hot springs and soak up the silence. After your dip, continue to Ishiteji Temple, a spiritual and architectural standout featuring a cave-linked inner temple and a gate so revered it’s a designated National Treasure. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Matsuyama
blocks.text: Start your day with a cable car ride to Matsuyama Castle, perched 433 feet above the city. Take off your shoes to explore its carefully preserved halls filled with relics from the Matsudaira Clan. After a visit to the Buddhist landmark Ishiteji Temple, where sacred artifacts meet sweeping pagodas, you’ll enjoy a local lunch before heading to Dogo Onsen. Here, a soak in Japan’s oldest hot spring le

blocks.heading: Uchiko & Ozu On Your Own
blocks.text: Wander through history at your own pace with this self-guided trip to two well-preserved towns. Uchiko, once rich from wax and paper, is now home to 90 original buildings and streets that feel frozen in time. From there, head to Ozu, a castle town with narrow alleys, gardens and riverside views that seem tailor-made for aimless exploring. No agenda and no pressure, just pure old-school charm. LEAR

blocks.heading: Highlights of Matsuyama
blocks.text: This rapid-fire tour takes you to the essentials. Visit Dogo Onsen for a look (or dip) into the bathhouse that inspired centuries of literature. Then head to Ishiteji Temple, part of the Shikoku Pilgrimage Route and packed with historic relics. Finish at Matsuyama Castle, where you’ll ascend to sweeping views and museum-quality displays that bring the Edo period to life. LEARN MORE

blocks.text: Princess ships dock within easy reach of the city, offering quick access to everything from castle towers to steam-filled bathhouses. blocks.heading: Things to do in Miyako
blocks.text: Miyako blends rugged coastal scenery with peaceful cultural sites, offering everything from dramatic cliffs and caves to quiet shrines tucked into the hills. It’s a destination where outdoor adventure and local history share the same shoreline.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Miyako
blocks.text: Miyako’s excursions take you deeper into the landscapes that define this part of Iwate, from towering sea cliffs and limestone caves to cultural landmarks shaped by centuries of history. Whether you prefer staggering coastlines or thoughtful heritage experiences, each tour offers a different way to see the Sanriku region.

blocks.heading: KAMAISHI: Daikannon Statue and The Iron and Steel Museum
blocks.text: Travel to the hilltop Kamaishi Daikannon Statue for panoramic views over the bay, then continue to the Iron and Steel Museum to trace the city’s role in Japan’s earliest industrial innovations. Hands-on displays and a full-size blast furnace replica bring the region’s history to life before your relaxed return drive to port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Iwate
blocks.text: See some of Iwate’s most dramatic natural wonders in one day, beginning with Ryusendo Cave, where underground lakes glow an unforgettable shade of blue. Then travel along the Sanriku coastline to view the towering Sannoiwa Rocks, stop for a fresh seafood lunch, and stroll Jodogahama Beach before boarding a coastal cruise to admire the shoreline from the water. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Chartered Sanriku Railway and Kitayamazaki Cliffs Observation Deck
blocks.text: Ride the Sanriku Railway along one of Japan’s most scenic coastlines, with sweeping views of rugged headlands and deep blue waters through panoramic windows. Continue to the Kuji Amber Museum, then travel to the Kitayamazaki Cliffs for an incredible vantage point over 656-foot formations stretching across miles of coastline. A local seafood lunch adds a regional touch to this full-day adventure. L

blocks.heading: KAMAISHI & TONO: Daikannon Statue, Tono Furusato Village and Fukuseji Temple
blocks.text: This cultural journey links seaside vistas with inland heritage. Visit the dramatic Kamaishi Daikannon Statue, perched high above the bay, then continue to Tono Furusato Village to explore preserved farmhouses and centuries-old rural traditions. After lunch, walk the peaceful grounds of Fukusenji Temple, home to a striking five-story pagoda tucked into the forested hillside. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Jodogahama Boat Cruise and Local Fish Market
blocks.text: Discover one of the Sanriku coast’s most beautiful stretches of shoreline with a stop at Jodogahama Beach, known for its white volcanic rocks and pine-covered ridges. A short walk leads you to a scenic cruise through sheltered waters, followed by time at the Miyako Fish Market to browse seasonal catches and meet local vendors. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Tsunami Remains Taro Kanko Hotel and Sanriku Geo Tour
blocks.text: Learn the region’s story of loss and recovery with a visit to the Taro Kanko Hotel, preserved as a memorial after the 2011 tsunami. After viewing the exhibits and dramatic vantage points inside the building, continue to the Sannoiwa Rocks for a geological perspective on the coastline’s power, then enjoy a quiet walk along Jodogahama Beach. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Miyakojima
blocks.text: Miyakojima pairs dazzling beaches with a laid-back island pace, offering coral-fringed coastlines, scenic bridges and viewpoints that show off the island’s bright blue waters. From local flavors to tropical landscapes, the island gives you plenty of reasons to explore between shores.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Miyakojima
blocks.text: Make the most of your day in Miyakojima with excursions that blend crystal water, island culture and scenic views. Whether you scuba or snorkel your way through the reefs or a guided look at the island’s natural landmarks, there’s an itinerary that fits your pace.

blocks.heading: Miyakojima North Explore
blocks.text: Head north for a half-day of island highlights, beginning at Miyakojima Marine Park where giant underwater windows reveal bright reef fish in their natural habitat. Visit the Yuki Shio Saltworks to see how the island’s famous mineral-rich salt is made, then continue to Ikema Bridge for views over jade-green water. A short walk through the Shimajiri mangroves wraps up this easy, nature-focused outi

blocks.heading: Best of Miyakojima
blocks.text: See Miyakojima’s standout sights on a full-day journey that pairs famous viewpoints with some of the island’s most loved beaches. You’ll stop at Irabu Ohashi Bridge for sweeping photo ops, visit the bird-shaped Makiyama Observatory and relax on Maehama Beach with its bright sand and calm, clear water. A stroll through Shimajiri Mangrove Park and a visit to the Yukishio salt facility round out this

blocks.heading: Maehama Beach On Your Own
blocks.text: Settle into a slow, sun-soaked morning or afternoon at Maehama Beach, a long curve of white sand with gentle waves and views of Kurima Island. Spend your free time swimming, lounging or renting water gear for a little extra fun. Food stands and small shops sit near the entrance, making it easy to grab a snack before the motorcoach brings you back to port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Highlights of Great Irabu bridge and island
blocks.text: Take a relaxed coastal drive to Miyako’s most photogenic corners, starting with Makiyama Observatory and its panoramic walkway above the sea. blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Miyazaki
blocks.text: Princess Cruises offers immersive excursions in Miyazaki that take you deep into southern Japan’s spiritual and cultural heritage. From ancient shrines in sea caves to quiet castle towns, each tour is crafted for meaningful connection with this serene region.

blocks.heading: Japanese-Language Guided Tours
blocks.text: Several excursions are also available with native Japanese guides for an enhanced local experience, including versions of the Aoshima & Obi Castle and Udo Jingu Shrine tours. These offer the same core itinerary but with in-language narration and cultural context for Japanese-speaking guests. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Aoshima & Obi Castle Town
blocks.text: Step into two of Miyazaki's most culturally rich locations. Begin your journey at Aoshima Island, where you’ll see the unique “Devil’s Washboard” rock formations and explore a vibrant shrine enveloped by subtropical forest. Then head to Obi Castle Town, a preserved samurai district with Edo-period architecture, offering a peaceful glimpse into Japan’s feudal past. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Aburatsu
blocks.text: This full-day experience gives you a deep dive into the highlights of southern Miyazaki. From coastal wonders to historical shrines and castle ruins, this excursion offers a perfect mix of natural beauty and cultural immersion. Explore the ruins of a unique 567-year-old castle and revered ancient shrines. This excursion is an ideal choice for first-time visitors who want to see it all. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Udo Jingu Shrine & Obi Castle
blocks.text: Visit Udo Jingu, an unforgettable seaside shrine dramatically built inside a coastal cave,one of Japan’s most unique sacred sites and over 2,000 years old. Then, continue to Obi Castle Ruins, where you'll wander the tranquil samurai-era streets of this historic town and imagine life in the Edo period. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Aoshima & Shouchu Brewery
blocks.text: Blend scenic beauty with cultural flavor on this half-day excursion. Explore the picturesque Aoshima Island ringed with beautiful, white sandy beaches, before heading to a local shochu brewery to learn about the production process of this beloved Japanese spirit — and enjoy a tasting, of course. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Muroran
blocks.text: Muroran is a must-see destination, offering stunning coastal scenery, dramatic cliffs and easy access to Hokkaido’s natural beauty. From the iconic Cape Chikyu Observatory to serene parks and cultural landmarks, it’s a stop packed with unforgettable views and experiences.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Muroran
blocks.text: Shore excursions in Muroran showcase the best of Hokkaido’s dramatic coastline, from the sweeping views at Cape Chikyu to the striking lava formations of nearby national parks. Whether you’re drawn to nature, culture or scenic photography, these tours offer unforgettable ways to experience the region.

blocks.heading: Mount Usu & Lake Toya
blocks.text: Board a motorcoach for a scenic drive through forested countryside to Shikotsu-Toya National Park and the dramatic “Rim of Fire.” Stop for photos at Lake Toya, a volcanic lake formed 100,000 years ago, before continuing to Mount Usu, one of Japan’s most active volcanoes. Ride the Ropeway gondola to the summit for sweeping views of the coast, Showa Shinzan and Mount Usu’s massive crater. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hokkaido Historical Village & Sapporo On Your Own
blocks.text: Depart Muroran by motorcoach for a scenic ride to the Historical Village, an open-air museum showcasing 53 preserved wooden and stone buildings from the Meiji and Taisho eras. Explore how early Hokkaido residents lived before returning to the city for free time in Odori Park, Sapporo’s beloved 13-block greenway. Enjoy lunch on your own, browse underground shops or ascend the TV Tower for sweeping

blocks.heading: Cruising Lake Toya & Crater Walk
blocks.text: Experience the dramatic landscapes of Shikotsu-Toya National Park on a journey through its volcanic wonders. Walk the Nishiyama Crater Trail to witness the impact of Mt. Usu’s 2000 eruption, then cruise across tranquil Lake Toya and explore its forested island. After a Japanese-style lunch, ride a gondola up Mount Usu for sweeping panoramic views before returning to port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Sapporo On Your Own
blocks.text: Create your own day of adventure in one of Japan’s most modern cities. After a scenic drive past forests and rolling countryside, explore Odori Park’s 13-block stretch of gardens, promenades and shops. Wander the historic Botanic Garden with its alpine plants, greenhouse and Ainu artifacts, or take a quick cab ride to the Sapporo Beer Museum for a taste of Japan’s iconic brew. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ainu Village & Show
blocks.text: Discover the rich culture of the Ainu, Hokkaido’s Indigenous people, with a visit to the National Ainu Museum and Park, also known as Upopoy. After a brief orientation, explore the preserved village, traditional huts and artifact-filled museum at your own pace. Enjoy live storytelling, music and dance performances before re-boarding your motorcoach for a scenic return to Muroran and your ship. LEA

blocks.heading: Ninja Show & Valley of Hell
blocks.text: Step into Japan’s vibrant past on a scenic motorcoach ride to Noboribetsu. Explore the Edo-period history park of Date Jidaimura, where ninjas, oiran courtesans, traditional games and lively street performances bring the era to life. Continue to Jigokudani, or “Hell Valley,” for a guided walk among volcanic craters, fumaroles and mineral springs before returning to modern-day Muroran. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Nagasaki
blocks.text: Nagasaki represents nearly infinite possibilities. Layered with cultural moments and spiritual depth, the city offers meaningful experiences around every corner. From its historic temples perched on mountainsides to bustling markets where East meets West, every street tells a story of resilience and renewal. The gentle harbor breeze carries whispers of centuries past while modern life pulses forwa

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Nagasaki
blocks.text: Princess shore excursions in Nagasaki are like flipping through a living travelogue — page after page of castles, coastlines, shops and even a few surprises you won’t find in your guidebook. Find the top things to do in Nagasaki below.

blocks.heading: Easy Nagasaki
blocks.text: Prefer to keep things relaxed? This low-effort tour covers Nagasaki’s highlights by coach, including a stop at Mt. Inasa for city views and a drive-by of major monuments like Urakami Cathedral and the Atomic Bomb Museum. It’s history, without all the legwork. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Nagasaki
blocks.text: Spend a full day discovering the city’s most iconic places. Visit Peace Memorial Park and the Atomic Bomb Museum, then tour Dejima Island (an artificial island created in the 17th century to house Dutch traders during Japan's period of isolation) and wind uphill to Glover Garden for a scenic look at Western-influenced architecture and panoramic harbor views. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Arita's Porcelain and Traditional Culture
blocks.text: See how a small mountain town helped shape Japan’s porcelain legacy. Visit a local kiln, browse artisan shops and enjoy a walk past historic homes. Wrap the day with a visit to Peace Memorial Park, where culture and remembrance meet. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Shimabara Castle & Samurai Village
blocks.text: Head out to the Shimabara Peninsula for a visit to a classic Japanese castle and its surrounding samurai neighborhood. With period architecture, cultural artifacts and dramatic history, this tour combines scenic travel with timeless storytelling. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Highlights of Sasebo
blocks.text: Head northwest to Sasebo, where the Kujukushima Islands set the scene for a leisurely boat cruise and sweeping views from Yumihari Hill. Learn about communities descended from Japanese Catholics who migrated to the area to escape persecution, and soak up the sea air as your captain shares local legends. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Highlights of Nagasaki
blocks.text: A thoughtful city drive introduces you to major historic sites, including Peace Memorial Park, the Atomic Bomb Museum and the one-legged Torii gate. It’s a comprehensive way to experience the city’s past and its ongoing message of unity and global kinship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Nagasaki port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Cruises to Japan come to life in Nagasaki, where the harbor welcomes you with calm waters and deep importance. Nagasaki is commonly included in broader Japan and East Asia Itineraries, often including Korea and China. The port is well-placed for reaching key sites like Peace Memorial Park and Dejima Island, yet it’s also a great spot to pause and take in the surroundings. Lush hills, historic ship

blocks.heading: Things to do in Nagoya
blocks.text: Nagoya is the kind of city where you can stroll through a centuries-old castle in the morning and tour a cutting-edge robotics exhibit by afternoon. With a skyline shaped by industry and a culture shaped by centuries of tradition, this central Japanese hub delivers an intriguing mix of the past and future. Nagoya is a city that celebrates innovation without letting go of its roots — and that makes

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Nagoya
blocks.text: Nagoya’s excursions reveal a side of Japan steeped in craft, culture and quiet surprises. These guided tours offer immersive ways to explore both the city and the surrounding countryside, with something to discover around every curved roofline and garden path.

blocks.heading: Tokugawa Art Gallery & Garden
blocks.text: Enter a world of elegance at the Tokugawa Art Museum, home to centuries-old samurai armor, scrolls and family treasures. Step outside to enjoy a stroll through the traditional Japanese garden, complete with a koi-filled pond, sculpted trees and a peaceful pavilion overlooking the water. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Nagoya
blocks.text: Take in the city’s greatest hits — from the iconic green-roofed Nagoya Castle to the elegant Atsuta Shrine, famed for its sacred treasures. Continue to the bustling Osu shopping district, where you’ll find Kannon Temple tucked between stalls, lanterns and the energy of daily life. It’s a snapshot of Nagoya’s past, present and spiritual depth. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Iga Ueno Castle, Ninja Museum & Seki-Juku
blocks.text: Step into feudal Japan with a visit to Iga Ueno Castle, perched on a hilltop with sweeping views. Explore the Ninja Museum of Igaryu and uncover the secrets of these legendary spies. Then stroll the historic post town of Seki-Juku, where wooden inns and stone paths evoke Japan’s Edo-era charm. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Nagoya Castle, Atsuta Shrine & Osu Kannon Temple
blocks.text: Experience three iconic landmarks in one journey. Start with Nagoya Castle’s shimmering gold dolphins and grand architecture. Then visit Atsuta Shrine, one of Shinto’s most sacred sites. Conclude with a walk through the lively Osu Kannon district — part spiritual site, part shopping arcade, and fully immersive. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Inuyama Castle & Castle Town
blocks.text: Visit one of Japan’s oldest original castles, designated a National Treasure for its impressive design and preserved history. Then explore the charming castle town at its base, where narrow lanes, merchant shops and local sweets invite you to linger. It’s a step into samurai-era life, right down to the stone walls. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Tokoname Pottery Town
blocks.text: Explore Tokoname, one of Japan’s six ancient kiln towns. Walk the quiet Pottery Footpath, past climbing kilns, red clay jars and local artisans who still use centuries-old techniques. If you’re a fan of Japanese ceramics — or just love a town with a strong sense of identity — this is your stop. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Nagoya port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Tucked along Honshu’s central coastline, the port of Nagoya offers a smooth blend of access and adventure. From here, it’s an easy jump into the city’s dynamic blend of culture and industry. When your Japan cruise stops here, spend your day discovering ancient castles and state-of-the-art museums, or venture out to nearby towns known for samurai lore and ceramic craftsmanship. blocks.heading: Things to do in Niigata
blocks.text: In a country where every port feels like a living museum of food, craft and culture, Niigata still manages to surprise. Tucked up on the west coast of Honshu, this city has a rice reputation worth writing home about (and yes, that means sake too). Add in sea-to-table seafood, mountain views and samurai lore, and you’ve got a destination that’s deeply local, quietly legendary and totally feast-wort

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Niigata
blocks.text: Each shore excursion peels back a layer of Niigata’s identity, revealing the rituals and rhythms that define this port. Whether you're into shrines, gardens, markets or geisha games, there’s an itinerary that delivers just the right dose of culture, cuisine and scenery.

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Japanese Garden & Breweries of Sake and Japanese Seasonings in Best Rice Producing Region
blocks.text: This tour is for anyone who believes food is culture. At DHC Sake Brewery, taste award-winning Koshino-Umesato sake and learn what makes Niigata’s rice so elite. Next, visit Yamada Brewery, known for crafting miso, soy sauce and miso-zuke pickles since 1891. Cap it all off with lunch at the Northern Culture Museum, where rice is cooked over fire in traditional hagama pots. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Niigata
blocks.text: Start high with a visit to the top of the Bandaijima Building for 360-degree views of the Shinanogawa River, Sado Island and the Gozu mountain range. Your guide then takes you deep into Niigata’s 500-year story at the City History Museum before treating you to a comforting soba lunch. After exploring local products at the Pavilion of Charm and Bazaar Pavilion, you’ll wrap the day at the Northern C

blocks.heading: Tsubamesanjo, the City of Craftmanship
blocks.text: This one’s for the tool nerds and design junkies. Head to Sanjo, where blades are made the old-school way: by people who definitely know the difference between sharpened and sharp. At the Suwada Open Factory, watch masters forge everything from bonsai scissors to nail clippers. Then shop locally made kitchenware at the Roadside Station: TSUBAMESANJO. After lunch, wind down with a visit to Yahiko S

blocks.heading: Yahiko Shrine & Teradomari Fish Market
blocks.text: Follow your guide through a towering torii gate into Yahiko Shrine, a serene pocket of cypress and stone. After that spiritual breather, it’s beach time at Teradomari. Across the road? blocks.heading: Things to do in Okinawa
blocks.text: Every Okinawa cruise is full of surprises, with ancient castles, tranquil gardens, colorful markets and hidden beaches seemingly popping up out of nowhere. The island’s mix of history, nature and culture makes it easy to fill your day with once-in-a-lifetime adventure — or just find a perfect spot to slow things down and take it all in.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Okinawa
blocks.text: It wouldn’t be an Okinawa cruise without a chance to see the sights. Get to know Okinawa your way, with these curated excursion opportunities designed to highlight some of the island’s most fascinating features.

blocks.heading: Seifa Utaki & Gangala Valley Hike
blocks.text: Spend the day among the meditative beauty of Okinawa's lush scenery, tropical sea breezes, wondrous rock formations, and ocean views. Your scenic journey takes you across the island to the Chinen Peninsula and Seifa Utaki, one of the most sacred sites in Okinawa. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Easy Naha
blocks.text: This relaxed tour is perfect for guests who prefer sightseeing with minimal walking. Enjoy a scenic drive past Okinawa’s southern coast, including the picturesque Nirai Kanai Bridge and the poignant Okinawa Peace Memorial Park. Along the way, take in views of city landmarks and bustling Kokusai Street — and if you’d like, hop off for some independent VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Battle of Okinawa
blocks.text: Take a powerful journey through Okinawa’s wartime history with a visit to the former Japanese Navy Underground Headquarters. This eye-opening tour continues to the Himeyuri Peace Museum and Monument, followed by the Okinawa Peace Memorial Museum and Park. It’s a thoughtful and immersive way to understand the scale and impact of one of World War II’s most significant battles. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Okinawa World & Kokusai Street
blocks.text: See the world-famous Okinawa World, where you’ll explore the spectacular Gyokusendo Cave and a replica Ryukyu village filled with local crafts and performances. Afterwards, stroll the trendy shops and soba stands of Kokusai Street — Naha’s bustling hub for people-watching, souvenir shopping and getting a taste of Japanese island life. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: History & Nature of Central Okinawa
blocks.text: Discover the beauty of history with a visit to the Katsuren Castle Ruins, a UNESCO World Heritage Site perched high above the sea. Photograph the iconic Kaichu Doro, learn about Okinawan sea salt production and wander through the colorful Southeast Botanical Gardens. It’s a scenic, sensory-rich journey through Okinawa’s central treasures. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Experience the Okinawa port on your next cruise
blocks.text: As a top destination for Japanese cruises, Okinawa is unmatched. When your Okinawa cruise docks in Naha, you’ll step right into the island’s capital — a city that places vibrant markets, cultural landmarks and ocean views within easy reach. blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Omaezaki
blocks.text: Discover Omaezaki through guided shore excursions that highlight its scenic lighthouse, rich history, serene beaches and fresh coastal cuisine. From cultural stops to outdoor adventures, there’s something for every kind of traveller.

blocks.heading: Highlights of Omaezaki
blocks.text: Immerse yourself in Japan’s rich history, art and culture with a visit to the Tea Museum Shizuoka, where interactive exhibits showcase 1,200 years of tea tradition and its influence on local arts and architecture. Stroll the serene garden and tea house before heading to the Horai Bridge, the world’s longest wooden pedestrian bridge and concluding with a tour of the Edo-era Ogane Family Residence.

blocks.heading: Kakegawa Castle & Kasuisai Temple
blocks.text: Discover the beauty of Shizuoka Prefecture as you visit two of its most treasured historic sites. Begin at Kasuisai Temple, a serene Zen oasis with more than 600 years of history, before heading to hilltop Kakegawa Castle, meticulously rebuilt using traditional methods. After exploring its scenic grounds, enjoy a stop at Roadside Station Kakegawa for local souvenirs before returning to port. LEARN

blocks.heading: Nihondaira Outlook & Kunozan Toshogu Shrine
blocks.text: Begin your day with a scenic motorcoach ride to Nihondaira Park Outlook for sweeping views of Suruga Bay and Mt. Fuji. Ride the ropeway to Kunozan Toshogu Shrine, an ornate Shinto complex honoring Tokugawa Ieyasu. Explore its vibrant halls, lantern-lined grounds and historic tomb. Descend by ropeway or the 1,000-step staircase before visiting the lively Yaizu Fish Market for colourful souvenirs. L

blocks.heading: Sunpu Castle Park & Shizuoka Sengen Shrine
blocks.text: Step back in time as you visit two of Shizuoka’s most significant cultural sites—Sunpu Castle Park and Shizuoka Sengen Shrine. Explore the castle’s reconstructed gate, serene gardens and historic ruins before continuing to the ornate Sengen Shrine complex. Conclude your journey at Yaizu Fish Market, where fresh seafood and local souvenirs await before your relaxing return to port. LEARN MORE

From the iconic Osaka Castle to the neon-lit Dotonbori district, Osaka and Kyoto offer elegance, energy and endless exploration — with a little something for every type of traveler. Known as Japan's "Water Capital," Osaka also offers local river and bay sightseeing

blocks.text: Enhance your Osaka cruise with curated shore excursions designed to showcase the region’s most compelling sights and stories — regardless of whether your tastes lean toward history, scenery, serenity, or succulent dining.

blocks.text: You'll drink to your good fortune when you visit Kobe's Sake Brewery Museum, honoring the country's 2,200-year tradition of rice wine. Upon arrival at the Sake Brewery Museum, you'll notice the scent of wood and straw. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Highlights of Osaka

blocks.heading: Best of Kyoto: Golden Pavilion, Nijo Castle & Heian Shrine
blocks.text: This all-day adventure covers Kyoto’s top sites, including the glittering Kinkaku-ji, the historic Nijo Castle and the elegant Heian Shrine. A perfect pick for history buffs and architecture lovers alike… or anyone else who wants to see the best that Kyoto has to offer. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Things to do in Sakaiminato
blocks.text: Sakaiminato may be compact, but its character stretches far beyond the coastline. Tucked into Tottori Prefecture along the Sea of Japan coast, between the water and the slopes of Mt. Daisen, this port town draws you in with seafood markets, mystical folklore and quiet spots where time seems to pause. Cruises to Sakaiminato open the door to wandering castle paths and art that’s very much alive in t

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Sakaiminato
blocks.text: The right excursion can turn a visit into something unforgettable, and Sakaiminato has no shortage of options. It doesn't matter if you're drawn to Shinto tradition or carefully curated gardens, each of these experiences reveals something deeper about this serene corner of Honshu.

blocks.heading: Tottori Flower Park
blocks.text: Spend the day among seasonal colors and floral displays that stretch as far as the eye can see. Tottori Flower Park is one of the largest botanical gardens in Japan, with covered walkways, expansive greenhouses and perfectly manicured outdoor beds. The scenery changes throughout the year, but the sense of wonder stays the same. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Izumo Grand Shrine & Lake Shinji
blocks.text: Visit one of Japan’s oldest and most venerated Shinto shrines, where mythology and quiet reverence fill the air. Izumo Grand Shrine is a spiritual landmark with massive thatched roofs and a timeless atmosphere. Afterward, make your way to Lake Shinji for a scenic stop where you can take in the beauty that surrounds this region. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Matsue Castle, Horikawa Boat Ride & Adachi Museum
blocks.text: Step into Japan’s feudal past with a visit to Matsue Castle, one of the country’s few remaining original castles. Drift through the city’s old canals on a Horikawa sightseeing boat before ending your day at the Adachi Museum, where modern art and traditional garden design come together in striking harmony. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Adachi Museum of Art & Yushien Garden
blocks.text: Begin at the Adachi Museum of Art, renowned for both its collection of 20th-century Japanese paintings and its award-winning gardens, seamlessly integrated into the gallery’s design. Then stroll through Yushien Garden on Daikon Island, a tranquil space of stone bridges, koi ponds and seasonal blooms that make the landscape feel like a painting in motion. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Experience the Sakaiminato port on your next cruise
blocks.text: A regular port of call on Japan cruise itineraries, Sakaiminato welcomes Princess sailings across multiple seasonal departures. Stepping off your ship, you land in a port where ancient history and modern whimsy meet. blocks.heading: Things to do in Sakata
blocks.text: Sakata, located in Yamagata Prefecture along the Sea of Japan, is a historic port city that flourished during the Edo period as a major merchant hub for rice trading, and today retains its Edo-era charm through well-preserved merchant warehouses, traditional sake breweries, historic temples and the Sankyo Soko Rice Storehouses, built in 1893. blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Sakata
blocks.text: Sakata is a city with agricultural roots, modern aquariums and historic spiritual buildings. Princess will help you make sure you see the best of Sakata and to step into its rich history.

blocks.heading: Kamo Aquarium and Sakata City Highlights
blocks.text: If you love marine life — especially jellyfish — then this is the excursion for you. The Kamo Aquarium is home to the largest collection of jellyfish on display in the world, and you can stand in the Jellyfish Dream Theater and soak in the beauty of 10,000 moon jellies in one place. blocks.heading: Mt.Haguro and Zenpo-Ji Temple
blocks.text: Looking for a little extra luck? Then you’ll love this excursion into the spiritual history of Japan! First, you’ll visit a five-story pagoda sitting at the base of Mt. Haguro. This pagoda is one of the oldest wooden towers in the world and the oldest pagoda of its kind in Japan. Legend has it that some of the ashes of Shakyamuni, the historical Buddha, are entombed beneath this tower. Then you’ll

blocks.heading: Highlights of Sakata
blocks.text: Dive into all things Sakata during this in-depth tour of two of the best museums in the area. You’ll start your day at the Honma Museum, which sits inside an 1813 mansion built by the Honma family and is one of the oldest private museums in Japan. blocks.heading: Mogami River Cruise and Agricultural History Tour
blocks.text: Ready to learn about the heart of Sakata? That’s right, this excursion teaches you all about two of the most important things in Sakata: farming and the river. Start by learning about farming techniques at the Shinjo Local History Museum and at the Sankyo Rice Storehouse where you can see historic rice storehouses from 1893. blocks.heading: Things to do in Shimizu (Mt. Fuji)
blocks.text: Nothing says "magical vacation" like standing in the shadow of the majestic, sacred Mt. Fuji. There's a reason this towering peak is one of the main symbols of Japan — but it's not the only thing to do in Shimizu. blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Nagasaki
blocks.text: Shimizu is your gateway to Mt. Fuji and so much more! Immerse yourself in samurai history by visiting the childhood home and burial place of the first Tokugawa shogun whose family would rule Japan for 250 years. blocks.text: Take an in-depth look at a few hidden gems enjoyed by local residents. Princess Cruises has teamed up with farmers who will share their knowledge with you. First, you'll learn how Shimizu Prefecture has the largest number of farmed rainbow trout in the country as you tour the Trout Farm followed by a sampling of the mild, succulent fish. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Views of Mt. Fuji, Tea Ceremony & Art Museum
blocks.text: Participate in the ancient “way of tea” on this excursion. The traditional Japanese tea ceremony has its roots in Zen Buddhism and is a precise and meditative process. With your host, you’ll purify yourself, kneel as the host prepares the kettle, prepare the matcha and finally enjoy a relaxing cup of tea. Finish off your excursion with breathtaking views of Mt. blocks.heading: Sunpu Castle Park, Views of Mt. Fuji & Shizuoka Sengen Shrine
blocks.text: Step into samurai history at Sunpu Castle Park — a careful reconstruction of the place where the first shogun of Japan grew up. Tokugawa Ieyasu was a samurai in the late 1500s who became the de facto leader of Japan — the shogun — and set up the Tokugawa shogunate that would rule the country until the Meiji era, and you can see his roots at this castle. blocks.heading: Nihondaira Outlook & Kunozan Toshogu Shrine
blocks.text: Surround yourself with traditional Japanese religion at the Kunozan Toshogu Shrine. Japanese shrines are typically dedicated to the Shinto gods — the original gods of the island — but this one is a little unique. It’s also the burial place of Tokugawa Ieyasu, the first shogun. blocks.heading: Things to do in Toba
blocks.text: Located in Mie Prefecture along the rugged coastline of Ise-Shima, Toba is a serene seaside city famous for being the birthplace of Japan’s cultured pearl industry. With its stunning ocean vistas, traditional ama (female free divers) culture and proximity to the sacred Ise Grand Shrine, Toba offers a unique blend of maritime heritage and spiritual significance — best experienced on Princess spring

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore Toba
blocks.text: See all of the best of Toba in a day with one of our Princess excursions. Whether you want to see the famous pearls or spend the day at the Ise Shrine, Princess can take care of all the details.

blocks.heading: Ocean Culture Experience with 'Ama' Divers and Lunch
blocks.text: Uncover the history of Toba's fishing traditions and culture with a visit to the Toba Sea-Folk Museum, the only museum in Japan dedicated to understanding the traditions of Toba's fisher-folk, and the relationship between man and the sea. For nearly half a century, the museum has been collecting the antique fishing equipment of fishing villages, and researched the traditions and religion of the ar

blocks.heading: Best of Ise and Shima
blocks.text: Walk on some of the most sacred grounds in all of Japan at Ise-jingu Shrine Complex. This stunning Shinto shrine is dedicated to Amaterasu-Omikami — the ancient sun goddess, ancestor of the emperors and the protector of Japan. The shrine is built out of ancient cypress wood that is joined together like puzzle pieces with no nails — which has helped this shrine last through years of earthquakes. Th

blocks.heading: Ise shrine, Skyline and Mikimoto Pearl Island
blocks.text: If you love pearls, you won’t want to miss this excursion to Mikimoto Pearl Island. Back in 1893, Kokichi Mikimoto figured out how to cultivate pearls in the water around his hometown of Toba and began hiring “sea women” to dive and harvest them. Today, you can see the museum that recounts how this process worked, find famous Mikimoto pearls and maybe even see a woman dive for more pearls. VIEW EX

blocks.heading: Highlights of Ise Shrine
blocks.text: Wander a historic village that used to be a major stop on historic Japanese pilgrimages to the Ise Shrine. Okage Yokocho is a three-acre street lined with Edo and Meiji architecture — some buildings have been reproduced and some have been transported from UNESCO World Heritage areas. You’ll feel like you stepped into the past as you explore the houses, shops and restaurants that have been serving

blocks.heading: Toba Aquarium and Kashikojima cruise
blocks.text: Calling all marine life lovers. The Toba Aquarium boasts more than 30,000 aquatic animals from 1,200 species — the most in any aquarium in Japan. See Serena the dugong (one of the only dugongs living in captivity in the world), the otters jumping from the water, a Japanese giant crab with a leg span of 12 feet and a Sunmeri whale. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Ise Shima Skyline
blocks.text: Nature is the premier attraction but there is also a deep culture and rich history to experience during this compact introduction to Toba's colorful and sacred sites. Once you board your coach you'll drive through Mt. Asama along Ise Shima Skyline, a nine-mile-long stretch of road that connects Toba and the town of Ise. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Things to do in Tokushima
blocks.text: Love quiet moments? Eager for excitement? This city delivers both — often in the same afternoon. Surrounded by mountains and steeped in tradition, Tokushima offers a rhythm all its own. It's a place that refuses to be defined by just one mood, inviting you to experience all sides of its captivating personality.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Tokushima
blocks.text: Tokushima’s highlights aren’t shy — they leap, they spin and sometimes they turn into a whirling maelstrom (looking at you, Naruto Whirlpools). Princess shore excursions put you face to face with both the land and the people of Tokushima.

blocks.heading: Awa Odori Dance Festival
blocks.text: Tokushima’s biggest party happens in August — but if you’re visiting outside of that window, don’t worry. At the Awa Odori Kaikan museum, the dance never stops. Reserved seating gives you front-row access to this joyful burst of color, music and movement. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Otsuka Museum of Art & Naruto Whirlpools
blocks.text: Big waves, bold art and a seemingly out-of-place ceiling fresco you’ll probably recognize — this full-day excursion pairs cutting-edge reproductions of famous artworks with a gravity-defying view of one of the world’s largest whirlpools. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Temples Along The Shikoku Pilgrimage Route
blocks.text: Scale spiritual heights (literally) on this temple-themed trek. Ride a cable car to Tairyu-ji, visit Byodo-ji and discover why pilgrims have been making this loop for over a millennium — one small step at a time. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Traditions of Tokushima
blocks.text: This half-day cultural sampler includes time in the preserved Udatsu District and a seat at a traditional Awa puppet show where drama, history and craftsmanship share the stage. Puppets as respected representatives of national identity? You’ve got to hand it to them. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Tokushima On Your Own
blocks.text: Feeling independent? Create your own adventure with this flexible excursion. Wander ruins, catch whirlpools or head up Mt. Biza. It’s your day, your way, so don’t be afraid to go rogue with your itinerary — just don’t go cashless (you’ll want to grab a few souvenirs). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Tokushima port on your next cruise
blocks.text: Cruises to Japan come in many flavors, and Tokushima’s got its own special spice. The port here is more than just practical — it’s a front-row seat to the wild, winding geography that defines Shikoku. blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Tokyo
blocks.text: Don’t stress over planning — experience the best Tokyo has to offer, stress-free, with Princess shore excursions. We’ll handle the details so you can relax and soak it all in.

blocks.heading: Hama-Rikyu Garden, Tokyo Tower and Ginza with Haneda Airport Drop Off
blocks.text: Blend the futuristic side of Tokyo with its traditional side on this tour. You’ll start in the beautiful Hama-rikyu Gardens that are full of Edo-period history. Then you’ll see the city from a birdseye view standing atop the iconic Tokyo Tower before spending a few hours in the Ginza district. This area is home to fantastic Japanese food and is the perfect place to pick up a one-of-a-kind souvenir

blocks.heading: Highlights of Tokyo
blocks.text: Immerse yourself in the ancient side of Tokyo at the Meiji Shrine and the Sensoji Temple. The Sensoji Temple is the oldest temple in Tokyo with a five-story pagoda and red paper lanterns decorating the Kaminarimon Gate. Right outside the gates is the famed Nakamise Shopping Street where you can find delicious snacks and handmade crafts to bring home as a souvenir. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kamakura: Image Of The Great Buddha & Shrine
blocks.text: Escape the hustle and bustle of the city by taking this day trip to Kamakura. You’ll start by driving down the cherry-tree lined Wakamiya-Oji before stopping at the 750-year-old Great Buddha at Kotokuin Temple. It’s 38-feet high, so when you stand by the base, you’ll really be able to soak in its majesty. Then you’ll go to the Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine, a shrine dedicated to Hachiman, the patro

blocks.heading: Meiji Shrine & Asakusa -Debark Tour Narita Airport
blocks.text: Step into the Meiji Shrine, where you’ll feel like you’re in an ancient jungle temple all while being mere feet away from downtown. Stand beneath twin 40-foot tall wooden Torii gates and explore the inner temple complex. You’ll also walk through the surrounding park and grounds, which is home to 120,000 trees. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Tokyo
blocks.text: Walk the grounds of Japan’s legendary Imperial Palace on this tour of the city. You’ll make your way through the city, past the modern Fuji Television and Ginza district, to the park that surrounds the home of Japan’s Emperor. Pose for a picture or two on Nijubashi Bridge, a picturesque two-tier bridge that looks straight out of a fairytale. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Tokyo Tower & Panoramic City Drive with Narita Airport Drop off
blocks.text: See the city how it’s meant to be seen: from above! On this tour, you’ll see all the highlights of the city like the National Diet Building where the government convenes before going to Tokyo Tower. This tower looks a lot like the Eiffel Tower but bright red, and you’ll climb it for panoramic views of the city beneath your shoes. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Toyama
blocks.text: Want a deeper dive into Toyama’s highlights than you’re likely to find on your own? These curated excursions pack in history, flavor and enough wow-factor to keep your social-media buzzing for days.

blocks.heading: World Heritage Site Gokayama & Wood Carving Village
blocks.text: Spend your day in the Nanto region, where Gokayama’s UNESCO-listed villages mix architectural genius with rural resilience. Then stop by Inami to see woodcarving masters in action, shaping everything from temple doors to modern drinkware. The entire area runs on tradition, but there’s nothing dusty or tired about it. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Best of Kanazawa
blocks.text: Start in Higashi Chayamachi, a geisha district where traditional tea houses still echo with 19th-century elegance. Then wander through Kenrokuen Garden, one of Japan’s most celebrated green spaces, complete with streams, teahouses and a stone bridge shaped like flying geese. Wrap things up in the Nagamachi Samurai District, where narrow lanes and preserved homes let you peek into the lifestyle of

blocks.heading: Tateyama & Kurobe Alpine Route
blocks.text: Tour Japan’s highest-altitude spectacle, where scenic roads wind through towering snow walls and alpine views stretch basically forever. You’ll ride by bus through the Tateyama Mountain Range, pass through the famous ‘snow corridor’ (if you visit during the spring) and stop at Murodo Station. Take a break for lunch, then walk the grounds where wild nature meets wild elevation. Bring layers! VIEW E

blocks.heading: Shirakawago Village On Your Own
blocks.text: This is your chance to explore one of Japan’s most visually striking spots at your own pace. Wander among steep thatched-roof homes built in gassho-zukuri style, designed to survive heavy snow with flair. Museums are optional, but the quiet, mountain-framed beauty of the village is the real show. Gokayama, just next door, shares its UNESCO badge and its timeless charm. VIEW EXCURSION

blocks.heading: Highlights of Toyama
blocks.text: Kick off with a visit to Zuiryuji Temple, a 17th-century masterclass in precision and peace. Next, explore Kansui Park, a canal-side hangout perfect for boat rides, relaxed walks and unforgettable meals (at one of the best-looking cafes in the country). End your tour at the Suiboku Museum for a close look at minimalist Japanese ink paintings and a teahouse filled with the kind of silence that feel

blocks.heading: Things to do in Tsuruga
blocks.text: Tsuruga might fly under the radar, but those who make landfall here discover a city where poetry, history and craftsmanship are all woven into daily life. This coastal gem in the Wakasa region is known for inspiring the haiku of Edo-period poet Matsuo Basho, who once wrote of moonlight shimmering over Tsuruga Bay. Today, that same ethereal beauty shows up in the pine-draped shores of Kehi-no-Matsu

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Tsuruga
blocks.text: Museum hopping, lakeside cable cars, cultural workshops — there are so many ways to get to know Tsuruga better as a visitor. No matter where you go, these activities and experiences will stick with you.

blocks.heading: Lake Mikatagoko Rainbow Drive & Chopsticks Making Experience
blocks.text: Follow the colorful Rainbow Line to panoramic views of the Mikata Five Lakes. After a scenic cable car ride to the mountaintop observatory, explore Wakasa’s charming town below. Visit a traditional workshop and polish your own set of lacquered chopsticks to take home. Wrap up with a relaxing stop at Wakasa Fisherman’s Wharf overlooking Obama Bay. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hikone Castle & Nagahama
blocks.text: Travel back to Japan’s feudal era with a visit to Hikone Castle, completed in 1622 and designated a National Treasure. Wander its storied grounds and adjacent Genkyu Garden before heading to Nagahama’s Kurokabe Square. Here, timeworn buildings from the Edo and Meiji periods house charming galleries, cafés and artisan shops. Enjoy free time to explore before returning to port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Eiheiji Temple & Ichijodani Asakura Clan Ruins
blocks.text: Step into the Muromachi Period at the reconstructed Ichijodani Asakura Clan Ruins, where merchant houses and samurai homes line a quiet 200-meter street. Then, journey to the sprawling Eiheiji Temple complex — home to 70 buildings and over 250 monks. Stroll covered walkways, learn about Soto Zen Buddhism and gain insight into centuries of spiritual practice in serene forested surroundings. LEARN M

blocks.heading: Traditional Arts and Crafts of Fukui
blocks.text: Explore the artful side of Fukui on a day of hands-on tradition. Watch master artisans at work in a lacquerware studio, then try your hand at washi paper-making by creating a custom postcard. At Takefu Knife Village, browse exquisite blades with roots in 14th-century swordsmithing. Cap it off with a soba noodle lunch and a scenic return to port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Highlights of Tsuruga
blocks.text: Perfect for a cruise to Tsuruga, this excursion packs in Tsuruga’s best-known sights. Begin at the pine-lined shores of Kehi-no-Matsubara, then visit Kehi Jingu Shrine, known for its 11-meter torii gate. Snap photos at the historic Red Brick Warehouse and visit the Port of Humanity Museum to learn about Chiune Sugihara’s WWII legacy. Finish at the Sea of Japan’s largest seafood market, with time t

blocks.heading: Experience the Tsuruga port on your next cruise
blocks.text: A port of call on Japan-focused itineraries, Tsuruga is featured on several Princess Circle Japan voyages roundtrip from Tokyo (Yokohama), often paired with stops like Sakaiminato, Busan, Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Visit this port as part of an enriching Japan cruise with Princess® and find something meaningful beyond the usual stops.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Wakayama
blocks.text: Wakayama is the cruise destination that invites you to take your time. It’s a place where hillside temples, waterfront markets and relaxing hot springs each create their own rhythm. And you’re welcome to follow whichever one speaks to you first. Cruises to Wakayama offer a quieter kind of magic, rooted in tradition but always full of movement. Start with Wakayama Castle, a 16th-century hilltop str

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Wakayama
blocks.text: Wakayama’s shore excursions connect you with centuries-old temples, coastal villages and culinary traditions that are still thriving today. Enjoy everything from mountain mysticism to handcrafted lacquerware. Each experience brings something vivid to your journey.

blocks.heading: Wakayama Castle & Kada
blocks.text: ake in the sweeping views from some of the most historical sites in Wakayama Prefecture beginning with a tour of Wakayama Castle. Originally built in 1585, bombing in WWII destroyed most of the original castle buildings but the faithful reconstruction has successfully recreated an aura of power and authority. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Mt. Koya and Kongobuji Temple
blocks.text: Ascend into Japan’s spiritual heart with a visit to Mt. Koya, home to sacred temples and peaceful cedar forests. At the center is Kongobuji, the head temple of Shingon Buddhism, known for its painted sliding doors and perfectly raked rock garden. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Wakayama
blocks.text: Get a well-rounded taste of the region with this full-day tour, where historic landmarks meet everyday culture. Wander the grounds of Wakayama Castle, browse local markets and admire waterfront views that hint at the prefecture’s maritime roots. It’s a great intro for first-time visitors who want to see it all (or almost everything). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Yuasa Soy Sauce Factory & Soy Sauce Museum Town Walking Tour
blocks.text: Step into the birthplace of Japanese soy sauce and discover how this everyday staple came to flavor a nation. Tour the working factory and explore the museum’s wooden tools and barrels. Then wander Yuasa’s quiet streets where the scent of fermentation still lingers. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Traditional Kishu Lacquerware & Nakano BC Plum Wine
blocks.text: This locally led tour pairs hands-on artistry with a taste of Wakayama’s prized ume (plum) wine. Watch as skilled craftspeople shape and finish pieces of Kishu lacquerware, then enjoy a guided tasting at Nakano BC, a winery known for blending tradition with innovation. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Mt. Koya and Buddhist Cuisine
blocks.text: Gain insight into the nature, history and culture of the Shikoku Pilgrimage route, a 745-mile long trail associated with the 9th century Buddhist monk Kobo Daishi, the founder of Shingon Buddhism. Your destination is Mount Koya, the mountain range in Wakayama Prefecture; there are numerous temples and monasteries nestled in the mountains and your first stop is Okunoin Temple. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Half Day Wakayama
blocks.text: Shop and sightsee for half a day in the castle town of Wakayama. Your adventure begins with a visit to Kuroshio Market, a well-known fish market where you can eat and buy fresh seafood. Next on the itinerary is Kishu Toshogu Shrine. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Experience the Wakayama port on your next cruise
blocks.text: When your ship docks at the Wakayama cruise port, you’ll step into a region that knows just how to make you feel welcome without needing to say much at all. blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Yatsushiro
blocks.text: There’s more to Kyushu than castles and gardens, but those are a pretty solid place to start. These curated excursions hit all the right notes, whether you're a sucker for samurai lore or just here for the Shochu tasting.

blocks.heading: Hitoyoshi & Shochu Brewery
blocks.text: This tour runs on fermentation and folklore. Start at Kamada factory for miso and soy sauce magic, then roll over to the Kuma Shochu Spirit Museum to learn about the regional spirit with a cult following (one taste and you will understand why). Round it out with a walk through the Aoi Aso Shrine — a national treasure with centuries of Shinto soul etched into its woodwork and walkways. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Kumamoto
blocks.text: Start with the icon: Kumamoto Castle. Originally built in 1607, this fortress still holds its ground in both stature and spirit. Your guide leads you along the stone walls and scenic grounds, and the views from the towers are as grand as the history they oversee. After a local lunch that doesn’t mess around, you’ll unwind in Suizenji Garden. Think koi-filled ponds, miniature Mount Fuji and 17th-ce

blocks.heading: Mt. Aso & Shirakawa Spring
blocks.text: Start slow with a stop at Shirakawa Spring. Then it’s off to Kusasenri, a sweeping grassland set against the backdrop of Japan's largest active volcano. A trip to the Aso Crater delivers heat, power and that delicious volcanic majesty. You’ll have time to breathe it all (sulfur and all) in before heading back to port with your camera full and your brain still processing what you just saw. LEARN MO

blocks.heading: Highlights of Kumamoto
blocks.text: For a slightly shorter hit list, this version still checks the big boxes. You’ll marvel at the exterior of Kumamoto Castle and stroll through the artful calm of Suizenji Garden. It’s a condensed dose of historic beauty that doesn’t skimp on the storytelling. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Mediterranean cruise ports of call
blocks.text: Discover some of the world-renowned destinations that await you on a Mediterranean cruise with Princess.

blocks.heading: Why cruise the Mediterranean
blocks.text: In lands where the culture is as flavorful as the cuisine, the splendor of the Mediterranean speaks for itself.

blocks.heading: Sun-kissed beaches
blocks.text: Visions of sparkling coasts and crystalline waters welcome you to the Mediterranean. Dip your toes on the black-sand coast of Santorini on a Greek cruise. Head to Salerno to spend the day in Positano relaxing on the white beaches and admiring the pastel houses that decorate the cliffs around you. Or travel to Mykonos with your loved ones and daydream on the city’s long stretch of golden sand and s

blocks.heading: World-class dining
blocks.text: With mouthwatering entrees and confections, the Mediterranean invites you to embark on a gourmet tour through iconic cities. Reawaken your taste buds with Italian classics like pastas, pizzas and gelato. Or fill your plate with gyros, keftethes and baklava on a Greek cruise. From breakfast to dinner and every delectable dessert in between, the best is before you with Princess.

blocks.heading: Rich wines
blocks.text: The countryside of Italy and Greece are home to some of the most flavorful wines around the globe. With sun and warm temperatures year-round, vineyards are flourishing with grapes by the harvest season. Sip on Italy’s red wines, or sample Greece’s white blends. From sweet Lambruscos to earthy Bordeauxs, fill up your glass on a Mediterranean cruise with Princess.

blocks.heading: Ancient ruins
blocks.text: From towers and temples to cities and shorelines, the Mediterranean is sprinkled with remains of civilizations past. Step back in time on a tour through ancient ruins on a Mediterranean cruise with Princess. Imagine life as a gladiator at the Colosseum, explore Greek mythology at the Parthenon and discover the archeological excavations of Pompeii — a lost city and UNESCO World Heritage Site.

blocks.heading: Art galleries & museums
blocks.text: From the treasures on land to the jewels within museums, the Mediterranean is a true work of art. On an Italian cruise, see portraits from the Renaissance period at the Uffizi Museum in Florence, and admire Michelangelo’s masterpieces at the Vatican Museum in Rome. Or walk in the footsteps of celebrated artists that called these regions home — like Picasso and Dali — and allow their work to spark

blocks.heading: Why cruise with Princess
blocks.text: Curated comfort, world-class entertainment and international flavors await you.

blocks.heading: Celebrations & Romance
blocks.text: It's difficult to imagine something more romantic than sailing through the alluring cities and charming countryside of Europe. While on board your European cruise, we cater to your sentimental side with private dining on your balcony — like breakfast for two or a sunset dinner — honeymoon packages, flowers and chocolates delivered to your room and couples-only massages in the Sanctuary.

blocks.heading: Accommodations
blocks.text: Your stateroom is where you rest and recharge between adventures. That’s why every room is equipped with the expertly designed Princess Luxury Bed, 100% Jacquard-woven cotton linens. blocks.text: Learn more about Mexico while touring historical landmarks, sharing a traditional meal with locals or relaxing on the sun-drenched beaches.

blocks.heading: Ships on this itinerary
blocks.text: Our Princess fleet includes ships that offer a multitude of amenities and feature the innovative MedallionClass® experience. From a balcony stateroom, take in the sights and sounds of the colorful cultures ashore before enjoying the “sabor” of local cuisine in one of our many eateries during your Mexican Riviera cruise.

blocks.heading: The Malecon
blocks.text: Spend an entire day walking along the Malecon, Puerto Vallarta’s beach boardwalk. Shop for regionally crafted goods — like woven baskets or a pair of leather boots — and meet the locals who created them. Stop for lunch at a nearby restaurant, where you can enjoy delicacies like tamales and pozole with a seafront view. Or watch street performers sing and dance, and get up close to larger-than-life

blocks.heading: Mazatlan Cathedral
blocks.text: On a Mexican Riviera cruise with Princess, travel back in time to the 19th century during a visit to Mazatlan’s Cathedral Basilica of the Immaculate Conception. Admire the Moorish and Gothic architecture, and marvel at statues of famous saints — like Matthew, Mark, Luke and John — that decorate the church’s exterior. Then head inside to see baroque decor, crystal chandeliers and gold-lined murals.

blocks.heading: Medano Beach
blocks.text: With an abundance of activities to do on both land and sea, Medano Beach offers something for the whole family. Relax on the golden shores, or indulge in a waterside lunch nearby. Float in the turquoise sea, or make some waves on a jet ski ride. Your dream beach day awaits on a Mexican Riviera cruise to Cabo.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Cabo
blocks.text: Cabo offers endless ways to spend your day. Lounge on sun-drenched beaches, dive into the deep blue to see colorful marine life or explore nearby towns filled with art and history. The city’s energy flows naturally between laid-back and lively, so you can plan your visit exactly the way you want it.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Cabo
blocks.text: Princess® shore excursions on cruises to Cabo blend natural wonders, cultural exploration and pure fun. Spend the day cruising past sea cliffs, tasting local flavors or venturing into the desert for an unforgettable perspective of Baja.

blocks.heading: Camel and Mexican Outback Adventure
blocks.text: Ride a gentle camel along a quiet Pacific beach, learn about the desert ecosystem and enjoy a homemade Baja lunch with fresh tortillas and tequila tasting. It’s a blend of culture, cuisine and scenery in one remarkable outing. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: El Arco Cruise & Playa Medano
blocks.text: Sail along Cabo’s rugged coastline for close-up views of El Arco before heading to Medano Beach to swim or sip something cool by the water. It’s the perfect mix of sightseeing and sea breeze. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hotel California & Todos Santos
blocks.text: Travel the Baja coastline to the oasis town of Todos Santos, where art galleries, mission architecture and the legendary Hotel California await. This peaceful escape feels worlds away from Cabo’s bustle. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cabo Art & Culture
blocks.text: Explore San José del Cabo’s colorful art district, visit the 18th-century mission and meet local artists whose studios fill the cobblestone lanes. Wrap up with authentic tacos and a refreshing drink before heading back along the coast. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Arts, Culture & Farm-to-Table Food Experience with Chef Enrique Silva
blocks.text: Spend the day discovering Baja’s creative and culinary roots. Visit glassblowing workshops, sample craft beer and cook alongside Chef Enrique Silva at his Tamarindo Organic Farm, where every ingredient captures the essence of the land. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Wild Canyon Park Pass
blocks.text: Adventure seekers can spend the day at Wild Canyon Park, home to zip lines, camel rides and Baja’s longest hanging bridge. The desert views and variety of activities make this one an instant favorite for families. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Cabo
blocks.text: Cabo is featured on a wide range of Mexico cruise itineraries aboard Princess®. Options include Cabo Getaways, short roundtrip voyages from California and longer Mexican Riviera or Panama Canal cruises that reveal more of Central America’s coastline. Guests tender ashore directly into the marina, placing beaches, cafés and shopping just steps away.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Ensenada
blocks.text: Ensenada greets you with warm Baja sun, Mediterranean‑style climate, friendly locals and a seaside buzz that’s just 90 minutes south of San Diego. You’ll explore marine geysers, wine valleys and shopping promenades — with a solid dose of food, wine and tequila to keep your spirits high. Whether you’re hunting silver jewelry or sipping cabernet in Guadalupe Valley, Ensenada delivers easy‑going adve

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Ensenada
blocks.text: Pick your passion — whether you’re sipping wine, riding ATVs or chasing natural thrills, these tours give you Ensenada cruises with flavor you won’t want to miss.…

blocks.heading: Snorkel by Boat at Todos Santos
blocks.text: Board a boat bound for the Todos Santos Islands off the Ensenada coast, gear up for snorkeling in kelp forests and crystal water, maybe spot dolphins or whales and then wrap with a fresh fruit and beverage break before the return ride. Your divemaster adds fun facts and ensures water safety while you float above a teeming marine world. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: City Drive & Mexican Folkloric Fiesta
blocks.text: Take the coastal drive through Ensenada, visit the boardwalk and scientific research centre, explore the gardens of Riviera del Pacifico, then settle into a lively folkloric fiesta with mariachi, traditional dances and craft shopping. Cap it all off with time to sip local drinks, browse handmade wares and chat with artists between performances. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Made in Mexico – Ensenada Eats
blocks.text: This foodie‑tour takes you to five spots: start at a taco stand, then fish taco haven, steamed clams venue, sea‑urchin tostada legend and finish with Baja wine tastings at Vinos Ensenada. Expect flavor explosions, street‑tour energy and a walking pace that means going full local. Along the way, you’ll learn why Ensenada is Mexico’s new food capital. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Mexican Dancing Horses & Tequila Tasting
blocks.text: Cruise into the Guadalupe Valley and arrive at Fuego Ranch for an equestrian show where dancing horses steal the scene, then return to town for an immersive tequila‑making and tasting session. You’ll also have time to mingle with locals, explore the grounds and snap your fill of scenic snaps. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Harris’s Hawk Falconry Encounter with Brunch
blocks.text: In the foothills of Guadalupe Valley, meet Harris’s hawks in a falconry demo on a vineyard property, learn how they assist in vineyard pest control, then brunch in the garden setting and soak in countryside breeze before heading back to the ship. Expect feathered theatrics, stunning vineyard views and a peaceful pause from city bustle. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Wine Country ATV Adventure
blocks.text: Hit the dirt trails in Guadalupe Valley on ATVs, race past vineyards and mountain back‑roads, enjoy dusty thrills followed by a chill local wine tasting to end the ride in contrast‑mode: adrenaline then cabernet. The rugged terrain keeps things exciting, while the vino delivers the calm. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Ensenada
blocks.text: When your ship docks at Ensenada’s deep‑water terminal as part of your Mexico cruise itinerary, you step off straight into Baja flavor — just minutes from downtown experiences. The industrial‑chic pier sits right by the action, so you move from ship deck to seafood stand without missing a beat. With nearby wineries, shopping and natural stunners, Ensenada is both easy and rich.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Huatulco
blocks.text: Ready to spring off the ship into something that actually feels like an adventure? These excursions highlight the heart and wild edges of Huatulco — from community kitchens to mangrove canoe rides, pre‑Columbian ruins to catamaran cruises. Pick your flavor, pack for sun (and maybe rain) and toggle that beach mode to full curiosity.

blocks.heading: Five Bays by Catamaran & Swim
blocks.text: This isn’t just a boat ride — it’s a moving postcard. Sail through five iconic bays with colorful commentary, cold drinks and one perfectly-timed swim stop. You’ll see ocean blowholes, (natural rock formations along the shore where waves force water through a narrow opening), old-man rock faces and beaches so untouched you’ll wonder if you're the first person to see them. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ancestral Wisdom & Cultural Treasures
blocks.text: This immersive half-day tour peels back the curtain on rural Oaxacan life. You’ll press tortillas at a community kitchen, learn how clay bricks are crafted, stroll a medicinal plant garden and visit a family-run ranch for tamales and storytelling. Along the way, catch views of the Sierra Madre that’ll make your camera work overtime. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Flavors of Colorful Mexico
blocks.text: Get a full taste of Huatulco’s culture — literally. You’ll start at a local herb garden with lemongrass tea and medicinal plant demos, then dive into handmade tortillas and nopal tastings. After that, it’s off to a 17th-century church and municipal square before finishing strong at a mezcal factory where you’ll learn (and sample) the secrets of this iconic Oaxacan spirit. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Amazing Eco Tour & Crocodile Sanctuary
blocks.text: Wildlife gets the spotlight on this half-day eco-adventure. After a scenic drive to La Ventanilla, hop into a canoe for a quiet float through mangrove-lined waters where crocodiles lurk and herons pose like runway models. Your guide whips up quesadillas on a secluded island, giving you the kind of rustic snack break that beats any mini-bar. Nature lovers, this one’s yours. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Copalita Archaeological Exploration
blocks.text: History buffs, meet your new obsession. These ruins — a mix of Zapotec and Olmec influence — are some of the oldest on Mexico’s Pacific coast. You’ll walk nearly two hours through ancient paths and ceremonial platforms as archaeologists continue to uncover secrets in real time. It’s raw, rarely crowded and steeped in pre-Columbian mystery that still refuses to explain itself. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Huatulco by Land & Sea
blocks.text: See Huatulco the lazy-smart way: catamaran first, town second. You’ll cruise by five scenic bays, spot wild rock formations and sip from the open bar while snapping panoramic shots. Then, it’s a guided land tour to La Crucecita for local flavor and unbeatable viewpoints. Two perspectives, one trip. And yes, your social feed is about to get jealous. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in La Paz
blocks.text: La Paz rolls out warm Baja air, golden‑sand beaches, turquoise waters and a cultural story that stretches back to Hernán Cortés sailing in 1535. Your day here could be spent strolling artsy esplanades, diving into clear sea life or sipping margaritas while tide laps near. Whether you’re chasing whale sharks or hand‑crafts, La Paz invites you to explore at your own pace.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in La Paz
blocks.text: Gear up for unique adventures — you’ll find snorkeling with sea lions, desert hikes and cultural bites that’ll make your Mexico cruise stop unforgettable.

blocks.heading: Whale Shark Encounter
blocks.text: Between October and May you may spot massive, gentle whale sharks gliding through La Paz Bay; with this excursion, the boat positions you for the best views. You might even snorkel alongside one of the planet’s biggest (and friendliest) fish before cruising back to dock. Seeing these spotted giants up close is equal parts thrill and awe. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Highlights of La Paz
blocks.text: Ride into town for a guided walk along the Malecon with its sculptures and sea‑breeze views, visit a museum filled with Baja relics, explore the Mission‑era cathedral and end with free time to shop or sip in the seaside plaza. Along the way, your guide shares stories that bring La Paz’s history and laid‑back spirit vividly to life. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: La Paz Street Food Experience ‑ Small Groups
blocks.text: Drive to the Malecon and explore three food stalls: fresh fish tacos, shrimp tostadas and a crisp Oaxacan tlayuda (followed by a mezcalita and gelato for dessert) Pause for souvenir shopping while the sea whispers and the city hums. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hiking Balandra & Beach Break
blocks.text: Join a naturalist guide on a hike through rugged terrain to Balandra Bay, admire ‘El Hongo’ limestone rock, swim in glassy water at Tecolote Beach and relax with a cold beer and fresh fish taco by the shore before heading back. The desert‑meets‑sea scenery makes every step feel like a dream that’s almost too gorgeous to be real. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kayak at La Paz Bay
blocks.text: After a scenic ride to the bay and some detailed kayaking instruction, launch into shallow turquoise water for over an hour of paddling. Soak in quiet coves and sea views, then come ashore and prepare to board for the return to port. Expect a meditative rhythm as your paddle cuts through the calm, crystal‑clear sea. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Snorkeling with Sea Lions
blocks.text: Board a boat for a cruise to San Rafaelito Bay to snorkel among sea lions, angelfish and sun‑drenched reef. Then visit Balandra Beach for a swim and some delicious snacks. Curious sea lions might even swim circles around you — don’t take it personally; they’ve been doing this longer than you have. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to La Paz
blocks.text: Your ship docks at Puerto Pichilingue, about 10‑15 miles from downtown, so you’ll transfer into town then step into Baja energy with ease. The terminal is in an industrial‑chic setting but gets you fast onto the sandy shores, colorful boardwalk and laid‑back culture of La Paz. This Mexico cruise stop is tranquil, engaging and rich with natural wonders.
