blocks.heading: Things to do in Loreto
blocks.text: From serene beaches to charming cobblestone streets, Loreto offers an authentic glimpse into Baja California’s natural beauty and history. Whether you’re kayaking along crystal-clear waters, exploring the centuries-old Mission of Our Lady of Loreto, or snorkeling in the Sea of Cortez, cruises to Loreto promise unforgettable adventures surrounded by breathtaking coastal scenery.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Loreto
blocks.text: Make the most of your time ashore on cruises to Loreto with unforgettable shore excursions that showcase its natural beauty and charm. From snorkeling in the Sea of Cortez and exploring desert canyons to wandering through the historic town center, every adventure reveals why Loreto is one of Baja’s most captivating destinations.

blocks.heading: Giganta Mountain Canyon Hiking
blocks.text: Experience rugged desert beauty and ocean-coast contrasts on this stunning hike through the canyon of the Sierra de la Giganta. You’ll traverse desert trails, discover hidden palm-lined pools, and absorb sweeping views of the shimmering sea beyond. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: From Ranch to Table & Mexican Fiesta
blocks.text: Savor the essence of Baja with an authentic ranch-to-table experience: ride through scenic countryside, harvest fresh produce, mingle with locals, and delight in a festive Mexican lunch under the sun complete with music, dancing and vibrant flavors. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Exploring Fossils In the Canyon
blocks.text: Journey through a breathtaking desert canyon where ancient marine fossils tell the story of a land once beneath the sea. As you walk along sunlit riverbeds, discover fossilized shells and coral, learn about unique desert plants and wildlife and experience the natural wonder that makes Loreto’s landscape unlike anywhere else on earth. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Baja Coast Kayaking
blocks.text: Paddle through the calm, turquoise waters of Bahía de Loreto National Park, surrounded by sunlit desert peaks and vibrant marine life. As sea lions play nearby and waves gently lap against your kayak, this peaceful coastal adventure offers a perfect way to connect with the natural beauty of the Sea of Cortez. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Loreto Walking Tour
blocks.text: Stroll beneath swaying palms and vibrant storefronts through the heart of a 300-year-old town, where you’ll wander the Main Plaza, visit a beautifully preserved mission, and discover rich history and local stories at every turn. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Horseback Riding at the Loreto Estuary & Beach
blocks.text: Saddle up for a scenic ride through serene estuary marshlands and along a pristine beach as you follow expert guides, feel the breeze of the Loreto coast and soak in stunning views of the Sea of Cortez. This immersive excursion blends gentle adventure with natural beauty and unforgettable moments. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Manzanillo
blocks.text: Manzanillo brings together fishing legends, laid‑back beaches and jungle‑rise backdrops in one gorgeous Mexican Pacific setting. History drifts in on sea breeze — from Spanish shipyards to modern cruise terminals — while you’re sipping Baja wine or casting a line for sailfish. And yes; the nickname ‘Sailfish Capital of the World’ doesn’t lie.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Manzanillo
blocks.text: Choose your own adventure — the bay, the countryside or both — and make your Manzanillo cruise stop one you’ll never forget.

blocks.heading: Cuyutlan Turtle Sanctuary and Salt Museum
blocks.text: Journey south to Cuyutlán where sea and land history meet: visit a salt museum in a century‑old barn, then the Tortugario sanctuary for endangered turtles and crocodiles, finish with refreshments and natural vistas before heading back to your ship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Manzanillo: Colonial Colima
blocks.text: Cruise the coastline into the state capital Colima where volcano silhouettes hover above colonial squares, then walk amid 2,000‑year‑old ruins at La Campana (complete with shaft tombs and ancient streets). After lunch of local specialties you’ll root into regional history before returning to the ship. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Magic Pueblos: Nogueras & Comala with Lunch
blocks.text: Visit two ‘Pueblos Mágicos’: Nogueras with narrow cobblestone alleys and rich displays in its hacienda‑museum, then the whitewashed town of Comala under volcano watch. Enjoy a sidewalk café lunch in the plaza, soak the views and meander at your pace before heading back. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Salt Flats & Countryside
blocks.text: Travel into the countryside where salt has been harvested for 600 years, join a seasonal salt‑harvest at the flats followed by a fruit‑farm stop and a visit to a brick‑making workshop, then finish at a beachside snack stop with ocean view. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Beach Resort Getaway for Families
blocks.text: Take a shuttle around Manzanillo Bay to a tropical resort with a private beach, pool laps, kids‑club fun and an optional spa session — all while you relax, swim or watch the sea do its thing before returning to port. Yeah, it’s an adventure… the kind you can fall into a deep contented sleep to. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Rum, Hacienda & Chocolate
blocks.text: Head into Colima with a motorcoach drive to a rum factory for production insights and tastings, then a 300‑year‑old hacienda in the foothills, then finish at a family‑owned chocolate factory where you’ll learn about cacao and enjoy a sample lunch before the return. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Manzanillo
blocks.text: Arriving by ship means you’re docked right in the heart of the bay, so shore time begins almost the moment you step off. Mexico cruise itineraries that include Manzanillo make it easy to slip into beach mode, explore historic centres or hit the water with minimal fuss. Whether you’re casting a line, sipping Baja wine or exploring town, the port is your launch pad.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Puerto Chiapas
Shore excursions to explore in Puerto Chiapas
blocks.text: Puerto Chiapas cruises are basically ‘choose-your-own-adventure’ stories — except the characters are ancient ruins, banana barons and agave-based spirits. These excursions peel back the layers of a region where nothing is boring, and everything tastes better with a little marimba in the air.

blocks.heading: Tapachula City & Rum Tasting
blocks.text: Start in the city, end at the distillery. This laid-back adventure combines Tapachula’s colonial core with a tour of a top-shelf rum factory. You'll walk away with new facts, tasty sips and an understanding of why Chiapas takes its spirits very seriously. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Tapachula Sampler & Time on Your Own
blocks.text: Half guided tour, half free-range exploring — this one drops you into Tapachula’s downtown to see stained glass windows that look like museum pieces and streets that double as dance floors. Marimbas echo, Chiapaneca dresses swirl and your only job is to soak it all in (and maybe snap a few photos for proof). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Folk Art, Tequila and Mezcal Tasting & Tapachula
blocks.text: Learn how blue agave becomes the stuff of legends, then taste why people write poems about mezcal. After sipping your way through a liquid history lesson, you’ll head to Tapachula’s plaza to roam, caffeinate or shop your way through the heart of the city — with just enough buzz to make everything sparkle. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Banana Farm & Community Exploration
blocks.text: This is where your cruise gets unexpectedly wholesome. Visit a community-run banana plantation and learn how sustainable farming powers an entire village. Then meet the locals (including the schoolkids your visit helps support). Spoiler alert: You’ll never look at your supermarket bananas the same way again. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Maya Tree Of Life & Chocolate Discovery
blocks.text: Ancient cosmology meets chocolate craftsmanship in this four-hour time warp. Explore the Izapa ruins, where millennia-old stone carvings still feel like they have something important to say — then head to a local village where the cacao flows freely and the dancing won’t wait for you to catch up. Seriously, pick up those feet! LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Izapa Ruins & Chocolate Demonstration
blocks.text: Get face to face with stone relics that are older than most countries, then watch locals whip cacao into something that's basically edible history. This combo of ruins and rich flavors isn’t just educational; it’s the kind of sensory overload you’ll be telling people about until they beg you to stop. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Puerto Vallarta
blocks.text: If you’re looking for the perfect mix of sun, sea and adventure, then Puerto Vallarta is a must-visit destination. This vibrant coastal gem offers everything from golden beaches and lush jungles to world-class dining and lively culture — making cruises to Puerto Vallarta an unforgettable way to experience Mexico’s Pacific paradise.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Puerto Vallarta
blocks.text: Make the most of your visit with unforgettable shore excursions in Puerto Vallarta. From snorkeling in hidden coves and ziplining through jungle canopies to savoring authentic Mexican cuisine by the beach, every experience captures the adventure and charm that make this port a highlight of any cruise.

blocks.heading: Speedboat, Horseback Ride, Snorkel & Lunch
blocks.text: Speed across the bay on a thrilling speedboat ride before journeying on horseback through lush jungle trails to a hidden waterfall. Afterward, dive into vibrant reef snorkelling, soak up the sun on an untouched beach and savour a delicious Mexican-style lunch with an open bar overlooking the waves. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Jungle Zipline and Rappelling
blocks.text: Soar above Puerto Vallarta’s lush jungle canopy on an exhilarating zipline adventure. Then descend waterfalls and natural rock walls on an unforgettable rappelling experience. Led by expert guides, this Jungle Zipline & Rappelling excursion combines heart-pounding thrills with breathtaking tropical scenery - perfect for travelers craving adventure in one of Mexico’s most stunning landscapes. LEARN

blocks.heading: Mahajuitas Cove, Yelapa & Lunch
blocks.text: Cruise along Banderas Bay aboard a catamaran, soaking in ocean views and spotting dolphins or humpback whales. Dive into the crystal-clear waters of Majahuitas Cove for snorkeling or kayaking, then enjoy a fresh buffet lunch. Continue to the secluded village of Yelapa, where you can hike to a jungle waterfall, swim or simply relax before a festive ride back to port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Whale Watching
blocks.text: Experience the thrill of a lifetime on this high-speed adventure in Puerto Vallarta. Cruise across the Bay of Banderas with expert guides as you spot humpback whales breaching, dolphins playing and sea turtles gliding by. With refreshments, expert narration and up-close encounters, this unforgettable excursion brings you face-to-face with the ocean’s most incredible wildlife. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Las Caletas Private Beach Getaway For Families
blocks.text: Set sail on a catamaran to the secluded paradise of Las Caletas, once the private hideaway of Hollywood director John Huston. Nestled in lush jungle and turquoise waters near Puerto Vallarta, the family-friendly escape features beach games, snorkelling, a kids’ adventure zone and buffet lunch - an unforgettable tropical shore excursion. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Sea Lion Swim & Lunch
blocks.text: Swim alongside playful sea lions in the warm waters of Puerto Vallarta, where these curious and friendly creatures delight guests with their energy and charm. After your unforgettable encounter, enjoy a delicious lunch overlooking the stunning ocean views. This is an experience that perfectly combines adventure, wildlife and relaxation. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Why cruise in the Mexican Riviera?
blocks.text: Learn more about Mexico while touring historical landmarks, sharing a traditional meal with locals or relaxing on the sun-drenched beaches.

blocks.heading: Ships on this itinerary
blocks.text: Our Princess fleet includes ships that offer a multitude of amenities and feature the innovative MedallionClass® experience. From a balcony stateroom, take in the sights and sounds of the colorful cultures ashore before enjoying the “sabor” of local cuisine in one of our many eateries during your Mexican Riviera cruise.

blocks.heading: The Malecon
blocks.text: Spend an entire day walking along the Malecon, Puerto Vallarta’s beach boardwalk. Shop for regionally crafted goods — like woven baskets or a pair of leather boots — and meet the locals who created them. Stop for lunch at a nearby restaurant, where you can enjoy delicacies like tamales and pozole with a seafront view. Or watch street performers sing and dance, and get up close to larger-than-life

blocks.heading: Mazatlan Cathedral
blocks.text: On a Mexican Riviera cruise with Princess, travel back in time to the 19th century during a visit to Mazatlan’s Cathedral Basilica of the Immaculate Conception. Admire the Moorish and Gothic architecture, and marvel at statues of famous saints — like Matthew, Mark, Luke and John — that decorate the church’s exterior. Then head inside to see baroque decor, crystal chandeliers and gold-lined murals.

blocks.heading: Medano Beach
blocks.text: With an abundance of activities to do on both land and sea, Medano Beach offers something for the whole family. Relax on the golden shores, or indulge in a waterside lunch nearby. Float in the turquoise sea, or make some waves on a jet ski ride. Your dream beach day awaits on a Mexican Riviera cruise to Cabo.

blocks.heading: Mexican Riviera excursions
blocks.text: On a seven-day Mexico cruise or a 10-day itinerary, you can find expertly crafted excursions on every itinerary. Zipline across forests and rappel down waterfalls in Puerto Vallarta. Spend the day catching marlin and tuna in the world-class fishing port of Mazatlan. Or scuba dive through Cabo’s protected marine sanctuary. blocks.heading: Why cruise in the Mexican Riviera with Princess?
blocks.text: Experience the country’s unique character the second you step on the ship with traditional Mexican cuisine, events and activities.

blocks.heading: Famous for a reason
blocks.text: Recognized by UNESCO for its cultural heritage and preservation of culinary techniques, Mexican and Spanish cuisine is a big part of the region’s culture. Sample the bold flavors and creative combinations for yourself on a cruise to Mexico with Princess. In many of our dining rooms, enjoy Mexican-themed dishes — like ceviche, fajitas and coconut cocadas — for breakfast, lunch and dinner.

blocks.heading: Mariachi and Margaritas
blocks.text: Sip, savor and sway to the music with onboard activities that give you a taste of Mexican tradition. Sample tequila while learning about the drink’s history from a local expert, and indulge your taste buds with tacos and fajitas. blocks.heading: Pottery
blocks.text: Also known as Talavera, pottery in Mexico is distinguishable by its vibrant blue and stark white complexion. This unique art form originated from Talavera de la Reina in Spain and was brought to Mexico during the 15th century. As the Talavera technique progressed, artists began incorporating yellows, greens and oranges, but blue and white continue to remain the primary colors. With Mexico’s abunda

blocks.heading: Salsa
blocks.text: No two salsas taste the same, which is why you should add it to your list of things to buy in Mexico as soon as you find one you like. From Pico de Gallo to salsa verde and everything in between, these unique blends of tomatoes, onions and spices can elevate any dish. blocks.heading: Mezcal or tequila
blocks.text: Exclusive to the state of Mexico, tequila and its smoky-tasting cousin Mezcal are true icons of the region. Since each spirit is so versatile, they’re one of the best things to buy in Mexico ports for a loved one or friend. Use them in your cocktails or sip and savor each one over ice. blocks.heading: Hand-blown glass
blocks.text: Mexico has been refining the art of glass blowing for over 500 years, making them a true master of the craft. Using specialized techniques and acute concentration, artists can create everything from jars and vases to pitchers and drinking glasses. blocks.heading: Jewelry
blocks.text: Silver has a long and rich history in Mexico, especially in the form of jewelry. This material dates to the Aztecs, who first recognized that it was one of the country’s most abundant resources. They quickly mastered the art of metal working to create special tokens of their culture. This resource is still as plentiful as ever, making it one of the easiest things to buy in Mexico. blocks.heading: Coffee
blocks.text: If you’ve ever tasted Mexican coffee, you know it’s a true culinary delight. From the earthy tones to the hint of sweetness and the final touch of spice on your palette, Mexican coffee is unlike any other. headings.text: Things to do in Manzanillo, Mexico

blocks.heading: Things to do in Manzanillo, Mexico
Zócalo
blocks.text: The center of life in Manzanillo is the zócalo, or the main plaza. This central square is constantly filled with townspeople going about their business, and during a visit to this locale, you can people-watch to your heart's content. In particular, locals like to gather here to throw rice to the many pigeons that populate the square. Moreover, the plaza's flowering trees, fountain and spectacular

blocks.heading: Manzanillo beaches
blocks.text: No list of things to do in Manzanillo, Mexico is complete without mentioning the city's bevy of beaches. The town has over 40 miles of pristine Pacific coast, with each beach seemingly a perfect blend of glowing golden sand and swaying palm trees. Whether you want to go for a dip, try your hand at sea kayaking or just lie out in the sun, Manzanillo's beaches are a must-see attraction.

blocks.heading: Start your Mexico adventure
blocks.text: VIEW CRUISES

blocks.heading: Las hadas golf resort
blocks.text: For a different kind of relaxation, you may want to pay a visit to Las Hadas Golf Resort. This world-class facility features amenities like an 18-hole championship golf course, a 70-slip marina and plenty of opportunities for aquatic fun, making it a great place to base your Manzanillo adventure.

blocks.heading: Cuyutlan turtle sanctuary
blocks.text: Just outside the city, you will find several other attractions that make the Mexican Riviera one of the world's greatest tourist attractions. You can witness the region's amazingly diverse wildlife when you visit the Tortugario Ecological Center, a facility dedicated to the conservation of endangered species. The most popular attraction here is the turtle sanctuary, which is the largest of its kin

blocks.heading: Colima and comala
blocks.text: A pair of other nearby attractions give you a glimpse into Mexico's rich cultural heritage. The city of Colima holds ruins dating back more than 2,000 years, while the town of Comala features 500 years of history and views of two stunning volcanoes. What's on your list of things to do in Manzanillo, one of the jewels of the Mexican Riviera? View Mexico cruises.

blocks.heading: Why a Baja California cruise?
blocks.text: On a Sea of Cortez cruise with Princess, discover culture around every corner.

blocks.heading: History
blocks.text: History is an important part of Mexico’s story. On a Baja California cruise, discover tales from ancient civilizations when you visit San Jose Del Cabo, just a short drive from Cabo San Lucas. Between the 18th-century architecture and the Spanish colonial character, let the preserved charm of this rural town transport you to Mexico’s past. Hear stories from locals, and learn city secrets from expe

blocks.heading: Cathedrals
blocks.text: Inspired by 19th-century California mission-style architecture, Mexico’s cathedrals tell a unique story of times past. On a Sea of Cortez cruise to La Paz, visit the Cathedral de Nuestra Senora de la Paz. Admire the preserved stained-glass windows that decorate its exterior. Then step inside to see a collection of paintings and statues dedicated to Virgin Mary, the city’s patron saint.

blocks.heading: Heritage
blocks.text: Taste, see and meet true Mexican heritage on a Baja California cruise with Princess. In Loreto, stroll down the cobbled streets decorated with multi-colored homes, shops and museums. Sample Mexican seafood — like “chocolate” clams cooked over rocks — while sipping on spicy margaritas. Or meet the locals on a visit to the Main Plaza or during a traditional Mexican fiesta.

blocks.heading: Natural wonderlands
blocks.text: From beaches to jungles, Mexico’s landscapes are untamed. During your Sea of Cortez cruise, see these terrains like never before. In Puerto Vallarta, take a boat to Las Caletas, a secluded oasis surrounded by sandy shores and forests. Hike through the island’s interior alongside a local guide, or zipline through the woods at the Kids Adventure Park. Then take a dip in the sea before your boat ride

blocks.heading: Mexico cruises onboard experience
blocks.text: Experience the country’s unique character the second you step on the ship with traditional Mexican cuisine, events and activities.

blocks.heading: Mexican and Spanish cusine
blocks.text: Recognized by UNESCO for its cultural heritage and preservation of culinary techniques, Mexican and Spanish cuisine is a big part of the region’s culture. Sample the bold flavors and creative combinations for yourself on a cruise to Mexico with Princess. In many of our dining rooms, enjoy Mexican-themed dishes — like ceviche, fajitas and coconut cocadas — for breakfast, lunch and dinner.

blocks.heading: Activities
blocks.text: Sip, savor and sway to the music with onboard activities that give you a taste of Mexican tradition. Sample tequila while learning about the drink’s history from a local expert, and indulge your taste buds with tacos and fajitas. Or let loose with your loved ones during a mariachi performance, and dance to the lively tune of violins and guitars. On a cruise to Mexico with Princess, activities lie

blocks.heading: Events
blocks.text: On select sailings in October and November, discover the region’s heritage with our Mexican Fiesta. Celebrate the Day of the Dead, a holiday to commemorate loved ones who have passed. From face painting to Aztec flower-making, there are activities for the whole family on a cruise to Mexico. Learn a traditional dance, decorate marzipan skulls and make a skeleton out of pasta. blocks.text: Mexico Cruise Excursions

blocks.heading: Beach getaways
blocks.text: From relaxation to exploration, Mexico’s beaches are filled with activities. Sunbathe on the shores of Manzanillo’s beaches, with vibrant waters and palm trees as your backdrop. Or embark on a snorkeling adventure off the coast of La Paz, kayak along the waters of Loreto and let the natural beauty of Cabo’s shores inspire your next love story. With Princess cruise excursions, Mexico’s best is at y

blocks.heading: Wildlife encounters
blocks.text: From whale sharks to sea turtles, meet the personalities that call these lands home with our Mexico cruise excursions. Come face-to-face with sea lions during a snorkel expedition. Swim with dolphins in Cabo San Lucas or watch whales rise above the water's surface as you explore the Gulf of California's marine sanctuary near Puerto Vallarta.

blocks.heading: Adventure in the outdoors
blocks.text: Thrill-seekers and nature-lovers unite on our cruise excursions through Mexico’s wilderness. From the mountains to the sea, explore Puerto Vallarta’s beauty in a 4-wheel ATV. Zipline through Cabo’s sierra range, and soar past vast canyons and granite walls. Or embark on an open-air, off-road adventure through Mexico’s lush jungles and traditional villages, where locals share stories of their cultu

blocks.heading: Historic and city highlights
blocks.text: See the Mexican Riviera’s most sought-after sights, from the cathedrals of La Paz to the galleries of Mazatlan. Shore excursions transport you back to the 19th century as colonial towns tell tales of times past. As you pass the 300-foot shipwreck in Manzanillo and the Jesuit Mission Museum in Loreto, expert guides offer insider history of the people, places and pursuits before you.

blocks.heading: Tequila tastings
blocks.text: Our Mexico shore excursions take you to the birthplace of tequila deep in the countryside. See how this beloved liquor is prepared — from agave gardens to your glass — during a chef-led demonstration in Puerto Vallarta. Learn about the cultural significance of tequila during your time at Hacienda Doña Engracia. Or visit some of Mazatlan’s finest distilleries, and sample varieties while enjoying sn

blocks.heading: Local artisan crafts
blocks.text: Known for its affluent museums and artisan goods, Puerto Vallarta is brimming with masterpieces. Stroll through galleries and craft shops during a full-day tour crafted by a local artist. Find everything from woven décor to pottery. During a visit to a nearby vista, try your hand at painting, and let our Mexico shore excursions spark your creativity.

blocks.text: Discover the beauty of New England with a variety of itineraries to choose from in both summer and fall. See New England's most scenic coastlines, taste Maine’s famous lobster, and visit some of the most iconic lighthouses. Explore Cape Breton Island (Sydney). The options are endless on cruises to New England with Princess.

blocks.text: Calling all history buffs - follow the Founding Fathers' footsteps around the historic Virginia triangle and visit Jamestown and Colonial Williamsburg on excursions through Norfolk. This unique itinerary sails from New York in the summer and visits popular ports where history was made. Explore the Freedom Trail in Boston, Fort Sumter in Charleston and more to gain a deeper understanding of what sh

blocks.heading: Why cruise New England?
blocks.text: See the charm & history of New England

blocks.heading: Savor fresh regional seafood
blocks.text: The quaint New England of earlier times is alive and well in charming port cities, like Portland and Newport. Grab a bowl of clam chowder or a lobster roll, or enjoy fresh Maine blueberries.

blocks.heading: Cruise from New York
blocks.text: A leading global metropolitan city, New York City influences the world’s commerce, finance, culture, fashion and entertainment. Sail roundtrip from the city that never sleeps and discover world-famous landmarks like the New York Stock Exchange or the Statue of Liberty. Explore iconic neighborhoods, and see the city through the eyes of the locals.

blocks.heading: Cruise from Quebec City
blocks.text: Feel like you’ve traveled to France without leaving North America. Duck into a café for wine and brie, and explore the architecture of Old Québec, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Enjoy the beautiful Quebéc City before you set sail on a 10-14 day Canada & New England cruise.

blocks.heading: Cruise from Boston
blocks.text: Discover the historic and cultural treasures and the quaint New England charm Boston has to offer. A city known for attracting history buffs, academics, sports fanatics and beer drinkers is now also calling foodies, outdoor enthusiasts, music lovers and cultural travelers to experience its beauty before embarking on a Canada & New England cruise.

blocks.heading: Cruise to iconic rocky coastlines
blocks.text: Cruise Eastern Canada and discover a decidedly French influence, from the idyllic coastal villages of Nova Scotia to the Rue St. Louis in Québec City. See the best-known sights, such as the lighthouse at Peggy's Cove in Halifax or the churches of Saint John.

blocks.heading: Revisit history from Colonial times
blocks.text: Cruise New England and discover America's roots along its rocky coastline. Visit historic cities like Philadelphia, home of the Liberty Bell, the house where Thomas Jefferson wrote the Declaration of Independence, as well as the great melting pot of New York City.

blocks.heading: All you need to know about New England

blocks.heading: Lifestyle & culture
blocks.text: Savor the unique tastes of an authentic Māori hangi or sample award-winning wines from Picton. See how the Māori’s rich heritage comes alive in the Bay of Islands / Pēwhairangi, and discover how Napier’s / Ahuriri beautifully preserved 1930s architecture pays homage to the Māori by merging the linear symmetry of Art Deco with tribal motifs.

blocks.heading: Natural wonders & landscapes
blocks.text: Witness the unparalleled beauty of what locals call “Godzone” (God’s own country) on a hike into Tauranga’s / Tauranga Moana Wai-O-Tapu thermal valley and be rewarded with spectacular mud pools, geysers and rainbow-colored lakes. Or venture farther south to explore the South Island’s rugged coastline and charming ports — from the Scottish-inspired city of Dunedin to Akaroa, where French influence

blocks.heading: Unique experiences on New Zealand / Aotearoa cruises
blocks.text: New Zealand’s vast, dramatic and diverse landscape is the unrivaled home of Tolkien’s mythical Middle Earth. Journey to the city of Edoras and walk in the footsteps of The Lord of the Rings in Wellington, and visit Peter Jackson’s Weta Studios. Marvel at the sight of twinkling glowworms in Auckland’s Glowworm Grotto, and explore Wellington’s Zealandia, nicknamed "Jurassic Park," in search of the g

blocks.heading: UNESCO world heritage sites
blocks.text: Sail into a world of surreal beauty in Fiordland National Park / Piopiotahi, where the verdant flanks of snowcapped peaks plunge into the crystalline waters of ice-carved fiords. Or visit the Tongariro National Park outside of Napier / Ahuriri, which holds the title of first park in the world to receive UNESCO World Heritage status for both its natural and Māori spiritual and cultural value.

blocks.heading: Landmarks
blocks.text: Don’t miss the famed Christchurch Botanic Gardens, which boasts the finest collection of exotic and indigenous plants in New Zealand, Port Chalmers’ Larnach Castle (the country’s only castle) or cruise to Auckland / Tāmaki Makaurau and see the Sky Tower, the tallest man-made structure in the southern hemisphere.

blocks.heading: Art, museums & historic treasures
blocks.text: Wellington’s number-one attraction, the Te Papa National Museum, showcases Māori and Pacific cultural treasures, New Zealand’s extraordinary natural life and its most important works of art.

blocks.heading: Celebrations & Romance
blocks.text: It's difficult to imagine something more romantic than sailing through the alluring cities and charming countryside of Europe. While on board your European cruise, we cater to your sentimental side with private dining on your balcony — like breakfast for two or a sunset dinner — honeymoon packages, flowers and chocolates delivered to your room and couples-only massages in the Sanctuary.

blocks.heading: Accommodations
blocks.text: Your stateroom is where you rest and recharge between adventures. That’s why every room is equipped with the expertly designed Princess Luxury Bed, 100% Jacquard-woven cotton linens. Whether you go interior or all-out in a suite, our staterooms will make you feel right at home. Especially for families traveling together who can enjoy the option of connected rooms.

blocks.heading: Dining
blocks.text: From savory Norwegian meatloaf to sweet Icelandic celebration cake, Northern Europe is bursting with flavor. Head ashore to enjoy Icelandic skyr with porridge for breakfast, and savor a Norwegian seafood dinner. Or embark on an all-encompassing culinary tour right on board with our Chef’s Table Lumiere. Or book an appointment at the Lotus Spa®. Enjoy soothing treatments — like facials, hot stone massages and detoxifying wraps — that will leave you energized for upcoming adventures.

blocks.heading: Enhance your adventure
blocks.text: Panama Canal Cruise Ports & Excursions

blocks.heading: Historic marvels & exotic sensations
blocks.text: We’re the destination experts. Every year, we sail more voyages to the Panama Canal than any other cruise line, so no one knows the exotic jungles of Panama, the historic roads of Colombia or the sandy beaches of Aruba like Princess®. Photo: Cartagena, Colombia

blocks.heading: Discovery at SEA & shore excursions
blocks.text: Princess® has joined forces with Discovery™ to introduce Discovery at SEA, offering immersive experiences you won’t find anywhere else. Onboard, participate in hands-on activities and events. On shore, Discovery™ and Animal Planet™ recommended excursions and exclusive options you can only get from Princess. Photo: Schooner cruise in Aruba

blocks.heading: Set Your Course for Adventure
blocks.text: Browse Shore Excursions

blocks.heading: Panama
blocks.text: Yes, the Panama Canal is a true wonder... But beyond the locks, there’s even more to see. Walk among the ruins of Casco Viejo, the original site of Panama City, a UNESCO site. Visit the architectural marvel known as the BioMuseo. Part art, part science, this museum is acclaimed as Panama’s newest icon. Enjoy traditional native music, song and dance at Embera village. See wildlife in their natural

blocks.heading: Costa Rica
blocks.text: Enjoy a gentle rafting adventure down the beautiful Corobici River in Puntarenas. Explore a vibrant rainforest filled with exotic tropical plants as you ride in a leisure boat down the world famous Tortuguero Canals. Be alert to spot the bird life along the riverbank as well as other animals such as caimans, turtles, monkeys, and sloths! Photo: Veragua rainforest

blocks.heading: Colombia
blocks.text: Cartagena is a vibrant city that harbors a fascinating and colorful past, and a lively, welcoming present. Admire the architecture of Cartagena’s Old City, born at the height of the Spanish empire and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Shop the quaint markets in search of that perfect souvenir. Applaud a Colombian folkloric professional dance and music show. Design your own emerald jewelry with a hands

blocks.heading: Mexico
blocks.text: From the Pyramids of La Campana in Manzanillo to the 227 species of birds that call the Copalita River home in Huatulco, and from a 200-year-old coffee plantation in Puerto Vallarta to the colorful coral that resides in the warm waters of Cabo San Lucas, Mexico’s ports of call are unlike any other on the Mexican Riviera. Photo: Tropical bird in Mazatlán, Mexico

blocks.heading: Guatemala
blocks.text: In Puerto Quetzal, trek up the active Pacaya Volcano and take in panoramic vistas of towering trees, and lush vegetation dotted with exotic orchids. Walk in the footsteps of Mayan warriors in the ancient ruins of Iximche. See how Guatemalan coffee is cultivated, harvested, and processed from the seeding of the coffee bean to the preparation of the coffee beverage during a tour of Filadelfia Coffee

blocks.heading: Caribbean
blocks.text: Tranquil aquamarine waters, a rich history and breathtaking landscapes make the captivating Caribbean a treasured paradise. View hundreds of exotic butterflies flying freely within large meshed enclosures in Aruba. Discover the undersea splendor of Grand Cayman aboard the world’s first submarine designed for passenger excursions. Photo: Horseback riding in Aruba

blocks.heading: Get to Know the Region
blocks.text: Our award-winning excursions help you discover sun-kissed beaches, lively cities and untold natural wonders

blocks.heading: Lifestyle & culture
blocks.text: The diversity of the cultures you’ll meet in Central and South America is a wonder to behold. Travel by dugout canoe to an Embera village in the heart of Chagres National Park in Fuerte Amador. Visit Fort San Lorenzo, one of the most complete and biggest forts built in Panama. Learn how your favorite coffee arrives in your cup with a tour of one of Guatemala’s most renowned coffee farms in Puerto

blocks.heading: Natural wonders & landscapes
blocks.text: Enjoy a bird's-eye-view of the world with a high-flying zipline ride in Costa Rica. Relax in a deluxe 1938 air-conditioned dome car for a different perspective on the Canal riding on the Panama Canal Railway—a Discovery™ recommended excursion. Cruise through the mangroves of Puntarenas to the sanctuary of the Scarlet Macaw. Listen carefully for chirping birds and monkey calls as you soar over Gamb

links.text: Learn more about Panama Canal excursions

blocks.heading: Unique adventures
blocks.text: Experience the rainforest world of sloths, learn why they're sooo slow and why these drowsy tree-dwellers sleep up to 20 hours a day when you visit the Sloth Sanctuary, an Animal Planet™ Exclusive excursion, in Limón. Step into the "birthplace of time," when you visit the Mayan archaeological site of Izapa just outside of Puerto Chiapas. Learn more about Panama Canal excursions Photo: Sloth Sanctu

links.text: Learn more about Panama Canal excursions

blocks.heading: A fiesta of flavors
blocks.text: Try authentic Panamanian cuisine, celebrating the cultural influences of African, Spanish and Native American, with traditional favorites such as empanadas, bollos and torrejitas. Sample the Grand Cayman’s world famous rum cake made with local rum. Raise your glass and say “salud” as you sip tequila at Puerto Vallarta’s Viva Tequila. Photo: Local cuisine

blocks.heading: UNESCO world heritage sites
blocks.text: Retrace the steps of 17th-century Spanish colonists with a walk through the well-preserved Old City of Cartagena. Stroll the historic quarter of Panama City, once renowned as one of the richest cities in the New World. Admire the architectural delights of Antigua in Puerto Quetzal, home to several 17th- and 18th-century landmarks. Photo: Cartagena, Colombia

Why cruise Baltic & Scandinavia
blocks.text: From astounding fjords to astonishing palaces, the treasures of Scandinavia and Baltic region welcome you to explore.

blocks.heading: Deep-rooted sauna
blocks.text: Deep-rooted sauna culture of the Baltic region – often paired with a bracing polar plunge – a revitalizing tradition that dates back to the 13th century. More than a ritual, sauna is a way of life, valued for cleansing the body and mind, restoring balance, fostering deep relaxation, and the sharing of ideas, it remains a place where time slows and connections are strengthened, best experienced the

blocks.heading: Museums
blocks.text: Get up close to historical gems on a Baltic cruise with Princess. View ships and treasures found in royal burial mounds of the Oslo fjord at the Viking Ship Museum. Or learn what it’s like to be a prize winner at Stockholm's Nobel Peace Museum, and get up close to the world’s oldest preserved warship at the Vasa Museum

blocks.heading: Fjords & viking legends
blocks.text: A Baltic cruise is your key to the Norwegian Fjords — Mother Nature’s crown jewel. Upon arriving in Stockholm, ride along the brinks of Tyrifjord, a 52-mile inlet that boasts greenery and deep blue waters. Relax amidst the serenity of Oslo Fjord, and discover treasures from beneath its seas at the Viking Ship Museum. With Princess, sail to Scandinavia’s oldest capital and revel in the natural wond

blocks.heading: Unique architecture
blocks.text: Travel to lands where ancient architecture abounds. Wander the cobbled streets of Stockholm’s old town, Gamla Stan, one of the largest and best-preserved medieval city centers in Europe. Explore a treasure trove of late Renaissance and Rococo architecture in Copenhagen, like Rosenborg Castle, Kronborg Castle or Frederiksborg Castle. Or walk through 'Upper Old Town,' home to some of Tallin's oldest

blocks.heading: Comfort culture
blocks.text: A region renowned for exceptional quality of life, deeply rooted in the cultural philosophies of hygge and lagom. These guiding ideals emphasize balance, comfort, and intentional living – fostering environments where wellbeing, community connection, and harmony with nature are prioritized.

blocks.heading: Why cruise with Princess
blocks.text: Curated comfort, world-class entertainment and international flavors await you.

blocks.heading: Celebrations & Romance
blocks.text: It's difficult to imagine something more romantic than sailing through the alluring cities and charming countryside of Europe. While on board your European cruise, we cater to your sentimental side with private dining on your balcony — like breakfast for two or a sunset dinner — honeymoon packages, flowers and chocolates delivered to your room and couples-only massages in the Sanctuary.

blocks.heading: Accommodations
blocks.text: Your stateroom is where you rest and recharge between adventures. That’s why every room is equipped with the expertly designed Princess Luxury Bed, 100% Jacquard-woven cotton linens. Whether you go interior or all-out in a suite, our staterooms will make you feel right at home. Especially for families traveling together who can enjoy the option of connected rooms.

blocks.heading: Dining
blocks.text: From the spice of Moroccan tagine to the sweetness of Greek Baklava, Europe’s flavor profile is incredibly diverse. On a Transatlantic cruise with Princess, taste the best of Europe on board with specialty dining. Say cheers during a lively lunch at a British-style pub and try English favorites like bangers and mash or shepherd's pie. Or savor hearty Italian pastas at Sabatini’s℠ Italian Trattoria

blocks.heading: Entertainment
blocks.text: Embark on adventures by day, and indulge in entertainment by night. Watch Movies Under the Stars® at our 300-square-foot outdoor theater. Attend original productions from Broadway legend Stephen Schwartz, composer of Wicked. Or learn traditional moves, like flamenco or Irish stepdance, and listen to popular music from the destinations on your itinerary. On a European cruise with Princess, the choi

blocks.heading: Relaxation
blocks.text: Your European cruise should be every bit as refreshing as it is inspiring. Unwind in the Sanctuary, a retreat just for adults, and relish in tranquility. Or book an appointment at the Lotus Spa®. Enjoy soothing treatments — like facials, hot stone massages and detoxifying wraps — that will leave you energized for upcoming adventures.

blocks.heading: Casino
blocks.text: Experience the thrill of cards, dice, roulette, and blackjack at our onboard casino during your European cruise. Learn from our expert staff or seasoned guests, and put your skills to the test. For a more relaxed pace, enjoy the slot machines, or join fellow travelers for Bingo and exciting group tournaments. The casino promises nonstop excitement, whether you're a seasoned player or just playing

blocks.text: History is an important part of Mexico’s story. On a Baja California cruise, discover tales from ancient civilizations when you visit San Jose Del Cabo, just a short drive from Cabo San Lucas. Between the 18th-century architecture and the Spanish colonial character, let the preserved charm of this rural town transport you to Mexico’s past. blocks.heading: Cathedrals
blocks.text: Inspired by 19th-century California mission-style architecture, Mexico’s cathedrals tell a unique story of times past. On a Sea of Cortez cruise to La Paz, visit the Cathedral de Nuestra Senora de la Paz. Admire the preserved stained-glass windows that decorate its exterior. Then step inside to see a collection of paintings and statues dedicated to Virgin Mary, the city’s patron saint.

blocks.heading: Heritage
blocks.text: Taste, see and meet true Mexican heritage on a Baja California cruise with Princess. In Loreto, stroll down the cobbled streets decorated with multi-colored homes, shops and museums. Sample Mexican seafood — like “chocolate” clams cooked over rocks — while sipping on spicy margaritas. Or meet the locals on a visit to the Main Plaza or during a traditional Mexican fiesta.

blocks.heading: Natural wonderlands
blocks.text: From beaches to jungles, Mexico’s landscapes are untamed. During your Sea of Cortez cruise, see these terrains like never before. In Puerto Vallarta, take a boat to Las Caletas, a secluded oasis surrounded by sandy shores and forests. blocks.heading: Mexico cruises onboard experience

blocks.heading: Mexican and Spanish cusine
blocks.text: Recognized by UNESCO for its cultural heritage and preservation of culinary techniques, Mexican and Spanish cuisine is a big part of the region’s culture. Sample the bold flavors and creative combinations for yourself on a cruise to Mexico with Princess. In many of our dining rooms, enjoy Mexican-themed dishes — like ceviche, fajitas and coconut cocadas — for breakfast, lunch and dinner.

blocks.heading: Activities
blocks.text: Sip, savor and sway to the music with onboard activities that give you a taste of Mexican tradition. Sample tequila while learning about the drink’s history from a local expert, and indulge your taste buds with tacos and fajitas. blocks.heading: Things to do in Buenos Aires
blocks.text: Buenos Aires is less of a city and more of a beautifully complicated character — part faded debutante, part revolutionary and part poet nursing a cigarette in the back of a bookstore. It doesn’t try to win you over; it challenges you to keep up. And with so much to see and do in the City of Fair Winds, you’ll love every minute of the chase.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Buenos Aires
blocks.text: You want to see what Buenos Aires has to offer. We want to show you. These curated excursions get you to the heart of what makes this port memorable, without the stress of logistics blunting your adventure.

blocks.heading: From Mate to Malbec
blocks.text: Roll up your sleeves and dive into the food culture: make mate, prep empanadas, taste provoleta and chorizo, sip Malbec and enjoy dessert. Hands‑on, delicious and oddly educational, this experience will send you on your way with a deeper understanding of Argentina’s culinary soul — and possibly a strong opinion about how mate should be brewed. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Buenos Aires: La Boca & Recoleta Cemetery
blocks.text: What city includes a cemetery in its ‘best of’ list? Buenos Aires does, and you’re going to see why. But first you’ll start by rolling through the city’s core — El Centro, the Bohemian San Telmo district, the Colon Theatre and the sprawling green of Palermo. Then you head into La Boca. After lunch, you’ll visit Plaza de Mayo with its Casa Rosada (yes, the famous Pink House). Finally, wander Recole

blocks.heading: Tango Show & City Drive
blocks.text: This one pairs dance with discovery in the best possible way. Drive through the neighborhoods, soak in the old and the new, stop at the Metropolitan Cathedral, stroll Plaza de Mayo and feel the heartbeat of the city. Then dive into La Boca, watch the tango in action and wrap it with lunch and an unforgettable performance. You’ll leave with a satisfied stomach, a rhythm in your step and a newfound

blocks.heading: Ultimate Buenos Aires: Iguazú Falls Discovery
blocks.text: Switch gears and fly from port to the thundering cascade of Iguazú Falls in a full‑day epic. See 275+ separate falls spanning more than 1.6 miles wide, ride the eco‑jungle train, stare into the Devil’s Throat and conclude the day drained, awed and ready for dessert. Between the rainforest mist and the roar of the water, it's like nature turned the volume all the way up. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Home‑Hosted Dinner Tour
blocks.text: You didn’t come all this way to eat at some Americanized burger joint, did you? Skip the generic restaurant. Arrive at a local home, sit at a table among locals, talk, taste yerba mate, savour homemade dishes and maybe make some new friends for life. It’s intimate, warm and worlds away from the tourist menu. No frills, no filter — just food, conversation and a window into what daily life in Argent

blocks.heading: Tigre Delta & River Cruise
blocks.text: Take a half-day break from the city and glide through the Tigre Delta’s thousand-island maze, where the Paraná River splits into quieter arms lined with freestanding row houses and Italianate villas. The breeze stays light, the birds stay loud and life moves at river speed. With expert narration and the occasional wave from locals on their docks, this is Argentina in soft focus — all color, calm a

blocks.text: When your ship docks at the port of Buenos Aires, you get prime access to the city. The port facility puts you close to the waterfront and downtown, letting you hit the Puerto Madero waterfront or stroll toward Plaza San Martín within minutes of stepping off the gangway. blocks.heading: Things to do in Cartagena
blocks.text: Cartagena explodes with colonial flair, sweeping sea views and pirate‑era drama. The city’s fortified Old Town, balconies dripping bougainvillea and Caribbean rhythms combine for an experience that’s as rich in history as it is in color. Expect fortress ramparts, boutique‑nick streets and local bites that make you pause mid‑chew just so you can hold onto the moment a little longer.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Cartagena
blocks.text: Step off the ship and choose your own adventure: fortress history, craft‑making, rainforest wildlife, rhythm‑filled street heat… or better yet, why not a little bit over everything?

blocks.heading: Canoe Tour of Mangrove Tunnels & Old City Walk
blocks.text: Take a scenic drive to La Boquilla canyon and board a rustic canoe through twisting mangrove tunnels alive with birds and crabs. Then pivot to Cartagena’s Old City for artisan shopping in Las Bóvedas. Expect a mix of natural calm, small‑village authenticity and city buzz (not a bad bit of adventuring, if we do say so ourselves). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Cartagena: San Felipe Fortress & Las Bovedas
blocks.text: This half‑day tour launches at the massive Castillo de San Felipe de Barajas, covers Las Bóvedas for shopping in former dungeons, takes you into the walled Old City and ends at the Historical Museum of Cartagena before a local drink break overlooking the harbor. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Emerald Jewelry Making Class & Diploma
blocks.text: Unleash your inner artisan at Cartagena’s Caribbean School of Jewelry: you’ll craft a sterling‑silver ring or pendant set with real emeralds, get schooled in mining history, shoot through a video and then shop the results. You’ll leave with your own handiwork — and a grin when you remember you made your favorite souvenir instead of just buying it. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Dancing into the Walled City
blocks.text: You step from the Clock Tower into vibrant Old City streets, warm up with three Afro‑Caribbean dance styles — salsa, champeta and cumbia — and then join a hands‑on lesson where you’ll shimmy like you mean it. The grand finale? A high‑energy performance by your instructors that’ll make you redefine what your next night out could be. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: National Aviary of Colombia
blocks.text: Bird‑nerd heaven: hop a 45‑minute coach ride outside Cartagena to a lush 17‑acre eco‑park where hundreds of species roam freely. Walk rainforest trails, peer into mangrove and desert‑station exhibits, sip a cool drink lakeside and collect shots of kingfishers, macaws and migratory flocks. Bring your binoculars—and maybe a louder, “See that one!” LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Tour of Getsemaní & the ‘Old City’
blocks.text: Start in the artsy, vibrant neighborhood of Getsemaní, sip coconut lemonade under palm fronds and then head toward Parque Bolívar and the Old City’s narrow colonial streets. You’ll pass Spanish‑era houses, the Gold Museum and street‑vendor stalls selling handcrafted oxcarts. Camera at the ready, because this one’s heavy on moments worth capturing LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Cartagena
blocks.text: Cartagena cruises drop you at a quay that sits within striking distance of city walls, cafés, artisan shops and taxi lines. You’ll hit narrow colonial lanes, street‑side empanadas and fortress ramps without a long ride. blocks.heading: Things to do in Easter Island
Shore excursions to explore in Easter Island
blocks.text: Stepping onto Easter Island is like stepping into an open‑air archive where the pages are made of basalt. Start at Orongo Village, the cliffside ceremonial site of the birdman cult, where petroglyphs stare back with big‑energy mythic gravitas. Head into the volcanic bowl of Rano Raraku, the quarry where hundreds of unfinished Moai rest mid‑creation. Wander Vinapu for stonework so precise it sparks

blocks.heading: Ultimate Easter Island Moai & Umu Feast
blocks.text: This five-hour feast-for-the-senses mixes ancient statues with stone-oven cooking and delicious folklore. After marveling at Ahu Akivi’s seven sea-gazing moai, you’ll head to Anakena Beach for a traditional umu meal… slow-cooked in hot lava rocks and wrapped in banana leaves. Add in a cultural performance, a few palm trees and a bit of ocean breeze, and you’ve got a serious contender for the best

blocks.heading: Best of Easter Island
blocks.text: If you're going big, go full moai. This full-day tour is a greatest hits collection of Easter Island, from the eye-popping moai at Ahu Tahai to the volcanic quarry at Rano Raraku (where hundreds of statues still cling to the hillside like a half-finished art project). You'll also hit Tongariki’s legendary lineup of 15 giants and wrap it all up with pink sands and two more moai platforms at Anakena

blocks.heading: Ahu Tahai & Rano Raraku
blocks.text: This 3-hour makes every second count. You'll kick off with the solemn, staring figures of Ahu Tahai (including the island’s only statue with restored eyes). Then it’s off to Vaihu’s temple ruins, followed by Rano Raraku’s eerie volcano quarry. Final stop: the 15 moai of Tongariki, all lined up for your consideration. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Orongo Village & Ahu Akivi
blocks.text: Want to stand on the edge of the world and look into a volcano? This 3-hour tour brings you face-to-face with the massive crater of Rano Kau before continuing into Orongo village. You'll also meet a moai with four hands (yes, four) and end with the only moai that look out to sea. Strange? Yes. Fascinating? Even more so. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ahu Tahai & Island Drive
blocks.text: This easy-going tour delivers major moai moments without the rush. First up: Ahu Akivi, where seven stone figures stand watch inland. Then it's on to Vaihu’s crumbled history before ending at Ahu Tahai. Here, no two statues are alike, and yes, one of them feels like it might be staring into your soul (you’ll know which one when you see it). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Fortaleza
blocks.text: Fortaleza may have started life as a Dutch stronghold, but today it’s more known for surf, sun and a personality that goes big. This northeastern Brazilian city throws cathedrals, craft markets and caipirinhas at you like it’s trying to win your affection by sheer force. The beaches are wild, the architecture is all kinds of extra and the weather forgot how to be bad — which is exactly what makes

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Fortaleza
blocks.text: This isn’t just a beach day. These excursions serve drama, architecture and actual dune buggies. Possibly in the same afternoon.

blocks.heading: Fortaleza by Private Car – Half Day with Guide
blocks.text: Prefer your chaos curated? This private car tour comes with your own driver-guide and the option to skip straight to what matters most to you. Architecture, beaches, back-alley art — it’s all on the table. Just remember, entrance fees aren’t included, so keep a little cash on hand. Or don’t, and see how good you are at saying “please let me in” in Portuguese. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Fortaleza City & Beach
blocks.text: Start with a coastal drive past Mucuripe’s fishing boats and Iracema’s statue-studded shore before hitting the Fortaleza Cathedral. From there, Mercado Central comes at you with handwoven everything and impulse-buy energy. Wrap it all up at Praia do Futuro where you can swim, snack or just nap under an umbrella like a sand-streaked genius. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Fortaleza
blocks.text: This tour’s got it all: Gawk at a Gothic-Roman cathedral, visit the iron-laced opulence of Teatro Jose de Alencar and then browse local wares at EMCETUR — a 19th-century jail turned handicraft market (because Brazil does irony better than anyone). Finish with ocean views from Espigão de Pedras Bridge and maybe a photo of you pretending not to sweat. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Fortaleza on Your Own
blocks.text: If you’ve ever wanted to drop into a Brazilian city with two hours and the vaguest inkling of a plan, this is your moment. A guide gives you tips, then sets you loose near markets, museums and sun-baked chaos. Good for seasoned travelers; bad for people who need to be told where to be and when. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Porto das Dunas Beach Escape
blocks.text: Hop a coach and head to Beach Park. FYI: this is not a beach-themed park; it's an actual oceanfront resort complex with waterslides, caipirinhas and a 134-foot free-fall ride that might rewire your brain. Spend three hours swimming, lounging or chasing adventure down the shoreline. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cumbuco Beach & Dune Buggy Ride
blocks.text: Why risk burning your feet on hot sand when you could have 2 tons of beach-churning rubber and metal as an insulator? It’s not a real visit to Cumbuco unless you’ve been hurled across sand dunes in a 4x4 that laughs at gravity. blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Lima (Callao)
blocks.text: Getting to Peru is only half the fun. Our curated shore excursions help you get the most out of your shoreday (and ensure that you’re back on board before your ship pulls up anchor).

blocks.heading: Evening City Drive & Dinner at Casa Aliaga
blocks.text: Start with a sweep through downtown Lima for photo ops at the Plaza de Armas, then move on to Miraflores, where stately mansions overlook the sea. After admiring the Park of Love and its mosaic-heavy sculpture garden, duck into the Indian Market to add something alpaca-adjacent to your suitcase. But the main event? Dinner at Casa Aliaga: a colonial mansion gifted by Pizarro himself that’s been hom

blocks.heading: Best of Lima
blocks.text: Your deep dive into the “City of Kings” starts at the Gold Museum, where 20,000 artifacts prove that the Inca were not playing around when it came to shine. From there, head to the Plaza Mayor — ground zero for Spanish colonial drama — and the Cathedral of Lima, final resting place of Francisco Pizarro (or at least his most likely remains). Continue on to Santo Domingo Convent with its pink walls

blocks.heading: Pachacamac Ruins & Peruvian Prancing Horses
blocks.text: Start at the Larco Museum to get your pre-Columbian fix, then trade artifacts for ancient ruins at Pachacamac, a massive site once used for sun-god worship. Afterward, you’ll head to a local hacienda where the Peruvian Paso Horse takes center stage. Between folklore dancing, buffet lunch and garden views, this day goes full-spectrum Peru before you return via the coastal Pan-American Highway. LEAR

blocks.heading: Lima by Night & Magic Fountains
blocks.text: See the city shine, literally. This evening tour cruises through Miraflores by motorcoach, stopping to admire the Park of Love before heading to the Park of the Reserve. There, the Magic Water Circuit lives up to its name with 13 interactive fountains synchronized to music and lasers. This isn’t your average splash pad; it’s a full-blown sensory show certified by Guinness and adored by everyone fr

blocks.heading: Scenic Boat Ride to the Palomino Islands
blocks.text: Hop a boat from the Callao marina and ride out past shipwreck sites, rocks and sea cliffs stacked with birds. The real stars, though, are the sea lions lounging around the Palomino Islands like they’ve got nowhere to be. The boat pauses near the colony so you can leap in (voluntarily!) for a quick swim. Cap it off with snacks and salty hair as you cruise back toward the pier. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Walk Around Plaza de Armas
blocks.text: A walking tour that hits every major landmark in Lima’s historic core. From the Presidential Palace to the Cathedral’s twin towers, the square is your personal checklist of must-see colonial architecture. Swing by the Basilica and Convent of San Francisco with its famous catacombs, stroll past the House of Osambela and stop for a juice break in the heart of Old Town. This is slow-travel at its bes

blocks.heading: Things to do in Manta
blocks.text: Manta is a sun-drenched escape where golden beaches, world-class seafood and vibrant coastal culture come together. Whether you’re chasing adventure or perfect relaxation, this seaside city delivers unforgettable experiences.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Manta
blocks.text: Manta offers a range of unforgettable shore excursions, from exploring artisanal villages and lush coastal landscapes to discovering pristine beaches and rich local culture. Each experience lets you dive deeper into the heart of Ecuador’s vibrant coast.

blocks.heading: Nature & Beach Escape at Las Tanusas
blocks.text: Escape to Las Tanusas Eco-Retreat & Spa, where Ecuador’s pristine Pacific coastline and lush tropical forest create a serene backdrop. Begin with a scenic drive, welcome drink, and guided hike before choosing yoga, a mixology class or a Valdivian-inspired pottery workshop. Enjoy a three-course Ecuadorian lunch and leisure time by the pool or beach, returning to port renewed and refreshed. LEARN MO

blocks.heading: Fish Market, Cancebi Museum & Ceviche Tasting
blocks.text: This relaxed Manta tour begins at the city’s bustling open-air fish market, where fresh snapper, lobster and tuna fill the stalls beside the beach. Stroll the scenic malecón before exploring the Cancebi Museum’s remarkable collection of artifacts. Then savor a traditional ceviche paired with a local beer, completing your sensory experience before returning to the pier. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Jaboncillo Ceremonial Hill Exploration
blocks.text: Travel to Picoazá to explore Cerro Jaboncillo, Ecuador’s largest archaeological site and the ceremonial center of the advanced Manteño culture. After a scenic motorcoach ride, browse artifacts at the Interpretation Center before an exclusive look inside the restoration room. Then walk the open-air museum’s ancient paths to hilltop ceremonial sites and panoramic views that bring this remarkable civ

blocks.heading: Trails & Crafts of the Pacoche Wildlife Refuge
blocks.text: Witness Ecuador’s diverse landscapes and culture on this four-hour journey to the Pacoche Wildlife Refuge. Travel from desert terrain to lush jungle before following your guide through forest trails in search of howler monkeys, tropical birds and native plants. Enjoy refreshments at a local lodge, explore traditional craft demonstrations, including sugarcane milling and Panama hat weaving. LEARN M

blocks.heading: The Magic of Corazon & Fragatas Islands
blocks.text: Embark on a full-day adventure to the Isla Corazón and Fragatas Wildlife Refuge, beginning with a scenic ride to Bahía de Caráquez and a warm welcome at Casa Ceibo Hotel. Cruise across the estuary to explore mangrove forests and vibrant birdlife, including Pacific frigatebirds. Weather permitting, walk a short trail to scatter mangrove seeds before enjoying a three-course Ecuadorian lunch. LEARN M

blocks.heading: Discovery Cocoa in Manabi
blocks.text: Discover Ecuador’s rich chocolate heritage on an immersive adventure. Travel from the port into the peaceful Manabí countryside to explore a working cacao plantation, where you’ll learn about cultivation, sustainability and cacao varieties. Then visit a local workshop to watch artisans transform beans into chocolate and try your hand at tempering, molding and tasting your own sweet creation. LEARN

blocks.heading: Things to do in Montevideo
blocks.text: Montevideo blends old-world charm with modern coastal energy, offering everything from historic plazas and colorful markets to sunlit beaches and vibrant neighborhoods. It’s a city made for wandering, discovering and savoring at your own pace.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Montevideo
blocks.text: Montevideo’s shore excursions let you experience the best of Uruguay—from historic city tours and vineyard tastings to coastal drives and lively cultural neighborhoods. Each outing offers a rich look into the country’s traditions, flavors and scenic beauty.

blocks.heading: Biking Montevideo
blocks.text: Explore Montevideo on an energizing bike tour that pairs sightseeing with a fun, eco-friendly ride. Starting at the pier, follow your guide through historic plazas, including Zabala and Constitution Square and admire landmarks like the Metropolitan Cathedral and Salvo Palace. Continue past coastal neighborhoods to the whimsical Pittamiglio House and Punta Carretas Lighthouse before cycling back to

blocks.heading: Best of Montevideo
blocks.text: Experience authentic gaucho life during a full-day visit to Estancia La Rabida, a 100-year-old working ranch outside Montevideo. After a scenic drive from the pier, meet the welcoming owners and explore the estate aboard tractor-drawn carriages and antique cars. Try traditional ranch activities, then enjoy a classic asado lunch with local wine, lively folk music and traditional gaucho dancing. LEA

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Montevideo & Spinoglio Winery
blocks.text: Explore Montevideo’s vibrant sights on a guided city tour featuring Independence Square, the historic Old City, the Solís Theatre and the majestic Legislative Palace. Along the way, enjoy photo stops and stories from your knowledgeable guide. Conclude at Spinoglio Winery with a tour of the 19th-century wine vault, a tango performance and a delicious lunch paired with local wines. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Montevideo Sightseeing & Varela Zarreanz Winery
blocks.text: Experience the best of Montevideo and its countryside on this six-hour journey through city landmarks and historic vineyards. Enjoy a panoramic tour of the capital, with stops at Independence Square and scenic Virgilio Square, before heading to Varela Zarranz Winery. Explore its 19th-century estate, learn about traditional winemaking and savor a Uruguayan barbecue lunch paired with local wines bef

blocks.heading: Colonia Del Sacramento
blocks.text: Explore Colonia del Sacramento, Uruguay’s oldest town and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. After a scenic drive, follow your guide on a walking tour through the 1745 walled city, wandering cobblestone streets, colorful colonial homes and landmarks like the Street of Sighs, the Basilica and San Francisco Convent. Visit the historic bullring, enjoy lunch at a local restaurant and browse for souvenirs.

blocks.heading: Montevideo Carnival & Performance
blocks.text: Experience Uruguay’s legendary Carnival by stepping into the role of a murga performer during South America’s longest celebration. Enjoy a guided tour of Montevideo before arriving at a lively tablado, where vibrant costumes, spirited singing and animated performances bring the festival to life. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Montevideo
blocks.text: Montevideo is a standout highlight on many South American cruise itineraries, offering a perfect blend of culture, history and coastal charm. pages.metaDescription: Cruise to Pisco with Princess and explore Peru’s sun-soaked coast. Vineyards, wildlife and ancient wonders await on your 2026–2027 adventure.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Pisco
blocks.text: Pisco offers a blend of coastal beauty, rich history and natural wonders, from charming plazas to stunning desert landscapes. It’s the perfect gateway to Peru’s famous vineyards, wildlife-filled islands and ancient archaeological sites.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Pisco
blocks.text: Pisco’s shore excursions open the door to some of Peru’s most unforgettable experiences—explore wildlife encounters at the Ballestas Islands, desert adventures in Paracas and visits to historic vineyards. Each outing showcases the region’s natural beauty, and culture.

blocks.heading: Islas Ballestas Wildlife Cruise
blocks.text: Set out on a scenic cruise to the Ballestas Islands, known as the “Galapagos of Peru,” where abundant marine wildlife and dramatic rock formations await. Glide past sea lions, fur seals, terns and endangered Humboldt penguins as they bask, dive and soar around you. With colonies of hundreds of thousands of birds and the striking Candelabra geoglyph, this half-day adventure is unforgettable. LEARN

blocks.heading: Nazca Lines Flight
blocks.text: Experience the breathtaking Nazca Lines from the best vantage point—the sky. After a short drive to Pisco Airport, board a small aircraft and soar above nearly 170 square miles of ancient geoglyphs carved by the Nazca between 500 B.C. and 500 A.D. As your captain shares their history and mysteries, you’ll spot iconic shapes like hummingbirds, monkeys, fish and more etched across the desert floor.

blocks.heading: Tambo Colorado
blocks.text: Explore the remarkably preserved Inca complex of Tambo Colorado, where kings, priests and warriors once walked. See the king’s throne platform, the high priest’s chambers and walls still marked with bands of ancient color. With expert guidance, gain vivid insights into the empire’s coastal presence before traveling through the Pisco Valley’s desert dunes and fertile farmlands. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Paracas National Reserve
blocks.text: Discover the beauty of the 877,000-acre Paracas National Reserve on this half-day tour featuring scenic drives, photo stops and short nature walks. Explore Peru’s oldest marine reserve, home to desert landscapes, sweeping dunes and abundant wildlife, including flamingos, migratory birds and diverse marine life. Along the way, your guide shares insights into ancient Paracas culture. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: The Pisco Route
blocks.text: Journey into Peru’s Pisco Valley to explore the vineyards and distilleries behind the country’s signature spirit. Continue to Fundo Al Arrabalm to witness time-honored methods, then tour the state-of-the-art Caravedo Distillery for a tasting of its acclaimed El Portón pisco. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Puerto Chacabuco
blocks.text: Tucked deep inside a narrow Patagonian fjord, Puerto Chacabuco is the jumping-off point for Chile’s wild Aysén region. Waterfalls spill down sheer cliffs, dense forests hug the water’s edge and quiet valleys lead inland to protected reserves filled with rare wildlife.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Puerto Chacabuco
blocks.text: Patagonia’s raw beauty takes center stage the moment you step ashore during your cruise to Puerto Chacabuco. Princess shore excursions bring you deeper into this remote corner of Aysén, where you will marvel at the glacier-fed rivers and valleys shaped by wind and water for thousands of years.

blocks.heading: Lake Los Palos Kayaking
blocks.text: Paddle the quiet waters of Lake Los Palos with guidance from local experts who share insights into the region’s wildlife and ecology. Glide toward the mouth of the Tabo River, where birds often gather along the shoreline, then step ashore to explore the forest on a short walk. A snack break adds a warm touch before the return paddle.

blocks.heading: Chacabuco & Río Simpson National Reserve
blocks.text: Trace the landscapes that define Aysén on a relaxed journey into Río Simpson National Reserve. Visit the small natural history museum, then follow easy paths through evergreen forest and along the rushing river, a favorite among local fly fishers. The drive back travels through Puerto Aysén, offering a glimpse of daily life in this remote Patagonian outpost.

blocks.heading: Coyhaique & Simpson Valley
blocks.text: Travel inland through glacier-carved scenery to explore the Río Simpson National Reserve before continuing on to Coyhaique, the region’s lively capital. Browse handicrafts in the Plaza de Armas, admire the surrounding peaks and learn about the area’s natural heritage at the reserve’s small museum. Light refreshments round out this scenic look at northern Patagonia.

blocks.heading: Discover Patagonian Nature
blocks.text: Immerse yourself in the sights and sounds of Aikén del Sur Private Park, known for its lush forest and glacier-fed waterways. A naturalist guide leads a gentle walk along the Waterfall Trail, where mosses, ferns and old-growth trees frame the rushing Barba del Viejo cascade. Afterward, unwind at the quincho with local snacks before returning to port.

blocks.heading: Oro Verde Trail Hike
blocks.text: Set out on a guided hike through one of northern Patagonia’s most evocative landscapes. The Oro Verde Trail winds through dense forest and over clear streams once used by early settlers. After your trek, relax at a traditional quincho for regional bites and a Calafate Sour before heading back toward the fjords surrounding Puerto Chacabuco.

blocks.heading: Patagonian Fjord & Hot Springs Experience
blocks.text: Cruise through the sheltered Aysén fjord toward Ensenada Perez, where open-air thermal pools sit between forested cliffs and calm water. Soak in mineral-rich springs, keep an eye out for seabirds and enjoy light snacks on the return voyage. The journey offers sweeping views of the Andes and the rugged channels that define this part of Patagonia.

blocks.heading: Snorkeling with Sea Lions
blocks.text: Cruise over the gulf where whales sometimes surface during breeding season. As you near Punta Loma you’ll probably hear the sea lions long before you see them. After anchoring, slip into a wetsuit, mask and fins and follow your guide into the water for an unbelievable swim session. The sea lions often glide and spiral around snorkelers with curious confidence, creating a moment that feels equal pa

blocks.heading: Best of Puerto Madryn: Punta Tombo Reserve
blocks.text: Begin your day on a long, open-road drive across the Patagonian steppe toward one of the world’s largest Magellanic penguin colonies. At Punta Tombo you’ll have the chance to see burrows, nesting pairs and chicks (depending on the season). Rangers keep watch, but the penguins are famously unbothered by human guests, which turns this into a rare close-range wildlife encounter. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Paleontology Museum & Punta Loma
blocks.text: Kick things off in Trelew at the region’s world‑renowned Paleontology Museum, home to a treasure trove of fossils and an entire lineup of dinosaur skeletons. After exploring Patagonia’s prehistoric side, continue to Punta Loma for a cliff‑top vantage point overlooking South America’s only permanent sea lion colony. blocks.heading: Things to do in Puerto Montt
blocks.text: Tucked between snow-dusted volcanoes and the deep-blue waters of Chile’s Lake District, Puerto Montt feels both peaceful and untamed. As the gateway to Patagonia, this vibrant port town connects travelers to alpine valleys, emerald lakes and the wild fjords of southern Chile.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Puerto Montt
blocks.text: Set out from the pier and discover the natural wonders that make Chile’s Lake District so extraordinary.

blocks.heading: Fly Fishing on the Maullin River
blocks.text: Cast your line in the clear waters of the Maullín River, where rainbow trout and king salmon thrive. Surrounded by the quiet forests of northern Patagonia, you’ll enjoy expert guidance, a riverside picnic and a day of pure tranquility before returning to port. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Puerto Montt
blocks.text: Spend the day surrounded by lakes, waterfalls and alpine beauty as you journey through Chile’s famed Lake District. Visit Petrohué Falls and the charming towns of Puerto Varas and Frutillar, where German heritage comes alive through architecture, local cuisine and the warm hospitality of southern Chile. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Lake Esmeralda, Petrohue River & Puerto Varas
blocks.text: Cruise across brilliant Lake Esmeralda, whose vivid color mirrors the forests and mountains that surround it. Visit Petrohué Falls inside Vicente Pérez Rosales National Park, then stroll the boutique shops of Puerto Varas before returning to port with a camera roll full of unforgettable lake views. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Osorno Volcano, Petrohue River & Puerto Varas
blocks.text: Ascend the slopes of Osorno Volcano, a perfectly symmetrical peak rising high above Chile’s Lake District. Explore Petrohué Falls and the lively resort town of Puerto Varas before a traditional lunch that blends local and German flavors in one of the most picturesque corners of Patagonia. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Frutillar & German Settlers Museum
blocks.text: Step into the region’s European past with a visit to Frutillar, a lakeside village founded by German settlers in the 19th century. Tour the German Colonial Museum, explore its gardens and millhouse, and stop in Puerto Varas to browse handcrafted wares before returning to Puerto Montt. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: A Taste of Chile Culinary Experience
blocks.text: Join a celebrated local chef for a hands-on exploration of Chile’s coastal cuisine. Shop for fresh seafood and produce at a local market, then cook and enjoy a meal paired with regional wines in the lakeside town of Puerto Varas. It’s the perfect blend of culture and flavor. LEARN MORE

Shore excursions to explore in Puerto Quetzal
blocks.text: Princess® shore excursions let guests uncover Guatemala’s many sides — past and present, mountain and coast, tradition and taste.

blocks.heading: Pacaya Volcano Hike & Countryside Drive
blocks.text: Few experiences rival standing on the flank of an active volcano. The Pacaya hike rewards guests with volcanic landscapes, sweeping views and a new appreciation for Guatemala’s raw, untamed side. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Past & Present Colonial Antigua
blocks.text: Antigua Guatemala blends history and color in every corner, from sun-washed plazas to ornate convent ruins. Wander among colonial landmarks and discover jade workshops that preserve the artistry of the Mayan world. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Country Drive & Coffee Plantation
blocks.text: Venture into Guatemala’s coffee heartland and see how one of the world’s most beloved beans goes from plant to cup. Rolling fields and volcanic soil frame this aromatic journey, ending with a freshly brewed taste of the country’s pride. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cerveceria 14: Beer, Food & Fun
blocks.text: Relax at Cervecería 14, a craft brewery tucked in the highlands outside Antigua. Sample local favorites as you take in sweeping views of Agua, Fuego and Acatenango volcanoes — proof that good beer pairs perfectly with great scenery. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Mayan Culture and Mystique & Lunch
blocks.text: Walk through the ancient site of Iximché, where stone pyramids and plazas still echo with Mayan ceremony. A guided visit and traditional lunch reveal Guatemala’s living connection between past and present. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Auto Chapin Drive-Through Nature Park & Zoo
blocks.text: Families can enjoy a relaxed adventure through Auto Chapín Park, home to giraffes, lions, tropical birds and native wildlife. The drive-through route and shaded walkways make it an easy, fun day surrounded by nature. LEARN MORE
