blocks.heading: Things to do in Punta Arenas
blocks.text: Punta Arenas sits at the end of the world like it owns the place — and honestly, it kind of does. Perched above the legendary Strait of Magellan, this town has been equal parts survival story, colonial outpost and penguin-adjacent curiosity. Expect ornate architecture from Patagonia’s wool-boom days, cemeteries that feel like sculpture gardens and more wind than your jacket is emotionally prepared

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Punta Arenas
blocks.text: Get into the land where the people are friendly, museums bring the past to life and the penguins do whatever it is that penguins do (waddling, swimming and eating fish, mostly). These excursions take you to where nature, history and culture combine.

blocks.heading: Condors of Patagonia
blocks.text: Head north to Estancia Olga Teresa and meet the only locals more dramatic than the penguins — the Andean condors. These birds don’t fly so much as levitate with attitude, and the Cerro Palomares viewpoint gives you front-row seats to their aerial show. Spot them with help from local guides and high-powered optics, then return to port feeling humbled and maybe just a little more likely to keep an e

blocks.heading: Salesian Museum & Fort Bulnes
blocks.text: Start your day with a dose of old-money architecture at Plaza de Armas Muñoz Gamero before diving into the Maggiorino Borgatello Museum’s mix of native tools, Catholic relics and Fuegian artifacts. Then tour Cementerio Municipal, a cemetery so over-the-top it makes Versailles look like a starter home. Wrap it up at Fort Bulnes — the hilltop replica of Chile’s OG settlement fort — with some sweepin

blocks.heading: Paine National Park
blocks.text: Hop on a charter flight and land in Torres del Paine National Park — home to surreal mountains, teal lakes and waterfalls that just won’t quit. Stops include Sarmiento Lake, Laguna Amarga and a drive-by of the Cuernos del Paine (a gigantic jagged rock formation that looks like a fantasy artist took things a little too far). Lunch at Cerro Castillo gives you a moment to regroup before you head back

blocks.heading: Exclusive Local Asado Experience
blocks.text: Touch the toe of the Magellan statue at Plaza de Armas Muñoz Gamero (local superstition says it guarantees that you’ll return someday). Then soak in the view from Cerro de la Cruz before heading into the countryside for a full-blown Patagonian asado. Lamb, open flames, Calafate sours and more red wine than you’ll admit to later — it’s the kind of feast that makes you forget how hard the wind is tr

blocks.heading: Magdalena Island Penguin Reserve
blocks.text: Sail two hours through the Strait of Magellan and arrive at Magdalena Island, home to 100,000+ Magellanic penguins living their best shrieky lives. Walk among their burrows, dodge their noise and learn what happens when penguins decide your hiking trail is actually their driveway. This is one of the best Punta Arenas cruises excursions for getting up close to wildlife. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Punta Arenas
blocks.text: Get a taste of everything. Start with a hilltop view at La Cruz, then hit Plaza de Armas Muñoz Gamero for a quick souvenir fix and statue selfie. The Salesian Museum delivers artifacts and cultural deep dives, while the Patagonia Institute gives you a crash course in how some early settlers survived with nothing but sheep and grit. End at Cementerio Municipal — not just for the history, but becaus

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Punta Arenas
blocks.text: Your ship docks at Muelle Prat (Prat Pier), placing you right at the edge of Punta Arenas — a city that’s chillier than it looks and way more stylish than it needs to be. Larger ships may require tendering, but once ashore, you’re minutes from key landmarks, shops and the kind of wind that’ll have you reconsidering your entire relationship with hats. This is a launchpad for South America and Antar

blocks.heading: Things to do in Rio de Janeiro
blocks.text: Set between rainforest-covered mountains and the Atlantic’s shimmering edge, Rio de Janeiro lives up to its nickname—the “Marvelous City.” The energy hums through every beach and street corner, where samba, sunshine and soul converge.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Rio de Janeiro
blocks.text: Rio’s landmarks sit across mountains, beaches and forested hillsides, so a guided excursion helps you take in the city’s biggest icons without worrying about distance or traffic. From cable car rides to forest safaris, each experience brings a different side of this dynamic city into view.

blocks.heading: Easy Rio de Janeiro
blocks.text: Take in Rio’s highlights at a comfortable pace. Visit the city’s modern cathedral and enjoy a photo stop among its soaring stained glass. Then follow the coastal drive along Ipanema and Copacabana, where white sand beaches curve past high-rise hotels and oceanfront cafés. A stop at Flamengo Park frames perfect views of Sugarloaf and Corcovado. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Christ the Redeemer Statue
blocks.text: Make your way through downtown Rio before boarding the scenic train that climbs Corcovado Mountain. The ride takes you through the lush Tijuca Forest as the city opens beneath you. At the summit, stand at the base of Christ the Redeemer and take in sweeping views over the beaches and bays that define Rio’s coastline. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: City Drive & Sugarloaf
blocks.text: See Rio from street level and sky-high vantage points on this half-day tour. Visit the striking Rio de Janeiro Cathedral, then continue along Flamengo Park toward the cable car. The ascent to Sugarloaf Mountain reveals a panorama of the city’s shoreline, including Copacabana and Botafogo, with photo stops at both the summit and Urca Station. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Tijuca Forest 4X4 Safari
blocks.text: Venture into the world’s largest urban rainforest aboard a 4x4. The Tijuca Forest is home to hundreds of species, and your open-air ride offers chances to spot monkeys, tropical birds and lush plant life. Stops include Chinese Lookout and Taunay Falls, where the forest gives way to broad views of Rio’s peaks and shoreline. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Rio de Janeiro
blocks.text: Combine Rio’s most famous landmarks in a single day. Ride the train up Corcovado for a visit to Christ the Redeemer, then enjoy a Brazilian churrascaria lunch before heading to Sugarloaf Mountain. Board the cable car for views that stretch across Guanabara Bay and the city’s golden beaches. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Petropolis
blocks.text: Leave Rio behind as you climb into the green hills of the Serra dos Órgãos. Petropolis blends imperial history with mountain scenery, and your visit includes the ornate Imperial Museum and the grand Catedral de São Pedro de Alcântara. A traditional churrascaria lunch rounds out this relaxed escape from the city. LEARN MORE

Shore excursions to explore in San Antonio (for Santiago)
blocks.text: Getting to San Antonio is fun, but let’s face it; without the right curated experiences you’re only getting part of the experience. Make sure to check out these local adventure opportunities before you reach port.

blocks.heading: Easy San Antonio & Villages by the Sea
blocks.text: This is sightseeing for people who want the views without the step count. Cruise through San Antonio’s port district, duck into El Totoral to see a 200-year-old adobe church, then coast up to Algarrobo and El Quisco where oceanfront resorts meet sleepy villages. Optional refreshments and photo ops are included, along with enough breezy coastline to fully recharge your internal battery. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of San Antonio: Santiago & Viña del Mar
blocks.text: This one’s a power combo. Start with Santiago: historic monuments, government palaces, colonial plazas and enough architectural bravado to remind you it’s been around for 477 years. After lunch, coast over to Viña del Mar (home to beaches, casinos, floral clocks and presidential summer pads). Then roll through Valparaíso, where houses defy gravity and street art wins awards. This is your crash cou

blocks.heading: A Visit to a Winery & Panoramic San Antonio
blocks.text: Start with San Antonio’s gritty charm — all fishing docks and port logistics — then swap concrete for grapevines in Rosario Valley. You’ll tour Matetic Vineyards, where sustainable winemaking meets drinkable art, followed by a tasting that’ll have you casually saying things like “notes of black currant.” Bonus points for the wine shop that also sells wool goods, because Chile is never a one-trick

blocks.heading: Pablo Neruda, Isla Negra & Valparaiso
blocks.text: This one’s for literature lovers, Neruda nerds and anyone who’s ever wanted to sip wine in a poet’s living room. You’ll visit two of Pablo Neruda’s homes: La Sebastiana in Valparaíso (ocean views and art-filled corners) and Isla Negra (designed to look like a ship and crammed with shells and nautical ephemera). In between, you’ll dine like a Nobel laureate — three courses, local wine and existenti

blocks.heading: Casablanca Valley Wine Tasting & Lunch
blocks.text: Wine country, activated. Casablanca Valley may be the new kid on the Chilean block, but it came in swinging. Tour two wineries, enjoy a tasting straight from the barrel, then head to Estancia El Cuadro for a folkloric show, a wine museum and a lunch that will make you grateful that you’re not the one driving. blocks.heading: Things to do in Falkland Islands (Stanley)
Shore excursions to explore in Falkland Islands (Stanley)
blocks.text: Once your boots hit land, you’re staring down penguin colonies, wind-lashed coastlines and remnants of a war that left a major mark on the region. Princess provides the curated adventure opportunities to help you see it all.

blocks.heading: Bertha’s Beach & Flatlands Wildlife Excursion
blocks.text: Drive off the beaten path and then keep going… right into East Falkland’s remote Bertha’s Beach. It’s white sand, Arctic‑adjacent cliffs and a RAMSAR‑designated wetland where penguins, seabirds and the national flower (Pale Maidens), live in areas Charles Darwin once catalogued. This one is about four hours long, so bring some grit and a healthy respect for the elements. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: City Drive & Museum
blocks.text: Board the tender, land in Stanley and start with a cruise through town’s colorful houses and rolling moorland. You’ll stop at Christ Church Cathedral, admire the Whalebone Arch, view the Government House and visit the Historic Dockyard & Museum. The museum highlights the maritime past and the islands’ role in conflict, including relics from the war. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: 74 Days to Victory
blocks.text: This panoramic tour takes you from quiet Stanley streets to the fierce battle sites of the Falklands war. You’ll drive to Fitzroy and witness memorials at Sapper Hill, Mt. William, Wireless Ridge and more. Guides will share stories of the brutal 74‑day campaign and you’ll follow roads that saw armored vehicles and war‑planes juxtaposed against sheep farms. It’s raw, emotional and unforgettable. LE

blocks.heading: Fitzroy Farm Tour
blocks.text: Swap coastlines for sheared sheep and patagonian winds on this half‑day farm experience. Visit Fitzroy Farms where dogs herd sheep, polytunnels grow produce and the locals break for “smoko” with scones and pastries. You’ll feel the land, meet the people and see how life ticks when you’re this close to the edge of the map. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Taste of the Falklands & City Drive
blocks.text: Mix culture, cuisine and cruising through this three‑hour outing. Drive through Stanley’s British‑influenced streets, photo the Whalebone Arch and stop at The Camber for local delicacies and libations. Who knew that a little car ride and a little cuisine could make some big memories? LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Gentoo Penguins Expedition at Newans Station
blocks.text: Your tender lands, you transfer to a 4×4, then off‑road across East Falkland’s wild landscape to Newans Station. There you’ll find about 200 breeding pairs of gentoo penguins hopping around, joined by Southern giant petrels, skuas and kelp gulls. The 4×4 ride is rugged and the wildlife doesn’t wait for you — and that’s what makes it such a fantastic adventure. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Ushuaia (Tierra del Fuego)
blocks.text: People talk about being on top of the world, but what about the bottom? Ushuaia, Argentina is widely considered the ‘southernmost city’ on the globe, and is where you’ll find a striking mix of wilderness, history and seaside culture. Ancient forests, the icy expanses of the Beagle Channel and a former penal colony all combine to make this port a gateway to daring landscapes and unforgettable excur

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Ushuaia (Tierra del Fuego)
blocks.text: Pick from carefully selected tours that bring you face‑to‑face with what makes this port so compelling.

blocks.heading: Beagle Channel by Catamaran & Magellan Penguin Rookery
blocks.text: Board a catamaran, glide through the Beagle Channel and pretend you’re Darwin with better snacks. You’ll spot sea lions, imperial cormorants and Magellanic penguins doing their penguin thing on Hammer Island. The boat doesn’t land there, but it gets close enough to confirm that yes, they are aggressively cute. Pro tip: penguins may be in their formal wear but you’re going to want something a bit w

blocks.heading: Best of Ushuaia: Drive to the "End of the World"
blocks.text: You’ll leave town behind and cruise into Tierra del Fuego National Park where the roads (and the continent) eventually end. Ensenada Bay sets the tone with Beagle Channel views, followed by a stroll near Roca Lake that’s basically Patagonia’s idea of a flex. End your day at Lapataia Bay, standing at the actual, literal end of the Pan American Highway. It's 12,000 miles long and it stops here, whic

blocks.heading: Tierra Mayor Natural Reserve Trek
blocks.text: Set out from a remote cabin in Refugio Nunatak into lenga forest, peat bogs and beaver dams within the reserve. On this two‑hour hike you’ll spot birds like cara‑caras and parakeets, enjoy apple‑pie and tea back at the cabin and then ride back to Ushuaia. It’s an opportunity to get to know a little more about the natural world at the end of the world. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Fishing Village, King Crab & Gourmet Experience
blocks.text: You’ll drive past a glacial lake, through terrain where trees lean away from the wind out of sheer respect and land in Puerto Almanza — a fishing village that’s basically one extended king crab appreciation society. Local chefs lead a hands-on workshop, which ends with you eating the evidence. This is not your typical cooking class… unless your usual classes are surrounded by fjords and full of pe

blocks.heading: Canoe Adventure in Tierra del Fuego National Park
blocks.text: Strap on waterproof layers, wedge into an inflatable canoe and paddle across Acigami Lake like it’s the most casual epic thing you’ve ever done. The water’s glacial, the birds don’t care that you’re here, and the surrounding peaks basically heckle you with beauty. Start practicing your look of reverent awe, because you’re going to be using it a lot. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Southernmost Railway & Ensenada Bay
blocks.text: Give new meaning to the term “end of the line” as you ride the historic End of the World Train through forest and valleys into Tierra del Fuego National Park. After the roughly 45‑minute vintage rail ride you’ll head by coach to Ensenada Bay for sweeping views of the Beagle Channel and surrounding islands. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Ushuaia (Tierra del Fuego)
blocks.text: Docking in Ushuaia means you’ll arrive at a bustling yet compact harbor with access to shops, cafés and local character right at the edge of the Beagle Channel. Major excursions launch just minutes away, and if you’re on one of those South America cruises that heads even further south, this is your jump-off point. It’s all mountains, sea spray and penguins from here on out. In other words, for gue

What will you do on a Southern Caribbean cruise?
blocks.text: See what adventures await you off the beaten path, whether it’s exploring a Dutch-style city or kayaking through a mangrove forest.

blocks.heading: Mambo Beach, Willemstad, Curaçao
blocks.text: Grab a lounger and relax on the soft white sands, rent snorkel equipment and swim through the pristine blue waters observing magnificent sea life, or grab a snack at the many eateries on the boardwalk as you indulge in some luxurious shopping.

blocks.heading: Eagle Beach, Aruba
blocks.text: Perfection might be the best word to describe the picturesque Eagle Beach. Aruba cruises offer soft white sand, shimmering turquoise water and a quiet atmosphere making relaxation easy. Take in the surroundings from a lounge chair, swim the calm warm waters and enjoy local cuisine right near the beach.

blocks.heading: Kenepa Beach, Curaçao
blocks.text: A picturesque beach, sheltered between two rock outcroppings, makes for calm azure waters and relaxing beach days. The sand is soft, white and warm and everything you could want to complement the beautiful scenery is right at your fingertips.

blocks.heading: Caribbean cruise onboard experience featured program
blocks.text: Award-winning programs. World-class chefs. And Caribbean-themed activities, day and night. With Princess, your ship is a destination all its own.

blocks.heading: Deeper experiences of the islands
blocks.text: Discover the history of local distilleries while sampling some of the region’s best rums, meet the parrots and macaws that call the Caribbean home in the ship's Piazza, or sink into the rhythms of the region with steel pan drum lessons. Our onboard activities give you the chance to gain a deeper connection and understanding to islands you'll visit on your voyage.

blocks.heading: Comfortable accommodations
blocks.text: Your stateroom is your home away from home where you can rest up and recharge between adventures. With the expertly designed Princess Luxury Bed, luxurious 100% Jacquard-woven cotton linens and our SLEEP program, specially created by a board-certified sleep expert, you might just get the best sleep of your life. We offer staterooms ranging from interior cabins to full suites, and we even offer con

blocks.heading: Bringing local life aboard
blocks.text: Embrace the spirit of the islands the moment you step on your ship with our Rhythm of the Caribbean program. Savor island cuisine, sip signature cocktails and engage in authentic regional experiences. Dance beneath the stars to vibrant island rhythms at exclusive parties, and immerse yourself in one-of-a-kind cultural activities — from concerts and crafts to talks from shark experts and treasure h

blocks.heading: Never miss a beat
blocks.text: Say goodbye to the daily grind with our new Sail Away Party poolside on the top deck, dance to local music at one of the many Caribbean inspired concerts, or be the envy of every pirate at our high-energy gold treasure-inspired Terrace Pool Gold Party. Throughout your Caribbean cruise there will be events that invite you to fully experience the islands.

blocks.heading: Ship activities for every cruise to the Caribbean
Family
blocks.text: Enjoy a ship full of activities for the whole family, from Broadway-style shows to Discovery’s Shark Week all summer long, your family will be engaged in the Caribbean. Go stargazing under the stunning expanse of the night sky, compete in a family game night and savor the flavors of the islands together.

blocks.heading: Relaxation
blocks.text: Pamper yourself in the Lotus Spa® with a massage, facial or manicure, and feel renewed. Enjoy The Sanctuary, a lounge just for adults, where you can relax with a light meal, specialty drink and al fresco massages while digging into that novel you've been looking forward to reading. If you prefer more active relaxation, we offer Zumba, yoga and tai chi classes to burn off stress and raise your hear

blocks.heading: Things to do in Bali
blocks.text: Bali offers a vibrant mix of lush landscapes, serene temples and sun-soaked beaches. Whether you’re exploring rice terraces, diving into turquoise waters or savoring local cuisine, the island delivers unforgettable experiences at every turn.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Bali
blocks.text: Shore excursions in Bali offer an immersive look at the island’s culture, nature and spirituality—from temple visits and traditional dance performances to scenic drives through rice terraces and artisan villages. It’s an easy way to experience Bali’s vibrant beauty in a single day.

blocks.heading: Ubud Arts & Crafts Shopping Tour
blocks.text: Explore Bali’s artistic heart on a journey through Ubud and its surrounding villages. Meet master goldsmiths in Celuk, then continue to Kemenuh to watch a traditional barong dance and observe skilled woodcarvers at work. In Ubud, browse vibrant paintings at a local gallery and visit the historic 19th-century Ubud King Palace before enjoying a scenic drive back to the pier. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Twin Lakes & Bali Highlands
blocks.text: Explore Bali’s stunning highlands on a full-day tour that starts in the lively Sangeh Monkey Forest and continues to Lake Bratan, home to the iconic Ulun Danu Temple. Enjoy a scenic stop at the island’s “twin lakes,” followed by lunch and a visit to Pasar Candi Kuning market. Conclude your day in Tohpati, watching artisans create intricate batik and browsing local crafts. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Mt. Batur & Rural Bali with Local Family
blocks.text: Experience daily life in rural Bali on this full-day cultural excursion. Begin with a traditional breakfast in a local home, followed by a village walk and views of farmers tending rice fields. Visit Kehen Temple, enjoy an Indonesian buffet lunch overlooking Mt. Batur and explore Kemenuh’s renowned woodcarving studios, where you can watch artisans at work and shop for handcrafted pieces. LEARN MOR

blocks.heading: Ayung Whitewater Rafting
blocks.text: Begin your whitewater rafting adventure with a scenic drive through Bali’s lush rainforest, rice terraces and tropical plantations. After meeting your expert guides and receiving a brief orientation, paddle down the river past jungle ravines, waterfalls, cliffs and hidden Hindu shrines. Watch for wildlife along the banks before heading ashore to freshen up, enjoy lunch at the Royal Pita Maha Resor

blocks.heading: Kuta On Your Own
blocks.text: Enjoy a scenic motorcoach ride to lively Kuta, where you’ll have approximately four hours to explore at your own pace. Wander bustling streets filled with shops and restaurants, relax along Kuta’s famous beach or browse local markets for souvenirs. With easy access to taxis and plenty to see and do, this independent outing lets you experience Kuta at your own pace. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Tunjuk Village & Traditional Farming
blocks.text: Spend the day living like a Balinese farmer as you journey to Tunjuk Village for a hands-on experience in the rice paddies and a lesson in coconut tree climbing. After a warm village welcome, join your host family for traditional farm chores before enjoying a hearty local lunch. On the return drive, stop to admire the serene, lotus-filled Taman Ayun Temple, built in 1634. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Conflict Islands
blocks.text: A stop at the Conflict Islands feels like stepping into a private South Pacific lagoon, where calm turquoise water and untouched coral gardens set the pace for the day. Most of the atoll is uninhabited, which means the beauty here revolves around reefs, wildlife and easy, barefoot exploring.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Conflict Islands
blocks.text: So much of the Conflict Islands experience revolves around the water. The Islands are a privately-owned, remote atoll of 21 uninhabited islands. Princess shore excursions make it easy to see the atoll’s bright reefs, quiet beaches and protected wildlife while giving you plenty of time to simply enjoy the lagoon.

blocks.heading: Private Beach Bungalow
blocks.text: Enjoy a full day in a secluded beachfront bungalow with space to unwind between dips in the lagoon. You’ll have shaded seating, freshwater showers and views across the atoll from your own quiet corner of the island. It’s an effortless way to spend a relaxed day surrounded by the South Pacific at its most peaceful. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Glass Bottom Boat
blocks.text: Glide above the lagoon on a shaded glass bottom boat and watch the reef come to life beneath your feet. Clear views reveal schools of bright reef fish, soft coral gardens and turtles drifting through the shallows while your guide shares insight into this protected ecosystem. It’s an easy, comfortable way to see the atoll’s underwater world without getting wet. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Conflict Island Cruise
blocks.text: Circle the atoll aboard the Undersea Explorer for a laid-back look at the Conflict Islands’ unspoiled beauty. As you move between the 21 islets, keep an eye out for turtles, dolphins and manta rays moving through the lagoon’s deeper channels. Enjoy commentary, local fruit and baked treats while taking in wide open views that show just how remote this part of the Coral Sea really is. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Private Beach Picnic
blocks.text: Trade the bustle of onboard life for a secluded beach with only soft sand and warm water for company. After a scenic boat transfer, settle into a quiet cove with a picnic of fresh fruit, cheese and chilled wine. Spend the afternoon swimming, lounging or exploring at your own pace before cruising back across the lagoon. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Turtle Interaction Tour
blocks.text: Visit the Conflict Islands Conservation Initiative’s turtle nursery to meet rescued hatchlings and learn how rangers safeguard vulnerable species. Feed the young turtles, hear how eggs are relocated from high-risk beaches and discover how conservation efforts protect the atoll’s biodiversity. It’s a hands-on experience that shows the heart behind local wildlife preservation. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Reef Snorkel Adventure
blocks.text: Use a custom swim platform as your launching point into one of the most vibrant reef systems in the region. As you drift over coral formations and sandy shelves, look for colorful fish, sea stars and turtles gliding between patches of living reef. Staff guides help point out marine life so you get the most from your time in the water. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Conflict Islands
blocks.text: Sailings that visit the Conflict Islands often weave through remote corners of the Coral Sea, making them standouts on longer South Pacific and world cruise itineraries. These routes blend quiet atolls with cultural ports across Papua New Guinea and beyond, giving you a mix of bright reefs, village life and open-ocean scenery.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Lifou
blocks.text: Lifou offers a perfect blend of natural beauty and cultural discovery, from its crystal-clear lagoons and hidden caves to traditional Melanesian villages. Enjoy snorkelling, scenic walks and authentic local experiences that showcase the island’s unique charm.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Lifou
blocks.text: Experience Lifou’s stunning landscapes and local traditions through guided shore excursions that take you from coral-filled lagoons to dramatic limestone cliffs. Whether you're exploring caves, visiting a traditional tribe or snorkelling in pristine waters, these tours offer a memorable way to discover the island.

blocks.heading: Melanesian Encounter
blocks.text: Swoon over Lifou’s stunning northern coastline on this engaging half-day excursion, traveling along tree-lined roads as your friendly local guide shares stories and insights about the island. Take in panoramic views, learn about Lifou’s culture and traditions and enjoy plenty of opportunities to appreciate the natural beauty that makes this corner of Lifou so unforgettable. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Scenic Island Drive
blocks.text: Enjoy a relaxing half-day escape across Lifou as you travel with a friendly local guide along scenic, tree-lined roads through Easo Village, Xepenehe, Komo and Wé. Your destination is Luecila Beach, a pristine stretch of white sand along Baie de Chateaubriand. Sip a fresh coconut, then unwind with time to swim, sunbathe, or stroll. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Cliffs of Jokin
blocks.text: Experience Lifou’s beauty and culture on a half-day tour through Easo Village, known for its bay views, traditional homes and lush gardens. Visit the historic Notre Dame de Lourdes Chapel before heading to Mucaweng Vanilla Plantation for a guided tour and tastings. Then take in the dramatic fossilized coral cliffs of Jokin and explore the village while enjoying fresh coconut milk. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Lifou Vanilla House
blocks.text: Sip and savor the peaceful charm of Lifou, a blue-green oasis far removed from the rush of everyday life. This two-and-a-half-hour excursion invites you to experience the island’s natural beauty and rich history while enjoying time to browse local shops. It’s a relaxing and memorable way to take in the highlights of this tropical refuge. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Tropical Forest Walk & Secret Grotto
blocks.text: Experience Lifou’s lush beauty on this immersive half-day tour. Travel through the village of Easo before heading into the Lifou Tropical Forest for a guided walk among vibrant tropical and medicinal plants. blocks.heading: Hike Through The Ancient Forest

As you follow shaded pathways beneath towering trees, you’ll learn about native flora, medicinal plants and the island’s unique ecosystem. blocks.heading: Things to do in Luganville
blocks.text: Experience the raw beauty of the South Pacific on a cruise to Luganville, Vanuatu. This quiet coastal town creates experiences you’ll always remember with its vibrant culture, pristine waters and unforgettable landscapes. Luganville is the ideal destination for travelers seeking an authentic island adventure.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Luganville
blocks.text: Vanuatu’s second-largest town invites you to experience its rich cultural heritage, natural beauty and wartime past through a range of immersive excursions.

blocks.heading: Blue Lagoon Swim
blocks.text: Travel through coconut‑lined countryside en route to the Blue Lagoon, a vibrant freshwater pool surrounded by rainforest. Relax on the banks or wade into the brilliant blue waters for a dip. Take part in this scenic escape on your Luganville journey to experience one-of-a-kind natural beauty in peace under the palms. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Runsuc Customs & Firewalking
blocks.text: Walk through rainforest paths to reach Runsuc Village, where you’ll be welcomed with traditional songs and greeted by young warriors performing fire‑walking. Observe artisans demonstrate their skill at sand drawing and watch village women teach the preparation of lap lap in an underground oven before returning along scenic coastal roads. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Relics of World War II
blocks.text: Explore Luganville’s war heritage with visits to the Japanese jail, the U.S.‑built BP Wharf and Euart’s Memorial. Then stand above Million Dollar Point, where tons of wartime equipment were jettisoned into the sea and now form a remarkable underwater reef. Book an excursion to experience the powerful history and natural wonder of Luganville. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Luganville Highlights
blocks.text: Experience a panoramic drive that showcases Luganville’s coastline, plantations and exquisite townscape. Your guide points out key landmarks, provides local insight and shares an authentic, personal view of everyday life. This tour is an ideal first look at the region of Luganville, setting you up for deeper cultural and natural adventures. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Leweton Cultural Experience
blocks.text: Visit Leweton Village for a vivid cultural exchange. Start by listening to history and tradition told through music, dance and water‑based performances by the women of the community. This immersive outing invites you into Melanesian life in a way that stays with you long after you depart. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Canoe The Riri River
blocks.text: Glide aboard a dug‑out canoe along the Riri River, paddling past lush vegetation and rainbow‑colored fish. As the water shifts from light azure to deep cobalt, you’ll arrive at the famous Luganville Blue Hole. Spend time here swimming or snorkeling in its clear, calm pool before your comfortable return. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Luganville
blocks.text: Luganville sits on Espiritu Santo, the largest island in Vanuatu, and makes a memorable stop on South Pacific cruise itineraries. From natural blue holes and lush jungles to historical World War II sites, this port is part relaxation, part adventure. Many Tahiti and South Pacific Princess cruises include Luganville as part of broader voyages through Fiji, Samoa and beyond.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Mystery Island
blocks.text: A half-mile off the coast of Aneityum, tucked away in the far-flung corner of the Vanuatu archipelago, sits an uninhabited blip called Mystery Island. It has no permanent roads, electricity or telephones, and yet somehow more life than most cities. Originally an Allied airstrip in World War II, it was kept secret for reasons of war-time security (which is how it got its name). Today, it’s less abo

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Mystery Island
blocks.text: Craving something curated? These excursions give you the best of Mystery Island with just the right amount of structure… and a whole lot of ‘wow.’

blocks.heading: Mystery Island Drift Snorkel
blocks.text: Hop aboard a small boat and sail to the edges of the marine sanctuary where the reef comes alive. A professional snorkel guide joins you in the water, helping you drift through coral forests alive with fish that look like they were designed by enthusiastic kids with a crayon box. Expect a gentle current, no-fuss navigation and water so clear it feels like floating in air. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Modern Village Tour
blocks.text: Cross the water by ferry and step straight into the daily life of Aneityum’s locals (warriors, dancers and all). After a ceremonial welcome, you're led through their village and into the homes of families who still live by the old ways. Expect traditional dances, cultural rituals and stories that haven’t made it onto Google. This two-hour cultural handshake is part time travel, part anthropology.

blocks.heading: Fire Walking and Kastom Magic Tour
blocks.text: Things heat up fast on this wild walk into Aneityum’s Kastom culture. Local guides introduce you to the spiritual side of island life, from firewalking rituals to leaf-based magic that’ll leave you questioning what you consider ‘real.’ It’s raw, it’s real and it’s about as far from a Vegas stage show as you can get. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Clear Kayak and Snorkel
blocks.text: First, glide over coral gardens in a see-through kayak. Then, hop out and snorkel a secluded white-sand cove where fish practically pose for you. This excursion is beginner-friendly shallow-water bliss, with enough of a discovery factor to keep even seasoned sea lovers grinning. Bonus: your return paddle features local landmarks, all highlighted by your guide. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Keamu Cultural Village Tour
blocks.text: Get hands-on with ancient survival skills in Keamu village, a place where traditions are lived (rather than preserved behind glass). Try your hand at mat weaving, examine fishing traps built like brain puzzles and learn how food is stored without modern tech. This isn’t just a tour, it’s a time capsule with a chance of sun tan. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Mystery Island
blocks.text: Step off the tender and into literal paradise(of the unspoiled, Garden of Eden variety). Mystery Island welcomes you with live island music, a pop-up marketplace and water activities galore. Everything’s walkable and accessible, with paths winding past souvenir stalls, food huts and snorkeling, kayaking and exploring the island’s beaches just steps from the pier. blocks.heading: Things to do in Nouméa
blocks.text: Nouméa is what you would get if France crashed into the South Pacific and decided to stay for beach day. With white‑sanded shores, a reef that just won’t quit and a downtown packed with French pastries and Kanak culture, you’ll feel both chic and salty at the same time.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Nouméa
blocks.text: Nouméa cruises offer a mix of coastal chill, wildlife wonder and French‑Pacific style that puts typical beach stops to shame.

blocks.heading: Tjibaou Cultural Centre
blocks.text: Visit the stunning Jean‑Marie Tjibaou Cultural Centre — its sail‑like pavilions designed by Renzo Piano are as artful as the exhibits inside. Walk the Kanak path, explore indigenous gardens and immerse yourself in native culture that extends back much further than French influence and out far beyond the beach. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Forest Parc and Cagou Encounter
blocks.text: Trees, wildlife and a day to remember: you’ll take a quick drive to Parc Zoologique et Forestier, set high above Nouméa with panoramas and tree‑lined walking paths. Spot the rare flightless bird Cagou (which sounds like a barking dog) and other native creatures, and enjoy the shifting backdrop of hills and sea along the way. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Nouméa City Highlights
blocks.text: This guided coach tour begins in the lively downtown, passes through the old residential district of Faubourg Blanchot, continues along the Promenade Pierre Vernier and ends at Anse Vata’s palm‑lined beach. Snap a photo at Rocher à la Voile, stroll local markets and see for yourself why Nouméa is called the “Paris of the Pacific.” LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Historical tour: Maritime Museum and WWII Museum
blocks.text: Hop aboard an air‑conditioned coach for this two‑hour deep dive into Nouméa’s past: start at the Maritime Museum with shipwrecks and navigators’ charts, then move to the World War II Museum and explore the island’s strategic role in the Pacific war theatre. It’s an eye-opening look at how trade and conflict can shape a region. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Scenic Drive with Cheese & Wine Tasting
blocks.text: Drive into the hills, past colonial homes and flaming red trees at Place des Cocotiers, until you reach Ouen Toro lookout. Then sit down at a local restaurant for French cheeses and wines paired perfectly with island scenery — yes, that’s French pastries and Pacific sunsets all in one beautiful Nouméan experience. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kayaking to Sainte Marie Island
blocks.text: Head to Ouémo district for a guided kayak across the lagoon toward Sainte Marie Island. Paddle through coral‑fringed waters, reach a secluded beach for a refreshment break (paddling is hungry work, after all) and learn all about New Caledonia’s mix of French and Kanak culture before returning to port. LEARN MORE

blocks.text: Port Vila is a layered kind of place: rainforest hikes meet beach days, coral reefs meet colonial legacies and the Blue Lagoon waits just a short drive away. It’s the capital of Vanuatu, but don’t expect suits and skylines; this is jungle, ocean and island culture served straight up with a twist.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Port Vila
blocks.text: Want to do more than wander? Choose from a range of specially curated Princess shore excursions designed to deliver a lively mix of nature, culture and unforgettable adventure:

blocks.heading: Semi‑Sub Reef Exploration
blocks.text: How about a literal deep dive into what makes Port Vila so special. Board a custom‑built semi‑submersible vessel called the Reef Explorer and take in the underwater world from a viewing room below deck. Or, jump in for a snorkel-assisted closer look at coral reefs and tropical fish species thriving in the clear water off Efate. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Aqua Quad Safari
blocks.text: Drive your own Zego Aqua Quad from the harbour outward past million‑dollar waterfront mansions and anchored yachts, then cruise on to Ifira Island for tropical‑fruit refreshment and a quick swim. Continue to Paradise Cove’s coral reef in crystal clear water, then return via Malapoa Peninsula and Fatmaru Bay for more harbor views. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Port Vila Clear Kayak & Snorkel
blocks.text: Paddle out onto the calm waters of the harbour in a transparent kayak and glide over coral reefs teaming with fish species. It’s like having your own window into the colorful and dynamic world below the surface… because that’s exactly what it is! Drift along the seafront where market houses sell fresh produce and local handicrafts. Finally, snorkel at the Iririki reef in the protected bay for an e

blocks.heading: Bridges of Eden
blocks.text: This excursion begins with a scenic drive into the lush eco‑garden of Eden on the River just outside Port Vila. After a safety briefing and walk through the forest edge you’ll cross three suspended bridges — one 23 m long, another 52 m 2–4 m above the river and a final 23 m span boasting a dramatic view of the river below. It’s equal parts paradise and height-induced panic (in a good way). LEARN M

blocks.heading: Ekasup Cultural Village
blocks.text: Board a minibus into the heart of the Erakor rainforest and meet the chief and warriors of the Ekasup in full regalia at the traditional Melanesian compound. Learn how native herbal medicines are prepared from flora, watch hunting/trapping demos, taste laplap (the local dish) and hear exciting tales of tribal history. Then browse woven handicrafts and refresh yourself with a selection of fresh tro

blocks.heading: Port Vila Horse Trek
blocks.text: Meet a friendly and knowledgeable riding instructor at Club Hippique (a 400‑acre copra plantation surrounded by rainforest and beach). After your skill level has been assessed, you’ll embark on a guided trail ride through hills and rainforest down to a saltwater lagoon. blocks.heading: Things to do in Rabaul
blocks.text: Jungles, volcanos and secret tunnels, oh my! Sail to Rabaul, which is home to a magnificent volcano, bubbling hot springs, sprawling jungles and WWII tunnels beneath it all. Whether you want to soak in the stunning scenery of Papua New Guinea or explore the area’s unique history during WWII and two volcanic eruptions, Rabaul is the place to go.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Rabaul
blocks.text: Don’t stress over planning — experience the best Rabaul has to offer, stress-free, with Princess shore excursions. We’ll handle the details so you can relax and soak it all in.

blocks.heading: Mask Festival on the Volcanic Ash Plains
blocks.text: Immerse yourself in the rich Rabaul culture at a mask festival held on the volcanic ash plains. You’ll watch 90 minutes of vibrant dancing as local performers dress in traditional headdresses and perform dances and rhythmic chants. This festival also helps raise money for the community to cover health and educational needs. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Bita Paka War Cemetery, Kokopo War & Cultural Museum
blocks.text: Step into Rabaul’s fascinating past by exploring fortified Japanese tunnels from WWII, the Bita Paka War Cemetery and the coconut plantation called Queen Emma's Steps. blocks.heading: Things to do in Raiatea
blocks.text: Raiatea offers an authentic glimpse into the heart of Polynesia, where history, culture and natural beauty come together. Explore ancient temples, cruise the tranquil lagoon and experience the island’s quiet charm that feels both grounding and unforgettable.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Raiatea
blocks.text: Raiatea’s shore excursions invite you to experience the island’s natural beauty and cultural depth at an easygoing pace. Whether on land or water, every outing captures the spirit and authenticity that make this island so special.

blocks.heading: Local Connections: A Taste of Vanilla & Tahaa Motu Picnic
blocks.text: Travel across the turquoise lagoon to a nearby island to learn how vanilla is grown and harvested. Then relax on a peaceful motu, where you can swim, enjoy the clear water and share a fresh picnic surrounded by stunning island views. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Tahaa Coral Gardens Drift Snorkel
blocks.text: Float through clear, shallow waters filled with colorful coral and tropical fish. After a short boat ride from the main island, you’ll drift gently along the reef near a small motu, surrounded by the calm beauty and vibrant marine life that make this spot one of Raiatea’s most memorable experiences. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Raiatea
blocks.text: Set out across Raiatea’s calm lagoon to take in sweeping views of emerald peaks and turquoise waters. Along the way, enjoy peaceful moments surrounded by nature before stepping ashore to explore the island’s historic sites and lush landscapes. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Kayak the Faaroa River
blocks.text: Journey along a peaceful river surrounded by dense tropical foliage and the sounds of island wildlife. As you move through calm waters, you’ll discover Raiatea’s lush interior from a new perspective—where nature, history and serenity come together in one unforgettable experience. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Raiatea: Land & Sea of Taha’a
blocks.text: This excursion begins with a scenic boat ride across the tranquil lagoon, followed by an off-road drive through lush valleys and rainforest. You’ll stop at a hillside viewpoint, learn about vanilla and pearl farming and explore vibrant coral gardens on a snorkeling stop — blending nature, culture and island charm into one adventure. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Raiatea Reef Discovery
blocks.text: Set out on a shaded catamaran across the calm lagoon northwest of the island, where a naturalist guide introduces you to vibrant coral gardens teeming with tropical fish. With easy water access, this relaxed adventure offers a peaceful way to experience the island’s spectacular underwater world. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Raiatea
blocks.text: Cruise itineraries to Raiatea reveal one of French Polynesia’s most culturally rich and naturally stunning destinations. Often called the “sacred island,” Raiatea offers a peaceful escape with lush valleys, calm lagoons and deep historical significance. blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Tahiti
blocks.text: Experience Tahiti’s stunning lagoons, waterfalls and cultural landmarks through curated shore excursions that highlight the island’s natural beauty and traditions. From snorkelling outings to guided island tours, these experiences offer a memorable way to immerse yourself in Tahiti.

blocks.heading: Easy Papeete
blocks.text: Explore Tahiti’s top landmarks on this half-day guided tour. Begin with a scenic drive to the Monument of Captain Bligh, then follow the island’s east coast past the well-known Papenoo surfing beaches. Continue to Tahara’a “One Tree Hill” for sweeping views of Matavai Bay before visiting historic Point Venus, where Captain Cook landed in 1769. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Papeete
blocks.text: Discover Tahiti’s cultural and natural wonders on a scenic journey to Tahara'a “One Tree Hill” for sweeping views of Matavai Bay, followed by a visit to Venus Point. Continue past Maraa Grotto, the lush Vaipahi waterfalls and gardens and an ancient marae before exploring the renowned Museum of Tahiti and Her Islands. Conclude your experience with a delicious Polynesian-style buffet lunch before re

blocks.heading: Circle Island Drive
blocks.text: Set out on a half-day, air-conditioned motorcoach tour showcasing Tahiti’s most iconic sights with lively English narration. Enjoy panoramic views from Tahara'a Hill, photograph historic Point Venus and take in village life en route to Papeari. Visit Vaipahi’s fragrant gardens and waterfall, explore Mara’a Fern Grotto Caves and relax with a refreshing beverage before returning to the ship. LEARN M

blocks.heading: Lagoon Sail & Snorkel Tour
blocks.text: Snorkel, swim and unwind in the warm waters of Papeete’s lagoon on this three-hour catamaran excursion departing directly from the pier. Sail across cerulean seas with views of Tahiti’s emerald volcanic peaks before slipping into clear, shallow waters filled with vibrant corals and marine life. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Papenoo Valley & Waterfall by 4WD
blocks.text: Board a 4WD vehicle to explore Tahiti’s wild east coast and the lush Papenoo Valley. Travel inland along the river, passing steep, rainforest-clad mountains, cascading waterfalls and river crossings with photo stops along the way. Enjoy a refreshing swim in a natural pool and visit a famous black-sand surfing beach before returning to the pier. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Undiscovered Tahiti
blocks.text: Trace Tahiti’s west coast through Punaauia to the sacred Marae Arahurahu, then continue past Paea and Papara to Mataiea, Paul Gauguin’s former home. Explore a 1920s colonial residence, capture photos at Vaipahi Gardens and Mara’a Grotto, and conclude at the Museum of Tahiti and Her Islands—one of the South Pacific’s finest showcases of Polynesian culture. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Tahiti
blocks.text: Cruise itineraries featuring Tahiti bring you straight into the heart of French Polynesia’s vibrant culture, turquoise lagoons and lush volcanic landscapes. Many South Pacific cruise routes feature this iconic port, giving travellers the chance to experience its rich culture, coastal scenery, and historic sites while exploring the South Pacific.

blocks.heading: Experience the Transatlantic on your next cruise
Why a Transatlantic Cruise
blocks.text: Our departure ports are as iconic as the destinations we visit. You can a little extra vacation to your vacation by arriving early or staying after your cruise and exploring the wonders that lie within these cities.

blocks.heading: Why cruise with Princess
blocks.text: Curated comfort, world-class entertainment and international flavors await you.

blocks.heading: Celebrations & Romance
blocks.text: It's difficult to imagine something more romantic than sailing through the alluring cities and charming countryside of Europe. While on board your European cruise, we cater to your sentimental side with private dining on your balcony — like breakfast for two or a sunset dinner — honeymoon packages, flowers and chocolates delivered to your room and couples-only massages in the Sanctuary.

blocks.heading: Accommodations
blocks.text: Your stateroom is where you rest and recharge between adventures. That’s why every room is equipped with the expertly designed Princess Luxury Bed, 100% Jacquard-woven cotton linens. Whether you go interior or all-out in a suite, our staterooms will make you feel right at home. Especially for families traveling together who can enjoy the option of connected rooms.

blocks.heading: Dining
blocks.text: From the spice of Moroccan tagine to the sweetness of Greek Baklava, Europe’s flavor profile is incredibly diverse. On a Transatlantic cruise with Princess, taste the best of Europe on board with specialty dining. Say cheers during a lively lunch at a British-style pub and try English favorites like bangers and mash or shepherd's pie. Or savor hearty Italian pastas at Sabatini’s℠ Italian Trattoria

blocks.heading: Entertainment
blocks.text: Embark on adventures by day, and indulge in entertainment by night. Watch Movies Under the Stars® at our 300-square-foot outdoor theater. Attend original productions from Broadway legend Stephen Schwartz, composer of Wicked. Or learn traditional moves, like flamenco or Irish stepdance, and listen to popular music from the destinations on your itinerary. On a European cruise with Princess, the choi

blocks.heading: Relaxation
blocks.text: Your European cruise should be every bit as refreshing as it is inspiring. Unwind in the Sanctuary, a retreat just for adults, and relish in tranquility. Or book an appointment at the Lotus Spa®. Enjoy soothing treatments — like facials, hot stone massages and detoxifying wraps — that will leave you energized for upcoming adventures.

blocks.heading: Casino
blocks.text: Experience the thrill of cards, dice, roulette, and blackjack at our onboard casino during your European cruise. Learn from our expert staff or seasoned guests, and put your skills to the test. For a more relaxed pace, enjoy the slot machines, or join fellow travelers for Bingo and exciting group tournaments. blocks.heading: Ocho Rios Bay Beach, Jamaica
blocks.text: One of the most popular beaches in Jamaica with both locals and travelers, Ocho Rios Bay Beach has everything needed for a relaxing day enjoying the Caribbean weather. Soft sand, crystal-clear water, plentiful loungers and ice-cold beverages. What more can you ask for when you visit Ocho Rios Bay Beach on a Jamaican cruise?

blocks.heading: Sosua Beach, Dominican Republic
blocks.text: The peaceful blue water and golden sands of Sosua Beach are picture perfect, but the real star of this beach is the atmosphere. The entire beach vibrates with excitement, fun and the sounds of locals and travelers reveling in a true Caribbean atmosphere. Lounge on the shore, snorkel through a coral reef, or grab a delicious lunch from a local cooking Dominican specialties, and fall in love with th

blocks.heading: Seven Mile Beach, Grand Cayman
blocks.text: Idyllic white sands that stretch as far as the eye can see in both directions, brilliant blue water beyond that and endless opportunities for activities makes Seven Mile Beach one of the best in the world. If you enjoy bars, resorts, boutiques and restaurants (that is, when you're not drinking in the stunning scenery), then you must visit Seven Mile Beach on your Grand Cayman cruise!

blocks.heading: Caribbean cruise onboard experience featured program
blocks.text: Award-winning programs. World-class chefs. And Caribbean-themed activities, day and night. With Princess, your ship is a destination all its own.

blocks.heading: Deeper experiences of the islands
blocks.text: Discover the history of local distilleries while sampling some of the region’s best rums, meet the parrots and macaws that call the Caribbean home in the ship's Piazza, or sink into the rhythms of the region with steel pan drum lessons. Our onboard activities give you the chance to gain a deeper connection and understanding to islands you'll visit on your voyage.

blocks.heading: Comfortable accommodations
blocks.text: Your stateroom is your home away from home where you can rest up and recharge between adventures. blocks.heading: Never miss a beat
blocks.text: Say goodbye to the daily grind with our new Sail Away Party poolside on the top deck, dance to local music at one of the many Caribbean inspired concerts, or be the envy of every pirate at our high-energy gold treasure-inspired Terrace Pool Gold Party. Throughout your Caribbean cruise there will be events that invite you to fully experience the islands.

blocks.heading: Unforgettable ports of call
blocks.text: Not only will you encounter some of the world’s most revered sites and cities from Tokyo to Sydney, but you’ll also have the opportunity to step ashore in lesser frequented ports, maiden calls, and first-time-ever calls for Princess — with shore excursions designed to help you experience the very best of each destination.

blocks.heading: Adventure of a lifetime
blocks.text: There are a million reasons to take a World Cruise – like exploring 6 continents on 1 voyage – but the reason to book one now is our richest offer yet. Nothing can beat the experience of a World Cruise. The camaraderie among guests, the shared experiences in fascinating ports across the globe, and the parties and celebrations on board and ashore all make this a true adventure that everyone should

blocks.text: Enjoy special activities unique to this epic voyage. Over 50 international guest entertainers keep you smiling; attend cocktail parties and themed deck parties, watch local folkloric shows, savor special officer dinners, commemorative take-home menus, cooking classes with Princess Cruises Chefs, and much more.

blocks.heading: Things to do in Cape Town
Shore excursions to explore in Walvis Bay
blocks.text: Dive into curated excursions that showcase just how much Namibia likes to keep you guessing: ancient desert ecosystems, seal-packed lagoons, defunct diamond camps and dune rides worthy of Mad Max.

blocks.heading: The Best of Cape Town
blocks.text: For those who want it all. Depart the pier and drive through Sea Point, Bantry Bay and Clifton toward Cape Point via the Atlantic coast. Visit the reserve where the two oceans meet, take the funicular at Cape Point if the weather allows, then stop at Boulders Beach to see the penguin colony. Free time in Kalk Bay for shopping rounds out the day before returning via the historic University of Cape

blocks.heading: Table Mountain Views
blocks.text: No visit to Cape Town is complete without a trip up Table Mountain, the city’s most celebrated landmark. You’ll head up Kloof Nek to the Lower Cableway Station. Ascending from 1,190 feet to 3,500 feet in a rotating car takes just under four minutes, and the summit opens onto a protected area with 2,285 plant species (more than the entire United Kingdom). LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: High Tea at Mount Nelson: A Small Group Tour
blocks.text: Your scenic drive out of the pier winds through Cape Town’s center past Parliament to the elegant Mount Nelson Hotel. Here, you’ll sip high tea in the terraced gardens, relax to piano music and absorb the grandeur. On the return drive you’ll cruise along Kloof Nek Road, Camps Bay, Clifton and Sea Point. It’s sightseeing with a scone in hand. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Easy Chapman’s Peak Scenic Drive
blocks.text: Drive away from the city along the Atlantic seaboard, through Sea Point, Bantry Bay, Clifton and Camps Bay, with a stop at Maiden’s Cove for ocean views. You then continue via the world‑renowned Chapmans Peak Drive. On your return you’ll pass Noordhoek Beach, the University of Cape Town and the historic Groote Schuur Hospital. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Amazing Aquila Game Reserve
blocks.text: Board an air‑conditioned coach from the pier to the semi‑scrub desert of the Southern Karoo Highlands and the private Aquila Game Reserve. After a welcome drink you’ll hop into a 4×4 safari vehicle searching for zebras, wildebeest, warthog, springbok and even lions. A buffet lunch follows, and you return to Cape Town with wild memories in tow. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: African Drumming and Dinner
blocks.text: Disembark the cruise ship and head out to the GOLD Restaurant for an evening of food, rhythms and culture. You’ll take part in an interactive djembe drumming session, feast on a 14‑dish tasting menu rooted in African culinary traditions (with vegetarian/vegan options) and enjoy live marimba & puppetry entertainment. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Casablanca
blocks.text: Pick from an array of adventures that stretch from mosque minarets to mountain deserts, each one serving up Morocco’s bold mix of tradition, color and cuisine.

blocks.heading: Cooking Demonstration & Central Market
blocks.text: Start with a walk through Casablanca’s Central Market (a living mural of fresh fish, spices and locals bartering). Then head to a hilltop restaurant overlooking the Atlantic for a Moroccan cooking demo and lunch. Watch chefs work magic with lemons and saffron, then taste the results for yourself. You’ll return to the ship full of flavor, both literal and cultural. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hassan II Mosque & Lunch at Rick’s Café
blocks.text: Your journey begins with a drive to the iconic Hassan II Mosque, a marvel of craftsmanship and engineering that appears to rise straight from the sea. Inside, sunlight filters through carved arches and mosaics that could make even the most jaded traveler whisper “wow.” Then, it’s on to Rick’s Café — a faithful recreation of the movie classic’s setting. Savor lunch as a pianist plays, and imagine B

blocks.heading: Wine Tasting at Domaine Thalvin
blocks.text: A short drive from Casablanca leads to the vineyards of Domaine Thalvin, Morocco’s largest and oldest winery. The landscape changes from city bustle to quiet rows of vines framed by dusty hills. You’ll tour the caves, meet local vintners and taste a range of wines paired with Moroccan nibbles that make ‘terroir’ taste like adventure. It’s a refined way to toast the country’s emerging wine scene be

blocks.heading: Best of Marrakech: Bahia Palace & Djemaa‑el‑F’na
blocks.text: All aboard for a sensory overload in Marrakech, where minarets meet snake charmers and the air hums with spice. After the scenic drive, you’ll stop for a photo op at Koutoubia Minaret, then tour the Bahia Palace’s painted ceilings, courtyards and tiled perfection. A traditional Moroccan lunch and folkloric show follow before heading into the old Medina, where Djemaa‑el‑F’na bursts to life with sto

blocks.heading: Casablanca & Rabat
blocks.text: This two‑city tour shows off Casablanca’s modern flair and Rabat’s regal calm. You’ll start at the Habous Quarter and its souks before visiting the Hassan II Mosque and Mohammed V Square. After lunch, continue to Rabat to admire the Royal Palace exterior, the Mausoleum of King Mohammed V and the red sandstone Hassan Tower. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Hassan II Mosque & Casablanca Sights
blocks.text: For travelers who like to explore on foot, this is Casablanca up close and personal. Begin with the towering Hassan II Mosque, then cruise the Corniche by motorcoach before ducking into Notre Dame de Lourdes to admire its stained glass glow. The tour ends in the Habbous Quarter, where you can roam souks for spices, ceramics and maybe a well-earned bargain. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Dravuni Island
blocks.text: Tiny but mighty, this small island in Fiji’s Kadavu Group delivers village charm, beach relaxation and splashy underwater action all in one perfect day. With fewer than 200 residents, the local community greets you with ‘bula’ (meaning ‘hello’) smiles and sometimes even a song, making a simple walk as memorable as snorkeling through the Great Astrolabe Reef. Expect tender boat access to Dravuni Is

blocks.heading: Explore the port in Dravuni Island
blocks.text: On Dravuni, the port day itself becomes the excursion. As your tender boat rides you ashore, you’ll step into island serenity: stretch your legs on walking trails, snorkel clear waters, greet villagers in the shade of coconut palms and simply savour the moment. Snorkeling gear, hiking shoes and a curious attitude are your must-have companions.

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Dravuni Island
blocks.text: When you book cruises to Dravuni Island, you arrive at a tender port that drops you into lagoon‑blue waters and gently swaying palms rather than commercial hustle. With no big resorts, only one small village and so much nature front and centre, this island stop is perfect for a diversion from big‑city ports. This makes it a unique and refreshingly simple part of your Tahiti & South Pacific cruise

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Lombok
blocks.text: Choose from curated tours that mix island intrigue with craft traditions, nature thrills and (of course) some seriously good beach time.

blocks.heading: Lingsar Temple, Mayura Water Palace & Craft Village
blocks.text: This full‑day tour starts at Sesela Market and visits Lingsar Temple (look for the sacred pool where devotees drop hard‑boiled eggs for eels), followed by the Mayura Water Palace — an open‑sided pavilion sitting on a man‑made lake. After a buffet lunch, you’ll drop by Sukarare craft village for songket shopping before heading back. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Sekotong Village & Sundancer Beach
blocks.text: This half‑day tour kicks off with a visit to Sekotong Village where you’ll peek into a grass‑roof factory crafting alang‑alang‑thatch, then head to Sundancer Beach with its protected bays, coral gardens and crystalline waters of the Lombok Strait. You’ll enjoy free time to swim, sunbathe or simply absorb the setting of lush green mountains meeting blue sea. A photo stop at a traditional brick fact

blocks.heading: Sasak Traditional Houses, Crafts Villages & Kuta Beach
blocks.text: This full‑day tour wraps culture, crafts and beach time into one. You’ll start in Banyu Mulek, watching local potters at their wheels and ride a horse cart through the village. Then it’s on to Sukarare for songket weaving, followed by Sade Village with its traditional Sasak houses. Lunch comes just before free time at Kuta Beach (one of Lombok’s best seascapes) before heading back to the ship. LEA

blocks.heading: Mataram Highlights
blocks.text: In this half‑day outing you’ll hit Lingsar Temple (a symbol of faith‑fusion on the island), browse through Mataram’s pearl shops and the Sayang‑Sayang Art Market for pottery, rattan‑woven baskets and wood carvings inlaid with mother‑of‑pearl. Final stop: the provincial museum where you’ll see songket cloths, Kris knives and ancient drums. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Senggigi On Your Own
blocks.text: Board your coach for about an hour’s drive north from the port area to Senggigi Beach. Along the way you’ll pass rice terraces and spice plantations. At Senggigi you’ve got time to explore craft galleries and trendy cafés or to take a snorkel adventure among reef‑lined shores. Then head back to the ship when you’re ready. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Craft Villages of Lombok
blocks.text: Drive inland to Sesela Village and watch artisans carve ketak wood and pearl shell into masks, frames and decorative wall hangings. Then continue to Banyumulek, famed for red‑clay pottery. You’ll ride a traditional horse cart (‘Cidomo’), watch clay being shaped and even be able to take a piece of pottery home before returning. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Things to do in Mindelo
blocks.text: Mindelo offers a vibrant blend of music, culture and coastal beauty, making it one of Cape Verde’s most charming cities. From colorful colonial streets to lively markets and scenic beaches, there’s something to explore at every turn.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Mindelo
blocks.text: Shore excursions in Mindelo introduce you to the city’s vibrant culture, scenic coastlines and musical heritage. From panoramic island tours to immersive cultural experiences, there’s an excursion for every kind of traveler.

blocks.heading: Viana Volcano Hiking Adventure
blocks.text: Embark on an adventurous 4x4 ride to Calhau before beginning an energizing hike up the extinct Viana volcano. Learn about the island’s geologic past as you ascend 163 meters to the caldera, where sweeping views of Calhau village and nearby islands await. After taking in the crater’s stunning scenery, descend and enjoy a refreshing drink at a local restaurant. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Snorkeling With The Turtles
blocks.text: Get ready for a splash of adventure as you zoom from the pier to your boat and set off across Cape Verde’s sparkling waters. Slip on your snorkel and dive in as curious sea turtles gather near the fishermen’s catch, gliding playfully just below the surface. It’s a lively, unforgettable encounter. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Walking Tour of Mindelo
blocks.text: Experience the vibrant island of São Vicente on a guided half-day adventure beginning right at the pier. Explore Mindelo on foot, visiting landmarks like the Diogo Afonso Monument, the Belem Tower replica and lively local markets filled with Crioulo rhythms. Continue through the historic district before driving to Monte Verde for sweeping views, then visit Baía das Gatas, a stunning white-sand bea

blocks.heading: Sounds, Arts & Crafts of Sao Vicente Island
blocks.text: Embark on a cultural journey through Mindelo as you explore the legacy of Cesária Évora and the vibrant arts of Cabo Verde. Visit the Cesária Évora Museum, learn about morna music and stop at the square to photograph Vhils’ striking mural. Enjoy local appetizers and melodies before visiting the National Center of Art, Crafts and Design, showcasing works by talented Cape Verdean artists. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Island Drive
blocks.text: Embark on a relaxed three-hour motorcoach journey through Mindelo’s volcanic landscapes, beginning with a scenic ascent to Monte Verde, the island’s highest peak, for sweeping views of surrounding islands. Continue along the coast to Praia Grande, where white sand meets black lava cliffs and you’ll enjoy a taste of local grogue or pontche. On the return, pass through Ribeira de Calhau to learn abo

blocks.heading: Around the Island By 4WD
blocks.text: Explore the natural beauty of São Vicente on a guided 4x4 adventure through its dramatic landscapes. Travel from Mindelo into the countryside beneath Monte Verde, pausing at Assomada for sweeping views of nearby uninhabited islands. Continue through volcanic valleys and coastal villages, stopping at Palha Larga’s black-sand beach before ending at Topim, a white-sand haven beloved by surfers. LEARN

blocks.heading: Things to do in Moorea
blocks.text: Known as Tahiti’s “sister island,” Moorea is a tropical paradise where emerald mountains meet sparkling lagoons. From swimming with rays and sharks to exploring lush pineapple fields, every corner of Moorea invites adventure and pure island bliss.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Moorea
blocks.text: Moorea’s shore excursions immerse you in the island’s breathtaking beauty and vibrant culture. Each experience offers a unique glimpse into what makes this tropical paradise so unforgettable.

blocks.heading: Local Connections: Moorea In Focus Photography Expedition
blocks.text: Set out on a relaxed 4×4-ride with a professional photographer by your side, weaving through lush landscapes, panoramic lookouts and serene bays. You’ll pause in picturesque spots along the way, snack on fresh tropical fruit and come away with stunning images of this island’s vibrant beauty. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Best of Moorea: Lagoon & Coral Motu Snorkel
blocks.text: Enjoy a relaxing day on the water as you cruise across Moorea’s stunning lagoon and visit a small island surrounded by colorful marine life. Swim, snorkel and unwind in paradise before heading back through the island’s breathtaking scenery. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ultimate Moorea: Motu Islet Beach
blocks.text: Spend a relaxing day on a beautiful island surrounded by clear blue water. Enjoy swimming, snorkeling and a traditional beach barbecue while experiencing the laid-back charm and natural beauty that make Moorea unforgettable. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Moorea Sail By Catamaran
blocks.text: Glide across a turquoise lagoon aboard a sleek catamaran and pause to snorkel in crystal-clear waters, surrounded by vibrant marine life and gentle underwater landscapes. When you’re ready to relax, drift back over gentle waves with fresh fruit in hand and the island’s lush peaks as your backdrop. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Moorea by 4WD
blocks.text: Embark on an adventurous journey through Moorea’s lush interior as you travel off the beaten path in a 4WD vehicle. Take in sweeping views, tropical landscapes and the island’s natural beauty at every turn—an unforgettable way to experience the heart of this Polynesian paradise. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Dolphin & Whale Watching
blocks.text: Cruise across Moorea’s crystal-clear waters with a naturalist guide as you search for playful dolphins and, during the right season, magnificent whales. Surrounded by the island’s dramatic peaks and vibrant blue sea, you’ll experience the wonder of observing these incredible creatures in their natural environment. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Explore itineraries with cruises to Moorea
blocks.text: Set sail on unforgettable adventures across the South Pacific with cruise itineraries that include the enchanting island of Moorea. Nestled among turquoise lagoons and emerald peaks, this destination is a favorite stop for travelers seeking both relaxation and adventure. Discover how a visit to Moorea fits seamlessly into our Tahiti and South Pacific Cruises for the ultimate island escape.

blocks.heading: Shore excursions to explore in Mauritius
blocks.text: Every excursion in Mauritius feels like someone turned up the saturation on real life: bold colors, big flavors and experiences you’ll be absolutely obnoxious in telling your friends about.

blocks.heading: Sugar World & Pamplemousses Botanical Gardens
blocks.text: Start at Sugar World (it’s as sweet as it sounds), where a former sugar factory now tells the island’s sticky, syrupy history through massive vats and museum displays. After hitting the boutique for edible souvenirs, you’ll continue to the Pamplemousses Botanical Gardens for a guided stroll past lily ponds, palm giants and a colony of giant tortoises. On the way back, stop at La Citadelle for one

blocks.heading: Best of Mauritius
blocks.text: Kick things off at Trou aux Cerfs, a dormant volcanic crater that doubles as a panoramic Instagram jackpot. Visit Voiliers de l’Océan to see teak ship models being built like it’s 1799, then head to Grand Bassin (a lake inside a volcano that doubles as a Hindu pilgrimage site). You’ll grab lunch, then wrap the day at Chamarel’s Seven Coloured Earth. Just don’t try to take it home with you — custom

blocks.heading: Journey Into Local Culture
blocks.text: If you’re the kind of traveler who wants to know why a place feels the way it does, this one’s for you. Start at the Nelson Mandela Centre for African Culture and learn how slavery shaped modern Mauritius. Then visit Aapravasi Ghat, a UNESCO site that traces the island’s Indian heritage. After wandering Chinatown and checking out a Hindu temple, sit down to a locally hosted lunch that mashes up Ch

blocks.heading: Eureka Colonial House & Port Louis Main Market
blocks.text: Wander through Eureka Colonial House then head into the city for full sensory overload. You’ll stop at the Marie Reine de la Paix Monument for sweeping views before hitting the bustling Port Louis market, where bargaining is a sport and the spices hit you like a very fragrant freight train. You’ll finish with shopping at the Caudan Waterfront and an exterior visit to a Tamil temple. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Shopping & Casela Nature And Leisure Park
blocks.text: Shop ‘til your rupees drop in Curepipe and Floreal (two of Mauritius’s best spots for textiles, crafts and more). Then head to Casela: part bird park, part nature reserve, part wildly photogenic hangout. Meet the famously rare pink pigeon, walk under towering palms and explore gardens that feel straight out of a fairy tale. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Ile Aux Cerfs Escapade
blocks.text: This is the full tropical fantasy. Cruise to Île aux Cerfs, where you’ll be greeted with fruit cocktails and a performance by Sega dancers that will make you want to revise your favorite playlist. Then it’s your time — lounge on the beach, explore the island, jump in the lagoon, go snorkeling or chat with coconut vendors under the casuarinas. blocks.heading: Things to do in Walvis Bay
Shore excursions to explore in Walvis Bay
blocks.text: Dive into curated excursions that showcase just how much Namibia likes to keep you guessing: ancient desert ecosystems, seal-packed lagoons, defunct diamond camps and dune rides worthy of Mad Max.

blocks.heading: The Living Namib Desert
blocks.text: Think nothing lives here? Think again. Join a desert whisperer (aka your guide) to discover critters like the sidewinder adder, palmetto gecko and chameleons living their best lives in the dunes. Your guide will ‘read the bushman paper’ (aka track animals like a desert Sherlock), share weird desert biology facts and maybe even catch some of the living marvels themselves so you can get a closer loo

blocks.heading: Sandwich Harbour
blocks.text: Ride a 4x4 through the Kuiseb River Delta and over undulating dunes. When conditions allow, you’ll reach Sandwich Harbour Lagoon — a tidal haven bursting with flamingos and fed by freshwater seeping under the sand. Enjoy snacks as you scan the landscape for migratory birds and dunes the height of apartment buildings. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Go Local: The 'Real' Namibia
blocks.text: This isn't your typical sightseeing trip. This is an invitation to get real with the residents of Mondesa Township. Learn how the Owambo, Damara and Herero communities have made a home just outside Swakopmund, and explore the traditions, flavors and challenges of everyday life. Taste mahango porridge, hear local music and walk away with something better than a souvenir: a real cultural connection.

blocks.heading: The Best of Walvis Bay: Lagoon Cruise & 4X4 Dunes Adventure
blocks.text: Start your day kicking up sand in a 4x4 as you traverse the soaring dunes of Sandwich Harbour. Then trade wheels for waves and hop on a boat for a 2.5-hour lagoon cruise. Along the way, you might catch dolphins playing tag with the boat and Cape fur seals serving lounging like celebrities. Expect pelicans, petrels, cormorants and more flamingos than seems statistically reasonable. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Pelican Point Kayaking Adventure
blocks.text: Hop in a kayak and say hello to 50,000 Cape fur seals (give or take). Cruise to Pelican Point by boat, then paddle your way past a century-old lighthouse, friendly dolphins and birds with complicated names. After your paddle, take a 4x4 drive back along the lagoon, because Namibia doesn’t believe in doing anything halfway. LEARN MORE

blocks.heading: Soaring over Sossusvlei
blocks.text: This isn’t just a flight; this is a two-hour-and-ten-minute airborne epic over 400 miles of unfiltered Namibian glory. You’ll soar above ancient vulture breeding grounds, past giant rust-red dunes, over diamond ghost towns and down the Skeleton Coast. Watch the earth shift from apricot sand to salt mine whites to shipwreck-strewn beaches. It’s like someone cranked Namibia’s cinematic settings to 1
